articles.title: Adaptive Spectral Analysis of Umbilical Venous Doppler Maternal-Fetal Power Ratio for Preeclampsia Risk Assessment.
articles.journal: Journal of ultrasound in medicine : official journal of the American Institute of Ultrasound in Medicine
articles.authors: Zhu J, Arenas G, Yao X et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To develop and evaluate adaptive spectral analysis for deriving the maternal-fetal power ratio (MFPR) from umbilical venous Doppler recordings and to assess MFPR for subsequent preeclampsia (PEC) risk discrimination across recording durations.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed second-trimester umbilical venous Doppler recordings in 2 datasets: 83 short acquisitions (mean, 3.4 seconds) from 46 subjects (15 with subsequent PEC), and 126 long acquisitions (mean, 6.9 seconds) from 66 subjects (30 with subsequent PEC). Power spectra were estimated by discrete Fourier transform, Welch, and Capon estimators with adaptive window selection, diagonal loading, and maternal and fetal heart-rate-guided peak localization. MFPR was defined as the decibel difference between the maternal and fetal spectral-peak powers and averaged across clips for each subject (median, 2 clips per subject in both datasets). Discrimination was assessed using group differences, receiver operating characteristic area under the curve (AUC), and Youden's J  .
RESULTS: Higher MFPR during the second trimester was associated with subsequent development of PEC. For short recordings, heart-rate-guided adaptive Capon performed best (AUC, 0.84; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.70-0.95). For long recordings, heart-rate-guided Welch performed best (AUC, 0.75; 95% CI, 0.60-0.88). Adaptive window selection reduced performance sensitivity to fixed window length, and diagonal loading stabilized covariance inversion.
CONCLUSIONS: Umbilical venous Doppler MFPR distinguished pregnancies that later developed PEC. The best-performing spectral-analysis pipeline differed between the short and long acquisition datasets. Prospective validation is needed.

articles.title: Decoding prognosis: multigene expression assays in breast cancer.
articles.authors: Kaur C, Agarwal D
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Breast cancer remains a leading cause of cancer-related death in women worldwide. In early-stage, hormone receptor-positive/-negative disease, tissue-based multigene expression assays refine prognosis and guide systemic therapy. Axillary nodal status is still determined by clinical examination, imaging and sentinel lymph node biopsy (SLNB).
AREAS COVERED: This narrative review separates prognostic, predictive and nodal-staging information. For MammaPrint, Oncotype DX, PAM50/Prosigna, EndoPredict and Breast Cancer Index, it summarizes the platform, validated population, level of evidence and guideline status. These assays estimate distant-recurrence risk and/or benefit from chemotherapy or extended endocrine therapy; none was developed or validated to predict nodal involvement. The dedicated gene-expression panels for nodal metastasis derive from retrospective or single-cohort studies, lack prospective validation and are not recommended for axillary staging. Liquid biopsy (ctDNA), multi-omics approaches, and cost, access and standardization are also reviewed.
EXPERT OPINION: The established assays answer narrow, population-specific answers on recurrence and systemic-treatment benefit, not axillary staging; omission of SLNB currently rests on clinical and radiological criteria (SOUND, INSEMA). Nodal signatures remain investigational, and ctDNA and multi-omics approaches are promising but not yet practice-changing, requiring prospective trials showing improved outcomes. Age- and menopausal-status-related chemotherapy effects derive largely from exploratory or subgroup analyses and are hypothesis-generating.

articles.title: Hysteroscopy for Retained Products of Conception in Japan: A Survey of Clinical Practice and Educational Needs.
articles.journal: The journal of obstetrics and gynaecology research
articles.authors: Yatsuki K, Nagasaka K, Sakai K et al.
articles.abstract:
AIM: To characterize the use of hysteroscopy for the management of retained products of conception (RPOC) and identify perceived barriers and educational needs among members of the Japan Society of Perinatal and Neonatal Medicine.
METHODS: An anonymous online survey was conducted among members of the Japan Society of Perinatal and Neonatal Medicine from October 16 to November 15, 2024. Responses were summarized descriptively using questionnaire-branch-specific denominators.
RESULTS: Seventy-seven perinatal clinicians responded, of whom 76 reported having diagnosed RPOC or suspected disease after delivery. Among these 76 respondents, 20 (26.3%) and 22 (28.9%) reported using diagnostic and operative hysteroscopy, respectively. Sixteen of the 20 diagnostic users (80.0%) reported obtaining useful information, and none reported complications during diagnostic hysteroscopy. Two operative users reported a complication or residual tissue, and one did not answer the complication question; these responses could not be used to estimate patient-level complication rates. Among 56 respondents who reported not using hysteroscopy to diagnose RPOC, 20 (35.7%) expressed interest in using it. The most frequently reported barriers were equipment and environmental limitations (26/56, 46.4%) and safety concerns (24/56, 42.9%). Overall, 56 of the 77 respondents (72.7%) expressed interest in hands-on seminars or training courses.
CONCLUSIONS: Diagnostic and operative hysteroscopy for RPOC were each used by fewer than one-third of respondents who answered the relevant management questions, whereas interest in training was common. These findings identify perceived barriers and educational needs that may inform hysteroscopy training and referral arrangements for RPOC care.

articles.title: Association Between Pre-Pregnancy and First-Trimester Hematological Parameters and HELLP Syndrome.
articles.journal: The journal of obstetrics and gynaecology research
articles.authors: Sundberg AJS, Turan GI, Jørgensen HL et al.
articles.abstract:
AIM: To investigate whether hematological biomarkers prior to pregnancy and during the first trimester are associated with subsequent development of HELLP syndrome.
METHODS: This case-control study was based on laboratory data from 2010 to 2023 in the Copenhagen Capital Region. Pregnant women were identified through first-trimester biochemical screening. A total of 216 women with HELLP syndrome were matched to 4302 controls according to maternal age and date of first-trimester biochemical screening. Hemoglobin, platelet count, and leukocyte count measured one year before pregnancy and during the first trimester were assessed. HELLP syndrome was defined biochemically following national guidelines.
RESULTS: Cases had higher hemoglobin levels before pregnancy (8.5 vs. 8.3 mmol/L, p = 0.04) and lower first-trimester platelet counts (238 vs. 256 × 109/L, p = 0.02) than controls. Hemoglobin levels > 8.5 mmol/L before pregnancy were associated with increased odds of HELLP (OR 2.22, 95% CI 1.15-4.31), whereas hemoglobin levels < 7.5 mmol/L in the first trimester were associated with reduced odds (OR 0.45, 95% CI 0.21-0.96). Lower platelet counts in the first trimester were associated with increased odds of HELLP (OR 0.81 per 25-unit increase, 95% CI 0.69-0.95). No associations were observed for leukocyte counts.
CONCLUSION: Higher hemoglobin levels before pregnancy were associated with increased odds of HELLP syndrome, whereas lower levels in the first trimester were associated with reduced odds; additionally, lower first trimester platelet counts were associated with increased odds of HELLP syndrome. These findings warrant further studies to evaluate whether hematological biomarkers improve prediction in multivariable HELLP screening models.

articles.title: Paeoniflorin Alleviates inflammatory injury in mastitis by targeting AKT1-Mediated mitochondrial damage and epithelial cell apoptosis.
articles.authors: Liu X, Wang Z, Lu S et al.
articles.abstract: Peony can clear heat, promote blood circulation, and relieve pain, and peony-containing formulas exert favorable therapeutic effects on mastitis. Paeoniflorin is the primary bioactive component of peony. This study aimed to investigate the therapeutic targets and underlying mechanism of paeoniflorin (Pae) against mastitis, leveraging network pharmacology to guide experimental validation. A mouse mastitis model was established using lipopolysaccharide (LPS). Three concentrations of Pae were administered to evaluate its dose-dependent therapeutic effects, with dexamethasone (DXMS) serving as the positive control drug. Pae treatment significantly ameliorated mastitis in mice, reduced the expression of inflammatory cytokines, and alleviated cellular injury. Network pharmacology analysis revealed that AKT serine/threonine kinase 1 (AKT1) signaling was the most significantly enriched pathway, strongly correlated with both Pae and mastitis. Molecular dynamics simulation and CO-IP experiments confirmed the direct binding between Pae and AKT1. In vitro, we used bovine mammary epithelial cells, in which LPS was applied to induce inflammatory injury, to further verify the protective effects of Pae against cellular damage. The results showed that Pae protected against LPS-induced cellular injury in an AKT1-dependent manner. Mechanistically, Pae suppresses AKT1 phosphorylation and promotes AKT1 protein degradation. Collectively, through an integrated approach of network pharmacology and experimental validation, we identified that the therapeutic mechanism of Pae against mastitis is mediated by direct targeting of AKT1. Pae can bind to AKT1 and subsequently inhibit AKT1-mediated mitochondrial damage and epithelial apoptosis.

articles.title: Mode of Birth and Bleeding Outcomes in Pregnancies at Risk of Fetal and Neonatal Alloimmune Thrombocytopenia: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.journal: BJOG : an international journal of obstetrics and gynaecology
articles.authors: Pothof R, van den Akker ESA, de Haas M et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To assess the impact of vaginal deliveries on the occurrence of intracranial haemorrhage (ICH) in subsequent pregnancies with Fetal and Neonatal Alloimmune Thrombocytopenia (FNAIT).
DESIGN: Retrospective data collection.
SETTING: Sanquin Diagnostic Services, the national institute for diagnostic FNAIT-testing and Leiden University Medical Center, the national referral centre for FNAIT-management.
POPULATION: 73 subsequent pregnancies with FNAIT; 16 high-risk and 57 standard-risk.
METHODS: All women with a confirmed index pregnancy with alloantibodies against human platelet antigens (HPA) and a subsequent HPA-incompatible pregnancy between March 1992 and February 2026 were included.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Severe bleeding or other bleeding symptoms in neonates, associated with mode of birth.
RESULTS: There were 63 index pregnancies and 73 subsequent pregnancies, of which 72 (99%) received weekly intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG). In the high-risk group (n = 16), there were 10 caesarean sections, of which four neonates had a platelet count below 50 × 109/L. Of the six vaginal deliveries, two neonates had a platelet count below 50 × 109/L. There were no bleeding complications. In the standard-risk group (n = 57), there were 19 caesarean sections of which eight neonates had a platelet count below 50 × 109/L. One ICH was identified antenatally before IVIG initiation, and three neonates developed petechiae or haematomas. Of 38 vaginal deliveries, 13 neonates had a platelet count below 50 × 109/L and one neonate developed petechiae. Overall (standard- or high-risk), no ICH was detected in neonates delivered vaginally (n = 44).
CONCLUSION: No ICH was observed in HPA-alloimmunised women who had a vaginal delivery and antenatally treated with IVIG.

articles.title: Comparative Efficacy and Safety of Modern Treatment Modalities for Genitourinary Syndrome of Menopause: A Systematic Review and Network Meta-Analysis.
articles.journal: BJOG : an international journal of obstetrics and gynaecology
articles.authors: Randombage PJS, Akurugodagama MS
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Genitourinary syndrome of menopause (GSM) is a chronic consequence of hypoestrogenism affecting vaginal, sexual and lower urinary tract health. Treatments include local vaginal oestrogen, intravaginal prasterone, oral ospemifene, hyaluronic acid preparations, moisturisers/lubricants and energy-based interventions, but comparative evidence is heterogeneous.
OBJECTIVES: To compare the relative efficacy and safety of contemporary GSM therapies using a systematic review and class-level network meta-analysis (NMA) of randomised controlled trials.
SEARCH STRATEGY: MEDLINE/PubMed, Scopus, Cochrane CENTRAL, Web of Science, Google Scholar, ClinicalTrials.gov and WHO ICTRP were searched from inception to March 2026, with backward and forward citation searching.
SELECTION CRITERIA: Randomised controlled trials enrolling postmenopausal women with symptomatic GSM or equivalent diagnoses.
DATA COLLECTION AND ANALYSIS: Two reviewers independently screened, extracted and linked reports from the same trial family and assessed RoB 2. The primary outcome was harmonised patient-reported symptom burden, using a prespecified hierarchy of global symptom score, most bothersome symptom, dyspareunia and vaginal dryness. A frequentist random-effects consistency NMA generated; Hedges g standardised mean differences (SMDs), 95% confidence intervals (CIs), prediction intervals and P-scores. Heterogeneity was estimated by REML; node splitting, a design-by-treatment interaction decomposition and sensitivity analyses assessed incoherence and influence. Confidence in all 21 network comparisons was evaluated with CINeMA using a validated percentage contribution matrix.
RESULTS: Twenty-six efficacy publications represented 24 unique trial families and 4958 randomised participants after denominator adjudication. The primary symptom NMA included 15 trial families, seven nodes and 3415 participants. Versus placebo/sham/control, local vaginal oestrogen was the only class with a CI excluding the null (SMD 0.34, 95% CI 0.02-0.66). Estimates were imprecise for prasterone (0.37, -0.10 to 0.84), hyaluronic acid (0.31, -0.10 to 0.72), ospemifene (0.24, -0.38 to 0.87), moisturiser/lubricant (0.15, -0.37 to 0.67) and CO2 laser (0.03, -0.56 to 0.61). Heterogeneity remained material (τ2 = 0.097; I2 = 65.6%). articles.title: Postpartum Perineal Assessment After Vaginal Birth and Detection of Obstetric Anal Sphincter Injury: A Scoping Review.
articles.journal: BJOG : an international journal of obstetrics and gynaecology
articles.authors: Ratto C, Sultan AH, Fernando R et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Obstetric anal sphincter injuries (OASIs) are often under-recognised. International guidelines vary, especially on postpartum reassessment and diagnostic escalation.
SEARCH STRATEGY, DATA COLLECTION AND ANALYSIS: A PRISMA-ScR scoping review mapped international guidance and supporting evidence, with AGREE II appraisal of formal guideline sets.
MAIN RESULTS: We included 14 core guidelines, 3 regional documents and 31 evidence sources. Guidelines addressed immediate postpartum perineal assessment, but recommendations varied considerably regarding digital rectal examination, role and timing of imaging, diagnostic escalation and structured follow-up. Guidance on implementation, including documentation, training and audit/quality improvement, was also inconsistent across documents.
CONCLUSIONS: These key gaps highlight areas for future research and guideline development.

articles.title: Which Urinary Incontinence Subtypes Are More Strongly Linked to Sarcopenia and Other Geriatric Syndromes? A Comparative Study in Community-Dwelling Older Adults.
articles.authors: Yilmaz Kars M, Cicek O, Turgut ZI et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: How urinary incontinence (UI) subtypes relate to other geriatric syndromes remains unclear. We evaluated the prevalence of UI and its subtypes and their associations with sarcopenia, frailty, malnutrition, and functional status in older adults.
METHODS: This retrospective cross-sectional study included 1042 patients aged ≥ 60 years undergoing comprehensive geriatric assessment (CGA) at a tertiary geriatric clinic (May 2023-January 2026). UI status and subtype were obtained from medical records. Sarcopenia was evaluated using SARC-F, handgrip strength (HGS), physical performance tests, and dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (EWGSOP2). Binary and multinomial logistic regression, sex-stratified, and sensitivity analyses were performed.
RESULTS: The median age was 79 years; 66.0% were women. UI was present in 62.4% of patients (61.5% of women and 64.1% of men, p = 0.404), and urge UI was the most common subtype. After adjustment, UI was associated with impaired physical performance, slower gait speed, lower HGS, higher SARC-F and Clinical Frailty Scale scores, and lower Mini Nutritional Assessment-Short Form and instrumental activities of daily living scores. Urge, mixed and functional UI were each associated with most of these parameters, whereas stress UI was not associated with any. Mixed UI was the only subtype associated with confirmed sarcopenia (OR 2.259, 95% CI 1.029-4.956). Most associations were observed in both sexes, although the association with gait speed was stronger in women.
CONCLUSION: UI is highly prevalent among older adults undergoing CGA and is associated with frailty, sarcopenia-related parameters, malnutrition risk, and functional decline in both sexes, with subtype-specific differences.

articles.title: Epidural in Labour and Obstetric Anal Sphincter Injury Risk: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.journal: BJOG : an international journal of obstetrics and gynaecology
articles.authors: Idzes D, Atkinson J, Gordon H et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Perineal injury during childbirth is common. The most severe injuries involve damage to the anal sphincter (obstetric anal sphincter injuries). Epidural analgesia provides effective labour pain relief but its impact on the risk of obstetric anal sphincter injury is unclear.
OBJECTIVE: To determine the association between epidural analgesia and the likelihood of obstetric anal sphincter injuries.
SEARCH STRATEGY: Ovid MEDLINE, Ovid EMBASE, PubMed, CINAHL and Web of Science were searched from database inception to October 18, 2025, using key words relating to epidural, perineal trauma and labour.
SELECTION CRITERIA: Randomised trials and observational studies (cohort, case-control, and cross-sectional studies) were included.
DATA COLLECTION AND ANALYSIS: Studies reporting the same outcomes were pooled, and odds ratios with 95% confidence intervals were calculated using a random effects meta-analysis.
MAIN RESULTS: From 24 977 identified studies, 86 were included (N = 9 826 330 women). Pooled adjusted analyses showed epidural use in labour was associated with a 15% reduced likelihood of obstetric anal sphincter injury in the overall population (n = 9 302 188; aOR 0.85 [95% CI 0.80-0.91]). Among nulliparous women, there was a 23% reduced likelihood of obstetric anal sphincter injury (n = 1 083 923; aOR 0.77 [95% CI 0.71-0.83]).
CONCLUSION: After pooling effect measures that corrected for important clinical confounders, our meta-analysis suggests that epidural use in labour may reduce the likelihood of obstetric anal sphincter injuries among nulliparous women. While our findings must be interpreted within the limitations of observational data, they provide valuable evidence to guide clinical practice and highlight the need for more high-quality studies to establish causality.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: PROSPERO Registration CRD42023412771, 09 April 2023 https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD42023412771.

articles.title: Lifetime Oestrogen Exposure Indices in Relation to Biological Aging and Future Life Expectancy: A Prospective Study of Two Cohorts.
articles.journal: BJOG : an international journal of obstetrics and gynaecology
articles.authors: Xiang Y, Wu G, Zhang N et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the associations of lifetime oestrogen exposure indices with biological aging, mortality and life expectancy.
DESIGN: Population-based cohort study.
SETTING: UK Biobank and the US National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES).
POPULATION OR SAMPLE: 112 381 postmenopausal women, including 107 218 from UK Biobank and 5163 from US NHANES.
METHODS: Lifetime oestrogen exposure was assessed using three reproductive-history-based indices: reproductive lifespan (RLS), endogenous oestrogen exposure (EEE), and total oestrogen exposure (TEE). Biological aging was measured by phenotypic age (PA). Multivariable linear regression examined associations with PA acceleration, Cox models assessed mortality, and flexible parametric survival models estimated life expectancy, with covariate adjustment.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: PA acceleration, all-cause and cause-specific mortality, and estimated life expectancy.
RESULTS: In the UK Biobank, higher RLS, EEE, and TEE were inversely related to PA acceleration, with estimates generally strongest for RLS and TEE (e.g., highest quartile RLS: β = -0.31, 95% CI: -0.40 to -0.22). In the US NHANES, inverse associations were clearest for TEE. Higher RLS and TEE were generally associated with lower risks of all-cause, cardiovascular, and respiratory mortality across both cohorts. The highest quartile of TEE was associated with increase in life expectancy of 0.64 years (95% CI: 0.30 to 0.97) in the UK Biobank and 1.35 years (95% CI: 0.20 to 2.50) in the US NHANES at age 45. In UK Biobank, RLS and EEE were associated with higher endometrial cancer incidence, and all three indices with higher breast cancer incidence.
CONCLUSIONS: Higher lifetime oestrogen exposure indices, particularly TEE, were generally associated with delayed biological aging and longer estimated life expectancy.

articles.title: Risk factors for positive depression screening at 6 weeks postpartum: a single center retrospective cohort study (2014-2023).
articles.authors: Jethwa AJ, Guo N, Harrison N et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: As universal postpartum depression screening is implemented, contemporary risk factors for positive screens in the United States population remain understudied. Our aim was to evaluate demographic, obstetric, neonatal, anesthetic and psychiatric factors associated with positive depression screening scores at 6 weeks postpartum.
METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted at an academic center in the United States (2014-2023). Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale scores recorded at 6 weeks postpartum were analyzed (positive screen score ≥ 10). We included adults (≥18 years) delivering a live or nonviable fetus from gestational age ≥ 20 weeks by any mode who completed screening at 6 weeks post-delivery; we excluded patients with an incomplete or missing score. The primary outcome was factors independently associated with a positive depression screen at 6 weeks postpartum. Secondary outcomes were to characterize depression scores and explore differences in inpatient pain outcomes based on positive or negative depression screening at 6 weeks postpartum.
RESULTS: Of 8155 deliveries analyzed, 13.6% (n = 1107) screened positive on the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale. Factors independently associated with higher odds of a positive screen included Hispanic ethnicity, single marital status, delivery of neonate with very low birth weight, worst postpartum pain score up to 48 h following delivery, and psychiatric diagnosis. Positive and negative screen median scores were 12 [IQR 11-16] {Range 10-27} and 3 [IQR 1-5] {Range 0-9}, respectively. The positive depression screening group experienced worse inpatient pain.
CONCLUSION: Future studies should explore inpatient pain as a potential predictor of positive 6-week depression screening.

articles.title: Identification of ovarian cancer cell based on mechanical properties of regional heterogeneity of cells.
articles.authors: Liu C, Tian L, Yang F et al.
articles.abstract: Cellular mechanical properties are emerging as promising biomarkers for tumor diagnosis and for elucidating cancer-related mechanisms. However, most studies treat cells as mechanically homogeneous entities, overlooking regional heterogeneity and its implications for classification. Atomic force microscopy was used to characterize the mechanical properties of hepatocytes, mammary cells, ovarian cystadenoma cells, and SKOV3 ovarian cancer cells. Fluorescent staining was used to analyze the correlation between cytoskeletal topology parameters and mechanical properties. Logistic regression and support vector machine (SVM) classifiers were used to compare the performance of whole-cell, region-specific, and cross-regional models. Mechanical properties distinguished cells representing normal, benign, and malignant phenotypes. For ovarian cells, a model integrating multiple mechanical features achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.95. Region-specific models yielded AUCs of approximately 0.85, demonstrating pronounced spatial heterogeneity in cancer-cell mechanics and region-dependent remodeling of cytoskeletal branching architecture. In cross-cell-type analysis, an SVM trained on 7702/HepG2 achieved an AUC greater than 0.90 when applied to ovarian cells, indicating substantial generalizability of mechanical features across cell types. These results support the cross-cell type generalization of mechanical properties and suggest the potential feasibility of establishing a mechanical fingerprint reference across cell types. Furthermore, the difference between perinuclear and cytoplasmic regions reveals the complexity of mechanical regulation in ovarian cancer cells and provides a new perspective for understanding cellular dynamics.

articles.title: Early third-trimester maternal cardiac function and morphometry in high-risk pregnancies that subsequently developed fetal growth restriction and/or pre-eclampsia.
articles.journal: Ultrasound in obstetrics & gynecology : the official journal of the International Society of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology
articles.authors: Martinez-Egea J, Daza M, Pumarola C et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate maternal cardiovascular function and cardiac morphology in early third-trimester pregnancies at high risk for fetal growth restriction (FGR) and compare findings between pregnancies that subsequently developed FGR and/or pre-eclampsia (PE) and uncomplicated pregnancies.
METHODS: This prospective cohort study included singleton pregnancies at high risk for FGR referred to the Maternal-Fetal Medicine Department at the Hospital Clinic of Barcelona, Barcelona, Spain, between August 2022 and August 2024, for a routine second-trimester fetal anomaly scan. The patients were assessed between 27 + 0 and 28 + 6 weeks' gestation and were only included in the analysis if they did not have a diagnosis of FGR or PE at the time of evaluation; those who subsequently developed FGR and/or PE were identified during follow-up. Maternal echocardiography was performed to assess cardiac output (CO), stroke volume (SV), systemic vascular resistance (SVR) and structural parameters including left ventricular (LV) wall thickness and chamber volumes. Results were compared between pregnancies that subsequently developed FGR (with or without PE), pregnancies that subsequently developed isolated PE and uncomplicated pregnancies. Multivariable analysis was performed using quantile regression of the medians for CO and SVR, adjusted for body mass index (BMI), with FGR and PE assessed independently.
RESULTS: A total of 948 patients were included in the final analysis, of whom 129 developed FGR and/or PE (including 59 that developed FGR (with or without PE) and 70 that developed isolated PE) and 819 had uncomplicated pregnancies. Median mean arterial pressure (MAP) was higher in the FGR (with or without PE) group (82.0 mmHg) and the isolated-PE group (84.8 mmHg) than in the uncomplicated group (79.7 mmHg; P = 0.027 and P < 0.001, respectively), with the isolated-PE group showing the highest MAP values (isolated PE vs FGR (with or without PE), P = 0.047). Median heart rate was elevated in the isolated-PE group (82.5 bpm) compared with the FGR (with or without PE) group (77.0 bpm; P = 0.03). In the multivariable analysis, FGR and PE were associated independently with lower CO and higher SVR prior to their development. Median SV was reduced in the FGR (with or without PE) group (59.7 mL) and the isolated-PE group (61.1 mL) compared with the uncomplicated group (64.2 mL; P = 0.030 and P = 0.016, respectively). articles.title: Association of heavy metal with sperm parameters and sex hormones: A systematic review and meta-analysis of observational studies.
articles.journal: European journal of obstetrics & gynecology and reproductive biology: X
articles.ta: Eur J Obstet Gynecol Reprod Biol X
articles.authors: Goodarzi S, Shafiee A, Rashidian P et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Findings regarding the reproductive toxicity effect of heavy metals on sperm parameters and sex hormones level remain inconsistent. This study systematically reviewed and pooled the existing literature to assess the associations of heavy metal levels with sperm parameters and sex hormones.
METHODS: In this systematic review, international databases including PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched until 31 March 2025 according to PRISMA guidelines. Observational studies assessing heavy metal concentrations in biological samples and their associations with sperm parameters or sex hormone levels were included. The chi-square-based Q test and I-squared statistics were used to assess the heterogeneity, and pooled estimates were obtained using a random-effects meta-analysis model.
RESULTS: Eighteen studies involving 4041 participants were included. Qualitative synthesis revealed heterogeneous findings across heavy metals and sperm parameters, with significant findings reported mainly for Cd and Pb, while most associations with reproductive hormones were non-significant. Meta-analysis demonstrated a significant inverse association between seminal Cd and sperm motility (pooled Fisher's z = -0.17, 95% CI: -0.30 to -0.04; I² = 0%), whereas no significant pooled associations were observed for seminal Pb.
CONCLUSIONS: The current evidence does not demonstrate consistent associations between heavy metal exposure and male reproductive parameters; however, limited significant inverse correlations were identified between seminal Cd and sperm motility. Evidence regarding reproductive hormones was limited and largely inconclusive, highlighting the need for larger, well-designed prospective studies.

articles.title: Association Between the HbA1c-To-HDL-C Ratio and Female Infertility Among Reproductive-Aged Women: Evidence from NHANES.
articles.authors: Wang X, Luo S, Cheng H
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Metabolic abnormalities have been increasingly implicated in female reproductive dysfunction. The HbA1c-to-HDL-C ratio may reflect the combined burden of chronic glycemic exposure and lipid-related metabolic status; however, its relationship with female infertility remains insufficiently understood. This study investigated the association between the logarithmically transformed HbA1c-to-HDL-C ratio [Log (HbA1c/HDL-C)] and infertility among reproductive-aged women.
METHODS: This cross-sectional study included women aged 18-45 years from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) conducted between 2013 and 2018. After applying the exclusion criteria, 2452 participants were included, comprising 329 women with infertility and 2123 without infertility. Log (HbA1c/HDL-C) was analyzed as both a continuous variable and quartiles. Weighted multivariable logistic regression models were used to estimate the association between Log (HbA1c/HDL-C) and infertility. Restricted cubic spline analysis was performed to evaluate the dose-response pattern, and subgroup analyses were conducted to assess potential heterogeneity across population characteristics.
RESULTS: Compared with women without infertility, those with infertility were older and had higher BMI, HbA1c, and Log (HbA1c/HDL-C) levels. In the primary multivariable model, higher Log (HbA1c/HDL-C) was associated with greater odds of infertility (OR = 1.93, 95% CI: 1.03-3.60). Women in the highest quartile had higher odds of infertility than those in the lowest quartile (OR = 1.90, 95% CI: 1.13-3.22), with a significant trend across quartiles. The association was more apparent among women younger than 35 years. After additional adjustment for BMI, the association was attenuated (OR = 1.64, 95% CI: 0.85-3.16).
CONCLUSION: Higher Log (HbA1c/HDL-C) was associated with greater odds of self-reported female infertility in models without BMI, but the association was attenuated after BMI adjustment. These findings suggest that adiposity may partly account for the observed relationship and require confirmation in prospective studies.

articles.title: Oocyte Maturation and Fertilization-Related Outcomes Following a Pro-Fertility Diet Combined with Omega-3 Supplementation in Women Undergoing Assisted Reproductive Technology: A Secondary Analysis of a Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.authors: Ghadimi-Yari M, Ghasemi-Tehrani H, Feizi A et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Oocyte developmental competence is a key determinant of IVF success, but randomized evidence on multi-component dietary interventions is limited. This paper reports prespecified secondary outcomes of a registered randomized trial (IRCT20130903014551N13) that examined whether a Pro-Fertility Diet (PFD) combined with omega-3 supplementation affects oocyte-related outcomes in women undergoing IVF/ICSI.
METHODS: In this randomized, parallel-group, single-blind (outcome assessors) trial at Hazrat Maryam Fertility Center (Isfahan, Iran), 180 infertile women aged 18-42 years were allocated (stratified block randomization by age and BMI) to a PFD plus omega-3 supplementation or to standard dietary advice for 8 weeks before IVF/ICSI. Embryo-related outcomes and fertilization rate from this trial have been published previously. The outcomes reported here for the first time are antral follicle count (AFC), cumulus-oocyte complexes (COCs), metaphase II (MII) oocytes and two-pronuclear (2PN) zygotes, analyzed in 167 women with available outcome data (complete-case analysis; 84 intervention, 83 control). Count outcomes were analyzed using Poisson regression with robust standard errors and fertilization rate (2PN per MII oocyte) using binomial regression, both adjusted for age and BMI.
RESULTS: Of the 180 randomized participants, 167 women (84 in the intervention group and 83 in the control group) were included in the complete-case analysis of oocyte counts. Compared with controls, the intervention group had higher MII oocyte counts (adjusted IRR = 1.16, 95% CI: 1.01-1.33; P = 0.035) and 2PN zygote counts (IRR = 1.38, 95% CI: 1.17-1.61; P < 0.001), as well as higher odds of fertilization (OR = 1.92, 95% CI: 1.41-2.63; P < 0.001). No statistically significant differences were observed for AFC or COC counts. After adjustment for multiple comparisons using the Holm and Benjamini-Hochberg procedures, the difference in 2PN zygote counts remained statistically significant (adjusted P < 0.001 with both methods), whereas the difference in MII oocyte counts did not (Holm-adjusted P = 0.104; BH-adjusted P = 0.069).
CONCLUSIONS: In this exploratory secondary analysis, the combined nutritional intervention was associated with a higher 2PN zygote count, which remained statistically significant after correction for multiple comparisons. Although a higher MII oocyte count was observed in the initial adjusted analysis, this finding did not remain statistically significant…

articles.title: Best Practice and Management of Sexual Dysfunction Following Diagnosis and Treatment of Gynecological Cancer.
articles.authors: Sha S, DiSilvestro J, Burnett C et al.
articles.abstract: Sexual dysfunction, defined as a clinically significant and persistent disturbance in sexual desire, arousal, orgasm, or pain during sexual activity, affects up to 90% of gynecologic cancer survivors. Sexual health is a well-established component of quality of life, and its assessment should be routinely integrated into survivorship care. Treatment with surgery, chemotherapy, and/or radiation can result in early menopause, disruption of pelvic vasculature and nerve innovation, and alteration of pelvic anatomy that profoundly impacts sexual health. These physical consequences from treatment can compound the psychological burden that accompanies a cancer diagnosis. Here we review the evidence and provide recommendations for the evaluation and management of sexual dysfunction following the diagnosis and treatment of gynecologic cancer. We will discuss the mechanisms by which cancer-directed therapies affect sexual health, multimodal symptom-based treatment approaches, and lastly highlights awareness for continued areas of advocacy with the goal of providing all patients with comprehensive survivorship care.

articles.title: Diagnostic Pitfall: Mixed Connective Tissue Disease-Associated Pulmonary Hypertension Presenting With Postpartum Right-Sided Heart Failure in a 21-Year-Old-Case Report.
articles.authors: Alla SSM, Khetan MS, Alla D et al.
articles.abstract: Mixed connective tissue disease is a multisystem autoimmune condition characterized by overlapping clinical and serological features related to anti-U1-RNP antibodies of at least two connective tissue diseases. It may present with myocarditis, pericarditis, pulmonary arterial hypertension, and, less commonly, heart failure. We present a 21-year-old female with bilateral foot swelling, cough, and shortness of breath 3 months after a vaginal delivery. On examination, she was hypotensive (90/70 mmHg), with an elevated jugular venous pressure, a pulmonary systolic murmur with loud P2, and a tricuspid regurgitation murmur. Bronchial breath sounds and fine crepitations were present in both lower lung fields. She was evaluated initially for suspected postpartum cardiomyopathy. Transthoracic echocardiography was suggestive of a probable moderate to severe PAH. High-resolution computed tomography showed bilateral moderate pleural effusions, honeycombing with partial atelectasis of the underlying lung, and cardiomegaly. Computed Tomography Pulmonary Angiography (CTPA) showed findings likely consistent with probable mild pulmonary hypertension. An antinuclear antibody panel was performed and was positive for anti-U1-RNP, SS-A, SS-B, and Jo-1 antibodies. She was started on Lasix 40 mg, Aldactone 25 mg, lisinopril 10 mg, and heparin. Treatment with 20 mg of prednisolone was started and gradually tapered. Her anasarca and dyspnea improved, and she was discharged with follow-up arranged with cardiology and rheumatology. Timely identification of MCTD-associated pulmonary hypertension and its cardiovascular complications is essential and allows early commencement of treatment, which further prevents the patients from developing heart failure.

articles.title: Pregnancy-Induced Hypertension Complicated by Posterior Reversible Encephalopathy Syndrome: A Case Series of Two Patients.
articles.authors: Zhao X, Yan M, Long F et al.
articles.abstract: Posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome (PRES) is a rare but potentially life-threatening neurological complication associated with hypertensive disorders of pregnancy. This report presents two cases of pregnancy-induced hypertension complicated by PRES, both clinically characterized by headache and visual disturbances, with characteristic neuroimaging findings. The clinical manifestations, laboratory findings, and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) characteristics of two patients are described. Following prompt multidisciplinary consultation and immediate interventions, including strict blood pressure control, seizure prophylaxis, infection prevention, and appropriate obstetric management, both patients achieved favorable clinical outcomes. No significant neurological abnormalities were observed at the 42-day postpartum follow-up. In patients with severe pregnancy-induced hypertension, PRES warrants recognition as a potential complication; management should prioritize rigorous blood pressure control, seizure prophylaxis, alleviation of pregnancy-related physiological stress, and timely neuroimaging to guide treatment, with strategies balancing maternal and fetal safety-early recognition and intervention underpinned by standardized protocols and multidisciplinary collaboration being critical to improving prognosis and reducing complications.

articles.title: Knowledge, attitude, and practice regarding menopause management among primary healthcare providers in Kelantan, Malaysia: A cross-sectional study.
articles.journal: Malaysian family physician : the official journal of the Academy of Family Physicians of Malaysia
articles.authors: Che Ibrahim NH, Ng YY, Muhammad J et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Menopause marks the end of a woman's reproductive years. Primary healthcare providers (PCPs) play a pivotal role in identifying menopausal symptoms, providing counselling and initiating management. However, information on their knowledge, attitudes and clinical practices in Malaysia remains limited. This study aimed to assess the knowledge, attitudes and practices regarding menopause management among PCPs in Kelantan.
METHODS: A cross-sectional study was conducted among PCPs in Kelantan health clinics using a self-administered questionnaire adapted from the Malaysian Clinical Practice Guidelines (CPGs) on Menopause Management. Simple and multiple linear regression analyses were used to identify factors associated with knowledge scores.
RESULTS: A total of 212 PCPs participated. The mean knowledge score was 19.45 (standard deviation [SD]=4.90) out of 30 (64.8%), while the mean attitude score was 38.97 (SD=3.83) out of 50 (72.4%). Among the participants, 42.0% often or always advised lifestyle modifications, whereas 52.8% had never prescribed menopausal hormone therapy (MHT) or referred women with menopausal symptoms for MHT. Higher knowledge scores were associated with older age (adjusted β=0.21; 95% confidence interval [CI]=0.08-0.34; P=0.002), family medicine specialist (FMS) designation (adjusted β=3.06; 95% CI=0.26-5.81; P=0.032) and use of CPGs as an information source (adjusted β=1.91; 95% CI=0.30-3.52; P=0.021).
CONCLUSION: The PCPs demonstrated moderate knowledge of several menopause-related concepts and favourable attitudes. Higher knowledge scores were associated with older age, FMS designation and CPG use. Targeted education and guideline support may strengthen menopause management in primary care.

articles.title: Financial navigation in gynecologic oncology: a qualitative study.
articles.authors: Smith AJB, Mora DC, O'Brien C et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Gynecologic oncology patients experience financial toxicity. Financial navigation, a program where individuals meet with a trained financial counselor to discuss estimated out-of-pocket costs, connect to assistance programs, and develop payment plans, may help reduce financial toxicity. Our objective was to examine the experiences of gynecologic oncology patients who received financial navigation services through qualitative data collection from patients and financial navigators.
METHODS: Since May 2022, we have offered financial navigation to patients seen in gynecologic oncology practices at a large academic health system. Financial navigators completed questionnaires to characterize services provided to patients, and we reported descriptive statistics of those served. We then recruited patients who participated for semi-structured interviews. Two team members used a thematic approach to code and identify themes.
RESULTS: In the first year, 31 patients were referred for financial navigation, and 28 received services. After review of insurance benefits by financial navigators, half had no estimated out-of-pocket costs for cancer care. Of patients with non-zero out-of-pocket, 42% of patients were referred for co-pay assistance of whom 40% ultimately received financial assistance grants. Patients reported transportation, rent, and food as major concerns, alongside medical costs. Patients appreciated the financial navigators' compassion and assistance navigating bureaucracy. Patients identified delayed insurance billing, high treatment-related out-of-pocket, external grants not meeting needs, and treatment-related fatigue as contributing to financial distress.
CONCLUSION: Financial navigation was positively perceived by patients. Half of patients referred had low to no out-of-pocket costs after meeting with financial navigators, although patients identified significant non-medical financial stresses. Receipt of financial assistance was low among patients with high out-of-pocket, and patients identified gaps in coverage. Financial navigation addressed patients' medical costs, yet further work is needed to help patients survive broader financial toxicity of cancer treatment.

articles.title: High Cholesterol Facilitates Ovarian Androgen Production and Contributes to the Development of Polycystic Ovary Syndrome.
articles.authors: Liu Y, Hu S, Liang X et al.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Cholesterol serves as an essential substrate for ovarian steroidogenesis, and its elevated levels are linked to female reproductive endocrine diseases, particularly polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS). However, the causal role and mechanistic basis of cholesterol overload in female reproductive dysfunction remain poorly defined. In this study, we analyzed a clinical cohort of 1615 women of reproductive age and found a significant positive correlation between circulating total cholesterol and testosterone levels. To establish causality, we developed a female mouse model of hypercholesterolemia through long-term feeding with a high-cholesterol diet (HCD). Beyond hyperlipidemia and ectopic lipid deposition, these mice exhibited multiple reproductive abnormalities, including disrupted estrous cycles, elevated circulating testosterone and luteinizing hormone levels, as well as polycystic ovarian morphology, collectively reflecting key clinical characteristics of PCOS. Ovarian transcriptomic analysis in HCD-fed mice revealed aberrant activation of steroidogenesis. We further identified the transcription factor FoxO1 as a candidate regulator modulating both cholesterol- and dehydroepiandrosterone-induced ovarian steroidogenic reprogramming. Importantly, these transcriptomic changes were confirmed in granulosa cells from women with PCOS. Collectively, our findings provide direct in vivo evidence that high cholesterol contributes to PCOS pathogenesis by promoting excessive testosterone production, underscoring the necessity for lipid metabolism management to protect women's reproductive health.
GRAPHICAL ABSTRACT: Abbreviations: CL, corpus luteum; T, testosterone; LH, luteinizing hormone; FSH, follicle-stimulating hormone; PCOS, polycystic ovary syndrome.
SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1007/s43657-026-00328-y.

articles.title: Efficacy, safety and mechanism of Jinfeng pill in the treatment of perimenopausal syndrome: A protocol for a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter trial.
articles.authors: Wu X, Zhou L, Hu J et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Perimenopausal syndrome (PMPS) refers to a series of physiological and psychological symptoms caused by the fluctuation or decline of sex hormone levels during the pre- and postmenopausal periods. With the acceleration of aging society, more and more women suffer from symptoms of PMPS. Jinfeng Pill (JFP) is a classic Chinese patent medicine for gynecological diseases, but it lacks rigorous clinical evidence for the treatment of PMPS.
METHODS/DESIGN: This randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter trial will be conducted across three hospitals in China. A total of 100 perimenopausal women will be randomly allocated in a 1:1 ratio to receive JFP or placebo for 12 weeks, followed by a 4-week post-treatment follow-up. The primary outcome is the modified Kupperman Index (KI), assessed at baseline and at weeks 4, 8, 12, and 16. Secondary outcomes include the Hot Flash scale (HFs), the Menopause-Specific Quality of Life (MENQOL) questionnaire, the Hamilton Depression Rating Scale (HAMD), the Hamilton Anxiety Rating Scale (HAMA), the Vaginal Health Index Score (VHIS), and Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) symptom score. Mechanistic outcomes encompass serum sex hormones and estrogen metabolites, inflammatory cytokines interleukin-6 (IL-6), tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α), gut microbiota composition (16S rRNA sequencing), faecal β-glucuronidase (β-GUS) activity, and short-chain fatty acid (SCFA) concentrations.
CONCLUSION: This is the first multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial to investigate the molecular mechanism by which JFP ameliorate PMPS by reshaping the gut microbiota structure, modulating β-GUS activity, optimizing SCFAs metabolism, suppressing inflammatory responses, and maintaining estrogen homeostasis. The results of this trial will help us to evaluate the efficacy, safety and possible mechanism of JFP in treating PMPS.
ETHICS AND DISSEMINATION: The protocol (Version 3.0, dated November 19, 2025) was approved by the Ethics Committee of Tongji Hospital, Tongji Medical College, Huazhong University of Science and Technology (approval number: TJ-IRB202512083). Written informed consent will be obtained from all participants prior to enrolment. Findings will be disseminated through peer-reviewed publications and academic conference presentations.
TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: NCT07606755 (https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07606755).

articles.title: Association between knee osteoarthritis and reproductive factors in Indian females: A case-control study.
articles.journal: Journal of clinical orthopaedics and trauma
articles.authors: Das L, Sharma PK, Singh G et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Knee osteoarthritis (KOA) disproportionately affects women, particularly following the onset of menopause. While the chondroprotective role of estrogen is recognised, the influence of diverse reproductive milestones on KOA risk in Indian women is poorly understood. This study investigated the association between various reproductive events in females and the prevalence of KOA.
METHODS: A case-control study included 1000 females aged ≥ 40 years, 500 cases with radiologically confirmed KOA [Kellgren-Lawrence (K-L) Grade ≥ 2], and 500 asymptomatic controls matched for age and body mass index (BMI). Comprehensive reproductive and obstetric histories and health-related quality-of-life (SF-12) data were collected through structured interviews. Multivariable logistic regression was performed to estimate adjusted associations with KOA.
RESULTS: Women with KOA experienced menopause at a significantly earlier age than controls. After adjustment, postmenopausal status showed the strongest association with KOA (aOR 6.27, 95% CI 4.06-9.67; p < 0.001). Earlier age at menopause (aOR 1.03 per 1-year decrease, 95% CI 1.00-1.07; p = 0.039), earlier age at natural menopause (aOR 1.09 per 1-year decrease, 95% CI 1.04-1.14; p < 0.001), surgical menopause (aOR 1.53, 95% CI 1.10-2.12; p = 0.012), hysterectomy (aOR 1.63, 95% CI 1.19-2.24; p = 0.002), polymenorrhea (aOR 2.81, 95% CI 1.45-5.47; p = 0.002), fibroid uterus (aOR 1.45, 95% CI 1.02-2.06; p = 0.039), steroid use (aOR 1.65, 95% CI 1.22-2.23; p = 0.001), and hypertension (aOR 1.63, 95% CI 1.18-2.25; p = 0.003) remained independently associated with KOA. KOA was associated with significantly lower physical and mental quality-of-life scores (p < 0.05).
CONCLUSION: Reproductive factors, particularly menopausal status, earlier menopause, surgical menopause, hysterectomy, and adverse reproductive events, were independently associated with higher odds of KOA. These findings demonstrate that female reproductive events are associated with knee joint degeneration, highlighting the potential role of musculoskeletal screening in women with premature or surgically induced menopause.
LEVEL OF STUDY: Level III.

articles.title: Serum CCL23 as a Potential Biomarker for Asthma in Pregnancy: A Prospective Case-Control Study.
articles.authors: Xie J, Yan X, Song Y et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Early identification of asthma in pregnancy is challenging due to limited feasibility of pulmonary function testing. We aimed to characterize serum CCL23 expression in pregnant women with asthma and to assess its potential as an auxiliary clinical marker.
METHODS: Transcriptomic sequencing first identified differentially expressed genes (DEGs) in peripheral blood between pregnant women with asthma and healthy pregnant controls. A validation cohort of 37 pregnant women with asthma and 36 healthy pregnant controls was then enrolled. Clinical data (EOS, pregnancy outcomes) were collected, and serum CCL23, IL-4, and IL-5 levels were measured. The expression characteristics and potential adjunctive identification value of CCL23 were evaluated using the Mann-Whitney U-test, Spearman correlation analysis, and binary logistic regression.
RESULTS: Transcriptomic sequencing revealed CCL23 upregulation in asthma (P < 0.01). ELISA showed higher serum CCL23 in pregnant women with asthma than in healthy pregnant controls (adjusted means 775.0 ± 91.42 vs 512.92 ± 92.95 pg/mL; adjusted P = 0.07). CCL23 correlated positively with EOS (ρ=0.74, P<0.01) and FeNO (ρ=0.35, P = 0.03) in the asthma group. Elevated CCL23 was independently associated with an increased risk of asthma in pregnancy (overall P < 0.01). ROC analysis showed an AUC of 0.74 (95% CI 0.63-0.86) for CCL23, 0.88 (0.80-0.95) for EOS, 0.87 (0.79-0.95) for CCL23 + EOS; combined model sensitivity 94.60% and specificity 66.70% at optimal cut-off. The combination did not improve discrimination over EOS alone (DeLong P = 0.13).
CONCLUSION: Serum CCL23 is elevated in pregnant women with asthma and positively correlates with peripheral blood EOS and FeNO, implicating a role in systemic type 2 inflammation. CCL23 was independently associated with asthma after adjustment for gestational age and maternal age, but adding it to EOS did not improve discrimination over EOS alone. These exploratory findings require validation in large-scale, multicenter cohorts before any clinical use.

articles.title: Gestational Diabetes Mellitus and Birth Weight: A Bidirectional Mendelian Randomization and Cohort Study in China.
articles.journal: Diabetes, metabolic syndrome and obesity : targets and therapy
articles.authors: Li X, Peng Y, Wang Y et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) is regarded as a driver of fetal macrosomia, yet observational estimates of its effect on birth weight (BW) are vulnerable to confounding. Whether GDM causally shapes fetal growth, and through which shared biology, remains unresolved.
METHODS: We performed a bidirectional two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) using FinnGen R11 GDM (16,802 cases) and the EGG Consortium birth-weight GWAS (n=286,868), with inverse-variance weighted (IVW, primary), MR-Egger, weighted median, weighted mode, RAPS estimators, MR-PRESSO and Bayesian colocalization. Multi-omics evidence (GSE92772, ST001948, INTERVAL cis-pQTLs) was integrated as hypothesis-generating evidence. In a cohort of 24,448 singleton pregnancies, linear and logistic regression, bootstrap mediation, and double/debiased machine learning (DML) were performed for verification.
RESULTS: The primary IVW estimate for GDM to BW was null (β=-0.004, P=0.889) under extreme heterogeneity, and robust estimators showed nominally positive signals. Seven of 21 instruments flagged as outliers overlapping six colocalizing loci. Therefore, it is impossible to precluding a reliable causal interpretation. Reverse MR (BW to GDM) was exploratory (five instruments, all outliers). Colocalization identified six loci (CCND2, MTNR1B, GPSM1, ADCY5, CDKAL1, TCF7L2) with evidence of a shared causal variant (PP.H4≥0.5). All established islet beta-cell/insulin-secretion genes suggested shared upstream biology. In the cohort, GDM was associated with higher rates of macrosomia (OR 1.21) and lower birth weight (LBW, OR 1.45). The association of macrosomia was largely attenuated after adjustment for maternal BMI and lipids (OR 1.01, P=0.913). Using bidirectional mediation analysis, five candidate mediators (BMI, TG, HDL-C, LDL-C, and TG/HDL-C ratio) were identified as significant mediators in both directions. Moreover, hypertensive disorders showed the largest associations with LBW (PE β=-0.204; GH β=-0.067) in DML analyses.
CONCLUSIONS: Evidence for a consistent causal effect of GDM on birth weight remains inconclusive. The observational association of macrosomia was largely explained by maternal metabolic status. The shared insulin-secretory biology more plausibly reflects genetic pleiotropy than a direct causal pathway. Hypertensive disorders showed stronger associations with birth weight reduction than GDM, supporting integrated management of glycemia, BMI, lipids and blood pressure.

articles.title: Integrative transcriptomic analysis and preclinical validation identify lansoprazole as a therapeutic candidate for preeclampsia.
articles.authors: Appierdo R, Pham G, Yin O et al.
articles.abstract: Preeclampsia is a pregnancy disorder with often severe consequences across the maternal-fetal dyad and limited treatment options. We performed an integrated meta-analysis of six placental transcriptomic datasets to identify a preeclampsia-specific gene expression signature, revealing dysregulated pathways related to hypoxia, immune dysfunction, and metabolism. Multivariate INTegrative (MINT) analysis was used to establish a smaller predictive signature with potential utility for identifying circulating biomarkers for earlier preeclampsia diagnosis and monitoring disease progression. This preeclampsia signature queried against a transcriptomic database of more than 1,000 compounds identified lansoprazole, a widely used proton pump inhibitor with an established safety profile, as the top-ranked compound based on its ability to reverse the preeclampsia-associated gene expression signature. Protective benefits of lansoprazole were confirmed using a murine model of immune-mediated fetal wastage where treatment overturned elevated soluble FLT1 levels with significantly improved pregnancy outcomes. These findings support further investigation of lansoprazole as a potential therapy for preeclampsia.

articles.title: METTL3-dependent m6A modification of SLC2A1 mRNA regulates trophoblast migration and invasion associated with preeclampsia under hypoxic conditions.
articles.authors: Wang C, Zhang Y, Mei H et al.
articles.abstract: Preeclampsia (PE) is a serious pregnancy complication closely linked to trophoblast dysfunction. Recent studies highlight the importance of N⁶-methyladenosine (m⁶A) modification in placental development; however, its role in PE-associated trophoblast dysfunction remains poorly understood. This study aimed to elucidate the regulatory role of METTL3 in trophoblast cell function under hypoxia, a key pathological feature associated with preeclampsia, with a focus on its downstream target SLC2A1. A hypoxic model was established using HTR-8/SVneo trophoblast cells. METTL3 expression was evaluated using RT-qPCR and western blotting. METTL3 expression was modulated through siRNA-mediated knockdown and plasmid-based overexpression. Cell proliferation, apoptosis, migration, and invasion were evaluated using EdU, flow cytometry, and Transwell assays. With SLC2A1 as our pre-selected candidate, ENCORI and SRAMP databases were used to investigate METTL3 as a potential upstream m⁶A regulator of SLC2A1. The regulatory impact of METTL3 on SLC2A1 m⁶A methylation and mRNA stability was assessed through MeRIP-qPCR and actinomycin D assays. To confirm the functional relationship between METTL3 and SLC2A1, combined knockdown of METTL3 and SLC2A1 was performed. Hypoxic stimulation significantly upregulated METTL3 expression in HTR-8/SVneo cells. METTL3 silencing markedly enhanced trophoblast cell proliferation, migration, and invasion, while reducing apoptosis, whereas METTL3 overexpression produced the opposite effects. Mechanistically, METTL3 promoted m6A modification of SLC2A1 mRNA and accelerated its degradation, thereby suppressing SLC2A1 expression. Moreover, co-silencing SLC2A1 significantly attenuated the pro-proliferative and pro-migratory effects induced by METTL3 knockdown, suggesting that SLC2A1 functions as a critical downstream effector in METTL3-mediated regulation of trophoblast cell function. METTL3 is aberrantly upregulated under hypoxic conditions and suppresses the mRNA stability and expression of SLC2A1 through m⁶A modification, thereby inhibiting the proliferative and invasive capacities of trophoblast cells.

articles.title: Long-term oncologic outcomes of pulmonary metastasectomy for lung-confined recurrent endometrial cancer: a single-institution case series.
articles.authors: Kawanaka M, Nishimura A, Motohara T
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pulmonary recurrence in endometrial cancer is generally regarded as a manifestation of systemic disease and is primarily managed with systemic therapy. However, the clinical significance of lung-confined recurrent endometrial cancer and the role of pulmonary metastasectomy remain uncertain.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the long-term oncologic outcomes of pulmonary metastasectomy in patients with lung-confined recurrent endometrial cancer and to explore whether lung-confined recurrence represents a clinically distinct pattern of recurrence.
STUDY DESIGN: This retrospective single-institution case series included consecutive patients with lung-confined recurrent endometrial cancer who underwent pulmonary metastasectomy between January 2005 and July 2026. Clinicopathological characteristics, long-term oncologic outcomes, and perioperative outcomes were evaluated.
RESULTS: Six patients underwent pulmonary metastasectomy for lung-confined recurrent endometrial cancer. The median interval from primary surgery to first pulmonary recurrence was 45.5 months (range, 19-227 months). Complete (R0) pulmonary resection was achieved in all patients without severe surgery-related adverse events. During a median follow-up of 103.5 months (range, 47-250 months) from primary surgery, all 6 patients remained alive, and 5 of 6 achieved durable disease-free status. Following the first pulmonary metastasectomy, 1 patient developed subsequent lung-confined recurrence and underwent repeat pulmonary metastasectomy, achieving additional long-term disease control. Notably, the 2 patients with synchronous bilateral pulmonary metastases also achieved durable disease-free survival following complete staged bilateral resection.
CONCLUSION: Pulmonary metastasectomy may provide durable long-term disease control in carefully selected patients with lung-confined recurrent endometrial cancer. Recognition of lung-confined recurrent endometrial cancer as a clinically distinct pattern of recurrence may support a shift from routine systemic therapy alone toward a more individualized multidisciplinary treatment strategy incorporating pulmonary metastasectomy.

articles.title: Bronchoalveolar lavage fluid cfDNA liquid biopsy-guided neoadjuvant lazertinib in resectable EGFR-mutant non-small cell lung cancer: a prospective phase II study.
articles.authors: Kim IA, Kim H, Hur JY et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Reliable preoperative molecular testing is increasingly important in resectable non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), particularly when tissue biopsy is not feasible or yields insufficient material. We evaluated the feasibility of bronchoalveolar lavage fluid cell-free DNA liquid biopsy (BALiquid) as a preoperative epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) genotyping platform and assessed the clinical efficacy of neoadjuvant lazertinib in patients with potentially resectable EGFR-mutant NSCLC.
METHODS: A total of 128 patients with computed tomography (CT) findings suggestive of potentially resectable lung cancer underwent bronchoscopy with bronchoalveolar lavage near the target lesion. EGFR genotyping was performed using polymerase chain reaction (PCR)-based BALF cfDNA analysis. Patients with sensitizing EGFR mutations detected by BALiquid received neoadjuvant lazertinib for 9 weeks followed by surgical resection. Diagnostic performance, radiologic response, surgical outcomes, pathologic response, and safety were evaluated.
RESULTS: Among 48 patients with BALiquid-detected EGFR mutations, 40 were enrolled and 34 completed neoadjuvant lazertinib followed by surgery. BALiquid EGFR genotyping demonstrated a sensitivity of 74%, a specificity of 97.0%, a positive predictive value of 97.4%, a negative predictive value of 71.7% and 83.3% of concordance rate compared with surgical tissue genotyping. The all-treated objective response rate (ORR) was 57.5% [23/40; 95% confidence interval (CI): 40.9-73.0%], and the ORR in the per-protocol population was 67.6% (23/34; 95% CI: 49.5-82.6%). R0 resection was achieved in 33 of 34 patients. Pathologic downstaging occurred in 55.9% of patients, and major pathologic response was achieved in 6 of 34 patients (17.6%). Grade 3 or higher treatment-related adverse events occurred in 4/40 patients (10.0%).
CONCLUSIONS: BALiquid may serve as a complemental preoperative EGFR genotyping approach to provide genetic information when tissue is unavailable or insufficient. BALiquid-guided neoadjuvant lazertinib demonstrated meaningful antitumor activity, favorable surgical outcomes, and an acceptable safety profile in patients with potentially resectable EGFR-mutant NSCLC.

articles.title: The role of carbonic anhydrases IX and XII in hypoxia-driven tumor adaptation and chemoresistance: an underexplored frontier for novel therapeutic strategies in ovarian cancer.
articles.authors: Velarde Calderón A, Guzmán Mendoza JJ, Sánchez-Ramírez B et al.
articles.abstract: Human carbonic anhydrases IX and XII (hCA IX/XII) regulate pH homeostasis and may facilitate tumor adaptation, progression, and therapeutic resistance. Although extensively studied in other malignancies, their roles in ovarian cancer (OC) remain insufficiently characterized. This narrative review critically examines their biological functions and therapeutic potential, emphasizing hypoxia and acidosis within the heterogeneous ovarian tumor microenvironment. Literature was searched in PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar, prioritizing studies on hypoxia, acidosis, chemoresistance, and carbonic anhydrase inhibition. Evidence from OC models was distinguished from findings in other cancers. Public transcriptomic data were additionally explored using GEPIA and Kaplan-Meier Plotter to examine CA9 and CA12 expression and survival associations. Available findings suggest potential roles for these isoenzymes in adaptation to acidic, hypoxic conditions, but OC-specific mechanistic and therapeutic evidence remains limited. We discuss preclinical inhibitors, key knowledge gaps, and priorities for future research.

articles.title: Extracellular DNA amplifies autoimmunity in Aicardi-Goutières syndrome.
articles.journal: Molecular therapy : the journal of the American Society of Gene Therapy
articles.authors: Sims D, Lester ER, Lopez SG et al.
articles.abstract: Aicardi-Goutières syndrome (AGS) is an early-onset encephalopathy caused by pathogenic variants in genes that degrade or sense cytoplasmic nucleic acids. In the DNA-sensing subtypes of AGS, including AGS1, accumulation of intracellular DNA activates cGAS-STING signaling, driving a type I interferonopathy resulting in multisystem inflammation, failure to thrive, and premature death. Although AGS is initiated by intracellular nucleic acid sensing, its clinical overlap with systemic lupus erythematosus suggests that extracellular nucleic acid signaling may also contribute to disease pathogenesis. Here, we tested this concept in the severe Trex1-/- murine model of AGS1 by treating mice with 1687, a dual-acting DNase1/DNase1L3 biologic, dosed weekly at 1 mg/kg s.c. Vehicle-treated Trex1-/- mice exhibited early clinical decline and high mortality, whereas 1687 significantly improved survival over 250 days, and partially normalized growth and gross disease manifestations. Treatment reduced cell-free DNA and normalized anti-dsDNA and anti-myosin heavy chain 6 autoantibodies, and dampened inflammatory mediators (IFN-γ, CXCL1, CXCL2). In contrast, the interferon-responsive mediators IFN-α, CCL5, and CXCL9 were unchanged, suggesting that 1687 does not uniformly suppress downstream signaling from persistent intracellular nucleic acid sensing. These findings identify an extracellular DNA-driven amplification loop in AGS and support DNase biologics as a mechanistically targeted therapeutic strategy.

articles.title: Guideline Implementation Gap in Preeclampsia Prevention: Adherence to Low-Dose Aspirin Use in Routine Obstetric Practice.
articles.authors: Tarhan NU, Durcanoğlu N, Yiğit SB et al.
articles.abstract: Evidence-based guidelines recommend the use of low-dose aspirin (LDA) to prevent preeclampsia. Gaps between recommended and actual care may limit the impact of proven preventive interventions. This study aimed to assess obstetricians' adherence to LDA prescription for preeclampsia prevention in accordance with the national guideline. This retrospective cohort study included 1150 women who delivered between November 2023 and December 2024. Eligibility for LDA use was determined according to guideline-defined risk criteria. Adherence was defined as prescribing LDA between 11 and 16 weeks of gestation. The rate of LDA recommendation was assessed and factors associated with LDA prescription were analyzed. 210 women (18.3%) met the criteria for LDA recommendation. However, LDA was prescribed to 97 (46.2%) of these women, indicating that more than half of the candidates missed the opportunity for prophylaxis. Among the 969 women who did not use LDA during pregnancy, 113 (11.7%) actually met the guideline criteria and should have received LDA. In this untreated group, the incidence of preeclampsia was approximately fourfold higher compared with women without an LDA indication (26.5% vs. 8.2%; OR 4.06, 95% CI 2.50-6.58, p < 0.001). Follow-up at a tertiary healthcare center at or before 16 weeks of gestation was associated with significantly higher rates of appropriate LDA prescription (p < 0.001). Adherence to national guideline for the prevention of preeclampsia remains suboptimal in Türkiye. This implementation gap represents missed opportunities for the prevention of preeclampsia and underscores the need for targeted educational initiatives and system-level interventions.

articles.title: Maternal and Neonatal Care in Custody: Providing Evidence-Based Care to Pregnant and Postpartum Youth and Adults Experiencing Incarceration and to Their Newborns.
articles.authors: Hall B, Knittel AK, Sufrin C
articles.abstract: Pregnant incarcerated adolescents and young adults experience intersecting medical and social vulnerabilities that require trauma-informed and patient-centered care. Evidence-based care during incarceration includes pregnancy and postpartum screening during intake, options counseling, and timely initiation of comprehensive obstetric, postpartum, and behavioral health services. Principles of safety, autonomy, and dignity are vital to perinatal and intrapartum care. Address lactation, contraception, and mental health explicitly during postpartum care. Pediatric clinicians play a vital role in coordinating care for affected infants and parents and ensuring continuity from incarceration through community reentry. Clinicians can promote maternal-infant stability, reduce disparities, and advance reproductive justice.

articles.title: Transplacental transfer efficiency and longitudinal dynamics of antibodies against RSV in early childhood: a paired mother-neonate cohort study in southern China.
articles.journal: Clinical microbiology and infection : the official publication of the European Society of Clinical Microbiology and Infectious Diseases
articles.authors: Xu M, Wang Y, Tong X et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Maternal antibodies provide early-life protection against severe respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection but wane rapidly. With the availability of maternal vaccine and half-life extended monoclonal antibodies for infants, understanding transplacental antibody transfer and subsequent antibody dynamics is important for optimising immunisation strategies.
METHODS: We conducted a longitudinal cohort study of 695 mother-neonate pairs in southern China between 2013 and 2021. Serum samples were collected from mothers at delivery and from children at birth, 2, 4, 6, 12, 24, 36 months, and 5-8 years of age. All samples were tested for RSV pre-F IgG antibodies using an enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay. A subset of samples was additionally tested for neutralizing antibodies (nAbs) using a foci reduction neutralization test.
RESULTS: Maternal and cord blood RSV pre-F IgG antibody levels were positively correlated ( = 0.87; P<0.001) with a mean transplacental transfer ratio of 1.44 (95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.40-1.47). A 10-fold increase in maternal antibody levels was associated with a 6.46-fold increase in cord blood antibody levels, corresponding to a 35% decrease in transplacental transfer ratios. Preterm birth was associated with 17% lower cord blood antibody levels than full-term birth. Maternally derived antibodies declined rapidly after birth, with an estimated half-life of 34.3 days (95% CI, 33.9-34.8); antibody levels reached a nadir at approximately 10 months of age and gradually increased thereafter. RSV pre-F IgG and nAb titers from children were strongly correlated (repeated-measures correlation: = 0.846, P < 0.001), and the correlation persisted after adjustment for age ( = 0.743, P < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: Our findings highlight the importance of addressing lower maternally derived antibody levels in preterm infants, particularly in the context of maternal immunisation. Longitudinal antibody dynamics reveal a distinct period of low antibody levels during infancy that may inform the timing of targeted RSV immunisation strategies.

articles.title: Dose-related effects of chronic dietary fructose consumption on sperm functional quality, chromatin packaging, and testicular redox homeostasis in C57BL/6 mice.
articles.authors: Darmishonnejad Z, Tavalaee M, Naderi N et al.
articles.abstract: Chronic consumption of high-fructose diets has been associated with metabolic disturbances, but its effects on male reproductive function and testicular redox homeostasis remain incompletely understood. This study investigated the effects of chronic exposure to different concentrations of dietary fructose on sperm quality, chromatin integrity, oxidative status, metabolic parameters, and cognitive function in male C57BL/6 mice. Mice were randomly assigned to control, 10% fructose (F10%), or 30% fructose (F30%) groups and received the respective solutions in drinking water for 15 consecutive weeks. Body weight, fasting blood glucose, glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c), adiposity, testicular morphometry, sperm concentration, motility, morphology, chromatin maturity, DNA integrity, intracellular reactive oxygen species (ROS), membrane lipid peroxidation, testicular malondialdehyde (MDA), total antioxidant capacity (TAC), fructose content, and spatial working memory were assessed. F30% exposure significantly increased body weight, adiposity, fasting blood glucose, and glycated hemoglobin (P < 0.05). Both F10% and F30% groups showed significantly reduced sperm concentration and progressive motility, increased morphological abnormalities, protamine deficiency, histone retention, DNA denaturation susceptibility, intracellular ROS, and membrane lipid peroxidation (P < 0.05). F30% further increased testicular MDA and fructose levels and decreased TAC (P < 0.05). Spontaneous alternation in the Y-maze was significantly reduced in both fructose groups, whereas exploratory activity decreased only in F30% mice (P < 0.05). Chronic fructose exposure adversely affects sperm function, chromatin integrity, and redox homeostasis even at 10%, while higher exposure intensifies reproductive, metabolic, testicular oxidative, and cognitive alterations.

articles.title: Nervous system and bladder alterations following mesenchymal stem cell administration in rats with IC/BPS.
articles.journal: European journal of obstetrics, gynecology, and reproductive biology
articles.ta: Eur J Obstet Gynecol Reprod Biol
articles.authors: Demir KK, Akkoç T, Cılıngır-Kaya OT et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Interstitial cystitis/bladder pain syndrome (IC/BPS) arises from multiple etiologic factors, and most studies suggest that stem cell therapy is beneficial. Although stem cells support bladder tissue regeneration, their effects on neuroinflammation and central pain pathways remain unclear. This study aimed to investigate how human umbilical cord-derived mesenchymal stem cells (HU-MSCs) delivered to the bladder wall influence neuroinflammatory mechanisms contributing to chronic pain in an LPS/PS-induced IC/BPS rat model.
MATERIAL AND METHOD: IC/BPS was induced in rats using lipopolysaccharide/protamine sulfate (LPS/PS) with 750 µg LPS and 10 mg PS administered weekly for 5 weeks via intravesical instillation. HU-MSCs were expanded to passage 3, and 1.2 × 106 cells in 0.2 ml PBS were injected into the bladder dome one week after LPS/PS treatment. Rats were euthanized one week later, and bladder and spinal cord tissues were paraffin-embedded. Bladder inflammation scores were assessed with H&E staining, while mast cell count and distribution were evaluated with toluidine blue. Neuroinflammation markers (Iba-1 and TNF-α) in spinal cord sections were analyzed by immunohistochemistry.
RESULTS: The LPS/PS group showed elevated bladder inflammation scores, increased mast cell infiltration, and higher anti-TNF-α and anti-IBA-1 levels compared with controls. HU-MSC treatment improved chronic inflammatory changes, reducing inflammation scores and mast cell infiltration. Immunohistochemistry demonstrated decreased spinal cord anti-TNF-α and anti-IBA-1 expression following HU-MSC administration.
CONCLUSION: HU-MSCs exhibit therapeutic potential for IC/BPS by promoting bladder regeneration, reducing inflammation and mast cell activity, and attenuating spinal neuroinflammation.
BRIEF SUMMARY: Intravesical hUC-MSC therapy reduced bladder inflammation, mast cell infiltration, and spinal dorsal horn neuroinflammation in IC/BPS rats, demonstrating both peripheral and central therapeutic benefits.

articles.title: Assessment of peripheral and tumor specific Tregs and Th17 cells in patients with endometrial cancer.
articles.authors: Nelson S, Diaz-Sylvester P, Badger T et al.
articles.abstract:
