OBJECTIVE: The frontline treatment for endometrial cancer (EC) is a hysterectomy; immunotherapy is approved, but has limited efficacy in all EC genotypes (mismatch repair genotypes). Understanding how EC pathogenesis affects the immune response is essential to determine effective interventions. Systemic inflammation, driven by T helper 17 (Th17) cells is induced in many cancers, while tumor induction of suppressive T regulatory cells (Tregs) is critical for immune evasion. We hypothesized that patients with EC have peripheral inflammation (evidenced by increased Th17:Treg ratio); yet, the EC tumor microenvironment (TME) remains immune tolerant (high Treg localization).
METHODS: We collected peripheral blood and endometrial tissue from 61 patients with EC and 15 controls on the day-of-surgery, and blood post-surgical intervention (PSI). Peripheral Tregs and Th17 populations were examined via fluorescence activated cell sorting, plasma cytokine levels were measured utilizing immune assays, and tissue abundance of Th17 and Tregs via immunohistochemistry.
RESULTS: Compared to controls, patients with early-stage (I, II) EC exhibited decreased peripheral unconventional Tregs (uTregs) and total Tregs, without changes in Th17 cell populations or the overall peripheral Th17:Treg ratio. Patients with proficient MMR genotyping also had reduced peripheral Treg populations. Patients with advanced disease (III, IV) had elevated peripheral inflammatory cytokines. The TME, regardless of stage, had increased abundance of Foxp3+, but decreased RORγt+ cells. EC patients had reduced peripheral inflammatory cytokine production at PSI.
CONCLUSIONS: EC patients exhibited increased peripheral inflammation, which decreased after tumor removal. EC TME indicated potential immune evasion through increased Tregs, but decreased Th17 localization within the tumor.

articles.title: Night-shift work during menopause: associations with menopausal symptom severity and limitations in work functioning.
articles.authors: Loef B, van Oostrom SH, Proper KI et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To examine associations of night-shift work with menopausal symptom severity and limitations in work functioning due to menopausal symptoms. Furthermore, the association between menopausal symptom severity and quitting night-shift work was examined to explore a potential "healthy shift worker" effect.
STUDY DESIGN: Data from 13,895 menopausal women from the Dutch Lifelines cohort were used. In 2021 and 2024, participants completed a questionnaire on night-shift work, menopausal symptom severity, menopause-related limitations in work functioning, and relevant covariates. In total, 4827 women had measurements available from both 2021 and 2024, while 9068 had measurements from only one year.
METHODS: Repeated-measures models were used to analyze associations of current night-shift work (vs. day work) with menopausal symptom severity (measured as score on the Greene Climacteric Scale [GCS]) and limitations in work functioning across the 2021 and 2024 measurements. Logistic regression was used to assess the association between symptom severity and quitting night-shift work between 2021 and 2024.
RESULTS: Night-shift workers reported lower overall menopausal symptom severity than day workers (B = -0.71, 95% CI -1.20, -0.22), as well as lower scores in the psychological, somatic, and sexual domains, while scores in the vasomotor domain were similar. No differences were found in limitations in work functioning due to menopausal symptoms (OR = 0.91, 95% CI 0.79, 1.05). Notably, night-shift workers with a high symptom score (defined as a GCS score ≥ 18, i.e. upper tertile) had higher odds of quitting night-shift work (OR = 1.98, 95% CI 1.03, 3.84), suggesting a selection effect.
CONCLUSIONS: Current night-shift work was not associated with higher menopausal symptom severity or greater limitations in work functioning due to these symptoms. As a high menopausal symptom score was associated with quitting night-shift work, these findings are consistent with a "healthy shift worker" effect, warranting further research using a more comprehensive assessment of night-shift work exposure to investigate potential selection mechanisms. Given the impact of menopausal symptoms on work functioning, adequate organizational support for menopausal women, whether engaged in night-shift work or not, remains important.

articles.title: Dehydroepiandrosterone in menopausal medicine: From adrenal aging to intracrinology and personalised therapy.
articles.authors: Parra-Armendaris MM, Parra-Yagnam FS, Simoncini T
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Dehydroepiandrosterone and its sulfate are the most abundant circulating steroids in women, yet they have no high-affinity nuclear receptor of their own. Their physiological role is that of a precursor pool from which active androgens and estrogens are generated locally, within peripheral target cells, through the tissue-specific expression of steroidogenic enzymes-the process Labrie termed intracrinology. After menopause, when ovarian estrogen secretion ceases, essentially all estrogens and a large fraction of androgens acting on peripheral tissues derive from the intracrine conversion of adrenal dehydroepiandrosterone. Because adrenal dehydroepiandrosterone production declines progressively from the third decade of life (adrenopause), the menopausal woman faces a dual hormonal deficit: ovarian and adrenal.
SEARCH STRATEGY: PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase and the Cochrane Library were searched for randomised trials, meta-analyses, mechanistic and pharmacokinetic studies, and current society position statements on dehydroepiandrosterone and prasterone in menopausal women, supplemented by hand-searching of key reference lists. This narrative review develops the intracrine framework as the conceptual bridge between adrenal aging and clinical therapeutics and critically appraises the evidence for two very different therapeutic strategies.
FINDINGS: Oral dehydroepiandrosterone, despite decades of investigation and a biologically coherent rationale, has not demonstrated convincing benefit on menopausal symptoms, sexual function, mood, bone or quality of life in women with normal adrenal function, and current guidelines do not endorse it. By contrast, intravaginal prasterone (6.5 mg dehydroepiandrosterone) exploits intracrinology at the level of a single estrogen- and androgen-responsive organ, improving the signs and symptoms of the genitourinary syndrome of menopause and moderate to severe dyspareunia while leaving serum sex-steroid levels within the normal postmenopausal range; it is approved by the United States Food and Drug Administration and the European Medicines Agency and is increasingly incorporated into international recommendations.
CONCLUSION: We summarise the comparative evidence against other menopausal therapies, review the safety signal, contrast the positions of the major societies, and outline how biomarker-guided, intracrine-informed precision medicine might define the future role of dehydroepiandrosterone. The dehydroepiandrosterone…

articles.title: Tear-fluid glial fibrillary acidic protein combined with optic-nerve ultrasonography for non-invasive assessment of cerebral involvement in severe pre-eclampsia: a cross-sectional study.
articles.authors: Taskina ES, Tsybikov NN, Mudrov VA et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To determine whether serum and tear-fluid glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP), anti-GFAP autoantibodies, and optic-nerve ultrasonography are associated with disease severity in hypertensive disorders of pregnancy, and to explore whether their combination adds to the identification of severe pre-eclampsia.
STUDY DESIGN: This prospective cross-sectional study included 184 pregnant women equally allocated to normotensive pregnancy, gestational hypertension, moderate pre-eclampsia, or severe pre-eclampsia (n = 46/group). Serum GFAP and anti-GFAP autoantibodies were measured in all participants, and tear-fluid GFAP in a predefined subgroup (22/group). Standardized optic-nerve ultrasonography assessed optic nerve sheath diameter (ONSD), optic disc height (ODH), optic nerve diameter, and scleral canal diameter. Associations were analysed using non-parametric statistics, Spearman correlation, and receiver-operating characteristic (ROC) analysis.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Between-group differences in biomarkers and ultrasonographic parameters, correlations with disease severity, and discrimination of severe pre-eclampsia by ROC analysis.
RESULTS: Serum GFAP increased only in severe pre-eclampsia, whereas tear-fluid GFAP increased progressively from moderate to severe disease (both P < 0.001). Anti-GFAP autoantibodies peaked in moderate pre-eclampsia. Tear-fluid GFAP correlated strongly with ODH (r = 0.772) and with clinical severity (all P < 0.001). ONSD (AUC 0.984) and ODH (AUC 0.973) were the most accurate individual markers; tear-fluid GFAP (AUC 0.908) outperformed serum GFAP (AUC 0.744).
CONCLUSIONS: Tear-fluid GFAP rises earlier than serum GFAP and tracks ultrasonographic signs of raised intracranial pressure, supporting it as a non-invasive marker of astroglial injury in pre-eclampsia. Optic-nerve ultrasonography provides the strongest discrimination of severe disease. Prospective multicentre studies with neurological outcomes are needed before clinical implementation.

articles.title: Early self-regulation in context: Multidimensional organization of neonatal non-nutritive sucking and its association with subclinical maternal depressive traits.
articles.authors: Faré O, Silvestri V, Morniroli D et al.
articles.abstract: From the very first days of life, infants' affective regulation unfolds within a dyadic co-regulatory system shaped by caregiver responsivity. In contexts of reduced maternal availability, such as maternal depressive states, infants may be required to compensate for diminished interpersonal regulation by increasingly relying on their internal resources. Neonatal non-nutritive sucking (NNS) represents one of the earliest spontaneously available regulatory behaviors, contributing to physiological and behavioral homeostasis from birth. However, it remains unclear whether its spontaneous organization is associated with early relational vulnerability indexed by maternal depressive symptoms. The present study aimed to characterize the spontaneous organization of NNS in a sample of newborns (N = 42) and to examine whether individual differences in NNS are associated with maternal postnatal depressive subclinical traits measured using the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS). Results from an exploratory principal component analysis indicated that neonatal sucking behavior was organized along two functional dimensions, reflecting overall sucking effort and behavioral activation, and the temporal organization of sucking bursts. Importantly, higher maternal depressive traits, though subclinical, were selectively associated with increased sucking effort, with infants of mothers reporting higher depressive traits showing more frequent and intense sucking, while no differences emerged for the organizational dimension. Overall, these findings suggest that individual differences in maternal depressive traits within the subclinical range may be associated with neonatal NNS effort, a precocious compensatory mobilization of regulatory resources, potentially serving both to support autonomous regulation and to elicit maternal engagement.

articles.title: PAQR5 links microvascular invasion, innate immune inflammatory amplification, and platinum resistance in ovarian cancer.
articles.authors: Huang S, Xu L, Li J et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Platinum resistance remains the principal obstacle to improving survival in ovarian cancer. Microvascular invasion (MVI) is associated with chemoresistance and immune remodeling, but the molecular regulators connecting vascular invasion, innate immune-driven inflammatory amplification, and treatment failure remain poorly defined.
METHODS: Three public datasets and 118 literature-curated MVI genes were integrated. Differential expression analysis followed by three-way intersection identified PAQR5 as the core candidate. Its clinical, immune-inflammatory, and pharmacological relevance was mapped using CIBERSORT, ESTIMATE, pRRophetic, and nomogram modeling, and validated by qPCR/Western blot, MTT/CCK-8, colony/wound-healing assays, flow cytometry, gamma-H2AX foci, EdU incorporation, and subcutaneous xenografts (n = 5-6 mice/group).
RESULTS: PAQR5 was the only gene shared among cisplatin-resistance signatures in vitro (303 DEGs), patient tissue resistance signatures (2507 DEGs), and the MVI gene set. TCGA tumors overexpressed PAQR5 2.8-fold compared with GTEx normal tissue (P < 0.001). High PAQR5 independently predicted shortened overall survival (HR = 1.18; 95% CI 1.02-1.44; P = 0.005) and 5-year progression-free survival (HR = 1.33; 95% CI 1.09-1.63; P = 0.04). In silico, PAQR5-high tumors showed an innate immune-skewed suppressive profile, with increased M2 macrophages (+28%) and Tregs (+17%) but reduced CD8+ T cells (-31%) and NK cells (-21%; all P < 0.01). They also displayed elevated cisplatin, docetaxel, and paclitaxel IC50 values (each P < 0.0001), whereas AKT-inhibitor VIII IC50 fell 1.7-fold. Functionally, PAQR5 overexpression increased proliferation, colony formation, migration, DNA damage tolerance, and xenograft growth, whereas silencing produced mirror-image suppression and restored cisplatin-induced apoptosis.
CONCLUSION: PAQR5 appears to couple MVI with platinum resistance by coordinating an immunosuppressive inflammatory tumor microenvironment, enhanced DNA damage repair, and reduced apoptosis. These findings nominate PAQR5 as a mechanism-linked biomarker and a therapeutic entry point for targeting inflammation-associated chemoresistance in ovarian cancer.

articles.title: Recurrent transcriptional signatures of acquired chemoresistance across cancer models.
articles.authors: Zampetakis I, Gkogkou E, Trougakos IP
articles.abstract: Chemoresistance is the innate or acquired ability of cancer cells to evade the cytotoxic effects of chemotherapeutic agents. This hypothesis-generating study presents a systematic comparative analysis of public transcriptomic datasets associated with acquired chemoresistance to major drugs including doxorubicin, cisplatin, and gemcitabine. The aim was to identify recurrent drug-specific gene expression patterns in drug-resistant cancer cells relative to their drug-sensitive parental cells. Publicly available microarray datasets of breast, ovarian, neuroblastoma, bladder, and gallbladder chemoresistant cell lines were retrieved from the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) database. Differential expression analysis using R/Bioconductor revealed distinct and overlapping signatures of chemoresistance across different cancer types. In doxorubicin-resistant breast cancer, recurrently dysregulated genes included IL-18, CD44, FN1, EGFR, and the histones H2BC10 and H2BC7. Neuroblastoma and ovarian cancer cell datasets shared Differentially Expressed Genes (DEGs) including ABCB1, RUNDC3B, CROT, and TP53TG1. TMEM47 was the only common DEG among all three (breast cancer, neuroblastoma, and ovarian cancer) doxorubicin-resistant datasets, although with tissue-dependent regulation. Gemcitabine resistance signatures in bladder and gallbladder cells include EPCAM, AGR2, NRP2, FGF1, CTH, TENM2, and the long non-coding RNAs APCDD1L-DT and LINC01234. Combined gemcitabine/5-FU resistance revealed common patterns of resistance in gallbladder and colon cancer cell lines. In cisplatin-resistant ovarian cancer cells, LAMA2 and SOX8 were differentially expressed with a consistent direction of change in all datasets in which they were measured. These recurrent associations do not establish causality; rather, they prioritize candidate genes for functional validation in future studies of chemoresistance.

articles.title: HPV vaccination in Germany: only a missed opportunity in cancer prevention or a symptom of structural weakness?
articles.authors: Lampl BM
articles.abstract: Human papillomavirus (HPV) is a leading vaccine-preventable cause of cancer, responsible for cervical cancer and a substantial share of anogenital and oropharyngeal malignancies. Although highly effective vaccines are available and recommended in Germany, vaccination uptake remains suboptimal. Evidence from Germany and other countries demonstrates significant reductions in HPV infections and precancerous lesions following vaccination, yet implementation gaps persist. These gaps are not primarily driven by scientific uncertainty, but by structural and behavioral barriers, including an opportunistic vaccination model, parental vaccine hesitancy, and inconsistent physician recommendation. More broadly, low uptake might reflect systemic weaknesses: prevention remains insufficiently prioritized, the public health service in Germany is comparatively weak, and healthcare continues to emphasize curative over preventive approaches. Improving HPV vaccination coverage therefore requires both targeted measures to enhance delivery and a broader shift toward embedding prevention as a central function of the German health system.

articles.title: Neutrophil extracellular traps and routine coagulation biomarkers predict pregnancy outcomes in recurrent pregnancy loss.
articles.authors: Liu Z, Wang J, Zhang L et al.
articles.abstract: Recurrent pregnancy loss (RPL) is a complex reproductive disorder involving immune dysregulation, inflammation and coagulation imbalance. Neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) may provide a mechanistic link between inflammatory activation and thrombosis-related placental dysfunction but their combined predictive value with routine coagulation biomarkers remains insufficiently defined. This single-center prospective study enrolled 350 pregnant women at 6-10 weeks of gestation, including controls, women with successful ongoing pregnancy (SOP), and women with RPL adverse outcomes during follow-up. Candidate biomarkers included NETs, myeloperoxidase-DNA complex, protein S (PS), protein C (PC), antithrombin (AT), D-dimer, and platelet aggregation indicators. After correlation-based screening, five predictors were retained: NETs, PS, PC, AT, and D-dimer. Logistic regression (LR), support vector machine (SVM), k-nearest neighbor (KNN), and decision tree (DT) models were developed and internally validated using five-fold cross-validation. SVM achieved the highest averaged area under the curve (AUC = 0.9420), whereas KNN showed the highest overall accuracy (81.43%). Multivariable regression indicated that elevated NETs and D-dimer were associated with increased risk of adverse pregnancy outcomes, whereas higher PS, PC, and AT were associated with protective effects. These findings suggest that NETs and routine coagulation biomarkers may provide useful information for early risk stratification in RPL. Further multicenter external validation and longer follow-up are required before clinical implementation.

articles.title: Trophoblast mitochondrial dysfunction in preeclampsia: Pathology-guided design of fetal-sparing placental nanotherapy.
articles.authors: Althumairy D, Saber S, Hamad RS et al.
articles.abstract: Preeclampsia is driven by placental pathology in which trophoblast stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, and anti-angiogenic signaling contribute to maternal endothelial injury and adverse fetal outcomes. Although nanomedicine offers a potential means of directing therapy to the placenta, placental accumulation alone does not establish productive trophoblast delivery, mitochondrial target engagement, or fetal safety. This review examines the pathological and bioenergetic features of the preeclamptic placenta that should guide nanocarrier design. Evidence linking abnormal placentation, respiratory instability, excessive mitochondrial reactive oxygen species, defective mitochondrial quality control, and soluble fms-like tyrosine kinase-1 release is discussed alongside the delivery consequences of syncytiotrophoblast injury, malperfusion, altered endocytosis, and mitochondrial depolarization. The principal novelty of this review is a sequential placental-mitochondrial targeting strategy designed to improve therapeutic localization while minimizing fetal exposure. In this approach, nanocarriers first accumulate at the maternal-facing placental surface and are subsequently internalized by trophoblast cells. Following cellular uptake, an intracellular trigger activates the previously masked mitochondrial-targeting component, enabling the therapeutic cargo to reach dysfunctional trophoblast mitochondria. This sequential delivery process aims to enhance placental selectivity and mitochondrial drug delivery while restricting transplacental passage into the fetal circulation. Current evidence from mitochondria-targeted antioxidants, placental sFlt-1 silencing, and pro-angiogenic mRNA delivery supports the biological feasibility of this strategy but remains limited by model fidelity, disease heterogeneity, and insufficient developmental safety assessment. Future translation will require pathology-calibrated human placental models, direct comparison of staged and constitutive targeting systems, quantitative maternal-placental-fetal biodistribution, and long-term evaluation of placental compatibility and offspring safety.

articles.title: Inhibition of CYP19A1 aromatase and suppression of estradiol production by polyhalogenated carbazoles: an in vitro and in silico study.
articles.authors: Sang J, Yang Z, Ding X et al.
articles.abstract: Polyhalogenated carbazoles (PHCZs) are emerging contaminants with largely unknown endocrine-disrupting effects. We evaluated 11 PHCZs against human and rat CYP19A1 via enzymatic, cellular, and computational assays. Three compounds (136-BCZ, 1-B-36-CCZ, 36-ICZ) inhibited human CYP19A1 with IC50 of 20.6, 18.1, and 4.7 μM (rat: 32.6, 28.3, 7.5 μM). Kinetic analyses showed mixed inhibition with Ki values of 24.29, 20.4, and 4.0 μM for human CYP19A1, indicating binding to both free enzyme and enzyme-substrate complex. Docking and 200 ns MD simulations revealed stable anchoring in the catalytic pocket via halogen-mediated hydrophobic interactions with Ile305, Val370, Met374, consistent with the strongest inhibitory activity of 36-ICZ due to iodine polarizability. Cellular assays in BeWo cells confirmed concentration-dependent estradiol suppression (5-20 μM) by all three. Network toxicology identified CYP19A1 as a central node linking PHCZs to polycystic ovary syndrome and osteoporosis; bivariate correlation and 3D-QSAR modeling further revealed logP and pKa as key determinants of activity. Collectively, this study provides the first direct mechanistic evidence that PHCZs inhibit CYP19A1, revealing a specific endocrine-disrupting pathway with reproductive health implications and a framework for risk assessment and safer design.

articles.title: When 'idiopathic' is not idiopathic: imaging-based differentiation of azoospermia in the APHRODITE algorithm.
articles.authors: Barak S, Waldenberg N, Bar G et al.
articles.abstract: The recently introduced APHRODITE criteria provide a structured framework for classifying and treating men with idiopathic male infertility, including azoospermic men in Group 2, who present with normal serum FSH and normal total testosterone concentrations and may be considered for hormonal therapy. However, a normal FSH concentration does not by itself distinguish obstructive from non-obstructive azoospermia, and obstructive azoospermia characteristically shares the same hormonal and testicular-volume profile that defines Group 2; non-obstructive azoospermia due to maturation arrest can present similarly, and hormonal therapy is unlikely to benefit these men either. Men with obstructive azoospermia or non-obstructive azoospermia due to maturation arrest who are misclassified in Group 2 may be exposed to prolonged, ineffective gonadotrophin therapy while definitive treatment is delayed. This commentary highlights this risk together with broader limitations of the APHRODITE criteria and proposes earlier imaging, using whichever modality is available at the treating centre, as a potential strategy to identify occult obstruction and avoid unnecessary hormonal therapy. This approach, however, requires prospective validation.

articles.title: Integrated Prenatal Cardiopulmonary Assessment Using Fetal Echocardiography in Isolated Left-Sided Congenital Diaphragmatic Hernia.
articles.authors: Yamoto M, Inamura N, Toyoshima K et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Prenatal severity assessment in congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH) primarily relies on lung-based parameters such as the observed-to-expected lung-to-head ratio (o/eLHR) and liver position; however, these markers do not fully reflect fetal cardiopulmonary adaptation. We investigated the prognostic significance of fetal echocardiographic parameters and integrated these in prenatal prediction models in left-sided CDH.
METHODS: This nationwide multicenter retrospective study included fetuses with prenatally diagnosed isolated left-sided CDH. Gestational age-adjusted Z-scores were generated for fetal cardiac dimensions. Receiver operating characteristic analyses were performed to evaluate prognostic performance for survival.
RESULTS: A total of 363 fetuses were included, with an overall survival rate of 74.9%. Non-survivors demonstrated significantly smaller right pulmonary artery and mitral valve dimensions than survivors. Among fetal echocardiographic parameters, the mitral-to-tricuspid valve ratio (MTR) demonstrated the strongest predictive performance, with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.77. In fetuses evaluated at ≤ 29 weeks' gestation, an exploratory model combining MTR with o/eLHR and liver-up status achieved an apparent AUC of 0.827.
CONCLUSION: Fetal echocardiographic parameters were associated with survival in CDH. Integrated prenatal cardiopulmonary assessment incorporating MTR may provide complementary prognostic information although independent external validation is required.

articles.title: Fetal Cells in Maternal Blood for Noninvasive Prenatal Testing-Is it Still a Distant Star?
articles.authors: Singh R, Ravn K, Jeppesen LD et al.
articles.abstract: Accurate and safe prenatal diagnosis of severe genetic disorders remains challenging despite advances in genomic technologies and increased use of cell-free noninvasive prenatal testing (cfNIPT). Currently, approximately half of pathogenic copy number variants (pCNVs) and most monogenic disorders are identified only postnatally. cfNIPT primarily detects aneuploidies. Some extended cfNIPTs perform genome-wide screening for larger pCNVs as well as selected microdeletion syndromes. Traditional invasive techniques, such as chorionic villus sampling (CVS), detect both aneuploidies and pCNVs but involve a slight risk of miscarriage. Emerging cell-based noninvasive prenatal testing (cbNIPT) represents a promising advancement, potentially increasing prenatal detection rates by enabling accurate, safe, and comprehensive genome-wide analysis, including small but clinically significant microdeletions, and monogenic disorders such as cystic fibrosis and sickle cell disease. In this review, we make a case for cbNIPT and describe its positioning with respect to cfNIPT. We also present the development of a cell-based technology from finding fetal cell specific biomarkers, streamlining the technology of isolating cells from maternal blood, generating clinical data, and launching a test in the market. This advancement could substantially enhance informed decision-making, timely clinical interventions, and pregnancy outcomes as compared to cfNIPT.

articles.title: Circadian Rhythm-Associated Diagnostic Biomarkers Reveal Immune Dysregulation and Molecular Subtypes in Recurrent Pregnancy Loss.
articles.journal: American journal of reproductive immunology (New York, N.Y. : 1989)
articles.authors: Chen Y, Li Y, Wang S et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Recurrent pregnancy loss (RPL) is a clinically complex reproductive disorder involving impaired maternal-fetal communication and immune imbalance. Circadian rhythm disturbance has recently attracted attention in reproductive failure, but its diagnostic relevance and possible connection with immune dysregulation in RPL remain insufficiently defined.
METHODS: GSE165004 was used as the discovery cohort, and GSE26787 was used as an independent small cohort for preliminary evaluation. Circadian rhythm-associated genes were collected from GeneCards. Differential expression analysis, weighted gene co-expression network analysis, and ssGSEA-based circadian rhythm scoring were integrated to identify RPL-associated circadian transcriptional alterations. Candidate genes were further evaluated by protein-protein interaction analysis, functional enrichment, receiver operating characteristic curve analysis, nomogram construction, immune infiltration assessment, molecular subtype identification, and ceRNA regulatory network prediction.
RESULTS: RPL samples showed a significantly lower circadian rhythm-associated gene score than control samples, indicating reduced circadian-associated transcriptional activity. Three genes, GJA1, UCP2, and GSN, were identified as circadian rhythm-associated candidate diagnostic biomarkers for RPL. In the discovery cohort, the AUC values of GJA1, UCP2, and GSN were 0.80, 0.77, and 0.81, respectively. Their diagnostic performance was further evaluated in an independent small cohort, where the AUC values were 0.72, 0.80, and 0.92, respectively. GSN showed a significant expression difference between RPL and control samples in the independent cohort, whereas GJA1 and UCP2 did not reach statistical significance. Immune infiltration analysis revealed changes in fibroblast, neutrophil, macrophage, Treg, T helper cell, and interferon-related signatures. Consensus clustering based on the three biomarkers classified RPL samples into two molecular subtypes with different immune-stromal characteristics, coagulation-related activity, and metabolic features. The ceRNA network contained 3 diagnostic mRNAs, 43 predicted miRNAs, and 61 upstream lncRNAs.
CONCLUSION: GJA1, UCP2, and GSN may represent circadian rhythm-associated candidate biomarkers for RPL. Their expression patterns may reflect circadian-immune dysregulation and molecular heterogeneity. These findings provide a circadian rhythm-based perspective for understanding RPL pathogenesis…

articles.title: Retinal and choroidal changes on optical coherence tomography in pre-eclampsia: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.authors: KamaliZonouzi S, Semnani F, Fattahniya S et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To summarize optical coherence tomography (OCT)-detected retinal and choroidal changes in pre-eclampsia (PE), to support clinicians in interpreting these changes within the clinical context.
METHODS: We systematically searched four databases (PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and Scopus) through February 2025 to identify observational studies comparing OCT metrics in PE versus control groups. Pooled mean differences (MD) and standardized mean differences (SMD) with 95% confidence intervals (CI) were calculated using random-effects models. Between-study heterogeneity was quantified with the I2 statistic and its sources explored by meta-regression and by subgroup analysis (PE severity, presence of retinal changes, risk of bias, OCT device, eye-selection method, and country); for each subgroup analysis the residual I2 was compared with the I2 of the corresponding overall analysis. Risk of bias was assessed using the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) checklist.
RESULTS: Fifteen studies with 854 eyes from women with PE, 631 eyes from women with normal pregnancy (NP), and 245 eyes from non-pregnant controls (NC) were included. Compared with NP, PE was significantly associated with reduced peripapillary retinal nerve fiber layer (p-RNFL) thickness (SMD: - 0.13, 95% CI: - 0.20 to - 0.06, P = 0.01, I2 = 0%). No statistically significant differences were observed for subfoveal choroidal thickness (SFCT; pre- and post-partum), nasal and temporal choroidal thickness, or central subfield macular thickness (CSMT) in the primary pooled analyses, most of which demonstrated substantial to considerable heterogeneity (I2 up to 94%). Exploratory subgroup analysis suggested that pathological retinal changes and PE severity partially (I2 reduction = 40%) or fully (I2 reduction = 92%) accounted for heterogeneity in pre-partum SFCT estimates.
CONCLUSION: The p-RNFL thickness is subtly reduced in PE compared to NP, representing subclinical structural change. While primary analyses found no significant choroidal or macular differences, subgroup analyses suggest a potential increase in SFCT in severe PE or in the presence of retinal pathology, warranting further investigation.

articles.title: Practical application and exploratory prognostic assessment of the FIGO 2023 stage IA3 criteria in endometrioid endometrial cancer with concurrent ovarian tumours.
articles.authors: Takahashi S, Chiyoda T, Kimura Y et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The FIGO 2023 classification introduced stage IA3 for synchronous low-grade endometrioid carcinoma of the uterus and ovary fulfilling four criteria; disease otherwise confined to these organs that fails any of them becomes stage IIIA1. How often the criteria are met, and how each relates to outcome, is unknown.
METHODS: We retrospectively studied 48 patients with concurrent endometrioid endometrial carcinoma and an ovarian tumour of borderline malignancy or higher. Pathology reports were re-abstracted for each criterion. The primary analysis was restricted to the 42 with an ovarian carcinoma, and each criterion was examined before and after restriction to low-grade histology.
RESULTS: Six of the 42 (14.3%) met all criteria; 12 (28.6%) would have qualified if unilateral FIGO 2014 stage I had been accepted in place of pT1a. Five of the 42 recurred. Endometrial grade 3 was associated with recurrence (five-year progression-free survival 25.0% versus 94.7%; hazard ratio 16.66, 95% CI 2.77-100.2, p = 0.002); ovarian histology was not significantly associated (p = 0.13). Direct extra-uterine/extra-ovarian extension was also associated with recurrence (hazard ratio 8.73, p = 0.018), but all three such recurrences had endometrial grade 3. One of the 31 with low-grade endometrioid carcinoma at both sites recurred. Thirty-four of 42 received adjuvant therapy.
CONCLUSIONS: In this cohort, stage IA3 was uncommon once capsule status and cytology were assessed. Endometrial grade 3 was associated with recurrence, whereas the prognostic contribution of the individual anatomical criteria could not be determined because of the small number of events and confounding by adjuvant treatment. These observations are hypothesis-generating.

articles.title: Postoperative Adverse Events Following Concurrent Midurethral Sling and OnabotulinumtoxinA for Mixed Urinary Incontinence.
articles.authors: Douglass KM, Crawford K, Zhang J et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION AND HYPOTHESIS: For mixed urinary incontinence, concomitant midurethral sling (MUS) and onabotulinumtoxinA (Botox® (BTX-A)) can be considered, but data regarding safety are sparse. Adverse event rates following combined MUS + BTX-A are hypothesized to be similar to those following MUS alone.
METHODS: This was a retrospective matched cohort study comparing adverse events in patients with mixed incontinence undergoing MUS (n = 200) versus combined MUS + BTX-A (n = 100) between January 1, 2011, and March 31, 2024. The primary outcome was culture proven urinary tract infection (UTI) at 3 and 6 months. Secondary outcomes included any UTI (culture proven or empirically treated), urinary retention, and postoperative overactive bladder (OAB) treatment. Logistic regression was used to assess the impact of baseline variables on outcomes.
RESULTS: Patients undergoing concurrent MUS + BTX-A were more likely to have prior stress incontinence surgery, OAB treatment, and postoperative prophylactic antibiotic use. Culture-proven UTI occurred more frequently in the MUS + BTX-A group at 3 months (23.0% vs 12.5%) and 6 months (25.0% vs 15.0%) on unadjusted analysis. After adjustment for measured covariates, the association was attenuated and not statistically significant at 3 months (adjusted OR 1.60, 95% CI 0.78-3.30) or 6 months (adjusted OR 1.47, 95% CI 0.75-2.91). Rates of retention-related events and subsequent OAB treatment were similar between groups.
CONCLUSIONS: Concurrent MUS + BTX-A was associated with higher crude of culture-proven UTI, although adjusted analyses did not demonstrate a statistically significant association. Larger studies are needed to better define the safety of concurrent treatment.

articles.title: Epigenetic reprogramming in Urothelial bladder cancer: mechanisms, biomarkers, and therapeutic opportunities.
articles.authors: Yuanjiang Q, Liming Y
articles.abstract: Urothelial bladder cancer (UBC) is a molecularly heterogeneous malignancy characterized by frequent recurrence, variable progression, and treatment resistance. In addition to recurrent genetic alterations, dysregulation of chromatin remodeling, histone modifications, DNA methylation, and enhancer activity contributes to the biological diversity of UBC. This narrative review critically evaluates the role of epigenetic reprogramming in UBC and integrates mechanistic evidence with biomarker development and therapeutic investigation. Recurrent alterations involving ARID1A, KDM6A, KMT2C/KMT2D, EP300, and CREBBP can modify chromatin accessibility and transcriptional programs, although the functional consequences and strength of causal evidence vary among regulators. Preclinical studies have identified therapeutically relevant dependencies, including the relationship between KDM6A loss, PRC2-mediated repression, and EZH2 inhibition, but clinical validation of most epigenetic targets remains limited. DNA methylation represents the most extensively investigated epigenetic biomarker class in UBC. Urine-based methylation assays have shown encouraging diagnostic performance, whereas plasma cell-free DNA methylation remains an emerging approach requiring further prospective validation. Clinical studies of epigenetic therapies have produced mixed results, emphasizing the need to distinguish biological rationale from demonstrated therapeutic efficacy. Collectively, current evidence supports epigenetic alterations as important contributors to UBC biology while highlighting the need for functional validation, biomarker-selected trials, and longitudinal epigenomic studies before routine clinical implementation.

articles.title: A nomogram model for analyzing risk factors of postpartum hemorrhage in twin pregnancies with cesarean section.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.authors: Zou J, Zhou L, Li K et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The rising prevalence of twin pregnancies and cesarean sections (CS) is a significant risk factor for postpartum hemorrhage (PPH), contributing to increased maternal morbidity and mortality globally. Establishing a reliable risk assessment model for PPH could facilitate timely identification and intervention, thereby improving maternal outcomes. This study aimed to develop an effective nomogram for predicting PPH in twin pregnancies undergoing CS.
METHODS: This retrospective study analyzed data from 1704 women with twin pregnancies who delivered by CS between 2016 and 2022 at the Second Affiliated Hospital of Wenzhou Medical University, China. To identify risk factors for PPH after CS in twin pregnancies, univariate analysis and LASSO (least absolute shrinkage and selection operator) regression were employed. A nomogram was subsequently developed based on the results of binary logistic regression analysis and the Akaike information criterion (AIC). Model validation was performed using bootstrap resampling, with performance assessed through discrimination (receiver operating characteristic curve), calibration (calibration plot and Hosmer-Lemeshow test), and clinical utility (decision cur analysis, DCA).
RESULTS: The nomogram for PPH was created using eight best predictor variables, namely, parity, assisted reproductive technology (ART), preeclampsia (PE), placenta previa, placenta accreta, anemia, the sum of the neonatal birthweight, and general anesthesia, which were all independent risk factors for PPH after CS in twin pregnancies. The nomogram demonstrated strong discrimination and calibration performance, with robust clinical utility as evidenced by area under the curve (AUC) analysis and DCA. Internal verification confirmed the consistency between predicted and actual values.
CONCLUSIONS: Parity, the use of ART, PE, placenta previa, placenta accreta, degree of prenatal anemia, total neonatal birthweight, and the use of general anesthesia are significant risk factors affecting the incidence of postpartum hemorrhage after CS in patients. The prediction model based on the above factors provides an accurate tool for assessing PPH risk, offering potential to guide clinical decision-making and further reduce maternal mortality.

articles.title: From cancer prevention to survivorship: Comprehensive menopause management after risk-reducing salpingo-oophorectomy.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.authors: da Silva Filho AL, Grandi G, Lopes TL et al.
articles.abstract: Risk-reducing salpingo-oophorectomy (RRSO) is the cornerstone of ovarian cancer prevention for women with hereditary cancer predisposition syndromes. When performed before natural menopause, however, RRSO induces immediate surgical menopause, with vasomotor symptoms, sexual dysfunction, accelerated bone loss, and potential long-term cardiometabolic consequences. For eligible women, menopausal hormone therapy (MHT) is the most effective treatment for vasomotor symptoms and prevents estrogen-deficiency bone loss. MHT should not be prescribed solely to prevent cardiovascular disease, and cardiometabolic risk requires standard preventive care. Concerns about breast cancer risk nevertheless limit its use. Recent observational evidence in BRCA1/2 pathogenic variant carriers found that estrogen-only MHT was associated with a lower breast cancer incidence in one prospective matched analysis, whereas combined estrogen-progestogen therapy was not statistically associated with increased risk; residual confounding and limited treatment duration preclude causal conclusions. For women with a personal history of hormone receptor-positive breast cancer, systemic MHT remains generally contraindicated, and non-hormonal options, including neurokinin receptor antagonists, selected antidepressants, gabapentin, and cognitive behavioral therapy, can reduce symptom burden. Genitourinary syndrome of menopause and sexual dysfunction require proactive, multidimensional management. This narrative review synthesizes international guidance, cohort studies, trials, and systematic reviews to provide a practical framework for preoperative counseling and long-term survivorship care after risk-reducing gynecologic surgery.

articles.title: Postpartum uterine artery Pulsatility Index as a predictor of retained products of conception - A prospective blinded study.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.authors: Bason Elkabaz HA, Nathan N, Simon N et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Postpartum retained products of conception (RPOC) are a major health concern. The aim of our study was to assess whether a single postpartum measurement of uterine artery blood flow can predict postpartum RPOC.
METHODS: As part of our routine practice, parturients considered at risk for RPOC underwent a series of sequential ultrasounds followed by hysteroscopy if needed. In this study, we measured uterine artery Pulsatility Index (PI) bilaterally at day 1-3 postpartum. Both the patients and the clinical team were blinded to the Doppler measurements. Cases in which RPOC was identified in hysteroscopy were compared with cases in which RPOC was ruled out.
RESULTS: Minimal uterine PI was strongly associated with RPOC (median PI 0.78 [interquartile range 0.69-0.85] vs. 1.19 [interquartile range 0.88-1.4], P = 0.004). Receiver operating characteristic analysis demonstrated an area under the curve of 0.837 (95% confidence interval 0.731-0.942). Minimal uterine artery PI was the best predictor of RPOC. A uterine PI value <0.95 had a sensitivity of 100% and specificity of 68.3% in predicting RPOC.
CONCLUSIONS: Low uterine artery PI, when measured in the first days after delivery, is the best single-parameter predictor of RPOC.

articles.title: Knowledge-access-outcome gap in sexual and reproductive health among adolescents with disabilities in sub-Saharan Africa: A scoping review with framework synthesis.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.authors: Afakorzi SH, Kumah A, Asante AO
articles.abstract: The aim of this review is to synthesize and map existing evidence on sexual and reproductive health (SRH) knowledge, behaviors, and service access among adolescents with disabilities in low- and middle-income countries, with particular focus on sub-Saharan Africa, and to examine the gap between knowledge, contraceptive access and health outcomes. Following the Arksey and O'Malley framework and the refinements by Levac and others, and reported per PRISMA-ScR guidelines, six databases were searched (MEDLINE/PubMed, EMBASE, Global Health, CINAHL, PsycINFO, Google Scholar) plus gray literature from WHO, UNFPA and UNICEF. Studies published between 2000 and 2024 reporting original SRH data on adolescents with disabilities aged 10-24 years were eligible. Data were synthesized using framework synthesis anchored to the knowledge-access-outcome gap framework. Forty-three studies met the inclusion criteria. A central paradox emerged where 60%-70% of adolescents with disabilities demonstrated good SRH knowledge, yet contraceptive access remained critically low and unsafe sexual practices were prevalent. Three barrier clusters were identified as individual-level (stigma, shame, communication barriers), institutional-level (non-inclusive facilities, inadequate teacher training), and structural-level barriers (poverty, discriminatory policies, provider attitudes). Adolescents with visual impairments consistently demonstrated superior knowledge, and coercive sexual experiences were disproportionately reported among females. SRH knowledge alone is insufficient without concurrent improvements in access infrastructure. Urgent action is needed from WHO, Ghana Health Service, and analogous bodies, encompassing disability-inclusive curricula, disability-competent provider training and removal of structural contraceptive barriers. Future research should prioritize longitudinal and participatory methodologies.

articles.title: Hormone Replacement Therapy and Cerebral Hemodynamics in Postmenopausal Women: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.authors: Vetter E, Vittalam K, Winter S et al.
articles.abstract: Background: Hormone replacement therapy (HRT) has well-established effects on systemic vascular function in postmenopausal women, but its effects on cerebral hemodynamics remain poorly understood. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the effects of HRT on ultrasound-based measures of cerebral hemodynamics. We hypothesized that HRT would be associated with reduced pulsatility index (PI), with stronger effects for estrogen-only formulations. Methods: Embase, PubMed, Web of Science, and CENTRAL were searched following PRISMA guidelines (January 25, 2026). Studies reporting PI, resistive index (RI), and cerebral blood velocity (CBV) in postmenopausal women using HRT were included. Risk of bias was assessed using validated tools. Multilevel meta-analytic models using restricted maximum likelihood accounted for dependency among effect sizes. Separate models examined between-group and within-individual comparisons. Moderator analyses examined hormone formulation and administration route. Results: Thirty-eight studies (27 meta-analyzed) were included. HRT was associated with lower PI versus controls, with a pooled mean difference of -0.051, 95% CI [-0.089, -0.012], p=0.009, k=31. Within-individual analyses demonstrated a reduction in PI over time, with a pooled mean change of -0.049, 95% CI [-0.081, -0.015], p=0.004, k=55. RI and CBV were not significantly altered (RI: p=0.74, CBV: p=0.54). Estrogen-only regimens were associated with greater reductions in PI than estrogen plus progestin or tibolone, while route of administration demonstrated no consistent effects. Between-study heterogeneity was substantial. Discussion: HRT was associated with reduced cerebrovascular pulsatility, suggesting a physiological effect on cerebral circulation. However, substantial heterogeneity across studies limits conclusions regarding factors that may modify this response.

articles.title: Pain Characterization: Presentation Patterns, and Multidimensional Assessment in Women with Advanced Gynecologic Cancer in a Palliative Care Service.
articles.authors: Allende-Pérez S, Domínguez-Ocadio G, Dávila JNS et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pain in advanced cancer is a complex and multidimensional phenomenon extending beyond intensity to include biological, psychological, and social components. In women with advanced gynecologic malignancies, pain is highly prevalent yet often undercharacterized, particularly in resource-limited settings where disparities in access and delayed integration of palliative care may influence its presentation and management.
OBJECTIVE: To characterize multidimensional pain features and identify distinct descriptive pain patterns in women with advanced gynecologic cancer receiving palliative care.
DESIGN: Observational study.
SETTING/SUBJECTS: Electronic medical records of women aged ≥18 years with advanced gynecologic cancer and documented pain, treated at a tertiary cancer center in Mexico between 2013 and 2023, were reviewed.
MEASUREMENTS: Sociodemographic and clinical variables were collected. Pain assessment included location, intensity, time of onset, and characteristics (somatic, visceral, neuropathic, or mixed). Psychosocial factors, including anxiety and depression, were also evaluated. Descriptive statistics were used to explore multidimensional pain patterns.
RESULTS: A total of 1,015 women were included (median age 56 years; most had≤12 years of education). Cervical and ovarian cancers predominated (43.4% and 32.3%). Pain was mainly pelvic or abdominal (81.0%) and commonly mixed visceral/neuropathic. Median intensity was moderate (4/10), with higher intensity in uterine sarcoma (median 7/10). Nearly half of patients presented anxiety or depression.
CONCLUSIONS: Pain in advanced gynecologic cancer is heterogeneous and multidimensional, with identifiable tumor-type-specific pain patterns that may inform individualized, patient-centered management strategies, particularly in resource-limited settings.

articles.title: Digital subtraction angiography-guided spermatic vein embolization plus sclerosis and microsurgical varicocelectomy in the treatment of varicocele: a comparative study with propensity score matching.
articles.journal: Quantitative imaging in medicine and surgery
articles.authors: Zhang J, Tian J, Cheng C et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Varicocele (VC) adversely affects spermatogenesis and is a recognized contributor to male infertility. This study aimed to compare the safety, efficacy, and clinical value of spermatic vein embolization plus sclerosis guided by digital subtraction angiography (DSA) vs. microsurgical varicocelectomy.
METHODS: This retrospective study included 181 patients with VC who were treated from January 2021 to December 2024. After propensity score matching (PSM) at a 1:2 ratio, 38 interventional and 76 surgical patients were included. The interventional group underwent embolization plus sclerosis guided by DSA under local anesthesia; the surgical group received microsurgical subinguinal varicocelectomy under general anesthesia. Postoperative outcomes and semen parameters were compared with a minimum follow-up of 12 months.
RESULTS: The interventional group had a significantly shorter procedure duration (52.11±16.97 vs. 67.89±27.91 min, P=0.0003), earlier ambulation [0.47 (0.32, 0.81) vs. 25.06 (24.48, 25.73) h, P<0.001], and shorter hospital stay [2.00 (2.00, 3.75) vs. 3.00 (2.00, 5.00) days, P=0.0173]. Pain relief rates were similar (94.73% vs. 93.42%, P>0.99). The complication rate was numerically lower in the interventional group but did not differ significantly [13.16% (5/38) vs. 28.95% (22/76), P=0.084], with no Clavien-Dindo grade III or higher complications in either group. At 1-year follow-up, both groups showed significant improvements in all semen parameters (all P<0.001), with no significant between-group differences in the degree of improvement (all P>0.05).
CONCLUSIONS: Spermatic vein embolization plus sclerosis guided by DSA may be a safe and effective alternative to microsurgical varicocelectomy, offering faster recovery and comparable semen parameter improvement, particularly for young infertile patients and day-surgery settings, pending further validation.

articles.title: Development and external clinical validation of a histology-inclusive prognostic nomogram for vulvar cancer based on the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results database.
articles.authors: Ke H, Xie N, Wu Q et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Vulvar carcinoma is a rare gynecological malignancy with rising incidence and suboptimal survival outcomes. Most existing prognostic nomograms for vulvar cancer are restricted to squamous-cell histology and lack cross-ethnic external validation, which creates an unmet clinical need for risk-stratification tools covering diverse histological subtypes. The Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER) registry provides large-scale population-based real-world clinicopathological and survival data across multiple histologic subtypes, making it suitable for deriving a new prognostic model. This study sought to develop and internally- and externally-validate a histology-inclusive prognostic nomogram for overall survival (OS) in patients with vulvar cancer.
METHODS: Patients diagnosed with invasive vulvar carcinoma between 2010-2022 were abstracted from the SEER registry. Eligible subjects were aged ≥18 years with pathological confirmation, complete survival follow-up, and non-missing key candidate predictors. Patients with synchronous primary malignancies were excluded. Variables encompassed age, histological subtype, grade, tumor size, International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics (FIGO) stage, surgery, chemotherapy, radiotherapy. The SEER cohort was randomly split at a 7:3 ratio into training (n=3,555) and internal-validation (n=1,524) datasets. An independent cohort (n=144) from Fujian Provincial Cancer Hospital served for external validation. OS was defined as time from pathological diagnosis to all-cause death or last follow-up contact. Survival information was obtained from registry linkage for SEER and from hospital medical records plus telephone follow-up for the external cohort. Cox proportional hazards modeling identified independent prognostic determinants, which were integrated into a nomogram. Model discrimination was assessed via Harrell's concordance index (C-index) and time-dependent area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC); calibration was evaluated graphically; clinical utility was evaluated by decision curve analysis (DCA). A risk-stratification system was derived from the prognostic index (PI).
RESULTS: A total of 5,079 SEER patients (training cohort: n=3,555, events =1,378; internal-validation cohort: n=1,524, events =573) and 144 external-validation patients (events =40) were analyzed. Baseline characteristics of the three cohorts were summarized. Neither histological subtype nor adjuvant…

articles.title: Breast Cancer and Diabetes Mellitus: Epidemiology, Pathophysiology, and Clinical Outcomes.
articles.authors: Saeed H, Habib R, Arnold E et al.
articles.abstract: Breast cancer and diabetes mellitus frequently coexist and share metabolic risk factors, with important implications for cancer risk, treatment, and survivorship. This review synthesizes epidemiologic, mechanistic, and clinical evidence, focusing on type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), the subtype most consistently associated with breast cancer. Meta-analyses indicate that women with T2DM have a 20%-27% higher breast cancer risk than women without diabetes, particularly after menopause (RR 1.20, 95% CI 1.12-1.28; SRR 1.27, 95% CI 1.16-1.39). Potential mechanisms include hyperinsulinemia, insulin-like growth factor-1 signaling, inflammation, obesity-related metabolic dysfunction, and altered sex hormone metabolism. Among patients with breast cancer, diabetes is associated with more advanced disease at diagnosis, increased treatment-related toxicity, and infectious complications. Meta-analyses also demonstrate higher all-cause mortality among patients with diabetes (HR 1.49, 95% CI 1.35-1.65; adjusted HR 1.51, 95% CI 1.34-1.70). Conversely, breast cancer survivors face a modestly elevated risk of developing T2DM, particularly following endocrine therapy or chemotherapy. These bidirectional associations support integrating metabolic assessment and diabetes management into oncology care. Future research should prioritize prospective subtype-specific studies, standardized glucose monitoring during systemic therapy, trials of integrated care, and evaluation of newer antidiabetic agents. These priorities may clarify causality and guide evidence-based interventions across the cancer care continuum.

articles.title: Sociodemographic factors and delays in care for gestational trophoblastic neoplasia.
articles.authors: Markert T, Peek EEH, Broadwater G et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Delays in care are associated with worse outcomes for patients with the most common gynecologic cancers, however, there is a paucity of research about health care access and gestational trophoblastic neoplasia (GTN) outcomes.
METHODS: This was a retrospective cohort study at a single academic institution of patients with gestational trophoblastic neoplasia diagnosed between 2000 and 2025. Aspects of care and management of GTN were compared across racial, ethnic, insurance, and geographic cohorts. Continuous data were summarized using median and interquartile range, and comparisons between groups were made using Wilcoxon rank sum, Kruskal Wallis, or chi-square tests.
RESULTS: Patients with public assistance insurance were more likely than patients with private insurance to present to the ED as their site of first contact for GTN care (p = 0.02). Non-White patients had a longer duration between initial GTN suspicion and initiation of GTN treatment than White patients (31 vs 13 days, p = 0.01). Hispanic patients had fewer days between first contact with the health care system to initiation of GTN treatment (30 vs 55 days, p = 0.04) and first imaging/labs concerning for GTN to treatment compared to non-Hispanic patients (10 vs 21 days, p = 0.04). There were no differences in GTN care and management when comparing patients who lived in counties local to or distant from the current institution.
CONCLUSIONS: Our findings suggest that disparities in access to GTN care may exist for non-White patients and patients with insurance through public assistance programs, however, Hispanic patients in our study more quickly initiated GTN treatment.

articles.title: Clinicopathologic features and prognosis of human papillomavirus-negative cervical cancer: a single-center analysis of 33 cases.
articles.authors: Du X, Li H, Zhang G
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cervical cancer is the fourth most common malignant tumor among women worldwide, with a high incidence and relatively high mortality rate. Approximately 90% of cervical cancer cases can be attributed to human papillomavirus (HPV) infection; however, 3-8% of cases remain HPV-negative cervical cancer. Current research indicates that HPV-negative cervical cancer has a poorer prognosis than HPV-positive cases. Consequently, systematic and in-depth research on HPV-negative cervical cancer is of significant value. This study aimed to investigate the clinicopathologic features, treatment patterns, and prognostic factors of HPV-negative cervical cancer.
METHODS: Clinical data of 33 patients with HPV-negative cervical cancer treated at Peking University People's Hospital between November 2009 and November 2023 were retrospectively analyzed. Survival was analyzed using the Kaplan-Meier method and the Cox proportional hazards regression model.
RESULTS: Among the 33 patients, gastric-type adenocarcinoma was the predominant histologic subtype (72.7%, 24/33). Univariate analysis showed that depth of cervical stromal invasion (P=0.02), parametrial involvement (P=0.01), adnexal involvement (P=0.046), and lymph node metastasis (P=0.02) were risk factors for progression-free survival (PFS) [all P<0.05, hazard ratio (HR) >1]. Multivariate Cox regression confirmed that only depth of cervical invasion was an independent risk factor for PFS (HR =4.311, P=0.01). For overall survival (OS), univariate analysis identified preoperative carbohydrate antigen 19-9 (CA19-9), preoperative carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA), receipt of neoadjuvant therapy, and the International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics (FIGO) stage as prognostic factors (all P<0.05), whereas no independent risk factor for OS was identified on multivariate analysis. Subgroup analysis demonstrated that the gastric-type adenocarcinoma group had higher preoperative CA19-9 levels (P=0.03), deeper cervical invasion (P=0.001), and a characteristic hormone receptor [estrogen receptor (ER)/progesterone receptor (PR)]-negative phenotype (ER: P<0.001; PR: P=0.03), supporting its identity as a subtype with distinct biological behavior.
CONCLUSIONS: HPV-negative cervical cancer exhibits aggressive clinicopathologic features, and depth of cervical invasion is an independent risk factor for recurrence. Gastric-type adenocarcinoma displays distinct heterogeneity, characterized by elevated CA19-9, deep cervical…

articles.title: SLC12A4 promoter methylation in plasma cell-free DNA as a candidate biomarker for thyroid cancer.
articles.authors: Wu W, Wang Y, Qu Y et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Plasma cell-free DNA (cfDNA) methylation has emerged as a promising non-invasive approach for cancer detection; however, methylation biomarkers for thyroid carcinoma (THCA) remain insufficiently defined. This study aimed to identify THCA-associated DNA methylation alterations and evaluate their potential diagnostic value in plasma cfDNA.
METHODS: Publicly available Illumina HumanMethylation450K data from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) were used to identify hypermethylated differentially methylated positions (DMPs) in matched THCA and adjacent non-tumor tissues, and the identified DMPs were subsequently evaluated in the independent Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) dataset GSE97466. Promoter cytosine-phosphate-guanine (CpG) sites associated with survival were further screened using univariate Cox regression, followed by methylation-expression correlation analysis. The selected SLC12A4 promoter region (chr16:67997880-67998180) was evaluated by methyl-CpG binding domain sequencing (MBD-seq) in tissue and plasma samples. Exploratory plasma diagnostic analyses were performed in seven patients with papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC), together with control and non-THCA comparator samples.
RESULTS: A total of 1,963 hypermethylated DMPs were identified in the TCGA discovery cohort. Of these, 1,959 showed concordant hypermethylation in GSE97466, and 1,881 remained significant after multiple-testing correction (FDR<0.05). Five methylation site-gene pairs, including cg09117114-SLC12A4, showed significant inverse correlations between methylation and gene expression. MBD-seq showed increased SLC12A4 promoter methylation enrichment in THCA tissues, with a similar directional pattern observed in four of five matched tumor-adjacent pairs, and the methylation signal was detectable in plasma cfDNA. In the exploratory comparison of seven PTC plasma samples with 1,301 normal controls, the area under the curve (AUC) was 0.938 [95% confidence interval (CI): 0.879-0.997]. At the exploratory cut-off of 12.2093 fragments per kilobase of exon model per million mapped fragments (FPKM), sensitivity was 0.857 (95% CI: 0.421-0.996) and specificity was 0.925 (95% CI: 0.909-0.938). These estimates should be interpreted as exploratory and require confirmation in independent cohorts.
CONCLUSIONS: Increased methylation enrichment at the SLC12A4 promoter region was observed in THCA tissue and was detectable in plasma cfDNA. These findings support SLC12A4 promoter methylation as a…

articles.title: Causal diagram-derived phenotypes of urinary urgency and urgency incontinence: a matter of degree rather than distinct categories.
articles.authors: Jelovsek JE, Amundsen CL, Andreev VP et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: To identify phenotypes of urinary urgency (URG) and urgency incontinence (UUI) from expert causal knowledge summarized as directed acyclic graphs (DAGs), and to determine whether they are discrete classes or probabilistic positions on a continuum.
METHODS: DAGs representing clinical phenotypes were constructed from knowledge elicited from urologists and urogynecologists. Ninety LURN II participants served as phenotype anchors; the remaining 539 were assigned to the nearest centroid. Compactness was each participant's distance to their centroid relative to median between-centroid distance. Validity was the prognostic information phenotypes added for symptom severity at 3 and 12 months beyond baseline severity.
KEY FINDINGS AND LIMITATIONS: 629 participants (336 females, 293 males) were assigned to eight phenotypes: polyuria (n=265), nocturnal polyuria (n=129), metabolic (n=96), affective (n=41), bowel and bladder dysfunction (n=22), pelvic organ prolapse (n=19, females), UTI (n=4, females), and benign prostatic enlargement (n=53, males). Continuous position was more informative than categorical labels: adjusted for baseline severity, distances added 9-18% of new prognostic information beyond labels, labels only 3-9% beyond distances, across strata. No participant met the 0.20 compactness threshold (smallest ratio 0.73 in women, 0.68 in men); baseline severity alone remained more prognostic than the phenotypes.
CONCLUSIONS AND CLINICAL IMPLICATIONS: URG/UUI patients can be described by eight DAG-derived phenotypes, but these are probabilistic positions, not discrete classes. Continuous representations retained modestly more prognostic information than labels, though both added little beyond baseline severity. These phenotypes are interpretable but not yet suitable for clinical use.

articles.title: Targeting miR-506 in leiomyosarcoma therapy: simultaneous suppression of metastatic potential and potentiation of pirarubicin efficacy.
articles.authors: Li T, Xing R, Li F et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Extensive studies have established that miR-506 inhibits epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) in epithelial ovarian cancer by upregulating E-cadherin while suppressing vimentin and N-cadherin. Additionally, miR-506 has been shown to enhance the therapeutic response of serous ovarian cancer to cisplatin and olaparib via modulation of RAD51. However, the functional role of miR-506 in leiomyosarcoma (LMS) remains unexplored. This study aims to investigate the expression and functional role of miR-506 in soft tissue LMS, focusing on its clinical relevance and impact on tumor progression and chemosensitivity.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective study of 61 Chinese patients diagnosed with soft tissue LMS between January 2000 and December 2012. Survival outcomes were assessed using Kaplan-Meier analysis with log-rank tests for statistical comparison. Furthermore, in vitro functional assays were performed to elucidate the role of miR-506 in soft tissue LMS pathogenesis and its underlying mechanism in modulating chemosensitivity.
RESULTS: Our findings demonstrated significantly downregulated miR-506 expression in tumor tissues compared with normal controls, with higher miR-506 expression associated with improved overall survival (OS). In our cohort of 61 LMS patients, Kaplan-Meier analysis revealed that positive expression of N-cadherin and vimentin correlated with poorer clinical outcomes. Similarly, elevated expression of DNA repair proteins (RAD51, RAD52, ATM, and ATR) was associated with reduced OS. In vitro functional studies showed that miR-506 upregulated epithelial markers (E-cadherin and β-catenin) while suppressing mesenchymal markers (vimentin and N-cadherin), consequently inhibiting LMS cell proliferation, migration, and invasion. Moreover, miR-506 enhanced pirarubicin sensitivity by dual mechanisms: (I) By downregulating DNA damage homologous repair proteins (ATM, ATR, RAD51, and RAD52), and (II) modulating EMT via targeting EMT-associated regulatory protein Slug and mesenchymal marker vimentin.
CONCLUSIONS: Our study demonstrates that miR-506 induces mesenchymal-epithelial transition-like phenotypic changes in vitro and modulates homologous recombination repair pathways, effectively inhibiting LMS cell proliferation, migration, and invasion while enhancing chemosensitivity.

articles.title: The Challenge of Sexual Reproductive Health in Sierra Leone: Gendered Perceptions of Family Planning.
articles.authors: Arnfield B, Vu MJL, Ritzler S et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND/INTRODUCTION: In Sierra Leone, persistent challenges in sexual and reproductive health (SRH), including high maternal mortality, poor maternal health outcomes, and gender inequality, underscore the critical importance of family planning. Despite progress, with contraceptive use among married women rising from 8% (2008) to 21% (2019), barriers related to knowledge and cultural norms remain. This study explored the family-planning perceptions of mothers and fathers, using a short film as a discussion stimulus.
METHODS: We conducted 11 focus group discussions following the screening of a health-promotion short film. Participants included 35 mothers and 21 fathers from the Bombali District. Discussions were analyzed using thematic analysis to identify gender-based perspectives.
RESULTS: Mothers predominantly expressed positive views, emphasizing the benefits of family planning for self-advocacy and control, child well-being, and health. In contrast, fathers primarily focused on concerns about contraceptive side effects and the impact on partner relationships. A notable theme among fathers was criticism of providing family planning to adolescent girls, based on fears it would promote promiscuity.
CONCLUSIONS: The stark contrast in perspectives underscores the need for family-planning programs that are tailored to address gender-specific concerns and that promote constructive communication amongst couples. The film effectively elicited nuanced discussions, suggesting that narrative-based media are valuable tools for qualitative research and health promotion. These findings provide key insights for refining SRH interventions in Sierra Leone and similar contexts.

articles.title: Perioperative outcomes and tissue trauma after uncomplicated total hysterectomy for benign uterine disease: a retrospective study.
articles.authors: Terranova C, Stermasi A, Montera R et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hysterectomy is the most frequently performed non-obstetric gynecological surgery for benign disease, and the surgical route affects perioperative outcomes and recovery. While minimally invasive approaches reduce surgical morbidity, their relative effect on the systemic inflammatory response remains incompletely characterized, particularly when indication and case complexity are accounted for. We compared tissue trauma, operative data, and early postoperative outcomes after uncomplicated vaginal hysterectomy (VH), laparoscopic hysterectomy (LH), and abdominal hysterectomy (AH).
METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed women aged 25-80 years who underwent total hysterectomy for benign indications at our institution (2021-2024). Patients with malignant disease, chronic inflammatory conditions, prophylactic drains, or complicated postoperative courses were excluded. Primary endpoints were postoperative C-reactive protein (CRP) levels and white blood cell (WBC) and neutrophil (Neu) count trajectories over the first three postoperative days; secondary endpoints were hemoglobin drop, operative time, blood loss, bowel function recovery, and length of stay. Multivariable models adjusted for age, body mass index, American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) physical status, surgical indication, and previous abdominal surgery, with uterine weight assessed in a sensitivity analysis; trajectories were modelled with linear mixed-effects models, and the route effect was examined within a single-indication (fibromatosis) subgroup.
RESULTS: We included 281 patients (84 VH, 86 LH, 111 AH). AH and LH required longer operative times than VH, and AH was additionally associated with higher blood loss, delayed gastrointestinal recovery, and longer hospitalization. In unadjusted analyses AH showed the highest CRP at all three days and higher WBC and neutrophil counts on Days 1 and 2; the haematological differences were attenuated after adjustment, whereas the CRP elevation persisted. Because route, indication, and uterine size were strongly collinear, the route effect was examined within the fibromatosis subgroup, where AH remained independently associated with higher CRP than LH across all postoperative days.
CONCLUSIONS: After uncomplicated hysterectomy for benign disease, surgical route was independently associated with the postoperative systemic inflammatory response. AH carried a greater inflammatory burden and slower functional recovery, whereas VH and LH were…

articles.title: Prenatal Exposure to Per- and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances, Metabolic Signatures, and Intellectual Development in Preschoolers: A Birth Cohort Study.
articles.authors: Huang Y, Xie Y, Zheng R et al.
articles.abstract: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are ubiquitous pollutants with potential neurodevelopmental toxicity. However, epidemiological evidence on prenatal exposure to PFAS particularly emerging PFAS and PFAS isomers in relation to children's intellectual development remain limited. This study aimed to examine associations of prenatal exposure to a variety of PFAS, including legacy, emerging, and branched PFAS, with children's intellectual development, and to evaluate early metabolic pathway changes potentially linking prenatal PFAS exposure to these outcomes. In 1,062 mother-child pairs from a prospective cohort in Wuhan, we quantified 32 PFAS in cord sera and conducted metabolomic profiling of cord plasma. At 6 years of age, children's intellectual development was assessed using the Wechsler Preschool and Primary Scale of Intelligence-Fourth Edition, a standardized and clinically validated instrument capturing multiple intellectual domains. Generalized linear models (GLM) and weighted quantile sum regression models were used to assess the association of individual PFAS and PFAS mixtures with children's intellectual development. A metabolome-wide association study (MWAS) using GLM was conducted to examine associations between PFAS exposure, individual metabolites, and children's intellectual development. Then, the meet-in-the-middle framework was applied to evaluate metabolic signatures as potential intermediary biomarkers. After adjusting for confounders, each doubling in 3,4,5m-PFOS concentration was associated with a decreased Full Scale Intelligence Quotient (FSIQ) of 0.92 (95% CI = -1.68, -0.17) points, with similar associations observed for the Cognitive Proficiency Index (CPI), Processing Speed Index (PSI), and Working Memory Index (WMI). Similarly, each doubling in 6m-PFOS was associated with decreased scores of 1.22 (95% CI = -2.02, -0.42) for CPI, 1.05 (95% CI = -1.82, -0.27) for PSI, and 0.89 (95% CI = -1.76, -0.01) for WMI. Furthermore, significant mixture effects of multiple PFAS on CPI and WMI were observed, with 6m-PFOS and 3,4,5m-PFOS identified as the primary contributors, respectively. Metabolomic analyses revealed that prenatal PFAS exposure was linked to changes in lipid metabolism pathways, potential serving as candidate intermediary biomarkers in linkages between prenatal PFAS and childhood intellectual development. In conclusion, prenatal PFAS exposure, particularly to branched PFOS isomers, was associated with lower…

articles.title: Docosahexaenoic Acid and the Gut-Ovarian Axis: A Potential Protective Role Against Environmental Endocrine-Disrupting Chemical-Induced Female Reproductive Toxicity.
articles.authors: Zhao J, Song J, Li H et al.
articles.abstract: The global burden of female infertility is substantial and rising, with environmental endocrine-disrupting chemicals (EEDs) now recognized as important modifiable contributors. Bisphenol A (BPA), phthalates, and their analogues have been shown to impair folliculogenesis, steroidogenesis, oocyte quality, and endometrial receptivity. These toxicants also reshape the gut microbiota, damage intestinal barrier integrity, and promote metabolic endotoxemia, thereby amplifying systemic inflammation and endocrine perturbations. Docosahexaenoic acid (DHA), a long-chain n-3 polyunsaturated fatty acid, exerts anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and pro-resolving activities, and is increasingly recognized as a modulator of the gut microbial ecosystem. This review proposes that DHA may antagonize EED-induced female reproductive toxicity through a gut-ovarian axis, by (i) restoring microbial diversity and beneficial taxa, (ii) strengthening tight-junction integrity and reducing lipopolysaccharide translocation, (iii) blunting Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4)/nuclear factor-κB (NF-κB)-mediated inflammation, and (iv) directly protecting granulosa cells and oocytes against oxidative stress. The strongest available evidence comes from DHA-enriched phosphatidylserine, which attenuates BPA-induced intestinal injury via restoration of Akkermansia, Butyricicoccus, and Lachnospiraceae and inhibition of TLR4/NF-κB signaling. Translational data from polycystic ovary syndrome models and in vitro oocyte maturation studies further support an ovary-protective role of n-3 fatty acids.
