However, ovarian protection mediated by the gut microbiota remains unproven: the strongest available data derive from rodent models with intestinal rather than ovarian endpoints, and human evidence is largely limited to metabolic and inflammatory outcomes that cannot be equated with preserved follicles or improved fertility. Responses may also vary with genetic background. Future studies should integrate multi-omics of the gut microbiota, metabolome, bile acids, and ovarian transcriptome, and evaluate DHA formulation, dose, and timing in at-risk populations.

articles.title: Mixture of Plasticizer Chemicals and Child Intelligence: A Weight-of-Evidence and Meta-Analysis-Informed Bayesian Approach in a Cohort with Improved Exposure Assessment.
articles.authors: Mustieles V, Rolland M, Pérez-Cantero A et al.
articles.abstract: Early-life exposure to plasticizer chemicals can affect child neurodevelopment. However, accurately characterizing exposure to these short-lived chemicals remains challenging. To address knowledge gaps, we examined the association between prenatal and infant exposure to a plasticizer mixture and child intelligence quotient (IQ) in a cohort with improved exposure assessment, informing the statistical analysis using the existing toxicological and epidemiological evidence. This work included 380 mother-infant pairs from the SEPAGES study, a French new-generation population-based birth cohort recruited between 2014 and 2018. Sixteen phenols and phthalate metabolites were quantified in pools of multiple urine samples collected at four time points during pregnancy and infancy (up to 21/week). Children's IQ was assessed using the Wechsler Preschool and Primary Scale of Intelligence at age 3. A structured review of the toxicological and epidemiological evidence was conducted to prioritize the chemicals with the highest weight of evidence (WoE) to be analyzed as a mixture. Meta-analyses of the retrieved epidemiological studies were performed and used as priors in single-chemical Bayesian regression models. Of 1189 references screened, we retrieved data from 30 toxicological and 57 epidemiological studies supporting the prioritization of bisphenol A and S, diethylhexyl phthalate metabolites, monoethyl phthalate (MEP), mono-n-butyl phthalate (MnBP), and mono-isobutyl phthalate (MiBP). Each quartile increase in maternal third-trimester concentrations of the high-WoE plasticizer mixture was associated with decreased full-scale (β: -2.86; 95% Credibility Interval, CrI: -5.05, -0.91), visual-spatial (-2.79; 95% CrI: -5.39, -0.82) and verbal (-1.95; 95% CrI: -3.84, 0.00) child IQ scores. Bayesian single-chemical models informed by meta-analysis-based priors also found that third-trimester concentrations of four of the six prioritized chemicals (bisphenol A, MEP, MnBP, and MiBP) were associated with reduced IQ scores. This novel evidence-based framework increased the biological plausibility and external validity of results, supporting that pregnancy exposure to a mixture of common plasticizers affects child IQ and represents a public health concern. The findings underscore the need to protect fetuses and children from plastic-associated chemicals and regulate them by class.

articles.title: Prenatal Exposure to Ambient Heat and Autism in California, USA: A Distributed Lag Analysis of Weekly Gestational Windows.
articles.authors: O'Sharkey K, Martinez B, Mitra S et al.
articles.abstract: Extreme heat is an increasing environmental health concern, yet its role in neurodevelopmental outcomes remains incompletely understood. Pregnancy represents a period of heightened vulnerability to environmental stressors, and heat-related physiological disruptions may influence fetal brain development. We examined associations between prenatal heat exposure and autism in a large, population-based cohort in California. We analyzed 2,013,431 singleton births in California (2015-2019), including 37,083 autism cases identified through linkage with Department of Developmental Services records. Prenatal heat exposure was assessed using daily average heat index, maximum temperature (Tmax), and minimum temperature (Tmin), assigned based on the maternal residential location. Logistic regression models estimated associations for full pregnancy and predefined gestational windows, and distributed lag nonlinear models (DLNMs) were used to evaluate weekly exposures across gestation. Models were adjusted for sociodemographic factors and for PM2.5. A higher pregnancy-average heat index was associated with increased odds of autism (odds ratio per 10°F increase = 1.14; 95% CI: 1.12, 1.17), with comparable positive associations observed for Tmin, a proxy of nighttime heat exposure, whereas Tmax showed little evidence of association. Window-specific analyses showed elevated associations during early and late pregnancy, with attenuation during mid-gestation. DLNMs revealed a consistent U-shaped temporal pattern across gestation. Associations were similar by sex but varied by socioeconomic status, with stronger relative associations observed in higher SES groups. Findings were robust across sensitivity analyses, including adjustment for ozone and season. Prenatal heat exposure, particularly sustained and nighttime heat, was associated with increased odds of autism, with evidence supporting multiple windows of susceptibility during gestation and potential modification by population-level differences in baseline heat exposure and acclimatization.

articles.title: Supplementation with cartilage hydrolysate and rosehip peel extract in physically active adults: main outcomes and exploratory findings of a randomized, placebo-controlled study on knee discomfort.
articles.journal: Frontiers in sports and active living
articles.authors: Noah L, Suarez CG, Jacquot A et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Joint discomfort and pain during physical activity are frequent conditions in healthy adults, which can lead to mobility limitations, with multiple consequences on health and quality of life. This study aimed to evaluate the effects of a food supplement which combines cartilage hydrolysate and a rosehip extract on knee pain and discomfort in physically active healthy adults, examining subgroups according to sex and menopausal status.
METHODS: In this randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, 138 participants received either 4 capsules/day of Chondractiv™ Move (CM, containing 1200 mg/day of hydrolyzed chicken cartilage and 380 mg/day of Rosa canina extract) or a placebo (maltodextrin) for 8 weeks. Activity-related knee pain was assessed on a 0-10 eVAS following a standardized single-leg step-down test (SLSD) and analyzed via an ANCOVA. Activity-related knee pain experienced during or after daily activities (0-100 eVAS), daily life pain (ICOAP questionnaire), knee function (KOOS questionnaire), quality of life (SF-12 questionnaire) and range of motion were also assessed throughout the intervention period.
RESULTS: Participants (39.9% men, 39.1% pre-menopausal women [PreMW] and 21.0% post-menopausal women [PostMW]) with a mean age of 46.4 years and a mean BMI of 24.4 kg/m2, practiced 5.6 hours of exercise per week on average. Knee pain after SLSD significantly decreased (p < 0.0001) during the intervention in both arms in the entire population (CM: -2.2; placebo: -2.4), but with no significant difference between arms (delta -0.2 [95%CI -1.1; 0.7], p > 0.05). However, exploratory analyses in PostMW showed that the change from baseline tended to be greater with CM versus placebo (-3.4 versus -1.2; delta 2.2 [95%CI -0.2;4.7], p = 0.0712). Further exploration indicated a benefit of CM over placebo on knee pain experienced during daily activities (entire cohort; p = 0.0255) and after activity (PostMW only; p = 0.0421), and in the Sport and recreation dimension of the KOOS (PostMW; p = 0.0381). Quality of life and range of motion evolved favorably, but with no between-arm difference.
CONCLUSIONS: After eight weeks of supplementation, CM did not demonstrate superiority over placebo for the primary endpoint (pain after SLSD) but exploratory analyses indicated clinically meaningful improvements in postmenopausal women, particularly. These findings require confirmation in further large-scale studies.
CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION:…

articles.title: Clinical Profile, Indications, and Maternal Outcomes of Obstetric Intensive Care Unit (ICU) Admissions: A Retrospective Study With Emphasis on Critical Care Interventions.
articles.authors: Madhukar SC, Anilkumar Jayachithra K, Rajubhai Zakhara R et al.
articles.abstract: Background Maternal morbidity and mortality continue to pose considerable problems to global health systems, especially in developing countries like India. The monitoring of the number of patients admitted to obstetric intensive care units (ICU) is an important measure of the incidence of severe maternal morbidity and the quality of emergency obstetric care available to patients. Objective To improve maternal health care services, there must be an understanding of the clinical characteristics, reasons for admission, and outcomes of these patients. Methods  A retrospective observational study was conducted in the obstetric ICU of a tertiary care teaching hospital from January 2025 through December 2025. A total of 120 obstetric patients (pregnant women and women within 42 days postpartum) admitted to the ICU were included. Information regarding patients' demographic characteristics, obstetric profile, reasons for ICU admission, critical care interventions performed, and maternal outcomes was obtained from medical records. The collected data were analyzed using SPSS version 25.0 (IBM Corporation, Armonk, USA). Results A total of 120 obstetric patients were admitted to the intensive care unit. Hypertensive disorders were the most common indication for ICU admission (42; 35%), followed by obstetric hemorrhage (36; 30%) and sepsis (18; 15%). Blood transfusion was the most frequently provided critical care intervention (84; 70%), followed by mechanical ventilation (48; 40%), vasopressor support (30; 25%), and dialysis/renal replacement therapy (6; 5%). Overall, 102 (85%) patients recovered and were discharged, while 18 (15%) patients died. Delayed referral, multi-organ dysfunction, and requirement for mechanical ventilation were significantly associated with maternal mortality (all p < 0.001). Conclusion Hypertensive disorders and obstetric hemorrhage were the leading indications for obstetric ICU admission. Delayed referral, multi-organ dysfunction, and requirement for mechanical ventilation were significantly associated with maternal mortality. Timely referral and access to multidisciplinary critical care remain important in the management of critically ill obstetric patients.

articles.title: Robotic Versus Laparoscopic Surgery for Colorectal Endometriosis: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Comparative Observational Cohorts.
articles.authors: Shaikh Z, Shaikh MR
articles.abstract: This review compares perioperative and selected postoperative outcomes between robotic-assisted surgery and conventional laparoscopy in females undergoing surgical treatment for colorectal or rectosigmoid endometriosis. This systematic review and meta-analysis followed the PRISMA 2020 guidelines. PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, Scopus, Cumulative Index to Nursing and Allied Health Literature (CINAHL), and African Journals Online (AJOL) were searched from January 2020 to August 2026 for comparative observational studies evaluating robotic-assisted versus conventional laparoscopic surgery specifically for colorectal or rectosigmoid endometriosis. Manual bibliographic searches of the reference lists of relevant articles were also conducted to identify additional eligible studies. Studies involving general, superficial, ovarian, or deep endometriosis without separately identifiable colorectal disease were excluded. Study selection, data extraction, and risk-of-bias assessment were performed independently by two reviewers, with disagreements resolved by discussion. Risk of bias was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale (NOS), and random-effects meta-analysis was undertaken only for outcomes with sufficiently comparable and non-duplicated data. Eight comparative observational reports met the eligibility criteria. Across studies reporting operative duration, robotic-assisted surgery was generally associated with longer operative time than conventional laparoscopy, although the magnitude and statistical significance of this difference varied between cohorts. Estimated blood loss, overall postoperative complications, conversion to open surgery, and most other perioperative outcomes were broadly comparable between approaches. Length of hospital stay showed inconsistent findings across studies, while selected reports suggested possible differences in voiding dysfunction, reoperation, recurrence, postoperative opioid use, and other longer-term outcomes. Considerable clinical and methodological heterogeneity was present because of differences in colorectal lesion complexity, extent of bowel surgery, associated pelvic procedures, institutional experience, follow-up duration, and outcome definitions. Potential overlap between several reports from the same specialist centre was addressed at the outcome level to avoid duplicate contribution of participants to pooled estimates. Overall, robotic-assisted surgery appears to be a feasible alternative to conventional…

articles.title: Oxidative stress in varicocele-associated male infertility: clinical evidence map and assessment of translational gaps-a bibliometric review.
articles.authors: Zhang X, Cai B, Sun D et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Varicocele is a common and potentially reversible condition associated with male infertility. Oxidative stress has been widely implicated in varicocele-related testicular dysfunction and impaired sperm quality. However, the development of this research field and the translational maturity of the available clinical evidence have not been systematically characterized. This study aimed to map the research landscape of oxidative stress in varicocele-associated male infertility from 2015 to 2025 and to assess clinical evidence domains, outcome levels, and translational gaps.
METHODS: The Web of Science Core Collection was searched for the bibliometric analysis, which was conducted using VOSviewer and bibliometrix. PubMed, Embase, and Scopus were searched separately for human clinical and translational studies, while ClinicalTrials.gov was examined to characterize prospective research activity. Eligible studies were classified according to their primary evidence domain, highest centrally analyzed outcome level, and translational stage using prespecified criteria.
RESULTS: The bibliometric analysis included 414 publications and showed an overall increase in research output. Research themes expanded from conventional redox markers and semen parameters to sperm DNA damage, mitochondrial dysfunction, inflammation, molecular profiling, and treatment-response assessment. The revised clinical evidence map included 142 studies. Molecular biomarkers/omics represented the largest evidence domain (51, 35.9%), followed by oxidative stress/redox biomarkers (28, 19.7%) and sperm DNA fragmentation (SDF)/DNA fragmentation index (DFI)/sperm DNA damage (27, 19.0%). Regarding outcome levels, 42 studies (29.6%) focused on biochemical/molecular outcomes, 49 (34.5%) on semen/sperm functional outcomes, 40 (28.2%) on SDF/DNA integrity outcomes, and only 11 (7.7%) on pregnancy, assisted reproductive technology (ART), or other fertility-related outcomes. Translational-stage assessment identified 73 association studies (51.4%), whereas only 3 studies (2.1%) were classified as replication/validation studies, indicating limited independent confirmation.
CONCLUSIONS: Research on oxidative stress in varicocele-associated male infertility has expanded in scope, but the clinical evidence remains dominated by association studies and laboratory or surrogate endpoints. Independent validation and patient-important reproductive outcomes are still uncommon. Greater assay standardization,…

articles.title: Particulate matter inhalation induces male reproductive dysfunction comparable to renal failure: insights from a rat model.
articles.authors: Jeon BJ, Tae BS, Cha JJ et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Particulate matter (PM), particularly PM2.5, is a pervasive environmental pollutant capable of penetrating alveolar tissues and causing systemic effects. Although its detrimental impact on the respiratory and cardiovascular systems is well documented, its effects on male reproductive function remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to investigate whether inhalation exposure to PM2.5 induces male reproductive dysfunction and to compare these alterations with those observed in renal insufficiency (RI), a systemic condition known to impair reproductive health.
METHODS: Male rats were divided into three groups: control, PM2.5 exposure (30 mg/kg/day, 3 h/day for 10 days), and RI induced by unilateral ureteral obstruction. Sperm parameters, including count, motility, and morphology, were evaluated. Testicular tissues were examined using angiotensin-converting enzyme 2 (ACE2) immunohistochemical (IHC) staining to assess alterations in the testicular renin-angiotensin system and quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction (PCR) to measure inflammatory and endothelial-related gene expression.
RESULTS: Exposure to PM2.5 resulted in a significant increase in sperm abnormalities, whereas sperm count and motility did not reach statistical significance. IHC analysis revealed altered ACE2 expression patterns in PM2.5 group, which partially overlapped with those observed in the RI group. Gene expression analyses indicated upregulation of inflammatory and endothelial activation markers in both the PM2.5 and RI groups.
CONCLUSIONS: PM inhalation induces measurable male reproductive dysfunction characterized by increased sperm abnormalities and molecular alterations in testicular tissues. The partially overlapping injury patterns between PM exposure and RI suggest shared oxidative and inflammatory stress-related mechanisms. These findings highlight the vulnerability of the male reproductive system to environmental toxicants and support consideration of PM exposure as a potential contributor to male reproductive impairment.

articles.title: Maternal iron deficiency, preterm birth, and disrupted microbial inheritance: a proposed double-hit hypothesis.
articles.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
articles.authors: Khan FZA, Ali SA
articles.abstract: The maternal microbiome is the infant's primary microbial inheritance, transmitted mainly through the maternal gut, vaginal delivery, breast milk, and skin-to-skin contact. Maternal iron deficiency (ID), with anemia, is a common and modifiable nutritional condition associated with impaired immune function and increased preterm birth (PTB) risk, whereas evidence for ID without anemia remains limited. It may influence maternal microbial ecology; however, its potential effect on maternal-to-infant microbial transmission remains unexplored. This review, conducted across PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science (January 2000-June 2026), proposes a double-hit hypothesis defined by the source and biological context of disruption rather than by a strictly temporal sequence. The first hit comprises potentially altered maternal-origin microbial and immunologic inputs from the vaginal, gut, and breast milk ecosystems; the second hit comprises PTB and neonatal intensive care (NICU)-associated disruption of early microbial succession. Human evidence directly linking ID to vaginal dysbiosis is limited to a single study, evidence relating maternal iron status to milk lactoferrin is inconsistent, and the contribution of vaginal communities to persistent infant gut colonization remains uncertain whereas vaginal exposure may have transient ecological or immunologic effects. No study has simultaneously evaluated maternal iron biomarkers, vaginal community state type (CST), breast milk composition, maternal gut microbiome and longitudinal infant gut microbiota. The proposed framework is therefore hypothesis-generating and identifies testable pathways through which maternal ID may alter maternal microbial and immunologic inputs, while also being associated with an increased risk of PTB. PTB, together with the resulting prematurity-related vulnerability and subsequent postnatal exposures, may further disrupt early infant microbiome development.

articles.title: The therapeutic role of gonadotropins in male factor infertility-a narrative review.
articles.authors: Patel M, Serage A, Al Dehneen H et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: A male factor is contributory in up to 50% of infertility cases, with a rising global prevalence. Gonadotropins are the principal endocrine effectors of the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal (HPG) axis, driving spermatogenesis via luteinising hormone (LH)-mediated Leydig cell testosterone production and follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH)-mediated Sertoli cell support. Their therapeutic role spans hypogonadotropic hypogonadism (HH), iatrogenic gonadotropin suppression, idiopathic male infertility (iMFI), and non-obstructive azoospermia (NOA). Evidence strength varies considerably across these indications. This review aims to provide a comprehensive overview of the clinical evidence underpinning gonadotropin therapy across these aetiologies.
METHODS: A narrative review was conducted using PubMed, Embase and the Cochrane Library supplemented by the current European Association of Urology (EAU) and American Urological Association/American Society for Reproductive Medicine (AUA/ASRM) guidance, covering January 2000 to June 2026. Evidence was synthesised narratively.
KEY CONTENT AND FINDINGS: In HH, the indication is well established, with a recent systematic review and meta-analysis of 1,583 patients demonstrating a pooled spermatogenesis induction rate of 74% and an overall pregnancy rate of 52%. Sequential treatment commencing with human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG) monotherapy, followed by the addition of FSH where required, is endorsed by both the EAU [2026] and AUA/ASRM [2024] guidelines. Baseline testicular volume, serum inhibin B, and anti-Müllerian hormone have emerged as clinically useful predictors of treatment response. In iatrogenic HH arising from exogenous testosterone or anabolic steroid use, emerging evidence supports gonadotropin-mediated spermatogenic restoration, including in men who are unable or unwilling to discontinue androgen use. For iMFI, FSH therapy demonstrates a modest benefit, though heterogeneity in response attributable to FSH receptor (FSHR) mutations and histopathological subtype limits its routine application. In NOA, pre-operative gonadotropin stimulation prior to microsurgical testicular sperm extraction (mTESE) has shown variable outcomes, and the current available evidence remains insufficient to support a strong guideline recommendation. Gonadotropin therapy has a favourable safety profile with injection-site reaction and gynaecomastia the principal considerations.
CONCLUSIONS: Gonadotropin therapy…

articles.title: Time From Anaesthetic Start to Surgery Start in Hysteroscopy and Theatre List Overrun in Gynaecology: A Retrospective Observational Study.
articles.authors: Alhusban F, Al Ajlouni Y, Bashall A et al.
articles.abstract: Background We evaluated patient-level factors associated with the interval from anaesthetic start to surgery start in hysteroscopy and list-level factors associated with overrun in elective gynaecology lists. Methods This retrospective observational study used 2025 nursing pre-assessment and theatre timing records from two hospitals within one National Health Service (NHS) trust. Duration was analysed using a lognormal mixed model with a theatre-list random intercept, adjusting for recorded pre-assessment characteristics, session, site, and mixed-list status. Body mass index (BMI) was modelled using a four-knot restricted cubic spline. Adjusted mean differences were reported in minutes. Secondary analyses used mixed-effects logistic regression for intervals ≥22 minutes and multivariable logistic regression for list overrun, defined as last-patient departure after the scheduled finish. Sensitivity analyses examined untransformed duration and excluded all-day lists. Results Among 913 hysteroscopies, 890 cases across 491 theatre lists were included in adjusted analyses. BMI was nonlinearly associated with duration (overall p<0.001; nonlinearity p=0.007). Compared with BMI 30 kg/m², adjusted mean intervals were 1.42 minutes longer (95% confidence interval (CI) 0.46-2.43) at 40 kg/m² and 4.67 minutes longer (95% CI 2.56-6.90) at 50 kg/m². These contrasts were similar in sensitivity analyses. Among 611 gynaecology lists, 302 (49.4%) overran. Lists combining minor and major procedures had higher odds of overrun than lists containing only minor procedures (adjusted odds ratio (OR) 3.10; 95% CI 2.00-4.80). Afternoon lists had lower odds than morning lists (OR 0.23; 95% CI 0.15-0.34), while odds were higher at University Hospital Lewisham than Queen Elizabeth Hospital (OR 2.18; 95% CI 1.49-3.20). Lists in which at least half of minor cases had prolonged intervals also had higher odds of overrun (OR 1.52; 95% CI 1.04-2.23), but evidence for this association was less certain after excluding all-day lists (OR 1.40; 95% CI 0.92-2.11). Conclusions Higher BMI was associated with longer intervals from anaesthetic start to surgery start in hysteroscopy. Lists combining minor and major procedures had higher odds of overrun. Prospective studies should evaluate whether accounting for preparation requirements and list composition improves scheduling. These findings do not establish a BMI threshold or booking rule.

articles.title: Urinary adverse events after robotic vs. non-robotic radical prostatectomy in Medicare beneficiaries.
articles.authors: Carlisle MN, Li KD, Abbasi B et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Robot-assisted radical prostatectomy (RARP) has become the dominant surgical approach for localized prostate cancer (PCa), yet its comparative urinary adverse event (UAE) profile in the mature surgical era remains incompletely characterized. This study aimed to compare UAE profiles after RARP versus non-RARP in a U.S. Medicare cohort.
METHODS: We performed a retrospective cohort study using linked Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results-Medicare data, including beneficiaries aged ≥66 years who underwent radical prostatectomy from 2010 through 2018. We identified UAEs using validated definitions aligned with Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events and estimated adjusted hazard ratios (aHRs) with Cox regression. We assessed the proportional hazards assumption and estimated interval-specific aHRs and evaluated treatment selection with propensity score weighting and matching. We classified non-RARP cases by surgical approach and conducted sensitivity analyses excluding indeterminate approach cases, external beam radiation therapy recipients, or both. A secondary model used open RP as the reference category.
RESULTS: The cohort included 17,441 beneficiaries (median age 70; median follow-up 3.7 years) with 14,769 RARP and 2,672 non-RARP. UAE incidences were 7.7% for RARP versus 15.3% for non-RARP [aHR 0.50, 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.45-0.57]. This association was driven primarily by bladder outlet obstruction (BOO) (2.3% vs. 9.8%; aHR 0.28, 95% CI: 0.24-0.33), and ureteral obstruction (1.0% vs. 1.8%; aHR 0.61, 95% CI: 0.43-0.86). We observed no meaningful adjusted difference for urinary incontinence. The association was strongest in the first postoperative year (aHR 0.31, 95% CI: 0.26-0.36) and was not detectable beyond 3 years (aHR 0.96, 95% CI: 0.72-1.27); the BOO association followed the same pattern (aHR 0.25 to 0.54 across intervals). It was consistent across restricted-cohort, propensity score (all measured covariates balanced after weighting), and complete-case analyses (aHR range, 0.45-0.51), including the secondary approach model.
CONCLUSIONS: Among Medicare beneficiaries undergoing radical prostatectomy in the mature robotic era, RARP was associated with lower postoperative UAE risk, concentrated in the first postoperative year and driven by lower BOO rates rather than a broad difference across all urinary complications. Claims-based measures did not detect a difference in procedure-requiring incontinence, and…

articles.title: Testicular microcirculation dysfunction-induced Sertoli cell injury-exosome therapy as a novel restorative strategy: a narrative review.
articles.authors: Lin S, Chen J, Men B et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Testicular microcirculation disorders, arising from systemic or local factors, have increasingly been recognized for their detrimental impact on male reproductive health. Sertoli cells are essential for maintaining the spermatogenic microenvironment, constructing the blood-testis barrier, and supporting spermatogenic cell proliferation. Dysfunction of Sertoli cells is a major contributor to testicular dysfunction and male infertility. This review aims to elucidate how testicular microcirculation disorders impair Sertoli cell function and to explore the potential of exosome-based therapies in restoring Sertoli cell function.
METHODS: A narrative literature search of PubMed and Web of Science was conducted up to August 25, 2026, to identify relevant publications on testicular microcirculation, Sertoli cell dysfunction, and exosome-based therapeutic strategies. Selected articles were reviewed and synthesized narratively.
KEY CONTENT AND FINDINGS: Testicular microcirculation disorders impair Sertoli cell function primarily through oxidative stress, disruption of the internal microenvironment, and endocrine/paracrine imbalances. These pathological processes collectively damage male reproductive health. In recent years, exosome-based technologies have shown significant promise in restoring Sertoli cell function. Specifically, exosomes derived from Sertoli cells or mesenchymal stem cells can protect and enhance Sertoli cell function by mediating intercellular communication and delivering bioactive molecules.
CONCLUSIONS: This review provides an in-depth analysis of the mechanisms linking testicular microcirculation disorders to Sertoli cell dysfunction and highlights the therapeutic potential of exosome technologies. These findings offer new insights and approaches for the treatment and prevention of male reproductive impairment.

articles.title: HPV prevalence and genotype distribution in rare cervical adenocarcinoma subtypes: A 10-year retrospective cohort study from Brazil.
articles.authors: de Oliveira Vieira PD, de Albuquerque LZ, Nobre AB et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: This study aimed primarily to determine human papillomavirus prevalence and genotype distribution in rare cervical adenocarcinoma subtypes. Secondary objectives were to evaluate associations between human papillomavirus status, clinicopathological characteristics, and survival outcomes.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort included patients with rare cervical adenocarcinoma subtypes treated at the Brazilian National Cancer Institute between 2011 and 2021. Human papillomavirus deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) detection and genotyping were performed in histopathological samples.
RESULTS: Among 107 patients, the median age at diagnosis was 44.00 years (interquartile range 37.00, 52.50). Tumor samples from 88 patients were available for human papillomavirus DNA analysis, of which 78 (88.64%) were positive. Genotype 16 (69.23%) was the predominant genotype. Non-mucinous adenocarcinomas were associated with poorer overall survival (HR 4.77; 95% CI 1.78, 12.76), whereas human papillomavirus status was not significantly associated with survival outcomes.
CONCLUSION: Human papillomavirus DNA positivity was high among rare cervical adenocarcinoma subtypes. Mucinous variants had significantly better overall survival than non-mucinous subtypes. These findings should be interpreted cautiously given the retrospective, single-center design and small number of human papillomavirus-negative cases, which limited statistical power for survival comparisons.

articles.title: Spatiotemporal Epidemiology of Echinococcosis in an Oasis Ecosystem - Xinyuan County, Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region, China, 2004-2025.
articles.authors: Sali D, Yang H, Ding D et al.
articles.abstract:
WHAT IS ALREADY KNOWN ABOUT THIS TOPIC?: Echinococcosis is hyperendemic in China, but its spatiotemporal epidemiology within oasis ecosystems remains poorly understood.
WHAT IS ADDED BY THIS REPORT?: This study identified temporal uncertainty and spatial heterogeneity, and evidence of dual domestic and sylvatic transmission networks. The annual reported incidence (ARI) of cystic echinococcosis (CE) showed nominal associations with climatic and vegetation factors at lags of 7-8 years, consistent with livestock cycles, whereas the ARI of alveolar echinococcosis (AE) showed nominal associations at lags of 1-3 years, consistent with rodent population dynamics.
WHAT ARE THE IMPLICATIONS FOR PUBLIC HEALTH PRACTICE?: These findings support a tailored One Health strategy that distinguishes CE from AE. Aligning interventions with disease-specific ecological lag periods may improve precision and effectiveness of control in oasis regions.

articles.title: Exploring the Association Between Occupational Noise Exposure and Perimenopausal Syndrome Among Female Workers - Five Provinces, China, 2023-2024.
articles.authors: Kou Z, Jiang W, Li X et al.
articles.abstract:
WHAT IS ALREADY KNOWN ABOUT THIS TOPIC?: Occupational noise is a multisystem hazard that can damage women's reproductive health.
WHAT IS ADDED BY THIS REPORT?: This study revealed a high prevalence (53.3%) (1,205/2,262) of perimenopausal syndrome (PMS) among female workers. Noise exposure and PMS scores were significantly correlated, with both the 8-h equivalent sound level and cumulative noise exposure exhibiting linear dose-response relationships with the PMS scores.
WHAT ARE THE IMPLICATIONS FOR PUBLIC HEALTH PRACTICE?: Targeted intervention strategies are necessary to address PMS among noise-exposed female workers, including noise risk management, occupational health education, and psychological support. Incorporating perimenopausal health monitoring into routine occupational physical examinations for female workers is essential.

articles.title: Serum prolactin as a shared inflammation-associated signal across inflammatory breast conditions: a four-group comparative study with exploratory inflammatory breast cancer subtype analysis.
articles.authors: Chen W, Li M, Dong M et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Inflammatory breast cancer (IBC) and nonpuerperal mastitis (NPM) present with closely overlapping inflammatory breast signs yet require entirely different management. No previous study has reported on the serum prolactin (PRL) level in the context of IBC or compared the PRL level between IBC and NPM. This study aimed to characterize serum PRL in IBC relative to NPM, invasive ductal carcinoma, and healthy controls, and to determine whether PRL adds discriminative information beyond systemic inflammatory markers for distinguishing IBC from NPM.
METHODS: A single-center, retrospective, four-group comparison [healthy controls (HC): n=121; invasive ductal carcinoma (IDC): n=123; IBC: n=42; NPM: n=226; total: N=512] was conducted on consecutive patients evaluated between January 2022 and December 2025. Three prespecified contrasts (NPM vs. HC, IBC vs. IDC, and IBC vs. NPM) were analyzed via multivariable logistic regression adjusted for age, body mass index (BMI), and menopausal status. Within-group PRL-inflammation correlations were compared across groups via Fisher r-to-z transformation. A combined model consisting of log(PRL), log[C-reactive protein (CRP)], log(neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio) and age, was evaluated for IBC-NPM discrimination.
RESULTS: PRL was elevated in both inflammatory conditions [NPM vs. HC: adjusted odds ratio (OR) 3.88, 95% confidence interval (CI): 2.52-6.20; P<0.001; IBC vs. IDC: adjusted OR 4.03, 95% CI: 2.19-7.97, median PRL 342 vs. 208 mIU/L, P<0.001]-the first report of PRL elevation in patients with IBC. However, PRL could not discriminate IBC from NPM (adjusted OR 0.94; 95% CI: 0.31-2.97; P=0.91). A four-variable model discriminated IBC from NPM (apparent area under the curve [AUC] 0.895; optimism-corrected 0.879), but this was driven by CRP (OR 0.68, P=0.04) and age (OR 1.19, P<0.001), not PRL (P=0.62). In NPM, PRL correlated with interleukin (IL)-6, IL-1β, and tumor necrosis factor (TNF)-α (P<0.001; false-discovery rate [FDR] q<0.001); this coupling was not detectable in the IBC cytokine subset (n=31; Fisher r-to-z for IL-6: P=0.10). Within IBC, hyperprolactinemia (PRL >496 mIU/L; 13/42, 31%) appeared more frequent in luminal B human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2)+ and triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) (Monte Carlo P=0.03; post hoc Fisher OR 10.4, P=0.006), with no cases in luminal A (0/8) or HER2-enriched (0/4). However, with only 42 IBC patients and 13 hyperprolactinemic cases, statistical power is…

articles.title: Sex-Stratified Transcriptomic Analysis of Cord-Blood Endothelial Colony-Forming Cells from Pregnancies Complicated by Gestational Diabetes.
articles.authors: Adegbaju MS, Babayeju O, Morenikeji OB et al.
articles.abstract: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) and maternal obesity are intrauterine metabolic exposures associated with altered fetal development and increased cardiovascular risk later in life. Increasing evidence suggests that fetal responses to these exposures are sex-dependent; however, the regulatory mechanisms underlying sex-specific vascular programming remain poorly understood. Using purified neonatal endothelial colony-forming cells (ECFCs), a progenitor population of fetal vasculature, we performed a sex-stratified transcriptomic analysis of pregnant mothers classified as lean, overweight, or GDM. Differential expression, pathway enrichment, transcription factor activity inference, kinase network reconstruction, and connectivity mapping were integrated to characterize sex-dependent regulatory responses to maternal metabolic dysfunction. Male and female ECFCs exhibited markedly divergent transcriptomic responses to GDM. Correlation between male and female fold-change estimates was negligible (r = -0.01), and the female-specific signal was not detectable when sex was modeled as a covariate rather than as a stratifying variable. Female GDM-exposed ECFCs demonstrated coordinated enrichment of cell-cycle- and DNA replication-associated pathways together with recurrent prioritization of E2F-family regulators across multiple analytical approaches. In contrast, the male response was comparatively limited and was associated with distinct transcriptional changes, including AKT3-associated pathways. Notably, E2F1 transcript abundance remained relatively stable despite coordinated expression changes among E2F-associated target genes. Independent endothelial transcriptomic datasets, drawn from previously published findings rather than independent reanalysis, provided complementary biological context rather than direct validation, consistent with enrichment of E2F-associated programs in GDM-exposed ECFCs and greater transcriptional responsiveness in female endothelial cells reported elsewhere. These findings indicate that fetal sex is a major determinant of the endothelial progenitor response to maternal metabolic dysfunction and that biologically relevant signals may be obscured in pooled analyses. Our results support the existence of sex-dependent regulatory programs associated with fetal vascular responses to GDM and identify an E2F1-associated regulatory framework as a candidate mechanism warranting further investigation.

articles.title: Relationship Between Preoperative PET-CT SUVmax Values and Solid Component in Endometrioid Type Endometrial Cancer.
articles.authors: Guven I, Ulger G, Yildiz H et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate the relationship between preoperative PET-CT SUVmax values and tumor solid component ratio in endometrioid type endometrial cancer patients.
METHODS: This retrospective study included 53 patients with endometrioid type endometrial cancer who underwent surgery between January 2018 and January 2024. All patients had preoperative PET-CT imaging. Clinicopathological features, SUVmax values, and solid component ratios were analyzed. Statistical analysis included correlation analysis and ROC curve analysis.
RESULTS: The median SUVmax value was 22.0 (4.4-66.5) and median solid component ratio was 2.0% (1-99%). SUVmax values showed significant correlations with tumor grade (p = 0.012), myometrial invasion depth (p = 0.035), tumor size (p = 0.009), and LVSI status (p = 0.034). A significant positive correlation was found between SUVmax values and solid component ratio (r = 0.359, p = 0.008). ROC analysis revealed that SUVmax > 29 could predict Grade 3 tumors with 83.33% sensitivity and 81.25% specificity (AUC = 0.851).
CONCLUSIONS: Preoperative PET-CT SUVmax values correlate significantly with important prognostic factors including solid component ratio in endometrioid type endometrial cancer. These findings suggest that SUVmax could serve as a valuable biomarker for risk stratification and treatment planning.

articles.title: Genital microbial profile of repeat breeding in a Kangal sheep flock: a survey of ewes and rams under natural mating.
articles.authors: Takcı A, Moğulkoç MN, Kıvrak MB et al.
articles.abstract: Infertility in sheep remains a significant concern in modern livestock production, with non-pregnancy rates during the breeding season increasing considerably in recent decades. The present study was conducted in a Kangal sheep flock with a documented history of reproductive failure, characterised by consecutive estrous cycles without conception. A total of 905 multiparous Kangal ewes (3-6 years old) and 44 Kangal rams (4-6 years old), all with documented fertility records, were enrolled at the beginning of the breeding season. Before mating, all ewes underwent transrectal ultrasonographic examination and evaluation of vaginal discharge. Following this screening, 880 ewes with no ultrasonographic abnormalities and normal vaginal discharge were monitored throughout the breeding season. Of these, 171 ewes that failed to conceive after the first mating underwent a second mating cycle, resulting in 50 additional pregnancies. The remaining 121 non-pregnant ewes underwent a third mating, resulting in 36 additional pregnancies. Blood samples were subsequently collected from the 85 ewes that remained non-pregnant after three consecutive mating attempts. Of these, 21 tested seropositive for Coxiella burnetii and border disease virus (BDV) and were excluded from the study. Vaginal swabs were collected from 25 of the remaining 64 ewes that tested negative for Brucella spp., C. burnetii, and BDV. These animals were classified as repeat breeders or clinically affected animals (Group 2). An equal number of ewes ( n = 25  ) that tested negative for these pathogens and conceived after a single mating cycle were assigned to the healthy control group (Group 1). Preputial swabs were also collected from 15 breeding rams to evaluate the potential for venereal transmission. All swab samples were subjected to microbiological culture and polymerase chain reaction (PCR) analysis following DNA extraction. The targeted pathogens included Brucella spp., Mycoplasma spp., Chlamydophila spp., Campylobacter spp., Coxiella burnetii, Salmonella Abortusovis, Trueperella pyogenes, and Klebsiella pneumoniae. Although Mycoplasma spp., T. pyogenes, and Campylobacter spp. were detected in swab samples from both groups, the prevalence of Mycoplasma spp. (  p adj < 0.001  ) and Mycoplasma bovigenitalium ( p adj = 0.05  ) was significantly higher in Group 2 than in Group 1. The increased detection of these microorganisms in reproductively compromised ewes suggests a potential role in the aetiology…

articles.title: Health beliefs and parental responses to human papillomavirus vaccination in the Middle East: a theory-informed narrative synthesis guided by the health belief model.
articles.authors: Abuzoor A, Jabin MSR, Jonker C
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Human papillomavirus (HPV) is the most common sexually transmitted infection in women and the primary cause of cervical cancer (CC). HPV vaccination and screening programs have significantly reduced CC incidence and mortality worldwide, preventing up to 70% of HPV-related CC and 90% of genital warts. Developing effective vaccination strategies is therefore essential.
OBJECTIVES: This study systematically synthesizes the attitudes and health beliefs of Middle Eastern (ME) parents regarding HPV vaccination, examines parental vaccine uptake, and assesses uptake among their children.
METHODS: This systematic review followed PRISMA guidelines. PubMed/MEDLINE, Web of Science, CINAHL, and Google Scholar were searched for studies published between January 2006 and May 2025. Thirty-three studies were included. A theory-informed narrative synthesis of predominantly quantitative evidence was conducted, with deductive mapping of findings to the health belief model (HBM) constructs. The review protocol was registered in PROSPERO (CRD42025645551).
RESULTS: The review included 32 quantitative cross-sectional studies and one qualitative study, involving 18,170 participants. Findings were organized according to HBM constructs, including perceived susceptibility, severity, barriers, benefits, self-efficacy, and cues to action. Parents generally demonstrated limited knowledge of HPV and vaccination. Major barriers included safety concerns, cost, limited access, lack of healthcare provider recommendations, and insufficient information. Cultural and systemic factors were also associated with vaccine uptake.
CONCLUSION: HPV-related knowledge in ME countries remains insufficient and is frequently associated with vaccination attitudes and acceptance across the included studies. Improving uptake requires targeted educational interventions, healthcare provider engagement, public health campaigns, financial support, and policy-level initiatives. Strengthening awareness and addressing structural barriers are critical for enhancing vaccination acceptance. Self-efficacy, where directly reported, appeared to be associated with more favorable vaccine attitudes; however, direct evidence for parental self-efficacy as a distinct HBM construct was limited across the included studies and should not be overstated.
SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/myprospero/CRD42025645551.

articles.title: The development and validation of a questionnaire to assess female athletes' and coaches' knowledge about hormonal contraception.
articles.journal: Frontiers in sports and active living
articles.authors: Fischer K, Kirschbaum EM, Nikoleizig L et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: In this study, a hormonal contraception knowledge questionnaire (HCKQ) for female athletes and coaches was developed and validated.
METHODS: An initial 17-item questionnaire (Pre-HCKQ), including items adapted from existing tools and newly generated items, was piloted with 325 recreational female athletes and 46 coaches. The analysis of item difficulty index and item-total correlation resulted in a 10-item HCKQ, which included questions about the safety of hormonal contraceptive (HC) use, function and effects of different HCs, risk factors and side effects of HC use, and the fertile window in the menstrual cycle. Eighteen experts evaluated the HCKQ for relevance (M = 5.5, SD = 0.8) and clarity (M = 5.5, SD = 0.9) using a 6-point Likert scale.
RESULTS: The HCKQ was subsequently administered to 562 elite female athletes and 170 coaches. The mean difficulty index was 46%, and the mean item-total correlation was r = .29. A significant difference in knowledge scores was found between female athletes, female coaches, and male coaches, as well as between HC users and non-users. Reliability was assessed through internal consistency (Cronbach's α = .61, McDonald's ω = .62, Guttman's λ₂ = .63) and test-retest in a separate, mixed-sex cohort of 64 sport science students (Spearman's ρ = .75; ICC(2,1) = .74).
DISCUSSION: The HCKQ provides a brief tool for assessing HC-related knowledge in sports contexts, with initial evidence supporting its content validity, known-groups validity, and reliability. Future research may use the HCKQ to evaluate the effectiveness of female health education programs in sport.

articles.title: Correlation between coagulation abnormalities and in vitro fertilization outcomes in infertile patients with endometriosis: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.authors: Du X, Hu W, Fu C
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate coagulation function in infertile patients with endometriosis (EMs) undergoing IVF-ET and analyze its correlation with reproductive outcomes, providing evidence for perioperative optimization.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 216 infertile patients (108 with EMs, 108 age-matched tubal-factor controls) undergoing IVF-ET from 2022 to 2024. Only the first IVF cycle and first embryo transfer per patient were included in the primary analysis to ensure independence of observations. Coagulation parameters (PT, APTT, TT, FIB, D-dimer, AT-III) were measured before controlled ovarian hyperstimulation. Coagulation abnormality was defined as the presence of at least one of the following: FIB > 4.0 g/L, D-dimer > 0.5 mg/L, or AT-III < 75%. PT, APTT, and TT were analyzed as continuous variables because no validated consensus threshold exists for defining shortened PT/APTT/TT as a hypercoagulable state. Baseline characteristics, COH parameters, IVF outcomes, and confounders were compared. EMs patients were stratified by this coagulation abnormality definition. Hierarchical logistic regression was used to identify factors associated with live birth failure.
RESULTS: EMs patients showed significantly shortened PT/APTT/TT, elevated FIB and D-dimer, and decreased AT-III when these parameters were analyzed as continuous variables (all P < 0.05); however, PT/APTT/TT were not used to classify patients as having coagulation abnormality. Based on the composite definition including FIB, D-dimer, and AT-III, the incidence of coagulation abnormalities was 48.15% (52/108) in the EMs group versus 7.41% (8/108) in the control group (P < 0.001). Among EMs patients, those with coagulation abnormalities had lower high-quality embryo rate, implantation rate, and live birth rate, and higher early abortion rate (all P < 0.05). Live birth rates decreased progressively across 0, 1, 2, and 3 abnormal parameters among FIB, D-dimer, and AT-III (44.6%, 29.6%, 16.7%, and 0.0%, respectively; P-trend = 0.002). In fully adjusted models, elevated D-dimer (OR = 2.864, 95% CI: 1.427-5.748, P = 0.003) and decreased AT-III (OR = 0.512, 95% CI: 0.276-0.949, P = 0.034) were independently associated with live birth failure, while high-quality embryo rate was protective (OR = 0.326, 95% CI: 0.154-0.689, P = 0.003). After additional adjustment for high-quality embryo rate, the association between elevated D-dimer and live birth failure was attenuated but remained…

articles.title: Histone Deacetylase 3-Progesterone Receptor Cooperation Regulates Progesterone Responsiveness in the Uterus.
articles.authors: Yun S, Li R, Kim SL et al.
articles.abstract: Endometriosis affects a substantial proportion of women of reproductive age, with 30%-50% affected by infertility. A defining pathological feature is progesterone resistance resulting from impaired progesterone receptor (PGR) signaling, yet the underlying mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Here, we define conserved shared target genes of histone deacetylase 3 (HDAC3) and PGR in the mouse uterus using integrated transcriptomic and cistromic analyses, supported by uterine-specific Hdac3 and Pgr knockout mice. Co-immunoprecipitation and proximity ligation assays indicate that HDAC3 associates with PGR, with reciprocal attenuation of their expression in Hdac3- and Pgr-deficient uteri. Multiplex immunofluorescence demonstrates colocalization of HDAC3 and PGR in endometrial epithelial and stromal cells. HDAC3 and PGR expression levels show a positive correlation in stromal cells in both controls and infertile women with endometriosis, whereas this correlation in epithelial cells is selectively preserved in a subset of infertile cases. Chromatin profiling demonstrates extensive co-occupancy of HDAC3 and PGR at regulatory regions associated with progesterone-responsive genes. Together, these findings support a model in which HDAC3 functions as a coregulator of PGR-dependent transcription in the uterus and indicate that HDAC3-PGR cooperation is a key determinant of endometrial receptivity. This work provides mechanistic insight into progesterone resistance underlying endometriosis-associated infertility.

articles.title: Maternal serum retinol, vitamin K, and ferritin profiles during pregnancy, gestational diabetes mellitus, and offspring neurodevelopment: a prospective case-control study.
articles.authors: Jiang C, Pang Y, Yu J et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) is associated with adverse offspring neurodevelopment, but the role of maternal circulating biomarkers-specifically serum retinol, serum vitamin K, and serum ferritin-in relation to offspring neurodevelopmental performance remains unclear. This study examined trimester-specific levels of these biomarkers in GDM vs. participants without GDM and their associations with infant neurodevelopmental outcomes at 12 months.
METHODS: In this prospective case-control study, 240 mother-infant pairs who were enrolled during pregnancy, classified according to GDM status after OGTT screening, and followed through delivery and offspring assessment at 12 months. Maternal serum retinol, serum vitamin K, and serum ferritin were measured in each trimester. Offspring neurodevelopment was assessed using the Gesell Developmental Schedules, with suboptimal neurodevelopmental performance defined as Total Gesell Score < 85. Multivariable logistic regression models were adjusted for maternal age, pre-pregnancy BMI, years of formal education, gestational age at delivery, infant sex, and maternal HbA1c. Linear regression models included the same covariates together with maternal CRP and IL-6.
RESULTS: Participants with GDM had significantly lower serum retinol and serum vitamin K concentrations and higher serum ferritin concentrations across all trimesters compared with control participants (all p < 0.001). Offspring in the GDM group had lower Total Gesell Scores (90.4 vs. 95.9, p < 0.001) and higher prevalence of Total Gesell Score < 85 (72.5% vs. 31.7%, p < 0.001) compared with offspring in the control group. Although the mean differences were statistically significant, the group means remained within broadly similar interpretive ranges, and the < 85 threshold includes borderline scores. In fully adjusted logistic regression, higher serum ferritin was independently associated with increased odds of suboptimal neurodevelopmental performance (OR = 1.22 per 10 ng/mL, 95% CI: 1.004-1.34, p = 0.036), while vitamin A and K were not significant. An exploratory composite Nutritional Risk Score of 1, indicating the presence of any one of the three prespecified sample-specific quartile-defined biomarker categories (serum retinol in the lowest quartile, serum vitamin K in the lowest quartile, or serum ferritin in the highest quartile), was associated with a nearly five-fold higher odds of suboptimal neurodevelopmental performance (OR = 4.92, 95%…

articles.title: Evaluation of a postpartum cardiovascular risk clinic after hypertensive disorder of pregnancy: First-year experience.
articles.authors: Ait Ouarab D, Lefebvre J, Côté AM et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy increase future cardiovascular risk. The Clinique Santé Globale PostPartum (CSGPP) was created to assess risk, provide lifestyle counseling, and inform primary care providers. This study was meant to assess its relevance, efficacy, and women's satisfaction to optimize the clinic.
METHODS: This descriptive, single-center prospective cohort study was conducted at the Centre Hospitalier Universitaire de Sherbrooke. Women were recruited at their first CSGPP visit. Data on attendance, lifestyle behaviors, motivation, follow-up with primary care providers, and satisfaction were collected at baseline and 12 months postpartum.
RESULTS: Of 104 referrals, 84 women (80.8%) attended the first visit, 65 agreed to participate, and 47 completed follow-up. Belief in the health benefits of lifestyle changes increased (P = .007), and satisfaction with the clinic was high.
CONCLUSION: Given the high adherence and satisfaction with the clinic, these findings support expanding access to the clinic to all conditions increasing CVD in this young population.

articles.title: A protocol for vaginal wall-derived organoids from women with pelvic organ prolapse and benign controls: limited applicability to pathological uterosacral ligament tissues.
articles.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
articles.authors: Yu X, Wu S, Tao Q et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Pelvic organ prolapse (POP) significantly impairs women's quality of life; however, the lack of reliable in vitro human-derived models has hindered the elucidation of its pathogenesis and the development of targeted therapies. This study aims to establish a reproducible protocol for generating patient-derived organoids from human vaginal wall and uterosacral ligament (USL) tissues and to define the boundaries of applicability of this model for POP research.
METHODS: Vaginal wall and USL tissues were obtained from patients with POP (stage ≥ III, n = 3) and benign controls (n = 2). Each biological sample was tested in three independent technical replicates for two parallel culture approaches, including dissociated primary cells and digested tissue fragments. The tissues were processed and digested using a combination of collagenase II and DNase. Primary cells and digested tissue fragments were cultured in a three-dimensional (3D) Matrigel system with specialized organoid culture medium supplemented with growth factors, including Wnt3a, R-Spondin 1, and Noggin. Successful organoid formation was prospectively defined as the formation of discrete, three-dimensional spherical or cystic structures with a clearly visible border, sustained growth for at least 7 days under bright-field microscopy, and a diameter ≥100 µm. Organoid formation, growth, and morphology were monitored over time. Immunofluorescence staining was performed on the organoids generated from patients with POP to analyze their cell composition. KRT14 (epithelial), vimentin (fibroblast-related), α-SMA (myofibroblast/smooth muscle-related), VWF (endothelial), and SM22 (smooth muscle) were detected.
RESULTS: Under light microscopy, primary cells from benign control vaginal wall tissue formed organoids within the first week of culture. By Day 11, clear three-dimensional structures measuring approximately 100-500 μm in diameter were observed. In contrast, vaginal wall-derived organoids from patients with POP exhibited similar morphology but were fewer and less dense. When undigested tissue fragments were cultured for 48 h to form cell aggregates and then dispersed and reembedded in Matrigel, the organoid yield was significantly greater than that when the cultures were initiated with discrete primary cells alone, and organoid growth was maintained through the second passage. Both primary cells and tissue fragments from benign control USL generated organoids, whereas USL tissues from patients…

articles.title: Higher TSH within the normal range is independently associated with reduced IVF clinical pregnancy odds: a K-means cluster analysis challenging the binary cutoff paradigm.
articles.authors: Amin MM, Hassanein SI
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The impact of thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) variation within the normal reference range on IVF outcomes remains controversial, with prior studies yielding conflicting results.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of 878 euthyroid women (TSH 0.25-4.0 µIU/mL) undergoing fresh IVF/ICSI cycles at Al-Hayat Hospital, Iraq (2022-2024). Patients were classified into four groups using k-means clustering of serum TSH values: Cluster 1 (2.9-4.0 µIU/mL), Cluster 2 (2.2-2.8 µIU/mL), Cluster 3 (1.4-2.0 µIU/mL), and Cluster 4 (0.25-1.3 µIU/mL). Clinical, hormonal, and embryological parameters were compared across clusters, and stepwise logistic regression was performed to adjust for confounders.
RESULTS: Clinical pregnancy was achieved in 474/878 women (54%). As expected, women with pregnancy were younger (30.1 ± 5.1 vs. 31.2 ± 5.5 years, p = 0.003) and had lower mean TSH (1.95 ± 0.85 vs. 2.08 ± 0.96 µIU/mL, p = 0.030). Ovarian reserve and response markers were higher in the pregnancy group, including antral follicle count (AFC) (11.3 ± 4.2 vs. 10.4 ± 4.2, p = 0.001), preovulatory follicle count (PFC) (11.9 ± 4.2 vs. 11.0 ± 4.2, p = 0.003), and oocyte yield (10.4 ± 5.0 vs. 9.6 ± 4.8, p = 0.010). Oocyte maturation (80.5 ± 15.5% vs. 76.9 ± 17.1%, p = 0.003) and fertilization rates (88.0 ± 14.0% vs. 84.2 ± 16.9%, p = 0.003) were also significantly higher, while women without pregnancy required more ampoules (41.2 ± 18.8 vs. 36.6 ± 16.5, p < 0.001). Stepwise regression identified age (OR = 0.97, p = 0.059), ampoules (OR = 0.99, p = 0.024), oocyte yield (OR = 1.04, p = 0.014), maturation rate (OR = 1.10, p = 0.002), fertilization rate (OR = 1.06, p = 0.015), and TSH clusters as independent predictors. Cluster 3 (TSH 1.4-2.0 µIU/mL) showed the highest pregnancy rate (58.2%), while Cluster 1 (TSH 2.9-4.0 µIU/mL) had the lowest (42.7%) and was independently associated with reduced odds (OR = 0.53, 95% CI 0.35-0.80, p = 0.0024). Subgroup analysis revealed that unexplained and ovarian factor infertility were most sensitive to thyroid variation, whereas male factor infertility remained stable and PCO cases diverged.
CONCLUSIONS: K-means clustering revealed that women with higher-normal TSH (Cluster 1: 2.9-4.0 µIU/mL) had independently reduced odds of clinical pregnancy (OR = 0.53, 95% CI 0.35-0.80, p = 0.002) compared with Cluster 3 (1.4-2.0 µIU/mL), challenging the adequacy of a single binary cutoff and supporting individualized, data-driven thyroid…

articles.title: The Billings Ovulation Method and Catholic Women's Health Activism in 1970s and 1980s Ireland.
articles.journal: Social history of medicine : the journal of the Society for the Social History of Medicine
articles.authors: Kelly L
articles.abstract: This article explores the history of the Billings Method, a form of 'natural' family planning, in Ireland from its initial popularisation in the 1970s to the beginning of its decline in the late 1980s. Drawing on oral history interviews with women who taught the method in Ireland in this period, as well as previously unexplored archival sources, the article seeks to nuance understandings of conservative women's activism in this period. It argues that the Billings movement had much in common with the tenets of feminist health activism. However, promoters of the method ultimately failed to garner support from members of the Irish medical profession and Catholic Church hierarchy.

articles.title: Association between short birth intervals and childhood anemia severity in India: evidence from the fifth National Family Health Survey (NFHS-5).
articles.authors: Barik S, Show A, Sonune M
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Anemia affects 67.1% of Indian children aged 6-59 months. Short birth intervals (SBI) may exacerbate this burden through maternal nutritional depletion; however, empirical evidence linking SBI with specific levels of childhood anemia severity remains limited in India.
METHODS: We analyzed nationally representative, secondary cross-sectional data from the National Family Health Survey-5 (NFHS-5, 2019-21), comprising an unweighted analytical sample of 101,240 mother-child pairs with children aged 6-59 months. Survey-adjusted multinomial logistic regression was used to assess the association between SBI and anemia severity (mild, moderate, and severe). Adjusted odds ratios (aOR) were estimated after controlling for key child, maternal, household, and geographic characteristics.
RESULTS: Compared with non-short birth interval (NSBI), SBI was significantly associated with a higher odd of moderate anemia (aOR: 1.10; 95% CI: 1.05-1.15) and severe anemia (aOR: 1.18; 95% CI: 1.05-1.34), but not mild anemia. The highest burden of severe anemia was observed among children aged 6-23 months, those with birth weight <2,500 g, and those born to mothers with severe anemia. Children from Scheduled Caste/Scheduled Tribe (SC/ST) communities, and the West, North, Central and South regions had higher odds of severe anemia, whereas higher maternal education, greater household wealth, and residence in the Northeast were associated with a lower odd of anemia.
CONCLUSION: SBI is associated with a higher odd of moderate and severe anemia among children in India, potentially associated with maternal nutritional depletion and intersecting structural inequities. Addressing this public health burden requires integrated strategies that promote optimal birth spacing, strengthen family planning services, and provide targeted maternal nutrition interventions for marginalized populations, thereby supporting progress toward the Sustainable Development Goals.

articles.title: MALAT1 exacerbates immune dysregulation in gestational diabetes by modulating the miR-576-5p/HNRNPU axis: Implications for inflammatory pathogenesis.
articles.journal: Malawi medical journal : the journal of Medical Association of Malawi
articles.authors: Ding H, Zhao A, Chen X et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) is characterized by systemic immune dysregulation and chronic inflammation that contribute to insulin resistance and β-cell dysfunction. The long non-coding RNA metastasis-associated lung adenocarcinoma transcript 1 (MALAT1) has been implicated in several inflammatory disorders; however, its role in GDM-related immune and metabolic disturbances remains unclear.
METHODS: A mouse model of GDM and insulin-resistant trophoblast cells were used to evaluate MALAT1 expression and its effects on inflammatory cytokines and β-cell apoptosis. Gene expression was analyzed by qRT-PCR and Western blotting, while histological and biochemical assays assessed pancreatic morphology, serum glucose, and inflammatory cytokine levels. Functional and rescue experiments were performed to explore the molecular interaction between MALAT1, miR-576-5p, and HNRNPU.
RESULTS: MALAT1 expression was markedly elevated in GDM mice and insulin-resistant trophoblasts, correlating with increased levels of TNF-α, IL-1β, and IL-6, as well as enhanced β-cell apoptosis. Silencing MALAT1 alleviated hyperglycemia, preserved pancreatic islet structure, and reduced inflammatory mediator secretion. Mechanistically, MALAT1 acted as a competing endogenous RNA by sponging miR-576-5p to upregulate HNRNPU, thereby promoting NF-ϰB activation. HNRNPU overexpression reversed the anti-inflammatory and anti-apoptotic effects of MALAT1 knockdown.
CONCLUSION: MALAT1 promotes immune-metabolic dysfunction in GDM through the miR-576-5p/HNRNPU/NF-ϰB axis. Targeting this pathway may offer a novel therapeutic strategy for reducing inflammation-associated complications in GDM.

articles.title: The association of a healthy lifestyle index with risk of all-cause hospitalization and mortality in US postmenopausal women.
articles.authors: Peila R, Xue X, La Monte MJ et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: A healthy lifestyle-characterized by physical activity, non-smoking, healthy diet, no alcohol, adequate sleep, and normal body mass index-has been linked to reduced chronic and acute disease risk. However, its impact on hospitalizations and mortality in postmenopausal women remains unclear. This study evaluated the association between a composite Healthy Lifestyle Index (HLI) and risk of all-cause hospitalization and mortality.
METHODS: We analyzed 111,000 postmenopausal women aged 50-79 years at enrollment in the Women's Health Initiative (1993-1998, United States), followed for up to 30 years. HLI scores (range 0-24; higher = healthier) were derived from baseline lifestyle and anthropometric measures. Outcomes included first hospitalization, recurrent hospitalizations, and mortality. Cox regression estimated hazard ratios (HRs) and 95 % confidence intervals (CIs), excluding events within two years.
RESULTS: A total of 75,703 women were hospitalized and 35,530 died. During the first 10 years, each HLI-unit increase was associated with lower risk of first hospitalization (HR 0.95, 95 %CI 0.94, 0.95) and mortality (HR 0.93, 95 %CI 0.92, 0.93). Associations remained consistent beyond 10 years.
CONCLUSIONS: Healthier lifestyle patterns were associated with reduced hospitalization and mortality risk in postmenopausal women, which supports public health efforts to promote healthy behaviors in aging populations.

articles.title: Undergraduate nursing students' perceptions of human papillomavirus and its prevention: a qualitative study guided by the Health Belief Model.
articles.authors: Mohamed RA, Aloufi M, Dakhilallah H et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Human papillomavirus (HPV) is a significant public health concern and the leading cause of cervical cancer as well as several other malignancies. Despite its importance, there is limited qualitative evidence examining nursing students' perceptions of HPV and its prevention in Saudi Arabia. This study sought to investigate undergraduate nursing students' perceptions of HPV and its prevention using the Health Belief Model (HBM) as a theoretical framework.
METHODS: This descriptive qualitative study utilized six focus group discussions (FGDs) involving 36 eligible undergraduate nursing students from the University of Bisha, Saudi Arabia. Participants were recruited through purposive sampling. Thematic analysis was conducted based on the HBM, employing its six constructs as predefined overarching analytic domains, while specific subthemes were developed inductively from participants' accounts.
RESULTS: The six deductive themes, perceived susceptibility, perceived severity, perceived benefits, perceived barriers, cues to action, and self-efficacy, correspond to the HBM constructs. Inductively developed subthemes included inadequate understanding of HPV, low perceived personal susceptibility, misconceptions about vaccination safety and transmission, stigma, and challenges in discussing sensitive sexual health issues. Participants also described perceived institutional and educational influences on communication preparedness, professional relevance, and HPV knowledge. These findings do not demonstrate the efficacy of specific teaching methods but highlight educational needs within this sample.
CONCLUSIONS: Undergraduate nursing students identified knowledge gaps, misunderstandings, stigma, societal challenges, and a lack of confidence when discussing HPV prevention. The findings emphasize the necessity of providing evidence-based and culturally sensitive education on HPV transmission, screening, vaccination, reproductive health issues, stigma, and communication skills. These needs could be met through case-based learning, role-playing, simulation and communication training, but the present study did not evaluate their effectiveness and further research is needed.

articles.title: Chemogenetically silencing NaV1.8+ sensory neurons with PSAM4-GlyR relieves chronic pelvic pain in interstitial cystitis in mice.
articles.journal: Molecular therapy : the journal of the American Society of Gene Therapy
articles.authors: Lv G, Liu H, Xu R et al.
articles.abstract: Sensitization of bladder afferents underlies chronic pain associated with interstitial cystitis/bladder painful syndrome (IC/BPS). Chemogenetic approaches have been used to silence peripheral sensory neurons and relieve pain in many pain models. PSAM4-GlyR is a chemogenetic system specifically designed for use in humans and is activated by the smoking cessation drug varenicline. This study investigated the translational value of PSAM4-GlyR in the treatment of pelvic pain associated with IC/BPS. AAV-Retro-CMV-DIO-PSAM4-GlyR-mCherry (PSAM4-GlyR) was injected into the bladders of NaV1.8-Cre mice to specifically express PSAM4-GlyR in bladder nociceptive afferents, and pain relief effects were examined in cyclophosphamide (CYP)-induced or lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced IC/BPS model mice. We found that activation of PSAM4-GlyR with varenicline could effectively inhibit the excitability of bladder sensory neurons in vitro. In vivo, activation of PSAM4-GlyR significantly alleviated pain and bladder overactivity (OAB) without affecting voiding pressure. Importantly, the therapeutic efficacy of PSAM4-GlyR was comparable to that of the Gi-DREADD, a more widely used chemogenetic system in preclinical studies. Mechanistically, the therapeutic effects of PSAM4-GlyR in IC/BPS mice are attributed to the reduction in neuronal calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP) release and neurogenic inflammation. These findings support the translational potential of PSAM4-GlyR in the treatment of chronic pain and OAB associated with IC/BPS.

articles.title: EXPRESS: Effect of inositol supplementation on plasma adipokine levels: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
articles.journal: Journal of investigative medicine : the official publication of the American Federation for Clinical Research
articles.authors: Reyes-Avitia V, Barragan-Zuñiga LJ, Leyva-Velázquez AP et al.
articles.abstract: Evidence suggests that inositol supplementation has anti-obesity, anti-hyperglycemic, antioxidant, and anti-inflammatory effects. Therefore, considering that adipokines are therapeutic targets in the management of metabolic diseases due to their involvement in various biological processes, the goal of this meta-analysis was to determine the effect of inositol supplementation on adipokine levels in gestational diabetes, postmenopausal women, polycystic ovary syndrome, and type 2 diabetes. The search process was conducted in PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and ClinicalTrials.gov databases from inception to February 2026. A restricted maximum likelihood model with Hartung-Knapp adjustment was conducted to calculate the pooled effect size. The leave-one-out method was employed to determine the impact of each study on the overall effect size. The meta-analysis of seven randomized controlled trials revealed that inositol supplementation has no significant effect on adiponectin (WMD: 2.70 µg/mL, 95% CI: -1.02, 6.41, p = 0.12, I2 = 91%; Figure 3), leptin (WMD: 1.57 ng/mL, 95% CI: -33.28, 36.42, p = 0.66, I2 = 64%; Figure 4) or resistin (WMD: -7.43 ng/mL, 95% CI: -89.30, 74.45, p = 0.45, I2 = 94). Additionally, the sensitivity analysis was robust for adiponectin, while the effect size was sensitive to one study for each leptin and resistin. In conclusion, our results suggest that inositol supplementation has no beneficial effect on circulating adipokine levels.

articles.title: Exposure to Maternal Pre- and Postnatal Psychological Distress: Associations With Brain Structure in 5-Year-Old Children.
articles.authors: Pulli EP, Audah HK, Svensk A et al.
articles.abstract: Maternal mental health is an important contributor to child neurodevelopment. While there are multiple studies on prenatal exposure, early postnatal exposure has received little attention in neuroimaging research. Five-year-old children (n = 161) were recruited from the FinnBrain Birth Cohort study. Maternal distress was assessed using questionnaires on depressive and anxiety symptoms at 14, 24, and 34 gestational weeks and postnatally at 3, 6, and 24 months. T1-weighted structural images were processed using a voxel-based morphometry pipeline to map associations between maternal distress exposure and regional gray matter (GM) volumes. Whole-brain voxel-wise general linear models were used, accounting for potential confounders. Additionally, a latent class mixed model approach was used to model longitudinal trajectories of distress exposure. We found widespread associations between maternal postpartum distress symptoms and offspring brain morphology. Postnatal distress at 3 months was negatively associated with GM volumes in the left supplementary motor cortex, right cerebellum/fusiform gyrus, and left anterior insula/frontal operculum. Postnatal distress at 6 months was positively associated with GM volumes in the right cuneus and lingual gyrus, right insula/operculum, and right inferior occipital gyrus, while distress at 24 months was negatively associated with GM volumes in the left inferior/middle frontal gyrus. There were no structural brain differences between the latent classes. This study provides support for hypotheses proposing that early-life exposure to maternal distress can influence the structural development of the brain. It highlights the role of the early postnatal period and calls for further research into this so far overlooked period and the developmental pathways that explain these associations.

articles.title: Fertility rates across generations in twins and singletons: a total population study in Finland.
articles.authors: Niemi de Paiva S, Hukkanen M, Latvala A et al.
articles.abstract:
STUDY QUESTION: Does twin status and zygosity (monozygotic vs dizygotic; same-sex vs opposite-sex) predict fertility outcomes and intergenerational reproductive patterns compared with singletons?
SUMMARY ANSWER: Dizygotic female twins had a modestly higher number of biological children than singletons and monozygotic twins and were more likely to have a twin birth, but we did not observe differences for males or intergenerational differences.
WHAT IS KNOWN ALREADY: Dizygotic twinning is associated with heritable hyperovulation and higher natural fertility but less is known about whether being a twin or zygosity influences reproductive outcomes across generations.
STUDY DESIGN, SIZE, DURATION: A population-based longitudinal cohort study using part of the Finnish Twin Cohort and national population registers. Participants included an Anchor Generation composed of monozygotic (MZ; N = 4068), same-sex dizygotic (SSDZ; N = 8890), opposite-sex dizygotic (OSDZ; N = 8474), unknown zygosity (XZ; N = 2320) twins, and singleton controls (N = 1 193 404) born between 1945 and 1957 (total N = 1 217 156; 49.1% female), their mothers, their children, and their grandchildren.
PARTICIPANTS/MATERIALS, SETTING, METHODS: Fertility outcomes (number of biological children, age at first birth, childlessness, multiple births) were derived from Finnish population registers. Analyses followed a preregistered plan (https://osf.io/qbwv3).
