MAIN RESULTS AND THE ROLE OF CHANCE: Differences in fertility between singletons and twins were modest and varied by sex and zygosity. Differences were observed generally in the mothers of twins and female twins themselves, with limited differences in the offspring of twins as compared to the offspring of singletons. Twins were slightly older at first birth, had fewer total biological offspring, but were more likely to have a twin birth. Dizygotic twins in particular differed from monozygotic twins and singletons.
LIMITATIONS, REASONS FOR CAUTION: Findings are limited to individuals born in mid-20th-century Finland and thus generalizability to recent populations or non-Nordic contexts may be restricted. Further, analyses are observational, and causal inference is limited due to alternative motivation behind fertility rates like social or cultural reasons.
WIDER IMPLICATIONS OF THE FINDINGS: These findings suggest that zygosity and sex interact to shape reproductive outcomes, offering insight into genetic and environmental contributions to…

articles.title: Needs Assessment: Expanding Perinatal Psychiatry Access Programs to Support Infant Care Professionals and Postpartum Individuals.
articles.authors: McDowell L, O'Neill-Arana M, Griffin J et al.
articles.abstract: The Perinatal Psychiatry Access Program model (i.e., Access Program) aims to address mental health (MH) inequities among pregnant and postpartum individuals by providing MH training and support to perinatal care professionals. Despite program expansion, perinatal MH and substance use disorders (SUDs) remain significant contributors to postpartum maternal mortality. Collaborating with infant care professionals may enhance detection and access to MH/SUD treatment. This needs assessment explored infant care professionals' interest in recognizing and responding to the MH/SUD needs of pregnant and postpartum individuals and assessed the degree to which the statewide Massachusetts Child Psychiatry Access Program for Moms (MCPAP for Moms), could meet the needs of these professionals. We conducted four focus groups (n = 34) and 20 interviews (n = 22) with public health professionals, MCPAP for Moms staff, and child-focused professionals. Sessions were transcribed and coded using iterative thematic analysis. Although most infant care professionals expressed interest in perinatal MH/SUDs, this interest varied based on their recognition of parental MH as within their purview. Training and systematic support for perinatal MH/SUDs was not common in infant care settings. These findings highlight infant care professionals' interest in supporting postpartum individuals with perinatal MH/SUDs as well as the need for an increased prioritization of workforce development to serve the infant care system and ultimately improve the lives of families. Hiring additional staff, including a liaison from the early childhood community, and leveraging existing networks to improve consultation, resource referrals, and communication with infant care professionals is recommended.

articles.title: ESOI-ESUR multicentre validation of a structured MRI report for cervical cancer staging.
articles.authors: Russo L, Pintican R, Woitek R et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To compare an International Federation of Gyneology and Obstetrics (FIGO)-anchored structured MRI report with conventional narrative reporting for cervical cancer staging by evaluating referring clinicians' satisfaction.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this prospective multicentre crossover study (January-June 2024), consecutive patients with biopsy-proven cervical cancer at any FIGO stage underwent staging MRI at five European centres. For each patient, one narrative and one structured report were produced and independently evaluated by gynaecologists and radiation oncologists using a 12-item questionnaire (5-point Likert scale): five general items (Q1-Q5) for both formats and seven feature-specific items (Q6-Q12) for structured reports only. The primary endpoint was the proportion of structured-report evaluations with an overall score ≥ 20 (target ≥ 80%). Paired comparisons used the Wilcoxon signed-rank test with matched-pairs rank-biserial correlation (r) as effect size.
RESULTS: One hundred patients were evaluated, yielding 200 report evaluations. Of 100 structured report evaluations, 98.0% (95% Clopper-Pearson CI: 93.0-99.8%) achieved an overall score ≥ 20, exceeding the 80% threshold, vs 78.0% (95% CI: 68.6-85.7%) for narrative reports. Structured reports scored significantly higher on all five general items and on the overall score (all p < 0.05), with the largest effects for readability (r = 0.95) and brevity (r = 0.85). The advantage was consistent across reader type, disease stage, and centre, with the strongest effect in locally advanced disease. Q6 (cervical stromal invasion) had the lowest feature-specific satisfaction (73.7% scoring ≥ 4), prompting template revision.
CONCLUSION: A structured MRI report for cervical cancer staging significantly outperformed narrative reporting across all quality domains in a multicentre crossover design.
KEY POINTS: Question Cervical cancer management is highly stage-dependent, yet evidence on clinician-centred benefit of structured vs narrative MRI staging reports in routine practice is scarce. Findings In a multicentre crossover study, a FIGO-anchored structured MRI report significantly outperformed narrative reporting on all five general quality domains. Clinical relevance A structured MRI report standardises the communication of staging features that drive cervical cancer management and is preferred by referring clinicians over narrative reporting across specialties, disease stages, and European…

articles.title: Altered autophagy in fetal growth-restricted rat offspring and its interaction with post-weaning high-fat diet exposure.
articles.authors: Santosa I, Arai Y, Tokita K et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Fetal growth restriction (FGR) is a growing concern in Japan, and postnatal nutrition strongly modulates metabolic risk in affected offspring. This study investigated whether FGR exacerbates the autophagic and metabolic consequences of post-weaning high-fat diet (HFD) exposure in rat models.
METHODS: Pregnant Sprague-Dawley rats (8-10 weeks) received either a regular diet (21% protein; Control) or a low-protein diet (7% protein; FGR) from gestational day 0 until weaning. After weaning, offspring were fed a regular diet (CC, FC) or HFD (CH, FH) until 12 weeks of age. Metabolic outcomes were assessed at 8 and 12 weeks by intraperitoneal glucose tolerance test and homeostatic model assessment of insulin resistance (HOMA-IR). Autophagic markers (Beclin-1, ATG12, LC3-I, LC3-II, p62) were assessed in the liver and posterior leg skeletal muscles by Western blot.
RESULTS: In 8 and 12 weeks, HOMA-IR was higher in the HFD groups, regardless of the FGR status. Beclin-1 expression was reduced in the soleus muscle of the CH group. Hepatic p62 levels were elevated in both FGR groups.
CONCLUSION: FGR did not exacerbate HFD-induced metabolic or autophagic consequences. Rather, HFD independently drove insulin resistance while the intrauterine environment remained the primary determinant of autophagic programming in FGR offspring.
IMPACT: Post-weaning HFD does not aggravate FGR-programmed autophagic dysfunction in liver and skeletal muscle, which is established in utero and persists independently of postnatal diet. Post-weaning HFD independently drives insulin resistance, but the intrauterine environment remains the dominant regulator of autophagic programming. FGR-programmed hepatic autophagy impairment persists into the post-weaning period and is resistant to modification by caloric excess, tracing a longitudinal development arc of autophagic dysfunction from birth onward. Prenatal nutritional quality is more critical than postnatal caloric intake for long-term metabolic health, providing a basis for revisiting nutritional management guidelines for low birth weight infants.

articles.title: The placental transfer of nirmatrelvir using the ex vivo human placental perfusion model.
articles.authors: Zabek M, Chan E, Lim YJ et al.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Nirmatrelvir is an effective therapeutic option for COVID-19 infection and is often administered after symptom onset in pregnant individuals, but few data are available on the associated fetal exposure. The placental perfusion model evaluates maternal-fetal drug transfer across the human placenta and thus can determine fetal drug exposure. The objective of our study was to quantify the amount of nirmatrelvir transfer across the human placenta using the ex vivo placental perfusion model.
METHODS: In a dual closed-closed perfusion of a single human placenta lobule, nirmatrelvir was added to the maternal circulation at its clinical concentration (2.21 μg/mL) or at 10 times this level (22.1 μg/mL). For each placenta studied, there was a 1-h perfusion control period followed by a 3-h exposure period. Samples of the perfusate were collected throughout the experiment to measure nirmatrelvir concentrations and placental viability markers.
RESULTS: Perfusions conducted with nirmatrelvir at 2.21 μg/mL (n = 4) and 22.1 μg/mL (n = 5) concentrations showed a fetal-maternal concentration ratio (F:M) of 0.34 and 0.42, respectively, at 180 min. F:M was adjusted for nonplacental physiological factors, including binding of albumin and α-1-acid glycoprotein, and ionization. The adjusted F:M ranged from 0.26 to 0.35 for placentas perfused with 2.21 μg/mL and from 0.33 to 0.47 for placentas perfused with 22.1 μg/mL of nirmatrelvir.
CONCLUSIONS: Nirmatrelvir readily crosses the term human placenta in a concentration-dependent manner. These transfer kinetics provide a foundation for future physiologically based pharmacokinetic modelling, supporting the development of personalized nirmatrelvir dosing strategies in pregnancy.

articles.title: The Primary Reasons People Participate in Maternal-Fetal Phase I Clinical Trials Are Psychosocial.
articles.authors: Brown JEH, Riddle LS, Canepa E et al.
articles.abstract: Recent critiques of ethical guidance for maternal-fetal therapy clinical trials has highlighted the need to weigh maternal, fetal, and societal interests, respectively, while deprioritizing psychosocial reasons for participation. Psychosocial reasons refer to the psychological and social influences on study participants' decisions, and they are often central to considerations about informed consent. However, psychosocial reasons are described as too indirect, subjective, and vague to incorporate into prenatal clinical and regulatory frameworks. This qualitative study examined the perspectives of 11 individuals (within eight couples) enrolled in one of two maternal-fetal therapy phase I clinical trials for rare genetic conditions. Interviews revealed that motivations to participate were primarily psychosocial, including existential concerns given prior bereavement and/or fear of loss; temporal control through taking action as opposed to feeling passive; hope and optimism; and intergenerational and social motivations given one's family experience with disease and desire for social connections. Psychosocial reasons for participating ought to be given more consideration in ethical frameworks for maternal-fetal therapy phase I clinical trials, as well as in the approach to informed consent. It is important for clinical research teams to be especially conscientious to ensure appreciation for participants' reasons for participating that extend beyond typical frameworks of clinical risk/benefit, and to support participants who might harbor optimistic expectations of medical procedures as they transition to postnatal realities.

articles.title: Radiotherapy for Cervical Cancer: Technical Advances, Clinical Applications, and Future Perspectives.
articles.journal: The journal of obstetrics and gynaecology research
articles.authors: Maemoto H, Toita T, Nishie A
articles.abstract: Radiotherapy is an essential treatment modality for cervical cancer and has evolved substantially with advances in image guidance and treatment delivery. This review summarizes recent technological developments in external beam radiotherapy and brachytherapy, their clinical applications, and future directions, with particular consideration of Japanese practice in an international context. In external beam radiotherapy, conventional techniques incorporating central shielding are increasingly being replaced by intensity-modulated radiotherapy (IMRT) and volumetric-modulated arc therapy (VMAT). Daily three-dimensional image-guided radiotherapy (3D-IGRT) is essential for the safe implementation of these techniques because of substantial uterine motion and deformation. In brachytherapy, the transition from two-dimensional point-based prescription to three-dimensional image-guided treatment has enabled individualized assessment of target coverage and doses to organs at risk. Although magnetic resonance imaging-based brachytherapy is internationally recommended, computed tomography-based planning predominates in Japan and has achieved favorable outcomes, despite some studies reporting lower cumulative target doses than those recommended internationally. Intracavitary/interstitial brachytherapy (IC/IS BT) further improves dose distribution by combining intracavitary applicators with interstitial needles, particularly when adequate target coverage cannot be achieved with standard intracavitary brachytherapy alone. Future advances may include artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted treatment planning and adaptive workflows, tissue spacers to overcome anatomical constraints, and the incorporation of genomic, multi-omics, and radiomics information. Integrating these approaches may enable cervical cancer radiotherapy to progress beyond increasingly safe and precise treatment toward personalized care tailored to individual patient and tumor characteristics.

articles.title: Triptonide alleviates sepsis-associated acute lung injury by suppressing the STAT3/HIF-1α-mediated aerobic glycolysis in macrophages.
articles.authors: Zhu J, Ou Z, Ma H et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Sepsis-associated acute lung injury (SA-ALI), represents a major contributor to mortality among septic patients during the early hyperinflammatory phase. Triptonide, a diterpenoids extract from Tripterygium wilfordii Hook f has anticancer and contraceptive effects. However, its potential and mechanism in SA-ALI are largely unknown. This study aims to evaluate the therapeutic efficacy and elucidate underlying mechanisms of triptonide in SA-ALI to identify new clinical strategies.
EXPERIMENTAL APPROACH: Lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced endotoxemia model or caecal ligation and puncture (CLP) model was used to induce SA-ALI in mice, accompanied by treatment with triptonide, triptolide and 2-methoxyestradiol. Parallel in vitro experiments involved LPS-treated mouse primary macrophages cultured with or without triptonide. Transcriptomic sequencing of macrophages was performed to explore the anti-inflammatory mechanisms of triptonide, which were further substantiated using specific activators, inhibitors and adeno-associated virus (AAV)-mediated gene targeting.
KEY RESULTS: Our data shows that triptonide effectively inhibits macrophage pro-inflammatory activation, reduces pulmonary inflammation and alleviates SA-ALI pathology (i.e. inflammatory cell infiltration, oedema and cell apoptosis), thereby improving the survival of septic mice. Transcriptomic sequencing combined with metabolic analysis shows that triptonide suppresses aerobic glycolysis in pro-inflammatory macrophages by inhibiting the Signal Transducer and Activator of Transcription 3 (STAT3)/Hypoxia inducible factor-1α (HIF-1α) axis. Notably, the therapeutic efficacy of triptonide against SA-ALI was abolished in myeloid cell-specific HIF-1α overexpressed mice (LyzM-CreDIO-hif1a mice).
CONCLUSIONS AND IMPLICATIONS: Triptonide protects against SA-ALI by suppressing the STAT3/HIF-1α signalling axis, thereby inhibiting aerobic glycolysis-mediated pro-inflammatory macrophage activation, which suggests that triptonide is a promising therapeutic strategy for SA-ALI.

articles.title: Alloimmunization from Non-RhD antigens - Challenges and opportunities.
articles.authors: Blumenfeld KA, Blumenfeld YJ
articles.abstract: Fetal and neonatal anemia resulting from red blood cell (RBC) alloimmunization, also known as hemolytic disease of the fetus and newborn (HDFN), remains a significant cause of morbidity and mortality globally. Though Rhesus group D (RhD) is the most common RBC antigen known to cause alloimmunization, maternal-fetal RBC antigen incompatibility and subsequent alloimmunization can result from over 50 RBC surface antigens. Moreover, despite the development and wide-spread use of RhD immune globulin, (RhIG) and the initial decrease in RhD HDFN, there has been a recent persistence in the burden of disease from RhD incompatibility, as well as a relative increase in the incidence of non-RhD alloimmunization cases. The goal of this review is to present data regarding the incidence and implications of non-RhD group alloimmunization to highlight this ongoing global health care issue. We will also detail the latest data on alloimmunization care, management, and present areas that would benefit from further research and education.

articles.title: Uro-gynecological disorders in women with non-celiac gluten/wheat sensitivity: a prospective study and response to a wheat-free diet.
articles.authors: Seidita A, Barbaraci R, Latteri F et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Women with irritable bowel syndrome (IBS)-like symptoms frequently report uro-gynecological complaints without identifiable organic disease. A substantial proportion are diagnosed with non-celiac gluten/wheat sensitivity (NCGWS), a condition characterized by systemic manifestations.
AIM: To prospectively assess the prevalence of uro-gynecological disorders in women with NCGWS and their evolution following a wheat-free diet (WFD).
METHODS: We enrolled 186 newly diagnosed NCGWS female patients and 403 age-matched healthy controls. A structured questionnaire evaluating menstrual, gynecological and urological symptoms was administered at baseline and repeated in NCGWS patients after 12 (T1) and 24 (T2) months of WFD. In a subgroup, cervical cytology was assessed before and after a 7-day open wheat challenge.
RESULTS: Uro-gynecological disorders were more prevalent in NCGWS patients than controls (54.3% vs 35.7%, P < 0.0001), across menstrual (41.9%vs 28.8%, P = 0.002), gynecological (46.8%vs 8.9%, P < 0.0001), and urological domains (39.2%vs 4.0%, P < 0.0001). Strict WFD adherence was associated with significant reduction in all symptom domains at 12 months (P < 0.0001), with further improvement at 24 months in adherent patients. Poor adherence was associated with symptom recurrence, particularly gynecological complaints (+88.9%, P = 0.008). Cytology showed mild-to-moderate inflammation with increased granulocytes, more evident after wheat reintroduction.
CONCLUSIONS: Women with NCGWS reported more uro-gynecological complaints than controls. Long-term adherence to WFD was associated with clinical improvement, while wheat exposure might (re)trigger urogenital inflammation. Controlled studies are needed to establish the specificity of these associations and the therapeutic effect of wheat exclusion. Nevertheless, these findings highlight the relevance of dietary management and multidisciplinary approach in NCGWS patients.

articles.title: Cesarean delivery and neonatal hypoglycemia in gestational diabetes: A stratified cohort study.
articles.authors: Wang Z, Yang C
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Neonatal hypoglycemia affects 15-30% of at-risk neonates and it is associated with adverse neurodevelopmental outcomes. Current guidelines recommend routine glucose screening for high-risk infants, yet the definition of "at-risk" regarding delivery mode remains in debate. The association between cesarean delivery and hypoglycemia is controversial due to structural confounding with labor duration.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using a stratified design to resolve this confounding. Among 601 mother-infant dyads with gestational diabetes mellitus (2020-2025), we compared hypoglycemia risk by delivery mode (full cohort) and assessed labor duration effects (vaginal subgroup). Modified Poisson regression estimated adjusted relative risks (aRR), adjusting for maternal age, pre-pregnancy BMI, gestational weight gain, fetal sex, birth weight, and intrapartum insulin use. Sensitivity analyses included multiple imputation, propensity score matching, and E-value calculation.
RESULTS: Hypoglycemia occurred in 21.1% (127/601). Cesarean delivery was associated with a more than doubled risk compared to vaginal delivery (32.2% vs. 15.5%; adjusted relative risk [aRR] 2.06, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.51-2.81), with an even stronger association observed in propensity score-matched analysis (aRR 3.05, 95% CI 1.97-4.72). Labor duration showed no association among vaginal deliveries (aRR 0.98 per hour, 95% CI 0.91-1.05, P = 0.54). The effect was stronger in male infants (aRR 2.54, 95% CI 1.66-3.87) than in female infants (aRR 1.63, 95% CI 1.02-2.59), though the interaction was not statistically significant (P = 0.19).
CONCLUSIONS: Cesarean delivery is independently associated with neonatal hypoglycemia in pregnancies complicated by gestational diabetes, with sensitivity analyses confirming robustness (propensity score-matched aRR 3.05, 95% CI 1.97-4.72). Among vaginal deliveries, labor duration showed no association with hypoglycemia, suggesting that the observed association is unlikely to be primarily explained by labor duration differences. Delivery mode warrants consideration for risk stratification in glucose screening. Causal interpretation is limited by the observational design.

articles.title: Sonographically Diagnosed Adenomyosis and Hemorrhagic and Placental Complications of Pregnancy: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.authors: Mappa I, Derme M, Ciolli P et al.
articles.abstract: To determine whether adenomyosis diagnosed by ultrasound using explicitly reported criteria is associated with postpartum hemorrhage (PPH) and placenta accreta spectrum (PAS). MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, and CENTRAL were searched to September 9, 2026. Observational studies were eligible if adenomyosis was diagnosed sonographically using explicitly reported criteria in at least 80% of exposed cases and if an unexposed comparator was available. Studies relying on magnetic resonance imaging alone, histology, self-report, or administrative coding, and studies in which ultrasound- and MRI-based diagnoses could not be disaggregated were excluded. Co-primary outcomes were PPH and PAS. Conformity with the Morphological Uterus Sonographic Assessment (MUSA) criteria was examined in a prespecified sensitivity analysis. Risk of bias was assessed with ROBINS-I and certainty of evidence with GRADE. Odds ratios (OR) were pooled using a DerSimonian-Laird random-effects model. Of 12 038 records, five studies were included (1356 exposed and 11 270 unexposed pregnancies). Three studies using the same PPH threshold (> 500 mL after vaginal and ≥ 1000 mL after cesarean birth) contributed to the primary analysis: the pooled OR was 1.56 (95% CI 0.69-3.49; p = 0.284) with substantial heterogeneity (I2 = 62.3%; τ2 = 0.298; 95% prediction interval 0.41-5.94). The pooled estimate was unstable on leave-one-out analysis, ranging from 1.10 (0.41-2.96) when the study recruiting from a symptomatic tertiary population was removed to 2.33 (1.36-4.00) when the registry-based study was removed. One study reporting severe PPH (≥ 1000 mL vaginal/≥ 1500 mL cesarean) reported an OR of 6.52 (2.24-19.03). Only two studies reported PAS, with 0/90 and 3/311 events among exposed women; these were not pooled. All studies were at serious risk of bias and certainty of evidence was very low for every outcome. When eligibility is restricted to adenomyosis diagnosed by ultrasound with explicitly reported criteria, an association with PPH is not demonstrable, and the pooled estimate depends entirely on whether the source population is symptomatic or unselected. Evidence on PAS is insufficient for synthesis. Published associations may in part reflect how cases were ascertained rather than the disease itself. Trail Registration: PROSPERO CRD420261495931.

articles.title: AgRP neurons as an integrative node linking the somatotropic and reproductive axes.
articles.journal: The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience
articles.authors: Alves GA, Vieira HR, de Sousa LMM et al.
articles.abstract: Growth hormone (GH) signaling contributes to pubertal development and reproductive function, yet the hypothalamic circuits mediating these effects remain incompletely understood. Kisspeptin and agouti-related protein (AgRP) neurons are key integrators of metabolic and reproductive cues and exhibit GH-responsive signaling pathways. We therefore investigated their contributions to the reproductive consequences of altered somatotropic signaling. Using genetic mouse models of chronic GH excess or deficiency, we examined the impact of altered GH signaling on pubertal maturation, fertility, and hypothalamic neuroendocrine function. Pubertal onset was unaffected in female mice, whereas males with either GH excess or GH deficiency exhibited delayed puberty. In contrast, GH hypersecretion selectively disrupted estrous cyclicity and impaired fertility in females. Female reproductive dysfunction occurred despite preserved kisspeptin signaling, as evidenced by the preservation of intrinsic electrophysiological properties of kisspeptin neurons and unaltered hypothalamic Kiss1 mRNA expression. Chronic GH excess increased hypothalamic Agrp mRNA expression and reduced Pomc and Tac2 mRNA expression compared to control mice; these transcriptional changes were prevented by AgRP-specific GH receptor (GHR) deletion, which also improved ovarian function. Notably, selective deletion of the GHR in AgRP cells markedly improved fertility in GH-hypersecreting females. Together, these findings identify AgRP neurons as a critical hypothalamic target through which chronic GH excess impairs female reproductive function. Our results further demonstrate that GH-induced infertility occurs independently of canonical kisspeptin-GnRH dysfunction, revealing a sexually dimorphic mechanism linking somatotropic signaling to reproductive competence.Significance Statement Reproductive dysfunction is a common consequence of chronic alterations in growth hormone (GH) secretion, but the underlying neural mechanisms remain poorly defined. We show that chronic GH excess induces a sexually dimorphic reproductive phenotype characterized by profound impairment of female fertility despite largely preserved kisspeptin neuronal function. In contrast, GH excess altered hypothalamic AgRP-associated pathways, and the selective deletion of GH receptors in AgRP neurons significantly improved fertility in GH-hypersecreting females. These findings identify AgRP neurons as key mediators of GH-induced reproductive…

articles.title: Discordance between levator hiatus morphology and function in pelvic floor dysfunction.
articles.authors: Xue Y, Mu L, Nan S
articles.abstract: This study aimed to characterize static anatomical and dynamic functional parameters of the levator hiatus in women with bladder prolapse and to examine their diagnostic performance. Primiparous women with a diagnosis of bladder prolapse were recruited as the prolapse group (n = 62), while healthy nulliparous women were included as the control group (n = 60). Nulliparous controls were selected to provide a reference group without childbirth-related pelvic floor remodeling; however, because parity differed systematically between groups, parity-related effects cannot be separated from prolapse-related effects in this case-control design. The levator hiatus area was measured both at rest and during maximal Valsalva maneuver, and the difference between these 2 measurements was calculated. Hierarchical regression analysis was performed to evaluate the independent and joint contributions of group status and body mass index (BMI) to these parameters. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis was used to assess diagnostic performance within the study cohort. The levator hiatus resting area, Valsalva area, and area change were all significantly greater in the prolapse group than in the control group (P < .001). Static anatomical parameters, including the resting and Valsalva areas, were associated with group status (P < .001), whereas the dynamic functional parameter, namely the area change, was associated with both group status (standardized β = 0.829, P < .001) and BMI (standardized β = 0.139, P = .003). ROC analysis showed very high apparent diagnostic performance for area change in this cohort (AUC = 1.000), compared with the static anatomical parameters (AUC = 0.999 and 0.920, respectively). These findings indicate different statistical association patterns for levator hiatus morphology and dynamic area change. Dynamic functional assessment may provide complementary information beyond static anatomical measures; however, its diagnostic performance requires confirmation in parity-matched and independent validation cohorts.

articles.title: Association between proinflammatory diet and infertility among US reproductive-aged women: A cross-sectional study from NHANES 2013-2018.
articles.authors: Du J, Tan Y
articles.abstract: This study aimed to examine the association between the Dietary Inflammatory Index (DII) and infertility among United States women of childbearing age and assess whether body mass index (BMI) modifies this relationship. A cross-sectional analysis of National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (2013-2018) included 2236 women aged 18 to 45 years. DII was derived from 24-hour dietary recall, and infertility was self-reported. Weighted logistic regression and interaction analyses were used. Higher DII scores were associated with increased infertility risk. Compared to the lowest DII quartile, the highest quartile had 54% higher odds of infertility (odds ratio = 1.54; 95% confidence interval: 1.02-2.32; P trend = .026). BMI significantly modified the association (P interaction < .0001). The strongest effect was observed in obese women (BMI ≥ 30 kg/m2), with predicted infertility probability reaching 30% at high DII levels. Proinflammatory diets are associated with higher infertility risk, particularly among obese women. Reducing dietary inflammation may be a promising strategy for infertility prevention in vulnerable populations.

articles.title: Complete blood count-derived inflammatory indices as potential markers in threatened abortion: A retrospective cohort study.
articles.authors: Karakaya H, Kusdogan M, Akarsu GD et al.
articles.abstract: This study aimed to evaluate complete blood count-derived inflammatory markers in women with threatened abortion and to investigate their association with threatened abortion. This retrospective cohort study included 802 pregnant women presenting before 20 weeks of gestation. Hematological parameters were compared between women with threatened abortion and healthy pregnant controls. Neutrophil, lymphocyte, platelet, neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), and platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR) values were evaluated. Multivariable binary logistic regression analyses were performed to identify factors independently associated with threatened abortion, with primary hematological parameters and derived inflammatory indices assessed in separate models to reduce multicollinearity. Women with threatened abortion had significantly lower lymphocyte counts and higher NLR and PLR values than controls (all P < .001), whereas neutrophil and platelet counts did not differ significantly. In multivariable analysis, lower lymphocyte count and higher neutrophil count were independently associated with threatened abortion. In the model including inflammatory indices, both NLR (odds ratio = 2.017, 95% confidence interval = 1.450-2.805; P < .001) and PLR (odds ratio = 1.033, 95% confidence interval = 1.022-1.044; P < .001) were independently associated with threatened abortion. Threatened abortion was characterized by lower lymphocyte counts and higher NLR and PLR values. These readily available inflammatory indices may serve as useful adjunctive markers for clinical assessment; however, prospective multicenter studies are needed to confirm their predictive utility.

articles.title: Calcium, 25-hydroxyvitamin D, and postpartum hemorrhage: A 2-sample Mendelian randomization study.
articles.authors: Zhang P, Wang F, Kan Z et al.
articles.abstract: We aimed to evaluate the causal effect of calcium and 25-hydroxyvitamin D [25(OH)D] on the risk of postpartum hemorrhage (PPH) using a 2-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) study. Instrumental variables for calcium and 25(OH)D were selected from corresponding large-scale genome-wide association studies. Summary-level data on PPH were obtained from the latest R10 release of the FinnGen consortium. Inverse-variance weighting (IVW) was performed as the main MR analysis, and MR-Egger and weighted median were performed to strengthen the final MR estimates. Sensitivity analyses were applied to detect possible heterogeneity or pleiotropy. One hundred and four single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) for calcium and 117 SNPs for 25(OH)D were selected as candidate instrumental variables. In this study, the MR estimates for calcium and 25(OH)D remained consistent before and after removing confounder-related SNPs. The IVW method suggested a potential inverse association between genetically predicted calcium and PPH (odds ratio [OR] = 0.89, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.80, 0.99, P = .036); however, this finding was not supported by the pleiotropy‑robust MR‑Egger (OR = 0.89, 95% CI: 0.72-1.11, P = .303) or weighted median (OR = 0.90, 95% CI: 0.74-1.10, P = .302) methods. No heterogeneity or pleiotropy was observed in Cochran's Q test (P = .825), MR-Egger intercept test (P = .976), or the MR-Pleiotropy Residual Sum and Outlier (MR-PRESSO) Global Test (P = .842) in the determination of the role of calcium levels in PPH. However, no significant genetic evidence was found to support a causal relationship between 25(OH)D and PPH (IVW: OR = 0.98, 95% CI: 0.85-1.12, P = .735; MR-Egger: OR = 1.01, 95% CI: 0.82-1.25, P = .912; Weighted median: OR = 1.08, 95% CI: 0.85-1.36, P = .525). In summary, our primary analysis suggested a potential inverse association between serum calcium and PPH, but this was not supported by sensitivity analyses robust to pleiotropy, warranting cautious interpretation. For 25(OH)D, our analysis did not provide sufficient evidence to support or refute a causal role in PPH, largely due to limited statistical power.

articles.title: Can the Finnish Diabetes Risk Score (FINDRISC) identify gestational diabetes?: A multicenter cross-sectional study in Türkiye.
articles.authors: Dagci S, Sertbas Y, Kizilay V et al.
articles.abstract: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) is a common pregnancy complication with short- and long-term adverse outcomes for mother and child. The Finnish Diabetes Risk Score (FINDRISC) is a simple, validated questionnaire for type 2 diabetes risk, but its ability to identify GDM is not well established. In this multicenter cross-sectional study, 797 pregnant women at 24 to 28 weeks of gestation who attended 3 tertiary hospitals in Istanbul, Türkiye, between June and September 2024 completed the Turkish FINDRISC at the same visit as their routine GDM screening. GDM was diagnosed by the 1-step (75-g oral glucose tolerance test [OGTT]) or two-step (50-g glucose challenge test followed by 100-g OGTT) approach. Univariable and multivariable logistic regression and receiver operating characteristic analysis were performed. GDM was diagnosed in 104 women (13.0%). The FINDRISC score was higher in women with GDM (median 8 [interquartile range 6-12] vs 7 [4-10]; P = .001); each 1-point increase was associated with 8% higher odds of GDM (OR 1.08; 95% confidence interval, 1.03-1.13). The area under the receiver operating characteristic curve was 0.599 (95% confidence interval, 0.542-0.655). At the optimal cutoff (≥8 points), sensitivity was 62.5%, specificity 53.2%, positive predictive value 16.7%, negative predictive value 90.4%, and negative likelihood ratio 0.70; 37.5% of GDM cases scored below this cutoff. A cutoff of ≥4 points yielded 88.5% sensitivity but would have avoided OGTT in only 22.0% of women. In multivariable analysis, age ≥ 35 years (adjusted OR 2.40), body mass index > 30 kg/m2 (adjusted OR 2.88), and non-daily fruit/vegetable intake (adjusted OR 1.70) were independently associated with GDM. When administered at 24 to 28 weeks, FINDRISC showed poor discrimination for concurrently diagnosed GDM. Its negative predictive value largely reflects the low prevalence of GDM, and no cutoff combined acceptable sensitivity with a meaningful reduction in OGTTs. FINDRISC should not replace universal OGTT screening; pregnancy-specific risk models evaluated prospectively in early pregnancy are needed.

articles.title: Causal association between gestational diabetes mellitus and peripartum mental disorders: Evidence from two-sample Mendelian randomization.
articles.authors: Yang C, Song W, Lu K et al.
articles.abstract: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) is associated with multiple maternal and neonatal complications, but its direct causal impact on peripartum mental health remains uncertain. This study used a two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) approach to assess whether genetically predicted GDM increases the risk of peripartum mental disorders, including depression, anxiety, and suicidality. Genetic variants associated with GDM were obtained from the FinnGen consortium, and summary data for peripartum mental disorders were derived from genome-wide association studies. Independent single-nucleotide polymorphisms (P < 5 × 10-6, r2 < 0.001) were analyzed using inverse-variance weighted, MR-Egger, and weighted median methods. Heterogeneity, pleiotropy, and causal direction were evaluated using Cochran's Q, the MR-Egger intercept, and Steiger filtering. Nineteen independent single-nucleotide polymorphisms were identified. Inverse-variance weighted analysis indicated a positive causal association between genetically predicted GDM and peripartum mental disorders. The estimated effect was β = 0.048, with a standard error (SE) of 0.014 and P = 8.3 × 10⁻⁴; the odds ratio was 1.049 (95% confidence interval = 1.020-1.0779). The results were consistent in all the sensitivity analyses, with no evidence of heterogeneity or pleiotropy. The MR findings provide genetic evidence supporting a causal link between GDM and peripartum mental disorders. These results underscore the need for integrated clinical management that simultaneously addresses metabolic control and psychological well-being in women diagnosed with GDM.

articles.title: Prognostic impact of positive peritoneal washing cytology in surgically treated cervical cancer.
articles.authors: Zhang Q, Li X, Wang Q et al.
articles.abstract: Positive peritoneal washing cytology is an uncommon but potentially clinically relevant finding in cervical cancer. This retrospective cohort study evaluated its association with recurrence, survival, and metastasis-related biomarkers in patients undergoing open surgery for cervical cancer between 2018 and 2023. A total of 120 patients were classified as peritoneal washing cytology-positive (n = 32) or cytology-negative (n = 88). Baseline clinicopathological characteristics were broadly comparable between groups. Kaplan-Meier analysis demonstrated poorer survival among patients with positive cytology. The estimated 5-year overall survival was 43.7% (95% CI, 26.8-59.4%) in the cytology-positive group and 67.9% (95% CI, 55.2-77.8%) in the cytology-negative group, whereas the corresponding 5-year progression-free survival estimates were 36.5% (95% CI, 20.5-52.6%) and 62.4% (95% CI, 49.8-72.8%), respectively. Recurrence was more frequent among cytology-positive patients, particularly distant-organ recurrence. Serum VEGF and tissue MMP-9 levels were higher in the cytology-positive group. In multivariable analysis, positive peritoneal washing cytology remained associated with poorer overall survival after adjustment for selected clinicopathological variables. A combined VEGF/MMP-9 model showed exploratory discrimination for lymph-node metastasis, although the model requires internal and external validation. These findings suggest that positive peritoneal washing cytology may identify a subgroup with adverse outcomes after surgery, but prospective and externally validated studies are required before clinical application.

articles.title: Nucleotide metabolism and cervical cancer: A comprehensive study of molecular subtypes and therapeutic targets.
articles.authors: Li F, Bao C, Liu Y et al.
articles.abstract: Cervical cancer (CC) is among the most prevalent malignancies in women worldwide. Tumor progression involves profound metabolic reprogramming, in which nucleotide metabolism sustains deoxyribonucleic acid/ribonucleic acid synthesis and proliferation; however, its role in CC remains unclear. Transcriptomic and clinical data of CC patients were obtained from The Cancer Genome Atlas. Nonnegative matrix factorization classified patients into molecular subtypes based on nucleotide metabolism-related genes and compared their survival, immune infiltration, somatic mutations, and drug sensitivity. Mfuzz soft clustering identified subtype-associated expression patterns. Gene set variation analysis scoring, differential expression analysis, and Gene Ontology/Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes enrichment of differentially expressed genes were then performed. Prognostic models were constructed using multiple machine learning algorithms, and the model with the highest concordance index (C-index) was selected. Patients were stratified into high- and low-risk groups and assessed using multivariate Cox regression, Kaplan-Meier, and time-dependent receiver operating characteristic analyses. Immune checkpoint inhibitor response was predicted using the tumor immune dysfunction and exclusion algorithm, and molecular docking was performed between core genes and candidate compounds. Nonnegative matrix factorization revealed 5 subtypes with distinct outcomes: cluster 2 showed the worst prognosis, whereas clusters 3 and 4 had favorable survival. TTN, KMT2C, HUWE1, and PIK3CA were frequently mutated across subtypes. B cells, regulatory T cells, CD8+ T cells, and M2 macrophages were enriched in clusters 3 and 4. VX-680, CIL70, and BRD-K01737880 exhibited significantly lower IC50 values in the poor-prognosis group. Seven key genes (SERPINE1, CAV1, SOD2, SLC16A1, XDH, CYP27B1, and NAGS) were identified by Mfuzz clustering. Forty-two differentially expressed genes between the high- and low-score groups were predominantly enriched in xenobiotic response, nutrient sensing, small-molecule catabolism, inflammatory response, tumor necrosis factor signaling, apoptosis, and hypoxia. The generalized boosted regression model achieved the highest C-index, with 1-, 3-, and 5-year area under the curves of 0.62, 0.67, and 0.61, indicating modest discrimination. Tumor immune dysfunction and exclusion analysis indicated reduced immune checkpoint inhibitor responsiveness in the high-risk group.…

articles.title: Effects and safety of Korean red ginseng on the clinical course of uterine leiomyoma: A double-blind randomized placebo-controlled trial.
articles.authors: Hur H, Park Y, Chung H et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Korean red ginseng (KRG) is widely used as a dietary supplement, but its effects on uterine leiomyoma growth and reproductive hormones are unclear. We evaluated whether KRG affects leiomyoma growth, routine laboratory indices, or endocrine profiles in premenopausal women with uterine leiomyoma managed expectantly.
METHODS: In this single-center, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled, parallel-group trial, premenopausal women aged 20 to 45 years with a uterine leiomyoma of 1 to 8 cm suitable for expectant management were allocated 1:1 to KRG 3 g/d or matching placebo for 6 months. Participants, investigators, ultrasonography examiners, and analysts were blinded. The primary outcome was the between-group difference in the 6-month change in maximal diameter of the index leiomyoma on ultrasonography, analyzed by analysis of covariance adjusted for baseline diameter. Secondary outcomes were complete blood count, ferritin, liver enzymes, and reproductive hormones.
RESULTS: Between December 2015 and September 2019, 69 participants were randomized (placebo 34, KRG 35) and 61 completed the 6-month assessment (placebo 30, KRG 31); all 8 noncompletions were losses to follow-up. Maximal diameter increased modestly in both groups, with no significant between-group difference in change (mean difference -0.11 cm; 95% confidence interval: -0.33 to 0.12; P = .34); the upper confidence limit lay below the prespecified target difference of 0.33 cm. There were no significant between-group differences in laboratory changes or in baseline-, age-, and body mass index-adjusted log scale hormone ratios, and the multivariate hormone profile did not differ between groups (Pillai's trace = 0.056; P = .68). In exploratory post hoc analyses, the internal correlation structure among hormone changes was similar in both arms. No treatment-related serious adverse event and no discontinuation for intolerance was documented, although adverse events were ascertained passively.
CONCLUSION: In premenopausal women with uterine leiomyoma managed expectantly, 6 months of KRG supplementation did not meaningfully alter leiomyoma growth, routine laboratory indices, or reproductive hormone homeostasis compared with placebo. Within the constraints of a modest sample size, incomplete characterization of the study product, and passive adverse-event ascertainment, these findings do not establish the safety of KRG, and they support no conclusion regarding nonserious adverse effects.

articles.title: Transvaginal ultrasound with color doppler in the diagnosis of polycystic ovary syndrome: A single-center case-control study.
articles.authors: Bu Y, Yu W, Zhao W et al.
articles.abstract: This study aimed to investigate the diagnostic value of transvaginal color Doppler ultrasonography and imaging indicators in polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS). In this case-control study, 100 PCOS patients (PCOS group) and 100 healthy subjects (control group) were selected. The total ovarian area, ovarian medullary area, peak systolic velocity (PSV), end-diastolic blood flow velocity (EDV), and resistance index (RI) were compared. The total ovarian area, ovarian medullary area, PSV, and EDV of PCOS patients were significantly higher than healthy subjects (P < .01). The RI of PCOS patients was significantly lower (P < .01). Each parameter was evaluated separately by receiver operating characteristic analysis: total ovarian area (area under the curve [AUC] 0.999), ovarian medullary area (AUC 1.000) and RI (AUC 0.997) showed the highest diagnostic performance, followed by EDV (AUC 0.877) and PSV (AUC 0.631). Transvaginal ultrasound, especially 2-dimensional morphological parameters, demonstrated high discriminative ability for PCOS. However, given the study population and potential incorporation bias, these results require external validation in broader cohorts.

articles.title: Prenatal Trio Exome Sequencing in Low-Risk Pregnancies: Diagnostic Yield and Clinical Implications.
articles.authors: Margiotti K, Fabiani M, Cima A et al.
articles.abstract: Prenatal exome sequencing (ES) is increasingly requested in pregnancies without ultrasound-detected structural anomalies, yet its diagnostic yield and clinical value in this low-risk setting remain incompletely defined. We reviewed 209 consecutive prenatal trio-ES cases performed in structurally normal pregnancies over a 3 year period. Variants were classified according to ACMG/AMP guidelines, and reporting was restricted to pathogenic (P) or likely pathogenic (LP) variants associated with childhood-onset disorders and/or medically actionable secondary findings. P/LP variants were detected in 30 of 211 fetuses (overall P/LP detection rate 14.2%; 95% CI 10.1%-19.6%). After reclassifying three adult-onset cancer-predisposition findings (BRCA2, MSH6, SDHD) as parental secondary findings and excluding them from the reportable set, the diagnostic yield was 27/211 (12.8%; 95% CI 8.9%-18.0%); this reportable definition is used throughout. Inherited variants predominated over de novo events (25/30; 83.3%), and autosomal dominant conditions were the most frequent category. Seven of the 30 positive cases involved genes on the ACMG SF v3.3 list. Pregnancy termination was elected in 2 of 30 positive cases (6.7%). In structurally normal pregnancies, the value of prenatal trio-ES lies less in detectability than in the nature of its findings mostly inherited, often incompletely penetrant and in their clinical and ethical implications: informing genetic counseling; guiding postnatal surveillance; facilitating familial cascade testing; identifying medically actionable secondary findings; and raising distinct questions of consent and the future child's autonomy.

articles.title: Follicular-fluid neonicotinoid exposure and endometriosis: Associations with reproductive outcomes and metabolic remodeling.
articles.authors: Liu Z, Zhao X, Shi H et al.
articles.abstract: Neonicotinoid insecticides (NEOs) are emerging environmental contaminants, but their presence and reproductive relevance in the human follicular microenvironment remain poorly understood. We quantified 16 NEOs and metabolites in follicular fluid from 174 infertile women undergoing assisted reproductive technology (ART), including 63 women with endometriosis and 111 controls. Associations with endometriosis and ART outcomes were assessed using single-analyte regression and mixture models. Untargeted metabolomics was performed in a nested subset of 40 women. NEOs were widely detected in follicular fluid, with N-desmethyl-acetamiprid (N-dm-ACE) showing the highest detection frequency. Each twofold increase in N-dm-ACE concentration was associated with higher odds of prevalent endometriosis (adjusted OR = 1.79, 95% CI: 1.38-2.32), and N-dm-ACE was consistently prioritized in mixture analyses. Several NEOs were also associated with adverse ART outcomes, including fewer mature oocytes, fewer two-pronuclear zygotes, and lower pregnancy odds, with stronger patterns among women with endometriosis. Metabolomic profiling identified 324 features differing between women with and without endometriosis at nominal P < 0.05, of which 54 remained significant after false discovery rate correction. Integrated exposure-metabolome analysis identified 47 features showing nominal associations with both N-dm-ACE and endometriosis. These findings identify cross-sectional associations between follicular-fluid NEO concentrations and existing endometriosis, alongside exploratory metabolic signatures involving lipid- and nucleotide-related features. Further longitudinal studies are needed to clarify their temporal and biological relevance.

articles.title: The tumor microenvironment of ovarian cancer through a spatial topological lens: From immune exclusion mechanisms to next-generation precision interventions.
articles.authors: Chen J, Lai Y, Peng L
articles.abstract: High-grade serous ovarian cancer (HGSOC) has a relatively high mortality rate and shows limited efficacy with conventional immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs). For a long time, this clinical immune resistance was attributed to a low tumor mutational burden or insufficient immunogenicity. However, recent studies in spatial biology have revealed that immune evasion is not a single-molecule event but rather a multilevel process driven by a precisely organized "spatial topological architecture." This review elaborates on three core spatial niches in the ovarian cancer tumor microenvironment (TME): the immune-exclusion stromal barrier formed by cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) and the extracellular matrix (ECM) they remodel; the immunosuppressive core composed of specific tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs); and the antitumor immune frontline constructed by tertiary lymphoid structures (TLS), which act as adaptive immune hubs. It also mentions how distance-dependent ligand-receptor communication, spatial gradients created by metabolic competition, and anatomical site-specific niche reprogramming collectively interact within the spatial architecture to establish an immunosuppressive network that limits effector T cell infiltration and function in the TME. Finally, this review develops a prospective translational roadmap for next-generation precision immunotherapy by shifting therapeutic strategies from "biochemical immune activation" to "spatial topological remodeling" targeting the TME (such as stromal specification and engineered cell therapies), providing a new theoretical basis and clinical perspective for overcoming spatial immune exclusion in ovarian cancer.

articles.title: Using diamond relaxometry to measure free radicals on human single spermatozoa: From boar to human.
articles.authors: Li HT, Hofsink N, Eliveld J et al.
articles.abstract: Oxidative stress is increasingly recognized as an important contributor to male infertility, yet current methods for measuring reactive oxygen species and free radicals in spermatozoa lack single-cell resolution and often rely on indirect or non-specific detection strategies. Diamond relaxometry, a quantum sensing technique based on nitrogen-vacancy centers in fluorescent nanodiamonds (FNDs), enables direct detection of local free radical production in living cells. Although previously demonstrated in boar spermatozoa, application at the level of individual human sperm cells required further methodological optimization. This study aimed to translate and optimize T1 relaxometry from a pre-clinical boar sperm model to human spermatozoa. A stepwise optimization strategy was applied in boar spermatozoa, systematically evaluating incubation time, temperature and processing media focusing on FNDs colocalization with spermatozoa head, cell metabolic activity, and protocol-induced effects on T1 measurements. The optimized protocol was subsequently translated to human spermatozoa. We showed that incubation time of 1h (vs. 3h), incubation temperature at room temperature (vs. 37°C) and albumin-containing processing medium, yielded a clinically compatible protocol that preserved sperm metabolic activity while ensuring robust FND binding and stable T1 relaxation times. Using the optimized protocol, significant reductions in T1 relaxation time were observed following menadione treatment in both boar (1 mM) and human spermatozoa (10 μM), demonstrating sensitivity to increases in free radical production at the single-cell level (p < 0.001 and p = 0.043, respectively). In human spermatozoa, fluorescent nanodiamond colocalization reached 36%, enabling successful relaxometry measurements. In conclusion, we successfully optimized and translated diamond relaxometry from boar to human spermatozoa and established a clinically compatible protocol for single-cell free radical detection in human spermatozoa. This work demonstrates the feasibility of quantum sensing in individual human sperm cells and provides a foundation for future studies investigating oxidative stress as a biomarker in male infertility.

articles.title: Microenvironment of Bone and Joint Infection: Examining the Microenvironment.
articles.authors: Abbaszadeh A, Damirchi MH, Soleimani M et al.
articles.abstract: Periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) is a major complication of arthroplasty, and conventional diagnostic methods for PJI remain limited by suboptimal sensitivity, long turnaround times, high cost, and patient inconvenience, particularly in biofilm-associated and culture-negative infections. Emerging data suggest that the infected joint microenvironment contains host- and pathogen-derived molecular signatures with substantial diagnostic potential. This review evaluates current evidence on microenvironment-related biomarkers in PJI, including host extracellular vesicles, host cell-free nucleic acids (microRNA/cell-free DNA), non-host-derived biomarkers, and sequencing-based pathogen detection techniques. Host-derived biomarkers show favorable discriminatory capability by characterizing inflammatory and immune responses, and metagenomic and sequencing-based technologies improve pathogen identification. Despite encouraging diagnostic performance, widespread clinical implementation remains limited due to a lack of standardization, cost, and limited prospective validation. Future prospective multicenter studies should integrate conventional microbiological methods with molecular and microenvironment-based approaches to improve diagnostic accuracy.

articles.title: Population pharmacokinetics of fibrinogen in postpartum haemorrhage during Caesarean section: a secondary analysis of the TRACES trial.
articles.authors: Hureau M, Lanoiselée J, Abraham E et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In severe postpartum haemorrhage (PPH), hypofibrinogenaemia is strongly associated with bleeding severity. To correct fibrinogen depletion, various fixed dosing regimens have been evaluated, but the optimal fibrinogen dosing regimen remains unknown. To date, fibrinogen pharmacokinetics have only been studied outside haemorrhagic settings (healthy or afibrinogenaemic patients) METHODS: This ancillary analysis of the TRACES trial assessed fibrinogen kinetics in 142 women with PPH > 800 ml during caesarean section, among which 31 received fibrinogen replacement. Plasma fibrinogen concentrations (n = 593) were measured using the Clauss method. A population pharmacokinetic model was developed using nonlinear mixed-effects modeling. Simulations were performed to estimate loading and maintenance doses required to achieve target fibrinogen concentrations.
RESULTS: A one-compartment logistic model adequately described plasma fibrinogen levels. Bleeding rate was identified as a key covariate to explain fibrinogen loss rate. Based on the estimated model, an optimised dosing regimen was derived to achieve and maintain predefined target fibrinogen levels. To achieve a target increase of 1 g.L-¹ in plasma fibrinogen level, the required fibrinogen loading dose is at least 2.7 g for a body weight of 50 kg. To maintain plasma fibrinogen level at a target of 2 g.L-¹ during a 1000 mL.h-¹ bleeding rate, a fibrinogen infusion rate of 0.9 g.h-¹ would be required.
CONCLUSIONS: This work supports that an individualized target-controlled fibrinogen dosing strategy is probably required to effectively correct fibrinogen levels. Integrating such models as a clinical decision support tool into a multimodal strategy that also utilizes viscoelastic testing could optimize PPH management.

articles.title: Combined baicalein and the neocryptolepine derivative Z2 enhance anti-ovarian cancer efficacy by inhibiting the CDK4/6-Rb signaling pathway.
articles.authors: Zhang H, Zhao Y, Zhao J et al.
articles.abstract: Ovarian cancer is a highly aggressive gynecological malignancy with poor prognosis, creating an urgent need for novel therapeutic agents and rational combinatorial strategies. Herein, a panel of pre-synthesized neocryptolepine derivatives was subjected to biological screening. Derivative Z2 exerted potent anti-proliferative activity against SKOV3 and ES2 ovarian cancer cells (IC₅₀ = 1.91 ± 0.07 μM, 2.21 ± 0.11 μM), with low cytotoxicity in normal KGN cells. As monotherapy, Z2 suppressed cell migration, induced G0/G1-phase arrest and mitochondria-dependent apoptosis by elevating intracellular ROS and reducing mitochondrial membrane potential. Subsequently, CompuSyn analysis confirmed strong synergistic anti-tumor interactions between Z2 and baicalein. Compared with monotherapy, their combination further enhanced G0/G1 arrest, apoptosis and migration inhibition. Mechanistically, molecular docking predicted stable binding of both compounds to CDK4. Western blot and CDK4/CDK6 agonist (INK4C-IN-2) rescue assays performed in SKOV3 and ES2 cells demonstrated that Z2 baicalein co treatment inhibited the CDK4/6-Rb cascade, and reactivation of this pathway partially abrogated the synergistic antitumor effect, indicating the essential role of the CDK4/6-Rb axis. Furthermore, acute-toxicity assays validated the favorable in vivo safety of Z2 within certain doses. In ID8 syngeneic tumor-bearing mice, Z2-baicalein co-treatment markedly suppressed tumor growth without obvious organ toxicity. Collectively, Z2 is a promising anti-ovarian-cancer lead compound, and Z2-baicalein combination constitutes a feasible synergistic regimen targeting the CDK4/6-Rb signaling axis.

articles.title: Probenecid promotes relaxation and potentiates the effects of cyclic nucleotide-elevating agents in the pig detrusor.
articles.authors: Leonardi GR, Moretti MB, Toledo TA et al.
articles.abstract: Probenecid is a uricosuric agent also used as an antibiotic adjuvant. It inhibits, organic acid transporters (OATs), multidrug resistance-associated proteins (MRPs) and pannexin-1 (Panx-1) channels and activates transient receptor potential vanilloid 2. We hypothesized that probenecid could modulate detrusor smooth muscle reactivity, either alone or in combination with relaxant agents. Functional, biochemical, and immunohistochemical approaches were employed. The relaxant effects of probenecid (1 nM-1 mM) were assessed in isolated pig detrusor alone and in combination with inhibitors or antagonists. The effects of probenecid preincubation (0.1, 0.3, and 1 mM) on relaxations induced by cAMP- or cGMP-elevating agents were also evaluated. Probenecid produced concentration-dependent relaxation with a maximal response of 56% and potentiated the relaxations induced by salbutamol, forskolin, riociguat, cilostazol, and tadalafil. Potentiation of salbutamol- and tadalafil-induced relaxations was prevented by the soluble guanylyl cyclase (sGC) inhibitor, ODQ. In detrusor stimulated with sGC modulators, probenecid increased intracellular and reduced extracellular cGMP levels, whereas the cAMP levels were unaffected. Selective pharmacological tools targeting OAT, P2X7, and Panx-1 did not reproduce the potentiating effects of probenecid. Immunofluorescence revealed PDE3A, PDE5, and MRP4 expression in the urothelium, lamina propria, and smooth muscle, with the highest intensity in the urothelium. In conclusion, probenecid potentiates detrusor relaxation, an effect associated with an increased intracellular-to-extracellular cGMP ratio. These findings support further investigation of probenecid, alone or combined with clinically approved agents such as tadalafil or cilostazol, as a potential therapeutic approach for overactive bladder dysfunction.

articles.title: Circulating GDF-15: an intriguing candidate biomarker for the differential diagnosis of ovarian masses.
articles.journal: Clinica chimica acta; international journal of clinical chemistry
articles.authors: Cicolani G, Farina A, Straface G et al.
articles.abstract: Epithelial ovarian cancer (EOC) remains one of the most lethal gynecological malignancies. Growth differentiation factor-15 (GDF-15), a stress-responsive cytokine, has emerged as a potential biomarker in several cancers. However, its biological and diagnostic significance in ovarian pathology remains poorly defined. This retrospective, single-centre, proof-of-concept study aimed to evaluate circulating GDF-15 levels in EOC and benign ovarian cysts (BOC). A total of 48 women with histologically confirmed EOC and 40 patients with BOC were included. Circulating GDF-15 levels were assessed by ELISA and Western blot (WB) analysis. Circulating GDF-15 levels were significantly higher in EOC patients compared with BOC. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis identified an optimal diagnostic threshold of 1020 pg/mL, yielding an Area Under the Curve (AUC) of 0.924 (95% CI: 0.863-0.984) with 93.8% sensitivity and 82.5% specificity (optimism-corrected via bootstrap resampling: 91.2% sensitivity and 80.5% specificity p < 0.0001). Vimentin, was evaluated by WB in serum samples and by immunofluorescence in tumour tissue sections. Vimentin expression was predominantly detected in sera from EOC patients. Immunofluorescence analysis of tumour tissue showed distinct populations of GDF-15-positive and vimentin-positive cells without direct structural colocalization. In conclusion, GDF-15 shows promise as a complementary biomarker within multi-marker panels, assisting with diagnosis in challenging scenarios such as indeterminate adnexal masses and gray zones with borderline or discordant results from conventional markers.

articles.title: Sex-specific associations of classical and 11-oxygenated androgens with body composition and metabolic markers in healthy young adults. The Fit Futures 3 study.
articles.authors: Pettersen T, Fuskevåg OM, Figenschau YA et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Recent studies suggest an association between 11‑oxygenated androgens (11-OxyA) and insulin resistance (IR). However, data from population-based cohorts are scarce. We aimed to investigate the association between circulating 11-OxyA, classical androgens, body composition, and metabolic markers in a population-based cohort of healthy young adults.
METHODS: This study used cross-sectional data from the third Fit Futures Study. Fasting serum samples were analyzed for androgens using liquid chromatography tandem mass spectrometry. Body composition parameters were measured by dual x-ray absorptiometry. Associations between androgens, body composition and metabolic markers were assessed by Pearson's correlation and linear regression analyses. Adjustments were performed for age, lean mass (LM) and fat mass (FM), and in females, combined hormonal contraceptive use.
RESULTS: The study included 334 females and 285 males (median age 27). In males, testosterone (T) was inversely and free androgen index (FAI) positively correlated with BMI and FM, while 11-ketotestosterone and 11β-hydroxyandrostenedione (11OHA4) were positively correlated with FM only. In females, FAI, 11-ketoandrostenedione, and 11OHA4 were positively correlated with LM, and FAI also with FM and BMI. Similarly, T was inversely, while FAI was positively, associated with IR indices, lipids and insulin. Also, 11-OxyA were positively associated with triglycerides and the Triglyceride-Glucose Index, but not with HOMA-IR or other lipids.
CONCLUSION: Although divergent with T, the associations between 11-OxyA and body composition parameters, metabolic markers, and insulin were in the same direction as with FAI, albeit less prominent. Overall, the results suggest weak associations between 11-OxyA and markers of metabolic health in young adults.

articles.title: Prevalence of Muscle loss during and after Pelvic Radiotherapy in Gynecological Cancer Patients.
articles.journal: International journal of radiation oncology, biology, physics
articles.ta: Int J Radiat Oncol Biol Phys
articles.authors: Laan JJ, Westerveld H, Hinnen KA et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Women undergoing pelvic radiotherapy are at risk of developing sarcopenia, defined by muscle loss. In patients treated with radiotherapy for cervical cancer, post-treatment muscle loss has been associated with poorer cancer-specific and overall survival. This study aimed to longitudinally assess sarcopenia and changes in muscle during radiotherapy and follow-up, and to evaluate whether bioelectrical impedance analysis can serve as an accurate bedside alternative to computed tomography (CT) for sarcopenia assessment.
METHODS AND MATERIALS: This prospective cohort study included women with histologically confirmed primary cervical, endometrial, vulvar, or vaginal cancer, all scheduled to undergo external beam radiotherapy (EBRT) with curative intent. Sarcopenia was assessed at baseline, during the last week of EBRT, and at the three- and six-month follow-up. Two methods were used to evaluate sarcopenia: lumbar skeletal muscle index measured via CT scan (gold standard) and appendicular skeletal muscle mass via bioelectrical impedance analysis. Fisher's exact test and the Mann-Whitney U test were used to compare baseline characteristics between women with and without sarcopenia during the last week of radiotherapy.
RESULTS: A total of 31 women were included. Based on CT scans, the prevalence of sarcopenia was 23% at baseline, 32% at the last week of radiotherapy, and 42% at the three-month follow-up. At the six-month follow-up, 29% of the women were sarcopenic. Bioelectrical impedance analysis detected sarcopenia in only 0% to 50% of cases across the various time points. Patients with FIGO stage III were significantly more frequently sarcopenic based on their appendicular skeletal muscle index as assessed by CT scan during the last week of EBRT.
CONCLUSIONS: The prevalence of sarcopenia is high in women treated with radiotherapy for gynecological cancer. An increase in the prevalence of sarcopenia was observed, reaching its highest point at the three-month follow-up. Sarcopenia may be underestimated when assessed using bioelectrical impedance analysis, as indicated by the low sensitivity observed.

articles.title: AI feedback for clinician assessment of umbilical and middle cerebral artery Doppler ultrasound: a multicenter randomized trial.
articles.journal: American journal of obstetrics & gynecology MFM
articles.authors: Bashir Z, Wong CK, Lin M et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Assessment accuracy for umbilical artery (UA) and middle cerebral artery (MCA) Doppler ultrasound assessment depends on operator expertise. Artificial intelligence (AI) based feedback may improve performance, but its effect on assessment accuracy and the role of clinical experience remain uncertain.
OBJECTIVE: To determine whether AI feedback improves assessment accuracy for standardized image-based umbilical artery and middle cerebral artery Doppler vignettes among novice and experienced clinicians.
STUDY DESIGN: This multicenter randomized clinical trial was conducted at five Danish hospitals. Ninety-six clinicians from obstetrics and gynecology departments, including residents, gynecologists, and obstetricians, were randomized 1:1 to AI-generated visual and textual feedback or no AI feedback. Each clinician evaluated 40 standardized image-based Doppler vignettes containing pre-existing static UA and MCA Doppler images. In total, 1,920 unique Doppler vignettes were evaluated across 48 clinician pairs matched by obstetric ultrasound experience. For color Doppler vignettes, clinicians indicated intended gate placement; for spectral Doppler vignettes, they judged waveform technical adequacy. Both are essential components of a technically valid Doppler measurement. No real-time scanning was performed. Intervention clinicians viewed the unannotated image alongside artificial intelligence feedback on gate placement, anatomical suitability, insonation angle, and spectral waveform quality, then entered their own response on the unannotated image. Accuracy was determined by expert consensus using predefined International Society of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology-based criteria. AI feedback was classified as correct or incorrect according to whether it agreed with expert consensus. Expert consensus was based on two fetal medicine sonographers with >10 years of obstetric ultrasound experience, with disagreements resolved by a fetal medicine consultant. Clinicians were classified as novices (<1 year) or experienced (≥1 year) according to duration of obstetric ultrasound experience, irrespective of prior UA or MCA Doppler experience. Secondary analyses examined responses when clinicians followed or did not follow AI feedback, performance with correct and incorrect feedback, and AI-alone performance. Randomized-group differences were compared at clinician level; secondary repeated-vignette analyses used generalized estimating equations.
RESULTS:…

articles.title: Opioid Analgesic Exposure and Mental Health Disorders During Pregnancy: Exploring Their Independent and Joint Association With Adverse Birth Outcomes.
articles.authors: Sznajder KK, Wang Y, Smith ML et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Opioid use, depression and anxiety during pregnancy are independently associated with adverse perinatal outcomes, but their joint associations are less understood.
OBJECTIVE: To examine the independent and joint associations, including interaction, of prenatal opioid analgesic exposure and maternal anxiety and depression with gestational age, preterm birth and birthweight-for-gestational-age percentile.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of 230,810 Wisconsin Medicaid singleton live births (2011-2019), linking Medicaid with birth record data. Multivariable regression models adjusted for maternal sociodemographics, comorbidities and year of delivery. Interaction was assessed using cross-product terms and the relative excess risk due to interaction (RERI). Exposure duration was evaluated for dose-response effects.
RESULTS: Prenatal anxiety, depression and opioid analgesic exposure were independently associated with modest reductions in gestational age and birthweight-for-gestational-age percentile, and increased risk for preterm birth. There was no evidence of interaction between opioid analgesic exposure and anxiety or depression. Individuals with ≥ 90 days of opioid exposure and anxiety or depression had the largest deficits in gestational age (anxiety: -0.29 weeks, 95% confidence interval [CI] -0.49, -0.10; depression: -0.34 weeks, 95% CI -0.53, -0.15) and birthweight-for-gestational-age percentile (anxiety: -4.14, 95% CI -6.63, -1.64; depression: -3.27, 95% CI -5.90, -0.64). For preterm birth, ≥ 90 days of opioid exposure was associated with increased risk among individuals with depression (RR 1.35, 95% CI 1.12, 1.63), whereas among those with anxiety, the association was strongest at 30-89 days of opioid exposure (RR 1.17, 95% CI 1.05, 1.30) and was not associated at ≥ 90 days (RR 1.18, 95% CI 0.97, 1.44).
CONCLUSIONS: Maternal anxiety or depression and prenatal opioid analgesic exposure were each associated with modest but consistent reductions in gestational age and birthweight-for-gestational-age. Individuals with co-occurring mental health conditions and prolonged opioid exposure experienced the greatest reductions, although there was no evidence of statistical interaction.

articles.title: A Rapid Ethnographic Study Exploring the Implementation of Gender-Affirming Hormone Therapy in Primary Care Settings.
articles.journal: Journal of primary care & community health
articles.authors: Humphrey-Straub J, Harris MS, Fauer AJ et al.
articles.abstract: ObjectiveAlthough standards of care recommend that gender-affirming hormone therapy (GAHT) be delivered by primary care providers (PCPs), few studies have specifically examined its implementation in U.S. primary healthcare settings. This study sought to explore how PCPs prescribe GAHT and incorporate it into routine practice.MethodsUsing a rapid ethnographic approach informed by the Theory of Planned Behavior, we conducted clinic observations and in-depth interviews with PCPs (N=17) across seven primary care clinics within two health systems in the U.S. Reflexive thematic analysis was conducted on fieldnotes and interview transcripts.ResultsOne overarching theme emerged: PCPs Use a Collaborative Approach to Incorporate GAHT into Their Practice and Navigate Time Constraints. This theme included two sub-themes: 1) Seeking out Guidance and 2) Adapting Informed Consent to Primary Care Practice. The findings highlight that while most PCPs did not have extensive experience prescribing GAHT, nearly all indicated they were willing incorporate GAHT into their practice, often driven by the values of comprehensive and patient-centered care that defines primary care.ConclusionFindings suggest that PCPs are willing to incorporate GAHT into practice. Organizational support, such as access to experienced colleagues for consultation and guidance, may help leverage this commitment to expand access to gender-affirming care.

articles.title: Association of reproductive factors with disease severity in women with relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis.
articles.authors: Sorosina M, Vanella G, Giliberti A et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: While reproductive factors have been linked to multiple sclerosis (MS) onset and activity, their association with disability remains unclear. We investigated the relationship between reproductive variables and MS severity, measured by the Age-Related Multiple Sclerosis Severity Score (ARMSS).
METHODS: in 242 Italian women with relapsing-remitting MS, reproductive factors (age at menarche, oral contraceptive use, full-term pregnancies and pregnancy losses) were collected through a structured environmental questionnaire. Associations with ARMSS were assessed using linear regression models. Key findings on obstetric factors were replicated in an independent cohort (n = 465).
RESULTS: longer oral contraceptive use before MS onset was associated with lower ARMSS (β = -0.048; p-value = 3.6 × 10-3). Contrasting associations were observed for obstetric factors, with number of full-term pregnancies being associated with lower ARMSS (β = -0.35; p-value = 0.042), while pregnancy losses being associated with higher ARMSS (β = 0.61; p-value = 0.036). Consistently, women with full-term pregnancies only showed lower disability than those with pregnancy losses only (β = -0.72; p-value = 0.026). The association with full-term pregnancies was replicated in the validation cohort (β = -0.44; p-value = 6.55 × 10-3), as well as the lower ARMSS observed in women reporting full-term pregnancies only compared to those reporting pregnancy losses only (β = -0.49; p-value = 0.013).
CONCLUSION: our results highlight how reproductive factors may contribute to individual variability in disease severity.

articles.title: Temporal dynamics of cytokine expression, oxidative stress, and endocrine dysfunction following Escherichia coli-induced epididymo-orchitis in rats.
articles.authors: Nomanzadeh A, Razi M, Hasanzadeh S et al.
articles.abstract: Bacterial epididymo-orchitis (EO) can compromise male reproductive function, but the temporal relationships among testicular inflammatory, oxidative, and endocrine changes remain incompletely characterized. This study examined these changes after Escherichia coli inoculation in rats. Ninety adult male Wistar rats were allocated to untreated control and 100-μL and 200-μL bacterial-inoculum groups and evaluated at 24 h and 1, 2, 3, and 4 weeks (n = 6 per group per time point). Histological, immunohistochemical, immunofluorescent, biochemical, hormonal, and molecular assessments characterized testicular injury, marker-positive cell distributions, immune cell accumulation, redox status, cytokine expression, and Leydig cell-associated endpoints.
