Changes in TAC, MDA, CAT, GSH, GSSG, and IL-10 were reported at 24 h, whereas significant SOD suppression and pro-inflammatory cytokine upregulation were reported from 1 week. The assayed steroid-related transcripts were reported to decrease at 24 h; reduced Leydig cell lipid-associated fluorescence and serum testosterone were apparent from 1 week. CD68-positive cell accumulation was greatest during the early period, particularly at 1 week, whereas CD45-positive leukocyte density peaked at 3 weeks. Testicular injury was accompanied by reduced THY-1- and NANOG-positive cell densities. Differences between inoculum-volume groups varied by endpoint and time point. These findings describe temporal associations among testicular injury and redox, inflammatory, and endocrine changes; they do not establish a causal sequence, functional spermatogonial stem cell depletion, or impaired fertility. The timing of potential clinical interventions requires separate validation.

articles.title: NFYA-transcriptionally activated MTHFD2 promotes cervical cancer progression by inducing mitochondrial dysfunction via AMT.
articles.authors: He Y, Xie T, Zhou F et al.
articles.abstract: Cervical cancer is the fourth most common cancer among women worldwide, and advanced disease remains difficult to treat due to recurrence, metastasis, and drug resistance. Abnormal mitochondrial metabolism, particularly one-carbon folate metabolism, plays a key role in cancer progression. This study investigated the role of MTHFD2, a key enzyme in one-carbon metabolism, in cervical cancer. By integrating transcriptomic data from public databases (GSE9750, GSE63514, TCGA-CESC), we identified 168 persistently upregulated genes mainly enriched in folate one-carbon metabolism pathways. Correlation analysis with a mitochondrial gene database identified four candidate genes, among which MTHFD2 showed the most pronounced upregulation in the three datasets and 20 paired clinical cervical cancer tissues, and was therefore selected for functional studies. Functional experiments in HeLa cells showed that MTHFD2 silencing significantly inhibited proliferation and invasion, promoted apoptosis, and impaired mitochondrial function, including increased reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels and reduced basal mitochondrial respiration and ATP production. Mechanistically, NFYA transcriptionally activated MTHFD2, and MTHFD2 interacted with AMT, upregulating AMT expression and activating the glycine cleavage system (GCS), thereby enhancing mitochondrial metabolism. Consistently, silencing either NFYA or AMT suppressed malignant phenotypes of cancer cells. In vivo, downregulation of NFYA, MTHFD2, or AMT inhibited the growth and mitochondrial metabolism of cervical cancer xenografts. In summary, this study identifies MTHFD2 as a potential therapeutic target for metabolic intervention in cervical cancer and provides new insights into its role in tumor biology.

articles.title: Effectiveness and timing of hatching poultry egg sanitization using a combination of hydrogen peroxide and ultraviolet light.
articles.authors: Cantu K, Coufal CD, Olson EG et al.
articles.abstract: Microbial contamination leads to increased hatching egg mortalities suggesting that sanitation could improve hatchery performance. The objective was to compare fresh and stored commercial broiler hatching egg sanitation on surface and subsurface microbial loads, hatchability, chick quality and 7 d grow-out mortality in 2 independent experiments. Experiment 1 included control (no treatment), sanitized with H2O2/UV advanced oxidative process (AOP) immediately after farm collection (sanitized fresh; SF), and sanitized following 1 d of storage in a farm cooler (S1). Experiment 2 included control, SF, and sanitized after 3 d of egg cooler storage (S3). The control for both experiments consisted of eggs not washed, sanitized, or cleaned. After incubation in the hatchery, on d 21, hatched chicks were enumerated. Chicks were group weighed, evaluated for quality and categorized as those with unhealed navels, culls or without defects. All unhatched eggs were classified as infertile, early dead (0 to 7 d), mid dead (8 to 14 d), late dead (14 to 21 d), pipped or rotten. In Experiment 1, treatments SF and S1 had lower eggshell surface APC and Staphylococcus aureus counts than control (P < 0.01). In Trial 2 SF and S3 reduced surface APC and S. aureus versus control (P < 0.01). In Experiment 2, late embryonic mortality control and S3 averages were lower than SF (P < 0.05). In conclusion, H2O2/UV AOP sanitization reduced surface aerobes and S. aureus without negative effects on embryonic mortality, hatchability, chick quality, and 7 d grow-out bird livability.

articles.title: Integrative mRNA and lncRNA transcriptome analysis of enhanced developmental competence of bovine GV stage oocytes vitrified in liquid helium.
articles.authors: Li X, Yan Q, Yuan B et al.
articles.abstract: Liquid helium (LHe) vitrification improves the post-thaw developmental competence of bovine germinal vesicle (GV) stage oocytes; however, the underlying key transcriptomic regulatory networks still unexplored. This study aimed to evaluate the mRNA and lncRNA transcriptomic and developmental competence of bovine GV stage oocytes vitrified with LHe versus liquid nitrogen (LN). Bovine GV-stage oocytes were vitrified using LHe or LN as the cryogen. Post-thaw developmental competence was assessed following in vitro maturation, in vitro fertilization, and in vitro culture. High-throughput sequencing was performed to profile mRNA and lncRNA expressions between the oocytes vitrified in LHe and LN, followed by functional enrichment and co-expression network analyses. The transcriptomic alterations were independently validated by RT-qPCR. The present study found that LHe vitrification significantly improved cleavage rate (43.0% vs. 33.6%) and blastocyst rate (12.1% vs. 8.5%) compared to LN (p < 0.05). Transcriptomic analysis identified 361 differentially expressed mRNAs and 137 differentially expressed lncRNAs between the two groups. GO and KEGG analyses revealed that these mRNAs were enriched in immune response and metabolic pathways, while the lncRNA target genes were associated with the mitotic DNA integrity checkpoint and homologous chromosome segregation. In silico co-expression network analysis predicted HORMAD1, CDYL, and TRIOBP as potential central hub genes. In conclusion, LHe vitrification enhances the developmental competence of bovine GV-stage oocytes, which may associate with distinct mRNA-lncRNA co-expression networks and specific molecular signatures related to meiotic integrity and stress adaptation. These findings provide valuable transcriptomic resources and potential biomarkers for optimizing oocyte cryopreservation.

articles.title: Identification and validation of circadian rhythm-related diagnostic biomarkers for endometriosis through integrating machine learning and single-cell analysis.
articles.journal: European journal of obstetrics, gynecology, and reproductive biology
articles.ta: Eur J Obstet Gynecol Reprod Biol
articles.authors: Chen D, Xu L, Cheng L et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Endometriosis (EMs) is a chronic inflammatory disease, and the lack of candidate molecular biomarkers remain a major clinical challenge. Circadian rhythm disruption plays a non-negligible role in EMs. However, the diagnostic potential of circadian rhythm-related biomarkers remains insufficiently validated.
METHODS: We performed weighted gene co-expression network analysis to screen for endometriosis-related hub modules. Four machine learning algorithms were used for feature selection in the training cohort, and the resulting diagnostic model was evaluated in three independent GEO validation cohorts. To evaluate the immune microenvironment, we applied MCPcounter, CIBERSORT, and single-sample gene set enrichment analysis. Single‑cell RNA‑seq data were processed with Seurat for cell clustering and annotation, cell‑cell communication networks were constructed using CellChat, and pseudotime trajectory analysis was performed with Monocle.
RESULTS: SMC2, SUV39H2, and TIMELESS were identified as candidate molecular biomarkers, demonstrating favorable diagnostic performance across three independent validation sets. Computational immune infiltration analysis suggested higher enrichment scores for B cells and CD8+ T cells, along with lower scores for Tregs and NK cells in EMs samples. Single-cell analysis revealed an increased proportion of mesenchymal cells in EMs samples and altered cell-cell communication involving BMP, CHEMERIN, and GRN signaling pathways. Pseudotime analysis further suggested transcriptional relationships among distinct stromal cell populations.
CONCLUSION: This study identified SMC2, SUV39H2, and TIMELESS as candidate tissue-based molecular biomarkers for EMs and revealed alterations in stromal cell populations and immune-related features associated with the disease.

articles.title: Implementation and outcomes of tube-sparing surgery for tubal ectopic pregnancy after a national guideline revision: A retrospective cohort study.
articles.journal: European journal of obstetrics, gynecology, and reproductive biology
articles.ta: Eur J Obstet Gynecol Reprod Biol
articles.authors: Talmatch LS, Goulimis AI, Tellum T
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: To assess uptake of salpingotomy for tubal ectopic pregnancy following revision of a national guideline recommending tube-preserving surgery where feasible, and to evaluate patient selection, surgical outcomes and preoperative ultrasound documentation.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of 457 consecutive operations for tubal ectopic pregnancy at a Norwegian tertiary hospital in 2018 and 2022-2025. Outcomes before and after guideline change in January 2024 included documented consideration, attempted and completed salpingotomy, conversion to salpingectomy, operative outcomes, patient selection and sonographic documentation.
RESULTS: Salpingotomy was completed in 36/457 operations (7.9%). After guideline revision, documented consideration increased from 4.9% to 46.6%, attempts from 4.1% to 22.0%, and completed salpingotomy from 3.0% to 14.7% (all p < 0.001). Operative time and hospital stay were similar; operative time was mainly associated with hemoperitoneum and only marginally with operator expertise. Reoperation occurred after 3/36 salpingotomies (8.3%; one case of persistent trophoblast) and 3/421 salpingectomies (0.7%). Women with risk factors for tubal disease were no more likely to undergo salpingotomy than other women (6.6% vs 8.5%, p = 0.59). The ectopic pregnancy was not documented as directly visualized in 41.4% of preoperative ultrasound examinations, and maximum size was documented in 52.5%.
CONCLUSIONS: Salpingotomy increased substantially following guideline revision, but one third of attempts were converted and treatment was not preferentially directed towards women with reduced tubal reserve. Preoperative ultrasound documentation frequently lacked information needed for planned tube-preserving surgery. Guideline implementation should be accompanied by targeted surgical and ultrasound training.

articles.title: Efficacy of low-intensity extracorporeal shockwave therapy for erectile dysfunction: an updated systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized sham-controlled trials.
articles.journal: European journal of obstetrics, gynecology, and reproductive biology
articles.ta: Eur J Obstet Gynecol Reprod Biol
articles.authors: Sánchez-Sierra A, Hernández Solar AF, Martín-García M et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Low-intensity extracorporeal shockwave therapy (Li-ESWT) has emerged as a potentially restorative treatment for erectile dysfunction (ED), particularly in men with vasculogenic disease. However, recent evidence remains inconsistent regarding its effectiveness and durability.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the efficacy of Li-ESWT for improving erectile function in men with ED through a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized placebo-controlled trials.
METHODS: A systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted according to PRISMA 2020 guidelines. PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and CENTRAL were searched to identify randomized controlled trials published between January 2022 and February 2026. Eligible studies included adult men with ED receiving Li-ESWT and compared outcomes with placebo or sham treatment. Erectile function assessed using validated questionnaires was considered the primary outcome. Pooled effect sizes were calculated using Hedges' g and a random-effects model. A leave-one-out sensitivity analysis was performed to assess the robustness of the pooled effect estimate.
RESULTS: Five randomized controlled trials met the inclusion criteria, and four studies involving 226 participants were included in the meta-analysis. Li-ESWT demonstrated a significant short-term improvement in erectile function compared with placebo (Hedges' g = 0.91; 95% CI: 0.61-1.21; p < 0.001). Although most studies reported favorable outcomes, substantial methodological heterogeneity was observed with respect to treatment protocols, shockwave devices, energy settings, and participant characteristics. The leave-one-out sensitivity analysis confirmed that the overall effect was not driven by any single study. The overall certainty of evidence was rated as moderate.
CONCLUSIONS: Li-ESWT may provide clinically meaningful short-term improvements in erectile function among men with probable vasculogenic erectile dysfunction. However, the magnitude of the observed effect should be interpreted with caution given the limited number of available studies and participants. Current evidence remains limited by methodological heterogeneity and relatively small sample sizes. Further high-quality multicenter trials with long-term follow-up are needed to establish the durability of treatment effects and clarify the role of Li-ESWT in clinical practice.

articles.title: Joint CTI-eGDR phenotypes and incident cardiovascular disease in CKM stages 0-3: A retrospective landmark analysis.
articles.authors: Tang N, Hu Y, Cheng S et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The joint cardiometabolic phenotypes of inflammatory-metabolic burden and insulin sensitivity based on repeated measurements their associations with the risk of cardiovascular disease (CVD) among individuals with cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome remain unclear. We aimed to identify joint phenotypes in relation to C-reactive protein-triglyceride-glucose index (CTI) and estimated glucose disposal rate (eGDR) based on repeated measurements and evaluate their associations with incident CVD.
METHODS: This retrospective landmark cohort analysis used prospectively collected CHARLS data from 4883 participants aged ≥45 years with CKM stages 0-3. CTI, eGDR, cumulative CTI (CuCTI), and cumulative eGDR were derived from measurements in 2011 and 2015. K-means clustering of repeated CTI and eGDR measurements was used to identify joint cardiometabolic phenotypes, and Cox models estimated hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Dose-response, subgroup, and sensitivity analyses were performed.
RESULTS: During a median post-landmark follow-up of 5.0 years, 1195 incident CVD events were identified. Three phenotypes were identified: low CTI-high eGDR (n = 2344), high CTI-intermediate eGDR (n = 1351), and intermediate CTI-low eGDR (n = 1188). The K = 3 solution showed high bootstrap reproducibility (median adjusted Rand index, 0.978), although cluster separation was modest. Compared with the first phenotype, the latter two were associated with higher CVD risk after multivariable adjustment (HR 1.25, 95% CI 1.08-1.46; and HR 2.12, 95% CI 1.86-2.42). Both CuCTI and cumulative low-eGDR burden were associated with CVD risk. Findings were generally robust across subgroup and sensitivity analyses.
CONCLUSIONS: Joint CTI-eGDR phenotypes based on repeated measurements were associated with incident CVD, with the intermediate CTI-low eGDR phenotype representing a higher-risk composite cardiometabolic profile.

articles.title: Anticipated and experienced barriers to safe discussion of menopausal symptom management: an exploratory qualitative comparison of premenopausal and postmenopausal women in the UK.
articles.authors: Sutaria A, Thavabalan K, Pierce P et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Menopausal symptoms affect wellbeing across home, healthcare and work, yet barriers to discussing their management remain pervasive. Qualitative research has focused on women already experiencing menopause, leaving the expectations of premenopausal women largely unexamined. This study explored barriers to the safe discussion of menopausal symptom management and compared those anticipated by premenopausal women with those experienced by postmenopausal women.
STUDY DESIGN: This exploratory qualitative study used semi-structured online interviews with 16 women based in the United Kingdom: 11 postmenopausal (median age 56) and five premenopausal (median age 37). Participants were recruited by purposive and snowball sampling and interviewed in April 2022. Reflexive thematic analysis examined similarities and differences between groups, with psychological safety as the organising concept.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Barriers to the safe discussion of symptom management at home, in healthcare and at work.
RESULTS: Four themes were identified: a learned onus to self-endure; a poor information environment; inadequate healthcare engagement; and disclosure contingent on relationship and setting. Even after raising concerns, women described difficulty discussing options or obtaining practical support. Several women felt clinicians had not recognised their symptoms as menopausal. Friends, rather than clinicians, frequently provided the route into care participants found helpful, though access was unevenly distributed. Supportive colleagues enabled workplace adjustments. Premenopausal participants anticipated difficulties resembling those reported by postmenopausal participants.
CONCLUSIONS: Raising a concern did not ensure that options were explored or that useful support followed. Preparation before symptoms begin and accessible, responsive discussion of management both warrant further evaluation.

articles.title: Defining and validating an HPV vaccination motivation score in Kenya and Malawi: A tool for use in low- and middle-income countries.
articles.authors: Moucheraud C, Li G, Ochieng E et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Studies have evaluated reasons for low HPV vaccine uptake globally but use instruments that were validated only in high-income countries. Our objectives were to (1) determine factors associated with vaccination against human papillomavirus (HPV) in two low- and middle-income countries; and (2) use them to develop and validate a simple score to measure motivation to vaccinate one's daughter against HPV.
METHODS: We undertook 3 rounds of data collection: Kenya 2022 (1345 parents/guardians of girls aged 10-16 years, via nationwide mobile phone random-digit dialing), Malawi 2022 (288 parents/guardians of girls aged 9-13 years, via household surveys in three communities), and Kenya 2024 (re-survey of 678 Kenya 2022 respondents who reported having no vaccinated daughters in 2022). The survey included items from the Vaccine Hesitancy Scale-Child and Vaccine Hesitancy Scale-HPV, the Human Papillomavirus Attitudes and Beliefs Scale, and the Wellcome Global Monitor, and parent-reported HPV vaccination of eligible girl(s) in the household.
RESULTS: We found four latent constructs significantly associated with vaccination status in the Kenya 2022 data: Confidence in Vaccine Benefits, Safety Concerns About the HPV Vaccine, Talks About HPV With Others, and Perceives Pro-HPV Vaccination Social Norms. We use these to create an HPV Vaccination Motivation Score; in the Malawi 2022 data (external validity), a 3-point increase in this score was associated with greater odds of having a vaccinated daughter (OR = 1.55; p < 0.0001), and in the Kenya 2024 data (predictive/temporal validity), a 3-point increase in the score was associated with significantly greater odds of vaccination in the intervening two years (OR = 1.14; p = 0.0008).
CONCLUSIONS: This HPV Vaccination Motivation Score can be used to investigate factors associated with HPV vaccination in diverse global settings - and this information can be used to design more effective interventions and programs to increase vaccine coverage and improve health outcomes.

articles.title: Beyond the surgeon's eye: towards a molecular definition of complete cytoreduction in advanced ovarian cancer.
articles.authors: Llueca A

articles.title: Prophylactic extended-field irradiation versus pelvic radiotherapy in high-risk locally advanced cervical cancer with radiologically negative para-aortic lymph nodes: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.authors: Shao H, Zhao Y, Cui T et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare para-aortic recurrence, survival outcomes, and treatment-related toxicity between prophylactic extended-field irradiation (EFI) and pelvic radiotherapy (PRT) in patients with high-risk locally advanced cervical cancer (LACC) who have radiologically negative para-aortic lymph nodes (PALNs).
METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed patients with FIGO 2018 stage III-IVA cervical cancer treated with definitive radiotherapy or concurrent chemoradiotherapy between December 2015 and December 2022. Eligible patients had radiologically negative PALNs and at least one high-risk feature: ≥2 positive pelvic lymph nodes, a maximum pelvic nodal short-axis diameter ≥ 1.5 cm, or pelvic sidewall involvement. Patients received EFI (n = 140) or PRT (n = 153). Survival outcomes were compared using Kaplan-Meier analysis and Cox regression.
RESULTS: Para-aortic recurrence occurred in 2.1% of patients receiving EFI and 11.1% receiving PRT. Five-year PARFS, PFS, and DMFS were higher with EFI than with PRT (97.8% vs 88.1%, P = 0.002; 70.9% vs 58.8%, P = 0.002; and 83.7% vs 75.2%, P = 0.032, respectively). Five-year OS was 79.1% versus 68.6% (P = 0.052). In multivariable analysis, EFI remained associated with improved PFS (HR, 0.532; P = 0.002), DMFS (HR, 0.554; P = 0.036), and PARFS (HR, 0.178; P = 0.006), but not OS (HR, 0.630; P = 0.054). Grade 3-4 leukopenia was more frequent with EFI, whereas other severe toxicities were similar.
CONCLUSIONS: Prophylactic EFI was associated with improved para-aortic control, PFS, and DMFS in high-risk LACC, with acceptable toxicity. These findings support further evaluation of a risk-adapted strategy for selecting patients who may benefit from prophylactic EFI.

articles.title: Combined effects of hatha yoga and astaxanthin on depression, quality of life, and oxidative stress in postmenopausal women: A randomized controlled trial.
articles.authors: Abdulrahman IJ, Abdullah HK
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Menopause is associated with oestrogen deficiency, oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, and depressive symptoms, yet effective non-pharmacological interventions remain limited. This randomized controlled trial investigated the independent and combined effects of Hatha yoga and astaxanthin supplementation on psychological status, oxidative stress, and mitochondrial-related signaling in postmenopausal women.
METHODS: One hundred sedentary postmenopausal women aged 55-60 years with mild-to-moderate depressive symptoms were randomly assigned to four groups for 12 weeks: control (CG), Hatha yoga (HYG; 75 min/session, three sessions weekly), astaxanthin supplementation (ASG; 12 mg/day), or combined Hatha yoga plus astaxanthin (HYASG). The Hatha yoga program included āsana, prāṇāyāma, relaxation, and brief meditation. Outcomes included Hamilton Depression Rating Scale (HAM-D), Menopause Rating Scale (MRS), Menopause-Specific Quality of Life Questionnaire (MENQOL), serum oxidative stress biomarkers (TAC, SOD, CAT, MDA, and TBARS), and peripheral blood expression of SIRT1, PGC-1α, and NRF1 assessed by qRT-PCR.
RESULTS: Significant group × time interactions were observed for all major outcomes (p < 0.001). HYASG demonstrated the greatest improvements, with HAM-D scores decreasing by 45.1%, compared with 28.5% in HYG and 10.9% in ASG. In HYASG, MRS and MENQOL scores decreased by 41.1% and 50.0%, respectively. Combined intervention also produced the largest increases in TAC, SOD, and CAT activities and the greatest reductions in MDA and TBARS concentrations. SIRT1 and PGC-1α expression increased significantly in both yoga-containing groups, whereas NRF1 upregulation was most pronounced in HYASG.
CONCLUSIONS: The combined intervention was associated with greater improvements in depressive symptoms, menopause-related outcomes, serum oxidative-stress biomarkers, and peripheral-blood mitochondrial-related gene expression than either intervention alone.

articles.title: A Multilingual AI-Driven Conversational System for Cervical Cancer Awareness and Risk Assessment: Development and Evaluation Study.
articles.authors: Olorunfemi T, Rashid S, Khashayar P
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cervical cancer is the fourth most common cancer among women globally, with an estimated 660,000 new cases and 350,000 deaths in 2022. It imposes a disproportionate burden on underserved populations in low- and middle-income countries, where language barriers, cultural stigma, and limited access to health care hinder awareness and uptake of preventive measures.
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to design, develop, and evaluate a multilingual AI-driven dialogue system for cervical cancer awareness, personalized risk assessment, and health care facility navigation, targeting underserved populations through a culturally adaptive and privacy-preserving digital health platform.
METHODS: A design science research framework guided the development of a 3-tier, cross-platform system comprising (1) a transparent, rule-based risk-stratification engine whose 30-item questionnaire mirrors the feature schema of the University of California, Irvine (UCI) Cervical Cancer Risk Factors dataset and whose weights encode established clinical risk factors drawn from World Health Organization, US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), and American Cancer Society guidance; (2) a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) chatbot powered by GPT-4o mini; and (3) a geospatial health care facility recommendation module. The system was implemented in TypeScript (NestJS) and Flutter (Google LLC) and deployed across Android, iOS, and web platforms with multilingual support for English, Spanish, Yoruba, and Swahili, of which English, Spanish, and Yoruba were included in the multilingual evaluation reported here. The risk engine was evaluated through clinical face-validity review of its factor weights; chatbot quality was assessed using retrieval precision, hallucination rate, large language model (LLM)-as-a-judge quality scoring, adversarial safety testing, and native-speaker rating of multilingual output.
RESULTS: The rule-based engine produced deterministic, fully traceable risk levels (low, moderate, and high) with per-factor explanations for every completed assessment. The RAG chatbot achieved retrieval precision@3 of 0.88 and a 71.4% reduction in hallucination rate compared with a non-RAG baseline. Automated LLM-as-judge evaluation rated factual correctness at 4.3/5, and independent clinician review of 50 responses identified factual errors in 8% (4/50) of RAG-grounded outputs compared with 28% (14/50) for a non-RAG baseline (Cohen κ=0.84). The geospatial module achieved…

articles.title: Knowledge, Attitudes, and Practices of Male Infertility Patients Regarding Idiopathic Oligoasthenoteratozoospermia.
articles.authors: Zhang F, Liang Z, Li J et al.
articles.abstract: BackgroundIdiopathic oligoasthenoteratozoospermia (iOAT) is common among men with infertility, yet patient awareness remains limited. This study assessed their knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) regarding iOAT.MethodsA cross-sectional study was conducted from October 2023 to July 2024 among male infertility patients to assess their KAP regarding iOAT. Demographic information and KAP data were collected through questionnaires administered to male infertility patients.ResultsA total of 467 valid responses from male infertility patients were included in the final analysis (effective response rate 93.4%). Male infertility patients exhibited inadequate knowledge (median 17, IQR 13-20), generally positive attitudes (median 35, IQR 31-38), and suboptimal practices (median 18, IQR 16-20). Correlation analysis revealed significant positive correlations between knowledge and attitude (r = 0.287, P < 0.001), knowledge and practice (r = 0.293, P < 0.001), and attitude and practice (r = 0.266, P < 0.001).ConclusionMale infertility patients demonstrated inadequate knowledge, generally positive attitudes, and suboptimal practices concerning iOAT, with educational level and income significantly influencing their KAP outcomes.

articles.title: Shape-memory scaffold targets inflammation and fibrosis to restore endometrium and fertility in intrauterine adhesions.
articles.authors: Yang K, Wu H, Ma T et al.
articles.abstract: Intrauterine adhesion (IUA) is a major cause of infertility, yet current treatments remain limited in preventing fibrosis and restoring functional endometrium. We report a bi-drug, bifunctional, biodegradable shape-memory regenerative (BiSMR) scaffold enabling minimally invasive implantation, sequential drug release, and barrier protection. Proteomic profiling of chemical, mechanical, and combined injury models revealed inflammatory activation, extracellular matrix remodeling, and impaired regenerative programs, providing a molecular rationale for combining epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG) with 17β-estradiol (E2). BiSMR couples an E2-loaded PLTG [poly(l-lactide)-co-trimethylene carbonate-co-glycolic acid] backbone with a PDA-EGCG@HAMA coating, enabling rapid EGCG release followed by sustained E2 delivery. In vitro, BiSMR promoted cell proliferation, migration, angiogenesis, and M2 polarization while suppressing myofibroblast transition. In rat IUA models, BiSMR restored endometrial structure and vascularization, reduced fibrosis, and improved implantation and live birth rates. Proteomics revealed down-regulation of fibrosis- and inflammation-related effectors and restoration of protein biosynthesis and regenerative pathways. BiSMR offers a promising strategy for IUA therapy and fertility restoration.

articles.title: Who will step up? A cross-sectional study on factors associated with medical students' willingness to provide abortion care.
articles.authors: Baumgart M, Rohmann A, Rutenkröger M et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The decreasing number of physicians performing abortions in Germany limits access to high-quality care for individuals with unintended pregnancy seeking abortions. To address the barriers preventing higher participation in abortion care, the aim of this study was to quantitatively explore the attitudes of medical students towards abortion. Furthermore, factors associated with medical students' attitudes towards abortion and their willingness to participate in abortion care were examined based on intergroup contact theory and the theory of planned behaviour.
METHODS: A Germany-wide online survey was conducted. Validated scales and single items were translated into German using the TRAPD protocol and adapted for medical students via cognitive interviews (n = 10). Survey data from n = 233 medical students were analysed using descriptive statistics, regression, and mediation analyses with abortion attitudes and willingness to provide abortion care as criteria.
RESULTS: Participants had overall positive attitudes towards abortion. Female gender and low religiosity were associated with positive attitudes. Fear of stigmatisation and perceived knowledge were negatively associated with attitudes towards abortion. Positive attitudes towards abortion were significantly associated with higher willingness to participate in abortion care. The association between attitudes and contact, as well as the expected mediation effects of fear of stigmatisation, perceived knowledge and perspective-taking, were nonsignificant.
CONCLUSIONS: This study demonstrates the association of medical students' attitudes towards abortion with their willingness to participate in abortion care in the future. However, lack of perceived knowledge and fear of stigmatisation may represent barriers for young physicians to provide abortion care in their later work life. Addressing structural barriers with targeted interventions and training programmes is essential that young physicians feel equipped, supported and safe to provide abortion care.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: The study was registered via AsPredicted.org prior to data collection (September 8th, 2023). Trial registration number: 142964.

articles.title: Sperm phospholipase C signaling via PLCζ1 and PLCδ4 is essential for Ca2+ oscillations and fertility in mice.
articles.authors: Gupta N, Zhang L, Akizawa H et al.
articles.abstract: Fertilization-induced calcium (Ca2+) oscillations are essential for egg activation and embryonic development in mammals. The sperm-specific phospholipase C isoform, PLCζ1, is the primary trigger of these oscillations. Functional and clinical studies have linked mutations or reduced expression of PLCζ1 to male infertility. However, whether PLCζ1 alone accounts for Ca2+ release at fertilization in all mammals remains uncertain. Male mice lacking Plcζ1 exhibit subfertility and reduced litter sizes; their sperm induce delayed, low-frequency Ca2+ oscillations, indicating a compensatory mechanism. Notably, mouse sperm express high levels of PLCδ4, essential for completing the acrosome reaction (AR). In Plcζ1-null sperm, PLCδ4 is upregulated and retained post-AR. These observations suggest a secondary functional role for PLCδ4. Using CRISPR/Cas9 genome editing, we generated Plcδ4 knockout (KO) mice. Plcδ4-null sperm trigger attenuated, delayed Ca2+ oscillations and significantly reduced fertilization rates, indicating that PLCδ4 contributes to but does not independently drive Ca2+ signaling. We therefore generated a Double Knockout (DKO) mouse line lacking both sperm-enriched PLCs. DKO males were sterile, with sperm failing to induce Ca2+ oscillations, and the isolated residual Ca2+ rise was insufficient to activate eggs. These findings reveal that PLCζ1, the primary oscillator, and PLCδ4, a compensatory factor, work cooperatively within a complex, multi-component PLC system that ensures robust fertilization. This work reveals molecular specialization among mammals in initiating the fertilization Ca2+ signals. It has implications for understanding male infertility, improving assisted reproductive technologies, and developing contraceptive strategies.

articles.title: A coupled model to value indirect impacts of maternal, newborn and child health interventions.
articles.authors: Walsh T, Vogel JP, Makama M et al.
articles.abstract: Outcomes associated with maternal, newborn and child health (MNCH) conditions have improved significantly over the past 20 years, however, they are not on track to meet the global SDG targets by 2030. Emerging interventions have the potential to greatly increase access to care, but estimating their impacts is difficult due to complicated interactions between interventions. Models exist to quantify outcomes and costs associated with scaling up interventions related to MNCH (e.g., The Lives saved tool (LiST)), but none have been designed to flexibly integrate novel interventions. This study aimed to develop a model that can estimate the impact of standard-of-care (SOC) and novel interventions on MNCH conditions, and present an example use case. We developed a compartment-based model with 15 interconnected population- and condition-specific modules for pregnant women (in different trimesters), newborns and children <5 years to quantify impacts of bespoke novel interventions. The model included modules for anemia, pre-eclampsia, obstructed labour, hemorrhage, maternal sepsis, preterm, small-for-gestation-age (SGA), respiratory distress syndrome (RDS), neonatal sepsis, birth asphyxia, wasting (neonates and children), stunting and modules that captures neonatal and childhood conditions not captured elsewhere in the model. The model captures dynamic interactions between MNCH conditions, including across trimesters, and accounts for the full impact of early detection and prevention of conditions during pregnancy. In an example use case, the model identified that scaling-up standard-of-care and novel diagnostic interventions for anemia and pre-eclampsia plus AI-ultrasound (for early detection of obstructed labour, hemorrhage and birth outcome risks, leading to facility referrals) to 60% could avert 207 million DALYs globally over 2024-2040. We have developed a modelling tool which can be flexibly adapted to assess the impacts of novel interventions for MNCH conditions, and can be applied at a global, regional, national or sub-national level.

articles.title: PINN-based functional inference in size-structured population models: Application to fish oogenesis.
articles.authors: Fostier L, Lesage M, Thermes V et al.
articles.abstract: Early oogenesis in juvenile fish establishes the ovarian reserve, which conditions lifelong reproductive capacity. This process is regulated by local hormonal feedback mechanisms, mainly involving Anti-Müllerian Hormone (AMH). In this work, we develop a mechanistic size-structured population model describing an unstructured germ-cell compartment and a population of growing oocytes, with AMH feedback on the renewal of the precursor cells compartment. Using repeated cross-sectional observations of oocyte size distributions in fish ovaries, we formulate and solve a nonlinear inverse problem with Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) to infer three demographic functions: the size-dependent oocyte growth rate, the AMH-regulated net renewal rate of the precursor cells compartment, and the recruitment rate of new oocytes. We introduce an auxiliary PINN formulation to handle the nonlocal interaction term and jointly infer unobserved state variables and demographic functions. Our inference strategy combines non-parametric PINNs with a data-guided model-selection step: demographic functions are first inferred without prescribing their functional forms, and the learned profiles are then used to select parsimonious parametric laws, whose parameters are subsequently estimated within a parametric PINN. We investigate identifiability at both the functional and parametric levels, combining structural identifiability analysis with synthetic-data experiments assessing the practical recovery of functions and parameters. The inference procedure is embedded within an individual-level bootstrap framework to assess sensitivity to repeated-cross-sectional sampling and stochastic training. Applied to juvenile fish oogenesis, the framework recovers interpretable growth and renewal dynamics, provides access to unobserved quantities, and enables conditional in silico investigation. More broadly, this work provides a framework for functional and parametric inference in size-structured population models with nonlocal interactions from sparse cross-sectional data.

articles.title: Efficacy of diadynamic currents versus transcutaneous electrical nerve stimulation for transcutaneous tibial nerve stimulation in subjects with overactive bladder syndrome: A double-blind randomized controlled trial.
articles.authors: Tedla JS, Lalaji SL, Midde AK et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In the traditional treatment of overactive bladder (OAB) with transcutaneous posterior tibial nerve stimulation (TTNS), physical therapists currently use only transcutaneous electrical nerve stimulation (TENS). However, the literature has commonly replaced TENS with diadynamic currents for various musculoskeletal pain syndromes. Moreover, no literature describes the use of diadynamic currents in the TTNS procedure. Therefore, our study aimed to determine the efficacy of diadynamic currents (DDC) versus TENS for TTNS in OAB Treatment.
METHODOLOGY: A randomized controlled trial was conducted among female patients with OAB aged 18-80 years. Subjects were randomly allocated to control and experimental groups. Participants in the control group received TTNS with TENS, and those in the experimental group underwent TTNS using DDC. Both groups received 8 TTNS sessions, two per week for 4 weeks. We measured pre- and post-intervention improvements using the International Consultation on Incontinence Questionnaire (ICIQ) for OAB and the ICIQ OAB Quality of Life (QOL). The study is registered with the Clinical Trials Registry of India under registration number CTRI/2025/12/099269.
RESULTS: The mean age of the included sample was 59.75 years. Pre- and post-intervention ICIQ-OAB and ICIQ-OAB QOL scores showed significant improvements in disease symptoms and quality of life among patients with OAB in both the control and experimental groups. Comparison of improvements between the two groups on the ICIQ questionnaires showed no significant difference (p-values of 0.87 and 0.95). Correlations between patient-related characteristics and improvements in outcome measures were also not significant.
CONCLUSION: Eight sessions of TENS and DDC, combined with conventional physical therapy, including Kegel and breathing exercises, can reduce OAB symptoms and improve QOL in subjects with OAB syndrome. Diadynamic current can be used as an adjunct to conventional TENS in TTNS for treating OAB syndrome.

articles.title: Harrowing experiences of vagina fistula victims in the Kpandai District of Ghana: A qualitative study.
articles.authors: Ahorsu EE, Adeti J, Selasie EK et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Vaginal fistula (VF), particularly vesicovaginal fistula (VVF), remains a significant reproductive health challenge in many low-resource settings, including the Kpandai District of Ghana. Despite its profound physical and psychosocial impact, the lived experiences of affected women in rural districts remain under-documented.
AIM: This study explored the lived experiences of women diagnosed with vesicovaginal fistula in the Kpandai District of Ghana, focusing on their physical, emotional, and social challenges, as well as coping strategies.
METHODS: A qualitative descriptive study was conducted using in-depth interviews with ten women with clinically confirmed VVF. Participants were initially identified through a district health facility and subsequently recruited using a combination of purposive and snowball sampling techniques. Interviews were audio-recorded, transcribed verbatim, and analysed thematically.
RESULTS: Prolonged and obstructed labour-often occurring at home-emerged as the primary reported cause of VVF. Cultural beliefs, gender-based decision-making dynamics, limited access to healthcare, and financial constraints were key barriers to timely medical intervention. Consequences included persistent urinary incontinence, social stigma, emotional trauma, marital dissolution (reported by eight participants), loss of livelihood, and social isolation. Coping strategies included frequent washing, use of absorbent materials, and reliance on perfumes or herbal remedies.
CONCLUSIONS: Vesicovaginal fistula remains a devastating yet largely preventable condition in rural Ghana. The findings highlight the need to strengthen maternal health services, improve timely referral systems, and integrate psychosocial support within community-based care frameworks.

articles.title: RPL22 mutation is a favourable prognostic subset within mismatch repair-deficient endometrial cancer: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.journal: Journal of obstetrics and gynaecology : the journal of the Institute of Obstetrics and Gynaecology
articles.authors: Lu CC, Tang WJ, Chao AS et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although mismatch repair-deficient (dMMR) endometrial cancers are highly immunogenic and commonly responsive to immune checkpoint inhibitors, their heterogeneous outcomes indicate that dMMR status alone is insufficient to predict therapeutic benefit. The RPL22 gene - frequently mutated in microsatellite instability-high tumours - represents a candidate biomarker whose prognostic significance in dMMR endometrial cancer remains largely unexplored.
METHODS: In this retrospective cohort study, we analysed 250 patients with immunohistochemically confirmed dMMR endometrial cancer diagnosed between 2008 and 2022. The RPL22 p.K15Rfs*5 mutation was detected by Sanger sequencing and analysed in relation to MMR protein expression pattern, histologic subtype, treatment modality, recurrence pattern, cancer-specific survival (CSS), and progression-free survival (PFS).
RESULTS: RPL22 mutations were identified in 78.4% (196/250) of dMMR tumours, at a comparable frequency in MLH1-PMS2-deficient (79.2%) and MSH2-MSH6-deficient (76.1%) cases (p = 0.596), and were unrelated to FIGO stage, treatment, or recurrence pattern. RPL22-mutant tumours had significantly better CSS (p < 0.001) and PFS (p = 0.002) than wild-type tumours. MLH1-PMS2-deficient tumours showed worse CSS than MSH2-MSH6-deficient tumours (p = 0.008); within this subgroup, RPL22-mutant tumours had better CSS and PFS than wild-type tumours (p < 0.001 and p = 0.005, respectively). In aggressive histologic subtypes, RPL22 mutations were associated with better CSS (p = 0.003). In multivariable analysis including FIGO stage, RPL22 mutations remained independently associated with better CSS (HR = 0.14; 95% CI, 0.05-0.43; p = 0.001) and PFS (HR = 0.43; 95% CI, 0.23-0.81; p = 0.009).
CONCLUSIONS: In this hypothesis-generating retrospective cohort, the RPL22 p.K15Rfs*5 mutation identified a favourable prognostic subset within dMMR endometrial cancers, particularly among MLH1-PMS2-deficient tumours and aggressive histologic subtypes. Because treatment was not modelled and cancer-specific deaths were few, prospective validation in treatment-annotated cohorts is required before routine clinical implementation.

articles.title: Introduction of contraceptive implants as a family planning strategy in Honduras and Chiapas: Results from the Salud Mesoamerica Initiative (SMI).
articles.authors: Santoro A, Basualdo N, Rolón F et al.
articles.abstract: Expanding access to a broad range of contraceptive methods is critical for reducing unintended pregnancies and improving reproductive health. This study evaluates the introduction of subdermal contraceptive implants in the selected areas of Honduras and Chiapas, Mexico, in the context of the Salud Mesoamérica Initiative, a results-based financing program focused on disadvantaged populations. Data were obtained from household surveys conducted between 2012 and 2022 among women aged 15-49 years in selected intervention and comparison municipalities in Chiapas, Mexico, and Honduras, using a two-stage sampling design. Indicators included contraceptive prevalence rates, reasons for method switching, and adoption by sociodemographic characteristics. Findings show a substantial increase in implant use in both settings over time. In the selected areas of Honduras, implant uptake increased gradually, reaching 7.9% in the 2022 SMI household survey, while in the selected areas of Chiapas use rose to 7.2%. Younger women aged 20-29 years and those with full literacy exhibited the highest adoption rates. In the selected areas of Chiapas and Honduras, implants most often replaced non-modern and short-acting hormonal methods, suggesting successful integration into the existing method mix. Variations in adoption across sociodemographic subgroups highlight persistent inequities. The results underscore the potential of subdermal implants to expand access to long-acting reversible contraception in resource-limited settings. To sustain and enhance this progress, strategies must address sociocultural and structural barriers, ensuring equitable access across all population groups and mitigating service disruptions. These findings may inform future strategies to expand informed contraceptive choice in similar resource-limited settings; their effects on reproductive health outcomes require further evaluation.

articles.title: Reproductive Health in Monogenic Kidney Disease: Practical Guidance for Fertility, Genetic Counseling, and Pregnancy Care.
articles.journal: Clinical journal of the American Society of Nephrology : CJASN
articles.authors: Lobo AS, Norouzi S, Shah S
articles.abstract: Monogenic kidney diseases, including autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD), Alport spectrum disorders, Fabry disease, and monogenic podocytopathies presenting as focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (FSGS), increasingly affect people of reproductive age. Reproductive care extends beyond pregnancy to fertility, menstrual and sexual health, contraception, assisted reproduction, inheritance counseling, and long-term shared decision-making. This review uses these four disease groups to illustrate distinct counseling challenges arising from autosomal dominant, X-linked, autosomal recessive, and genetically heterogenous inheritance, including the underrecognized disease burden in heterozygous women with X-linked Alport syndrome or Fabry's disease. Across diseases, adverse maternal and fetal outcomes are driven primarily by reduced kidney function, chronic hypertension, proteinuria, prior preeclampsia and major extrarenal disease, whereas genotype, inheritance pattern, and syndromic features further shape counseling and reproductive genetic decisions. Preconception counseling should integrate maternal risk stratification; discontinuation or planned transition of fetotoxic agents, such as renin-angiotensin system inhibitors, tolvaptan, SGLT2 inhibitors, mycophenolate, and migalastat; and genetic counseling that addresses recurrence risk, cascade testing, and reproductive options, including prenatal diagnosis and preimplantation genetic testing for monogenic disorders (PGT-M). During pregnancy, close co-management by nephrology, maternal-fetal medicine, and genetics is essential to control blood pressure, provide low-dose aspirin prophylaxis, monitor kidney function and proteinuria, distinguish preeclampsia from progressive glomerular disease, and anticipate disease-specific complications such as cyst infection, intracranial aneurysm, nephrotic syndrome, and cardiac arrhythmia. Postpartum care should include medication re-optimization, breastfeeding counseling, kidney and cardiovascular surveillance, and revisiting contraception and future reproductive goals. Reproductive decision-making should be nondirective and centered on patient values, access to care, and tolerance for uncertainty. Evidence remains limited, largely retrospective, and enriched for milder disease, particularly regarding fertility outcomes, male reproductive implications, the reproductive safety of emerging targeted therapies, and genotype-specific pregnancy risk, underscoring the…

articles.title: Drug Therapies and Incidence of Dementia Among Adults With Overactive Bladder.
articles.authors: Sheyn D, Rhodes S, Mohamed Z et al.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Concern that anticholinergic medications for overactive bladder (OAB) are associated with increased dementia risk has encouraged a shift toward β3 adrenergic agonists, which are presumed cognitively safer. Whether this presumption is justified is uncertain.
OBJECTIVE: To compare the risk of incident dementia among adults initiating high-risk anticholinergic, low-risk anticholinergic, or β3 agonist therapy for OAB and to evaluate the association of treatment duration with risk.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This retrospective cohort study used Epic Cosmos electronic health record data from 2012 to 2025. Adults aged 40 to 90 years newly treated for OAB within 1 year of diagnosis without preexisting dementia were included.
EXPOSURES: First prescribed medication class: high-risk anticholinergics (oxybutynin, tolterodine, or solifenacin), low-risk anticholinergics (darifenacin, trospium, or fesoterodine), or β3 agonists (mirabegron or vibegron).
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Incident dementia by diagnosis code or dementia-specific medication. Inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) and Cox proportional hazards models were used, with analyses stratified by age and sex and an exploratory landmark duration-response analysis.
RESULTS: Among 830 393 patients (585 198 female [70.5%]; median [IQR] age, 67 [57-76] years), incident dementia occurred in 65 134 patients, with a median (IQR) follow-up ranging from 1046 (571-1809) days for β3 agonists to 1568 (857-2614) days for high-risk anticholinergics. After IPTW, high-risk anticholinergics were associated with a lower hazard of dementia than β3 agonists (hazard ratio [HR], 0.90; 95% CI, 0.87-0.93) and low-risk anticholinergics (HR, 0.93; 95% CI, 0.90-0.96); low-risk anticholinergics did not differ from β3 agonists (HR, 0.97; 95% CI, 0.93-1.01). Weighted 10-year dementia risk was highest for β3 agonists (20.0%; 95% CI, 18.8%-21.2%) and lowest for high-risk anticholinergics (18.1%; 95% CI, 17.9%-18.3%). E-values of 1.29 (high-risk anticholinergics vs β3 agonists) and 1.20 (high-risk vs low-risk anticholinergics) suggested that observed differences could be explained by a modest amount of unmeasured confounding. Longer anticholinergic duration was not associated with increased risk.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this cohort study of patients undergoing treatment for OAB, β3 agonists were not associated with a lower dementia incidence compared with anticholinergics. These findings suggest that…

articles.title: The metabolic role of prolactin in pregnancy.
articles.authors: Scairati R, Del Vecchio G, Verde N et al.
articles.abstract: Prolactin has evolved from being viewed solely as a lactogenic hormone to being recognized as a key regulator of maternal metabolic adaptation during pregnancy.However, clinical studies have reported apparently conflicting associations between circulating prolactin and gestational diabetes, maternal adiposity and metabolic health, limiting its clinical interpretation despite compelling experimental evidence for its metabolic effects.Experimental models demonstrate that prolactin receptor (Prlr) signalling regulates pregnancy-induced β-cell expansion and insulin secretion, adipose tissue remodelling and maternal energy allocation, while also contributing to the endocrine network governing calcium homeostasis and skeletal adaptation. By contrast, human studies show heterogeneous relationships between circulating prolactin and glucose homeostasis, gestational diabetes, adiposity and lipid metabolism, with limited evidence linking physiological prolactin concentrations to maternal bone remodelling.These discrepancies may partly reflect dynamic changes in prolactin across gestation and differences in maternal metabolic phenotype. Accounting for gestational timing and metabolic context may therefore improve the interpretation of circulating prolactin and help define its contribution to maternal metabolic adaptation across pregnancy and lactation.

articles.title: MRI-based deep-learning radiomics nomogram for differentiating FIGO 2023 stage I from stage II-IV endometrial cancer: a multicenter study.
articles.authors: Chu X, Gao L, Wang X et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Preoperative identification of FIGO 2023 stage I endometrial cancer (EC) is important for treatment planning. We aimed to develop and validate a deep-learning radiomics nomogram (DLRN) based on multiparametric MRI to distinguish stage I EC from stage II-IV disease.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This study retrospectively enrolled patients from three centers. Patients from Centers 1 and 2 were randomly split into a training set (n = 616), and an internal test set (n = 158), and Center 3 served as an external test set (n = 232). The DLRN integrated deep-learning features, intratumoral and peritumoral radiomics features, and clinical characteristics. The DLRN was compared with clinical, radiomics, and deep-learning models. Discrimination was evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), with AUCs compared using DeLong's test.
RESULTS: A total of 1006 patients (mean age, 56.5 ± 9.7 years) were analyzed. In the internal test set, the DLRN achieved an AUC of 0.852, higher than the clinical (0.673; p = 0.001), original radiomics (0.765; p = 0.030), and combined radiomics (0.793; p = 0.050) models. In the external test set, the DLRN remained robust (AUC = 0.829) and outperformed the clinical, original radiomics, and combined radiomics models (AUC = 0.680, 0.681, and 0.743; all p < 0.005). With DLRN assistance, radiologists showed improved diagnostic performance.
CONCLUSION: The MRI-based DLRN showed robust discrimination between FIGO 2023 stage I and stage II-IV EC across test sets, supporting its potential for preoperative risk stratification and decision support.
KEY POINTS: Question The introduction of the FIGO 2023 staging system has made the differentiation between stages more challenging, highlighting the need for better tools. Findings A new MRI-based deep-learning radiomics nomogram (DLRN) accurately identifies high-risk patients, significantly outperforming traditional and individual clinical prediction methods. Critical relevance statement This tool helps doctors make better preoperative treatment plans, potentially improving patient outcomes in endometrial cancer.

articles.title: Borrelia-specific cell-free DNA in plasma from adults with Lyme neuroborreliosis: an explorative study.
articles.journal: European journal of clinical microbiology & infectious diseases : official publication of the European Society of Clinical Microbiology
articles.ta: Eur J Clin Microbiol Infect Dis
articles.authors: Fjordside L, Pedersen MS, Ellegaard K et al.
articles.abstract: Current blood-based diagnostic modalities for LNB have significant limitations. Using Next Generation Sequencing, we investigated blood samples from patients with LNB and non-LNB controls for Borrelia burgdorferi-specific cfDNA (Bb-cfDNA). Blood-samples from 61 adults suspected for LNB were analysed with amplification-free Nanopore metagenomic sequencing and detected cfDNA was cross-referenced with human and Bb-genome databases to identify Bb-specific-cfDNA. Bb-cfDNA was detected in 3 of 45 patients with LNB (6.7%) and in none of the 16 controls. Positive samples contained low levels of Borrelia-classified reads. Bb-cfDNA is unlikely to become a relevant blood-based diagnostic test for LNB in immunocompetent adults.

articles.title: The effects of androgen replacement therapy on tear osmolarity and ocular surface parameters in androgen deficiency.
articles.authors: Kalyoncu M, Arıtürk N, Yeter V et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate ocular surface findings in androgen deficiency and assess changes after androgen replacement therapy (ART).
METHODS: This study included 77 male participants, with only the right eye of each subject evaluated. Serum total testosterone levels were measured, and participants were categorized as Group 1 (testicular hypofunction, n = 37, testosterone < 231 ng/dL) and Group 2 (eugonadal controls, n = 40, testosterone > 346 ng/dL). AMS and OSDI scores were recorded. Ophthalmologic examinations included BCVA, IOP, Meibomian Gland Dysfunction- Grading System (MGD-GS) score, corneal staining, TBUT, Schirmer I/II tests, and tear osmolarity. Anterior segment OCT assessed inferior tear meniscus parameters. Group 1 received intramuscular testosterone (Sustanon 250 mg) every two weeks, and evaluations were repeated at Weeks 6 and 18. Correlations between testosterone levels and ocular surface parameters were analyzed.
RESULTS: At baseline, AMS and OSDI scores, MGD-GS score, corneal staining and tear osmolarity were significantly higher in Group 1. At the same time, Schirmer I/II values, TBUT, tear meniscus area (TMA), tear meniscus height (TMH), and tear meniscus depth (TMD) were lower (p < 0.05). After ART, testosterone levels increased significantly, with AMS and OSDI scores, tear osmolarity, MGD-GS score and corneal staining decreasing (p < 0.05). Schirmer I/II, TMA, TMH and TMD increased (p < 0.05). TBUT increased; however, the difference was not statistically significant (p > 0.05). Testosterone levels correlated negatively with AMS, OSDI, and tear osmolarity (r = - 0.656, - 0.497, - 0.597) and weakly with MGD-GS score and corneal staining (r = - 0.351, - 0.342). Positive correlations were observed with TBUT, Schirmer II, TMA, TMH and TMD.
CONCLUSION: Androgen deficiency significantly impacts ocular surface health, particularly in dry eye disease. ART was associated with favorable changes in several ocular surface parameters and symptoms in individuals with androgen deficiency, supporting a potential role of androgens in ocular surface homeostasis.

articles.title: Effects of intradermal lymphocyte therapy in patients with recurrent pregnancy loss: secondary analysis of a randomized controlled trial investigating purinergic signaling, inflammation, and cellular energy status.
articles.authors: Yildirim O, Gundogdu H, Abbas-Kabiri D et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Recurrent pregnancy loss (RPL), a multifactorial and complex reproductive disorder, is diagnosed when there are two or more documented back-to-back failed pregnancies. Intradermal lymphocyte therapy (ILT) emerged as a promising intervention, aiming to modulate the intricate immunological milieu implicated in RPL. This study was designed to assess the effects of ILT on pregnancy and live birth rate and also provide insight into potential immunometabolic mechanisms underlying the clinical efficacy of lymphocyte therapy in RPL.
METHODS: The study included 100 patients with RPL, who received ILT (treated group, n = 50) or routine treatment (untreated group, n = 50), as well as 30 healthy women with a history of successful pregnancy as a control group. Low-dose ILT (Three injections of 20 × 10^6 PBMCs) was administered according to a standardized protocol, and flow cytometric analysis of CD39 and CD73 expression, ELISA measurement for serum levels of TNF-α, TGF-β, IL-1, and IL-10, as well as intracellular ATP and AMP using commercially available enzymatic colorimetric assay kits, were conducted.
RESULTS: Pregnancy and live birth rate were significantly higher in the treated group compared with the untreated group (p < 0.001). In patients with successful pregnancy, across all measured cytokines (TNF-α, TGF-β, IL-1, and IL-10), as well as ATP/AMP ratio and CD39⁺CD73⁺ cell frequency, treated patients exhibited significant pre- to post-treatment changes, whereas routine treatment patients showed no statistically meaningful differences. After treatment, between-group differences were statistically significant across all measured outcomes, although the level of statistical significance varied across outcomes.
CONCLUSION: Low-dose ILT may be associated with improved successful pregnancy and live birth rates in RPL patients. These clinical outcomes coincided with changes in purinergic signaling, inflammatory cytokines, and cellular energy status; however, formal mediation cannot be inferred from the present analysis.

articles.title: Postpartum repair of umbilical hernias following conservative management during pregnancy: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.journal: Hernia : the journal of hernias and abdominal wall surgery
articles.authors: Almulhim A, Almulhim S, Alarfaj H
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The optimal timing of elective umbilical hernia repair following conservative management during pregnancy remains controversial. Physiological postpartum changes, including persistent abdominal wall laxity and elevated intra-abdominal pressure, may influence surgical outcomes and recurrence risk. This study evaluated the clinical outcomes and impact of surgical timing on postpartum umbilical hernia repair.
METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted at a tertiary referral center between January 2010 and December 2018. Pregnant women diagnosed with umbilical hernia were initially managed conservatively unless emergent intervention was required. Patients subsequently underwent elective open mesh repair during the postpartum period. Primary outcome was hernia recurrence. Secondary outcomes included operative time, length of hospital stay (LOS), postoperative pain assessed using the Visual Analog Scale (VAS), and perioperative complications. Statistical analysis was performed using ANOVA, Chi-square, and Fisher's exact tests.
RESULTS: A total of 114 women underwent elective postpartum umbilical hernia repair following conservative management during pregnancy. Mean age was [Formula: see text] years, and mean BMI was 38.8 kg/m², with most patients classified as obese and multiparous. Overall recurrence rate was 3.5% (n = 4). All recurrences occurred either in patients undergoing early repair (< 6 months postpartum) or in those who became pregnant within one year after surgery. Delayed repair was associated with significantly improved perioperative outcomes. Mean operative time decreased from 145 min in the early repair group to 91 min in patients repaired after 24 months postpartum (p < 0.001). Mean LOS decreased from 49 to 30 h (p < 0.001). Patients undergoing delayed repair also demonstrated significantly lower postoperative pain scores (VAS 3.2 vs. 6.8, p < 0.001) and reduced postoperative complication rates. No recurrences were observed in women who delayed subsequent pregnancy for more than two years after repair.
CONCLUSION: Elective postpartum umbilical hernia repair following conservative management during pregnancy is safe and associated with favorable perioperative outcomes. Delayed repair was associated with reduced operative complexity, postoperative pain, and complications. Although recurrence events were observed predominantly after early repair or subsequent early pregnancy, larger prospective studies are required to clarify…

articles.title: IGF2BP1-mediated stability of TMEM165 promotes the migration and invasion of trophoblast cells.
articles.authors: Yang C, Liu L, Deng C et al.
articles.abstract: Preeclampsia (PE) is a serious pregnancy-related hypertensive disorder characterized by insufficient trophoblast invasion, yet the underlying molecular mechanisms remain incompletely understood. This study aims to investigate the role of transmembrane protein 165 (TMEM165) and its regulatory mechanism in trophoblast migration and invasion within the context of PE. We examined TMEM165 and insulin-like growth factor 2 mRNA-binding protein 1 (IGF2BP1) expression in eight normal and eight preeclamptic placental tissues using qPCR and western blotting. The CCK8 assay was performed for assessing cell viability, while cell migration and invasion capabilities were examined via wound-healing and Transwell assays. RNA immunoprecipitation (RIP), RNA pull-down, and actinomycin D assays were used to validate the IGF2BP1-TMEM165 interaction and mRNA stability. Our results showed that TMEM165 and IGF2BP1 were significantly downregulated in PE placentas and exhibited a strong positive correlation. Overexpression of TMEM165 enhanced trophoblast viability, migration, and invasion, accompanied by upregulation of MMP2, MMP3, N-cadherin, and vimentin, while TMEM165 knockdown produced the opposite effects. Mechanistically, IGF2BP1 directly bound to TMEM165 mRNA and prolonged its half-life, as demonstrated by RIP, RNA pull-down, and actinomycin D decay assays. Rescue experiments confirmed that IGF2BP1 promoted trophoblast migration and invasion through TMEM165 stabilization. Collectively, these findings identify the IGF2BP1-TMEM165 axis as a novel regulator of trophoblast motility, offering new mechanistic insights into PE pathogenesis and suggesting potential therapeutic targets for PE intervention.

articles.title: Obliterative versus Reconstructive Surgery for Advanced Pelvic Organ Prolapse in Older Women: A Systematic Review for Preference-Sensitive Surgical Decision-Making.
articles.authors: Wang Q, Jiang X, Lin C
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION AND HYPOTHESIS: The choice between obliterative and reconstructive surgery for older women with advanced pelvic organ prolapse is preference sensitive. This review synthesized comparative evidence across perioperative safety, durability, urinary, bowel/anorectal, and patient-reported outcomes.
METHODS: PubMed, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were searched through 1 May 2026. English-language comparative studies in older advanced-prolapse populations were included. Two reviewers independently screened records, extracted data, assessed risk of bias using Risk Of Bias In Nonrandomized Studies of Interventions, and rated certainty using Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation. Findings were narratively synthesized because of heterogeneity.
RESULTS: Of 664 records, 29 reports representing 27 study families were included. Safety outcomes were reported in 23 reports, durability/recurrence in 16, urinary outcomes in 12, bowel/anorectal outcomes in 9, and broad patient-reported outcomes/quality of life in 10. Twelve of the 14 non-overlapping comparisons reported shorter operative time after obliterative surgery; blood loss favored obliteration in 8 of the 12 comparisons and hospital stay in 5 out of 11. Overall complications were not consistently lower. Anatomical/composite durability numerically favored obliteration in 7 out of 10 comparisons, and recurrence-related reoperation was lower in 7 out of 8. Urinary, bowel, and patient-reported outcomes were inconsistent or similar. Certainty was low for operative time and very low for other key outcomes.
CONCLUSION: Current evidence supports a more definitive conclusion about lower procedural burden, particularly shorter operative time, than about global complications, anatomical superiority, or functional outcomes. Findings should inform counseling that integrates frailty, comorbidity, sexual goals, functional symptoms, durability expectations, treatment burden, and patient preference.

articles.title: Changes in Urinary Incontinence Status and Subsequent Falls, Functional Decline, and Depressive Symptoms Across Five International Aging Cohorts.
articles.authors: Xu C, Zheng H, Yan Y et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION AND HYPOTHESIS: Urinary incontinence (UI) often changes over time. Although UI has been associated with falls, disability, and psychological outcomes, it remains unclear whether newly developed, remitting, or persistent UI is associated with different subsequent risks across aging populations.
METHODS: We conducted a harmonized longitudinal analysis of 85,788 cohort-specific analytical records from five international aging cohorts. Both men and women were included. UI status between baseline and follow-up was classified as persistent non-UI (no UI at either assessment), incident UI (no UI at baseline and UI at follow-up), remitting UI (UI at baseline and no UI at follow-up), or persistent UI (UI at both assessments). The three prespecified primary outcomes, assessed subsequently, were incident falls, worsening of basic activities of daily living (ADLs), and incident depressive symptoms. Cohort-specific logistic regression estimates were pooled using random-effects meta-analysis, and absolute risk differences were summarized for clinical interpretation.
RESULTS: Baseline UI prevalence ranged from 5.7% in Survey of Health, Ageing and Retirement in Europe to 28.4% in Korean Longitudinal Study of Aging. Baseline UI was associated with incident falls (pooled OR 1.43, 95% CI 1.30-1.58), ADL worsening (OR 1.70, 95% CI 1.55-1.86), and incident depressive symptoms (OR 1.59, 95% CI 1.42-1.78). Compared with persistent non-UI, incident, remitting, and persistent UI were each associated with all three outcomes. Associations were strongest for ADL worsening, particularly for incident UI (OR 2.28, 95% CI 1.91-2.71) and persistent UI (OR 2.16, 95% CI 1.78-2.61). Baseline UI corresponded to absolute risk differences of 7.5 percentage points for falls, 9.9 for ADL worsening, and 6.4 for depressive symptoms.
CONCLUSIONS: Changes in UI status were associated with subsequent falls, functional decline, and depressive symptoms. Incident and persistent UI were most strongly associated with later ADL deterioration, whereas remitting UI remained associated with a higher risk than persistent non-UI. Repeated assessment of continence status may therefore provide clinically useful information beyond a single baseline UI report.

articles.title: Bridging the Gap Between Dermatology and Gynecology for Menopausal and Perimenopausal Patients.
articles.journal: Dermatologic surgery : official publication for American Society for Dermatologic Surgery [et al.]
articles.authors: Limon P, Morakabian S, Momin F et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Menopause is a universal, multisystem physiologic transition affecting the integumentary, genitourinary, and many other organ systems. Dermatologists frequently encounter manifestations of genitourinary syndrome of menopause (GSM), yet these symptoms remain underrecognized, underdiagnosed, and undertreated.
OBJECTIVE: The aim of this article was to improve dermatologists' care of the perimenopausal and menopausal patients and strengthen collaboration with gynecology.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: A PubMed search was conducted through June 2026 using terms related to menopause, GSM, vulvovaginal symptoms, vaginal estrogen, and vulvar dermatoses. Relevant articles and professional society guidelines addressing the diagnosis and management of GSM and menopause-related care were reviewed.
RESULTS: GSM is diagnosed clinically, but symptoms may mimic, exacerbate, or coexist with inflammatory vulvar disease. Incorporating a structured menopause history into dermatologic evaluation improves recognition of overlapping conditions and guides referral or collaborative care. Low-dose vaginal estrogen is safe, first-line therapy for GSM, whereas other therapies, including energy-based devices, require cautious counseling given limited evidence.
CONCLUSION: GSM and its downstream effects are relevant to dermatologic care and may overlap with inflammatory, irritant, and neoplastic vulvar disease. Menopause-informed history taking, initiation of or referral for low-dose vaginal estrogen, and collaboration with gynecology can improve diagnosis and reduce fragmented care.

articles.title: Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor use in third trimester of pregnancy and birth outcomes after vaginal birth - a Swedish retrospective register study 2005-2015.
articles.journal: Journal of psychosomatic obstetrics and gynaecology
articles.authors: Thies-Lagergren L, Hildingsson I, Johansson M
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs) are prescribed for depression during pregnancy, yet the impact on maternal and neonatal outcomes remains insufficiently studied. The study aimed to describe the prevalence of prescribed SSRIs to pregnant women and its association with birth outcomes after a vaginal birth.
METHODS: A registry study included 405,936 term vaginal births in Sweden. SSRI prescriptions were identified. Crude and adjusted odds ratios with 99% confidence intervals were calculated, with statistical significance set at p < 0.001.
RESULTS: SSRIs were prescribed to 6.374 women (1.6%), with prevalence rising from 0.3% to 2.6% between 2005 and 2015. SSRI was associated with significantly higher rates of labor induction, epidural anesthesia and PPH > 1000 mL. postpartum. Women prescribed SSRIs were more likely to give birth at 37-38 weeks' gestation and have neonates with head circumference < 35 cm and with Apgar score < 7 at 5 min.
CONCLUSIONS: SSRI prescriptions increased significantly between 2005 and 2015 and were associated with higher risks of adverse maternal and neonatal outcomes. Until more conclusive evidence is availble midwives and obstetricians should remain vigilant when supporting pregnant women with depression or anxiety, considering the potential risks of pharmacological treatment alongside non-pharmacological management of maternal mental health conditions.

articles.title: Autologous Muscle-Derived Cell Therapy for Female Stress Urinary Incontinence: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis of Efficacy, Safety, and Patient-Reported Outcomes.
articles.journal: Medical principles and practice : international journal of the Kuwait University, Health Science Centre
articles.authors: Abu-Zaid A, Baradwan S, Hafedh B et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Autologous muscle-derived cell (MDC) therapy is a regenerative option for stress urinary incontinence (SUI), but its overall efficacy and safety remain uncertain.
METHODS: We conducted a PRISMA-compliant systematic review and meta-analysis of clinical studies from 2000 onwards evaluating autologous MDC injections for SUI. PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Cochrane CENTRAL were searched until November 2025, and citation tracking was performed. We included randomized and non-randomized studies in adults or children with SUI treated by periurethral, transurethral, or intrasphincteric MDC injections, reporting continence or safety outcomes.
RESULTS: Of 885 records, 15 studies (5 RCTs and 10 non-RCTs; 1,140 participants) met the inclusion criteria. Across three RCTs, MDCs did not significantly improve mean incontinence episode frequency (IEF) reduction versus placebo and did not significantly increase the proportion achieving ≥50% IEF reduction, but significantly increased the likelihood of ≥75% IEF reduction. A trend toward more patients achieving ≤1 stress incontinence episode favoured MDCs but was not statistically significant. Treatment-related adverse events (TRAEs) were similar between MDCs and placebo, and pooled single-arm data showed low overall TRAE rates (∼5-11%), without clear differences by follow-up duration, injection route, imaging guidance, or use of electrical stimulation. Single-arm meta-analyses demonstrated significant improvements in IIQ-7, IQOL, UDI-6, and pad test leakage, despite substantial heterogeneity.
CONCLUSIONS: MDC therapy for SUI appears safe and may increase the probability of high-level symptom improvement and quality-of-life gains, although average benefits over placebo are modest. Larger, standardized trials are needed to refine patient selection and clarify long-term outcomes.

articles.title: Zinc and copper target molecular complexity and revert endometriosis phenotypes being a promising therapy for disease progression and infertility.
articles.authors: Garcia-Acero P, Sanz FJ, Sebastian-Leon P et al.
articles.abstract: Current treatments for endometriosis address symptoms rather than causes, are not always effective, and produce side effects. We used a computer-based approach to compare gene expression in healthy endometrial tissue and in endometrial tissue affected by endometriosis. This helped us identify which genes may be involved in the disease and which existing drugs might be worth testing as possible treatments. We found that endometriosis disease and infertility-associated genes share similarities, suggesting that both conditions may have similar underlying causes.
