We looked for existing drugs and compounds that might target those underlying causes more effectively than current treatments. We found that zinc and copper might be promising treatments for endometriosis because they may target the disease's underlying causes. Since these drugs are already used for other purposes, repurposing them may reduce the time and cost of clinical trials.

articles.title: Sequential sperm population enrichment for ICSI: DGC-MACS versus MACS-DGC - a hypothesis-generating perspective.
articles.authors: Sheikhi A, Sheikhi M, Shushizadeh MH et al.
articles.abstract:
ABSTRACT: Intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI) requires selecting a suitable spermatozoon from an adequate pool of candidates. The order of density gradient centrifugation (DGC) and magnetic-activated cell sorting (MACS) may influence the characteristics of the recovered sperm population, but its clinical significance remains uncertain. This commentary hypothesizes that DGC followed by MACS (DGC-MACS) may offer practical advantages over the reverse sequence (MACS-DGC) when sperm availability is sufficient. DGC enriches motile, apparently morphologically normal spermatozoa while reducing debris and other cells; subsequent MACS enriches the population for spermatozoa without detectable externalized phosphatidylserine (PS). However, PS negativity does not establish complete functional competence, and DGC has not been validated as a measure of intrinsic sperm stress resistance. We, therefore, discuss membrane sialidase activity and mitochondrial membrane potential (MMP) as illustrative, exploratory biomarkers of complementary functional domains. Their assessment is proposed in parallel research aliquots, not for real-time selection of individual spermatozoa for ICSI. We also introduce a provisional PS-negative enrichment ratio (PSNER) based on the relative proportions of PS-negative spermatozoa before and after DGC-MACS, while acknowledging its dependence on processing conditions, baseline semen quality, and selective recovery. Direct randomized comparisons of DGC-MACS and MACS-DGC, with live birth as the primary outcome, alongside validation of the proposed biomarkers and index, are needed before clinical implementation.
LAY SUMMARY: In some fertility treatments, a specialist helps fertilization by injecting a single sperm directly into an egg. Before this step, laboratories use different methods to prepare sperm samples and increase the chances of selecting a suitable sperm. Two methods can be used together. One separates sperm from unwanted cells and other material, while the other helps remove sperm showing certain changes on their surface. However, it is not yet clear whether the order in which these methods are performed affects the chances of having a baby. In this study, we suggest that using the first method before the second may offer practical advantages when enough sperm are available. We also propose studying additional signs of sperm health and developing a new way to describe changes in sperm samples during preparation. These ideas have not…

articles.title: Obstetric pharmacometabolomics.
articles.authors: Eke AC
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Pregnancy-related physiologic and metabolic changes influence drug exposure and response. Yet therapeutic decisions often lack individualized biologic guidance. Obstetric pharmacometabolomics uses endogenous metabolic signatures to investigate and potentially predict and monitor drug response in pregnancy.
AREAS COVERED: PubMed/MEDLINE and Google Scholar were searched from inception through October 12, 2026, using terms related to metabolomics, pharmacometabolomics, medication exposure, treatment response, maternal-placental-fetal metabolism, pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, and obstetric medications. Human pregnancy studies, longitudinal investigations, drug-perturbation experiments, and mechanistic preclinical studies were prioritized. This review examines pregnancy-specific metabolic adaptations, analytical approaches, and potential applications involving aspirin, antihypertensives, antidiabetic therapies, antiretrovirals, antimicrobials, corticosteroids, and psychiatric medications. It also considers pharmacometabolic approaches to preeclampsia, gestational diabetes mellitus, preterm birth, fetal growth disorders, obesity, and HIV-associated pregnancy.
EXPERT OPINION: Obstetric pharmacometabolomics offers a promising framework for individualized therapeutics, but clinical implementation requires longitudinal studies, standardized biospecimen collection, rigorous exposure assessment, validated biomarkers, and diverse populations. Integration with pharmacogenomics, pharmacomicrobiomics, pharmacoproteomics, and model-informed drug development can improve therapeutic precision, provided that clinical utility is demonstrated.

articles.title: Cardiometabolic Outcomes in Dahl Salt-Sensitive Rat Pregnancies: Impact of a Maternal Hypertensive High-Fat Diet.
articles.journal: American journal of physiology. Endocrinology and metabolism
articles.authors: Gomes VCL, Bailey VN, Kim LG et al.
articles.abstract: Excessive adiposity and chronic hypertension are major risk factors of preeclampsia, a leading hypertensive disorder of pregnancy. Yet, mechanisms underlying the complex interplay between adiposity, chronic hypertension, and preeclampsia remain incompletely understood, partly due to the limited availability of experimental models that capture these interactions. Herein, we explored maternal cardiometabolic adaptations in high-fat diet (HFD)-fed Dahl Salt-Sensitive rats, an established model of HFD-associated chronic hypertension. We hypothesized that HFD-fed dams would display a superimposed preeclampsia-like phenotype compared to control diet (CD)-fed Dahl Salt-Sensitive females. HFD-fed dams exhibited attenuated gestational weight gain, increased ketogenesis, cardiovascular dysfunction and blunted uteroplacental vascular adaptation to pregnancy. HFD feeding was associated with high blood pressure pre-pregnancy and during most of gestation and lactation. Interestingly, however, both groups displayed a drop in blood pressure during late gestation, with lower blood pressure nadir and lower urine protein excretion in HFD-fed dams. Short-term pregnancy outcomes were largely preserved in HFD-fed dams, including litter size, pup viability, and placental efficiency. Long-term, dietary normalization failed to reverse the hypertensive phenotype of HFD-exposed dams, with blood pressure remaining 10-15 mmHg higher than controls for at least 14 weeks post-weaning. In conclusion, HFD-fed Dahl salt-sensitive females developed chronic hypertension and impaired metabolic and cardiovascular adaptations to pregnancy. Yet, neither CD- nor HFD-fed dams exhibited hallmark preeclampsia features, including late-gestation blood pressure rise, proteinuria, and fetal growth restriction. This model therefore provides a valuable platform to investigate adaptive cardiometabolic mechanisms that may attenuate preeclampsia risk in obese and chronic hypertensive patients.

articles.title: Serum Multiomics Profiling of Infertile Women Stratified by Etiology Reveals Distinct Metabolic, Lipidomic, and Exposomic Signatures.
articles.authors: Pan W, Wang L, Cen M et al.
articles.abstract: Female infertility is evaluated primarily by hormonal assays and anatomical imaging, and its molecular landscape remains largely uncharacterized. We enrolled 247 women of reproductive age: 57 nonpregnant controls (NP), 59 women with normal pregnancies (Preg), and 131 infertile patients stratified into polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome-related (PMOS, n = 49), organic/anatomical/inflammatory (OAII, n = 26), other endocrine/autoimmune (OEAI, n = 8), and unexplained (UEI, n = 48) infertility. Fasting serum underwent untargeted metabolomic, lipidomic, and exposomic profiling; classifiers were built with nested cross-validation and integrated via DIABLO, and exposure mixtures were assessed by BKMR. The integrated classifier separated PMOS (AUC 0.892) and UEI (AUC 0.993) from NP, whereas OAII was less separable (AUC 0.729, permutation p = 0.14); lipidomics alone outperformed the integrated model for PMOS and OAII (both DeLong p < 0.001). PMOS was marked by long-chain lipid upregulation, OAII by pan-lipidomic upregulation, and UEI by global lipid downregulation; etiology-stratified sensitivity analyses indicated that OAII heterogeneity diluted, rather than drove, its pooled signal. The pregnant reference group showed coordinate lipidomic and metabolomic remodeling that opposed the infertile acylcarnitine signature. Octabenzone (PIP > 0.98) and propylparaben (PIP 0.75-1.00) emerged as key exposures. Lipidomics emerged as the most informative layer, supporting precision molecular phenotyping of female infertility.

articles.title: Low-Input Spatial Proteomics of FFPE Tissues Reveals Proteins Important for Mouse and Human Meiotic Progression of Spermatocytes.
articles.authors: Wang Y, Chen H, Zhou X et al.
articles.abstract: In order to detect precious clinical FFPE samples at single-cell resolution and fully retain spatial localization information, we optimized a method suitable for low-input spatial proteomics based on laser capture microdissection (LCM) and successfully identified nearly 2000 proteins in about 100 spermatocytes cut from formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE) tissue sections. We used the optimized spatial proteomics technology to research on prophase (pachytene, diplotene)/metaphase transition of spermatocytes in meiosis I in both mouse and human testicular tissues. It was found that the protein characteristics of mouse pachytene and diplotene spermatocytes were more similar and new key proteins MPI and UBE2N were discovered during this transition. Spatial proteomics of pachytene spermatocytes with normal spermatogenesis in patients with obstructive azoospermia (OA) and pachytene spermatocytes with prophase/metaphase transition disorder in patients with meiotic-arrest (MA) azoospermia revealed that the upregulated proteins in pachytene spermatocytes of MA all belong to the glutathione metabolic pathway. Inhibition of IDE and IDH2, two human-mouse homologous proteins upregulated in pachytene spermatocytes of OA, affected metaphase I formation.

articles.title: Quantitative Proteomics Reveals CBX4 Promotes Cervical Cancer Cell Proliferation by Regulating PFKFB4.
articles.authors: Su R, Sun A, Zhao T et al.
articles.abstract: CBX4 is an E3 SUMO ligase involved in the initiation and progression of multiple malignancies. However, the molecular mechanism underlying the functional significance of CBX4 in cervical cancer (CC) cells remains unclear. Here, we used CRISPR/Cas9 genome editing to generate CBX4-knockout cell lines and found that CBX4 loss markedly suppressed HeLa cell proliferation. A label-free quantitative proteomics approach based on data-independent acquisition (DIA) was employed to systematically profile CBX4-regulated proteins in HeLa cells. In total, 263 proteins showed significant changes upon CBX4 knockout, among which 171 proteins were downregulated, and 92 were upregulated. Bioinformatics analysis revealed that these differentially expressed proteins (DEPs) are associated with diverse cellular pathways, especially metabolic pathways. Furthermore, our results demonstrated that CBX4 promotes CC cell proliferation by regulating the expression of 6-phosphofructo-2-kinase/fructose-2,6-biphosphatase 4 (PFKFB4). Mechanistically, PFKFB4 is a direct target of the transcriptional activator SP1, and CBX4 interacts with SP1 and increases its SUMOylation. Therefore, CBX4 may exert its effects in CC cells through enhancing SP1-mediated PFKFB4 transcription. In conclusion, the current study establishes a proteome-wide CBX4 regulatory network and provides novel insights into the molecular pathogenesis of CC.

articles.title: Integrative Single-Cell Proteomics and Network Analysis Identifies DHX9 as a Key Regulator of Oocyte Maturation and a Therapeutic Target for Oocyte Developmental Arrest.
articles.authors: Cao GY, Liu SP, Guo AL et al.
articles.abstract: Oocyte developmental arrest at the germinal vesicle (GV) or metaphase I (MI) stage is a major cause of infertility, yet its molecular mechanisms remain poorly understood. Here, we performed ultradeep single-cell proteomics on 8 human oocytes (4 GV-stage and 4 MI-stage) and 12 mouse oocytes (3 GV, 3 MI, 3 MII, and 3 FGO) to investigate the proteomic landscape of developmental arrest. We identified an average of 5,574 proteins per human oocyte (range: 4,350-6,157) and 3,477 per mouse oocyte (range: 3,315-3,634), revealing aberrant activation of mRNA splicing pathways in arrested oocytes. Integrative network analysis identified the RNA helicase DHX9 as a central hub within a conserved coexpression module. Mechanistically, elevated DHX9 expression maintained transcriptional hyperactivity, preventing the transition to transcriptional quiescence required for maturation. Critically, pharmacological inhibition of DHX9 with ATX968 restored transcriptional silencing and significantly rescued meiotic maturation, achieving 95% GVBD and 80% PBE at 1 μM ATX968, comparable to wild-type controls (98%/82%) and significantly exceeding vehicle-treated arrested oocytes (8% GVBD; p < 0.001). In summary, our study demonstrates that DHX9-driven dysregulation of RNA splicing is a key mechanism underlying oocyte developmental arrest. These findings highlight DHX9 as a promising therapeutic target and provide a potential strategy for improving oocyte competence in clinical infertility treatment.

articles.title: Integrated Proteomic and Ubiquitinomic Reveal Ubiquitination Remodeling in Pelvic Organ Prolapse.
articles.authors: Liu W, Gao Y, Gao Y et al.
articles.abstract: Pelvic organ prolapse (POP) is characterized by localized vaginal-wall tissue failure, but post-translational regulation remains incompletely understood. We integrated quantitative proteomic and ubiquitinomic profiling of vaginal tissues from 10 women with POP and 8 controls. Differentially expressed proteins were enriched in ECM-associated, cytoskeletal, and adherens-junction pathways, whereas the ubiquitinome revealed reproducible site-specific changes. Integrated analysis highlighted β-catenin (CTNNB1) and collagen type III alpha 1 chain (COL3A1), including the previously reported CTNNB1 K233 site and two newly identified ubiquitination sites, CTNNB1 K672 and COL3A1 K674. Representative MS/MS spectra supported assignment of these sites. Together, these data define POP-associated ubiquitination remodeling and nominate adherens-junction and ECM-linked proteins for future functional validation.

articles.title: Sustained-release microneedles for drug delivery: advances and prospects.
articles.authors: He P, He C, Yu J et al.
articles.abstract: Sustained-release microneedles (SR-MNs) are designed to establish a prolonged drug supply process within the dermis or local tissues after a single short-term application. This process can last from hours to months. In this way, it combines minimally invasive administration, reduced dosing frequency, and maintenance of local or systemic drug exposure. Unlike the broader category of controlled-release microneedles, the systems discussed in this review mainly rely on the intrinsic properties of materials and structural design to achieve prolonged drug output. They are not predominantly governed by externally triggered release. Over the past 15 years, the field has gradually evolved along three major technical routes: slowly degrading matrix microneedles, particle-loaded microneedles, and drug-loaded hydrogel microneedles. In addition, separable or implantable tips have emerged as an important structural strategy for constructing intradermal drug depots. Current studies show that different material systems and design routes correspond to distinct release mechanisms and application windows. These systems have also been extended to chronic disease management, vaccines, contraception, and anti-HIV therapy. Overall, the further translation of SR-MNs will depend on whether effective drug loading, preservation of drug activity, long-term safety, and scalable manufacturing can be optimized in parallel.

articles.title: Development and Temporal Validation of a Thromboelastography-Based Nomogram for Queensland-Defined High Thrombotic Risk in Postpartum Women.
articles.authors: Zhou D, Du J, Luo Y et al.
articles.abstract: This study developed and temporally validated a nomogram that integrates thromboelastography (TEG) and maternal clinical factors to identify women classified as having high thrombotic risk according to the 2020 Queensland Clinical Guideline at postpartum reassessment after 24 h. The derivation cohort included 447 women who delivered at Foshan Women and Children Hospital between January 1, 2021, and December 27, 2022; 346 had Queensland scores of 0-2 and 101 had scores of ≥3. A same-center temporal validation cohort included 207 women who delivered between December 28, 2022, and February 14, 2025. Candidate clinical and TEG variables were evaluated using multivariable logistic regression, and model performance was assessed using receiver operating characteristic analysis, calibration, and decision curve analysis. The final model retained hypertensive disorders of pregnancy, maternal age, current body mass index, native-cup TEG reaction time (R), and 24-h postpartum blood loss. Discrimination was acceptable in the derivation cohort (area under the curve [AUC], 0.791; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.737-0.845; sensitivity, 70.3%; specificity, 77.2%) and good in the temporal validation cohort (AUC, 0.847; 95% CI, 0.771-0.923; sensitivity, 75.8%; specificity, 85.6%). The model estimates Queensland-defined high thrombotic risk rather than objectively confirmed venous thromboembolism. It may support simplified postpartum reassessment after the first 24 h, but multicenter validation against objectively confirmed thrombotic outcomes is required before claims regarding event prediction or clinical implementation can be made.

articles.title: Cervicovaginal microbiome modulates HPV genotype-specific clearance/persistence: role of bacterial dysbiosis in cervical carcinogenesis.
articles.authors: Zhang J, Ji M, Lv N et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: This study focuses on the distinct epidemiological features of high-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV) genotypes in Asian populations: HPV52/56/58 show uniquely high prevalence and strong correlation with cervical intraepithelial neoplasia, but their detection rates drop sharply in invasive cervical cancer, a pattern clearly different from the persistent dominance of HPV16/18 throughout malignant progression.
METHODS: To further elucidate the potential host-microbe interactions underlying these epidemiological observations, we integrated a 16S rRNA-sequenced cross-sectional discovery cohort and an independent longitudinal validation cohort from a Chinese population, with strict experimental quality control throughout the workflow.
RESULT: The preliminary analytical results demonstrate that a Lactobacillus-dominant cervicovaginal microbiome (CVM) is significantly and positively associated with HPV viral clearance, while enriched abundance of Gardnerella, Saccharofermentans and Atopobium exhibits a robust correlation with persistent HPV52/56/58 infection. Three undercharacterized microbial taxa-Chryseobacterium, Sphingobacterium and Enhydrobacter are closely linked to sustained HPV16/18 prevalence across advanced disease stages, and show negative correlation with the above obligate anaerobes, which aligns with the sharp decline of HPV52/56/58 in tumor tissues. A hormone-linked Chryseobacterium enrichment were also identified, a taxon with previously reported progesterone-degrading functional properties.
CONCLUSION: While further longitudinal studies are required to establish causal relationships, our results indicate that CVM dysbiosis may modulate the natural history of these high-burden HPV genotypes, and provide a foundational rationale for subsequent development of genotype-specific, microbiota-targeted cervical disease intervention strategies.

articles.title: Competing Endogenous Ribonucleic Acid Networks in Cervical Cancer: Mechanisms and Clinical Implications.
articles.authors: Shi L, Khan MU
articles.abstract: Cervical cancer (CC) remains a leading cause of cancer-related mortality among women, with persistent infection with high-risk human papillomavirus (HR-HPV) representing its primary etiological factor. Long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs), circular RNAs (circRNAs), and pseudogenes can function as competing endogenous RNAs (ceRNAs) by competing with messenger RNAs (mRNAs) for binding to microRNAs (miRNAs), thereby reducing miRNA-mediated repression of target mRNAs. This review categorizes the ceRNA axes reported in CC as oncogenic or tumor-suppressive and examines their convergence on major signaling pathways, including Wnt/β-catenin, phosphoinositide 3-kinase (PI3K)/Akt, mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK), Hippo, and Notch, together with the strength of the supporting evidence. The roles of these networks in prognosis, resistance to cisplatin and radiotherapy, and responses to bioactive compounds are also evaluated. Most reported axes are supported primarily by cell-line experiments, whereas absolute RNA quantification is frequently unavailable and patient-level validation remains limited. Accordingly, ceRNA networks represent potential biomarkers and therapeutic targets, although additional mechanistic and clinical evidence is required to establish their clinical applicability.

articles.title: From folate to the epigenetic clock: one-carbon metabolism in oocyte quality and ovarian ageing.
articles.authors: Fu X, Yang Y, Jiang L et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: One-carbon metabolism (OCM) supports nucleotide synthesis and S-adenosylmethionine (SAM)-dependent methylation; its links to sulfur metabolism connect it to glutathione (GSH) synthesis and hydrogen sulfide (H2S) signalling. These functions are relevant to oocyte growth, epigenetic programming, and developmental competence, but their contribution to ovarian ageing remains incompletely understood. Existing reviews address pregnancy, embryo development, or female fertility broadly, leaving OCM in stage-specific oocyte biology and ageing insufficiently integrated.
OBJECTIVE AND RATIONALE: This review examines OCM in oocyte development, epigenetic regulation, and ovarian ageing, focusing on substrate supply, enzyme regulation, and methyl-donor metabolism. It evaluates experimental and clinical evidence on metabolic disturbances and nutritional interventions, and identifies knowledge gaps that limit clinical translation.
SEARCH METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE was searched for English-language literature published from January 2008 to September 2026. OCM substrate, enzyme, and methylation terms were combined with oocyte, follicular, ovarian, embryo, and ART terms. Reference lists were hand-searched. Evidence was assessed by species, tissue, design, and outcome, prioritizing mechanistic perturbations, prospective cohorts, and clinical trials.
OUTCOMES: Mouse studies indicate transient leucovorin uptake in growing oocytes and cumulus-supported serine transfer. Methylenetetrahydrofolate reductase (MTHFR) phosphorylation shows developmental regulation, whereas methionine adenosyltransferase 2A (MAT2A) inhibition after the eight-cell stage reduces bovine blastocyst development. DNA methylation supports imprint establishment; reducing methionine from 50 to 10 µM in bovine embryo culture altered methylation at more than 1600 genes. Porcine homocysteine (Hcy) exposure impaired mitochondrial and developmental endpoints, with an increased mitochondrial DNA 16S methylation signal whose causal role requires validation. Multi-component supplementation containing 5-methyltetrahydrofolate (5-MTHF) increased bovine blastocyst yield during maturation (34.9% vs 17.1%), without establishing a human protocol. In a selected recurrent-miscarriage/repeated-ART-failure cohort, over 40% were homozygous or compound heterozygous for common MTHFR variants, without appropriate controls establishing enrichment. Higher Hcy was associated with poorer implantation and clinical pregnancy in…

articles.title: Elabela in pregnancy: Physiology, associated disorders and translational perspectives (Review).
articles.authors: Xie Y, Yang S, Meng C et al.
articles.abstract: Elabela (ELA) has emerged as a critical regulator of reproductive success, signaling through the cognate apelin receptor (APJ) (encoded by the APLNR gene) to orchestrate embryonic development and placental function. The present narrative review summarizes evidence spanning from molecular mechanisms to clinical phenotypes, evaluating the role of ELA in both physiological pregnancy and major complications, including preeclampsia, fetal growth restriction and gestational diabetes, as well as emerging associations with placental disorders and early pregnancy loss. The present review addresses three key challenges: i) The receptor paradox in APJ‑low or APJ‑negative contexts; ii) inconsistencies among clinical ELA measurements; and iii) the need to distinguish direct ELA evidence from inference drawn from apelin studies. Current findings position ELA as a candidate biomarker and experimental therapeutic target; however, its clinical utility remains unproven due to pre‑analytical variability across sample types (plasma vs. serum), inconsistencies between detection platforms (ELISA vs. immunohistochemistry), and biological heterogeneity across specific disease subtypes (such as preeclampsia and heart failure). Future work should focus on defining receptor‑ and isoform‑specific signaling, standardizing ELA measurement and establishing pharmacokinetics, dose‑response relationships, delivery strategies and maternal‑fetal safety.

articles.title: Cervicovaginal lipid mediator profiles during high-risk HPV infection associated with subsequent viral clearance or persistence: an exploratory pilot study.
articles.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
articles.authors: Mucci M, Recchiuti A, Moscicki AB et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: High-risk human papillomavirus (HPV) infection is the primary cause of cervical cancer, whereas most infections are spontaneously cleared. Although local immune and microbial factors associated with HPV outcomes have been investigated, the contribution of lipid mediators within the cervicovaginal microenvironment remains poorly characterized.
METHODS: Cervicovaginal wash samples from 30 participants in a prospective longitudinal HPV cohort were analyzed by targeted liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry. Samples were obtained from HPV-negative women, HPV-positive women who were negative for the relevant HPV type at the subsequent visit (subsequent-clearance group), and HPV-positive women in whom the same HPV type remained detectable at the subsequent visit.
RESULTS: Six lipid mediators were detected in cervicovaginal wash samples. During HPV infection, women with subsequent clearance had higher measured concentrations of total 12-HETE and total 14-HDHA than HPV-negative women. In the secondary percentage-based analysis, the relative contribution of PGE2 was lower in the subsequent-clearance group than in both the HPV-negative and subsequent-persistence groups, while the relative contribution of total 14-HDHA was higher in the subsequent-persistence group than in HPV-negative women. Direct comparison of correlation coefficients identified an opposite TxB2-14-HDHA relationship in subsequent clearance and persistence.
CONCLUSIONS: Higher cervicovaginal concentrations of total 12-HETE and total 14-HDHA during HPV infection were associated with clearance of the relevant HPV type at the subsequent visit. The opposite TxB2-total 14-HDHA associations observed in subsequent clearance and persistence further suggest outcome-associated differences in lipid-mediator coordination. These exploratory findings identify lipid mediators as candidate correlates of HPV outcomes.

articles.title: Twice the Joy, but Added Risk: Exploring Twin Birth Outcomes at the East Suffolk and North Essex NHS Foundation Trust Maternity Service, England.
articles.authors: Aakanksha, Mon PE, Sharma A et al.
articles.abstract: Background and aim Twin pregnancy carries higher maternal and neonatal risk than singleton pregnancy, and local data on chorionicity and national benchmarking remain limited. This study primarily aims to describe maternal characteristics, timing and mode of birth, and maternal and neonatal outcomes of twin deliveries in a two-site NHS maternity service. Secondary, hypothesis-generating aims were to explore factors associated with cesarean birth and early delivery and to make an indicative comparison with UK national audit data. Materials and methods We conducted a retrospective, descriptive, and analytical cross-sectional study of 55 women who delivered twins (110 fetuses) between October 2, 2025, and June 18, 2026, following STROBE and RECORD guidance. Key proportions are presented with 95% CIs. Timing of birth was assessed against chorionicity-specific National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) windows. Analyses were exploratory and unadjusted, and no formal comparison with national data was made. Results Mean maternal age was 31.8 ± 5.7 years. Of the 55 pregnancies, 46 (83.6%) were dichorionic diamniotic (DCDA), nine (16.4%) were monochorionic diamniotic (MCDA), and 10 (18.2%) followed assisted conception. Mean gestation at delivery was 36.1 ± 1.6 weeks; 33 women (60.0%) delivered before 37 weeks. Compared with chorionicity-specific NICE windows, 24 of 46 DCDA pregnancies (52.2%) delivered before 37+0 weeks, and seven of nine MCDA pregnancies (77.8%) before 36+0 weeks. Cesarean birth of both twins occurred in 42 women (76.4%; 95% CI 63.7-85.6): 24 (43.6%) elective and 18 (32.7%) unscheduled. Postpartum hemorrhage (≥500 mL after vaginal birth or ≥1000 mL after cesarean) occurred in 19 women (34.5%), and composite maternal morbidity in 18 (32.7%). Mean birthweight was 2417 ± 457 g; nine of 53 pairs (17.0%) had ≥20% birthweight discordance. At least one twin was admitted to the neonatal unit (any level of care) in 20 of 54 pregnancies (37.0%), including four of four (100%) born before 34 weeks. One fetus (one of 110, 0.9%) died in utero at 23+3 weeks; there were no neonatal or maternal deaths. Conclusions Preterm birth, cesarean birth, postpartum hemorrhage, and neonatal unit admission were common in this twin population. With 55 women, CIs were wide, so the study cannot show whether local outcomes differ from national data. Early delivery of MCDA twins relative to the NICE window and the reasons recorded for cesarean birth warrant local…

articles.title: Community-Based Preeclampsia Screening by Midwives and Community Health Workers in Low- and Middle-Income Countries: A Scoping Review and Evidence-Informed Framework for Indonesia.
articles.authors: Wibowo AFQ, Prosfera RHE, Permata YR et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: This scoping review mapped evidence on community-based preeclampsia screening delivered by midwives and community health workers (CHWs) in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), identified implementation barriers and facilitators, and developed evidence-informed design requirements for an Indonesian community screening framework.
DESIGN AND METHODS: Guided by the Population-Concept-Context framework and reported in accordance with PRISMA-ScR, we searched PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science for English-language studies published from 2016 to February 2026. A total of 133 records were identified across the databases. After deduplication and screening against prespecified eligibility criteria, nine studies were included in the scoping review. A structured data-charting form, informed by the review questions and Joanna Briggs Institute scoping-review guidance, was piloted using two purposefully selected studies before full extraction. Included evidence was mapped descriptively and synthesized thematically.
RESULTS: The included studies were conducted in Indonesia, Mozambique, Nigeria, India, Ecuador, South Africa, and other LMIC settings. The evidence, which was predominantly qualitative and mixed methods, suggested that community-level blood-pressure measurement, danger-sign assessment, simple decision support, and linkage to referral may be feasible and acceptable when supported by training, supervision, appropriate equipment, defined roles, documentation, and functional referral pathways. The evidence did not permit definitive conclusions about clinical effectiveness or safety across settings. Five implementation domains informed the proposed COMPREP Screen framework: workforce capability; tools and supplies; role clarity and accountability; documentation and data use; and referral-system functioning.
CONCLUSION: Community-based screening led by midwives and CHWs may support earlier recognition of preeclampsia risk and timely linkage to facility-based assessment and care. Because the evidence base is limited and heterogeneous, COMPREP Screen should be regarded as an evidence-informed, context-sensitive framework that requires stakeholder validation and prospective implementation evaluation in Indonesia.

articles.title: Predictive Value of the Miscarriage Prediction Index for Early Miscarriage After Frozen Embryo Transfer.
articles.authors: Wang J, Song Z, Fang F et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate whether the Miscarriage Prediction Index (MPI), a novel ratio derived from early pregnancy hormonal changes, can identify women at increased risk of early miscarriage after frozen embryo transfer.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 1337 women with confirmed intrauterine pregnancies following frozen embryo transfer at two reproductive centers. Serum hormone levels were measured during early pregnancy, and the Miscarriage Prediction Index (MPI), reflecting the balance between trophoblastic activity and estrogenic support, was calculated from dynamic hormonal changes. Participants were followed through 12 weeks of gestation. Statistical analyses assessed the association between MPI and early miscarriage risk and explored age-related differences.
RESULTS: Higher MPI values were significantly associated with an increased risk of early miscarriage and reduced likelihood of ongoing pregnancy. The relationship between MPI and miscarriage risk was nonlinear, with risk rising markedly beyond specific threshold values. MPI showed modest discriminatory performance, with an AUC of 0.670 (95% CI, 0.627-0.719) in the development cohort and 0.688 (95% CI, 0.630-0.747) in the external cohort. The association was stronger in women younger than 35 years, while MPI demonstrated modest and consistent predictive performance in both development and external cohorts and provided additional predictive information beyond maternal age alone.
CONCLUSIONS: Elevated MPI is associated with early miscarriage risk after frozen embryo transfer and may reflect early endocrine imbalance and pregnancy instability. Age-specific MPI may better interpret MPI values and support more individualized risk stratification, early identification miscarriage, and monitoring among women, which may provide a potential window for timely clinical assessment and intervention.

articles.title: Suprapubic-Assisted Umbilical Dual-Port versus Four-Port Laparoscopic Myomectomy: A Retrospective Comparative Study.
articles.authors: Yuan H, Xie X, Feng Y et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This retrospective non-randomized study was performed to compare the safety, clinical efficacy and cosmetic satisfaction between suprapubic-assisted umbilical laparoendoscopic dual-site surgery (SAU-LEDS) and traditional multiport laparoscopic myomectomy for myomectomy.
METHODS: Seventy-five patients diagnosed with uterine fibroids in our Hospital between June 2022 and June 2024 were enrolled in this study, 35 cases underwent SAU-LEDS (dual-port group) and 40 cases underwent four-port laparoscopic surgery (four-port group). We mainly compared operative time, intraoperative blood loss, myoma removal time, wound suturing time, time to first flatus, postoperative maximum body temperature, length of hospital stays, numeric rating scale (NRS) pain score at 24 h postoperatively, postoperative cosmetic scale score and satisfaction at 1 month postoperatively between the two groups.
RESULTS: Both groups underwent surgery successfully without the conversion to laparotomy or major surgical complications. There were no statistically significant differences between the two groups in operation time, intraoperative blood loss, time to first flatus, postoperative maximum body temperature, and length of hospital stays (p > 0.05). However, compared with the four-port group, the dual-port group exhibited the shorter myoma removal time (15.49 (6.42) vs 25.78 (7.26), p = 0.003), the lower NRS pain score at 24 h postoperatively (1.20 (0.40) vs 1.62 (0.74), p = 0.045), the higher postoperative incision cosmetic scale score (16.80 (3.78) vs 10.80 (2.10), p = 0.009), and better satisfaction (3.60 (0.40) vs 3.00 (0.50), p = 0.032).
CONCLUSION: SAU-LEDS appeared feasible and may provide cosmetic and pain-related advantages in selected patients, but prospective studies are needed.

articles.title: Targeting histone methylation with ROS nanoparticles delivering PARPi prodrugs to amplify the stimulation of cGAS-STING for immunotherapy in ovarian cancer.
articles.authors: Sun Y, Li H, Zhang H et al.
articles.abstract: Poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase inhibitors (PARPi) has improved survival in ovarian cancer (OC), yet its efficacy is severely compromised by the restoration of homologous recombination repair and enhanced drug efflux. Here, we report a reactive oxygen species (ROS)-responsive nanoparticle (DP@NP) for the co-delivery of PARPi and DOT1L inhibitor (DOT1Li) to overcome these limitations through a dual-function mechanism. DP@NP can be triggered by ROS in cancer cells, whereupon the released PARPi induces DNA damage, while DOT1Li augments DNA damage accumulation by suppressing PARPi efflux and impairing DNA repair. This coordinated dual action promotes the accumulation of cytosolic double-stranded DNA, thereby robustly activating the cyclic GMP-AMP synthase-stimulator of interferon genes (cGAS-STING) pathway. In vivo, DP@NP exhibits efficient tumor targeting and elicits pronounced antitumor activity across multiple OC models. Notably, it remodels the tumor immune microenvironment and upregulates PD-L1, thereby significantly enhancing tumor responsiveness to immune checkpoint inhibitors. This study presents a co-delivery strategy that enhances PARPi efficacy while concurrently promoting antitumor immune activation, offering a viable avenue for the treatment of OC.

articles.title: Bio-dissociable platinum quantum dot cluster nanozymes for nonhormonal endometriosis therapy through microenvironment remodeling.
articles.authors: Cao C, Ding J, Hao H et al.
articles.abstract: Endometriosis (EMS) is a chronic inflammatory disorder marked by ectopic endometrial lesions that commonly cause pain and infertility. Existing surgical and hormonal therapies are limited by adverse effects and high recurrence rates, while nanozyme-based approaches offer opportunities to develop alternative therapeutic strategies. Here, we developed bio-dissociable platinum quantum dot clusters (PtQDC) as nanozymes for nonhormonal EMS therapy. PtQDC undergoes gradual dissociation in lesion tissue fluid and exhibits sustained scavenging activity toward reactive oxygen and nitrogen species. The resulting shift of endometriotic cells from their highly oxidative state beyond a favorable redox window was accompanied by impaired energy metabolism, mitochondrial dysfunction, and apoptosis. In the mouse model of EMS, PtQDC reduced lesion number and volume, remodeled the peritoneal microenvironment, inhibited pathological angiogenesis, and attenuated pain-associated signaling. PtQDC also reduced proinflammatory factors, increased IL-10, and modulated macrophage phenotypic profiles. RNA-seq analysis further revealed downregulation of Ptgs2, Mmp3, and Postn, genes associated with inflammation, invasion, and fibrosis. Thus, PtQDC integrates antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, antifibrotic, and antiangiogenic activities as a potential multitarget nonhormonal therapy for EMS.

articles.title: Reproductive carrier screening: perspectives for a future implementation in Germany.
articles.journal: Medizinische Genetik : Mitteilungsblatt des Berufsverbandes Medizinische Genetik e.V
articles.authors: Rudnik-Schöneborn S, Zerres K, Sänger N et al.
articles.abstract: Reproductive carrier screening (RCS) has made its way into the health care system in various countries. Current data suggest that 3.5 % of European couples are carriers for the same autosomal recessive disease and an additional 1.0 % of women are carriers of an X-linked disease. Once an increased genetic risk has been identified, couples can choose between a range of options, including prenatal or preimplantation diagnostics. Also alternatives apply such as gamete donation, reconsidering their desire to have children, adoption, or accepting a child with the condition. Improved reproductive autonomy is the main argument for RCS along with the concept of the best possible personalized medicine according to the current state of science and technology. The individual desire of couples to determine genetic risks for future children should be acknowledged and politically legalized. The authors outline the legal, genetic and reproductive, and ethical perspectives for RCS in the German healthcare system.

articles.title: Non-invasive prenatal testing - new possibilities on the horizon and old problems.
articles.journal: Medizinische Genetik : Mitteilungsblatt des Berufsverbandes Medizinische Genetik e.V
articles.authors: Weise A, Liehr T
articles.abstract: Non-invasive prenatal testing (NIPT) is a screening method that accesses placenta-derived DNA. Contrary to its name, no foetal DNA is tested here, despite the fact that it is often referred to as a test of 'free foetal DNA'. NIPT is available in at least five different technical variants and can test for aneuploidies of chromosomes 13, 18 and 21, with or without testing the sex chromosomes. It can also test all chromosomes for aneuploidy, although polyploidy is only accessible with a single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP)-based test system. It can also check for targeted microdeletion/microduplication syndrome critical regions. Among others, as NIPT uses placental DNA, a certain rate of false-positive and false-negative results is to be expected in the case of copy number variation detection. For some years now, existing commercial NIPT variants have been expanded to include single-gene-mutation-oriented testing. Here, foeto-placental divergence seems to play a minor role, while distinguishing maternal and placenta-derived cell-free DNA remains challenging. This article reviews the milestones of NIPT and its current developments, focusing on the challenges of incorporating this approach into existing prenatal care schemes and the situation in Germany.

articles.title: Population-specific differences in ClinVar pathogenic and likely pathogenic variants of epilepsy-associated genes between East Asian and non-finnish European populations: a nucleotide-resolved gnomAD v4.1.1 analysis.
articles.authors: Lai JX, He MF, Fan ZC et al.
articles.abstract: Pathogenic and likely pathogenic (P/LP) variants in ClinVar guide variant interpretation in clinical genetic testing, yet their population-specific frequency differences have not been systematically examined in epilepsy. We compiled 199 epilepsy-associated genes, extracted 46,746 unique P/LP variants from ClinVar, and retrieved allele frequencies from gnomAD v4.1.1 gene-level tables using nucleotide-resolved matching. Fisher's exact test with Benjamini-Hochberg correction (q < 0.05) identified nine variants significantly enriched in East Asian (EAS) relative to non-Finnish European (NFE) populations, with odds ratios of 36.3-867.9. Eight additional low-frequency EAS signals met the same enrichment criterion with at least two EAS alleles and an uncorrected p < 0.01 and are reported as exploratory. Thirteen of the seventeen variants reside in seven autosomal recessive genes, namely, ALDH7A1, ST3GAL5, GOSR2, AARS1, BRAT1, WWOX, and UBA5. In parallel, an rsID-level workflow, the standard approach in database mining, yielded 60 candidate EAS-enriched variants. Nucleotide-resolved matching confirmed only fifteen of these and additionally recovered two signals the rsID workflow missed, a false-positive rate of 75.0%. These findings show that epilepsy P/LP variant frequencies differ substantially between EAS and NFE populations and concentrate in recessive genes with direct relevance to carrier screening. rsID-level ClinVar-gnomAD integration systematically overestimates population specificity, and nucleotide-resolved allele matching should become a standard step in population frequency analyses.

articles.title: Recent Advances in the Management of Heart Failure, Including the Role of AI and Advances in Gene Therapy.
articles.journal: The International journal of angiology : official publication of the International College of Angiology, Inc
articles.authors: Kattamuri L, Sharma K, Mukherjee D
articles.abstract: Heart failure (HF) remains a major cause of morbidity and mortality despite significant advances in its management. This study aimed to synthesize recent advances in HF management, including the role of artificial intelligence (AI) and advances in gene therapy. PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and Google Scholar were searched for original research (2020-January 2026) on recent advances in HF management, including AI and gene-based therapies. While guideline-directed management and therapy (GDMT) substantially reduce mortality and hospitalization in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF), utilization of such therapies is frequently constrained by delayed initiation, incomplete titration, noncompliance, and cost. Beyond foundational therapy, finerenone, sodium glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) across the ejection fraction (EF) spectrum, and glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist (GLP-1 RA) for obesity-related heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) extend phenotype-directed options. Transcatheter mitral and tricuspid repair/replacement has shifted mitral and tricuspid regurgitation from a bystander lesion to a treatable contributor to improvement of symptoms and quality of life. Adjunctive transcatheter mitral interventions have expanded treatment options for selected symptomatic HFrEF patients with secondary mitral regurgitation (MR) despite optimized GDMT, improving MR severity, functional status, and reducing HF hospitalizations. Donor-derived cell-free DNA rejection surveillance, donation after circulatory death to expand donor supply, and refinement of left ventricular assist device (LVAD) antithrombotic strategies are evolving in advanced HF. AI tools and gene therapies are showing promising results but require further large-scale studies for validation and clinical adoption. Contemporary HF management is increasingly phenotype- and trajectory-guided, but its clinical adoption is limited by optimal implementation and access barriers. Future research should focus on outcomes-based validation with a clear patient-selection framework to enable durable real-world implementation to improve outcomes further.

articles.title: Whole-tumor histogram analysis of non-Gaussian diffusion MRI models combined with clinicopathological indicators for assessing lymph node metastasis in endometrial cancer.
articles.authors: Zang Y, Wang H, Ge W et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To investigate whether whole-tumor histogram features derived from five non-Gaussian diffusion models, combined with clinicopathological factors, are associated with lymph node metastasis (LNM) in endometrial cancer (EC).
METHODS: This prospective study enrolled 73 patients with histologically confirmed EC and known nodal status. All underwent preoperative 3.0T MRI including diffusion-weighted imaging with 16 b-values. Thirteen parametric maps were derived from five non-Gaussian models: intravoxel incoherent motion (IVIM), diffusion kurtosis imaging (DKI), stretched exponential model (SEM), fractional-order calculus (FROC), and continuous time random walk (CTRW). Clinicopathological data were collected, including demographics, comorbidities, serum markers, pathological type, myometrial invasion, cervical involvement, and MRI-based local stage. Clinical, radiomics, and combined logistic regression models were built. Performance was evaluated using AUC, calibration curves, decision curve analysis, and bootstrap analysis of intercept variability.
RESULTS: LNM was confirmed in 21 of 73 patients. The clinical model achieved an AUC of 0.837, the radiomics model achieved an AUC of 0.856, and the combined model achieved an AUC of 0.924, with 90.5% sensitivity and 82.7% specificity. DeLong tests revealed no significant AUC differences among models (P = 0.090-0.140). The combined model had the lowest Brier score (0.092) and provided higher net benefit across threshold probabilities of 0.1-0.3.
CONCLUSION: Non-Gaussian diffusion histogram parameters, particularly DKI_K_energy, demonstrate potential for predicting LNM in EC. A combined model incorporating DKI_K_energy with age and pathological type shows promise as a potential biomarker for risk stratification.

articles.title: Financial toxicity, disease acceptance, and health-related quality of life in women with endometriosis: a cross-sectional mediation analysis.
articles.authors: Pietrzak K, Szablewska AW, Skrzypek-Czerko M et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Endometriosis is a chronic disease associated with substantial impairment in health-related quality of life (HRQoL) and considerable financial burden. This study aimed to examine how patient-reported financial toxicity and disease acceptance are associated with HRQoL in women with endometriosis and to assess the potential mediating role of disease acceptance in this relationship.
METHODS: This cross-sectional study included 411 women with endometriosis recruited in Poland through online patient communities, social media channels, endometriosis-related networks, and a collaborating Women's Health Center. Patient-reported financial toxicity, disease acceptance, and HRQoL were assessed using the COST-FACIT, Acceptance of Illness Scale (AIS), and Endometriosis Health Profile-30 (EHP-30), respectively. The potential mediating role of disease acceptance in the association between financial toxicity and HRQoL was examined using regression-based mediation analysis with 5,000 bootstrap samples, adjusting for age, household income, previous surgical treatment, and infertility treatment.
RESULTS: Higher COST-FACIT scores, indicating lower financial toxicity, were associated with greater disease acceptance [B = 0.618, 95% CI (0.552; 0.683), p < 0.001] and better HRQoL [B = -0.537, 95% CI (-0.711; -0.362), p < 0.001]. Greater disease acceptance was also associated with better HRQoL [B = -0.963, 95% CI (-1.144; -0.784), p < 0.001]. Mediation analysis showed a statistically significant indirect association between financial toxicity and HRQoL through disease acceptance [B = -0.595, 95% CI (-0.731; -0.472)], while the direct association remained statistically significant. Older age and previous infertility treatment were independently associated with better HRQoL (lower EHP-30 scores), whereas household income and previous surgical treatment were not.
CONCLUSION: Patient-reported financial toxicity was associated with both disease acceptance and HRQoL in women with endometriosis. The observed indirect association through disease acceptance is consistent with the possibility that psychological adaptation may represent one component of the relationship between financial toxicity and HRQoL. however, the cross-sectional design does not allow the temporal ordering or causality of these associations to be established. These findings support considering financial well-being alongside psychological factors when evaluating the broader impact of endometriosis on…

articles.title: Maternal and Neonatal Outcomes Across Female Genital Mutilation Types in Somalia: An Exploratory Analysis at a Tertiary Referral Hospital.
articles.authors: Mohamud SA, Mohamed MM, Yusuf AM et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Type-specific evidence on maternal and neonatal outcomes associated with female genital mutilation (FGM) in Somalia remains limited. We explored selected outcomes in a tertiary referral hospital.
METHODS: This exploratory analysis used prospectively collected data from 30 May 2022 through January 2026. Recruitment depended on specialist obstetricians being available or on duty. FGM was assessed by genital examination at admission for delivery after consent. Planned elective cesarean deliveries were excluded. Of 371 cleaned episodes, 337 had documented FGM classification. Type IV was descriptive only. Binary logistic regression compared Types II and III with Type I, adjusting for age and parity, with additional gestational-age adjustment for the neonatal composite.
RESULTS: The classified sample included 23 women without FGM, 60 with Type I, 139 with Type II, 110 with Type III, and five with Type IV. Cesarean delivery was numerically highest in Type II (35.3%); maternal/obstetric complications (19.4%) and stillbirth or early neonatal death (7.3%) were highest in Type III. No statistically significant global differences were detected for these outcomes. No statistically significant adjusted associations were detected for Type II or III vs Type I. In the neonatal logistic model, the adjusted odds ratio per additional gestational week was 0.73 (95% confidence interval 0.64-0.82).
CONCLUSIONS: The selected outcomes showed no statistically significant adjusted associations for Types II or III compared with Type I. These exploratory findings do not establish equivalence or estimate FGM-associated risk relative to no FGM. Selection, imprecision, residual confounding, incomplete management data, and outcome-coding limitations constrain interpretation.

articles.title: Acute cardiac failure in pregnancy: diagnosis and treatment.
articles.journal: Archivos peruanos de cardiologia y cirugia cardiovascular
articles.authors: Muñoz-Ortiz E, Gándara-Ricardo JA, Holguín-González É et al.
articles.abstract: Heart disease affects approximately 4% of pregnancies and is the leading non-obstetric cause of maternal death during pregnancy in many countries. The physiological hormonal and haemodynamic changes that occur during this period can unmask previously undiagnosed cardiac disease and destabilise pre-existing cardiovascular conditions. Acute heart failure during pregnancy is uncommon; however, it can lead to severe maternal and fetal complications. Although the diagnostic criteria are the same as those used in the general population, diagnosis can be challenging because the cardinal signs and symptoms of heart failure overlap with several symptoms and clinical findings that commonly occur during pregnancy. A comprehensive clinical history therefore remains fundamental to the diagnostic approach, enabling the rational use of complementary investigations and, in many cases, guiding treatment. Management of acute heart failure during pregnancy must be highly individualised and may involve decisions regarding continuation of the pregnancy and the optimal mode of delivery. Care should therefore be led by an experienced multidisciplinary team with expertise in the diagnosis and management of cardiovascular disease during pregnancy, with the aim of achieving the best possible outcomes for both the mother and the fetus.

articles.title: Quercetin ameliorates gestational diabetes mellitus-induced placental dysfunction by modulating the AGE-RAGE-associated oxidative and inflammatory signaling network.
articles.authors: Liu X, Qi X, Liang Z et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) induces placental structural and functional disturbances associated with dysregulated AGE-RAGE/ROS signaling and inflammatory responses. Existing flavonoid-related studies merely observed changes in pathway protein levels, lacking direct experimental proof of molecular binding between candidate compounds and core receptors. This study aimed to investigate the potential involvement of RAGE in the protective effects of quercetin and to characterize the associated AGE-RAGE/ROS/NF-κB-related signaling changes in GDM placental injury.
METHODS: Network pharmacology was used to screen quercetin's therapeutic targets for GDM. Molecular docking was performed using the human RAGE structure to predict the potential interaction between quercetin and RAGE, and molecular dynamics simulation was conducted to evaluate the stability of the predicted complex. A combined streptozotocin-high-fat diet GDM rat model and 30 mM high-glucose HTR-8/SVneo trophoblast injury model were constructed. FPS-ZM1 was used as a pharmacological tool to perturb RAGE-associated signaling in vitro. ROS, inflammatory cytokines, and key pathway gene and protein expression were examined to characterize the associated signaling changes.
RESULTS: Network pharmacology identified SERPINE1 (a critical regulator of placental vascular remodeling) as the core hub gene, with the AGE-RAGE pathway showing the highest enrichment score. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations predicted a dynamically stable complex formed between quercetin and the ligand-binding domain of RAGE. GDM induction was associated with increased AGE accumulation, RAGE expression, ROS production, phosphorylated NF-κB p65, and SERPINE1 expression, together with an increase in Nrf2 expression, whereas quercetin treatment attenuated these alterations. Quercetin intervention also improved glucose tolerance and placental pathological changes.
CONCLUSION: Quercetin alleviates GDM-associated placental dysfunction by improving metabolic abnormalities, oxidative imbalance, and inflammatory responses. Computational analysis suggests a potential interaction between quercetin and RAGE. These findings provide evidence that quercetin may regulate the AGE-RAGE-associated oxidative and inflammatory signaling network and improve placental homeostasis under diabetic conditions.

articles.title: Structured effects of exercise on circulating brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) in postmenopausal women: a meta-analysis.
articles.authors: Zhou Y, Chai J, Wang J et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To systematically evaluate the effect of structured exercise interventions on circulating brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) levels among postmenopausal women, and to clarify the moderating effects of intervention modality, population characteristics, training duration, exercise intensity and energy-supply pattern on intervention outcomes, so as to provide evidence-based references for precise exercise interventions targeting brain health in postmenopausal women.
METHODS: Following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) statement, electronic databases including PubMed, Web of Science, EBSCO and CNKI were searched for original studies regarding the effects of various exercise interventions on BDNF in postmenopausal women, from database inception to August 1, 2026. The Cochrane Risk-of-Bias Tool was applied for randomized studies. For quasi-randomized and non-randomized intervention studies, we explicitly acknowledge limitations of this tool and interpret methodological assessments cautiously; studies with insufficient randomization reporting were rated as unclear risk of bias. Meta-analysis was performed using Review Manager 5.4 software. Effect sizes were presented as standardized mean difference (SMD) with 95% confidence interval (95% CI). Subgroup analysis, sensitivity analysis and publication-bias evaluation were also conducted.
RESULTS: Twelve studies involving 351 participants were finally included, with 173 subjects in the intervention group and 178 subjects in the control group. All included trials adopted chronic long-term structured exercise interventions without acute single-bout exercise protocols. Pooled meta-analysis demonstrated that structured exercise interventions significantly elevated BDNF levels in postmenopausal women compared with control conditions [SMD = 0.64, 95% CI (0.11, 1.17), P = 0.02], with substantial between-study heterogeneity (I² = 81%, P < 0.0001). Subgroup analyses (only subgroups with ≥3 studies included for quantitative synthesis) indicated that intervention modality, population characteristics, training duration and energy-supply pattern were potential main sources of heterogeneity. Statistically-significant maximum effect sizes were observed in the resistance training subgroup [SMD = 1.07, 95% CI (0.12, 2.01), P = 0.03], healthy older/postmenopausal-women subgroup [SMD = 0.30, 95% CI (-0.05, 0.65), P = 0.009], anaerobic-energy-supply-predominant subgroup…

articles.title: Transvaginal flap-fistula repair with offset suturing for vesicovaginal fistula.
articles.journal: Wideochirurgia i inne techniki maloinwazyjne = Videosurgery and other miniinvasive techniques
articles.authors: Wang XQ, Cui YL, Li L et al.
articles.abstract: Vesicovaginal fistula (VVF) is the most common type of urogenital fistula. It is typically caused by iatrogenic injuries, such as those sustained during pelvic surgery. Transvaginal repair is considered the preferred approach due to its minimally-invasive nature. However, the traditional Latzko procedure or layered closure techniques often sacrifice an excessive amount of vaginal wall tissue, which can lead to postoperative vaginal shortening and dyspareunia. This study aimed to introduce a modified transvaginal flap-fistula offset repair technique. This technique utilizes offset suturing of anatomical layers, not only improving the fistula closure rate but also maximally preserving vaginal length and function. A 48-year-old patient who developed VVF following total hysterectomy successfully underwent this procedure, with the operative time of 45 minutes and an estimated intraoperative blood loss of 5 ml. The urinary catheter was removed 4 weeks postoperatively, and the patient experienced no leakage. At 3-month follow-up, cystoscopy showed complete closure of the fistula. Vaginal anatomical morphology and length recovered well, with no sexual dysfunction. The Female Sexual Function Index score improved from 6 points preoperatively to 27 postprocedure. The transvaginal flap-fistula repair using an offset method can construct a robust tissue barrier and help avoid overlapping suture lines. It is a safe, effective, and minimally-invasive option that maintains vaginal length.

articles.title: Maternal vitamin B12 deficiency in pregnancy: burden, associated outcomes, and implications for antenatal care in South Asia-a narrative review.
articles.authors: Yadav A, Gandhi KY, Puri M
articles.abstract: Vitamin B12 (cobalamin) deficiency during pregnancy carries a disproportionate burden in South Asia, yet it remains outside India's national antenatal supplementation programme, which continues to prioritize iron and folic acid alone. This narrative review is organized around three questions of programmatic relevance: how large is the burden of maternal vitamin B12 deficiency and what drives it; what maternal and offspring outcomes are associated with low maternal vitamin B12 status, and how strong is the supporting evidence; and what these findings imply for antenatal practice and policy in resource-limited South Asian settings. Following a documented literature search of two databases (January 2000-March 2026), we synthesize evidence on prevalence, dietary and socioeconomic determinants, biological mechanisms, and clinical outcomes, and appraise the strength of inference underpinning each major claim. Pooled global prevalence estimates range from approximately 17% to 25%, whereas Indian and South Asian estimates in pregnancy commonly reach 40-70%. Low maternal vitamin B12 status has been associated predominantly through observational evidence with preeclampsia, pregnancy loss, gestational diabetes, neural tube defects, fetal growth restriction, preterm birth, and impaired offspring neurodevelopment, with hyperhomocysteinaemia, disrupted one-carbon metabolism, and altered methylation as the principal proposed pathways. India's folate-only supplementation policy may contribute to a low-vitamin B12/high-folate imbalance that has been associated with adverse metabolic outcomes in offspring. Randomized evidence, including the recent MATCOBIND trial, consistently demonstrates improvement in biochemical markers of vitamin B12 status; however, evidence for corresponding clinical benefits remains limited. On current evidence, a targeted, risk-based approach to screening and supplementation, rather than universal supplementation, is best supported and can be readily integrated into existing antenatal infrastructure. Priorities for future research include pregnancy-specific diagnostic thresholds, adequately powered trials with long-term follow-up, independent replication of recent intervention findings, and cost-effectiveness analyses in South Asian populations.

articles.title: From biomarker discovery to prediction models: clinical translation of multi-omics for early prediction of gestational diabetes mellitus.
articles.authors: Yan H
articles.abstract: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) affects roughly one in seven pregnancies worldwide, yet diagnosis by oral glucose tolerance testing at 24-28 weeks of gestation leaves only a narrow window for intervention. The demonstrated benefit of treating early-diagnosed GDM has intensified interest in first-trimester prediction. This narrative review synthesises recent advances in early-pregnancy biomarkers for GDM, shifting the emphasis from biomarker discovery to clinical translation. Conventional lipid indicators and composite indices provide moderate predictive power at minimal cost (odds ratios 1.4-1.7; AUCs 0.75-0.82). Metabolomic and lipidomic studies have identified recurrent signatures - phospholipid remodelling, glycerolipid accumulation, fatty acid and acylcarnitine excess, branched-chain amino acids and bile acids - that map onto insulin resistance, lipotoxicity and hepatic steatosis, and omics-enhanced models report derivation-stage AUCs of approximately 0.83-0.95 with apparent incremental value over clinical factors alone, although these estimates derive predominantly from small cohorts that have rarely undergone external validation. Gut-microbiome features, thyroid parameters and environmental exposures further widen the aetiological frame. Translation remains limited, however, by small derivation cohorts, scarce external validation, analytical heterogeneity and the absence of trials testing biomarker-guided early intervention. We propose a pragmatic roadmap towards clinically deployable first-trimester prediction, with particular attention to high-burden Asian populations.

articles.title: Dietary fatty acid profiles in obesity-associated female infertility: mechanisms and reproductive implications.
articles.authors: Wu Y, Qin M, Zhao M et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Dietary fatty acids are membrane components and lipid mediator precursors in the ovarian microenvironment. It is currently unclear how their composition determines the reproductive outcome in obesity-related infertility.
AIMS: To map how saturated, monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fatty acids and their proportions affect oocyte competence, steroidogenesis and early embryonic development under obesity and high-fat diets.
METHODS: The system retrieved English-language literature published from January 1, 2017 to September 30, 2026 in PubMed, Web of Science, Cochrane Library and Scopus. Predefined keywords for fatty acid types, reproductive outcomes and metabolic background were used, supplemented by manual searches. Two reviewers independently screened the titles, abstracts and full texts according to the pre-defined inclusion and exclusion criteria; eligible evidence included observational studies in humans, animal experiments and in vitro mechanism studies. Results were presented in a narrative summary; due to significant heterogeneity, no meta-analysis was conducted.
RESULTS: A total of 699 retrieval records were identified, among which 82 studies met the inclusion criteria and were included in the data extraction. The analysis of these studies showed that the effect direction depended on the type of fatty acid and the context, rather than any single fatty acid: palmitic acid and stearic acid caused damage to oocyte maturation and blastocyst formation through endoplasmic reticulum stress (IRE1-XBP1) and mitochondrial stress (ceramide-AMPK/SIRT3). Oleic acid buffered lipid toxicity through lipid droplets, but excessive amounts inhibited CYP19A1 steroid synthesis and activated NLRP3/IL-1β. Omega-3 competed with arachidonic acid at COX-2 and exerted effects through NF-κB, Nrf2/GPX4 and GPR120, while omega-6-derived prostaglandins supported ovulation and implantation.
CONCLUSION: Reducing palmitic acid, moderating oleic acid, increasing EPA and DHA and limiting omega-6 excess opens a non-pharmacological route, informing preconception nutrition in obesity and PCOS, refining assisted reproduction, and guiding ratio-based trials.

articles.title: T cells in autoimmune thyroid disease and pregnancy: an emerging immunological interface.
articles.authors: Perić I, Fischer L, Ilić Tomaš M et al.
articles.abstract: Pregnancy is a condition that requires highly coordinated immunological adaptations to ensure maternal-fetal tolerance while preserving effective immune defense. Among adaptive immune cells, T lymphocytes play a central role in regulating the balance between immune activation and immune tolerance throughout gestation. Distinct T-cell subsets-including T helper (Th)1, Th2, Th17, regulatory T (Treg), and T follicular helper (Tfh) cells-contribute to the dynamic immune changes necessary for a successful pregnancy. Autoimmune thyroid disease (AITD), encompassing Hashimoto's thyroiditis and Graves' disease, is characterized by dysregulated T-cell-mediated immune responses, including enhanced Th1 and Th17 activity and impaired Treg-mediated immune regulation. As AITD frequently affects women of reproductive age, the interaction between AITD and pregnancy-related immune adaptation represents a clinical and immunological challenge. Increasing evidence suggests that persistent immune dysregulation may contribute to thyroid dysfunction and adverse pregnancy outcomes, including pregnancy loss, preterm birth, preeclampsia, and fetal growth restriction. This review summarizes current evidence on T-cell-mediated immune regulation in normal pregnancy and AITD, with particular emphasis on the immunological interactions between these conditions. We discuss physiological changes in major T-cell subsets during pregnancy, mechanisms of immune dysregulation in AITD, and their potential implications for maternal and fetal outcomes. The potential roles of T-cell memory and postpartum immune changes are also briefly considered. A better understanding of T-cell dynamics at the intersection of pregnancy and thyroid autoimmunity may provide further insight into underlying immunological mechanisms and, with further validation, potentially inform future approaches to risk stratification and individualized management.

articles.title: Predicting outcomes in locally advanced cervical cancer treated with radiotherapy: a systematic review of nomograms.
articles.authors: Bae J, Kim U, Kang S
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To systematically evaluate published nomograms developed for patients with locally advanced cervical cancer (LACC) treated with radiotherapy, focusing on prognostic performance, core predictive variables, and implications for future model development.
METHODS: A systematic literature search of PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library identified studies published between 2010 and 2025 that developed new nomograms for LACC cohorts treated with radiotherapy or chemoradiotherapy. Data extraction included study population, predicted outcomes (overall survival [OS], progression-free survival [PFS], or disease-free survival [DFS]), model performance (C-index), validation methods, calibration, and predictor variables. Predictor patterns were summarized primarily by frequency of inclusion across nomograms, with β-coefficients used only for exploratory within-model descriptions.
RESULTS: Nine studies met the inclusion criteria; eight developed nomograms for OS and three evaluated disease progression outcomes (PFS or DFS), with two studies evaluating both outcome categories. Reported C-indices ranged from 0.68 to 0.835, indicating moderate to good discrimination. Lymph node status, FIGO stage, and tumor size were among the most frequently incorporated predictors, while histology and SCC-Ag were also recurrently included. Validation in independent cohorts remained limited. Graphical calibration was commonly reported, whereas quantitative calibration measures and decision-curve analyses were inconsistently reported.
CONCLUSIONS: Nomograms for LACC treated with radiotherapy generally demonstrate moderate-to-good discriminative performance and frequently incorporate lymph node status, stage, and tumor size. However, methodological heterogeneity, incomplete validation, and evolving treatment paradigms limit their immediate generalizability. Future work should focus on robust external validation, recalibration, and evaluation in contemporary treatment cohorts before clinical implementation.

articles.title: Dose- and time-resolved immune states in cervical cancer radiotherapy: dynamic multimodal biomarkers for adaptive immunoradiotherapy.
articles.authors: Xiao C, Tian F, Kang M et al.
articles.abstract: Concurrent and maintenance immune checkpoint blockade improves survival for select high-risk locally advanced cervical cancer patients treated with definitive chemoradiotherapy, yet population-level efficacy cannot identify responders, optimal timing of benefit, or actionable biological targets for resistance. Fractionated pelvic radiotherapy induces dynamic immune perturbation: antigen release and interferon signaling occur alongside lymphocyte depletion, impaired antigen presentation, suppressive myeloid remodeling and resistant tumor clone selection. Pretreatment biomarkers fail to capture this evolving biological landscape. This review synthesizes evidence for dose- and time-resolved tissue/blood immunity, longitudinal MRI/PET imaging, delta radiomics, multimodal artificial intelligence, and HPV circulating tumor DNA. Two key conclusions are drawn. First, serial studies show heterogeneous immune remodeling modulated by radiation dose, sampling site, assay platform and time point. Second, mid-treatment tumor regression has reproducible prognostic evidence, and post-treatment viral circulating tumor DNA has prospective validation for residual-risk assessment and monitoring. We categorize biomarker functions as response assessment, prognosis, treatment-effect prediction and monitoring, define six evidence gates, and propose trial-restricted decision windows to guide future translational investigations.

articles.title: Anesthetic Management of Pregnant Patients With Cardiovascular Disease: A Practical, Lesion-Based Clinical Review.
articles.authors: Iosovich A, Ronenson A, Guasch E et al.
articles.abstract: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is a major cause of maternal morbidity and mortality and increasingly complicates pregnancy as more women with congenital and acquired heart disease reach reproductive age. Anesthetic management of these patients requires integrating lesion-specific cardiovascular physiology, pregnancy-related hemodynamic changes, obstetric considerations, and the anticipated effects of labor, anesthesia, delivery, hemorrhage, and the postpartum transition. Despite contemporary cardiovascular and obstetric guidelines, translating lesion-specific physiology into practical anesthetic decisions remains challenging. This narrative review provides a practical framework for the peripartum anesthetic management of pregnant patients with CVD. We discuss contemporary risk assessment using the modified World Health Organization 2.0 classification and the Cardiac Disease in Pregnancy II risk model, followed by principles of Pregnancy Heart Team planning, labor analgesia, cesarean delivery, monitoring, anticoagulation, uterotonic therapy, and postpartum surveillance. Lesion-specific considerations are reviewed for mitral stenosis, aortic stenosis, aortic disease and coarctation, pulmonary hypertension, pregnancy-associated myocardial infarction, peripartum cardiomyopathy, congenital heart disease, and Fontan circulation. Particular attention is given to maintaining appropriate preload, ventricular filling, systemic vascular resistance, cardiac rhythm, and oxygenation while avoiding abrupt changes in vascular resistance or cardiac loading conditions. The review emphasizes individualized anesthetic planning rather than universal preferences for a particular anesthetic technique or mode of delivery. Neuraxial anesthesia can be advantageous in selected patients but should be considered in the context of ventricular function, pulmonary pressures, anticoagulation, urgency, and the expected hemodynamic response. General anesthesia remains an important option when neuraxial anesthesia is contraindicated or inadequate, rapid delivery is required, airway or ventilatory control is necessary, or maternal or surgical circumstances dictate. Uterotonic therapy should similarly be individualized according to cardiovascular physiology, with careful attention to dose, route, and hemodynamic effects. Close multidisciplinary planning and coordinated postpartum care are particularly important for women with pulmonary hypertension, ventricular dysfunction, complex congenital…

articles.title: Knowledge, Attitudes, and Practices Related to Polyendocrine Metabolic Ovarian Syndrome Among Women with PMOS in Jiangsu Province, China: A Cross-sectional Study.
articles.authors: Shi X, Ma J, Wang X et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To assess knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) related to polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS; formerly polycystic ovary syndrome [PCOS]) among patients in Jiangsu Province, China, and explore factors associated with health-related practices.
METHODS: This cross-sectional study included 422 patients with PMOS recruited from a tertiary hospital in Jiangsu, China, between July 2023 and December 2024. Sociodemographic, clinical, biochemical, and KAP data were collected. Correlation analysis, univariable and multivariable logistic regression, and observed-score path analysis were performed.
RESULTS: The median knowledge, attitude, and practice scores were 12/20 (IQR 9-14), 142/190 (IQR 126-159), and 20/40 (IQR 14-25), respectively.
