Overall, 38.63% of participants had poor knowledge, 64.22% had positive attitudes, and 54.98% had poor practices. In multivariable analysis, higher attitude scores (aOR per 10 points=2.241, 95% CI 1.762-2.852) and receipt of both dietary and exercise guidance vs no guidance (aOR=3.681, 95% CI 1.678-8.075) were associated with higher odds of good practice, whereas higher body mass index and waist-to-hip ratio were inversely associated with good practice. Path analysis showed positive knowledge-to-attitude and attitude-to-practice associations, with a significant positive indirect association between knowledge and practice through attitude.
CONCLUSIONS: Patients with PMOS demonstrated generally positive attitudes but insufficient knowledge and health-related practices. These findings identify health-related beliefs, self-efficacy, and practical lifestyle guidance as potential targets for future intervention studies.

articles.title: The cervicovaginal microbiome as a candidate correlate and potential predictor of HPV clearance and treatment response after HSIL therapy: a scoping review.
articles.authors: Mwesige B, Angucia B, Mbodi L et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Persistent high-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV) infection causes virtually all high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions (HSIL) and cervical cancer, but only a minority progress, implicating host and microenvironmental cofactors. The cervicovaginal microbiome (CVM), particularly Lactobacillus-dominated communities, may influence hrHPV persistence, clearance, and response to HSIL treatment.
OBJECTIVE: To map evidence linking the CVM with hrHPV clearance and outcomes after HSIL treatment, including loop electrosurgical excision procedure (LEEP) and conization, using PRISMA-ScR and Arksey and O'Malley frameworks.
METHODS: Literature on cervicovaginal microbiota, community state types (CSTs), HPV natural history, HSIL/CIN treatment, probiotics, microbiome-directed interventions, and predictive biomarkers was systematically searched and narratively synthesized using a Population-Concept-Context framework.
RESULTS: Sixty-six sources were charted. Lactobacillus crispatus-dominated communities (CST-I) were associated with hrHPV clearance and favorable post-treatment outcomes, whereas CST-IV, bacterial vaginosis, and increased alpha-diversity were associated with hrHPV persistence, greater HSIL severity, and treatment failure. Proposed mechanisms include lactic acid-mediated pH regulation, D-lactic acid signaling, and modulation of viral oncoproteins and immune responses. Excision altered the CVM, with restoration of Lactobacillus dominance accompanying viral clearance. Microbial-signature machine-learning models showed promising but preliminary predictive performance. Oral and intravaginal probiotics showed inconsistent but generally favorable trends, with strongest evidence for intravaginal L. crispatus transplantation. Gut microbiome diversity may also influence chemoradiotherapy outcomes in invasive cervical cancer.
CONCLUSION: The CVM is a promising predictor of hrHPV clearance and HSIL treatment response. However, methodological heterogeneity, small cohorts, and limited prospective evidence restrict clinical translation. Large prospective studies and rigorously designed trials are needed to validate predictive signatures and determine whether microbiome profiling or targeted modulation can improve HSIL management and outcomes.

articles.title: Global Trends and Disparities in Maternal Mortality: A Longitudinal Multi-Country Analysis.
articles.authors: Woudneh AF, Gebrie YF, Nigussie MM et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Maternal mortality is one of the most significant global public health challenges and an important indicator of health-system performance and socioeconomic development. Although substantial reductions have been achieved since 1990, progress has slowed in recent years, and substantial disparities persist across countries and regions.
METHODS: This longitudinal ecological study used country-level panel data from the Maternal Mortality Dataset compiled by Banerjee (2021), covering 182 countries from 1990 to 2021. Maternal mortality ratio (MMR), expressed as deaths per 100,000 live births, was natural-log transformed for statistical modeling. Human Development Index (HDI) group and continent were included as fixed-effect predictors, while linear mixed-effects models with country-specific random intercepts and random slopes for centered year were used to account for between-country heterogeneity and differences in temporal trajectories.
RESULTS: Maternal mortality declined over the study period (β = -0.029, 95% CI, -0.032 to -0.026; p < 0.001). Compared with the High HDI group, countries in the Low HDI group had higher log(MMR) (β = 1.803, 95% CI, 1.458-2.147; p < 0.001), as did countries in the Medium HDI group (β = 1.042, 95% CI, 0.767-1.317; p < 0.001), whereas the Very High HDI group had lower log(MMR) (β = -1.004, 95% CI, -1.268 to -0.739; p < 0.001). Compared with Africa, log(MMR) was lower in America (β = -0.488, 95% CI, -0.813 to -0.162; p = 0.004), Asia (β = -0.838, 95% CI, -1.134 to -0.542; p < 0.001), Europe (β = -1.698, 95% CI, -2.067 to -1.330; p < 0.001), and Oceania (β = -0.953, 95% CI, -1.404 to -0.502; p < 0.001). Adding random slopes improved model fit (χ 2 = 8041.6, df = 2; p < 0.001), indicating heterogeneity in country-specific temporal trajectories. Marginal and conditional R 2 were 0.849 and 0.997, respectively.
CONCLUSION: Maternal mortality declined substantially between 1990 and 2021, but disparities persisted across HDI groups, geographical regions, and countries. The findings highlight the importance of socioeconomic and geographical context when interpreting global maternal mortality patterns and support context-specific approaches to further reduce maternal mortality.

articles.title: Long-term effectiveness of app-based therapy for female urinary incontinence: 48-week follow-up of a randomised controlled trial.
articles.authors: Frey L, Haferkamp A, Lehmacher W et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Long-term data for digital therapeutics in urinary incontinence are scarce. We assessed whether improvements with app-based multimodal therapy are sustained over 48 weeks, and outcomes after a 12-week delay in initiation.
METHODS: In this prespecified 48-week follow-up of the DINKS (Digital Incontinence Study) randomised waitlist-controlled trial, women (≥18 years) with stress, urge, or mixed urinary incontinence recruited between April 30 and September 2 2024 across Germany received app-based therapy immediately or after a 12-week waitlist, alongside standard care. The primary outcome was change from baseline in ICIQ-UI-SF (International Consultation on Incontinence Questionnaire-Urinary Incontinence Short Form) score at weeks 12, 24, 36, and 48. Trial registration: NCT06389838.
FINDINGS: Data availability declined progressively from 186 of 194 participants (95.9%) at week 12-66 (34.0%) at week 48. Pooled improvements exceeded the minimal clinically important difference at 12, 24, and 36 weeks after therapy start (ICIQ-UI-SF at 36 weeks -4.13, 95% Confidence Interval (CI) -4.80 to -3.47), and 73-77% of participants met the responder threshold. Differences between immediate and delayed initiation were small (ICIQ-UI-SF at 36 weeks 0.08, -1.09 to 1.25). The week-48 estimate (-3.88, -4.74 to -3.03) was intervention-group only, from 27 of 96. No adverse events were reported.
INTERPRETATION: App-based multimodal therapy was associated with clinically meaningful improvements sustained through at least 36 weeks after intervention start. Differences between immediate and 12-week-delayed initiation were small relative to the minimal important difference, but no non-inferiority margin was prespecified and only one delay was tested; symptoms were unchanged while waiting, so waiting times should still be minimised. Confirmation in larger trials with active comparators is needed.
FUNDING: Kranus Health GmbH.

articles.title: Interconnected metabolic and reproductive signaling axis in type 2 diabetes mellitus and polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome.
articles.authors: Padder KA, Ganie MA, Jahan N et al.
articles.abstract: Polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS) and type 2 diabetes milletus (T2DM) are interlinked endocrine and metabolic disorders characterized by insulin resistance (IR), hyperinsulinemia and chronic low-grade inflammation. Both these abnormal physiological and metabolic conditions share overlapping cellular and molecular pathways involving insulin signaling, PI3K/Akt dysregulation, oxidative stress (OS) and inflammatory cascades. In PMOS, these disturbances further intersect with reproductive axis dysfunction including hyperandrogenism and follicular arrest. This manuscript reviews the shared metabolic and reproductive signaling pathways in PMOS and T2DM, highlighting insulin signaling defects, AMPK-mTOR imbalance, WNT/β-catenin dysregulation and inflammatory mediators. Understanding these common pathways may facilitate development of unified and more specific therapeutic strategies targeting both metabolic and reproductive dysfunction among these disorders.

articles.title: Health policy effects of budgetary actions under the second Trump administration.
articles.authors: Jarman H, Kulikoff R, Yaver M et al.
articles.abstract: We analyze the impact of the second Trump administration's budgetary actions on policies affecting health. Using the Social Determinants of Health framework, we review executive actions, including funding freezes and rescissions, and the One Big Beautiful Bill Act. We conclude that these measures weakened federal capacity, public health infrastructure, education, scientific research, global health programs, and environmental protections. Medicaid, Affordable Care Act policies, family planning, and food assistance face reduced eligibility, greater administrative burdens, and substantial funding cuts, while funding grows for immigration and carceral policies that damage health. Noncitizens, low-income communities, racial and ethnic minorities, disabled people, and rural populations will bear disproportionate harms. State and local governments may mitigate some effects, but fiscal, legal, political, and institutional constraints limit them. Rebuilding federal health policy will require more than restoring previous funding; policymakers must design stronger, resilient institutions suited to damaged institutions.

articles.title: Predictors of Psychological Stress and Infertility Among Reproductive-Age Women in Jammu and Kashmir: A Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.authors: Sharma K, Bhushan I, Sistla S
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Infertility affects nearly one in six individuals globally, with a substantial proportion of cases remaining idiopathic. Emerging evidence suggests that psychological stress may influence reproductive outcomes through neuroendocrine and immune pathways, potentially influencing the vaginal microbiome and the reproductive microenvironment. This study aimed to assess the prevalence of stress and infertility and examine their association among women of reproductive age in Jammu and Kashmir.
METHODS: A cross-sectional study was conducted among 1068 married women aged 18-48 years in Jammu and Kashmir, including women with idiopathic infertility and fertile controls. Data on sociodemographic characteristics, perceived stress, symptoms of reproductive tract infections (RTIs), sleep patterns, and physical stress manifestations were collected using a structured interviewer-administered questionnaire. Binary logistic regression analysis was performed to identify factors associated with psychological stress and infertility.
RESULTS: Overall, 37.6% of participants reported stress, while 29.3% had infertility. Stress was significantly associated with older age groups, employment status, lower financial status, RTI symptoms, physical stress manifestations, sleep duration, and infertility. Women with infertility had markedly higher odds of stress. Infertility was significantly associated with a history of stress, age, employment status, financial status, RTI symptoms, and sleep duration.
CONCLUSION: Psychological stress is strongly associated with infertility and related health and socioeconomic factors among women in this population. These findings highlight the potential interplay between psychological, reproductive, and social factors in reproductive health. Further longitudinal studies are needed to clarify causal pathways and inform targeted interventions.

articles.title: Patient preference for intraoperative opioid strategy and early postoperative recovery after noncardiac surgery: a prospective partially randomised patient-preference trial (the PERFECT trial).
articles.authors: Gricourt Y, Boulos NM, Delaporte A et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patient-centred care increasingly encourages patients to participate in decisions regarding their anaesthetic management. However, whether expressing a preference regarding their anaesthetic management is associated with improved postoperative recovery remains unknown. We evaluated the association between preference expression and quality of recovery after noncardiac surgery.
METHODS: In this prospective partially randomised patient-preference study conducted at two academic hospitals, adults undergoing minimally invasive abdominal, urologic, or gynaecologic surgery received standardised information on opioid-based and opioid-free anaesthesia, co-developed with patient partners. Participants expressing a preference received their preferred strategy, whereas those without a preference were randomised 1:1 to either strategy. The primary outcome was the Quality of Recovery-15 (QoR-15) score on postoperative day (POD) 1.
RESULTS: Among 220 analysed participants, 177 (80.5%) expressed a preference, and 43 (19.5%) underwent random allocation. Mean [standard deviation] QoR-15 scores on POD 1 were higher among participants expressing a preference than among randomised participants (108.8 [18.2] vs 100.8 [23.5]), with an unadjusted mean difference of 7.9 points (95% confidence interval [CI] 1.5-14.4; P=0.017). The adjusted marginal mean difference was 7.1 points (95% CI 0.3-13.9; P=0.042). Scores on the QoR-15 also remained higher on POD 2. Sensitivity analyses showed consistent effect estimates but attenuated statistical significance. Secondary outcomes, including postoperative nausea and vomiting and bradycardia, were similar between groups.
CONCLUSIONS: Expression of a preference regarding intraoperative opioid management was associated with better reported early postoperative patient-reported recovery. Given the non-randomised comparison and limited precision, -generating and support further investigation into the role of patient-preference expression in perioperative recovery.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: The full, long-term study is pre-registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (identifier, NCT06855641; first posted, 3 March 2025; Alexandre Joosten). https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06855641.

articles.title: Household income and women's reproductive strategies in Almaty (Kazakhstan): urban stratification of access to health.
articles.authors: Bakytzhanova A, Alimbekova G
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: The aim of this article is to demonstrate how household financial status and the spatial structure of opportunities in the metropolis are interrelated with women's reproductive strategies in Almaty, where formal access to healthcare is combined with uneven access costs in terms of time, money, quality, and predictability of service delivery.
METHODS: The empirical basis consisted of a cross-sectional survey of women of reproductive age in eight districts of Almaty (N = 934). The analysis utilized a scale reliability assessment (Cronbach's α), χ2 contingency tables with Cramer's V, and interdistrict comparisons using the nonparametric Kruskal-Wallis test and the median test. The urban environment was operationalized through an infrastructure provision index, comprising six domains: Education, clinics, retail and service environment, leisure, sports, and safety.
RESULTS: The resulting six-item index demonstrated good internal consistency (Cronbach's α = 0.814; standardized α = 0.815; n = 780). Statistically significant interdistrict heterogeneity was found in accessibility of clinics (χ2 = 16.048; p = 0.025), retail and service infrastructure (χ2 = 28.472; p < 0.001), leisure (χ2 = 32.640; p < 0.001), sports (χ2 = 31.666; p < 0.001), and safety (χ2 = 17.801; p = 0.013), while no differences were found in educational infrastructure (p = 0.844). The most significant predictors of reproductive practices and attitudes were household financial well-being and education level. The results demonstrate that the formal availability of services does not imply equality in actual access to them.
CONCLUSION: Inequality in reproductive opportunities is reproduced through hidden transaction costs of access, waiting, transportation logistics, the need for paid alternatives, and additional support resources. Neighborhood of residence is not only a territorial characteristic but also an indicator of the organizational structure of everyday life, influencing care-seeking behavior and family planning strategies. The proposed framework of the Atlas of Reproductive Opportunities can be used to identify local bottlenecks and inform targeted preventive and management decisions.

articles.title: Self-collected first-void urine cytology as a non-invasive triage tool for endometrial cancer detection.
articles.authors: Johnson JE, Narine N, Chandraya AR et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Sequential tests that measure, visualise and sample the endometrium are currently used to confirm disease status in women with suspected endometrial cancer. These tests are invasive and unpleasant, with moderate diagnostic accuracy. A non-invasive test that accurately triages women with postmenopausal bleeding (PMB) for routine diagnostics would improve patient care. The aim of this study was to measure the potential for self-collected first-void urine cytology to detect endometrial cancer in women with PMB.
METHODS: This was a prospective diagnostic accuracy study of women referred with suspected endometrial cancer to St Mary's Hospital in Manchester. Self-collected first-void urine (10 mL Colli-Pee™ device with preservative for the first 94 participants, 20 mL with preservative thereafter) and clinician-collected vaginal samples (Delphi screener) were obtained prior to routine diagnostics. Cytology was evaluated by a cytologist blinded to participant disease status. The primary outcome was the sensitivity, specificity and accuracy of self-collected first-void urine cytology compared to vaginal cytology for endometrial cancer detection. Endometrial histopathology was the reference standard when performed; disease-negative status was defined by discharge from the cancer exclusion pathway and no cancer diagnosis at 6 months' follow up.
RESULTS: In 200 women with PMB (102 endometrial cancer cases; 98 cancer-free controls), self-collected first-void urine cytology demonstrated a sensitivity of 73.3% (95% CI 63.5-81.6) and specificity of 90.7% (95% CI 83.1-95.7) for endometrial cancer detection, with an AUC of 0.85 (95% CI 0.80-0.89). Vaginal cytology showed higher sensitivity 92.2% (95% CI 85.1-96.6), lower specificity 84.4% (95% CI 75.5-91.0) and an AUC of 0.94 (95% CI 0.91-0.97). Agreement between urine and vaginal cytology was substantial (κ=0.70), with discordant results predominantly in low-risk tumours. Urine cytology had good sensitivity in high-risk disease and remained a strong independent predictor of endometrial cancer on multivariable analysis (adjusted OR 23.8). In an exploratory but underpowered comparison, increasing Colli-Pee™ device collection volume from 10 mL to 20 mL increased sensitivity (70% vs 74.6%, p=0.629).
DISCUSSION: Self-collected first-void urine cytology shows moderate sensitivity and high specificity for endometrial cancer detection, however its diagnostic accuracy is currently insufficiently high to recommend…

articles.title: Male gonadal function and cancer treatment: Current perspectives.
articles.authors: Chiba K, Miyake H
articles.abstract: Recent advances in cancer treatment have markedly improved survival outcomes, increasing the importance of long-term quality of life issues, including male gonadal function. Cancer-related gonadal dysfunction results from the combined effects of the malignancy itself and anticancer therapies and primarily manifests as impaired spermatogenesis, although Leydig cell dysfunction may also contribute to long-term endocrine sequelae. Conventional treatments, including radiotherapy, surgery, and cytotoxic chemotherapy, have well-established gonadotoxic effects, whereas the long-term reproductive and endocrine consequences of newer anticancer therapies, such as molecular targeted agents and immune checkpoint inhibitors, remain incompletely understood. Although recovery of spermatogenesis is possible in some patients, persistent azoospermia and compensated or overt hypogonadism may develop after treatment. Sperm cryopreservation before gonadotoxic therapy remains the cornerstone of fertility preservation and should be considered for all eligible patients. In selected cancer survivors with persistent post-treatment azoospermia, microdissection testicular sperm extraction may provide an opportunity for biological fatherhood. In addition, increasing evidence suggests that long-term endocrine follow-up should address not only overt testosterone deficiency but also compensated Leydig cell dysfunction. As oncological outcomes continue to improve, clinicians should strive not only to cure cancer but also to preserve the long-term reproductive and endocrine health of cancer survivors through individualized treatment strategies and survivorship care.

articles.title: Myometrial invasion and tumor free distance from serosa as prognostic factors in endometrial endometrioid carcinoma.
articles.authors: Candotti G, Altieri A, Saponaro C et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Our aim was to investigate the prognostic role of myometrial invasion (MI) and tumor free distance (TFD) from serosa in patients with endometrial endometrioid carcinoma (EEC).
METHODS: In this retrospective multicenter study patients diagnosed with EEC with MI ≥50% were enrolled and treated at Policlinico Monserrato (Cagliari) and San Raffaele (Milan) from January 2016 to June 2023, with at least one year follow up. Youden index was determined for stratification, obtaining as cut off 82.5% for MI and 3 mm for TFD. Subgroups were related to lymph node (LN) status, grading, lymph vascular space involvement (LVSI), recurrence and survival.
RESULTS: Overall, 127 patients were included; 20 (15.7%) had positive LN; 20 (15.7%) relapsed. Considering 82.5% as cut off for MI, 68 patients (53.5%) had MI <82.5%, 59 (46.5%) ≥82.5%. Considering 3 mm as cut off for TFD, 64 patients (50.4%) had TFD ≥3 mm, 63 (49.6%) <3 mm. At multivariate analysis, MI ≥82.5% was associated with LN metastases (p=0.002) and recurrence (p=0.019); TFD <3 mm was related to recurrence (p=0.003), especially at distant sites, but not LN metastases (p=0.100). MI and TFD retained significance for disease free survival (DFS) alone (p=0.039 and p=0.007, respectively) and in combination (p=0.041).
CONCLUSION: MI and TFD represent crucial prognostic factors for recurrence, DFS and LN metastases, also providing information about recurrence site. Further studies are required to evaluate their role.

articles.title: Diagnostic and triage performance of CDO1 and CELF4 methylation in cervical exfoliated cells compared with serum biomarkers for endometrial cancer in abnormal bleeding women.
articles.authors: Shen Z, Wang Y, Lin J et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To validate CDO1 and CELF4 methylation analysis in cervical scrapings as a non-invasive diagnostic tool for endometrial cancer (EC) in women with abnormal uterine bleeding (AUB), aiming to develop an evidence-based triage strategy that reduces unnecessary invasive procedures.
METHODS: In this prospective cross-sectional study (January 2024-October 2025), 492 women with AUB underwent diagnostic evaluation before histopathology, including CDO1/CELF4 methylation testing in cervical scrapings, serum biomarker measurements, and transvaginal sonography (TVS)-based endometrial thickness (ET). Diagnostic performance was assessed by the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). Multivariate logistic regression, incorporating multiple imputation for missing data, identified independent EC predictors, and screening-triage strategies were compared.
RESULTS: Methylation-based assays outperformed conventional methods, with the combined CDO1/CELF4 test achieving the highest AUC (0.913) versus ET (0.608) and the best serum biomarker, human epididymis protein 4 (HE4; 0.752). After multiple imputation, CDO1 (odds ratio [OR]=30.0; 95% confidence interval [CI]=7.4-122.1) and CELF4 (OR=30.6; 95% CI=7.7-121.9) remained independent EC predictors, while HE4 lost significance. Methylation testing provided the most effective risk stratification, indicating a 75% EC risk when positive versus 4.5% when negative; in women with abnormal ET, risk was 76.7% if positive versus 7.6% if negative.
CONCLUSION: CDO1 and CELF4 methylation analysis in cervical scrapings offers superior diagnostic and triage performance for EC compared with serum biomarkers and ET, enabling accurate risk identification and minimizing invasive procedures in low-risk women. As this strategy was derived in a high-prevalence, referral-based cohort, further validation in lower-prevalence primary care populations is needed before clinical implementation.

articles.title: Depressive symptoms, semen parameters, and sexual outcomes in men undergoing fertility evaluation: a cross-sectional study.
articles.authors: Untan I, Untan S, Yesiloglu C
articles.abstract: This cross-sectional study examined the associations between depressive symptoms, semen parameters, employment status, and sexual outcomes in 308 men (age, mean ± standard deviation [s.d.]: 31.9 ± 6.5 years) undergoing fertility evaluation at Kirsehir Ahi Evran University Training and Research Hospital, Kirsehir, Türkiye, between January 2024 and January 2026. Participants completed the questionnaires of Beck Depression Inventory-II (BDI-II), Beck Anxiety Inventory (BAI), Golombok-Rust Inventory of Sexual Satisfaction (GRISS), and the International Index of Erectile Function-15 (IIEF-15). Semen analysis was performed according to the World Health Organization 2021 guidelines. Multiple linear regression revealed that depressive symptoms were the strongest independent factor associated with both erectile dysfunction (IIEF-15: β = -0.393, P < 0.001) and sexual dissatisfaction (GRISS: β = 0.421, P < 0.001), whereas semen parameters, anxiety, and age were not independently associated with sexual outcomes (all P > 0.05). Progressive motility showed a weak bivariate correlation with sexual dissatisfaction but was not an independent correlate in multivariable analysis, where depressive symptoms accounted for the observed variance. Unemployed men demonstrated lower progressive motility, normal morphology, and sperm concentration compared with employed men in bivariate analyses (all P < 0.05). These findings suggest that depressive symptoms, rather than semen quality, are the primary modifiable factor associated with sexual dissatisfaction and erectile dysfunction in men seeking fertility assessment. Routine depression screening in fertility clinics may help identify men at risk for adverse sexual outcomes.

articles.title: Evaluating Intravaginal and Transvaginal Electrical Stimulation Techniques for Urinary Incontinence: A Systematic Review with Meta-analysis.
articles.authors: Nazareth JVS, Ciriaco da Silva J, Lopes EA et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study aimed to determine the effectiveness of intravaginal electrical stimulation for managing urinary incontinence.
METHODS: Searches were conducted across PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, Scopus, Web of Science, Latin American and Caribbean Health Sciences Literature, and gray literature sources including Google Scholar, OpenGrey, and ProQuest. Risk of bias was evaluated using the Cochrane tool. The primary outcome was pelvic floor muscle (PFM) pressure, while secondary outcomes included PFM strength, involuntary urine loss, frequency of urinary leakage episodes, and quality of life.
RESULTS: Seven randomized controlled trials met the inclusion criteria, comprising a total of 505 women. Two of the included reports (Amaro 2005 and Amaro 2006) derived from the same patient population were treated as a single study for the purpose of this review. The pooled analysis showed significant improvements in PFM pressure (3.92 cm H2O, 95% CI, 1.50-6.34; P = .001; I2 = 55%), PFM strength (0.89, 95% CI, 0.37-1.41; P = .0008; I2 = 52%), frequency of urinary leakage episodes (-0.41 episodes/day, 95% CI, -0.78 to -0.03; P = .03; I2 = 73%), based on conversion of diary data to a common daily unit. No significant effects were observed for involuntary urine loss (3.68 g, 95% CI, -13.01 to 20.38; P = .67; I2 = 97%) or quality of life (standardized mean difference = 0.28, 95% CI, -0.42 to 0.98; P = .43; I2 = 85%).
CONCLUSION: Intravaginal/transvaginal electrical stimulation appears to enhance PFM pressure and strength and reduces leakage episodes in the short term. However, its effects on objective urinary loss and quality of life remain inconclusive, and the evidence is of very low certainty. Cite this article as: Nazareth JVS, Silva JCd, Lopes EA, Carvalho ARd, Buzanello MR, Bertolini GRF. Evaluating intravaginal and transvaginal electrical stimulation techniques for urinary incontinence: a systematic review with meta-analysis. Eurasian J Med. 2026, 58(4), 1298, doi: 10.5152/eurasianjmed.2026.251298.

articles.title: Artificial intelligence-assisted microdissection testicular sperm extraction improves sperm retrieval efficiency and clinical outcomes in men with non-obstructive azoospermia: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.authors: Peng LF, Yu H
articles.abstract: This study compared the efficacy, safety, and intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI) outcomes of artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted versus conventional microdissection testicular sperm extraction (micro-TESE) in men with non-obstructive azoospermia (NOA). To this end, we retrospectively analyzed 1286 consecutive NOA patients undergoing micro-TESE at the two reproductive medicine center of Sichuan Provincial People's Hospital (Chengdu, China) and Sichuan Jinxin Xinan Women's and Children's Hospital (Chengdu, China) from January 2020 to December 2024, including 542 patients receiving AI-assisted procedures and 744 undergoing conventional surgery. The primary outcome was sperm retrieval rate (SRR), while secondary outcomes covered intraoperative parameters, postoperative complications, and ICSI outcomes, and univariable and multivariable logistic regression were performed to identify independent predictors of SRR and live birth. The results showed that the overall SRR reached 56.2% in the entire cohort, and the AI group had a significantly higher SRR (68.1% vs 47.6%, P < 0.001), with the most prominent improvement observed in patients with Sertoli cell-only syndrome (47.2% vs 22.7%, P < 0.001). The AI group also exhibited shorter operative time, less intraoperative blood loss, fewer biopsy sites, shorter postoperative hospital stay, and lower complication rates (all P < 0.001), as well as superior ICSI outcomes including higher fertilization, high-quality embryo, blastocyst, clinical pregnancy, ongoing pregnancy, and live birth rates (all P < 0.01). Further multivariable analysis confirmed that AI-assisted surgery serves as an independent predictor of both successful SRR (odds ratio [OR] = 3.182, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 2.374-4.265, P < 0.001) and live birth rate (OR = 1.876, 95% CI: 1.325-2.656, P < 0.001). Taken together, AI-assisted micro-TESE improves sperm retrieval efficiency, reduces perioperative morbidity, and enhances ICSI and live birth outcomes in NOA patients as an independent predictor for both SRR and live birth rate, and prospective multicenter randomized trials are warranted for further validation.

articles.title: Fetal Liver Volume and Morphology in Growth-Restricted Fetuses and Their Association With Neonatal Morbidity: An MRI Study.
articles.journal: Journal of magnetic resonance imaging : JMRI
articles.authors: Misochnik M, Olender A, Schonberger D et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Fetal growth restriction (FGR) may induce redistribution of the fetal circulation to preserve perfusion of vital organs. Reduced hepatic delivery of oxygen- and nutrient-rich blood may cause volumetric and morphological remodeling.
PURPOSE: To quantify fetal liver volume and morphology in FGR and assess associations with adverse neonatal outcomes.
STUDY TYPE: Single-center, prospective and retrospective.
POPULATION: Ninety-two singleton pregnancies: 36 FGR cases (prospective) and 56 appropriate-for-gestational-age (AGA) controls (retrospective).
FIELD STRENGTH/SEQUENCE: 3-T, True Fast Imaging with Steady-State Free Precession (TrueFISP) for fetal liver and body imaging, and TrueFISP or Half-Fourier Acquisition Single-shot Turbo Spin-Echo for brain imaging.
ASSESSMENT: The fetal liver, body, and brain were segmented using deep learning tools. Liver volume, liver-to-body and brain-to-liver volume ratios, and 12 liver PyRadiomics shape features were assessed. Neonates were followed for composite adverse neonatal outcomes (CANO) until discharge.
STATISTICAL TESTS: Linear regression assessed associations with gestational age in AGA fetuses. Linear mixed-effects models compared groups, adjusting for gestational age and fetal sex. Univariable logistic regression assessed associations with CANO. Benjamini-Hochberg correction controlled the false discovery rate at 0.05.
RESULTS: FGR fetuses had significantly lower liver volume than AGA fetuses (74.95 ± 1.76 vs. 114.89 ± 2.18 cm3), lower liver-to-body ratio (0.053 ± 0.001 vs. 0.057 ± 0.001), and higher brain-to-liver ratio (2.637 ± 0.085 vs. 1.978 ± 0.047). FGR fetuses demonstrated significantly less elongated liver geometry, (10.7% higher PyRadiomics elongation values) and had a significantly higher surface-to-volume ratio (11.9%). CANO occurred in 30/92 neonates (27 FGR, 3 AGA). Higher brain-to-liver ratio (OR = 4.12, 95% CI: 1.93-8.77), PyRadiomics elongation values (less elongated geometry; OR = 2.04, 95% CI: 1.26-3.30), PyRadiomics flatness values (less flattened geometry; OR = 1.69, 95% CI: 1.07-2.65), and surface-to-volume ratio (OR = 3.26, 95% CI: 1.80-5.90) were significantly associated with CANO.
DATA CONCLUSION: FGR was associated with reduced fetal liver size and altered geometry, which were associated with neonatal morbidity.
EVIDENCE LEVEL: 2.
TECHNICAL EFFICACY: 2.

articles.title: Personalized anticoagulation and drug monitoring for pregnancy-associated venous thromboembolism in hereditary type IIa antithrombin deficiency.
articles.journal: Blood coagulation & fibrinolysis : an international journal in haemostasis and thrombosis
articles.authors: Gong X, Wang W, Tian H et al.
articles.abstract: Pregnant women with hereditary type IIa antithrombin deficiency (ATD) are at significantly increased thrombotic risk. We present the case of a woman with four consecutive pregnancy losses due to venous thromboembolism (VTE), subsequently diagnosed with type IIa hereditary ATD. Type IIa ATD is exceptionally rare. The principal therapeutic challenge lies in the absence of established guidelines regarding optimal anticoagulant selection, dosing strategies, and monitoring approaches for such patients, contributing to treatment failure in her first four pregnancies. The patient was referred to our institution before her fifth conception. Preconception intervention began, and we instituted low-molecular-weight heparin (LMWH) therapy, with dose titration guided by thrombin-antithrombin complex (TAT) and anti-Xa activity levels. This regimen demonstrated safety and efficacy, achieving a maximum nadroparin dose of 10 250 IU twice daily. Under close pharmacotherapeutic monitoring by a clinical pharmacist using this individualized protocol, the patient achieved a successful term delivery and was discharged.

articles.title: Enlightening pregnancy as a potential pathway to protect maternal circadian functioning and postpartum mood.
articles.authors: Arrieta-Laurent A, Cabrera M, Silva A
articles.abstract: The perinatal period is characterized by profound psychological, physiological, and behavioral changes that may increase sleep, circadian, and affective disturbances. While sleep disruption across pregnancy and postpartum has been widely documented, far less is known about how this transition shapes circadian health and whether circadian characteristics during pregnancy predict postpartum circadian and affective outcomes. In this study, we characterize circadian preference, circadian phase, circadian function, and light exposure across the transition from late pregnancy to early postpartum, and examine their predictive value for postpartum circadian function and depressive and anxiety symptomatology. Women were followed from the third trimester of pregnancy to 1 month postpartum. At both time points, participants wore a wrist actigraph to derive circadian parameters including the circadian function index (CFI) and circadian phase (L5c), and to quantify mean light exposure. Circadian preference and affective states were also assessed by questionnaires (MEQ, EPDS, STAI-T). Within-subject changes from pregnancy to postpartum were examined, and regression models were used to test whether prenatal circadian and affective measures predicted postpartum circadian function and depressive symptomatology. The transition to postpartum was marked by a significant reduction in CFI and mean light exposure, whereas circadian preference and L5c remained largely stable. During pregnancy, higher CFI was associated with morningness and greater light exposure; however, these associations were no longer evident postpartum. Postpartum CFI was predicted by prenatal CFI and circadian preference, with lower values observed among women with more evening-oriented profiles. In parallel, prenatal affective symptoms showed continuity into the postpartum period, and both prenatal CFI and circadian preference contributed to the prediction of postpartum depressive symptoms. Together, these findings indicate that early postpartum is characterized by a decay in circadian function rather than a shift in circadian phase, identify eveningness as a vulnerability factor during the transition to motherhood, support the use of CFI as an integrative marker of maternal circadian health, and highlight pregnancy as a potential window for circadian-informed interventions aimed at improving postpartum circadian and mood outcomes.

articles.title: Circulating TGF-β1 Increases During Vaginal Progesterone Therapy in Women With a Short Cervix.
articles.authors: Laštůvka Z, Černý V, Škvorová A et al.
articles.abstract: Progesterone is an effective tool for the secondary prevention of spontaneous preterm birth. The aim of this prospective exploratory pilot study was to evaluate the effect of progesterone administration on the number of regulatory T cell (Treg) populations and on the concentrations of the immunoregulatory cytokines IL-10 and TGF-β1 during in vivo progesterone treatment in women at risk of preterm delivery. Pregnant women with a singleton pregnancy (22-30 weeks of gestation) who were at risk of spontaneous preterm delivery and required progesterone therapy were included (n = 21). Peripheral blood was sampled before progesterone administration and twice thereafter during treatment. Seventeen women attended the second visit, while only seven attended the third visit. The control group consisted of prospectively recruited low-risk women (n = 8). Treg numbers were determined by flow cytometry, and plasma concentrations of TGF-β1 and IL-10 were measured by ELISA. In women at risk, plasma TGF-β1 concentrations increased significantly between the first and second sampling (p ≤ 0.01) and remained at a similar level at the third sampling. In contrast, TGF-β1 levels in the control group remained low without statistically significant change. IL-10 concentrations were generally low in both groups. This pilot study was associated with an increase in the immunoregulatory cytokine TGF-β1 following progesterone administration. Although TGF-β1 is produced by several cell types in addition to Tregs, our findings raise the possibility that progesterone reinforces an immunoregulatory pathway relevant to the maintenance of pregnancy in women at risk of preterm birth; however, the present study does not establish this mechanism.

articles.title: Epicardial Fat Thickness in Fetal Growth Restriction: Impact on Neonatal Outcomes and Predictive Value.
articles.authors: Tonyalı NV, Sucu S, Örgül G et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Fetal growth restriction (FGR) is a condition associated with heightened risks of perinatal morbidity and mortality. Epicardial adipose tissue (EAT) has been identified as a potential marker for metabolic changes in fetuses, but its role in FGR remains underexplored. This study aimed to assess fetal epicardial fat thickness (EFT) in the third trimester and its correlation with FGR diagnosis and fetal measurements.
METHOD: A cross-sectional analytical study was conducted at a Perinatology Clinic involving 82 pregnant women, including 43 with FGR and 39 controls. FGR diagnosis was based on Delphi criteria. EFT measurements were performed using echocardiography techniques, and statistical analyses were conducted to assess correlations and predictive values. Fetal EFT was measured using ultrasound, and interobserver reliability was assessed using the Intraclass Correlation Coefficient (ICC).
RESULTS: In the FGR group, EFT was significantly lower than in controls (p < 0.001). A significant moderate positive correlation was observed between EFT and fetal abdominal circumference (r = 0.363, p = 0.017). ROC analysis identified an EFT cutoff value of ≤ 1.41 mm for discriminating FGR, with 60.5% sensitivity and 92.3% specificity (AUC = 0.802, p < 0.001). In addition, EFT showed significant discriminatory ability for composite adverse neonatal outcomes (AUC = 0.727, p = 0.001).
CONCLUSION: This study highlights the potential clinical significance of fetal EFT thickness in FGR diagnosis and neonatal outcome prediction. EFT measurements offer valuable insights into fetal metabolic status and may aid in early identification of high-risk pregnancies. Further research is warranted to validate these findings and integrate EFT assessments into routine prenatal care for improved perinatal management strategies.

articles.title: Navigating the Information Gap: Women's Experiences of Dichorionic Diamniotic (DCDA) Twin Pregnancy Care.
articles.authors: O'Connor C, Leitao S, O'Donoghue K
articles.abstract:
AIM: To explore women's lived experiences of dichorionic diamniotic twin pregnancies, including their information and support needs to inform future maternity care and service development.
DESIGN: An empirical qualitative study guided by Braun and Clarke's reflexive thematic analysis.
METHODS: Fifteen women who had experienced a dichorionic diamniotic twin pregnancy in Ireland within the previous 18 months participated in semi-structured interviews between 2022 and 2023. Interviews were analysed primarily inductively using Braun and Clarke's six-phase approach to reflective thematic analysis, using NVivo for data management.
RESULTS: Three themes were generated: Information Provided, Searching for Information and Postnatal Information. Participants described inconsistent risk discussions, limited twin-specific antenatal education and written resources and insufficient preparation for birth and the postnatal period. Many sought information independently, particularly online, which could increase uncertainty and anxiety. Women valued information and reassurance from healthcare professionals with twin-specific knowledge, particularly midwives. Postnatally, women described gaps in maternal support, breastfeeding guidance, practical preparation for caring for two infants, and preparation for neonatal unit admission.
CONCLUSION: Women with dichorionic diamniotic twin pregnancies experienced gaps in twin-specific information, education, and support across pregnancy and the postnatal period. More consistent provision of tailored information and preparation is needed across maternity services.
IMPLICATIONS FOR THE PROFESSION AND/OR PATIENT CARE: Midwives, particularly those with twin-specific expertise, have an important role in providing consistent information, education and support throughout twin pregnancy and the postnatal period.
IMPACT: The findings identify areas where twin-specific information, education, and support could be strengthened to improve women's preparedness and experiences of maternity care.
REPORTING METHOD: The Standards for Reporting Qualitative Research were followed.
NO PATIENT OR PUBLIC CONTRIBUTION: Women participated in the study as research participants; there was no patient or public involvement in the design, analysis or reporting of the study.

articles.title: A comprehensive assessment of cervical cancer risk factors, screening modalities, and cytological outcomes.
articles.journal: JPMA. The Journal of the Pakistan Medical Association
articles.authors: Nisar B, Naseem N
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To assess risk factors, awareness, screening practices and cytological outcomes related to cervical cancer.
METHODS: The cross-sectional study was conducted from January to October 2023 at a private school in Karachi after approval form the ethics review board of Jinnah Sindh Medical University, Karachi, and comprised children aged 6-12 years from grades 1-6. Data was collected from the parents of the enrolled children using a pilot-tested structured questionnaire. This was followed by oral examination of the children. Data was analysed using SPSS 20.
RESULTS: Among the 90 female subjects with 28.6 ± 7.4 years early childbirth 69(76.7%), multiparity 57(63.3%) and recurrent cervicovaginal infections 79(87.8%) were the most common factors. No subject was familiar with the human papillomavirus, and none had ever undergone a Papanicolaou test. Cytological analysis showed inflammation in 65(72.2%) cases, and atypical findings in 23(25.6%). Additional findings included infections, such as Escherichia coli 17(18.9%) and methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus 10(11.1%), with 29(32.2%) participants testing positive for Trichomonas vaginalis.
CONCLUSION: The level of awareness regarding cervical cancer and screening practices was alarmingly low, underscoring the need for structured cervical cancer screening and education programmes in Pakistan.

articles.title: Quality of life before & after genitourinary fistula repair - Insights from WHOQOL-BREF.
articles.journal: JPMA. The Journal of the Pakistan Medical Association
articles.authors: Shaikh I, Mahar NA, Piyarali S et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare preoperative and postoperative quality of life in women undergoing genitourinary fistula repair.
METHODS: The quasi-experimental study was conducted at the Department of Urology, Sindh Institute of Urology and Transplantation, Karachi, from January to December 2023, and comprised female patients diagnosed with vesicovaginal fistula secondary to gynaecological and obstetric procedures or trauma. The quality of life was assessed using the brief version of the World Health Organization Quality of Life scale. The participants completed the questionnaire both before the surgical intervention and three months after successful fistula repair. Data was analysed using SPSS 26.
RESULTS: There were 30 women with mean age 35.50±8.87 years. Mean quality of life score at baseline was 12.17±5.77 which improved significantly to 96.67±11.86 post-intervention (p=0.0001).
CONCLUSIONS: Genitourinary fistula repair significantly and positively impacted the patients' quality of life.

articles.title: Maternal Avocado Consumption and Pregnancy and Newborn Outcomes: Prospective Kuopio Birth Cohort.
articles.journal: The journal of obstetrics and gynaecology research
articles.authors: Cheng FW, Ford NA, Backman K et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Maternal fruit and vegetable intake during pregnancy has been associated with improved pregnancy and newborn outcomes. However, the role of individual foods-specifically avocados, which are rich in key micronutrients-has not been studied in relation to perinatal health. Thus, this study aimed to examine expectant mother avocado consumption and its association with pregnancy and newborn outcomes using the Kuopio Birth Cohort (KuBiCo)-a prospective cohort study.
METHODS: Maternal avocado intake was assessed using a validated food frequency questionnaire in the first and third trimesters. Avocado consumers were defined as participants who reported consuming any avocado (> 0 g) during pregnancy, and avocado non-consumers were defined as those who didn't report consuming any avocado (0 g). Pregnancy outcomes included preeclampsia, gestational hypertension, gestational diabetes, excessive bleeding during childbirth, and delivery by cesarean section. Early neonatal outcomes included being large or small for gestational age, low birth weight, macrosomia, preterm delivery, admission to neonatal intensive care, diagnosis of developmental disorder, and Apgar scores at 1 and 5 min. Logistic regression models were used to estimate associations between maternal avocado consumption and pregnancy and neonatal outcomes, adjusting for relevant covariates.
RESULTS: Pregnant individuals who consumed avocados (mean intake: 19.5 g/day) had 26.5% lower odds of undergoing a cesarean delivery compared to those who did not, even when adjusting for relevant covariates (e.g., overall diet quality). No statistically significant associations were observed for other pregnancy and newborn outcomes.
CONCLUSION: Avocado consumption during pregnancy was associated with lower odds of cesarean delivery, even when accounting for potential confounding covariates.

articles.title: Automated Insulin Delivery in Pregnancies Complicated by Type 1 Diabetes: A Real World Observational Study of Available Systems.
articles.journal: The Australian & New Zealand journal of obstetrics & gynaecology
articles.ta: Aust N Z J Obstet Gynaecol
articles.authors: Teasdale SL, Pavey J, Lee M et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Only one automated insulin delivery (AID) system is licensed in Australia for use in pregnancies complicated by Type 1 diabetes (T1D); however, some women using other AID systems have continued to use these 'off-label' in pregnancy. Usage patterns from a single centre in Australia will be of interest to clinicians supporting women with T1D in pregnancy.
AIMS: This is an observational study evaluating outcomes in women treated with different AID systems through a pregnancy cared for at a tertiary maternity centre.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: All women using AID in one or more trimesters of pregnancy through a 3-year study period are included in the reporting of glycaemic and insulin delivery measures in each trimester of pregnancy. All women using AID throughout the duration of a pregnancy within the study period are included in the reporting of birth outcomes.
RESULTS: Four AID systems had been used during the study period, MiniMed with Smartguard, T:slim with Control IQ, YpsoMed with CamAPS and Omnipod with SmartAdjust. Small numbers of YpsoMed and Omnipod users precluded these from statistical analysis. Women using MiniMed and T:slim AID systems differed in terms of early HbA1c and smoking history with MiniMed users representing suboptimal pre-pregnancy diabetes control. Use of continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) was additionally significantly lower for users of the MiniMed system. Median pregnancy-specific time in range (pTIR) was above 62% for all systems by trimester 2 and above 64% for all systems by trimester 3 with no significant difference between MiniMed and T:slim systems. There was less pregnancy-specific time below range (pTBR) and/or time well below range (pTWBR) for the MiniMed system in all trimesters compared with the T:slim system.
CONCLUSIONS: AID systems without the tight target considered necessary for pregnancy were still able to achieve good glycaemic outcomes.

articles.title: Global Practice Patterns in the Diagnosis and Management of Adolescent Varicocele: Results of an International Survey and Global Andrology Forum Experts' Recommendations.
articles.journal: The world journal of men's health
articles.authors: Hashimi MA, Mostafa T, Pescatori E et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate contemporary global practices in the diagnosis and management of adolescent varicocele among urologists and andrologists, identify areas of consensus and controversy, and develop expert recommendations using a modified Delphi process.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: A cross-sectional, international web-based survey was conducted between July and September 2025 following Checklist for Reporting Results of Internet E-Surveys (CHERRIES) guidelines. The 68-item questionnaire assessed clinician demographics, diagnostic evaluation, imaging, hormonal and semen testing, treatment indications, surgical preferences, and follow-up strategies. Distributed through the Global Andrology Forum (GAF) and collaborating societies, responses from 193 clinicians were analyzed using descriptive statistics and subgroup comparisons. Subsequently, 23 international experts participated in a modified Delphi process to formulate consensus-based expert recommendations.
RESULTS: A total of 193 clinicians completed the survey, primarily experienced physicians. Clinical examination in the standing position with the Valsalva maneuver was used either alone (96.37%) or in combination with scrotal Doppler ultrasonography (91.71%). Hormonal assessment remained controversial, with 51.81% considering it clinically useful. Conservative management (46.11%) and surgical intervention (44.04%) were nearly equally favored. Testicular volume discrepancy was the strongest determinant for intervention, with a discrepancy >20% being the most widely accepted surgical threshold (61.66%). Microsurgical subinguinal varicocelectomy was the preferred operative technique (79.27%), with routine lymphatic preservation reported by 90.16% of respondents. Considerable variability was observed regarding semen analysis, hormonal testing, imaging utilization, and follow-up protocols.
CONCLUSIONS: Management of adolescent varicocele demonstrates substantial international heterogeneity, particularly regarding hormonal evaluation, semen analysis, imaging, and surveillance strategies. However, broad agreement exists regarding the central role of clinical examination, the importance of testicular volume discrepancy in clinical decision-making, and the preference for microsurgical repair. Although the survey included respondents from multiple countries, the uneven geographic distribution with a predominance of Asian participants limits worldwide generalizability. The accompanying Delphibased recommendations aim…

articles.title: Sperm Retrieval Outcomes in Men with Y Chromosome AZFc Microdeletion Undergoing Testicular Sperm Extraction: Real-World Data from a Large Multicenter Cohort.
articles.journal: The world journal of men's health
articles.authors: Boeri L, Graziani A, Manfredi C et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To assess the real-life sperm retrieval (SR) outcome in men with non-obstructive azoospermia (NOA) and Y-chromosome AZFc microdeletions.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Data from 126 men with NOA and AZFc microdeletions who underwent SR procedures in 13 centers between January 2019 and September 2025 were analyzed. All men underwent a comprehensive diagnostic work-up including medical history, physical examination, testicular ultrasound, hormonal and genetic blood testing and semen analysis according to World Health Organization reference criteria. Testicular histology was documented. Either classic testicular sperm extraction or microsurgical TESE (mTESE) were performed. Descriptive statistics and logistic regression analyses were conducted to identify predictors of +SR.
RESULTS: Overall, median (interquartile range) age at surgery and median testicular volume were 35 (31-40) years and 8 (6-12) mL, respectively. Median baseline serum follicle stimulating hormone (FSH) and total testosterone were 16.6 (9.1-23.8) IU/L and 4.1 (3.2-5.6) ng/mL, respectively. mTESE was performed in 87 (69.1%) cases. SR was achieved in 30 patients (23.8%). Histological evaluation revealed Sertoli cell-only syndrome (SCOS) in 50 (61.0%), maturation arrest (MA) in 20 (24.4%), and hypospermatogenesis (HS) in 12 (14.6%) men, with a median Johnsen score of 4 (2-8). Median FSH was significantly lower in men with +SR (11.3 vs. 21.2 IU/L, p=0.02), while Johnsen score was significantly higher (7 vs. 2, p<0.001). +SR was inversely associated with severity of testicular histology (58.3% for HS, 15.0% for MA and 14.0% for SCOS, respectively; p<0.001). Multivariate logistic regression analysis showed that SCOS (0.1, p=0.01) and MA (0.1, p=0.02) histologies were associated with lower likelihood of +SR, after accounting for FSH values.
CONCLUSIONS: SR rate in this cohort was 23.8%, with testicular histology being the strongest independent predictor of success. These findings support evidence-based counseling, individualized prognostication, and informed surgical planning in this population.

articles.title: GAF Survey on the Management of Hypogonadism in Men with Concomitant Varicocele: Gaps between Real-World Practice and Current Guidelines.
articles.journal: The world journal of men's health
articles.authors: Russo GI, Pescatori E, Shah R et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Emerging evidence suggests that varicocele may impair Leydig cell function and contribute to hypogonadism. This global survey assessed real-world clinical attitudes, diagnostic practices, and management strategies, and discrepancies between clinical practice and current guidelines.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: An anonymous, cross-sectional, web-based survey was conducted under the Global Andrology Forum. Practicing urologists, andrologists, and reproductive clinicians worldwide were invited to participate. The questionnaire evaluated perceptions of the association between varicocele and hypogonadism, screening and hormonal assessment practices, indications for varicocele repair, and clinician-reported endocrine and symptomatic outcomes.
RESULTS: A total of 210 clinicians from 46 countries were included. Most respondents were experienced urologists and andrologists, and 73.8% reported at least a moderate association between varicocele and hypogonadism. Routine screening for varicocele in hypogonadal men was reported by 49.5%, while 37.6% measured testosterone levels in men with varicocele. Varicocele repair was offered to improve testosterone levels by 83.3% of respondents, primarily in fertility-motivated patients or selected hypogonadal men. The modal clinician's estimate of testosterone normalization following repair was the 25% to 49% category (reported by 23.3% of respondents, with improvements typically observed within 3 to 6 months). Among active respondents only, the modal estimate of testosterone normalization (25% to 49% of patients) was reported by 46.7% (49/105 respondents). Factors such as obesity, smoking, sedentary lifestyle, and environmental exposures were perceived to negatively impact hormonal outcomes.
CONCLUSIONS: Although limited by voluntary participation, an approximately 10% response rate, and recruitment predominantly from andrology-focused networks, the findings reveal substantial variation between guideline recommendations and reported real-world practice. Among responding clinicians, many consider varicocele a potentially modifiable factor in hypogonadal men and incorporate hormonal evaluation and repair into management. The findings underscore the need for adequately powered prospective studies to clarify patient selection, endocrine outcomes, and the role of varicocele in hypogonadism.

articles.title: Associations of Sexual Quality of Life and Marital Adjustment With Psychological Resilience in Women With Gynecological Cancer.
articles.journal: The journal of obstetrics and gynaecology research
articles.authors: Ünal E, Dönmez ÇÇ, Khatib G
articles.abstract:
AIM: This study examined the associations of sexual quality of life and marital adjustment with psychological resilience among women with gynecological cancer.
METHODS: This single-center, descriptive, cross-sectional, and correlational study was conducted with 102 married women followed in a gynecologic oncology outpatient clinic in Türkiye. Data were collected using a Personal Information Form, the Sexual Quality of Life-Female Scale, the Marital Adjustment Scale, and the Brief Resilience Scale. Clinical characteristics and treatment-related information were based on participants' self-reports. Descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation analysis, and hierarchical multiple regression analysis were used to analyze the data.
RESULTS: Sexual quality of life and marital adjustment were positively and significantly correlated with psychological resilience. The sociodemographic variables entered in Model 1 did not explain a statistically significant proportion of the variance in psychological resilience (R2 = 0.020, p = 0.377), and the addition of clinical variables in Model 2 did not significantly increase the explained variance (ΔR2 = 0.038, p = 0.147). Sexual quality of life significantly increased the explained variance by 20.6% (ΔR2 = 0.206, p < 0.001), and marital adjustment contributed an additional 6.5% (ΔR2 = 0.065, p = 0.003). The final model explained 32.9% of the variance in psychological resilience (adjusted R2 = 0.287). In the final model, income level (β = 0.211, p = 0.017), sexual quality of life (β = 0.387, p < 0.001), and marital adjustment (β = 0.276, p = 0.003) were significantly and positively associated with psychological resilience.
CONCLUSIONS: Psychological resilience in women with gynecological cancer was associated not only with socioeconomic resources but also with sexual and relational well-being. These findings suggest that sexual and relational concerns may represent relevant dimensions of psychosocial well-being in gynecologic oncology care; however, prospective and intervention studies are needed to clarify their implications for supportive care.

articles.title: Monoclonal Antibody Dispensing Around Pregnancy: A Descriptive Analysis Using Electronic Health Records in Italy.
articles.authors: Aiton E, Nazzari V, Cornish R et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To describe trends in dispensing of monoclonal antibody biologics (mAbs) for autoimmune conditions during and around pregnancy.
METHODS: We conducted a population-wide study of women of reproductive age (14-49 years) resident in Lombardy, Italy, between 2012 and 2024. We described trends over time in the prevalence of mAb dispensations among women of reproductive age, and during pregnancy. For each pregnancy, we assessed the prevalence of mAb dispensations before, during, and after pregnancy in trimesters. We described dispensing patterns and explored maternal factors associated with discontinuation.
RESULTS: We included 1 871 929 women of reproductive age and 855 865 pregnancies. Prevalence of mAb dispensing during pregnancy increased over 60-fold over the study period, from 0.0041% in 2012 to 0.27% in 2024. Pregnancy affected mAb dispensing, with prevalence decreasing from 0.081% before pregnancy to 0.051% by the third trimester. Over half (n = 385/722, 53.3%) of pre-existing mAb users discontinued before or during pregnancy, while switching between mAbs during pregnancy was rare (n = 24/722, 3.3%). Discontinuation decreased over time, and varied substantially between mAbs. We found limited evidence that sociodemographic factors were associated with discontinuation, but that some health factors may be, such as use of assisted reproductive technology (OR = 1.92, 95% CI: 0.98-3.77).
CONCLUSIONS: Italian population-wide data from 2012 to 2024 show an increase in mAbs dispensed during pregnancy, and fewer instances of discontinuing these drugs over time. These trends may reflect increasing drug availability, accumulating safety evidence, and recent changes in guidelines for mAb use in pregnancy.

articles.title: Lifetime Hormonal Exposure and Risk of Lung Cancer in Women: Results From a French Population-Based Case-Control Study (The WELCA Study).
articles.authors: Gueye Y, Duverger EC, Guénel P et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: With 2 million new cases annually, lung cancer is among the most frequent and the leading cause of cancer-related death worldwide. Incidence trends differ by gender, decreasing in men but increasing in women, partly due to later tobacco uptake. However, biological differences may also contribute, including the potential role of estrogen exposure. This study aimed to investigate the influence of lifetime hormonal exposure on lung cancer risk in women.
METHODS: WELCA is a multicenter population-based case-control study conducted in Ile-de-France between 2014 and 2017 among women aged 18-75 years. The study included 716 cases of incident primary lung cancer and 756 controls frequency-matched by age and area of residence. Information was collected through standardized questionnaires on lifestyle factors, occupational history, reproductive history, and use of exogenous hormones. Odds-ratios (OR) and confidence intervals (CI) were estimated using multivariable logistic regression models.
RESULTS: A later age at last pregnancy (≥ 33 vs. ≤ 28 years) and ever use of hormonal contraceptives was associated with a lower risk of lung cancer (OR = 0.60; 0.42-0.85 and OR = 0.57; 0.39-0.84, respectively). However, a later age at cessation of the pill use was associated with an increased risk (≥ 39 vs. ≤ 30 years: OR = 1.46; 1.06-2.03). Finally, a longer reproductive lifespan was inversely associated with lung cancer (≥ 39 vs. ≤ 36 years: OR = 0.69; 0.50-0.95).
CONCLUSION: These findings suggest lifetime hormonal exposure may influence lung cancer risk in women. They support the hypothesis of a hormonally mediated pathway and highlight the need for further studies on sex-specific lung cancer risk.

articles.title: Revealing the Action Mechanism of WISP2 in Miscarriage Based Multi-Omic Analysis and Experimental Validation.
articles.authors: Leng Z, Yan B, Wang F et al.
articles.abstract: Recurrent miscarriage (RM) is a major unresolved issue in reproductive medicine. Although WISP2 is known to participate in multiple cellular processes, its function in trophoblast biology and pregnancy maintenance remains unknown. We performed single-cell RNA sequencing on chorionic villus tissues from RM patients and normal controls to identify cell-type-specific transcriptional alterations, which led to the identification of WISP2 as a candidate gene in the SCT/EVT subpopulation. Fetal membrane samples (chorion) were obtained from Qingdao Women and Children's Hospital's Surgical Outpatient Department: 20 RM patients and 20 healthy controls. Using qRT-PCR, Western blot, and immunohistochemistry to detect gene and protein expression. HTR-8 cells were used to construct WISP2 overexpressing cells, and MTT, wound healing and Transwell experiments were performed for functional experiments. Eleven cell classes in the sample were demonstrated by single-cell analysis. Among these cells were DSCs and SCT/extravillous trophoblasts (EVT). The level of WISP2 is low in SCT/EVT cells from RM patients. In chorionic villus tissues, both WISP2 and E-cadherin were significantly upregulated in the RM group relative to the control group (all p < 0.05). Immunohistochemistry confirmed elevated WISP2 and E-cadherin protein levels in RM chorionic villi (both p < 0.05), with predominant cytoplasmic and membranous localization, respectively. In HTR-8 cells, WISP2 overexpression suppressed proliferation (35%, p < 0.01), migration (45%, p < 0.01), and invasion (50%, p < 0.001), upregulated E-cadherin (p < 0.05), downregulated Vimentin (p < 0.05), and increased p-ERK (p < 0.05) without altering total ERK1/2 (p > 0.05), suggesting that WISP2 promotes an epithelial-like phenotype accompanied by ERK pathway activation. In summary, WISP2 is dysregulated in RM and suppresses trophoblast invasion and EMT in vitro, suggesting a potential role in RM pathogenesis, though in vivo validation is required.

articles.title: Classification of brain variants on fetal ultrasound: international Delphi consensus.
articles.journal: Ultrasound in obstetrics & gynecology : the official journal of the International Society of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology
articles.authors: Lesieur E, Sheikh J, Desnous B et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To develop an expert consensus classification and management framework for fetal-brain variants identified on prenatal ultrasound across all trimesters of pregnancy that cannot be categorized confidently as either benign or pathological.
METHODS: A two-round international Delphi survey was conducted among experts in fetal medicine and neurosonography, with survey data collected between September 2025 and March 2026. Forty-eight fetal-brain variants, identified through a scoping literature review of PubMed/MEDLINE from database inception to August 2025, performed between June and August 2025, and illustrated with representative ultrasound images, were evaluated. Brain variants were classified according to clinical significance and recommended management into three predefined categories: 'green' (benign variants requiring no additional investigation or follow-up), 'orange' (requiring neurosonographic follow-up) and 'red' (requiring dedicated neurosonography, fetal-brain magnetic resonance imaging and/or genetic investigations). Consensus was predefined as ≥ 70% agreement. In Round 2, experts confirmed their agreement regarding categorization of variants that had reached consensus in Round 1 and reassessed variants that did not reach initial consensus.
RESULTS: Forty-eight experts from 14 countries participated in Round 1 and 39 (81.3%) completed both rounds. Of the 48 evaluated variants, 35 (72.9%) reached consensus after two rounds: 12 were classified as 'green', seven as 'orange' and 16 as 'red'. Green variants included isolated choroid plexus cysts < 10 mm across all trimesters, regular asymmetry of the choroid plexuses, isolated cavum septations, cavum vergae, cavum velum interpositum, isolated small cavum septi pellucidi with intact corpus callosum and dolichocephaly with normal head circumference and normal brain morphology. Orange variants included isolated enlargement of intracranial translucency with preserved anatomy, large or bilateral choroid plexus cysts, isolated enlargement of subarachnoid spaces without compression and isolated cyst of the cavum septi pellucidi. Red variants included abnormal posterior fossa markers (loss of normal three-space anatomy, increased brainstem-vermis angle, reduced brainstem-occipital bone distance), periventricular cysts associated with adjacent white-matter abnormalities, thickened corpus callosum and distortion of the interhemispheric fissure, among other findings. Thirteen (27.1%) variants failed…

articles.title: CT-Derived Body Composition Enhances Risk Prediction for Early Progression and Platinum Resistance in High-Grade Serous Ovarian Cancer.
articles.authors: Singh J, Meng X, Kokenberger G et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with high-grade serous ovarian cancer (HGSOC) who develop resistance to platinum-based chemotherapy experience significantly poorer outcomes and shorter progression-free survival (PFS). This study evaluates whether pretreatment CT-based abdominal body composition is associated with platinum resistance and PFS, and whether its incorporation alongside clinical variables improves prognostic model performance.
METHODS: This retrospective study included 321 patients with HGSOC (mean age 65 ± 10 years; 28.0% platinum-resistant) treated with platinum-based chemotherapy between 2011 and 2023. Deep learning algorithms quantified abdominal body composition features from pretreatment CT scans, including skeletal muscle, bone, subcutaneous (SAT), visceral (VAT), and intramuscular (IMAT) adipose tissues. Platinum resistance, defined as disease progression during therapy or within 6 months of the final infusion, was the primary outcome. PFS was analyzed as a secondary outcome using Cox proportional hazards modeling. Analyses were stratified by chemotherapy sequence (neoadjuvant vs. adjuvant). Survival models incorporating clinical and CT-derived features were evaluated using 10-fold cross-validated time-dependent AUC over a 5-year follow-up window to predict PFS. External validation was partially performed in an independent cohort of 58 patients with HGSOC.
RESULTS: Increased SAT and IMAT and decreased skeletal muscle density were independently associated with platinum resistance, with high SAT remaining significant in both the internal and external cohorts (p < 0.05). High adiposity and low muscle density were similarly associated with shorter PFS. Survival models combining clinical and CT-derived features consistently outperformed clinical-only models across all evaluated model classes. The Elastic Net Cox regression model incorporating both feature sets achieved the highest AUC of 0.704 (95% CI: 0.660-0.748).
CONCLUSIONS: Pretreatment CT-derived abdominal body composition is independently associated with platinum resistance and PFS in HGSOC, and its incorporation into predictive clinical models improves discrimination. Body composition assessment may help identify patients at increased risk of platinum resistance and early disease progression.

articles.title: Reconnecting with the body in menopause: A holistic health experience through Pilates as a leisure activity among Turkish women.
articles.authors: Yalçın C, Yaşar Sönmez B, Ekinci E
articles.abstract: Menopause constitutes a multifaceted transitional phase characterized by biological, psychological, and social changes that shape women's health experiences. Nevertheless, the prevailing literature predominantly frames menopause within a biomedical paradigm and has paid insufficient attention to how women construct their health experiences within leisure contexts. This study explores how Turkish women navigating menopause interpret Pilates as a leisure activity and its contribution to their holistic health. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with 10 women aged 45-60 years who regularly practiced Pilates. Data were analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis informed by the Biopsychosocial Model. The analysis yielded three principal themes: reconnecting with the body, achieving mental and emotional wholeness, and women's solidarity and social integration. Participants described Pilates as supporting adaptation to bodily changes, supporting emotional balance, and challenging taboos by fostering social connections. These results indicate that participants perceived mind-body leisure activities such as Pilates as providing a holistic context that supports multiple dimensions of health. The study highlights the importance of experiential and social leisure practices in interventions aimed at advancing women's health.

articles.title: Laryngeal Cancer Microbiome Study Reveals Parvimonas and Campylobacter as Potential Therapy Targets.
articles.authors: Lad H, Shah A, Thompson ER et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Laryngeal cancer accounts for 40% of head and neck malignancies and 1% of all cancer-related deaths worldwide. We evaluated the laryngeal cancer microbiome to identify cancer-specific genera as potential treatment targets.
METHODS: A prospective study was conducted using 57 laryngeal mucosal samples from 24 treatment-naive laryngeal cancer patients and 33 patients who were undergoing otolaryngological surgery unrelated to oral or laryngeal diseases (01/2023-09/2025). DNA was extracted and amplified in triplicate, targeting the V3/V4 region of the 16S rRNA gene, followed by paired-end 2 × 300 bp sequencing on the Illumina NextSeq 2000. Amplicon sequence variants were identified via DADA2 and assigned to genera using a naive Bayes classifier. Two samples with zero classified read pairs were excluded.
RESULTS: Most patients were male (87.5% cancer, 66.7% controls) and smokers (83.3% cancer, 54.5% controls). Cancer patients' core laryngeal microbiomes uniquely contained Parvimonas (3.67%; 95% CI: 0.70%-6.64%), and Campylobacter (1.12%; 95% CI: 0.60%-1.63%), while control patients' uniquely contained Corynebacterium (2.97%; 95% CI: 0.00%-7.67%) and Alloprevotella (1.34%; 95% CI: 0.64%-2.04%). Cancer samples were significantly enriched in 19 genera, notably Peptococcus (2.93, q = 0.0003), Campylobacter (1.68, q = 0.009), and Parvimonas (2.02, q = 0.03), compared to controls.
CONCLUSIONS: Laryngeal cancer patients' samples displayed microbial dysbiosis, with enrichment of microbes present in gastrointestinal cancers, cervical cancer, and inflammatory states; they also exhibited loss of immunoprotective taxa. These findings support that microbiome profiling can distinguish malignant mucosa and guide future studies targeting genera increased in cancer, including Parvimonas and Campylobacter.

articles.title: Determinants of comprehensive knowledge of mother-to-child transmission of HIV among currently married women in Somalia: analysis of the 2020 Somali Demographic and Health Survey.
articles.authors: Mohamud LA, Hersi AH, Yusuf OA et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: A significant proportion of HIV infections in infants results from vertical transmission, largely due to inadequate maternal knowledge of mother-to-child transmission (MTCT) and its prevention. Although several global studies have assessed women's MTCT knowledge, nationally representative evidence from Somalia remains limited. This study addresses this gap by examining factors associated with comprehensive knowledge of MTCT of HIV among currently married women aged 15-49 years in Somalia.
METHODS: Multivariable logistic regression was used to examine the association between comprehensive MTCT knowledge of HIV and sociodemographic factors using data from the 2018-2019 SDHS.
RESULTS: Overall, 66.67% of currently married women had good knowledge of MTCT of HIV. Women residing in Cluster 7 (Gedo and Lower Juba) (AOR = 0.39, 95% CI 0.31-0.50) and Cluster 6 (Bay and Bakool) (AOR = 0.53, 95% CI 0.39-0.71), those who never listened to the radio (AOR = 0.71, 95% CI 0.57-0.88), and women in the richest wealth category (AOR = 0.72, 95% CI 0.59-0.87) were significantly less likely to have comprehensive MTCT knowledge.
CONCLUSION: Policy interventions should focus on strengthening MTCT of HIV awareness through targeted education for younger women, those with limited media exposure, and women in Cluster 6 and Cluster 7.
