Expanding community-based and antenatal care-based HIV education is essential. Efforts should also reduce socioeconomic and regional disparities by improving access to HIV information among low-income and underserved populations to ensure equitable knowledge distribution.

articles.title: Association between internet use and modern contraceptive uptake among women of reproductive age in Rwanda: evidence from the 2019-2020 Rwanda DHS.
articles.authors: Ndayishimye S, Olorunfemi G, Nahayo B et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Modern contraceptives are pertinent to the reduction of unintended pregnancies, unsafe abortion, and maternal mortality. Unfortunately, the prevalence rate of modern contraceptive use is low in most Sub-Saharan African (SSA) countries including Rwanda. The use of internet promotes access to information on the need for childbearing postponement, prevention of unintended pregnancy, child spacing, and limiting family size. However, there is dearth of knowledge on the link between internet use and modern contraceptive use among Rwandan women. This study was therefore designed to fill the gap by assessing the relationship between exposure to the internet and uptake of modern contraceptives in Rwanda.
METHODOLOGY: This cross-sectional design study was a secondary data analysis of the Rwanda Demographic and Health Survey. Sexually active women aged 15-49 years (n = 7290) were included in the study. The outcome variable and key independent variable was modern contraceptive use and internet use respectively. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, Chi-square test, and logistic regression model (α0.05).
RESULTS: Modern contraceptive prevalence rate was 58.8%, and 10.9% of the women were using internet services. Adjusting for other factors revealed that women who used internet had about 16% (AOR: 1.16, 95% CI: 0.93-1.45) increased odds of modern contraceptive use compared to women who did not. Other predictors of modern contraceptive use included age, marital status, educational level, religion, occupation, and the number of living children.
CONCLUSION: Internet usage increased the utilization of modern contraceptive among Rwandan women of reproductive age. Thus, strategies to improve the use of modern contraceptive among Rwanda women of reproductive age should include providing appropriate easily accessible internet information about modern contraceptives. Government investment in appropriate social marketing of modern contraceptive through internet services is strongly recommended.

articles.title: Inequalities in modern contraceptive use among men: a HEAT Plus analysis of population-based cross-sectional surveys in East Africa.
articles.authors: Kayemba V, Kabagenyi A, Najjuma S et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Male involvement is essential for effective family planning, yet men in most of sub-Saharan Africa remain less engaged than women. Their participation is shaped by the socioeconomic context, but evidence on how modern contraceptive use varies across socioeconomic groups among men is limited. This study therefore examined socioeconomic inequalities in modern contraceptive use among men in East Africa.
METHODS: This study analyzed weighted, nationally representative Demographic and Health Survey data from two survey rounds per country for sexually active men aged 15-54 years in Burundi (2010 and 2016), Kenya (2014 and 2022), Rwanda (2014 and 2019), Tanzania (2010 and 2022), and Uganda (2011 and 2016). Inequalities in modern contraceptive use were assessed using HEAT Plus, applying simple (Difference) and complex (Population Attributable Fraction) measures.
RESULTS: Modern contraceptive use among men varied across the five countries. Burundi recorded a modest increase between 2010 and 2016, Rwanda and Uganda showed a consistent increase, while Tanzania and Kenya experienced declines between 2014 and 2022. Across the five countries, education, place of residence, wealth index, and decision making on how to spend earnings emerged as the most salient dimensions of inequality in modern contraceptive use among men. Education-related inequalities were particularly pronounced, with PAF estimates indicating that national levels of modern contraceptive use could have been higher by up to about 34.6% in Burundi in 2016, 20.8% in Uganda in 2016, 15.3% in Tanzania in 2022, 8.5% in Kenya in 2022, and 5.6% in Rwanda in 2019 had educational disparities been eliminated.
CONCLUSION: Family planning strategies should prioritize men as direct users of contraception by targeting educational, economic, and access related inequalities, with tailored approaches for men with lower education, those in rural, and poorer settings.

articles.title: Emergency obstetric referrals in public primary health care centres in Benin City, Nigeria: a qualitative study.
articles.authors: Odjesa E, Imongan W, Ntoimo LF et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The aim of this study was to assess the mechanisms, procedures, and processes of the referral system for emergency obstetric care (EmOC) in public primary health care centres (PHCs) in Benin City, Edo State, Nigeria, with recommendations offered to address the challenges.
METHODS: A qualitative study was conducted in Egor Local Government Area (LGA), purposively selected from the three LGAs in Benin City. From the 11 public PHCs in Egor LGA, nine were selected based on their provision of maternal care and performance of EmOC in the three months preceding this study. Nine key informant interviews were conducted using a semi-structured interview guide, with one nurse or midwife, serving as a senior health care provider or health facility manager, selected as the participant per PHC. Data saturation was achieved with this sample. The interviews were audio-recorded, transcribed verbatim, and analysed thematically using NVivo V.12.0 software.
RESULTS: From the responses of all the participants, three themes emerged following data analysis: (1) mechanisms, procedures, and processes for the referral of obstetric emergencies. From many of the participants' responses, the associated categories were availability of emergency transport vehicles; process for receiving feedback and follow-up, among others; (2) Challenges encountered with the referral system. From many of the participants' responses, the associated categories were infrastructural deficits such as nonavailability of ambulances. For some participants, other challenges mentioned were presence of bad roads leading to the PHCs; logistics constraints such as shortage of staff and stock-out of referral letters; and patient-related challenges such as financial constraints, and preference for traditional care; and (3) recommendations for improving the referral systems. From many of the participants' responses, the associated categories were strengthening the infrastructure through addressing logistics and resource challenges.
CONCLUSIONS: Public PHCs in Egor LGA have existing procedures for referring obstetric emergencies. However, challenges exist in terms of nonavailability of written referral protocols and emergency transportation, poor two-way communication, inadequate staffing and logistics, thereby limiting its effectiveness. Strengthening these health system components could improve the quality of referrals and contribute to reducing preventable maternal mortality in Edo State, with…

articles.title: Can artificial intelligence counsel expectant mothers? Expert evaluation of ChatGPT's educational performance in gestational diabetes mellitus.
articles.authors: Balcı MF, Akdemi̇r C, Yildirim F
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) is an increasingly common pregnancy complication associated with adverse maternal-fetal outcomes and long-term risk of type 2 diabetes. Artificial intelligence (AI) tools such as ChatGPT have emerged as potential instruments for patient education, yet their reliability and safety in obstetric counseling remain underexplored. This study aimed to evaluate the educational quality of ChatGPT-5 responses to frequently asked questions about GDM.
METHODS: This cross-sectional study was conducted between January and June 2025 at Torbalı State Hospital, İzmir, Türkiye, following STROBE guidelines. Twenty frequently asked questions about gestational diabetes mellitus, identified from routine antenatal counseling through clinician observation and consensus, were entered into ChatGPT-5 using a standardized prompt. Thirty physicians specializing in obstetrics and gynecology from Türkiye, the United Kingdom, Canada, and Germany independently rated the AI-generated answers on a 5-point Likert scale across five domains: accuracy, comprehensiveness, clarity, safety, and appropriateness. Reliability was analyzed using Cronbach's α and intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC). Comparative analyses were performed using Friedman and Dunn-Bonferroni tests.
RESULTS: Overall, ChatGPT-5 achieved high ratings for accuracy (4.23 ± 0.32), clarity (4.18 ± 0.27), and appropriateness (4.09 ± 0.31), while comprehensiveness (3.92 ± 0.29) and safety (3.88 ± 0.34) scored lower. Internal consistency was strong (Cronbach's α = 0.87) and interrater reliability was good (ICC = 0.79). Among thematic domains, "Definition, causes, and risk factors" received the highest scores (4.20 ± 0.30), whereas "Follow-up and treatment" scored the lowest (3.96 ± 0.33). Safety ratings were significantly lower than accuracy and clarity (p = 0.018).
CONCLUSION: ChatGPT-5 demonstrated high accuracy and clarity in GDM counseling, suggesting its potential use as a physician-supervised educational support tool. However, limitations in comprehensiveness and safety highlight the need for guideline-based refinement and human oversight to ensure ethical and reliable integration of AI in obstetric patient education.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Not applicable. This study is an observational cross-sectional design and did not involve patient enrollment or intervention.

articles.title: Innovative abdominoperineal surgery for fertility-preserving cervicovaginal reconstruction in five patients with the rare condition of congenital cervical malformation coexisting with vaginal atresia.
articles.authors: Tang J, Liu J, Li B et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Congenital cervical malformation coexisting with vaginal atresia is a rare but challenging anomaly that obstructs menstrual outflow and threatens future fertility. This study aimed to describe a fertility-preserving laparoscopic abdominoperineal cervicovaginal reconstruction technique and present preliminary clinical outcomes from a small case series.
METHODS: In this retrospective case series, between September 2019 and June 2024, five patients diagnosed with congenital cervical malformation coexisting with vaginal atresia through clinical evaluation and imaging were treated at Renmin Hospital of Wuhan University. All patients subsequently underwent fertility-preserving laparoscopic abdominoperineal cervicovaginal reconstruction. Key surgical steps included anatomical preservation of the ascending branches of the uterine artery to help preserve uterine blood supply, resection of the atretic cervical segment with conservation of viable cervical tissue containing mucosa whenever feasible, mobilization of pelvic peritoneum to cover the lower uterine segment and neocervix, and placement of a self-assembled modified T-shaped utero-vaginal device to sustain neocervical canal patency. Postoperative and functional outcomes were assessed by clinical follow-up, ultrasonography, and hysteroscopic evaluation.
RESULTS: All five patients successfully underwent laparoscopic-vaginal reconstruction without intraoperative complications or conversion to laparotomy. The mean patient age was 14.2 ± 1.72 years (range, 12-17). No intraoperative complications occurred. Normal menstrual flow resumed in all cases within one month after surgery. During a mean follow-up of 23.6 ± 9.0 months, no restenosis, hematometra, infection, or recurrent obstruction occurred. Ultrasonography consistently demonstrated stable uterovaginal continuity, normal uterine morphology, and adequate neovaginal length throughout the follow-up period.
CONCLUSION: This small case series suggests that laparoscopic abdominoperineal cervicovaginal reconstruction may be a feasible fertility-preserving option for selected patients with congenital cervical malformation coexisting with vaginal atresia. The procedure restored menstrual outflow and achieved stable early uterovaginal patency, but further studies with larger cohorts and longer follow-up are required to validate its safety, reproducibility, and fertility-related value.

articles.title: Multidimensional barriers to women's access to maternal health services in Herat Province, Afghanistan: a cross-sectional study.
articles.authors: Hassam AF, Yosufi SA, Azizi Z et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Maternal health remains a critical public health priority in Afghanistan, which has one of the highest maternal mortality ratios. Women's access to maternal health services is influenced by multiple interacting dimensions; however, comprehensive evidence on the relative contribution of structural, sociocultural, and informational barriers in provincial contexts remains limited. This study aimed to examine the multidimensional barriers to women's access to health services in Herat Province, Afghanistan.
METHODS: A cross-sectional study was conducted between September 2025 and January 2026 among 365 reproductive-age women in Herat province. A multi-stage stratified cluster sampling method was employed, with participants selected from public health facilities using systematic random sampling. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire assessing sociodemographic characteristics, structural and sociocultural barriers, maternal health awareness, and service quality. Reliability was confirmed using Cronbach's alpha (0.704-0.811). An exploratory factor analysis was conducted to identify the underlying structure of the barriers. The Kaiser-Meyer-Olkin (KMO) measure was 0.680, indicating borderline but acceptable sampling adequacy for factor analysis. Nonparametric tests (Mann-Whitney U and Kruskal-Wallis tests), Spearman's correlation, and nominal logistic regression were used for data analysis.
RESULTS: The mean age of the participants was 30.36 ± 9.87 years. The majority were illiterate (76.7%), resided in rural areas (67.7%), and had monthly incomes below 7,000 Afghanis (90.7%). Exploratory factor analysis revealed four dimensions: structural access barriers, sociocultural barriers, maternal care and awareness, and service quality. Sociocultural barriers had the greatest impact on access (mean = 3.15), followed by structural barriers (mean = 2.83). A moderate positive correlation was observed between structural and sociocultural barriers (ρ = 0.298, p < 0.01), whereas sociocultural barriers were negatively correlated with awareness (ρ = -0.301, p < 0.01). Lower education was the strongest predictor of barriers, with illiterate women having significantly higher odds of access limitations (Exp(B) = 21.535), distance barriers (Exp(B) = 23.155), need for permission (Exp(B) = 9.541), and shame/Haya (Exp(B) = 6.131). Rural residence was associated with higher structural and sociocultural barriers and lower awareness levels. Service quality was…

articles.title: Integrative bioinformatics and preliminary experimental validation suggest the therapeutic potential of lycorine in uterine corpus endometrial carcinoma.
articles.authors: Dong P, Xia L, Zhao L et al.
articles.abstract: Uterine corpus endometrial carcinoma (UCEC) is one of the most prevalent gynecological malignancies worldwide and remains a significant threat to women's health. Lycorine, a natural alkaloid isolated from plants of the Amaryllidaceae family, has attracted considerable attention owing to its diverse pharmacological activities, particularly its anti-tumor properties. However, the potential therapeutic targets and action mechanism of lycorine in UCEC remain unclear.In this study, an integrated strategy combining bioinformatic analysis and preliminary experimental validation was used to elucidate the anti-tumor mechanisms of lycorine in UCEC. Potential targets of lycorine were predicted using public databases and intersected with differentially expressed genes derived from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) UCEC dataset. Subsequently, a protein-protein interaction (PPI) network was constructed, and Gene Ontology (GO) and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) enrichment analyses were used to investigate the biological functions and pathways associated with these targets. Prognostic analysis and Cox regression were used to establish a risk prediction model. Immune infiltration analysis was performed to evaluate the relationship between key genes and the tumor immune microenvironment.Results revealed 10 potential targets of lycorine associated with UCEC. Functional enrichment analysis indicated that these genes were mainly involved in cholinergic synapse and neuroactive ligand-receptor interaction pathways. Three key genes (ACHE, MAN2B1, and PNP) were further identified to construct a prognostic model, which showed moderate predictive performance in survival analysis. Immune infiltration analysis revealed that these genes were associated with multiple immune cell populations in the tumor microenvironment. Molecular docking revealed that the binding energies of ACHE, MAN2B1, and PNP with lycorine were ≤ - 7.0 kcal/mol, indicating stable binding. In vitro experiments confirmed that lycorine significantly inhibited the proliferation of Ishikawa endometrial cancer cells.In conclusion, this study provides new insights into the potential therapeutic effects of lycorine in UCEC and identifies ACHE, MAN2B1, and PNP as promising therapeutic targets for further investigation.

articles.title: Unrecognized and unheard: Experiences of black mothers navigating the "good NICU mother" ideal across the preterm birth continuum.
articles.authors: Warren KF, Dail RB, Felder TM et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Black mothers who experience preterm birth and neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) hospitalization face intersecting structural and institutional challenges that shape their early maternal experiences. While racial disparities in maternal and neonatal outcomes are well documented, less is known about how racialized narratives of Black motherhood are enacted across everyday perinatal care interactions. Grounded in the principles of respectful maternity care (RMC), this study examines how Black mothers navigate birth, neonatal transport, and NICU hospitalization, and how institutional expectations of the "good NICU mother" shape maternal identity and legitimacy within these settings.
METHODS: This qualitative study used a reflexive thematic analysis of in-depth interviews with five Black mothers whose preterm infants (born at 24-28 weeks gestation) required neonatal transport to a tertiary NICU in South Carolina. Interviews were conducted during or shortly after the infant's NICU hospitalization and analyzed using Braun and Clarke's six-phase approach. Findings were contextualized using an adapted National Institute on Minority Health and Health Disparities research framework.
RESULTS: Three phases of experience were identified: (1) preterm labor and initial contact with the healthcare system, (2) preterm birth at a referral hospital and neonatal transport, and (3) the postpartum period during NICU hospitalization. Across all three phases, participants described dismissal of their concerns, constrained communication, limited agency, and physical and emotional mistreatment; these experiences directly conflict with the core principles of RMC. The "good NICU mother" emerged as a regulatory standard (defined by constant bedside presence, emotional composure, breastmilk production, and fluency in medical terminology) that participants were evaluated against but structurally unable to meet. For Black mothers, these expectations intersected with racialized assumptions about maternal competence and responsibility, intensifying experiences of surveillance and scrutiny.
CONCLUSIONS: Institutional systems of perinatal care function as sites where maternal legitimacy is interpreted and evaluated, often in ways that undermine RMC for Black mothers. Extending RMC principles beyond labor and delivery into neonatal intensive care settings is essential for achieving equitable, dignity-centered care. Structural reforms to visitation policies, documentation…

articles.title: Glycemic changes during first 48 h postpartum in mothers with gestational diabetes mellitus and non-diabetic mothers - a comparative study.
articles.authors: Jayawardane MAMM, Rusta MMF, Gangodawila TH et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) is a common metabolic disorder in pregnancy and is associated with an increased risk of maternal complications and future development of type 2 diabetes mellitus. While glycemia is expected to normalize after delivery due to loss of placental hormones, early postpartum glycemic changes are not well understood. This study aims to assess the rate of normalization of blood glucose levels in the immediate postpartum period among mothers with GDM and to compare these changes with physiological glycemic patterns in non-diabetic mothers.
METHODS: This descriptive observational comparative study was conducted among postpartum mothers at the Professorial Unit, Ward 21, Colombo South Teaching Hospital. Mothers with GDM diagnosed using a 75 g oral glucose tolerance test were compared with non-diabetic mothers. Eligible women were recruited (n = 60; 30 per group) using stratified sampling, and capillary blood glucose was measured using validated glucometers within 2 h of delivery and before and 2 h after meals over 48 h. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire and medical records and analyzed using IBM SPSS Statistic. A p-value < 0.05 was considered statistically significant.
RESULTS: Mothers with gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) demonstrated consistently higher mean glucose levels compared to non-diabetic mothers during the early postpartum period. Statistically significant differences were observed at the majority of preprandial and postprandial time points within the first 48 h (p < 0.05). However, by the sixth meal, both preprandial and postprandial glucose values showed no statistically significant difference between the two groups (p > 0.05), indicating convergence of glucose levels and a trend toward normalization in mothers with GDM.
CONCLUSIONS: Postpartum mothers with GDM show significantly higher glucose levels than non-GDM mothers during the first 48 h after delivery, with marked postprandial spikes and elevated pre-meal values despite a trend toward normalization by the 6th meal point. Early postpartum hyperglycemia resolves quickly by the sixth meal. Standard six week postpartum and long term diabetes screening remain the standard of care regardless of rapidity of glucose normalization.

articles.title: Population-level trends, risk factors and predictors of hypertensive disorders of pregnancy in the U.S, 2014-2023.
articles.authors: Idowu KA, Torres CM, Dongawar D et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP) remain a leading cause of maternal and perinatal morbidity in the United States. Despite advances in care, recent data suggest a rising prevalence.
METHOD: Using National Center for Health Statistics (NCHS) National Vital Statistics System (NVSS) natality data from 2014-2023 (n = 37.7 million births), we examined temporal trends, risk factors, and outcomes associated with chronic hypertension (CH), gestational hypertension (GH), and eclampsia.
RESULTS: HDP affected 9.9% of all pregnancies, increasing substantially across all racial/ethnic groups. Maternal obesity was the strongest modifiable predictor, with extreme obesity conferring > 6-fold higher odds of HDP. Non-Hispanic (NH) Black mothers had consistently higher prevalence of every subtype. HDP was strongly associated with preterm birth and low birth weight.
CONCLUSION: Findings suggest that rising HDP burden reflects both true epidemiologic shifts and improved diagnostic awareness, with implications for prenatal care, equity-focused interventions, and intergenerational cardiometabolic health.

articles.title: Machine learning for early prediction of preterm birth.
articles.authors: Teshome F, Gidi NW, Choe SW et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Preterm birth (PTB), defined as delivery before 37 completed weeks of gestation, remains a major cause of neonatal mortality and long-term morbidity worldwide. Conventional risk assessment strategies, including cervical length measurement and biomarker-based screening, have shown limited predictive performance. Machine learning (ML) may improve PTB prediction by integrating heterogeneous clinical data and identifying complex risk patterns.
METHODS: A structured narrative review was conducted by systematically searching PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, IEEE Xplore, and Google Scholar for studies published between January 2010 and April 2024. Studies were screened according to predefined eligibility criteria, and 14 studies evaluating ML models for PTB prediction using human pregnancy datasets were included in the final narrative synthesis. Data on study characteristics, predictor variables, ML methods, validation strategies, and model performance were extracted and synthesized narratively.
RESULTS: A total of 14 studies met the predefined eligibility criteria and were included in the final narrative synthesis. ML models generally performed better when they used longitudinal electronic health records (EHRs), repeated measurements, or richer maternal clinical histories. Ensemble approaches such as random forest, gradient boosting, and stacking models, as well as deep learning (DL) methods including artificial neural networks (ANNs), recurrent neural networks (RNNs), and long short-term memory networks (LSTMs), were frequently among the best-performing models. Across the included studies, previous PTB, cervical length, maternal age, hypertensive disorders, diabetes, and body mass index (BMI) emerged as the most consistently reported predictors of ML model performance. However, the evidence was highly heterogeneous in data sources, outcome definitions, validation methods, and performance reporting. External validation, calibration assessment, and real-world clinical evaluation were limited.
CONCLUSION: ML shows considerable promise for improving early PTB risk stratification, but clinical translation will depend on early prediction, interpretable outputs, and robust external validation. Although ML models generally demonstrated promising predictive performance, interpretation of these findings is limited by methodological heterogeneity and inconsistent external validation across studies. Future studies should prioritize standardized reporting,…

articles.title: Prevalence and factors associated with maternal near-miss at the Regional Hospital Bamenda.
articles.authors: Pisoh DW, Tcheudeu AMT, Mforteh AAA et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Maternal Near Miss (MNM) is a woman who nearly died but survived a complication that occurred during pregnancy, childbirth or within 42 days after childbirth. It assesses and monitors the activities aimed at the prevention of maternal mortality. A 2019 systematic review estimated the global prevalence of MNM at 18.67 per 1000 live births. This study aimed to determine the prevalence of maternal near miss and the associated factors at the Regional Hospital Bamenda.
METHODS: A hospital-based cross-sectional study was conducted for a period of three months at the Regional Hospital Bamenda. Data were collected from women who were admitted during pregnancy, childbirth or within 42 days after the termination of pregnancy using a structured pretested questionnaire. Data collected were analysed using R studio. Descriptive analysis was done followed by bivariate and multivariable logistic regression. Chi-squared test was used to determine the strength of association between variables. Statistical significance was considered at a p value < 0.05 and confidence interval of 95%.
RESULTS: Among the 725 live births occurring during the study period, 44 women experienced maternal near-miss events, yielding a maternal near miss prevalence of 60.7 per 1000 live births. Of 252 women enrolled in the study, severe haemorrhage and severe pre-eclampsia were the leading causes of MNM. After multivariable logistic regression analysis, ANC follow-up was independently associated with reduced odds of maternal near-miss (aOR = 0.04, 95% CI: 0.01-0.11), while referral was associated with increased odds of maternal near-miss (aOR = 4.16, 95% CI: 1.85-9.59).
CONCLUSION: There was a high prevalence of maternal near-miss at the Regional Hospital Bamenda. Women with no ANC follow-up and women referred were at risk of having maternal near-miss.

articles.title: Antibiotic susceptibility of genital tract isolates in pregnant women with premature pre-labour rupture of membranes (PPROM) in a low-resource setting.
articles.authors: Alatawi Z, Abdalla E, Mohammed AG et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Premature pre-labour rupture of membranes (PPROM) is a significant obstetric complication that contributes to preterm births, maternal infections, and neonatal morbidity. The role of genital tract infections in the etiology of PPROM is well established, yet data on microbial isolates and antibiotic susceptibility patterns in resource-limited settings remain scarce. This study aimed to determine the microbial profile and antibiotic resistance patterns among women with PPROM in Sudan.
METHODS: A hospital-based case-control study was conducted at Omdurman Maternity Hospital, Sudan, from June to December 2022. A total of 140 participants were enrolled, including 70 women with PPROM and 70 gestational age-matched controls without PPROM. Endocervical swabs were collected under sterile conditions and cultured for microbial identification. Antibiotic susceptibility testing was performed using the disk diffusion method following CLSI 2021 guidelines. Data were analysed using SPSS version 25, and associations were assessed using odds ratios (OR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI); p < 0.05 was considered statistically significant.
RESULTS: Positive cultures were significantly more frequent among PPROM patients (60.0%) than controls (27.1%) (OR = 4.03; 95% CI: 1.98-8.20; p < 0.001). The predominant isolates in PPROM cases were Staphylococcus aureus (34.3%; OR = 11.47; 95% CI: 3.20-62.94; p < 0.001), Enterobacter spp. (12.9%; OR = 4.97; 95% CI: 0.97-49.00; p = 0.055), and Escherichia coli (11.4%). In contrast, Candida albicans was more common in controls (12.9%; OR = 0.10; 95% CI: 0.002-0.75; p = 0.017). Antibiotic susceptibility testing showed high resistance to amoxicillin and amoxiclav, while cefotaxime (95.8% susceptibility for S. aureus) and erythromycin (87.5% for E. coli) were the most effective agents.
CONCLUSION: Genital tract infections play a significant role in PPROM, with Staphylococcus aureus, E. coli, and Enterobacter spp. being the predominant isolates. The high prevalence of in vitro resistance, particularly to penicillins, supports the need for continuous antimicrobial surveillance and periodic review of empirical regimens. As pregnancy and neonatal outcomes were not assessed, these findings should be interpreted as microbiological observations that may help inform, but do not by themselves establish, screening or treatment policies in low-resource settings.

articles.title: Neonatal SARS-CoV-2 positivity and short-term outcomes.
articles.authors: Dutra LV, Gonçalves GL, Silva MH et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Neonatal SARS-CoV-2 positivity among newborns born to infected mothers appears to be uncommon, and factors associated with neonatal positivity and short-term outcomes remain incompletely understood.
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to compare short-term outcomes between SARS-CoV-2-positive and SARS-CoV-2-negative newborns born to mothers with COVID-19 during pregnancy.
METHODS: In this matched case-control study, 263 pregnant women with COVID-19 were identified during the study period, and 218 newborns underwent RT-PCR testing for SARS-CoV-2 within the first 48 h of life. Among them, 23 newborns tested positive and were matched (1:2) with 46 newborns who tested negative according to clinically relevant maternal and neonatal characteristics, including the interval between maternal infection and delivery, maternal disease severity, gestational age, newborn sex, and birth weight appropriateness for gestational age.
RESULTS: The mean gestational age and birth weight of the newborns were 38.2 ± 1.7 weeks and 2994.2 ± 464.5 g, respectively. Fifteen newborns (21.7%) experienced complications during hospitalization, most commonly hypotonia/hypoactivity (13.0%) and early respiratory distress (10.1%). Respiratory distress was associated with neonatal SARS-CoV-2 positivity (OR = 21.31; 95% CI 2.24-201.68; p = 0.008). In addition, maternal COVID-19 infection occurring closer to delivery was associated with an increased likelihood of neonatal SARS-CoV-2 positivity (OR = 1.007; 95% CI 1.001-1.014; p = 0.026).
CONCLUSIONS: SARS-CoV-2-positive newborns appeared to experience respiratory complications more frequently during hospitalization, while maternal infection closer to delivery was associated with neonatal positivity. Given the observational design and relatively small sample size, these findings should be interpreted with caution.

articles.title: Attentive interpretable tabular learning (TabNet) for miRNA expression classification in cervical cancer and Alzheimer's disease.
articles.authors: Haznedar H, Özsert Yiğit G, Haznedar B
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: The classification of RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) data presents a fundamental challenge in computational biomedicine: raw read counts are high-dimensional, over-dispersed, and heteroscedastic, requiring careful preprocessing before machine learning models can be applied. Existing deep learning approaches for RNA-seq classification have largely overlooked the tabular nature of genomic expression data and have offered limited embedded interpretability. This study proposes TabNet, an attentive interpretable tabular learning architecture, as a framework for miRNA-based disease classification and evaluates its performance and interpretability against three established baseline models.
METHODS: Two publicly available miRNA expression datasets were examined: a cervical cancer cohort (58 samples, 714 miRNAs) and an Alzheimer's disease cohort (70 samples, 503 miRNAs). Raw count data were preprocessed following the MLSeq framework, encompassing DESeq median-ratio normalisation, near-zero variance filtering, supervised gene ranking based on DESeq differential expression analysis, and the DESeq variance-stabilising transformation (vst). Gene subsets corresponding to 5%, 10%, and 30% of the post-filtering feature space were evaluated. TabNet was benchmarked against eight baselines spanning four learning paradigms: a 1D Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), a Long Short-Term Memory network (LSTM), Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), Random Forest, ElasticNet-regularised logistic regression, a Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP), the prior-fitted transformer TabPFN, and the inherently interpretable Explainable Boosting Machine (EBM). Each configuration was assessed over 50 independent random train/test splits (70%/30%) under a strict leakage-free protocol in which all preprocessing, hyperparameter selection, and early stopping relied exclusively on inner validation subsets of the training partitions; all metrics are reported as mean ± SD.
RESULTS: Under the leakage-free protocol, a group of four methods reached a statistically indistinguishable accuracy ceiling: on the cervical cancer dataset, ElasticNet (95.06% ± 4.66), EBM (94.94% ± 4.60), TabPFN (94.71% ± 4.64), and Random Forest (94.35% ± 5.82); on the Alzheimer's disease dataset, TabPFN (70.86% ± 10.26), EBM (70.67% ± 12.67), and ElasticNet (70.48% ± 9.76) led. TabNet reached 85.18% ± 11.10 (cervical) and 64.38% ± 11.23 (Alzheimer's) at its respective best levels -- below the top tier, but with the…

articles.title: Pyroptotic Macrophage Extracellular Vesicles Drive miR-103a-3p Mediated Mitochondrial Dysfunction in Granulosa Cells in Diminished Ovarian Reserve.
articles.authors: Ju W, Xin X, Xiao Y et al.
articles.abstract: To define the role of pyroptotic macrophage-derived extracellular vesicles (EVs) in diminished ovarian reserve (DOR) and to elucidate whether EVs-mediated transfer of miR-103a-3p drives mitochondrial dysfunction in granulosa cells. Single-cell RNA sequencing data from public GEO datasets were analyzed to characterize pyroptosis-associated features in ovarian macrophages across age groups. EVs were isolated from pyroptotic macrophages and applied to granulosa cells (KGN) to assess mitochondrial function, oxidative stress, and apoptosis. miRNA sequencing was performed to identify EVs-enriched miRNAs. miR-103a-3p expression was further evaluated in follicular fluid EVs from DOR patients and correlated with ovarian reserve markers. Mechanistic studies were conducted using in vitro assays and an in vivo mouse model. Pyroptosis signatures were enriched in ovarian macrophages with aging. EVs from pyroptotic macrophages were enriched in miR-103a-3p and induced mitochondrial dysfunction in granulosa cells, characterized by reduced ATP, increased ROS, and enhanced apoptosis; these effects were alleviated by miR-103a-3p inhibition. Clinically, miR-103a-3p was elevated in follicular fluid EVs from DOR patients and negatively correlated with AMH and AFC. Mechanistically, miR-103a-3p targeted MFN2 and BCL2L13, disrupting mitochondrial homeostasis in KGN cells. Restoration of these targets mitigated dysfunction in KGN cells. In vivo, AAV-mediated inhibition of miR-103a-3p improved follicular development and ovarian function. Pyroptotic macrophages may contribute to DOR progression through EVs-mediated delivery of miR-103a-3p, which impairs mitochondrial homeostasis in granulosa cells by targeting MFN2 and BCL2L13.

articles.title: CRIP1 Promotes Ovarian Cancer Progression by Mediating the KRAS-USP7 Interaction and Stabilizing KRAS.
articles.authors: Zhan Q, Zhuang Y, Wang H et al.
articles.abstract: Ovarian cancer (OC), a leading cause of gynecological cancer mortality, demands deeper molecular understanding. This study investigates the role of Cysteine-Rich Protein 1 (CRIP1) in OC pathogenesis. In this study, CRIP1 expression and its correlation with prognosis were analyzed using public databases and clinical OC tissue samples. OC cell line HEY and SKOV3 were employed in the in vitro experiments. Gene and protein expression were measured by qRT-PCR, Western blotting (WB), immunohistochemistry (IHC), and immunofluorescence (IF). Cell proliferation was assessed via CCK-8 and EDU assays. Cell migration and invasion were evaluated using Transwell and wound healing assays. Protein-protein interaction between CRIP1, KRAS, and USP7 was confirmed by co-immunoprecipitation (Co-IP). The in vivo role of CRIP1 was validated using xenograft mouse models. Our results showed that CRIP1 expression was significantly upregulated in OC tissues compared to adjacent normal tissues, and high CRIP1 expression correlated with poor patient prognosis. Overexpression of CRIP1 enhanced OC cell proliferation, migration, and invasion, while CRIP1 knockdown suppressed these malignant phenotypes. Mechanistically, CRIP1 facilitated the interaction between KRAS and the deubiquitinase USP7, leading to KRAS protein stabilization. CRIP1 overexpression increased USP7-bound KRAS and elevated total KRAS protein levels. Treatment with USP7 inhibitor (P5091) destabilized KRAS. More importantly, KRAS knockdown reversed the effect of CRIP1 overexpression on cell proliferation, migration and invasion. Finally, CRIP1 overexpression significantly accelerated OC progression in xenograft models. Collectively, our findings demonstrate that CRIP1 promotes ovarian cancer progression by mediating the KRAS-USP7 interaction and stabilizing KRAS. This study elucidates a novel molecular mechanism underlying OC progression and identifies CRIP1 as a potential therapeutic target.

articles.title: Diagnostic performance of MRI and transvaginal ultrasound for urinary tract endometriosis: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.authors: Pitsillidi A, Vona L, Kyriakoulis K et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare the diagnostic accuracy of transvaginal ultrasound (TVUS) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) for detecting urinary tract endometriosis (UTE), including ureteral and bladder involvement.
METHODS: A systematic review and meta-analysis were conducted according to PRISMA 2020 guidelines. PubMed, Embase, and Scopus were searched from inception to December 2025 for diagnostic accuracy studies evaluating TVUS and/or MRI for UTE. Surgical findings, with or without histopathological confirmation, were used as the reference standard. Studies reporting sufficient data to construct 2 × 2 contingency tables were included. Pooled sensitivity and specificity with 95% confidence intervals (CI) were calculated using a bivariate random-effects model, with separate analyses for ureteral and bladder endometriosis.
RESULTS: Thirty-six studies met the inclusion criteria. For ureteral endometriosis, TVUS demonstrated a pooled sensitivity of 0.89 (95% CI 0.65-0.97) and specificity of 1.00 (95% CI 0.97-1.00), while MRI showed a pooled sensitivity of 0.96 (95% CI 0.50-1.00) and specificity of 1.00 (95% CI 0.96-1.00). For bladder endometriosis, TVUS yielded a pooled sensitivity of 0.70 (95% CI 0.55-0.81) and specificity of 1.00 (95% CI 0.99-1.00), whereas MRI demonstrated a pooled sensitivity of 0.77 (95% CI 0.58-0.89) and specificity of 0.99 (95% CI 0.98-1.00). Substantial heterogeneity was observed, particularly for sensitivity estimates.
CONCLUSION: TVUS and MRI show excellent specificity for diagnosing urinary tract endometriosis. MRI provides slightly higher sensitivity for ureteral disease, while both modalities demonstrate moderate sensitivity for bladder involvement. A complementary, site-specific imaging approach is, therefore, supported, with cautious interpretation of negative findings.

articles.title: Evaluation of the Idylla system for rapid detection of POLE mutations in colorectal and endometrial cancers.
articles.journal: Virchows Archiv : an international journal of pathology
articles.authors: Barbe S, Quang VT, Saal C et al.
articles.abstract: Pathogenic exonuclease domain mutations in POLE define a hypermutated subtype of colorectal and endometrial cancers, with prognostic and therapeutic implications, particularly for immunotherapy. Detection currently relies on next-generation sequencing, which is sensitive but costly and time-consuming. The Idylla™ POLE-POLD1 Mutation Assay (Biocartis) is a fully automated real-time PCR for rapid detection of hotspot mutations, but its performance has not been fully evaluated.We retrospectively analyzed a cohort of 40 patients to evaluate the performance of the Idylla™ assay. All tumors underwent targeted NGS of POLE exons 9-14. DNA from formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded tissue was analyzed with the Idylla™ assay and results were compared with NGS. The assay's limit of detection was also determined.The Idylla™ assay detected POLE hotspot variants with 96% sensitivity and 100% specificity. Limit of detection experiments indicated reliable detection only in samples with DNA concentration > 5 ng/µL and tumor cell content > 20%.The Idylla™ POLE-POLD1 Mutation Assay enables rapid, robust detection of POLE hotspot variants in colorectal and endometrial cancers, with high concordance to NGS. Integrating Idylla as a front-line screening tool could accelerate molecular classification, though NGS remains necessary for samples with low tumor content or low DNA input.

articles.title: Metabolic Landscape and Immune Microenvironment in Ovarian Cancer: Mechanisms of Remodelling and Therapeutic Opportunities.
articles.authors: Zhao Y, Wang Y, Huang L et al.
articles.abstract: Ovarian Cancer (OC) is the most lethal gynaecological malignancy worldwide, with a 5-year survival rate of less than 50%. Most patients still face tumour recurrence and drug resistance, which is mainly attributed to its highly complex tumour immune microenvironment (TIME) and metabolic heterogeneity, where metabolic remodelling severely suppresses immune cell function. OC cells exhibit distinctive metabolic reprogramming during tumour development and progression. In addition, various cells such as tumour-associated macrophages and neutrophils collectively construct an immunosuppressive network through their respective metabolic pathways. In the hypoxic peritoneal niche, hypoxia-inducible factor-1α directly drives the expression of galectin-1 and intersects with the IDO1-kynurenine-AhR axis, jointly reinforcing regulatory T-cell expansion and T-cell exhaustion. Targeting metabolic reprogramming to reshape the TIME has become a research hotspot, and emerging strategies including the delivery of metabolic inhibitors via nanoplatforms have shown synergistic antitumour potential. This article elaborates the mechanisms of metabolic reprogramming between OC cells and various cell types within the TIME, focusing on breaking immune tolerance by correcting metabolic disorders, so as to provide theoretical support for novel therapeutic regimens for OC based on immunometabolic regulation.

articles.title: Global trends, regional disparities, and causes of maternal mortality - a systematic review.
articles.authors: Sabatine TC, Durães TA, Nagahashi DM et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To synthesize current evidence on global maternal mortality trends, focusing on regional disparities, leading causes of maternal death, and methodological challenges in estimating maternal mortality across different health system contexts.
METHODS: A systematic review was conducted following PRISMA guidelines. Searches were performed in PubMed/MEDLINE and SciELO using terms related to maternal mortality, health systems, and social determinants. Observational studies, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, and institutional reports with explicit methodology were included. Studies focusing only on morbidity, lacking clear methodology, or those not available in English or Portuguese were excluded. Data on maternal mortality ratios, trends, causes of death, and structural determinants were extracted and synthesized narratively due to methodological heterogeneity.
RESULTS: A total of 513 records were identified; after removing 173 duplicates, 340 were screened. Following title and abstract review, 299 records were excluded. Forty-one full-text articles were assessed, and 30 were excluded. Eleven studies were included in the qualitative synthesis (three observational studies, three systematic reviews/meta-analyses, and five institutional reports). Maternal mortality declined substantially between 1990 and 2015, but progress slowed thereafter. Approximately 287,000 maternal deaths occurred in 2020. Major regional disparities persist, with the highest burden in Sub-Saharan Africa. Hemorrhage, hypertensive disorders, and sepsis remain the leading direct causes, while indirect causes - especially cardiovascular disease - are increasingly relevant.
CONCLUSION: Although maternal mortality has declined since 1990, progress has slowed and major regional inequalities persist. Indirect causes are becoming more prominent, and methodological differences complicate global estimates. Further reductions will require stronger healthcare systems, improved surveillance, and policies addressing social determinants of maternal health.

articles.title: Is the risk of venous thromboembolic disease truly an absolute contraindication for menopause hormone therapy?
articles.authors: Fait T, Šimková S, Dvořáková V
articles.abstract: Oral menopause hormone therapy (MHT) is associated with a two- to four-fold increased risk of venous thromboembolism (VTE). According to the majority of studies, the increased risk of venous thromboembolic disease does not apply to transdermal administration. Transdermal MHT is considered safe even in women at a high risk of thromboembolic disease (such as those with overweight, obesity, thrombophilic conditions, recent surgery, immobilization, varicose veins, malignancy, or smoking). Acute VTE represents an absolute contraindication to both oral and transdermal administration of MHT. A personal history of VTE is an absolute contraindication to oral MHT, but only a relative contraindication for the transdermal route of MHT. Menopause hormone therapy must be personalized for each woman.

articles.title: Female ejaculation and squirting - definition, classification and differential diagnosis.
articles.authors: Pastor Z
articles.abstract: Women may release various types of fluids during sexual arousal and orgasm, representing either a physiological sexual response or a manifestation of urinary incontinence. The origin of periorgasmic fluids, their volume, biochemical composition, and mechanism of expulsion depend on anatomical and physiological predispositions as well as the degree of sexual arousal. These phenomena include vaginal lubrication, female ejaculation, squirting, and coital incontinence. This paper provides an overview of the evolution of perspectives on these phenomena and highlights inaccuracies in some previous studies. Differential diagnosis of these "sexual" fluids is based on their volume, appearance, characteristics, and women's subjective perceptions - however, objective verification requires biochemical analysis and use of imaging methods. Squirting is defined as massive transurethral expulsion of a clear fluid originating from the urinary bladder, whereas female ejaculation represents the secretion of a very small amount of thick fluid from the paraurethral (Skene's) glands. The paper presents current definitions, systematic classification, and differential diagnosis of these phenomena.

articles.title: Hysteroscopic septum resection and reproductive outcomes - a retrospective cohort study.
articles.authors: Özgül ZS, Madakbaş AÇ, Yıldız P et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Uterine septum is one of the most common congenital uterine anomalies associated with infertility, recurrent pregnancy loss, and adverse reproductive outcomes. This study aimed to evaluate reproductive outcomes after hysteroscopic septum resection and to identify factors associated with live birth.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this retrospective cohort study, 218 women who underwent hysteroscopic septum resection at a tertiary referral center in Istanbul between January 1, 2015 and August 31, 2020 were included. Among them, 160 had a history of infertility and 58 had a history of recurrent pregnancy loss. Demographic characteristics, preoperative and postoperative live birth outcomes, and pregnancy complications were obtained from hospital electronic records, the national e-Nabız system, and follow-up telephone interviews.
RESULTS: Among the overall cohort, the live birth rate increased from 17.4% before septum resection to 53.7% after the procedure (P < 0.001). In the infertility subgroup, the live birth rate increased from 10.6% to 46.9% (P < 0.001), whereas in the recurrent pregnancy loss subgroup it increased from 36.2% to 72.4% (P < 0.001). Patients who underwent repeat septum resection had a higher live birth rate than those who underwent a single procedure (74.0 vs. 44.0%, P < 0.001). Pregnancy complications were observed in 23.9% of pregnancies.
CONCLUSION: Hysteroscopic septum resection may be associated with improved live birth outcomes in women with infertility or recurrent pregnancy loss. However, these findings should be interpreted cautiously given the retrospective design, and prospective studies are needed to define the benefit of surgical intervention.

articles.title: Transverse B-Lynch suture - specific modality of a uterine compression suture.
articles.authors: Maule M, Brychtová P
articles.abstract: Peripartum life-threatening bleeding is a significant cause of maternal morbidity and mortality worldwide. Rapid and massive blood loss requires quick and effective intervention. In addition to conservative treatments, we often have to use surgical interventions, including compression sutures. In our work, we describe the indication, technical conditions, and performance of a specific B-Lynch transversal compression suture. It is an effective surgical method, often in connection with an inverted or low-seated placenta during caesarean section. We compare the B-Lynch II with the B-Lynch I variant. If we consider the relative simplicity of the principle of the B-Lynch transversal suture effect and our own utilization of this modality, then we ask what is the cause of the persistent distrust and reservation when deciding to implement the suture in clinical practice and recommended procedures from the obstetrician. An explanation is offered that the introduction of this method into routine practice is limited mainly by a lack of knowledge, a lack of understanding the complexity of the intervention, and without a doubt, the fear of complications. Recommending the application of a compression suture only after the failure of other surgical methods can also lead to the discrediting of this method. However, we have experience that the application of a B-Lynch transversal suture as an ultimum refugium (before a possible indication of hysterectomy) is ineffective and often impossible in altered terrain and increasing blood loss. In a typical indication, we recommend using B-Lynch II as the method of first choice. We have our own set of 16 successful cases, which will be the subject of another communication.

articles.title: Methylation test versus dual staining in the triage of HR-HPV positive women - pilot data from cervical cancer screening.
articles.authors: Bartošová M, Kinkorová Luňáčková I, Bouda J et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Introduction of high-risk human papillomavirus (HR-HPV) testing into cervical cancer screening increases the detection of high-grade cervical lesions, but also identifies women with transient HR-HPV infections who are at a low risk of progression. To improve risk stratification, biomarkers that can be assessed from the same cervical sample used for HPV testing may be employed, particularly p16/Ki-67 dual-stain cytology and host-cell DNA methylation analysis. Dual staining identifies cells showing HPV-induced transforming activity, but may not fully capture the biological variability of either the host or the HPV infection. Methylation testing reflects epigenetic changes associated with persistent HR-HPV infection and biologically advanced cervical lesions that may therefore provide a more direct indication of the short-term risk of lesion progression.
OBJECTIVE: To compare performance of p16/Ki-67 dual staining and DNA methylation analysis for risk stratification of HR--HPV-positive women.
METHODS: The study included 44 HR-HPV-positive women (median age, 35 years) participating in the Czech cervical cancer screening program who underwent cervical biopsy or conization. Histologically confirmed HSIL/AIS was diagnosed in 52% of cases. Results of both triage methods were evaluated according to age, HPV genotype, and histological findings.
RESULTS: The two methods showed concordant results in approximately 60% of cases, with the highest concordance observed in women older than 35 years. Among women aged 35 years or younger, discordant results were more frequent, most commonly consisting of positive dual staining combined with a negative methylation test. High concordance between the two methods was observed in HPV16-associated lesions, whereas among infections with other HR-HPV genotypes, positive dual staining accompanied by a negative methylation result was more common.
CONCLUSION: These findings suggest that methylation testing may be particularly useful for the triage of younger HR-HPV-positive women, potentially helping to reduce unnecessary referrals and invasive procedures without compromising the detection of clinically relevant cervical lesions. The findings of this pilot study are currently being validated in a larger prospective study conducted in collaboration with a specialized colposcopy clinic.

articles.title: Associations of Maternal and Neonatal Characteristics with Infant Airway and Parenchymal Function.
articles.authors: Tepper RS, Slaven JE, Bjerregaard J et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To determine whether gestational age (GA) at birth, maternal and infant characteristics, and factors in the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) are associated with worse infant lung function.
STUDY DESIGN: In a cohort of infants born preterm we assessed forced expiratory flow at 75% expired forced vital capacity (FEF75; FVC), lung diffusion (DL), and alveolar volume (VA) following NICU discharge. Using maternal, infant and NICU data obtained from electronic medical records, we evaluated the relationships of these factors and lung function expressed as z-scores.
RESULTS: Most mothers received antenatal steroids and delivered by cesarean section; 10% smoked during pregnancy, 32.9% had hypertensive disorders of pregnancy, and <10% were diagnosed with chorioamnionitis. Infants had a mean gestational age of 31.3 weeks; 51% received surfactant and 15.4% received postnatal corticosteroids. Mean duration for respiratory support was 24 days for oxygen supplementation, 36.6 days for non-invasive ventilation (NIV), and 4.8 days for invasive mechanical ventilation (IMV). Maternal characteristics were not associated with lung function; however, GA at birth was associated with lower airway and lower parenchymal function over the wide GA range of our participants. The inclusion of additional potential characteristics along with GA indicated that longer non-invasive ventilation (NIV) treatment was also associated with lower airway function. Our findings also suggest that NIV accounted for much of the association between GA and lower airway function. In contrast the effect of GA upon parenchymal function was not mediated through NIV.
CONCLUSIONS: We found an association between more days of NIV and lower FEFs; however, we did not find a similar association for the parenchymal function of gas exchange. Future research is required to evaluate whether this is a causal relationship, which would suggest the need to optimize NICU ventilatory support to minimize its potential adverse effects upon lung growth and development following preterm birth.

articles.title: Etiological Spectrum of Primary Ovarian Insufficiency in a Group of Children and Adolescents: A Tertiary Single-Center Experience.
articles.journal: Journal of pediatric and adolescent gynecology
articles.authors: Karataş MÇ, Köprülü Ö, Cinleti T et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Primary ovarian insufficiency (POI) with a 46,XX karyotype is rare in pediatric and adolescent populations. It is a heterogeneous condition with important implications for pubertal development, fertility potential, genetic counseling, and long-term health. This study aimed to characterize the clinical, genetic, and etiological spectrum of pediatric and adolescent POI and to evaluate the diagnostic contribution of genetic testing.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed pediatric and adolescent patients diagnosed with POI before 18 years of age. Demographic characteristics, presenting features, auxological data, hormonal profiles, imaging findings, molecular investigations, treatment-related exposures, and etiological classifications were analyzed.
RESULTS: Twenty-five patients were included. The median age at diagnosis was 14.83 years (interquartile range [IQR]: 11.81-15.71). Primary amenorrhea was the most common presentation, observed in 44% of patients, followed by diagnosis during endocrine surveillance for chronic diseases in 24%, short stature in 20%, and secondary amenorrhea in 12%. Genetic etiologies were identified in 56% of patients, with variants detected in MCM9, HAX1, TALDO1, HFM1, and MTRFR (C12orf65). Familial clustering was particularly prominent among patients with MCM9 and HAX1 variants. Iatrogenic POI occurred in patients previously exposed to gonadotoxic chemotherapy, radiotherapy, or gonadotoxic conditioning regimens administered before hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT).
CONCLUSIONS: In this study, we present the clinical characteristics of pediatric and adolescent patients with POI, including different etiologies and phenotypic presentations. Our findings underscore the value of targeted Next-Generation Sequencing (NGS) analysis in routine clinical practice. Moreover, the recurrent identification of the same MCM9 variant in unrelated families raises the possibility of a founder effect.

articles.title: Paternal zearalenone exposure impairs transgenerational male spermatogenesis via the METTL14-m6A-Thap1-glutathione axis.
articles.authors: Chen C, Ren YT, Lin S et al.
articles.abstract: Zearalenone (ZEA), a widespread mycotoxin with endocrine-disrupting activity, poses a potential risk to male reproduction. However, the transgenerational effects of paternal ZEA exposure on offspring spermatogenesis and the underlying epitranscriptomic mechanisms remain poorly understood. Here, we investigated whether paternal ZEA exposure causes transgenerational male reproductive toxicity and elucidated the associated epitranscriptomic mechanism. In mice, chronic paternal ZEA exposure (5 mg/kg/day for 10 weeks) significantly reduced sperm count and motility, increased the sperm malformation rate, and disrupted testicular histomorphology in F1 and F2 male offspring. Mechanistically, multi-omics analysis revealed a marked reduction in testicular GSH levels. This reduction was attributable to decreased expression of GSS, the terminal enzyme catalyzing the final step of de novo GSH synthesis, and of GGT7, a GSH hydrolase involved in GSH degradation/recycling; both enzymes are transcriptionally activated by THAP1. Notably, paternal ZEA exposure is associated with increased METTL14-mediated m6A enrichment at candidate sites of Thap1 mRNA, which may promote YTHDF2-dependent decay and reduce THAP1 protein. Knockdown of Mettl14 in paternal testes or targeted overexpression of Thap1 in offspring testes rescued GSH levels, restored spermatogenesis, and alleviated reproductive impairment. Collectively, our findings identify a previously unrecognized epitranscriptional mechanism by which paternal ZEA exposure transmits reproductive toxicity across generations via the METTL14-m6A-Thap1-GSH axis, providing a potential target for intervention against mycotoxin-induced male infertility.

articles.title: Single-cell Bioinformatics Analysis and In Vitro Validation Explore Core Genes and Signaling Pathways of Iron Metabolism in Fetal Left Heart Function Injury in Gestational Diabetes Mellitus.
articles.authors: Su Q, Chen J, Guo L
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) is a common metabolic disorder during pregnancy that significantly affects fetal cardiac development. However, the molecular mechanisms underlying iron metabolism-related pathways in GDM-induced fetal left heart dysfunction remain incompletely understood.
METHODS: This study employed single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) technology combined with bioinformatics analysis and published echocardiographic data validation to comprehensively characterize the cellular landscape and iron metabolism signatures in publicly available GDM fetal cardiac transcriptomic data from the GEO database (GSM5261695 and GSM5261697).
RESULTS: Analysis of 4,531 cells identified 17 distinct clusters comprising 9 major cardiac cell types. Cardiomyocytes exhibited the highest iron metabolism dysregulation scores. Ferroptosis pathway analysis revealed elevated GPX4 and SLC7A11 expression with concurrent ACSL4 downregulation in GDM samples. Clinical ultrasound validation demonstrated significant left ventricular dysfunction in GDM fetuses, including reduced ejection fraction and impaired diastolic function. RT-qPCR validation confirmed significant upregulation of GPX4 (2.45-fold), SLC7A11 (2.87-fold), and FTH1 (2.31-fold) in high glucose-treated cardiomyocytes, with concurrent ACSL4 downregulation (0.52-fold). GPX4 protein validation by immunofluorescence and Western blot further showed higher GPX4 signal in the OGD group and reduced GPX4 expression after GPX4 knockdown.
CONCLUSION: This study reveals that dysregulated iron metabolism and ferroptosis resistance in fetal cardiomyocytes serve as critical mechanisms underlying GDM-induced left heart dysfunction. The identification of cell type-specific iron metabolism signatures provides novel therapeutic targets for preventing and treating fetal cardiac complications in GDM pregnancies.

articles.title: Impact of sexological follow-up on the sexual function of patients treated with chemo-radiotherapy and brachytherapy for locally advanced cervical cancer: results of the prospective FEMINICOL study.
articles.journal: Radiotherapy and oncology : journal of the European Society for Therapeutic Radiology and Oncology
articles.authors: Menard J, Lusque A, Attal J et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Radiotherapy and brachytherapy (BT) for locally advanced cervical cancer (LACC) are associated with high rates of sexual morbidity, particularly vaginal stenosis. The prospective FEMINICOL study assessed sexual function and vaginal toxicity in patients treated with chemoradiotherapy (CRT) and image-guided adaptive BT, with systematic sexological support.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This single-centre prospective cohort study (NCT03956498) included patients treated with concomitant CRT and BT between October 2019 and December 2020. A certified sex therapist met each patient before BT, at 2 months and 1 year after treatment. The primary objective was to evaluate sexual function one year after treatment using the FSFI questionnaire.
RESULTS: Sixty patients were included in the study. Among patients who received clinical follow-up (54 at 2 months and 47 at 1 year), compliance with sexological follow-up was 98.1 % (53/54) at two months and 100 % at one year. Fifty-six patients with baseline evaluation and at least one post-treatment evaluation were analyzed. Median age was 54.5 years (31-77). At one year, 55.3 % of patients adhered to vaginal rehabilitation and 45.7 % were sexually active. Median FSFI score improved from 4 (range: 2-33.2) at baseline to 12.5 (2-34.8) at 1 year (paired test p < 0.001). Median sexual activity (QLQ-CX24) increased from 0 (0-66.7) to 33.3 (0-100) at 1 year (p < 0.001), while sexual anxiety remained stable (p = 0.93). At 1 year, Grade ≥ 3 vaginal toxicity occurred in 12.7 % of patients, mainly narrowing (8.5 %). Most patients (81.4 %) were satisfied with the sexological support.
CONCLUSION: In this prospective cohort, systematic sexological support during and after CRT and BT was feasible and was associated with encouraging compliance with vaginal rehabilitation and favorable sexual function outcomes over time.

articles.title: Baclofen Vaginal Suppositories in Chronic Pelvic Pain: a Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo Controlled Trial.
articles.journal: American journal of obstetrics and gynecology
articles.authors: Rothenberger RW, Abraham A, Gaskins JT et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pelvic floor muscle dysfunction is a common contributor to chronic pelvic pain (CPP), yet targeted treatment options remain limited.
OBJECTIVE: To determine whether baclofen vaginal suppositories in CPP is safe and effective when compared with placebo.
METHODS: This randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial compared 20mg baclofen vaginal suppositories to placebo suppositories nightly in women with CPP. Women older than18 years without allergy to baclofen or the suppository base were included if they had ≥40/100 mm pain on a visual analogue scale (VAS) with palpation of the obturator internus or levator ani on standardized pelvic exam. Improvement in this standardized pelvic exam 100mm VAS pain score represented the primary outcome. Participants completed Patient-Reported Outcomes Measurement Information System (PROMIS) pain interference, PROMIS global health, PROMIS sexual function at baseline, 4, and 8 weeks, with repeat pelvic examination at 8 weeks. The study was powered to detect the minimum clinically important difference (MCID) of 20mm on a 100mm VAS pain scale on a standardized pelvic floor muscle examination with a total sample size of 34, 17 in each group. Adverse events, pill count, and other treatments for CPP during the study period were collected. Differences between treatment groups were assessed using the Mann-Whitney test, and multiple imputation was used to account for missing data.
RESULTS: A total of 39 women were enrolled in the study with 37 randomized.19 patients received baclofen vaginal suppositories and 18 received placebo suppositories. Demographic data was similar between groups, with similar mean age (42.5 ± 12.5 baclofen vs 46.3 ± 12.2 placebo) and body mass index (29.4 ± 6.7 vs 29.8 ± 7.6). There was a statistically and clinically significant improvement in the primary outcome of change in the 100mm VAS pain score on pelvic floor muscle examination at 8 weeks relative to baseline in the baclofen group as compared to placebo (median improvement of 33.5 mm [IQR: 30 to 46.230.0] baclofen vs 7.2 mm [0.0 to 10.0] placebo, p=<0.001). Further, patient-reported overall 100mm VAS pain was also significantly improved with baclofen when compared to placebo (median improvement 32.0 mm [14.0 to 43.0] baclofen vs 0.0 mm [-6.5 to 11.8] placebo, p=0.001) (Figure 2). Other validated questionnaires demonstrated no significant differences between baclofen and placebo. Medication compliance, assessed using Spearman…

articles.title: Urgency urinary incontinence, one condition, or many? Cluster analysis of physiological variables in the Symptoms of Lower Urinary Tract Dysfunction Research Network (LURN) II cohort.
articles.journal: American journal of obstetrics and gynecology
articles.authors: DeLancey JOL, Andreev VP, Andrews C et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Our understanding of the pathophysiology of urgency urinary incontinence (UUI) remains incomplete, limiting treatment selection. Although UUI is considered to be multifactorial, evidence for which factors contribute is limited and there has tended to be a focus on bladder dysfunction, rather than taking a more multi-dimensional view.
OBJECTIVE: To identify physiologically distinct phenotypes of UUI by cluster analysis of bladder and urethral motor and sensory function tests.
METHODS: Secondary analysis of data from the Symptoms of Lower Urinary Tract Dysfunction Research Network (LURN) II Organ project which included 56 women with UUI and 31 asymptomatic controls was performed. Participants underwent urethral motor and sensory assessments, and rapid-fill cystometry before and after intravesical lidocaine instillation. Thirty-two physiological variables were analyzed using a validated, resampling-based consensus clustering pipeline. Cluster differences were assessed using ANOVA with false discovery rate correction ("Padj") and logistic regression.
RESULTS: Three distinct phenotypes were identified. Cluster A (n=15) showed detrusor overactivity during both saline and post-lidocaine fills, and reduced bladder sensation volumes (39-55% of controls) with normal urethral function. Cluster B (n=18) demonstrated significant lidocaine-related capacity increase of 138 mL (72%) (Padj ≤ 0.003 and Padj ≤ 0.0001, respectively) and a 30% decrease in maximum urethral closure pressure (Padj = 0.0076). Cluster C (n=23) exhibited minimal change in volumes post-lidocaine and a general lack of detrusor overactivity. Demographics and symptoms were similar across clusters. In regression analysis adjusting for age, BMI, and vaginal parity, primary predictors for A were detrusor overactivity (AUC = 0.95); for B, lidocaine-related capacity change (AUC = 0.92); and for C, low first desire to void (post-lidocaine) normalized by the functional (bladder diary) bladder capacity (AUC = 0.83).
CONCLUSIONS: In this exploratory analysis, clustering of physiological data identified three potential UUI phenotypes with differing bladder and urethral characteristics. If validated in larger cohorts, these phenotypes could guide trials testing whether phenotype-directed treatment improves outcomes.

articles.title: CTRP6-AdipoR1 signaling promotes testosterone production and alleviates obesity-associated male reproductive dysfunction.
articles.authors: Cheng CY, Yu XY, Mu Y
articles.abstract: Obesity is a major risk factor for male infertility, yet the molecular mechanisms linking obesity to impaired spermatogenesis remain poorly defined. Here we show that C1q/TNF-related protein 6 (CTRP6) is a Leydig cell-derived regulator of testosterone production whose local expression is reduced in obesity. High-fat diet (HFD) feeding selectively reduced CTRP6 expression and secretion in Leydig cells despite elevated circulating CTRP6 levels, indicating tissue-specific dysregulation within the testicular microenvironment. Leydig cell-specific CTRP6 overexpression markedly alleviated HFD-induced testicular atrophy, restored seminiferous tubule architecture, improved sperm parameters and reproductive outcomes, and rescued testosterone production. Conversely, Leydig cell-specific CTRP6 knockout impaired spermatogenesis and reduced male reproductive capacity under normal-diet conditions, supporting an important role for endogenous CTRP6 in reproductive homeostasis. The combined secretion, genetic and extracellular-protein experiments are consistent with an autocrine contribution. Transcriptomic analyses identified CYP51A1 as a candidate downstream mediator. CTRP6 associated with adiponectin receptor 1 (AdipoR1), and AdipoR1 knockdown attenuated rhCTRP6-associated changes in PI3K/Akt phosphorylation, SREBP2 and CYP51A1 abundance, cholesterol content and testosterone production. Notably, intratesticular administration of recombinant human CTRP6 (rhCTRP6) effectively rescued HFD-induced spermatogenic dysfunction in vivo. Together, these findings uncover a previously unrecognized local Leydig cell-derived CTRP6 signaling model linking obesity to male reproductive dysfunction.

articles.title: Health System and Contextual Barriers to Integrating Postpartum Family Planning Into Maternal Health Services in Northeast Ethiopia: A Qualitative Study.
articles.journal: Inquiry : a journal of medical care organization, provision and financing
articles.authors: Zikie DT, Abdulahi M, Debelew GT
articles.abstract: IntroductionPostpartum family planning (PPFP) use remains low in sub-Saharan Africa, particularly in Ethiopia. Low PPFP uptake is partly due to its limited integration with maternal health services. Understanding the barriers to PPFP service integration at health facilities and strengthening engagement with service providers, postpartum women, male partners, and community stakeholders could improve PPFP integration with maternal health services. This study explored health-system and contextual barriers to integrating postpartum family planning into maternal health services in northeast Ethiopia.MethodsA descriptive qualitative study was conducted from March to April 2023 in northeast Ethiopia. Data were collected from 33 participants through key informant interviews (healthcare providers and facility managers/coordinators) and focus group discussions (postpartum women, male partners, community leaders, and religious leaders). Participants were selected using heterogeneous purposive sampling to capture diverse perspectives. Semi-structured, pretested interview and discussion guides were used until data saturation was reached. Audio recordings were transcribed in Amharic, translated into English, coded, and analyzed inductively using conventional content analysis with ATLAS.ti 7 software.ResultsSix major categories were identified. The barriers included PPFP service-delivery barriers, poor client-centered PPFP counseling, knowledge, attitudes, and concerns about contraceptive methods, male-partner influence on family planning decisions, security problems and disruptions to reproductive health services, and community, religious, and peer support challenges for family planning services.ConclusionThe study highlights the need for strengthened counselling, supply chain resilience, and conflict-sensitive programming. Health facility-focused integrated interventions and community-based information, education, and communication are needed to improve postpartum family planning integration with maternal health services.

articles.title: Periconceptual Progesterone Use and Hypertensive Disorders of Pregnancy: A Population-Based Cohort Study.
articles.journal: BJOG : an international journal of obstetrics and gynaecology
articles.authors: Atkinson JA, Hiscock RJ, Forsythe A et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate whether periconceptual use of progesterone is associated with an altered risk of new-onset hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (gestational hypertension, preeclampsia, or superimposed preeclampsia).
DESIGN: Population-based cohort study using statewide pregnancy and birth data from Victoria, Australia, linked with hospital and medication prescribing data.
SETTING: Victoria, Australia (2009-2020).
POPULATION: Nulliparous women who gave birth between 2009 and 2020 in Victoria, Australia. Women with missing delivery dates, medicine dispensation dates, or who were exposed to progesterone in the second or third trimester were excluded.
METHODS: We compared nulliparous women exposed to progesterone in the periconceptual period (6 weeks preconception until the end of the first trimester) with those not exposed to progesterone. Inverse probability-weighted regression adjustment was used to control for confounding factors and investigate the effect of progesterone on the risk of preeclampsia (including superimposed preeclampsia) and gestational hypertension.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Development of preeclampsia or gestational hypertension.
RESULTS: Among 386 475 pregnancies, 5657 (1.5%) women used progesterone in the periconceptual period. Progesterone use was associated with a statistically significant reduction in the risk of any new onset hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (adjusted risk ratio [aRR] 0.81 [95% confidence interval [CI] 0.67, 0.98]; adjusted risk difference [aRD] -1.72% [95% CI -3.21%, -0.24%]). Investigating type of hypertension, we found progesterone use was associated with a 1.69% absolute reduced risk of gestational hypertension (aRR 0.60 [95% CI 0.43, 0.83]; aRD -1.69% [95% CI -2.52%, -0.86%]) but no significant change was observed for preeclampsia (aRR 0.97 [95% CI 0.75, 1.25]; aRD -0.13% [95% CI -1.49%, 1.23%]).
