Restricting our analyses to pregnancies conceived via assisted reproductive technology only, we found similar results, with a statistically significant reduction in the risk of gestational hypertension (aRR 0.80 [95% CI 0.67, 0.95]; aRD -1.02% [95% CI -1.73%, -0.30%]) but not preeclampsia (aRR 0.96 [95% CI 0.83, 1.11]; aRD -0.25% [95% CI -1.23%, 0.72%]).
CONCLUSIONS: Among 386 475 nulliparous women, we found periconceptual progesterone use to be associated with a statistically significant reduction in the risk of gestational hypertension, but not preeclampsia. However, these findings are unlikely to be…

articles.title: A one-step C-type natriuretic peptide, 17β-estradiol and amphiregulin workflow for bovine oocyte maturation.
articles.authors: Pytel AT, Tobolski D, Gajewski Z et al.
articles.abstract:
CONTEXT: C-type natriuretic peptide (CNP)-based pre-maturation can improve bovine oocyte developmental competence but adds a separate culture and transfer step to in vitro embryo production (IVP).
AIMS: To develop a one-step CNP and 17β-estradiol (E2) modification of conventional in vitro maturation (IVM), demonstrate its application, and assess timed amphiregulin (AREG) supplementation.
METHODS: Two experiments used 3182 abattoir-derived cumulus-oocyte complexes. Experiment 1 compared conventional 24-h IVM (control), CNP during recovery only (recovery-only), 6-h CNP-E2 pre-IVM followed by 24-h IVM (biphasic), and 24- or 30-h CNP-E2 IVM (one-step 24-h and one-step 30-h). Experiment 2 compared control, one-step 24-h, and one-step 24-h + AREG, with AREG added after 6 h. Cleavage and blastocyst development were assessed on Days 3 and 7-8, respectively.
KEY RESULTS: In Experiment 1, biphasic and one-step 24-h increased Day 8 total blastocyst yield relative to control (26.5% vs 19.7%, P = 0.022; and 25.7% vs 19.7%, P = 0.042, respectively). In Experiment 2, one-step 24-h increased Day 7 total blastocyst yield (31.6% vs 23.8%; P = 0.017). One-step 24-h + AREG increased Day 8 hatching blastocysts relative to control (16.0% vs 9.9%; P = 0.013) but not relative to one-step 24-h.
CONCLUSIONS: Direct CNP-E2 supplementation during 24-h IVM eliminated the separate pre-IVM transfer while improving blastocyst endpoints relative to conventional IVM.
IMPLICATIONS: The modification preserves a conventional 24-h IVM schedule; however, external validation using embryo-quality and post-transfer outcomes is warranted.

articles.title: Digital patient advocacy and Black maternal health: Reimagining communication infrastructure in prenatal and postpartum care.
articles.authors: Walker KL
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To examine how digital patient advocacy tools may address communication barriers that contribute to Black maternal health disparities in the United States.
METHODS: This discussion paper draws on interdisciplinary literature in maternal health equity, health communication, and digital health technologies. Sources were identified through targeted searches of peer-reviewed journals, public health reports, and policy analyses.
RESULTS: Communication failures between patients and providers are a documented contributor to preventable maternal deaths, and Black women are disproportionately affected. Digital advocacy tools that support pre-visit preparation, real-time symptom documentation, and post-visit follow-up represent a promising but underexplored intervention.
CONCLUSION: Digital patient advocacy platforms, including the Patient Advocate App, may help mitigate communication barriers that contribute to racial disparities in maternal outcomes. Equity-centered implementation and rigorous evaluation are essential.
PRACTICE IMPLICATIONS: Clinicians and health systems should evaluate digital advocacy tools as a supplement to in-person advocacy in prenatal and postpartum care, with co-design involving Black patients and testing for usability, accuracy, and equitable access. Future research must evaluate whether these tools reduce disparities in clinical responsiveness.

articles.title: Ovarian response to FSH differs by ethnicity: evidence from clinical outcomes and genetic clustering.
articles.authors: Neves AR, Casarini L, Carretta C et al.
articles.abstract:
RESEARCH QUESTION: Does the ovarian response and the distribution of genetic variants in genes involved in folliculogenesis and steroidogenesis differ according to patients' ethnicity?
DESIGN: This was a post-hoc analysis of a prospective, multicentre, multiethnic study including Vietnamese and White patients aged less than 38 years with normal ovarian reserve undergoing their first or second ovarian stimulation cycle. All participants received a fixed dose of 150 IU recombinant FSH in a short antagonist protocol. Genotyping was performed for 67 predefined genetic variants related to folliculogenesis, steroidogenesis and folate metabolism. Ovarian response parameters were compared between ethnic groups.
RESULTS: A total of 368 participants were included. Compared with White participants, Vietnamese patients had a shorter duration of stimulation (8.86 ± 1.24 versus 9.60 ± 1.45 days; P < 0.001), lower consumption of recombinant FSH (1329.00 ± 186.64 versus 1439.29 ± 217.30 IU; P < 0.001) and higher oestradiol concentrations on the day of triggering (2808.62 ± 1963.27 versus 2089.29 ± 1175.05 pg/ml; P < 0.001), despite a lower number of growing follicles (15.30 ± 4.55 versus 17.58 ± 6.98; P < 0.001). The number of oocytes retrieved did not differ between groups. Principal component analysis based on single-nucleotide polymorphism frequencies showed a separation of individuals consistent with self-reported ethnicity.
CONCLUSIONS: Ovarian response to exogenous FSH differs between Vietnamese and White patients with normal ovarian reserve. Variations in the distribution of genetic variants involved in folliculogenesis and steroidogenesis may partly contribute to these differences and provide a basis for future pharmacogenetic models and the progressive individualization of ovarian stimulation strategies.

articles.title: The assessment of General Movements of term small for gestational age infants in comparison to term appropriate for gestational age infants in early infancy: A prospective observational study.
articles.authors: Modak A, Mukherjee S, Das AK
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIM: Term small for gestational age (SGA) infants carry a higher burden of adverse neurodevelopmental outcomes than term appropriate for gestational age (AGA) infants, yet apparently healthy term SGA infants rarely receive structured neurodevelopmental follow-up in resource-limited settings. A simple, low cost reliable tool may be used to assess the neurodevelopmental outcome of high risk infants in Low and Middle Income Countries (LMIC). The Prechtl General Movement Assessment (GMA) is a validated, non-invasive, easy-to-go tool for early prediction of neurodevelopmental trajectory. The study was conducted to compare General Movement Optimality Score-Revised (GMOS-R) at term age and Motor Optimality Score-Revised (MOS-R) at fidgety age between term SGA and AGA infants, and to study the influence of antenatal risk factors on general movements in SGA infants.
METHODS: In this hospital-based prospective observational study conducted at a tertiary teaching hospital in Eastern India, term-born infants were enrolled and classified as SGA or AGA using Fenton's growth chart. Video-recorded general movements were scored using GMOS-R at 37+0-41+6 weeks postmenstrual age and MOS-R was scored at 9-20 weeks post-term (fidgety) age. Group comparisons were done using Pearson's Chi-square and Mann-Whitney U tests, with p < 0.05 considered significant.
RESULTS: Among 60 enrolled infants, 50 infants (25 SGA, 25 AGA) completed follow-up. Poor repertoire movements (GMOS-R < 29) were observed in 36% of infants overall (10 SGA vs 8 AGA; p = 0.56). At fidgety age, all infants displayed fidgety movements; MOS-R scores were optimal (≥25) in 76% of infants, with no significant difference between SGA and AGA groups (p = 1.0). Pregnancy-induced hypertension/preeclampsia (20% vs 12%) and oligohydramnios (12% vs 0%) were more frequent in SGA mothers, though not statistically significant. No significant association was found between antenatal risk factors and GMOS-R and MOS-R scores in either group.
CONCLUSION: GMOS-R and MOS-R did not differ significantly between term SGA and AGA infants, although SGA infants showed a trend toward more poor repertoire (PR) movements at term age. Routine General Movement Assessment (GMA) in apparently healthy looking term SGA infants may help in early identification of subtle motor differences that may manifest in form of cognitive/ learning / behavioural problems in later age. So timely intervention can reduce the adverse…

articles.title: The role of circCHD2 in gestational diabetes mellitus-induced endothelial dysfunction in human umbilical vein endothelial cells.
articles.authors: Bao Y, Li Q, Huang J et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The risk of cardiovascular diseases is high in the offspring of patients developing gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM). However, it remains unclear how the intrauterine hyperglycemic environment of GDM patients impacts vascular endothelial dysfunction in their offspring. This study centers on GDM-induced endothelial dysfunction to explore the regulatory mechanism of circRNA chromodomain helicase DNA binding protein 2 (circCHD2)/miR-33b-3p/UNC-51-like kinase 1 (ULK1) axis in this regard.
METHODS: The expression levels of circCHD2, ULK1, and miR-33b-3p in human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs) extracted from patients with GDM and in high glucose (HG, 25 mM)-exposed HUVECs were detected using the qRT-PCR and Western blot. HUVEC function was assessed using CCK-8, wound healing, and tube formation assays. Mitochondrial autophagy in HUVECs was determined by transmission electron microscopy and dual fluorescent staining for mitochondria and lysosomes.
RESULTS: In HUVECs derived from GDM and in HG-induced HUVECs, the expressions of circCHD2 and ULK1 were upregulated, while the expression of miR-33b-3p was downregulated. Moreover, alterations in mitophagy markers alongside activation of the PINK1/Parkin pathway were detected in these cells. Silencing circCHD2 or overexpressing miR-33b-3p enhanced the proliferation, wound-closure, and tube-forming abilities of HUVECs under HG conditions, and simultaneously blocked the PINK1/Parkin pathway. However, both the mitophagy inducer CCCP and the downregulation of miR-33b-3p counteracted the regulatory effects of circCHD2 silencing on HG-induced HUVEC dysfunction. In contrast, the overexpression of ULK1 reversed the inhibitory effect of miR-33b-3p overexpression on HG-induced HUVEC dysfunction.
CONCLUSION: The regulatory function of the circCHD2/miR-33b-3p/ULK1 axis in the HG-induced dysfunction of HUVECs might be related to the activation of the PINK1/Parkin signaling pathway.

articles.title: Magnesium gluconate protects syncytiotrophoblast plasma membranes from hypoxia-induced lipid peroxidation and loss of Ca2+-ATPase activity in human term placental explants.
articles.authors: Rangel H, Piñero S, Rojas D et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Preeclampsia is a pregnancy-specific syndrome in which placental hypoxia and oxidative stress damage the syncytiotrophoblast (STB). Magnesium sulfate (MgSO4), the standard agent for seizure prophylaxis in severe disease, requires intravenous administration and has a narrow therapeutic window. Magnesium gluconate (Mg-gluconate) is well absorbed orally and has greater antioxidant capacity than MgSO4 in non-placental experimental systems, yet its effects on the STB plasma membrane are unknown.
METHODS: Human term placental explants were cultured under normoxia (8% O2), hypoxia (2% O2), or hypoxia with 2 mM Mg-gluconate for 18 h, after which microvillous (MVM) and basal (BM) plasma membranes were isolated. Explant viability was confirmed by hCG release under all conditions. Lipid peroxidation (conjugated dienes and TBARS), plasma membrane Ca2+-ATPase (PMCA) activity, PMCA-4 and HIF-1α protein expression, membrane lipid composition, and lipid molar ratios were measured.
RESULTS: Hypoxia increased lipid peroxidation in both membranes, raised HIF-1α expression, increased cholesterol and decreased total phospholipids, and shifted lipid ratios toward a more rigid bilayer; PMCA activity fell in both MVM and BM while PMCA-4 expression was unchanged, indicating reduced catalytic turnover rather than reduced pump abundance. Mg-gluconate prevented each of these changes, preserving membrane composition and fluidity, maintaining PMCA activity, and normalizing HIF-1α expression.
CONCLUSION: Mg-gluconate protects the STB plasma membrane against hypoxia-induced oxidative and structural damage, supporting further evaluation of oral Mg-gluconate as a pathology-directed intervention in preeclampsia.

articles.title: Survival and lineage marker acquisition by wisent (Bison bonasus) somatic cells in the bovine embryonic environment.
articles.authors: Ziętek MM, Sampino S, Bernat A
articles.abstract: The wisent (Bison bonasus) survived near-extinction in the twentieth century but remains genetically vulnerable. Induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC) technology may support genetic rescue; however, iPSC derivation in Bovidae remains challenging. Here, we investigated whether bovine preimplantation embryos provide a permissive environment for wisent somatic cells expressing reprogramming factors. Wisent adult fibroblasts were engineered to express either the fluorescent reporter mKO2 alone (BAF-KO2) or mKO2 together with six reprogramming factors (OCT4, SOX2, KLF4, c-MYC, NANOG, and LIN28; BAF-6TF-KO2) delivered using the PiggyBac transposon system. Five wisent cells were microinjected into eight-cell-stage bovine embryos produced by in vitro fertilization. A subset of BAF-6TF-KO2 cells was additionally cultured under pluripotency-promoting conditions before injection (BAF-6TF-KO2-IND). Injected embryos developed to the blastocyst stage at rates comparable to sham-injected controls. mKO2-positive wisent cells were detected in 75% of blastocysts injected with BAF-KO2 and 91% of those injected with BAF-6TF-KO2 (p < 0.05). Cells expressing reprogramming factors localized within the embryo significantly more often than controls. Most wisent cells showed limited proliferation and signs of compromised nuclear integrity. However, a subset of BAF-6TF-KO2 cells expressed CDX2, suggesting responsiveness to trophectoderm-specifying signals. These findings show that bovine preimplantation embryos can accommodate wisent somatic cells up to the blastocyst stage and suggest that reprogramming-factor expression improves their retention and internal localization. This study provides a foundation for further development of interspecies embryo complementation approaches in Bovidae for conservation purposes.

articles.title: Menopausal symptom severity, perceived stress, and autonomic stress response: insights from the cross-sectional Frauenherzen study.
articles.authors: Müeller YM, Pavicic E, Schürch E et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Menopause marks a major life transition. Menopausal symptoms may act as stressors, while stress may exacerbate symptom burden. This study examined the associations between menopausal symptom severity and both perceived and autonomic stress, and evaluated whether stress levels differed across reproductive stages among midlife women.
STUDY DESIGN: This cross-sectional study included 253 apparently healthy women aged 40-68 years (M = 52.14, SD = 6.84) recruited in Switzerland. Autonomic stress was measured continuously over seven days using a wearable device (a smartwatch that captured physiological data).
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Menopausal symptoms were assessed using the Menopause Rating Scale II, perceived stress was assessed with the Perceived Stress Scale 10, and a wearable-derived stress score was calculated using an algorithm based on heart rate variability that reflects autonomic nervous system activity.
RESULTS: Pearson correlations revealed a significant positive association between menopausal symptom severity and perceived stress (r = 0.42, p < 0.001), with the strongest association observed for psychological symptoms. No significant association was found between symptom severity and the wearable-derived stress score. Analyses of covariance showed that perceived stress and wearable-derived stress scores did not differ significantly across reproductive stages.
CONCLUSIONS: Perceived stress was associated with menopausal symptom severity, whereas stress levels did not differ significantly across reproductive stages. Interventions focusing on symptom management and coping strategies may be helpful to support women in relation to perceived stress and quality of life during menopause.

articles.title: A phase I trial of intravenous vesicular stomatitis virus expressing thyroidal sodium iodide symporter (NIS) and human interferon beta (hIFNβ) in metastatic or recurrent endometrial cancer.
articles.authors: Warring SK, Peng KW, Atherton PJ et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: We report the results of a Phase I trial of intravenous (IV) vesicular stomatitis virus (VSV) engineered to express human interferon beta (hIFNβ) and thyroidal sodium iodide symporter (NIS) in patients with stage IV or recurrent endometrial cancer (EC).
METHODS: Eligible patients with stage IV or recurrent EC with largest tumor diameter ≤ 5 cm were enrolled and received a single IV infusion of VSV-hIFNβ-NIS in a standard '3 + 3' dose escalation. Five dose-levels were planned. Primary endpoint was determination of the maximum tolerated dose (MTD). Secondary endpoints included pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, tumor response, and immune correlates. An exploratory post-hoc analysis evaluated clinical responses to subsequent immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI)-based therapies.
RESULTS: From 9/15/2017-1/10/23, 21 eligible patients were treated. One patient at DL2 experienced grade 3 dehydration associated with cytokine release syndrome (CRS) and one experienced transient grade 4 asymptomatic lymphopenia, prompting protocol modification of the DLT definition. One of six patients at DL4 experienced grade 3 delirium meeting DLT criteria. Dose escalation to DL5 was not feasible because of investigational agent production limitations; MTD was not reached. The most common treatment related AEs were transient hematologic toxicities, liver enzyme elevations, and CRS. At day 29, 8 patients had progressive disease (PD); 1 entered hospice due to PD before day 29. Two patients had stable disease for at least 6 months following VSV-hIFNβ-NIS. Of the 15 patients who received subsequent ICI-based therapy following VSV-hIFNβ-NIS, 4 had durable SD with a median follow up of 40.4 (95% CI 30.4-not reached) months.
CONCLUSIONS: IV VSV-hIFNβ-NIS had an acceptable safety profile in patients with advanced or recurrent EC. Further investigation of VSV-hIFNβ-NIS, particularly in combination with immune checkpoint blockade, is warranted.

articles.title: Novel orthotopic uterine leiomyosarcoma model demonstrated enhanced tumor growth, metastasis, and chemosensitivity compared to subcutaneous counterparts.
articles.authors: Doherty ME, Malik M, Otsuka Y et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Uterine leiomyosarcoma (uLMS) maintains a poor prognosis due to its aggressive behavior and limited therapeutic response. Preclinical progress is severely hindered by traditional subcutaneous models that often fail to metastasize, despite one-third of uLMS patients displaying metastases at diagnosis. This study aimed to establish a reproducible, physiologically accurate orthotopic uLMS murine model that faithfully recapitulates disease progression and chemotherapeutic response.
METHODS: Primary subcutaneous tumors were established via SK-LMS-1 cell injections in NOD/SCID mice. Harvested xenografts were surgically implanted heterotopically (subcutaneous flank) or orthotopically (uterine myometrium). Eight days post-implantation, mice were randomized to receive intraperitoneal doxorubicin (1.2 mg/kg twice weekly) or vehicle control for 3 weeks. Tumor growth was tracked longitudinally via MRI (orthotopic) or caliper measurement (subcutaneous). Immunohistochemistry evaluated tumor vitality, microenvironment hypoxia, vascular density, and metastatic spread.
RESULTS: Orthotopic tumors exhibited significantly accelerated growth kinetics compared to subcutaneous counterparts. This expansion was supported by co-option of host uterine vasculature, resulting in ample tumor perfusion, suppressed tissue hypoxia, and robust proliferation. Crucially, 37% of primary orthotopic tumors developed spontaneous, multi-organ metastases to pulmonary, omental, and intraperitoneal sites by 4 weeks. Orthotopic tumors demonstrated heightened sensitivity to doxorubicin, achieving a 55% volume reduction compared to 44% in subcutaneous controls, mediated by superior intratumoral drug delivery supported by increased cleaved caspase-3-dependent apoptosis.
CONCLUSIONS: Surgical orthotopic xenografting recapitulates clinical uLMS, demonstrating site-dependent vascular co-option, spontaneous systemic metastasis, and enhanced chemosensitivity. By mimicking physiological characteristics of human uLMS, this orthotopic model offers significant potential for enhancing understanding of uLMS and evaluating novel therapies.

articles.title: Exploring normality: Mapping the endometrial microbiome in healthy reproductive-aged women from Argentina.
articles.authors: Nazario C, Solari L, Sciara M et al.
articles.abstract: The human microbiome varies according to individual and geographic characteristics. The endometrial microbiome plays a relevant role in reproductive physiology; however, data from healthy South American populations remain scarce. This prospective observational study aimed to characterize the endometrial microbiome in healthy reproductive-aged women from Rosario, Argentina and to establish a regional baseline for future research. A total of 100 healthy women aged 22-50 years from Rosario, Argentina, were included. Endometrial samples were obtained by aspiration biopsy during the follicular phase of the menstrual cycle or under hormonal contraception. Microbiome analysis was performed using 16S rRNA gene sequencing targeting the V4 region on the Illumina NextSeq 500/550 platform (2×150bp). Bioinformatic analysis was carried out in QIIME2. Of the 98 samples successfully amplified, 86 met quality criteria and were included in the final analysis. The endometrial microbiome was predominantly composed of Firmicutes, particularly members of the Lactobacillaceae family. The most abundant species were Lactobacillus iners and Lactobacillus helveticus/crispatus. No significant differences in alpha diversity were observed among age groups; however, a progressive increase in Gardnerella, Prevotella, and Megasphaera was detected with advancing age. This study provides the first regional characterization of the normal endometrial microbiome in healthy Argentine women and establishes a reference framework for future studies addressing endometrial dysbiosis and reproductive disorders.

articles.title: Fertility rates of leatherback sea turtle (Dermochelys coriacea) eggs in southeastern Florida, USA.
articles.authors: Turla E, Wyneken J
articles.abstract: Leatherback sea turtle (Dermochelys coriacea) nests have highly variable hatching success that trends lower than that of other sea turtle species. This egg failure is the result of either embryo mortality or infertility. To investigate fertility rates of leatherback turtle eggs, we used non-lethal methods in a controlled ex situ incubation study. We collected 30 freshly laid eggs from 19 leatherback nests (n = 570 eggs) in Boca Raton, Jupiter, and Juno Beach, Florida, USA in 2023 and 2024. Using multiple criteria to identify fertilization (i.e., visualization of eggshell chalking and membrane vascularization, egg necropsy, and investigation of the perivitelline membrane (PVM) using fluorescent microscopy) we found a fertility rate of 97.5%. This high level suggests that infertility is not currently a major contributor to egg failure in this species and nesting population. Fertility rates did not vary significantly among females, ranging from 86.7% to 100%. Additionally, sperm were counted on the PVMs of fertilized and unfertilized eggs; there was no significant difference in sperm counts, suggesting that this metric cannot be used as a reliable method to determine fertility status. This experiment is the first to quantify fertility rates in sea turtle eggs using fluorescent microscopy techniques in a controlled experiment and to evaluate sperm counts of fertile and infertile eggs. These findings provide insight into the reproductive biology of leatherback sea turtles, suggesting that low hatching success in Florida's nesting population is driven primarily by factors other than infertility and highlighting the importance of understanding the mechanisms underlying embryonic failure.

articles.title: Trends in common laboratory markers during pregnancy in women with IBD in clinical remission.
articles.authors: Gottlieb ZS, Glamour B, Helmus D et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Physiologic pregnancy changes can alter commonly monitored laboratory values and mimic active inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), complicating prenatal disease monitoring. Biomarker trajectories in women with IBD in remission are not well established. We aimed to characterize trimester-specific changes in key biomarkers among women with IBD in remission before and throughout pregnancy.
METHODS: We performed a retrospective review of pregnant women with IBD in remission enrolled in a prospective preconception/pregnancy registry. Eligible patients had laboratory data from the preconception period and at least 1 trimester (first trimester [T1], second trimester [T2], or third trimester [T3]). Parameters included complete blood counts, albumin, C-reactive protein, erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR), iron studies, and fecal calprotectin (FC). Changes from preconception were assessed using Wilcoxon signed rank tests and McNemar's test when applicable.
RESULTS: Sixty-eight pregnancies from 61 women were included (68.9% Crohn's disease, 27.9% ulcerative colitis; median age 33 years; 83.8% on biologics). Compared with preconception, ESR and white blood cell count rose across trimesters (ESR PT2T3 < .001; white blood cell PT1-T3 < .001). Hemoglobin, hematocrit, platelets, and albumin declined significantly, particularly in T2/T3 (all P ≤ .008). C-reactive protein rose during all trimesters (PT1 = .003; PT2, T3 < .001), whereas FC remained stable and within normal range throughout pregnancy (all P > .05). Most biomarkers trended toward baseline postpartum.
CONCLUSIONS: In pregnant women with IBD in remission, most laboratory changes appear physiologic, requiring cautious interpretation. FC was the only stable biomarker throughout pregnancy and remains the most reliable marker of inflammation during this period. These trimester-specific data may improve interpretation of biomarkers in pregnant patients with IBD.

articles.title: Miscarriage Risk Prediction for Women With Polycystic Ovary Syndrome Who Achieve Clinical Pregnancy After Fresh Embryo Transfer: Multicenter Development, Geographic External Validation, and Prospective Temporal Validation Study.
articles.authors: Tong J, Zhang Y, Liu Y et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Women with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) who achieve clinical pregnancy following fresh in vitro fertilization (IVF)/intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI) carry an elevated miscarriage risk. However, individualized risk stratification after clinical pregnancy confirmation but before outcome determination remains challenging in clinical practice.
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to develop, externally and prospectively validate over time, and interpret a machine learning-based risk stratification model for women with PCOS who had achieved a confirmed clinical pregnancy after fresh IVF/ICSI.
METHODS: This multicenter study included 8911 clinical pregnancy IVF/ICSI cycles across development (n=7241; miscarriages: n=973), external validation (n=1170; miscarriages: n=146), and prospective temporal validation (n=500; miscarriages: n=62) cohorts. Prespecified predictors contained no observed missing values; training-fold median imputation was kept only as a leakage-safe fallback. A total of 13 candidate machine learning and traditional statistical algorithms were compared internally using repeated stratified 5-fold cross-validation (5 repeats) within the development cohort; preprocessing and hyperparameter tuning were performed exclusively in training folds. A prelocked Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) model was carried forward unchanged for external and prospective temporal validation. Cross-fitted logistic recalibration of averaged XGBoost out-of-fold probabilities was evaluated as a secondary development-sample diagnostic analysis. Model performance encompassed discrimination, precision-recall, calibration, threshold-based metrics, decision curve analysis, risk stratification, and Shapley additive explanations-based interpretability.
RESULTS: Miscarriage rates were 13.4% (973/7241), 12.5% (146/1170), and 12.4% (62/500) for the development, external validation, and prospective temporal validation cohorts, respectively. In repeated cross-validation, XGBoost (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve [AUC] 0.885, 95% CI 0.874-0.896) and LightGBM (AUC 0.882, 95% CI 0.871-0.893) showed comparable discrimination; the paired XGBoost-LightGBM DeLong test was not significant (Holm-adjusted P=.07). Raw XGBoost out-of-fold probabilities overestimated absolute risk (mean predicted risk 30.3% vs observed risk 13.4%); cross-fitted recalibration within the development cohort improved calibration but was not propagated to validation cohorts. The…

articles.title: Effects of Lactobacillus crispatus-Containing Probiotics and Metformin on Insulin Resistance, Inflammation, and Gut Microbiome in Polycystic Ovary Syndrome: Protocol for an Open-Label Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.authors: H B, Sahu S, Balakrishnan D et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) affects 9% to 12% of reproductive-age women worldwide, with higher prevalence reported in India. Its pathophysiology involves insulin resistance, hyperandrogenism, and chronic low-grade inflammation, increasingly linked to gut dysbiosis and lipopolysaccharide-driven toll-like receptor 4 signaling. Elevated calprotectin and suppressed acylated ghrelin (AGH) reflect this inflammatory-metabolic disruption. While metformin remains standard therapy, it does not address underlying gut dysbiosis. Lactobacillus crispatus, with its antibacterial and immunomodulatory properties, is a promising but untested gut-targeted adjunct. This trial evaluates whether combining metformin with L. crispatus supplementation improves metabolic and inflammatory outcomes beyond either therapy alone.
OBJECTIVE: This study aims to compare probiotic, metformin, and combination therapy for reducing insulin resistance in PCOS over 12 weeks and assess their effects on gut barrier integrity, microbiome composition, hyperandrogenemia, glycemic control, and clinical outcomes.
METHODS: This open-label randomized, hospital-based trial at the All India Institute of Medical Sciences, Bhubaneswar, will assess the effects of probiotic and/or metformin therapy in women aged 18 to 40 years diagnosed with PCOS per Rotterdam criteria. A total of 135 participants will be randomized equally into 3 groups: probiotics only, metformin only, and combination therapy. The 3-month intervention includes metformin (1000 mg per day) and a specified L. crispatus-containing probiotic (2 capsules per day). The primary outcome is the change in Homeostatic Model Assessment for Insulin Resistance (HOMA-IR). Key secondary outcomes include changes in serum and fecal calprotectin, AGH, total testosterone, and fecal microbiome profile.
RESULTS: Participant recruitment began in January 2026. As of August 30, 2026, 26 of the planned 135 participants had been enrolled. Enrollment and data collection are projected to conclude by December 2026; statistical analysis will begin after database lock, with study completion anticipated by June 2027 and publication targeted for mid- to late 2027.
CONCLUSIONS: This trial will provide critical, mechanistic evidence on whether the targeted action of L. crispatus can work additively with metformin to heal the intestinal mucosal barrier, arrest systemic endotoxemia, and rescue disrupted gut-brain-endocrine signaling. By validating this novel…

articles.title: Nicardipine for the Treatment of Severe Hypertension in Pregnancy: An Updated Review.
articles.authors: Nij Bijvank Md SWA, Duvekot Md PhD JJ
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: To reduce morbidity (and mortality) due to severe hypertension in pregnancy by searching the most effective and safe treatment.
OBJECTIVE: Update of our review (2010) on efficacy and safety of intravenous nicardipine for treatment of severe hypertension in pregnancy.
EVIDENCE ACQUISITION: Articles were identified through electronic databases (Medline and Cochrane). Date of search: January 2010 to September 2025. Following search terms were used: pregnancy, severe hypertension, and nicardipine. Included women had chronic or gestational hypertension with or without marked proteinuria. Primary outcomes: reduction of systolic/diastolic and/or mean arterial pressure, time needed to target blood pressure, severe maternal (hypotension, tachycardia), severe fetal (CTG abnormalities needing direct intervention), and side effects.
RESULTS: Five studies were added to the original review. Results of 1125 patients were available. All women had a significant reduction of both diastolic and systolic blood pressures. Treatment resulted in a success rate of 99.2%. Time until successful treatment was short with a median of 37 minutes. Comparison of nicardipine versus labetalol showed a significantly greater reduction of blood pressure and a shorter time to success for nicardipine. No severe maternal or fetal side effects were recorded.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: This updated review strengthens our conclusions of 2010: nicardipine is a very effective therapy for the treatment of severe hypertension in pregnancy and may be a better alternative to other available treatment options. More studies are needed to provide safety aspects of nicardipine compared with other agents. Apparently, this is dependent on political choices on the distribution of budgetary scarcity.

articles.title: A Review of Current Management Strategies for Hypoactive Sexual Desire Disorder in Postmenopausal Patients.
articles.authors: Darivemula S, Moreno C, Mateas CI et al.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Hypoactive sexual desire disorder is one of the most prevalent concerns among postmenopausal patients. There is a lack of consolidated information on current treatments, both FDA-approved and off-label, risks, and benefits for routine clinical use.
OBJECTIVE: To review current evidence on diagnosis and treatments for HSDD in the postmenopausal population and to offer practical advice for use in clinical counseling.
EVIDENCE ACQUISITION: A PubMed search was performed using appropriate keywords to identify and evaluate journal articles focused on this subject. Current guidelines and recommendations were obtained from the websites of national and international organizations.
RESULTS: There is a dearth of information on current and practical screening tools, medical treatments, and nonmedical treatment options specifically designed and validated for the postmenopausal population. In addition, studies involving postmenopausal patients with HSDD are limited in diversity of enrollment and, therefore, generalizability to the diverse US population.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Health care professionals providing care for postmenopausal patients with HSDD should utilize screening tools to identify HSDD and approach their clinical counseling with a patient-centered focus. This counseling should include resources for supplies, risks, and benefits of each treatment option, and a review of any financial barriers to accessing treatments. This review suggests best practices to improve diagnosis, treatment, and counseling around HSDD specifically in this vulnerable population.

articles.title: The Expanding Role of the Physician Informaticist in Obstetrics and Gynecology: Bridging Digital Innovation and Clinical Care.
articles.authors: Kernberg A, Nguyen TA
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Digital transformation has fundamentally reshaped obstetrics and gynecology (OB/GYN). Electronic health records (EHRs), clinical decision support systems (CDSS), telehealth, and artificial intelligence (AI) are now central to care delivery. Physician informaticists uniquely bridge clinical expertise with health information technology to optimize safety, quality, and equity in women's health.
OBJECTIVE: To synthesize current evidence regarding the roles, impact, and competencies of physician informaticists in OB/GYN.
EVIDENCE ACQUISITION: Literature from 2019 to 2026 was reviewed, including studies on clinical informatics, AI-augmented CDSS, predictive modeling, and digital patient communication in OB/GYN.
RESULTS: Physician informaticists improve workflow efficiency, reduce errors, and enhance guideline adherence. In OB/GYN, informatics leadership supports these goals through CDSS, predictive modeling, and digital patient communication. AI-driven CDSS demonstrate growing utility in pregnancy care, including diagnostic support, risk prediction, and therapeutic recommendations, though implementation gaps and bias remain. Machine learning models show promise in predicting obstetric interventions such as labor induction. In addition, large language models (LLMs) can generate accurate and relevant responses to gynecologic patient questions, though limitations include readability and safety oversight.
CONCLUSIONS: Physician informaticists are essential to modern OB/GYN practice, particularly as AI and predictive analytics become embedded in care delivery. While strong evidence supports informatics interventions in safety and quality improvement, emerging AI applications require rigorous validation, governance, and equity-focused implementation.

articles.title: Evaluating Frontline Health Workers' Responses to Patient Inquiries With and Without Large Language Model Support in Nigeria: Observational Study.
articles.authors: Moosa Munnee M, Malumi O, Chinedu S et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Frontline health workers in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) often face barriers that compromise care quality, including limited training, high patient loads, inadequate access to updated clinical guidance, and resource constraints. Working in underserved settings further exacerbates challenges to providing accurate, complete, and empathetic responses. Addressing these gaps requires innovative tools to support FLWs in real time.
OBJECTIVE: This study aims to evaluate the effectiveness of ChatGPT-3.5 (OpenAI) in enhancing the quality of FLWs' responses to health inquiries in Lagos, Nigeria.
METHODS: In this observational study, 36 licensed frontline health workers (doctors, nurses, and community health workers) practicing general or primary care in Lagos, Nigeria, generated responses to 15 patient-generated health questions covering maternal and neonatal health, family planning, and sexually transmitted infections. Each FLW produced responses using their own knowledge and available resources (human-only) and with ChatGPT-3.5 assistance (GPT-aided). A panel of 4 clinicians evaluated responses using a 5-point Likert scale for accuracy, empathy, contextualization, completeness, safety, and overall preference. In addition, 8 nonclinician health seekers assessed a subset of responses across 3 themes: Caring, Trust, and Ease of Understanding.
RESULTS: Across 1080 responses from 36 frontline health workers, GPT-aided responses significantly outperformed human-only responses on all clinician-rated metrics (P<.001), with the largest gains observed in completeness, empathy, and overall preference, particularly among community health extension workers (CHEWs). Nonclinician evaluators also favored GPT-aided responses across all themes, with a strong preference for trust.
CONCLUSIONS: This study provides empirical evidence that a large language model (ChatGPT-3.5) enhances the completeness, empathy, and perceived trust of responses by frontline health workers in Lagos, Nigeria. These findings underscore the potential of integrating ChatGPT-3.5 to strengthen health care delivery in resource-limited settings, highlighting the necessity for capacity building and further investigation into its safe, equitable, and effective implementation.

articles.title: The Effect of Health Anxiety on Cervical Cancer Attitudes and Beliefs.
articles.authors: Muslu A, Kilci Erciyas Ş
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To determine the relationship between health anxiety and health beliefs regarding cervical cancer and Papanicolaou (Pap) testing in women presenting to gynecology outpatient clinics.
PARTICIPANTS AND SETTING: Women who applied to the gynecology outpatient clinics of a university hospital in the Aegean region of Türkiye from June 2023 to February 2024 were recruited for the study.
METHODOLOGIC APPROACH: This descriptive cross-sectional study used face-to-face administration of an individual identification form, the Health Belief Model Scale for Cervical Cancer and the Pap Smear Test, and the Turkish version of the Short Health Anxiety Inventory. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, one-way analysis of variance, and Pearson correlation analysis (p < 0.05).
FINDINGS: Among 215 women, 60% had not undergone a Pap test in the past five years. Higher income perception was significantly associated with greater perceived benefits (F = 18.18, p < 0.001) and health motivation (F = 12.333, p < 0.001), as was higher education level. Positive correlations were found between physical symptom hypersensitivity and perceived seriousness (r = 0.177, p = 0.009), perceived benefits (r = 0.151, p = 0.027), and health motivation (r = 0.198, p = 0.004).
IMPLICATIONS FOR NURSING: Nurses should prioritize educating women about cervical cancer symptoms and risk factors, and the importance of regular Pap testing. Because higher scores on the physical symptom hypersensitivity subdimension of the Short Health Anxiety Inventory were associated with greater perceived seriousness and motivation for cervical cancer screening, nurses should assess women's anxiety levels and provide supportive counseling to reduce fear and encourage preventive behaviors.

articles.title: Targeting hormone conversion through dietary fiber improves polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome.
articles.authors: Qi X, Chen H, Nie Q et al.
articles.abstract: Excessive androgens serve as a primary driver for many phenotypic features of polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS). Although dietary fiber has been shown to alleviate PMOS, its effects on androgen concentrations and the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. In a clinical trial, we demonstrated that a dietary fiber combination consisting of inulin, resistant starch, and β-glucan reduces androgen concentrations in patients' plasma. Mechanistically, dietary fiber increased the abundance of Bacteroides xylanisolvens, which converts androstenedione into a nonandrogenic secondary hormone metabolite we named coproandrosterone, which is further metabolized by gut microbiota into dihydro-coproandrosterone. This metabolic pathway was validated in a mouse model. These findings highlight the potential of dietary fiber to alleviate PMOS by modulating androgen homeostasis through gut microbiota, offering insights for prebiotic and probiotic therapies.

articles.title: Community-based delivery of lifesaving maternal and newborn health interventions in vulnerable Ethiopian communities: Lessons from implementation research.
articles.authors: Tiruneh GT, Semahegn A, Mirkuzie AH et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: In Ethiopia, women in remote agrarian and pastoralist regions face major barriers to accessing timely, quality maternal and newborn health (MNH) services, leading to high rates of home births and preventable mortality. This study assessed the implementation of the Village Health Leader (VHL)-led community-based MNH package in vulnerable agrarian and pastoralist communities in Ethiopia.
METHODS: Implementation research deploying a mixed-methods process evaluation across seven health centers and 38 vulnerable communities in the Afar, Somali, and Oromia regions was carried out from December 2023 to July 2025. VHLs were trained to deliver community-based MNH interventions that included misoprostol for the prevention of postpartum hemorrhage, chlorhexidine for umbilical cord care, iron-folic acid for the prevention of anemia, and postpartum family planning counseling and services. Quantitative program monitoring data were collected from 3,980 pregnant women and analyzed descriptively. Qualitative data were collected through 90 in-depth interviews and 14 focus group discussions with VHLs, health workers, postpartum women, community members, and supervisors. Qualitative data were coded in ATLAS.ti using both deductive and inductive approaches. Findings from the quantitative and qualitative components were integrated to provide a comprehensive assessment of implementation.
RESULTS: The intervention reached about 4,000 pregnant women, with high rates of uptake for lifesaving MNH services. Among women who gave birth, 35% delivered at home, 92% used misoprostol, and almost all applied chlorhexidine to the umbilical cord stump. Qualitative findings indicated generally positive perceptions of the intervention and highlighted its acceptability and feasibility. VHLs demonstrated strong adherence to protocols and timely referrals to health facilities. Challenges included supply shortages, lack of incentives for VHLs, and weak referral feedback systems. Despite these constraints, the intervention improved access, enhanced equity, and did not disincentivize facility-based deliveries.
CONCLUSIONS: Community-based delivery of lifesaving MNH interventions by VHLs is both feasible and acceptable in most underserved communities. The model strengthens the primary health care system by extending its reach, improving the continuum of care, and addressing persistent access barriers. However, sustainability requires reliable supply chains and tailored approaches for…

articles.title: Women's experiences of emergency post-abortion care at Kawempe National Referral Hospital, Uganda: A qualitative descriptive study.
articles.authors: Sessimba KS, James AG, Andrew B et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Post-abortion care (PAC) encompasses emergency treatment, counselling, contraceptive services, and referral linkages. Emergency post-abortion care (EPAC), the life-saving component of PAC, addresses acute abortion-related complications, including haemorrhage, sepsis, retained products of conception, and severe pain. In Uganda, where abortion is legally restricted and socially stigmatised, women's care experiences are shaped by clinical urgency, fear, moral vulnerability, provider interactions, and structural health system constraints. Despite EPAC's centrality to maternal survival, qualitative evidence on how women interpret and evaluate their care experiences in referral hospital settings in Uganda remains limited. This study explored women's experiences of EPAC at Kawempe National Referral Hospital (KNRH) and identified the factors that shaped those experiences.
METHODS: A qualitative descriptive design employing inductive thematic analysis was used. Sixteen in-depth interview transcripts from women who received EPAC at KNRH in March-April 2026 were analysed. The Socio-Ecological Model (SEM) was subsequently applied as a post-hoc organising framework to situate findings across individual, interpersonal, facility, and community levels.
RESULTS: Six themes were identified: (1) survival and physical relief as the immediate measure of good care; (2) pain, fear, and emotional distress during treatment; (3) reassurance and support as buffers against vulnerability; (4) dignity under pressure: communication and privacy in EPAC; (5) structural barriers across the pathway of care; and (6) experiences beyond discharge: incomplete recovery and uncertainty. Care was frequently evaluated through the lens of survival, yet these accounts co-existed with intense procedural pain, compromised privacy, delays, financial burden, and inadequate post-discharge support. EPAC at KNRH was experienced as a complex encounter shaped by bodily vulnerability, interpersonal dynamics, and system-level constraints.
CONCLUSIONS: Strengthening EPAC requires patient-centred approaches that integrate clinical effectiveness with respectful communication, pain management, improved triage, and structured post-discharge support.

articles.title: Supporting engagement, behavior change, and equitable self-management in menstrual and menopausal health: A multi-agent digital-health framework.
articles.authors: Yuji K, Yuji W, Nariai M et al.
articles.abstract: Menstrual-cycle-related conditions and, later, menopausal symptoms are highly prevalent across the female life course and impose a large, under-recognized burden on quality of life and work, yet digital tools to support self-management are fragmented, hard to sustain, and unevenly reached. We propose HERA (Health Engagement and Reflective Agent architecture), a conceptual, hypothesis-generating framework for supporting engagement, behavior change, and equitable self-management in menstrual and menopausal health across the life course. Under human governance, HERA combines two adaptive agents (interpretation and orchestration) with three rule-based modules (self-monitoring and data integration, guidance and content governance, and equity and engagement monitoring) that integrate self-monitoring, deliver personalized feedback, surface governed guidance, monitor equity, and coordinate hand-offs to clinicians and occupational-health services. Distinct from clinician-facing diagnostic agents, HERA is patient-facing and treats equity and engagement as first-class. We distinguish technically feasible from aspirational elements and set out a staged, threshold-gated evaluation plan. HERA is a design reference, not a validated system.

articles.title: Cost-effectiveness of atosiban versus placebo for threatened preterm birth (APOSTEL 8 trial).
articles.authors: van der Windt L, Oudijk M, Klumper J et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: To assess the cost-effectiveness of treatment with atosiban compared to placebo for threatened preterm birth from 30+0 to 33+6 weeks of gestation.
METHODS: We performed an economic evaluation from a societal perspective alongside the multicentre randomised controlled APOSTEL 8 trial, including 755 participants with threatened preterm birth from 30+0 to 33+6 weeks of gestation who were randomised to atosiban or placebo, of whom 752 (884 infants) were included in the intention-to-treat analysis. Costs, collected between randomisation and three months corrected child age, were measured using a combination of hospital records and the self-reported iMTA Medical and Productivity Cost Questionnaires and estimated at infant level. The main outcome measure was cost-effectiveness expressed in terms of incremental cost per severe adverse neonatal outcome prevented. Multiple imputation by chained equations was used to handle missing data. Non-parametric bootstrapping was used to estimate statistical uncertainty surrounding incremental cost-effectiveness outcomes.
FINDINGS: The difference in mean costs between the atosiban group (€40,743.1) and the placebo group (€40,793.6) was not statistically significant (mean difference: -€50.5; 95% confidence interval (CI) -4037.6 to 3936.7). The incremental cost per severe adverse neonatal outcome prevented was dominant (-€5286.6), falling in the south-east quadrant of the cost-effectiveness plane, indicating cost-savings and reduced severe adverse neonatal outcomes by atosiban. However, the bootstrapped cost-effect pairs were distributed across all four quadrants of the cost-effectiveness plane, indicating high uncertainty surrounding cost-effectiveness estimates. The probability of cost-effectiveness of atosiban reached 50% at a willingness to pay threshold of €33,023.3 per severe adverse neonatal outcome prevented.
INTERPRETATION: This economic evaluation did not demonstrate that atosiban is a cost-effective treatment for threatened PTB from 30+0 to 33+6 weeks gestation. In addition to the absence of clinical benefit, our findings show no economic advantage, further discouraging its routine use at this gestational age. These results contribute to optimizing evidence-based management of threatened preterm birth.

articles.title: Study on Wall Shear Stress Changes in the Aortic Arch and Isthmus in Fetuses With Aortic Coarctation Using Vector Flow Mapping.
articles.authors: Xu Z, Zeng S, Tong X et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate segmental peak systolic wall shear stress (WSSmax) in the aortic arch and isthmus of fetuses with coarctation of the aorta (CoA) and to explore its relationships with conventional anatomical and hemodynamic parameters.
METHODS: This prospective study included 58 CoA fetuses and 58 gestational age-matched normal controls. Vector flow mapping measured WSSmax at the inner and outer curvatures of the aortic arch and isthmus. Within the CoA group, Spearman correlation was used to assess relationships between isthmus WSSmax and the isthmus Z-score, PA/AO, TV/MV, isthmus Vmax, and RV/LV. Multivariable linear regression was performed using the isthmus Z-deficit (-Z), PA/AO, and isthmus Vmax.
RESULTS: Arch WSSmax did not differ between groups (all p > 0.05). Isthmus WSSmax (general, inner, and outer curvature) was significantly higher in the CoA group than in controls (all p < 0.05). Within the CoA group, isthmus WSSmax was lower than arch WSSmax (all p < 0.05). Isthmus WSSmax was correlated with the isthmus Z-score, PA/AO, and isthmus Vmax. In multivariable regression, isthmus Z-deficit (B = 0.271, 95% CI 0.031-0.510, p < 0.05) and isthmus Vmax (B = 0.01, 95% CI 0.001-0.020, p < 0.05) were independently associated with isthmus WSSmax, whereas PA/AO was not significant (p > 0.05).
CONCLUSION: Isthmus WSSmax is elevated in fetuses with CoA and is independently associated with greater isthmus hypoplasia and higher isthmus flow velocity, suggesting a role in CoA pathophysiology. Its incremental diagnostic value could not be assessed because the control group consisted of normal fetuses. WHAT IS ALREADY KNOWN ABOUT THIS TOPIC?: Prenatal diagnosis of aortic coarctation (CoA) has a high false‑positive rate. Hemodynamic changes in CoA include increased velocity and turbulence, but biomechanical assessment in fetuses is limited. WHAT DOES THIS STUDY ADD?: This study uses VFM to quantify WSSmax in the fetal aortic arch and isthmus. Isthmus WSSmax is significantly elevated in fetuses with CoA and is independently associated with greater isthmus hypoplasia and higher isthmus flow velocity, providing mechanistic insights into the biomechanical alterations of fetal CoA.

articles.title: Systemic Immune-Inflammation Index and Serum Uric Acid for Predicting Short-Term Delivery in Women With Threatened Preterm Labor.
articles.journal: American journal of reproductive immunology (New York, N.Y. : 1989)
articles.authors: Acer MH, Şanlı M, Özbek H
articles.abstract:
PROBLEM: This study evaluated the independent and combined predictive value of the systemic immune-inflammation index (SII) and serum uric acid for short-term delivery in women hospitalized with threatened preterm labor.
STUDY DESIGN: This retrospective cohort study included women hospitalized with threatened preterm labor between January 2020 and December 2025. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis assessed the predictive performance of SII and serum uric acid for delivery within 48 h and 7 days. Multivariable logistic regression models were adjusted for clinically relevant covariates. Internal validation was performed using 1000 bootstrap resamples, with Firth penalized models used for the 48-h outcome because of separation during resampling.
RESULTS: Among 621 women, 51 (8.2%) delivered within 48 h and 239 (38.5%) within 7 days. SII and serum uric acid levels were significantly higher in women who delivered within both time intervals (all p < 0.001). SII showed numerically higher AUCs than serum uric acid for delivery within 48 h (0.932 vs 0.876) and within 7 days (0.882 vs 0.843); however, paired DeLong tests did not demonstrate statistically significant differences (p = 0.0686 and p = 0.0504, respectively). Both biomarkers remained independently associated with delivery within 48 h in multivariable Firth penalized logistic regression and within 7 days in standard maximum-likelihood logistic regression. Observed delivery proportions increased stepwise across the combined biomarker categories.
CONCLUSION: SII and serum uric acid were independently associated with short-term delivery. Their combined assessment may provide additional information for short-term risk stratification using routinely available laboratory tests. External validation is required before clinical implementation.

articles.title: Cervical Neoplasia Among Canadian Armed Forces Regular Force Members, 2012-2024: A Descriptive Case Series.
articles.authors: Guo Y, Galanakis C, Shehata N et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Cervical cancer is preventable through human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination, routine screening, and timely follow up of abnormal results. However, limited evidence is available regarding cervical cancer burden and screening patterns and barriers within the Canadian Armed Forces (CAF). This study describes the demographic, military, clinical, and screening characteristics of cervical neoplasia cases diagnosed among CAF Regular Force members between 2012 and 2024.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: A retrospective descriptive case series was conducted using electronic medical records from the Canadian Forces Health Information System. The International Classification of Diseases, 10th Revision (ICD-10) codes in the clinical extract were used to identify any cervical neoplasia diagnoses from January 1, 2012 to December 31, 2024. Incident cases were confirmed based on colposcopy‑directed biopsy results. Demographic and military-specific data at diagnosis were obtained from the Master Patient Index. Variables extracted from the health record included age at diagnosis, rank, screening history, HPV vaccination status, diagnostic pathways, stage at diagnosis, referral timelines, and follow-up outcomes. Descriptive statistics were used to summarize case characteristics and identify gaps in screening participation and follow-up adherence.
RESULTS: A total of 23 incident cervical neoplasia cases were confirmed during the study period. The median age at diagnosis was 37 years (range: 24-52), and 47.8% were officers. 21.8% reported smoking at diagnosis. 43.5% of cases had missed (n = 7) or delayed (n = 3) at least 1 routine cervical cancer screening before diagnosis. 39.1% experienced delayed or missed follow-up after abnormal Pap results. Reported barriers to routine screening and follow-up included pandemic-related service interruptions, deployment or domestic posting, pregnancy, and childcare challenges. 39.1% (n = 9) had an abnormal result at the first recorded Pap test in the system. HPV vaccination completion was recorded for 52.2% of cases, and among those tested for HPV (n = 19), 31.6% were positive for types 16 or 18. Invasive cancer accounted for 56.5% of diagnoses, with 92.3% of invasive cases presenting at International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics (FIGO) stage I. Histology included squamous cell carcinoma (69.2%) and adenocarcinoma (30.8%). The median interval from abnormal screening result to diagnosis was 3.1 months (range: 0.7-61.9). No…

articles.title: Decidua-accumulated effector-like memory CD8+ T cells orchestrate localized antimicrobial defense without compromising fetal tolerance.
articles.authors: Liu L, Huang X, Yin T et al.
articles.abstract: Deciphering immune privilege at the maternal-fetal interface is essential for understanding how reproductive success and host defense are simultaneously maintained. Decidualization, occurring within the specialized stromal tissue encapsulating the fetus and placenta, shapes local immune adaptation required for healthy pregnancy. Here, we identify a decidua-enriched effector-like memory CD8+ T cell subset marked by CD45RA in humans and CX3CR1 in mice. These cells preferentially accumulate in the decidua, which harbors a CX3CL1-dominant chemokine niche, and disruption of Cx3cr1 or uterine Cx3cl1 impaired their decidual recruitment and tissue localization. Human CD45RA+ and murine CX3CR1+ decidual memory CD8+ T cells shared conserved transcriptional and functional features, including enhanced cytotoxic potential and limited inflammatory cytokine production. Functionally, CX3CL1-mediated CD8+ T cell accumulation improved local control of prenatal Listeria monocytogenes infection and reduced infection-associated fetal loss. In contrast, fetal antigen-specific CD8+ T cell accumulation and fetal resorption occurred independently of uterine CX3CL1. Together, our findings define the maternal-fetal interface as an active immunological gatekeeper, that compartmentalizing CD8+ T cell-mediated antimicrobial adaptive immunity through the conserved CX3CL1-CX3CR1 axis, supporting pathogen-specific defense while preserving fetal tolerance.

articles.authors: Angus DC, O'Connor MB, Young LJ

articles.title: Indoor Radon and Incident Heart Failure Among Postmenopausal Women.
articles.authors: Chen S, Shi C, Collins JM et al.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Evidence has shown an association of radon exposure with heart failure risk factors, but whether there is an association with heart failure remains unclear.
OBJECTIVE: To assess whether indoor radon concentrations are associated with incident heart failure among US postmenopausal women.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This prospective cohort study used data from the Women's Health Initiative (WHI) observational study and clinical trials. Participants were postmenopausal women from 40 US clinical centers who were aged 50 to 79 years and did not have self-reported heart failure at enrollment or randomization (September 1993 to December 1998) but had physician adjudication of heart failure during follow-up through February 17, 2024.
EXPOSURE: Geocoded participant address-based assignment of county-level, US Environmental Protection Agency-categorized indoor radon concentration (<2, 2-4, or >4 picocuries [pCi]/L).
MAIN OUTCOME AND MEASURE: Incident hospitalization for acute decompensated heart failure was ascertained through physician adjudication of medical records. Hazard ratios (HRs) for heart failure by indoor radon concentration were estimated with Cox proportional hazards regression models.
RESULTS: Among 43 188 postmenopausal women (mean [SD] age, 63 [7] years), 36% were exposed to a radon concentration less than 2 pCi/L; 41%, to a concentration of 2 to 4 pCi/L; and 23%, to a concentration of more than 4 pCi/L. Over a mean (SD) follow-up of 16.2 (8.4) years, 3446 incident heart failure events occurred. The fully adjusted HR for heart failure was 1.19 (95% CI, 1.07-1.33) at more than 4 pCi/L vs less than 2 pCi/L, changing little in sensitivity analyses. The HR was higher for heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (1.24; 95% CI, 1.04-1.49) and heart failure mortality (1.37; 95% CI, 1.12-1.69) at radon concentrations more than 4 pCi/L vs less than 2 pCi/L, but these HRs were not different from the null at concentrations of 2 to 4 pCi/L vs less than 2 pCi/L. The HR at concentrations greater than 4 pCi/L approximated that of a 16-mm Hg increase in systolic blood pressure or an increase of 4.8 in body mass index (calculated as weight in kilograms divided by height in meters squared).
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this cohort study of US postmenopausal women, higher indoor radon concentrations were associated with an increased risk of incident heart failure, suggesting that radon may be a modifiable environmental determinant of heart…

articles.title: Nonlinear association between age and volumetric breast density in Japanese women.
articles.authors: Matsubara M, Uematsu T, Ito T et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Volumetric breast density (VBD) is influenced by age, body mass index (BMI), and reproductive factors, yet the shape of the age-VBD association and age-specific VBD distributions in Japanese women remain incompletely characterized. We examined the associations of age, BMI, menopausal status, and parity with software-derived VBD and characterized age-specific VBD distributions, including the proportion of women with VBD ≥ 7.5%.
METHODS: This cross-sectional study included 719 asymptomatic Japanese women undergoing screening mammography (mean age, 58.7 ± 12.6 years; range, 20-87 years) in whom no breast lesion was identified. VBD was quantified using Volpara Density. Age was modeled using restricted cubic splines, adjusted for BMI, menopausal status, and parity. Regression analyses used 672 complete cases. Mean VBD ≥ 7.5% defined volumetrically dense breasts.
RESULTS: Overall, 72.7% (523/719) had VBD ≥ 7.5%. Mean VBD was 17.34%, 13.41%, 11.01%, and 11.72% at ages 40-49, 50-59, 60-69, and 70-79 years, respectively, and 16.81% versus 11.85% in pre- versus postmenopausal women. Age was associated with VBD (P < 0.001), with significant nonlinearity (P = 0.027); adjusted VBD was lower with increasing age until the mid-60s and then largely plateaued. Higher BMI (β = -1.08; 95% CI, - 1.20 to - 0.97; P < 0.001) and parity (β = -2.21; 95% CI, - 3.43 to - 0.98; P < 0.001) were independently associated with lower VBD, whereas menopausal status was not (β = -1.07; 95% CI, - 2.85 to 0.71; P = 0.239).
CONCLUSIONS: Age was nonlinearly associated with VBD in Japanese women, plateauing after the mid-60s. VBD ≥ 7.5% was common, while BMI and parity remained independently associated with lower VBD.

articles.title: Morphokinetic characterization of human embryos derived from capacitation in vitro maturation versus controlled ovarian stimulation with intracytoplasmic sperm injection: a retrospective cohort study using time-lapse imaging.
articles.journal: Journal of assisted reproduction and genetics
articles.authors: Dang AH, Nguyen TC, Pham TD et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To characterize the morphokinetic profile of blastocyst-stage embryos derived from biphasic capacitation in vitro maturation (CAPA-IVM), using a contemporaneous cohort of controlled ovarian stimulation with intracytoplasmic sperm injection (COS-ICSI) embryos as the reference, with standardized time-lapse imaging.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study was conducted at an assisted reproduction center from March 2021 to December 2024. Eligible women were aged < 40 years and had no prior fertilization failure, gamete donation, planned preimplantation genetic testing, or significant male factor infertility. CAPA-IVM and COS-ICSI cycles were matched 1:1 on a propensity score built from female age and the number of analyzable embryos in the cycle. Embryos were cultured to the blastocyst stage with time-lapse monitoring. Morphokinetic timings were compared using crude, adjusted mixed-effects, and trajectory analyses, with a crude subgroup analysis of good-quality G1/G2 embryos.
RESULTS: Overall, 232 couples contributed 876 embryos (421 CAPA-IVM and 455 COS-ICSI). In crude analyses, CAPA-IVM versus COS-ICSI embryos showed later pronuclear appearance (+ 0.71 h; p < 0.001), earlier pronuclear fading (- 0.92 h; p < 0.001), earlier t3 (- 1.42 h; p < 0.001), and earlier t5 (- 1.40 h; p = 0.017), but later compaction (+ 2.00 h; p < 0.01) and blastulation (+ 1.67 h; p < 0.01). Later pronuclear appearance, earlier pronuclear fading, earlier t3, and earlier t5 with CAPA-IVM versus COS-ICSI remained statistically significant after adjustment. There was a lower proportion of good-quality G1/G2 embryos after CAPA-IVM versus COS-ICSI (29% vs. 39%; p < 0.01). In the G1/G2 embryo subset, CAPA-IVM showed later pronuclear appearance but earlier pronuclear fading, t3, and t4.
CONCLUSIONS: CAPA-IVM embryos showed a distinct, non-uniform morphokinetic profile, highlighting the need for maturation pathway-specific interpretation of time-lapse data.

articles.title: Extracellular vesicle-based therapeutics and biomarker potential for polycystic ovary syndrome and endometriosis: from human/animal cell-derived to plant-derived EVs.
articles.authors: Rahman MU, Liu T, Dilfuzakhon S et al.
articles.abstract: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) and endometriosis are prevalent gynecological disorders associated with chronic inflammation, oxidative stress, hormonal dysregulation, and impaired fertility. Current treatments primarily focus on symptom management and may be limited by adverse effects and disease recurrence. Extracellular vesicles (EVs) are promising cell-free therapeutic and diagnostic platforms that transport bioactive cargo, including microRNAs, proteins, and lipids. This review explores the therapeutic and diagnostic potential of human-, animal-, and plant-derived EVs in PCOS and endometriosis, distinguishing direct evidence from disease-specific models from indirect evidence obtained in other experimental conditions. Mesenchymal stem cell-derived EVs exhibit anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, antifibrotic, and regenerative effects in preclinical models, while plant-derived EVs from ginger, aloe, garlic, grapefruit, rice, pomegranate, and tomato demonstrate diverse biological activities with varying relevance to these disorders. Notably, ginger-derived EVs have shown beneficial effects in experimental endometriosis models by reducing inflammation, angiogenesis, and cellular invasion while promoting apoptosis. Findings from other disease models provide indirect support for potential mechanisms but do not establish therapeutic efficacy in PCOS or endometriosis. EVs may also serve as biomarkers for disease diagnosis and monitoring. This review discusses EV isolation, characterization, proposed mechanisms, preclinical evidence, and translational challenges. Future research should prioritize disease-specific mechanistic studies, standardized EV isolation and characterization, rigorous evaluation of biodistribution and safety, and well-designed clinical trials to establish diagnostic utility and therapeutic efficacy. Although EV-based approaches hold promise, further validation is essential before clinical application.

articles.title: A hemicyanine-based activatable near-infrared probe for cysteine and its fluorescence response in a mouse model of polycystic ovary syndrome.
articles.authors: Zhao WB, Wu ZB, Zhao R et al.
articles.abstract: Altered sulfur amino acid metabolism motivates the investigation of cysteine (Cys)-responsive fluorescence in polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS)-related models. We developed HD-ZWB, an acrylate-caged hemicyanine probe that exhibits near-infrared fluorescence enhancement upon exposure to Cys. The response is consistent with a proposed Michael addition-cyclization pathway that releases the hemicyanine fluorophore. Under the specified buffer conditions, emission at 740 nm increased linearly over 1-10 µM Cys, with a reported detection limit of 0.01 µM, and approached a plateau within approximately 60 min. Preferential fluorescence activation by Cys was observed relative to the tested interferents. Cell viability remained above 80% at probe concentrations up to 50 µM. In OVCAR3 cells, the activated fluorescence overlapped with a mitochondrial marker and showed treatment-dependent endpoint differences following exposure to PMA, SIN-1, LPS, or N-acetylcysteine. Curcumin also reduced the endpoint signal in a high-content screen. In the PCOS mouse model, fluorescence was detectable at 15 min and peaked near 30 min; probe-treated PCOS serum showed approximately five-fold higher fluorescence than control serum. These results support exploratory fluorescence measurements with HD-ZWB in PCOS-related models. Independent Cys quantification and further chemical validation are required to assign the biological signals quantitatively to Cys, and the present data do not establish reversible sensing or diagnostic performance.

articles.title: To interpret gypenoside-L mediated PIWI/piRNA regulatory effect on cuproptosis in ovarian cancer and the mechanism based on PANDORA-seq.
articles.authors: Sun X, Zhang J, Zhao J et al.
articles.abstract: Ovarian cancer (OC) poses a significant threat to women's health, and has limited therapeutic options. Small RNAs play a critical role in the regulation of OC, and the initiation and progression of OC are closely associated with the aberrant regulation of the PIWI/piRNA pathway. Gypenoside-L (Gyp-L), a bioactive saponin with antitumor potential, has not been fully studied for its mechanisms against OC. In this study, we investigated the effects of Gyp-L on ovarian cancer cells and the underlying molecular mechanisms involving the PIWI/piRNA pathway and the regulation of cuproptosis. Molecular docking, colony formation, scratch wound healing, PANDORA-seq, western blotting, and qRT-PCR were used to evaluate binding affinity, cell functions, and molecular expression. Using PANDORA-seq, we identified nine piRNAs with significant differential expression in Gyp-L-affected ovarian cancer cells. Our results showed that PIWIL1, PIWIL2 were upregulated, and nine specific piRNAs were downregulated in OC tissues. Gyp-L inhibited proliferation and migration of OVCAR3 and SKOV3 cells dose-dependently, downregulated PIWIL1/PIWIL2, and upregulated dysregulated piRNAs. Knockdown of piR-hsa-2,804,461 upregulated FNBP4 and suppressed cuproptosis, which was reversed by Gyp-L. Collectively, Gyp-L inhibits ovarian cancer cell progression by modulating the PIWI/piRNA pathway, regulating piR-hsa-2,804,461/FNBP4, and reactivating cuproptosis, highlighting its potential as a therapeutic candidate for OC.

articles.title: Discovery-locked cross-platform evaluation of a cervical epithelial transcriptional state.
articles.authors: Zheng Y, Yi H, Zhu L et al.
articles.abstract: Cross-platform claims about tumour-cell states can be inflated when each cohort is reanalysed to favour a new definition. We evaluated whether a cervical epithelial transcriptional state selected in one discovery cohort remained recoverable without changing its frozen genes or thresholds. E-MTAB-12,305 was the sole discovery cohort and contained 100,453 cells from ten samples; 11,224 cells were assigned to the discovery-defined epithelial state. We froze 123 sample-aware pseudobulk signatures and evaluated them in an external single-cell cohort, four Visium samples, a 22-sample Xenium cohort using an 11-gene proxy, and a local dataset containing 30,280 manually selected epithelial cells from 14 specimens representing 11 participants. Leave-one-sample-out analyses preserved gene-level direction in evaluable folds but showed sample-sensitive significance. Xenium scores exhibited within-score spatial clustering after joint-label coordinate permutations (median odds ratio 1.97; 19 of 22 odds ratios > 1). In the local cohort, patient-level associations with CytoTRACE2 were not significant, although within-participant cell-level correlations were consistently negative. Recomputed TCGA-CESC analyses did not support a stable prognostic association after accounting for score definition and time dependence. The results support a discovery-locked, cross-platform recovery framework and a context-dependent epithelial-state hypothesis, but not malignant identity, metastatic lineage, clinical prognosis, or causal communication.

articles.title: Analysis of Educational Content on TikTok Regarding Antenatal Perineal Massage.
articles.authors: Vergara-Soria T, Sacomori C, Alencar de Miranda Y et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION AND HYPOTHESIS: Antenatal perineal massage (APM) is recommended by international organizations as a strategy to reduce the risk of perineal trauma during childbirth. The increasing prevalence of misinformation on digital platforms highlights the need to assess content quality, including those related to APM.
METHODS: This cross-sectional study evaluated the quality and reliability of educational content about APM on TikTok videos in Spanish, Portuguese, and English. A purposive sampling strategy was applied using a newly created TikTok account and relevant hashtags. Two researchers independently selected eligible videos and assessed content quality using the DISCERN scale, with near-perfect inter-rater agreement (κ > 0.90). Data extracted from the videos included interaction metrics, characteristics of the content creators, and specific instructions related to APM.
RESULTS: Of the 1306 videos identified, 250 were included in the final analysis and 214 (85.6%) presented a "poor" or "very poor" level of informational content, with no significant differences between languages (p = 0.147). Although most were produced by healthcare professionals (n = 200; 80.8%), minimal mention of information sources, risks, or therapeutic alternatives was observed. Of the total videos analyzed, 94 (37.6%) complied with the recommendations to begin at week 34 of gestation, and 78 (31.2%) recommended a massage duration of between 5 and 10 min. Video duration was positively correlated with the total DISCERN score (rho = 0.489; p < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: Results may indicate a potential concern regarding the quality of health information available related to APM. Promoting digital health literacy and encouraging the creation of evidence-based content are recommended.

articles.title: Pelvic Girdle Pain in Pregnancy and Postpartum: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.authors: Abawa AM, Bidkhori HR, Hennes DMZB et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION AND HYPOTHESIS: Pelvic girdle pain (PGP) is a common musculoskeletal disorder that can substantially affect quality of life during pregnancy and the postpartum period. We aimed to estimate the pooled prevalence of PGP, identify associated factors and summarise commonly used clinical assessment methods.
METHODS: We searched MEDLINE/PubMed, Embase, CINAHL, Emcare, Scopus, and PEDro from inception to 24 July 2026. Methodological quality was assessed using Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) critical appraisal tools. Random-effects meta-analysis with subgroup and sensitivity analyses were conducted. Heterogeneity was assessed using the I2 statistic. Certainty of evidence was assessed using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation approach.
RESULTS: Thirty-two studies (N = 145,091) were included. The pooled prevalence of PGP was 59% (95% CI 49-68%; I2 = 97.2%) during pregnancy (predominantly in the third trimester) and 32% (95% CI 19-45%; I2= 98.8%) within the first year postpartum. Both estimates showed substantial heterogeneity.
