Factors associated with postpartum PGP included prior low back pain (OR 1.89; 95% CI 1.43-2.50), antenatal emotional distress (OR 2.11; 95% CI 1.33-3.33) and a positive bilateral posterior pelvic pain provocation (P4) test during the peripartum period (OR 1.72; 95% CI 1.30-2.27). The certainty of evidence was very low for all quantitatively synthesised outcomes. The P4 and active straight leg raise tests were most frequently used assessment methods.
CONCLUSIONS: Pelvic girdle pain was commonly reported during pregnancy and within the first postpartum year. However, given substantial heterogeneity and very low certainty of evidence, findings should be interpreted with caution, thereby limiting generalisability across populations.

articles.title: The (R)evolution of vNOTES in gynecology.
articles.authors: Farulla A, Comandini R, Del Villano N et al.
articles.abstract: Transvaginal natural orifice transluminal endoscopic surgery (vNOTES) has emerged as an innovative minimally invasive approach in gynecologic surgery, aiming to combine the benefits of vaginal surgery and conventional laparoscopy while avoiding abdominal incisions. Over the past two decades, its clinical applications have expanded considerably, encompassing an increasingly wide range of gynecologic procedures. The of this study was to provide a comprehensive narrative review of the evolution of vNOTES in gynecology, summarizing current evidence on surgical indications, perioperative outcomes, limitations, and future perspectives. A comprehensive literature search was performed in PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and the Cochrane Library from January 2004 to June 2026. Original studies, randomized trials, systematic reviews, and meta-analyses evaluating vNOTES in gynecologic surgery were included. vNOTES has evolved from an experimental access technique to an established minimally invasive approach for benign hysterectomy and adnexal surgery. Emerging applications include myomectomy, endometriosis surgery, urogynecologic procedures, gynecologic emergencies and selected oncologic indications. While high-quality evidence is available for hysterectomy and adnexal surgery, comparative data remain limited for most other gynecologic procedures, although preliminary results are highly promising. Learning curve, patient selection, and technical constraints remain key determinants of successful implementation. vNOTES represents a significant evolution in minimally invasive gynecologic surgery, with clear benefits in selected benign indications. However, its broader adoption is currently limited by heterogeneous evidence and technical challenges. Future studies should focus on standardization, training, and long-term oncologic and functional outcomes.

articles.title: Effectiveness of 25 µg vaginal misoprostol for labor induction in women with obesity: outcomes according to obesity class.
articles.authors: Mocarzel CC, Araujo Júnior E, Brito VM et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The aim of this study is to evaluate the effectiveness of 25 µg vaginal misoprostol for labor induction in pregnant women with obesity.
METHODS: This observational analytical study was conducted with a total of 116 pregnant women with singleton gestation, Body Mass Index (BMI) ≥30 kg/m2 at the beginning of prenatal care, and gestational age ≥37 weeks who underwent labor induction with 25 µg vaginal misoprostol were included. Participants were stratified according to obesity class as class I (N.=18), class II (N.=16), and class III (N.=82). The primary outcome was vaginal delivery. Multivariable logistic regression analysis was performed to evaluate the association between obesity class and vaginal delivery, adjusting for maternal age, gestational age, neonatal birthweight, and prior vaginal delivery. Secondary analyses included oxytocin use, duration of labor induction, and neonatal Apgar scores according to obesity class.
RESULTS: Obesity class was not significantly associated with vaginal delivery after adjustment for covariates. The adjusted odds ratios were 0.89 for class I versus class II (95% CI 0.19-4.15; P=0.887), 0.95 for class III versus class II (95% CI 0.28-3.16; P=0.952), and 0.94 for class I versus class III (95% CI 0.29-2.97; P=0.916). The mean maternal age was 29.0±5.5 years, and the mean BMI was 49.4±9.4 kg/m2. Chronic hypertension was present in 53.4% of participants, and 36.2% had gestational diabetes mellitus. The mean duration of labor induction was 34.3±17.6 hours. Cesarean delivery occurred in 58.6% of cases, whereas 41.4% achieved vaginal delivery. Baseline maternal, obstetric, and clinical characteristics were similar across obesity classes, except for chronic hypertension with superimposed preeclampsia, which was more frequent in class II (31.3%) compared with class I (16.7%) and class III (8.5%) (P=0.035). Among women who achieved vaginal delivery, oxytocin use and induction duration did not differ significantly across obesity classes. Prior vaginal delivery was significantly associated with mode of delivery in the current pregnancy (χ2<inf>(1)</inf>=11.6; P<0.001), with a higher likelihood of vaginal delivery among women with a history of vaginal birth.
CONCLUSIONS: In this cohort of pregnant women with obesity, labor induction with 25 µg vaginal misoprostol was effective, and increasing obesity class was not associated with lower vaginal delivery rates. Prior vaginal delivery was significantly associated with a…

articles.title: Alpha-lipoic acid in pregnancy: a review of potential effects on maternal and fetal health.
articles.authors: Parodi C, Monari F, Massa V et al.
articles.abstract: Alpha lipoic acid (ALA) is a naturally occurring micronutrient with potent antioxidant and anti-inflammatory activities. For these characteristics, ALA dietary supplementation has been suggested in pregnancy with the aim of reducing the risk of adverse pregnancy outcomes in cases associated with the effects of inflammation and/or oxidative stress. In this review, we synthesize evidence for the uses of ALA in recurrent pregnancy loss (RPL), threatened miscarriage, preterm birth, and gestational diabetes, showing both the results of clinical trials and animal/in-vitro studies. Our opinion, based on the current knowledge, suggests that ALA may reduce paternal sperm DNA fragmentation and maternal endometrial inflammation in cases with a high risk of RPL and may improve the resorption of subchorionic hematoma in threatened miscarriage. ALA is also promising in helping cervical length in women at high risk for preterm delivery and in improving glucose and lipid metabolism in gestational diabetes. Although the current evidence about ALA supplementation in human pregnancy is preliminary, the available studies encourage planning further powered randomized controlled clinical trials aimed at confirming these promising effects, with the ambitious aim of improving pregnancy outcomes in high-risk conditions.

articles.title: Clinical Implications of Background Parenchymal Enhancement on Breast MRI.
articles.authors: Zamora KW, Coffey K, Colvin S et al.
articles.abstract: Breast MRI is an essential tool for breast cancer detection, evaluation, and characterization, offering greater sensitivity than mammography and ultrasound. Normal breast tissue demonstrates variable enhancement on MRI, known as background parenchymal enhancement (BPE), which reflects the physiologic enhancement of fibroglandular tissue after gadolinium administration. Initially considered an incidental finding, BPE is now recognized as a dynamic imaging feature influenced by several factors, including age, menopausal status, exogenous hormone use, and prior breast cancer treatments. Increasing evidence supports its clinical relevance since variations in BPE have been associated with differences in breast cancer risk, lesion detection, and imaging interpretation. Background parenchymal enhancement (BPE) is emerging as an important imaging biomarker with potential applications in risk stratification, evaluation of disease extent, and monitoring response to neoadjuvant therapy. Differences in BPE patterns may also correlate with tumor biology and molecular subtypes, further supporting its role in personalized breast imaging assessment. This article provides a comprehensive review of BPE, highlighting its biologic basis, imaging characteristics, and clinical implications in breast cancer care. It also examines the evolving role of artificial intelligence tools in the assessment and quantification of BPE, which may improve standardization and integration into clinical decision-making and research.

articles.title: Neighborhood deprivation and the risk of stillbirth in New York.
articles.authors: Williford EM, Aydin-Ghormoz H, Fisher SC et al.
articles.abstract: Stillbirth (fetal death ≥ 20 weeks gestation) occurs in approximately 21,000 births each year in the United States. Previous studies have observed associations between neighborhood deprivation and adverse perinatal outcomes. We estimated associations between neighborhood deprivation and singleton stillbirth in New York. We performed a cross-sectional study of stillbirths and live births from hospital claims data from the Statewide Planning and Research Cooperative System (2022-2024). Neighborhood deprivation index (NDI) at the census tract level was assigned to geocoded addresses at delivery. Risk ratios (RR) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were estimated using a generalized estimating equations model adjusted for individual-level maternal variables of age at delivery, race/ethnicity, marital status, and primary health insurance payer. Our analysis included 3,128 stillbirths and 552,361 live births. The NDI quartiles were associated with stillbirth, with higher levels of deprivation corresponding to increased risk compared to the least deprived quartiles. We observed the highest risk of stillbirth among women in the most deprived quartile (RR 1.42; 95% CI 1.25-1.61). The association of NDI quartile on the risk of stillbirth did not differ by race/ethnicity. Our findings highlight that women residing in the most deprived NDI quartile could benefit from enhanced prenatal services and support.

articles.title: CT55 variants impair GABARAP-dependent autophagosome maturation to cause asthenoteratozoospermia in humans.
articles.authors: Wang G, Zheng L, Ni X et al.
articles.abstract: Asthenoteratozoospermia (AST) is a major cause of male infertility, yet the molecular connection between autophagy and sperm structural remodeling remains incompletely defined. Here, we identify two novel hemizygous cancer-testis antigen 55 (CT55) variants in unrelated men with severe AST: a multi-exonic truncation (exon1_4del; p.Met1_Glu180del) and a missense mutation (c.433C > T; p.Pro145Ser). Using integrated ultrastructural, immunofluorescence, and biochemical analyses, we show that these variants are associated with the altered CT55-mediated regulation of GABARAP-dependent autophagosome maturation through potentially distinct mechanisms. The truncating variant produces a shortened CT55 isoform that retains measurable GABARAP interaction but may impair downstream autophagosome maturation, whereas the missense variant reduces CT55 expression and weakens the CT55-GABARAP interaction in cell-based assays. Patient spermatozoa exhibit p62 accumulation, elevated LC3-II/LC3-I ratios, and broad cytoplasmic remodeling defects, including acrosomal malformation, midpiece disorganization, and axonemal instability. These findings support CT55 dysfunction as a cause of human AST and suggest that the disrupted CT55-associated autophagic regulation may contribute to multi-compartment sperm abnormalities. Our work expands the genetic and mechanistic framework of CT55-related male infertility and provides insights for molecular diagnosis and genetic counseling.

articles.title: Identification and dating of pregnancies in administrative healthcare claims databases: An updated, transparent, and transportable algorithm.
articles.authors: Makadia R, Voss EA, Swerdel J et al.
articles.abstract: Studies using routinely collected healthcare data are essential for understanding the benefit-risk profile of medications in pregnancy. However, reproducibility is limited by the lack of shared pregnancy identification algorithms, and generalizability is constrained by their development primarily in commercial insurance databases. A previously developed pregnancy identification algorithm was updated for ICD-10-CM and translated into a standardized format to support transport across diverse databases. Algorithm implementation characteristics were evaluated in three US health insurance claims databases (2000-2025), including commercially and publicly insured populations. Overall, 5.8 million and 3.0 million pregnancies were identified in two commercial databases (Merative™ and Optum) and 2.3 million pregnancies in Merative™ MarketScan® Multi-State Medicaid Database (MDCD). Across databases, live birth prevalence ranged from 76-83%, miscarriage/abortion 15-23%, ectopic pregnancy 1%, and stillbirth ≤0.5%, with a higher proportion of live births in MDCD. Pregnancy dating methods varied substantially across coding eras: use of gestational age records increased from 4-9% in the ICD-9-CM era to 87-92% during the ICD-10-CM era, with greater use in MDCD. Using a standardized algorithm, this study demonstrates how database characteristics and coding transitions influence pregnancy identification and dating in healthcare data, highlighting methodological considerations for reproducible pregnancy research across data sources.

articles.title: The impact of gestational weight gain on perineal injury in primiparous women with normal pre-pregnancy BMI.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.authors: Amikam U, Hertz M, Gold R et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Our objective was to determine the association between gestational weight gain (GWG) and the risk of perineal injury in nulliparous women with normal pre-pregnancy body mass index (BMI).
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study (January 2012-January 2024) at a single tertiary center including nulliparous women with normal pre-pregnancy BMI (18.5-24.9 kg/m2) who delivered a singleton, live, term infant (≥37 weeks) vaginally, excluding pregestational or gestational diabetes. Participants were stratified by GWG per American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists guidelines (recommended 11.5-16 kg) into below-, within-, and above-recommended GWG groups. The primary outcome was perineal injury (1st-4th degree). Multivariable logistic regression assessed the independent association between GWG and perineal trauma.
RESULTS: Of 26 828 women, a total of 9019 (33.6%) had below-, 11 527 (43.0%) within-, and 6282 (23.4%) above-recommended GWG. Overall perineal injury was more common with above-recommended GWG (86.4% vs. 84.9% vs. 84.2%, P = 0.001), whereas obstetric anal sphincter injury (OASI) rates were comparable (0.9% vs. 0.7% vs. 0.7%, P = 0.506). The above-recommended group had higher rates of induction and epidural analgesia, longer second-stage duration, and higher birthweight (all P < 0.001). After adjustment, GWG category was not independently associated with overall perineal injury (above-recommended: odds ratio [OR] 1.021; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.930-1.120, P = 0.665) or OASI (above-recommended: OR 1.065; 95% CI 0.743-1.526, P = 0.733). Independent risk factors for perineal injury included vacuum extraction (OR 3.288), epidural analgesia (OR 1.489), occiput-posterior position (OR 1.450), induction (OR 1.285), and higher birthweight (OR 1.957 per kg).
CONCLUSION: Among nulliparous women with normal pre-pregnancy BMI, GWG, whether below, within, or above American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists recommendations, did not independently affect the risk of perineal tears or OASI. Intrapartum and fetal factors remain the primary determinants of perineal injury.

articles.title: Frontal Cortical Volumes Differ by Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder Symptom Presentation in School-Aged Children Born Preterm.
articles.authors: Uberos J, Carrasco-Solis M, Laynez-Rubio C et al.
articles.abstract:
AIM: To investigate whether cortical and subcortical brain volumes differ according to attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) symptom presentation in school-aged children born very preterm.
METHODS: This cross-sectional study included 81 children born before 32 weeks of gestation: 64 without ADHD symptoms, 7 with predominantly inattentive symptoms and 10 with combined symptoms, classified using the Vanderbilt parent questionnaire. Magnetic resonance imaging was analysed using FreeSurfer. General linear models were adjusted for gestational age, birth weight, sex and total intracranial volume. False discovery rate (FDR) correction was applied.
RESULTS: Left rostral middle frontal gyrus (RMFG) volume was the only region significantly associated with symptom presentation after FDR correction (partial η2 = 0.179; p = 0.030). Adjusted RMFG volume was larger in children with combined symptoms than in those without ADHD symptoms (mean difference, 3610 mm3; 95% CI, 1155-6064; adjusted p = 0.002). The inattentive group had the lowest adjusted mean volume, but the difference from the asymptomatic group was not significant. RMFG volume correlated positively with inattentive and hyperactivity/impulsivity symptom scores. No other regional associations remained significant after correction.
CONCLUSION: ADHD symptom presentation was associated with left RMFG volume, showing a non-monotonic pattern across groups. Larger longitudinal studies are needed to clarify the developmental significance of these findings.

articles.title: Carcinoma In Situ Skip Lesions of the Uterine Corpus in Cervical Squamous Cell Carcinoma: Impact on Target Setting in Radiotherapy.
articles.authors: Harada M, Hagiwara Y, Kabasawa T et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In definitive radiotherapy for FIGO Stage I-III cervical cancer, external beam radiotherapy and/or brachytherapy are used-alone or in combination with concurrent chemotherapy depending on stage-with target delineation largely guided by clinically apparent disease. However, discontinuous carcinoma in situ (CIS) "skip lesions" within the uterine corpus are well described in cervical adenocarcinoma, whereas their presence in cervical squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) has not been systematically evaluated.
AIMS: This study aimed to investigate the presence or absence of CIS skip lesions in the uterine corpus of patients with cervical SCC.
METHODS AND RESULTS: This retrospective study included all patients who underwent total or radical hysterectomy for cervical SCC at Yamagata University Hospital between January 2013 and April 2020. Patients who underwent prior radiotherapy or preoperative chemotherapy, or had non-squamous histological components, were excluded. Fifty patients were enrolled. Pathological examination of serially sectioned uterine specimens was conducted to identify skip lesions, defined as discontinuous CIS lesions in the uterine corpus, as confirmed by a pathologist and a radiation oncologist. Pathological evaluation showed that 29 patients (58%) had FIGO Stage I disease, 6 patients (12%) had FIGO Stage II disease, and 15 patients (30%) were classified as FIGO Stage IIIC1. Preoperative imaging studies did not identify any skip lesions in the uterine corpus. However, one patient (2%; Clopper-Pearson 95% confidence intervals: 0.05%-10.5%) presented with a histologically confirmed CIS skip lesion located in the uterine corpus, approximately 2 cm cranial to the primary tumor margin, that was undetectable on imaging. The primary tumor after biopsy measured 3 mm and was diagnosed as non-keratinizing SCC without > 1/3 stromal invasion. Lymphovascular space invasion, parametrial invasion, and corpus invasion were not observed.
CONCLUSION: Although rare, CIS skip lesions in the uterine corpus can occur in patients with cervical SCC.

articles.title: First-Trimester Hematologic Inflammatory Markers and Pregnancy Loss in Women With Unexplained Recurrent Pregnancy Loss: A Retrospective Study of Associations and Discrimination.
articles.authors: Wang R, Mu F, Zhang W et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aims to investigate whether complete blood count (CBC)-derived systemic inflammation indices are associated with pregnancy loss in women with unexplained recurrent pregnancy loss (URPL).
METHODS: This retrospective observational study included 517 women with URPL who were recruited from Lanzhou University Second Hospital between September 2019 and December 2022. Participants were categorized into the pregnancy loss (n = 265) group and live birth (n = 252) group. CBCs obtained at 4-8 weeks of gestation were used to calculate the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), monocyte-to-lymphocyte ratio (MLR), platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR), systemic immune-inflammation index (SII), and systemic inflammation response index (SIRI). We fitted multivariable logistic regression models adjusted for age, education, ethnicity, and body mass index. We assessed in-sample discriminative performance using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves.
RESULTS: Compared with the live birth group, the pregnancy loss group had higher neutrophil counts, NLR, SII, SIRI, MLR, and PLR, and lower lymphocyte counts (all p < 0.001). After adjustment, higher NLR (OR = 3.05, 95% CI: 2.25-4.21), SIRI (OR = 2.74, 95% CI: 1.77-4.33), and SII (per 100-unit increase, OR = 1.36, 95% CI: 1.24-1.51) were associated with greater odds of pregnancy loss. In tertile analyses, compared with the lowest tertile, the highest tertile was associated with higher odds of pregnancy loss for NLR (OR = 5.51), SII (OR = 2.88), SIRI (OR = 2.55), MLR (OR = 2.41), and PLR (OR = 3.41), with all p-values for trend < 0.001. In ROC analyses, NLR showed the highest in-sample discriminative performance (AUC = 0.752), followed by SII (AUC = 0.716).
CONCLUSION: First-trimester CBC-derived inflammatory indices, particularly NLR and SII, were associated with pregnancy loss in women with URPL and may have potential discriminative value within this cohort. These findings require confirmation in prospective, multicenter studies with broader confounder assessment and external validation before any clinical application can be considered.

articles.title: Assessment of genomic instability and homologous recombination repair in ovarian cancer using the Oncomine Comprehensive Assay Plus.
articles.authors: Goetting I, Rau A, Russ L et al.
articles.abstract: Copyright: © 2026 Goetting et al. This is an open access article distributed under the terms of the Creative Commons Attribution License (CC BY 4.0), which permits unrestricted use, distribution, and reproduction in any medium, provided the original author and source are credited. Homologous recombination deficiency (HRD) is associated with response to poly (ADP-ribose) polymerase inhibitors (PARPi) in ovarian cancer and can be assessed through BRCA1/2 loss-of-function alterations and overall genomic instability. HRD status was characterized in 58 ovarian cancer samples, primarily high-grade serous ovarian carcinoma (HGSC, n = 52), using the Oncomine™ Comprehensive Assay (OCA) Plus. HRD status was determined based on BRCA1/2 variants and a genomic instability metric (GIM) and compared with the FDA-approved gold standard method MyChoice® CDx assay. Overall, 33 samples (56.9%) were HRD-positive, including 53.4% of HGSC samples. BRCA1/2 mutations were detected in 11 samples (19.0%), with BRCA1 more frequently affected. Concordance between OCA Plus and MyChoice CDx assays was 91.4% for BRCA1/2 alterations, 83.3% for GIM, and 86.0% for HRD classification. Additional alterations of potential clinical relevance such as variants in homologous recombination repair genes, including ATM, PTEN, FANCE, and CDK12, CCNE1 amplifications, and TP53 mutations (86.2%) were detected. Loss of heterozygosity in BRCA1/2-mutated samples suggested potential biallelic loss-of-function. HRD-positive tumors, including both BRCA1/2-mutated and BRCA-wild type cases, showed significantly longer recurrence-free survival and apparent clinical benefit from PARPi treatment. This study supports the feasibility of in-house HRD assessment using comprehensive genomic profiling panels for precise molecular characterization.

articles.title: PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors plus chemotherapy in cervical cancer: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.journal: Turkish journal of obstetrics and gynecology
articles.authors: Wijayanto FPS, Simanjuntak AMT, Sirait PCNB et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to appraise the comparative efficacy and safety of appending programmed death-1 (PD-1) or PD-ligand 1 (PD-L1) checkpoint blockade to standard chemotherapy in cervical cancer, with prespecified analyses across both the full randomized cohort and the PD-L1-enriched subset.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: In accordance with PRISMA 2020 guidelines, a comprehensive electronic search was conducted across PubMed, Scopus, the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, and ProQuest up to September 2025, targeting phase III randomized trials that incorporated PD-1 or PD-L1 blockade into a chemotherapy backbone. Pooled effect estimates were derived using random-effects modeling, generating hazard ratios (HR) for survival endpoints and risk ratios (RR) for tumor response. Methodological rigor was gauged with the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 tool, while small-study effects were explored through DOI plots supplemented by the LFK index.
RESULTS: Five phase III randomized controlled trials comprising 3,302 patients were included. The addition of PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors to chemotherapy significantly improved overall survival [HR: 0.66, 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.60-0.73] and progression-free survival (HR: 0.68, 95% CI: 0.60-0.78), with low heterogeneity I2=0%. Objective response rates was modestly increased (RR: 1.14, 95% CI: 1.02-1.26). Survival benefits were mainly driven by PD-1 inhibitors (pembrolizumab and cadonilimab), whereas PD-L1 inhibitors showed less consistent effects. Absolute survival gains within 24 months were modest. Immune-related endocrine events, particularly hyperthyroidism and hypothyroidism, were more frequent, but severe toxicities (grade ≥3) were not significantly increased.
CONCLUSION: PD-1-targeting immunochemotherapy prolongs survival in cervical cancer while maintaining acceptable tolerability, positioning it as a leading treatment option for eligible patients. Further biomarker-driven and head-to-head trials are needed to optimize treatment selection.

articles.title: The CLARK ratio: a novel metric for the conduct of outpatient hysteroscopy.
articles.authors: Clark TJ
articles.abstract: There is a balance between procedural success and patient acceptability in outpatient hysteroscopy. Reporting either outcome alone inadequately reflects how well the procedure was conducted. A new metric is proposed: the "Clark ratio", defined as patient acceptability divided by procedural failure, to capture this trade-off. Higher ratios indicate better performance. The limitations of data from randomised controlled trials and need for real-world evidence and standardised outcome measures to validate feasibility and patient experience is discussed. The Clark ratio is a new concept and could potentially be adopted, if found to be valid and useful, as a simple, easily interpretable, pragmatic benchmark for quality assurance and outcome in research for outpatient hysteroscopic procedures.

articles.title: Association of Lactate-to-Albumin Ratio With 28-Day Mortality in Critically Ill Patients With Obstructive Sleep Apnea: A Retrospective Cohort Study Based on the MIMIC-IV Database.
articles.authors: Zhou J, Chi C, Yu F et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is not uncommon among critically ill patients, especially in those with acute hypercapnic respiratory failure. Its high mortality rate remains a major challenge in the intensive care setting. The frequent apnea and respiratory failure during sleep in OSA patients, along with the intermittent hypoxemia caused by it, are accompanied by a series of systemic pathological and physiological changes. Metabolic imbalance is a key characteristic of the underlying pathological mechanism of this disease. However, the association between lactate-to-albumin ratio (LAR) and the prognosis of OSA patients remains to be fully elucidated. To date, a paucity of studies has evaluated the prognostic capabilities of these indicators. The majority of these studies have focused on the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) and platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR), and the results are contradictory, insufficient to fully clarify their clinical significance. Relying solely on lactate may not fully reflect patients' physiological conditions, whereas integrating LAR can provide a more comprehensive and accurate description of the metabolic state. This study aims to explore the relationship between LAR and 28-day mortality rates in ICU patients with OSA, using data from the MIMIC-IV database.
METHODS: Patients diagnosed with OSA were selected from the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV (v.2.2) database, identified by specific ICD-9 and ICD-10 codes (detailed in the Methods section). To assess the predictive power of LAR, receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis, Kaplan-Meier (K-M) survival curve analysis, logistic regression analysis, and subgroup analysis were employed. LAR was analyzed both as a categorical variable (based on the optimal cutoff) and as a continuous variable.
RESULTS: The sample population comprised 807 patients diagnosed with OSA who were admitted to the intensive care unit for the first time. The 28-day mortality rate was 20.44%. The area under the ROC curve (AUC) for LAR was 0.730 (95% CI: 0.686-0.772), which was comparable with OASIS (0.736; 95% CI: 0.695-0.776) and superior to SOFA (0.637; 95% CI: 0.591-0.683; DeLong test p = 0.500). The optimal cutoff value for LAR was 0.791. The high-LAR group demonstrated a poor prognosis in the K-M analysis (p < 0.001). Multivariate logistic regression demonstrated a significant association between LAR and unfavorable outcomes, with an odds ratio (OR) of 3.00…

articles.title: Adaptation to Clean Intermittent Catheterization From Introduction Through Implementation: What Patients and Families Need to Know: A Position Document From the International Children's Continence Society (ICCS).
articles.authors: Nieuwhof-Leppink AJ, Hayes LC, Clothier J et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Clean intermittent catheterization (CIC) plays a key role in the management of children whose neurological, anatomical, or functional conditions hinder complete or spontaneous bladder emptying. Its significance extends beyond clinical outcomes, influencing family relationships, psychosocial development, school experiences, and the child's long-term independence.
AIM: This position paper outlines the consensus of experts from the International Children's Continence Society (ICCS) on the broader impact of CIC on children with bladder dysfunction and their families. It offers practical recommendations for everyday life, integrating family perspectives, clinical experience, and observational insights. The paper addresses key aspects such as family dynamics, body image, self-esteem, school participation, peer relationships, and the transition to self-management and adulthood.
METHODS: The content is based on evidence from the scientific literature, supplemented by expert consensus in areas where direct research evidence is limited. Due to the paucity of studies specifically containing cohorts involving just children, studies involving heterogeneous populations (both children & adults) are cited. This is not meant to be a systematic review of all available literature involving CIC.
RESULTS: Central topics include optimal timing and preparation for initiating CIC, strategies to foster independence and reduce family stress, and school accommodations such as access to private facilities and flexible schedules to maintain privacy and dignity. It also highlights guidance on communication, social inclusion, and adolescent sexuality, supported through youth-focused counseling and peer networks. It provides checklists and evidence-based recommendations to help healthcare professionals, educators, and caregivers design individualized CIC plans that promote adherence, psychosocial well-being, and quality of life from childhood to adulthood.

articles.title: Understanding Cervical Screening Engagement Among Young South Asian Women: Perspectives of Women and Healthcare Professionals.
articles.journal: Health expectations : an international journal of public participation in health care and health policy
articles.authors: Merry K, Laheri Z, Johns S et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite increased uptake of the human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine, cervical screening participation among younger South Asian women has declined, particularly in deprived areas in England. The reasons for this pattern remain poorly understood. This study explored barriers and facilitators to cervical screening among South Asian women aged 25-29 in a deprived locality.
METHODS: Semi-structured interviews were conducted with South Asian women aged 25-29 (n = 15) and healthcare professionals involved in cervical screening delivery (n = 6) in Blackburn with Darwen. Data were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis.
RESULTS: Barriers to screening were multifactorial and included limited understanding of cervical screening and HPV, cultural norms surrounding modesty and sexuality, fear of community judgement and embarrassment, and structural challenges such as appointment access and competing responsibilities. Family networks acted as both barriers and facilitators. Healthcare professionals described adapting language to reduce fear, but highlighted service pressures related to staffing and funding, which constrained proactive engagement. Although most women reported receiving the HPV vaccination, understanding of HPV and the continued importance of cervical screening remained limited, highlighting opportunities to reinforce cervical screening education.
CONCLUSION: Cervical screening engagement among young South Asian women is shaped by intersecting cultural, emotional, and structural influences, which may be intensified in deprived settings. HPV vaccination should be accompanied by clear communication about the continued importance of cervical screening, particularly where knowledge and awareness remain low. Culturally responsive communication, flexible service provision and community partnership approaches are needed to address persistent inequalities in screening uptake.
PATIENT OR PUBLIC CONTRIBUTION: The study was informed by prior community engagement and public involvement work with underserved populations. Interview guides were developed in collaboration with a public advisor from the South Asian community to ensure they were relevant, inclusive, and reflective of community priorities.

articles.title: Calycosin Promotes Ferroptosis in Cervical Cancer via the AMPK/PI3K-TFEB-Autophagy-Lysosome Axis.
articles.authors: Zhang L, Shen Q, Zhu J et al.
articles.abstract: Cervical cancer ranks among the most common malignancies in women globally, and chemoresistance is a primary cause of treatment failure and patient mortality. Ferroptosis, an iron-dependent form of programmed cell death driven by lipid peroxidation, has been shown to reverse chemoresistance in tumor cells. Calycosin, a major active component of the traditional Chinese medicine Astragalus membranaceus, exhibits broad anti-tumor activity; however, whether it exerts anti-tumor effects in cervical cancer by inducing ferroptosis remains unclear. This study aimed to investigate the anti-tumor effects of calycosin on human cervical cancer cell lines and the molecular mechanisms underlying its induction of ferroptosis, with a specific focus on the regulatory roles of autophagy and lysosomal biogenesis and the associated signaling pathways. Cell viability was assessed using the CCK-8 assay, and cell proliferation was observed via EdU staining. Ultrastructural changes were examined by transmission electron microscopy (TEM). Levels of malondialdehyde (MDA), glutathione (GSH), and Fe2+ were measured using commercial kits. Protein expression related to ferroptosis, autophagy, lysosomes, and signaling pathways was detected by Western blotting. Mechanistic validation was performed using the ferroptosis inhibitor Fer-1, the autophagy inhibitor 3-MA, the lysosomal inhibitor chloroquine, and the PI3K inhibitor LY294002. An in vivo xenograft tumor model was established in nude mice. Calycosin significantly inhibited the proliferation of cervical cancer cells and induced ferroptosis, characterized by mitochondrial shrinkage, increased MDA and Fe2+ levels, decreased GSH levels, and downregulated expression of SLC7A11, GPX4, and FTH1 proteins. Concurrently, calycosin induced autophagy and lysosomal biogenesis, which enhanced the ferroptosis process. Mechanistically, calycosin promoted Beclin1-dependent autophagy by activating the AMPK/ULK1 pathway and inhibiting the PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway; furthermore, it promoted lysosomal biogenesis via the ERK/TFEB pathway, ultimately enhancing ferroptosis. In conclusion, calycosin induces ferroptosis in human cervical cancer cells through multi-pathway synergistic effects. The specific mechanisms include: (1) direct disruption of the System Xc-/GSH/GPX4 axis, triggering lipid peroxidation; (2) induction of protective autophagy via AMPK/ULK1 activation and PI3K/AKT/mTOR inhibition, thereby promoting ferroptosis; and (3) regulation of the…

articles.title: Predictive Nomogram for Reducing Urinary Tract Infection-Related Cancellations in Female Urodynamic Testing.
articles.authors: Wood NJ, Kasoff M, Carmain M et al.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Same-day cancellation of office-based urodynamic testing, frequently due to urinary tract infections (UTIs), can introduce financial and strategical burdens for both the patient and the clinic.
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to develop and internally validate a clinical prediction model for urodynamic procedure cancellation due to suspected UTI.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included patients scheduled for urodynamic testing at a single academic urogynecology practice (August 1, 2022, to April 30, 2024). Data was collected via electronic medical record review. Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator (LASSO) regression with 10-fold cross-validation was used for variable selection. A clinical prediction nomogram and web-based calculator were developed for clinical implementation.
RESULTS: A total of 841 patients were included (mean age 63 ± 13.9 years; mean BMI 29.7 ± 6.7 kg/m2). UTI-related cancellation occurred in 57 (6.8%) patients. After LASSO selection, 5 predictors were retained: age, POP-Q stage, BMI, recurrent UTI history, and diabetes. The model demonstrated good apparent discrimination (C-statistic 0.759; sensitivity 75.4%, specificity 62.8%, NPV 97.4%) with a Brier score of 0.060. Full-process bootstrap validation revealed a calibration slope of 0.992. Decision curve analysis confirmed net clinical benefit across threshold probabilities of 2--40%.
CONCLUSIONS: Several variables predict suspected UTI-related urodynamic cancellation, the most significant of which is age. This nomogram and online calculator provide clinicians with practical tools for identifying patients at elevated risk of procedure cancellation, enabling targeted preprocedural intervention.

articles.title: A virtual physicist framework integrating dose prediction and large language models for automated treatment planning.
articles.journal: Journal of applied clinical medical physics
articles.authors: Zhu H, Li J, Liang Y et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Automated radiotherapy treatment planning has benefited from data-driven approaches; however, achieving consistently high plan quality across patients remains challenging. Dose prediction models provide patient-specific priors but lack adaptive optimization, whereas large language models (LLMs) offer strong reasoning capabilities but raise concerns regarding stability and safety in clinical use.
PURPOSE: To develop and validate a fully automated VMAT treatment planning framework integrating dose prediction and LLM-driven dynamic optimization, termed the Virtual physicist (VP), and to evaluate its dosimetric performance, plan complexity, and consistency relative to manual and other automated planning strategies.
METHODS: A total of 70 cervical cancer patients previously treated with VMAT were retrospectively collected. The dataset was divided into 50 cases for training, 10 for validation, and 10 for testing. The input data consisted of patients' planning CT images with contoured planning target volumes (PTVs) and organs at risk (OARs). The outputs included predicted three-dimensional dose distributions (upper-, middle-, and lower-dose bands) and automatically generated VMAT treatment plans with corresponding dosimetric and plan complexity metrics. The VP framework was implemented in the MOZI treatment planning system via a Python scripting interface. A dose-band prediction model was used to initialize patient-specific optimization constraints. During optimization, an LLM iteratively adjusted objectives and weights based on real-time dosimetric feedback, subject to a rule-based safety engine enforcing clinical and physical constraints. Plans generated using dose prediction only (DP-only), LLM only (LLM-only), and combined dose prediction with LLM (DP + LLM) were compared with clinically delivered manual plans.
RESULTS: The DP + LLM strategy significantly improved sparing of the bladder and bilateral femoral heads compared with all three other strategies and significantly reduced rectal doses relative to the DP-only and manual plans (P < 0.05), while maintaining PTV Dmean, HI, CI, and GI comparable to those of the manual plans (P > 0.05). For dual-layer MLC plan complexity, DP + LLM produced a more balanced modulation pattern than manual planning, with lower distal-layer complexity-significant for d-C/A and d-MCS but not d-BA-and higher proximal-layer complexity across all three metrics. Compared with DP-only and LLM-only plans, DP + LLM showed a…

articles.title: PLP1-Associated Demyelinating Neuropathy in 2 Female Patients.
articles.authors: Brito da Silva A, Nicolas Vela M, Lai M et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The aim of this study was to report 2 unrelated women with demyelinating motor-predominant neuropathy in whom pathogenic variants in the proteolipid protein 1 gene (PLP1) were identified.
METHODS: Two unrelated female individuals underwent nerve conduction studies, EMG, evoked potential tests, neuroimaging, and targeted genetic testing.
RESULTS: The first patient, a 34-year-old woman, presented with foot drop and had electroneurographic findings consistent with a demyelinating motor-predominant neuropathy, with genetic testing revealing a pathogenic PLP1 variant. The second patient, also middle-aged, had a different pathogenic PLP1 variant and a clinical diagnosis of progressive spastic paraplegia, with detailed electrophysiologic assessment demonstrating a coexistent demyelinating motor-predominant neuropathy.
DISCUSSION: These cases demonstrate that PLP1-related disease in women can present in the fourth and fifth decades as a sporadic demyelinating motor-predominant neuropathy, which may be mistaken for an acquired immune-mediated neuropathy. In middle-aged women presenting with an apparently sporadic demyelinating motor neuropathy, genetic testing should, therefore, include PLP1. Recognizing PLP1 disease has important implications, such as access to emerging genetic therapies and the opportunity to offer preimplantation genetic testing to reduce the risk of transmission to offspring.

articles.title: Pre-exposure prophylaxis awareness, interest, and modality preferences to prevent HIV among cisgender women in the Dominican Republic and the United States.
articles.authors: Kerrigan D, Davis W, O'Rourke A et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Significant inequities in HIV incidence and prevalence exist among cisgender women (hereafter women), including a disproportionate burden of the epidemic among Black women in the United States and female sex workers globally. Women have limited awareness of and access to pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) for HIV pharmacoprevention.
METHODS: We explored PrEP awareness, interest, and modality preferences [daily oral vs. long-acting injectable (LAI) PrEP] in Santo Domingo, Dominican Republic (DR) and Washington, DC (DC) in the United States through in-depth interviews (IDIs) with women (N = 40) and healthcare providers (HCPs; N = 20) in 2021-2022 and surveys of women (N = 602) in 2022-2023. Thematic analysis andmultivariate regression were utilized.
RESULTS: Across settings, women were aged ≥18 years and HIV-negative; most were Black or multiracial, single, in their 30s, with >1 child. In IDIs, women characterized PrEP as an empowerment tool and welcomed modality options; HCPs across sites relayed a lack of comfort and preparation to address the unique needs of women and discuss LAI PrEP. In surveys, women reported low PrEP awareness and use: 29% (DC) and 6% (DR) had heard of daily oral PrEP, <6% had heard of LAI PrEP across sites, and 3% (DC) and 1% (DR) had ever used PrEP. Strong interest in taking PrEP varied (DC, 5%; DR, 80%). Modality preferences were similar, with most preferring LAI vs. daily oral PrEP (DC, 73%; DR, 71%). Across sites, preference for LAI PrEP was inversely associated with concern for injection pain/tenderness. In DC, LAI preference was associated with a higher score on a PrEP optimization/ considerations scale. In the DR, LAI preference was associated with injectable medication/contraception experience and alcohol use and inversely associated with PrEP stigma and partner violence.
DISCUSSION: Diverse groups of women have shared and unique drivers of PrEP modality preferences which should be considered when developing and tailoring multi-level interventions to promote PrEP awareness and uptake among women. These interventions should address social determinants and side effects and include HCP training and tools that promote shared decision-making.

articles.title: Treg and immune proliferative programs characterize anti-PD-1-responsive endometrial cancer: an integrative single-cell, spatial transcriptomic, and TCGA-UCEC reanalysis.
articles.authors: Zheng Y, Chen J, Wang Q et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The responses to programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1)-based therapy in advanced endometrial cancer are heterogeneous. The cellular programs associated with such responses remain incompletely defined, particularly when the immune cell composition, spatial expression patterns, and population-level transcriptomic features are considered together.
METHODS: Publicly available TCGA-UCEC and GSE251923 data were reanalyzed using bulk transcriptomics, single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), and the Visium expression space platform. The GSE251923 dataset included one anti-PD-1 responder and one non-responder; hence, all comparisons between these two cases are descriptive. Prespecified immune- and proliferation-related signatures were evaluated across the datasets, and the Visium clusters were assigned broad marker-based expression compartments. Exploratory quantitative reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (qRT-PCR) assays were used to examine selected transcripts in the Ishikawa and HEC-1A endometrial cancer cell lines under 1% O2 hypoxia and in primary neutrophils exposed to endometrial-cancer ascites-conditioned medium. These assays were used as ancillary models of condition-associated transcription; neither hypoxia nor ascites exposure was treated as a direct model of clinical immune checkpoint inhibitor response.
RESULTS: After quality control, we obtained 16,725 single cells that were assigned to 14 populations. Compared with the non-responder sample, the responder sample contained higher proportions of CD8 T cells [+3.1 percentage points (pp)], regulatory T cells (Tregs; +3.3 pp), B cells (+6.7 pp), plasma cells (+5.4 pp), CD4 T cells (+5.9 pp), and proliferating cells (+7.7 pp); the non-responder sample dominantly contained epithelial/tumor and endothelial cells. In TCGA-UCEC (553 tumors and 35 normal tissues), a high Treg signature was associated with longer overall survival [log-rank p = 0.047; hazard ratio (HR) = 0.58; 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.34-1.00], whereas a high proliferation signature was associated with shorter overall survival (HR = 1.72; 95% CI: 1.01-2.94; p = 0.046). The responder Visium section showed descriptively higher Treg and proliferation scores with lower epithelial and extracellular matrix scores. Under hypoxia, the two endometrial cancer cell lines showed higher MKI67, FOXP3, CXCL13, PDCD1, and CTLA4 transcript levels; the ascites-conditioned medium increased PAD4 and ELANE expressions in primary…

articles.title: Heart Transplant Rejection: From Histological Diagnosis to Precision Medicine.
articles.authors: Marzullo A, Salzillo C
articles.abstract: Heart transplantation remains the treatment of choice for patients with end-stage heart failure who are unresponsive to medical therapy or ventricular assist devices. Despite significant advances in surgical techniques and immunosuppressive protocols, heart transplant rejection (HTR) remains a major cause of morbidity and mortality among recipients. This narrative review summarizes current knowledge on HTR, with particular emphasis on immunopathogenic mechanisms, diagnostic approaches, histological classification, and therapeutic strategies, including the most recent non-invasive monitoring techniques. A narrative review of recent literature was conducted, including key publications and the updated International Society for Heart and Lung Transplantation (ISHLT) guidelines on rejection mechanisms, histological grading systems, and therapeutic strategies. HTR occurs via hyperacute, acute cellular, antibody-mediated, and chronic mechanisms, each characterized by complex immunological interactions between donor and recipient. Endomyocardial biopsy (EMB) remains the diagnostic gold standard, while innovations such as gene expression profiling, donor-derived cell-free DNA (dd-cfDNA), and donor-specific antibody (DSA) testing are redefining rejection monitoring. Modern immunosuppressive therapies, particularly tacrolimus-based regimens and B-cell-targeted agents, have reduced the incidence of rejection and improved graft survival. Ongoing refinement of diagnostic techniques and personalized immunosuppressive strategies is essential to enhance post-transplant outcomes. A multidisciplinary approach remains crucial for optimal management of HTR.

articles.title: Reproductive Factors and Pain Among Middle-Aged and Older Chinese Women: Cross-Sectional and Longitudinal Evidence from CHARLS.
articles.authors: Ding N, Sun H, Zhao J et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To examine reproductive factors and pain in middle-aged and older Chinese women.
METHODS: We used CHARLS data, combining the core survey with the Life History reproductive module. The cross-sectional analysis included 8532 women in 2018; the longitudinal analysis included 3856 women pain-free at the 2011 baseline with pain assessments in 2013, 2015, or 2018. The outcome was self-reported any pain, not clinically diagnosed chronic pain. Survey-weighted logistic regression estimated odds ratios (ORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Menopause exposures were evaluated in a postmenopausal-baseline sensitivity analysis; musculoskeletal pain sensitivity analyses tested robustness.
RESULTS: Cross-sectionally, three or more biological children (vs one, OR 1.30, 95% CI 1.06-1.61) and three or more miscarriages (vs none, OR 1.83, 95% CI 1.07-3.13) were associated with prevalent self-reported any pain in 2018. Longitudinally, 2743 women first reported pain during follow-up. Menarche after age 18 was associated with lower odds of first reported pain in the primary cumulative model (OR 0.66, 95% CI 0.49-0.87) and the discrete-time person-period analysis (OR 0.75, 95% CI 0.61-0.92). Three or more miscarriages were associated with higher odds in the primary longitudinal model (OR 3.66, 95% CI 1.01-13.32) but were imprecise and not significant in the person-period analysis. Early menopause was associated with follow-up pain only in the postmenopausal-baseline sensitivity analysis (OR 1.61, 95% CI 1.08-2.40). Cross-sectional findings were supported by musculoskeletal pain sensitivity analyses.
CONCLUSION: Later age at menarche was associated with lower odds of self-reported follow-up pain across two complete-case longitudinal modeling approaches, a signal that requires confirmation. Higher parity and multiple miscarriages were associated with prevalent pain cross-sectionally. The longitudinal signals for multiple miscarriages and early menopause were less robust and exploratory. Because the outcome was self-reported any pain rather than clinically diagnosed chronic pain, these associations are hypothesis-generating; prospective studies with standardized, chronic-pain-specific outcomes are needed.

articles.title: Nerve-Sparing Surgery for Parametrial Endometriosis.
articles.journal: JSLS : Journal of the Society of Laparoendoscopic Surgeons
articles.authors: Moustafa S, Zaradna A, Uzianbaeva L et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Surgical excision of parametrial endometriosis carries a risk of postoperative bladder, bowel, or sexual dysfunction due to pelvic autonomic nerve injury. Nerve-sparing surgery reduces these adverse effects and improves quality of life. However, experience remains limited, and further studies are needed to evaluate its feasibility and functional outcomes.
METHODS: This retrospective case series included 29 patients with advanced parametrial endometriosis who underwent nerve-sparing surgery. The primary objective was to evaluate postoperative urinary and defecatory function; the secondary objective was to assess surgical complications.
RESULTS: Among 29 patients, 7 (24.1%) had stage III disease and 22 (75.9%) had stage IV disease per American Association of Gynecologic Laparoscopists (AAGL) criteria. Surgical approaches included laparoscopy in 17 (58.6%), robotic surgery in 10 (34.5%), and conversion to laparotomy in 2 (6.9%). All cases involved nerve-sparing radical excision of endometriosis. Additional procedures included ureterolysis in all 29 patients (100%), enterolysis in 19 (65.5%), bowel shaving in 9 (31.0%), discoid resection in 5 (17.2%), segmental resection in 3 (10.3%), diaphragm excision in 2 (6.9%), partial cystectomy in 2 (6.9%), appendectomy in 3 (10.3%), and abdominal wall excision in 1 (3.4%). Operative time was 284 ± 99.3 min; estimated blood loss was 201 ± 216 mL. There was 1 intraoperative and 3 postoperative complications. One patient reported incomplete voiding with a postvoid residual under 100 mL, resolving within 1 week. Another reported increased bowel frequency that resolved within 1 month.
CONCLUSION: Nerve-sparing is critical in the surgical treatment of parametrial endometriosis to minimize compromise of urinary and defecatory function.

articles.title: Pararectal Leiomyosarcoma Following Total Laparoscopic Hysterectomy (TLH) for Initially Diagnosed Uterine Leiomyoma.
articles.authors: Monjé N, Alexa M, Hasenburg A et al.
articles.abstract: This case report highlights the diagnostic challenges of clinically distinguishing leiomyomas and leiomyosarcomas and the importance of post-hysterectomy monitoring. Patients with extensive prior oncological treatments and genetic cancer predisposition require individualized surveillance strategies, as they remain at elevated risk for secondary malignancies that may present in unusual locations or timeframes.

articles.title: Eicosapentaenoic acid exhibits antitumor effects and synergistically enhances carboplatin sensitivity in endometrial cancer.
articles.authors: Zhang H, Kong W, Chen S et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Obesity-related metabolic dysfunction and chronic inflammation are well-established drivers of the carcinogenesis and progression of endometrial cancer (EC). Eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA) is a long-chain omega-3 polyunsaturated fatty acid that has previously demonstrated broad anti-inflammatory and anti-tumor properties in various cancer models. In this study, we evaluated the anti-tumorigenic effects of EPA in EC cell lines and in a genetically engineered mouse model of endometrioid EC.
METHODS: Human EC cell lines, KLE and HEC-1B, were used to evaluate the effects of EPA alone or in combination with carboplatin on cell proliferation, invasion, cell cycle profile, stress response, and apoptosis. An LKB1 fl/fl p53  fl/fl genetically engineered mouse model of endometrioid EC was used to examine the effects of EPA on endometrial tumor growth.
RESULTS: EPA treatment markedly suppressed cell proliferation and colony formation in a dose-dependent manner. Mechanistically, EPA induced G1 cell cycle arrest, promoted cellular stress, and activated cleaved caspases, while inhibiting cell adhesion and migration. These phenotypes were accompanied by robust inhibition of the AKT/mTOR signaling axis and activation of MAPK-mediated stress pathways. Inflammatory signaling was similarly attenuated, as evidenced by reduced TNF-α-induced COX-2 expression and decreased phosphorylation of NF-κB. Importantly, EPA synergized with carboplatin to enhance anti-tumor efficacy. Combination treatment produced stronger suppression of cell proliferation and invasion, increased apoptotic activity, and downregulation of key survival and oncogenic regulators, including phosphorylated AKT, Bcl-2, β-catenin, and CDK4. Four weeks of EPA administration significantly reduced endometrial tumor burden in both obese and lean mice, accompanied by decreased expression of Ki-67, Bcl-xL, β-catenin, and COX-2 in endometrial tumor tissues.
CONCLUSION: EPA exerts potent anti-tumor activity in EC through coordinated modulation of oncogenic signaling, inflammatory pathways, cellular stress responses, and apoptosis. Moreover, its ability to enhance carboplatin sensitivity highlights the potential of EPA as an adjuvant therapeutic candidate for EC and warrants further investigation in preclinical models of EC.

articles.title: Clinical Outcomes and Safety Profile of Camrelizumab Plus Famitinib in Persistent, Recurrent, or Metastatic Cervical Cancer.
articles.authors: Liu X, Hua B, Xia Y et al.
articles.abstract: Background: Comparative real-world evidence for camrelizumab plus famitinib versus PD-1 inhibitor plus platinum- and/or taxane-based chemotherapy with or without bevacizumab in persistent, recurrent, or metastatic cervical cancer remains limited. This study evaluated the clinical outcomes and safety of these strategies. Methods: This single-center retrospective cohort study included 111 patients treated between July 2023 and October 2025; 42 received camrelizumab plus famitinib and 69 received the control regimen. Progression-free survival (PFS) was the primary endpoint. Overall survival (OS), tumor response, treatment-related adverse events (TRAEs), propensity score-based robustness analyses, and exploratory post-baseline marker analyses were also assessed. Results: Full-cohort and propensity score-matched Kaplan-Meier analyses showed longer PFS with camrelizumab plus famitinib (p = 0.026 and p = 0.004, respectively). Treatment-effect estimates also favored camrelizumab plus famitinib in unadjusted Cox (p = 0.028), residual imbalance-adjusted Cox (p = 0.041), 1:1 propensity score-matched Cox (p = 0.010), trimmed inverse probability of treatment weighting Cox (p = 0.006), and overlap-weighted Cox analyses (p = 0.005), whereas the prespecified baseline-adjusted Cox model was not statistically significant (p = 0.062). Disease control rate was higher (p = 0.038), grade 3-5 myelosuppression was lower (p = 0.010), and hypertension was higher (p = 0.023) with camrelizumab plus famitinib. OS did not differ significantly. Liver metastasis (p = 0.001) and higher baseline neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (p = 0.037) were associated with shorter PFS. Conclusions: Camrelizumab plus famitinib showed a favorable PFS signal across several analyses, higher disease control, and a distinct safety profile, while the primary baseline-adjusted estimate and OS remained statistically non-significant.

articles.title: Single-cell sequencing reveals immune networks and metabolic reprogramming in gynecological malignancies.
articles.authors: Ren L, Li X
articles.abstract: Gynecological malignancies, encompassing ovarian cancer (OC), endometrial cancer (EC), and cervical cancer (CC), represent a group of aggressive neoplasms that pose substantial threats to women's health worldwide. The complex tumor microenvironment (TME) plays a pivotal role in disease progression and therapeutic resistance. In recent years, single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) has enabled systematic characterization of the heterogeneity, functional states, and metabolic reprogramming features of tumor-infiltrating immune cells at unprecedented cellular resolution. Although remarkable progress has been achieved in this field, critical challenges persist, including insufficient understanding of the dynamic mechanisms governing immune cell subset transitions and the intricate regulatory networks underlying metabolism-immune crosstalk. This review summarizes recent advances in single-cell technologies applied to gynecological malignancies, focusing on immune cell subset diversity, intercellular communication networks, and the interplay between metabolic reprogramming and immunosuppression. Furthermore, we discuss potential therapeutic targets and biomarkers derived from these findings, aiming to provide a novel theoretical framework and translational strategies for precision immunotherapy.

articles.title: Institutional Perspectives on Assisted Reproductive Technology Using Third-Party Gametes in Japan: A Nationwide Survey of Assisted Reproductive Technology Facilities.
articles.authors: Takahashi N, Harada M, Koike H et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To clarify institutional perspectives on assisted reproductive technology (ART) using third-party gametes.
METHODS: We surveyed 634 facilities registered with the Japan Society of Obstetrics and Gynecology, and 416 responses were included in a descriptive analysis.
RESULTS: Psychosocial and economic stability of ART recipient couples were considered necessary in most facilities (94.6%). Japanese nationality and legal marriage were necessary recipient criteria in 36.8% and 54.3% facilities, respectively. Lower and upper age limits for female recipients were 20-25 and 43-45 years, respectively, whereas most male partners had no upper age limit (34.6%-36.6%). The most common upper age limit for oocyte donors was 35 years (67.9%). In contrast, upper age limits for sperm donors were more dispersed, with 40 years being the most common age at response to intrauterine insemination (35.6%) and in vitro fertilization (35.9%). The most accepted indications were hypergonadotropic hypogonadism for oocyte donation (87.5%) and failure to retrieve sperm via micro-testicular sperm extraction for donor sperm treatment (97.3%). Most facilities considered psychosocial support necessary.
CONCLUSIONS: This study provides a comprehensive overview of institutional perspectives on third-party ART in Japan. Although facilities showed substantial agreement on core principles, their views on specific eligibility and operational criteria varied.

articles.title: Ovarian Carcinoma: Signal Pathways and Clinical Studies.
articles.authors: Long Y, Shi H, Ye J et al.
articles.abstract: Ovarian carcinoma is the most lethal gynecologic malignancy, with a 5-year survival rate for advanced patients that has remained stubbornly low due to high recurrence and acquired drug resistance. Despite advances in surgery and chemotherapy, a critical gap remains in translating an understanding of the tumor's complex molecular heterogeneity into effective, durable treatments. This review systematically dissects the latest advances in key signaling pathways driving ovarian carcinoma pathogenesis, including the Notch, HER2, DNA damage repair (DDR), PI3K/AKT/mTOR, and angiogenesis (VEGF) pathways, and critically evaluates the clinical progress of corresponding targeted therapies. We particularly focus on the regulatory networks within the tumor microenvironment and the mechanisms of crosstalk between pathways that contribute to treatment resistance. The review synthesizes clinical study outcomes for novel agents such as PARP inhibitors (olaparib and niraparib), antibody-drug conjugates (e.g., T-DXd), and anti-angiogenic therapies (bevacizumab), while analyzing the challenges of primary and acquired resistance. By bridging fundamental pathway biology with emerging clinical data, this review provides a strategic framework for advancing precision medicine and developing rational combination therapies to improve outcomes for patients with this devastating disease.

articles.title: Contraceptive use and mental health among women of reproductive age: insights from the Mozambique Demographic and Health Survey.
articles.authors: Anaba EA, Wright ME, Alor SK et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Contraceptive use among women of reproductive age has increased significantly worldwide. However, little is known about contraceptive use and mental health among women in sub-Saharan African countries.
AIMS: This study sought to investigate contraceptive use and self-reported measures of depression and anxiety symptoms among reproductive-age women in Mozambique using the most recent national data.
METHOD: The study used secondary data from the 2022-2023 Demographic and Health Survey of Mozambique. A total of 6910 (weighted) sexually active women aged 15-49 years were included in this analysis. Anxiety and depression scores were measured using self-report questionnaires. Linear regression analysis was conducted to assess the associations between depression and anxiety and contraceptive use.
RESULTS: The prevalence of contraceptive use was 36.41%. About half of the hormonal contraceptive users (49.38%) were using injectables and 25.99% were using implants. In total, 9.14 and 2.83% of the women had moderate or high scores of self-reported anxiety respectively. Additionally, 5.24 and 5.42% reported moderate or high scores of depressive symptoms respectively. The use of hormonal contraceptives decreased anxiety symptoms by 0.47 units (β = -0.47; 95% CI -0.75 to -0.18; P < 0.001) compared with no contraceptive use. The use of hormonal contraceptives decreased depressive symptoms by 0.75 units (β = -0.75; 95% CI -1.11 to -0.39; P < 0.001) compared with no contraceptive use.
CONCLUSIONS: This study has demonstrated a naturalistic association between contraceptive use, particularly hormonal contraceptives, and decreased anxiety and depression among Mozambican women of reproductive age. This likely reflects a complex, bi-directional relationship, the nature and mechanism of which should be investigated in further experimental research.

articles.title: Metabolic Syndrome and Hand Osteoarthritis in Postmenopausal Women: Association With Disease Severity and Bone Mineral Density.
articles.authors: Rachidi S, Ait Malek S, Mariam E et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Hand osteoarthritis (HOA) is highly prevalent in postmenopausal women and may reflect an underlying metabolic disorder. Chronic low-grade inflammation driven by obesity, hyperglycemia, and estrogen deficiency may contribute to this metabolic phenotype. This study aimed to investigate the association between metabolic syndrome (MetS), its individual components, and HOA, and to explore its relationship with bone mineral density (BMD).
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective observational study, with descriptive and analytical components, including 252 postmenopausal women aged ≥50 years presenting with hand pain. MetS was defined according to the National Cholesterol Education Program Adult Treatment Panel III (NCEP-ATP III) criteria. HOA was assessed clinically and radiographically using the Kellgren-Lawrence (K&L) grading system. BMD was measured using dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DEXA), and vertebral fractures were evaluated using vertebral fracture assessment (VFA).
RESULTS: The mean age of participants was 62.6 ± 7.3 years, with a mean body mass index (BMI) of 32.3 ± 6.5 kg/m². The prevalence of symptomatic HOA was 28.3%, while radiographic HOA was observed in 19.1% of patients. MetS was present in 30.3% (n=76) of the cohort. HOA was significantly associated with advanced age, higher BMI, and MetS (p < 0.001). Radiographic severity of HOA increased significantly with age, body weight, duration of menopause, and metabolic abnormalities. Increased severity was also associated with lower BMD and a higher prevalence of vertebral fractures (p < 0.001). In multivariate analysis, MetS was independently associated with symptomatic HOA (OR 4.3; 95% CI: 1.92-9.12; p < 0.001), along with hypertension. While no overall association was found between HOA and BMD, lower BMD and vertebral fractures were significantly associated with increased radiographic severity of HOA.
CONCLUSION: HOA in postmenopausal women is strongly associated with MetS, supporting the concept of a metabolic phenotype of osteoarthritis. These findings emphasize the importance of comprehensive cardiometabolic risk assessment in the management of HOA and suggest a link between disease severity and bone fragility. As the first study of its kind conducted in Morocco, further large-scale multicenter studies are needed to confirm these findings.

articles.title: Prenatal diagnostic outcomes and positive predictive values in 1,326 pregnancies with high-risk non-invasive prenatal testing results.
articles.authors: Du R, Zhao B, Shi X et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the prenatal diagnostic outcomes of pregnant women with high-risk non-invasive prenatal testing (NIPT) results and to explore factors influencing the positive predictive value (PPV) of NIPT.
METHODS: Clinical data from 1,326 pregnant women with high-risk NIPT results who underwent invasive prenatal diagnosis at Hebei General Hospital between January 2014 and December 2023 were retrospectively analyzed. Chromosomal karyotyping, fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH), and/or copy number variation sequencing (CNV-seq) were used as confirmatory diagnostic methods. PPVs were compared across different types of chromosomal abnormalities, maternal age groups, Z-score categories, ultrasound findings, and before and after implementation of the free NIPT screening policy.
RESULTS: Among the 1,326 pregnancies with high-risk NIPT results, 648 were confirmed as true positives, yielding an overall PPV of 48.87%. The PPVs for trisomy 21 (T21), trisomy 18 (T18), trisomy 13 (T13), and sex chromosome abnormalities (SCAs) were 78.61%, 56.36%, 10.53%, and 47.11%, respectively. The PPVs for common autosomal trisomies were higher in the advanced maternal age group than in the non-advanced maternal age group. After implementation of the free screening program, the PPVs for T21, T18, and T13 showed a slight numerical increase, the difference between groups was not statistically significant. PPVs increased with higher Z-scores and were further elevated when multiple ultrasound soft markers or structural anomalies were present. Among SCAs, the PPV for sex chromosome gains was significantly higher than that for sex chromosome losses.
CONCLUSION: NIPT demonstrated high screening performance for T21 and T18, whereas T13 and SCAs were associated with relatively high false-positive risks. Clinical interpretation of high-risk NIPT results should integrate maternal age, Z-score, ultrasound phenotype, and confirmatory prenatal diagnostic findings to facilitate stratified genetic counseling and optimize pregnancy management.

articles.title: Clinical Characteristics Associated with Biochemical Pregnancy Occurrence Among IVF Patients with Tubal Disorders: A Single-Centre Retrospective Cohort Study in Indonesia.
articles.authors: Pertiwi IP, Syam HH, Achmad ED
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Infertility is a complex reproductive health condition requiring individualized management. Although in vitro fertilization (IVF) has become an established treatment option, early pregnancy outcomes vary among patients due to differences in maternal, ovarian, uterine, and treatment-related characteristics. This study aimed to evaluate clinical characteristics associated with biochemical pregnancy occurrence among women undergoing IVF, with further evaluation among patients with documented tubal disorders.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: This retrospective cohort study was conducted at the Infertility Clinic of Aster, Dr. Hasan Sadikin General Hospital, Bandung, Indonesia. Women who underwent IVF between January 2019 and December 2023 were identified from clinical records and invited to participate. Biochemical pregnancy occurrence was defined as a positive serum β-human chorionic gonadotropin (β-hCG) result following IVF treatment, obtained through structured telephone interviews based on participants' reported results. Clinical characteristics were analyzed using Chi-square or Fisher's exact test for categorical variables and independent t-test or Mann-Whitney U-test for continuous variables, as appropriate. A p-value of <0.05 was considered statistically significant.
RESULTS: Among 89 women included, biochemical pregnancy occurred in 40 patients (44.9%). Female age (p=0.033), duration of infertility (p<0.001), and AMH level (p=0.003) were associated with biochemical pregnancy occurrence. Among patients with tubal disorders (n=40), diminished ovarian reserve (p=0.031), uterine fibroids (p=0.038), and history of pelvic inflammatory disease (p=0.004) were associated with biochemical pregnancy occurrence.
CONCLUSION: Several clinical characteristics were associated with biochemical pregnancy occurrence among women undergoing IVF. These findings should be interpreted as exploratory associations because multivariable adjustment was not performed. Further prospective multicenter studies with comprehensive IVF-related data are needed to validate these findings.

articles.title: Complete Surgical Resection of Rare Solitary Anterior Mediastinal Metastasis From Ovarian Clear Cell Carcinoma.
articles.authors: Chiba T, Yano K, Imoto T et al.
articles.abstract: Epithelial ovarian cancer typically spreads via transcoelomic dissemination and lymphatic pathways. Extra-abdominal metastases presenting as solitary anterior mediastinal lesions are rare. Ovarian clear cell carcinoma (CCC) is characterized by aggressive local behaviour but has a lower propensity for distant metastasis than serous carcinoma. Furthermore, it is less sensitive to platinum-based chemotherapy than other epithelial ovarian cancers. Here, we report a rare case of ovarian CCC with a solitary anterior mediastinal metastasis after primary surgery. A woman in her 50s had a 2.6-cm anterior mediastinal mass during postoperative surveillance. Considering progressive lesion enlargement and increased 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose uptake on positron emission tomography-computed tomography, complete surgical resection via median sternotomy was performed. Histopathological and immunohistochemical findings confirmed the presence of metastatic ovarian CCC. The patient remained disease-free for 6 months postoperatively. Complete surgical resection may represent an effective treatment option for isolated recurrence of chemoresistant histological subtypes.

articles.title: Impacts of Oliceridine versus Sufentanil on the Quality of Postoperative Recovery in Elective Gynecological Laparoscopic Surgery: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.authors: Jiang C, Song R, Wang D et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Oliceridine is a novel μ-opioid receptor agonist selectively activating the G protein signaling pathway. This study aimed to explore the influences of patient-controlled intravenous analgesia (PCIA) employing oliceridine and sufentanil on the postoperative recovery of patients undergoing elective laparoscopic gynecological surgery.
METHODS: This study included 136 patients aged 18-65 years who were randomized to receive elective gynecological laparoscopic surgery under general anaesthesia with administering PCIA with oliceridine or sufentanil. The primary outcome was the Quality of Recovery - 15 (QoR-15) score on postoperative day 1 (POD 1). Secondary outcome measures comprised: the overall benefit of analgesic score (OBAS) on POD 1; time to first flatus; time to first ambulation; postoperative hospital stay; QoR-15 score on POD 2 and 3; PCIA total injected drugs; the number of patients requiring rescue analgesia and rescue antiemetics; VAS scores from T1 to T6, and MOAA/S scores from T1 to T5; the incidence rate of adverse events; perioperative vital signs.
RESULTS: In the primary ITT analysis using multiple imputation (n=136), analysis of covariance adjusting for baseline QoR‑15 score showed that the group O had significantly higher QoR‑15 scores on POD 1 than the group S, with the adjusted mean difference of 11.94 points (95% CI: 10.02-13.86; p < 0.001). Statistical differences between the two groups were observed in POD 1 OBAS score, time to first flatus, time to first ambulation, hospital discharge duration, and QoR-15 scores on POD 2 and 3. In addition, compared with the sufentanil group, the oliceridine group was observed to have a lower incidence of opioid-related adverse events.
CONCLUSION: In this single-center study of relatively young and healthy female patients undergoing gynecologic laparoscopic surgery, oliceridine demonstrated superior recovery quality compared with sufentanil, with a between-group difference exceeding the 6-point MCID threshold. It also significantly accelerated gastrointestinal recovery, shortened hospital stay.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: This study was registered with the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR2400090783).

articles.title: Association between preconception serum lipid levels and pregnancy complications in singleton live births from IVF/ICSI with fresh embryo transfers.
articles.authors: Cai WY, Luo X, Zhang Q et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: This study aimed to examine how preconception serum lipid profiles are associated with pregnancy complications in women who achieved singleton live births following assisted reproductive technology (ART).
METHODS: This study included 1,036 women who had singleton births after ART. Preconception serum lipid measurements included low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C), high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C), total cholesterol (TC), and triglycerides (TG).
