The pregnancy complication outcomes included cesarean section, gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM), preeclampsia, preterm delivery (PTD), small for gestational age (SGA), large for gestational age (LGA), low birthweight (LBW), macrosomia, and neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) admission.
RESULTS: The incidence of cesarean section, GDM, preeclampsia, PTD, SGA, LGA, LBW, macrosomia, and NICU admission was 51.6%, 3.8%, 0.7%, 7.6%, 6.8%, 15.6%, 6.4%, 5.7%, and 1.8%, respectively. Women with dyslipidemia had higher rates of GDM (11.7% vs. 2.1%, p < 0.001), PTD (13.9% vs. 6.3%, p < 0.001), and LWB (10.6% vs. 5.5%, p = 0.012). After adjusting for possible confounders, TG (OR 1.49[1.11-1.99]) was positively associated with PTD. TC (OR 1.48[1.08-2.02]), LDL-C (OR 1.48[1.03-2.14]), and HDL-C (OR 3.03[1.19-7.73]) were positively associated with SGA. TC (OR 2.22[1.63-3.04]) and TG (OR 1.20[1.00-1.44]) were positively associated with GDM.
CONCLUSION: Preconception serum lipid levels were associated with pregnancy complications in women receiving ART.

articles.title: Exploring Health-Seeking Behaviors in Iranian Women with High-Risk Pregnancy: A Qualitative Study.
articles.journal: International journal of community based nursing and midwifery
articles.ta: Int J Community Based Nurs Midwifery
articles.authors: Jamali S, Mohammadi S, Javadifar N et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Health-seeking behaviors are essential for preventing pregnancy complications and improving maternal and fetal health outcomes. In high-risk pregnancies, these behaviors constitute a complex process influenced by various individual, cultural, and socioeconomic factors. This study aimed to explore the health-seeking behaviors of Iranian women experiencing high-risk pregnancy.
METHODS: This qualitative study was conducted from August 2024 to March 2025 in Ahvaz, Iran. Using purposive sampling with maximum variation, 24 participants (18 women with high-risk pregnancies and 6 healthcare providers) were interviewed. Data were collected using in-depth, semi-structured interviews and continued until data saturation was achieved. The data were analyzed using conventional qualitative content analysis based on the Elo and Kyngäs framework. MAXQDA software version 20 was used for data organization and management.
RESULTS: The data analysis identified three main categories and seven subcategories. The categories included proactive health-seeking behaviors (health monitoring and care, and lifestyle-related behaviors), reactive health-seeking behaviors (therapeutic and care reactions, information-seeking reactions, and psychological reactions for stress management), and avoidant behaviors (avoidance of seeking help and medical services and avoidance of social interaction).
CONCLUSION: Women with high-risk pregnancies exhibit diverse health-seeking behaviors. A comprehensive understanding of these patterns enables healthcare providers and intervention program designers to deliver targeted education and support, thereby reducing avoidant behaviors, promoting proactive actions, and ultimately improving maternal and fetal health outcomes.

articles.title: Maternal cardiac and perinatal outcomes among pregnant individuals with tetralogy of Fallot.
articles.authors: Patel R, Singer A, Gentile B et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Tetralogy of Fallot (TOF) is associated with maternal-fetal risks during pregnancy, particularly in those with uncorrected or residual defects.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study identified pregnancies with TOF and compared them with pregnancies with other congenital heart diseases (CHDs) using ICD-10 codes, between 5/23/22 and 5/22/25. Demographic and clinical characteristics were analyzed using analysis of variance or Student's t-tests for continuous variables and chi-square tests for categorical variables.
RESULTS: There were 1574 women (1961 pregnancies) with TOF compared to 37,899 women (47,239 pregnancies) with other CHD. Significant differences in cardiac outcomes were observed in arrhythmias (32.9% vs. 18.3%), particularly ventricular arrhythmias (6.8% vs. 2.1%) and endocarditis (2.4% vs. 1.5%). Significant perinatal outcomes included preterm delivery (17% vs. 14.1%) and earlier gestational age at delivery (37.4 ± 3 vs. 38.9 ± 1.7).
CONCLUSIONS: Pregnancies with TOF have a greater occurrence of adverse cardiac outcomes, particularly arrhythmias and endocarditis, and obstetric outcomes, including preterm delivery.

articles.title: Improving detection and treatment of psychological distress during menopause: evidence from a clinical hormone replacement therapy cohort.
articles.authors: Hendriks O, Kamal A, Saini P et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Menopausal transition is a period of psychological vulnerability, yet suicidality remains underassessed. Hormone replacement therapy (HRT) may influence mood symptoms, but its mental health effects - particularly regarding suicidality - are poorly understood.
AIMS: To evaluate changes in depressive symptoms, menopause-related distress and suicidality among menopausal women attending a specialist clinic, and explore whether outcomes differed across HRT regimens and baseline risk factors.
METHOD: We analysed routinely collected data from 957 women attending a UK menopause clinic. All participants received some form of treatment following their initial consultation. Participants completed the Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9) and Menopause Depression Rating Scale (MENO-D) at baseline and follow-up (2-6 months later). Mixed-design analyses of variance assessed changes over time, including interaction effects for HRT type and baseline risk factors (body mass index (BMI), smoking, suicidality, antidepressant use).
RESULTS: Depressive symptoms and menopause-related psychological distress significantly declined over time (around 46% reduction on average). The largest improvements were observed among women receiving oestrogen-progesterone-testosterone combinations, although similar gains were also seen in oestrogen-progesterone and oestrogen-testosterone groups. Suicidality (PHQ-9 item 9) decreased by 92% among those with baseline ideation, but this was not moderated by HRT type. Self-worth (MENO-D item 4) also improved, but similarly showed no significant moderation by HRT regimen. Higher BMI was associated with worse baseline mental health, but did not moderate treatment outcomes.
CONCLUSIONS: Combined HRT, including formulations with testosterone, was associated with substantial improvements in mental health outcomes. Suicidality was a distinct symptom profile, often underdetected by general depression scores. However, findings are exploratory and should be interpreted cautiously because of the lack of a control group, observational design and small sample sizes in some subgroups. These results highlight the need for menopause-sensitive mental health assessments and integration of psychological screening into routine menopausal care.

articles.title: Transcriptomic analysis of the fungal pathogen Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. albedinis (Foa) during colonization of date palm reveals distinct temporal transcriptional trajectories and uncovers novel candidate effectors.
articles.authors: Mbaye AL, Diouf AM, Deh M et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Bayoud disease, caused by Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. albedinis (Foa), represents a major threat to date palm cultivation and oasis ecosystems. Understanding the molecular mechanisms underlying Foa infection is essential for developing effective control strategies.
METHODS: In this study, we performed a temporal transcriptomic analysis of three Foa isolates (FoaER10, FoaER20, and FoaZG10) during colonization of date palm roots at four infection stages (0, 8, 16, and 24 days post-inoculation).
RESULTS: Differential gene expression analysis revealed extensive and stage-dependent transcriptional reprogramming, with the number of significant differentially expressed genes ranging from 4,914 to 6,895 per isolate, and 8,453 unique genes significantly differentially expressed across the three isolates. Comparative analysis identified a core set of 1,079 consistently up-regulated and 123 down-regulated genes, alongside 2,376 genes showing opposite regulation directions between isolates. Functional annotation highlighted carbohydrate-active enzymes (CAZymes), MFS membrane transporters, and candidate effectors including necrosis-inducing-like proteins (NLPs), Hce2/Ecp2, and SIX proteins.
DISCUSSION: This study provides a comprehensive transcriptomic resource for understanding Foa-date palm interactions and establishes a foundation for targeted disease management strategies.

articles.title: Preoperative ovarian vascular parameters and perioperative factors associated with ovarian reserve marker decline after laparoscopic endometrioma cystectomy: a retrospective prediction study.
articles.authors: Wu M, Qin M, Zhang L
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Laparoscopic cystectomy is a commonly used surgical treatment for ovarian endometrioma, but postoperative reduction in ovarian reserve markers is a recognized concern. Preoperative identification of women at increased risk may support counseling and surgical planning. This study evaluated whether multidimensional ovarian vascular and hemodynamic ultrasound parameters are associated with subsequent decline in ovarian reserve markers.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the association of preoperative multidimensional ultrasound parameters with postoperative ovarian reserve marker decline and to develop an exploratory perioperative prediction model.
METHODS: A retrospective cohort of 280 reproductive-age women undergoing laparoscopic ovarian endometrioma cystectomy (May 2021-May 2024) was analyzed. Transvaginal color Doppler ultrasound on menstrual cycle days 2-5 yielded 2D morphological parameters [ovarian volume [OV], antral follicle count [AFC]], 3D vascular parameters [vascularization index [VI], flow index [FI], vascularization-flow index [VFI]], and spectral Doppler parameters (resistance index [RI], pulsatility index [PI], peak systolic velocity [PSV], end-diastolic velocity [EDV]). Serum AMH, FSH, LH, and E2 were measured. Ovarian reserve markers were reassessed at 3, 6, and 12 months. The primary 6-month outcome was a study-specific composite decline in ovarian reserve markers. Exploratory multivariable logistic regression was used to construct a perioperative model, and internal optimism was estimated by 1,000 bootstrap resamples. Apparent discrimination was assessed by ROC analysis.
RESULTS: At 6 months, 118 of 280 patients (42.1%) met the study-specific composite outcome. Women meeting the outcome had lower preoperative VI, VFI, FI, PSV, and EDV and higher RI and PI (all P < 0.01). Pearson correlations showed moderate associations of vascular parameters with 6-month AMH and FSH levels. AMH decreased after surgery in both groups, with a greater reduction in patients meeting the composite outcome; significant effects of time, group, and group-by-time interaction were observed (all P < 0.001). The exploratory perioperative logistic model retained age, bilateral cysts, preoperative maximum cyst diameter, intraoperative r-AFS score, preoperative VI, and preoperative RI. Higher VI was associated with lower odds of the composite outcome, whereas higher RI was associated with greater odds. The composite model had an apparent AUC of 0.888 (95% CI…

articles.title: Six-Month Changes in BMI, Menstrual-Cycle Characteristics, and Ferriman-Gallwey Scores Associated With a Multi-ingredient Nutritional Supplement Blend in Women With PCOS: A Prospective Observational Study.
articles.authors: Abdelrazzak A, Salman FK, Hammoud A et al.
articles.abstract: Introduction Multi-ingredient nutritional supplements combining insulin-sensitizing and anti-androgenic compounds are increasingly used in polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), yet evidence on their combined clinical effects remains limited. This study aimed to evaluate whether the use of a multi-ingredient nutritional supplement blend containing myo-inositol, α-lipoic acid, N-acetylcysteine, saw palmetto, and folic acid was associated with six-month changes in body mass index (BMI), menstrual-cycle characteristics, and Ferriman-Gallwey hirsutism scores in women with PCOS. Methods Thirty-five Lebanese women with PCOS aged 18 to 40 and not receiving metformin or hormonal therapy were enrolled. BMI, menstrual cycle frequency, and Ferriman-Gallwey hirsutism scores were assessed at baseline. Hirsutism was reassessed at two and six months, while BMI and cycle regularity were reassessed at six months. Paired analyses and a linear mixed-effects model for repeated Ferriman-Gallwey scores were applied as appropriate, with significance set at p < 0.05. Three participants were lost to follow-up. Results At six months (N=32), mean BMI decreased significantly from 26.5 ± 2.8 to 25.7 ± 2.5 kg/m² among participants with complete paired BMI data (mean change = -0.88 ± 1.56 kg/m²; p = 0.003). Ferriman-Gallwey scores declined from 15.3 ± 3.2 at baseline to 15.1 ± 3.0 at 2 months and 14.4 ± 2.6 at 6 months. In a linear mixed-effects model, the baseline-to-six-month reduction remained statistically significant (mean difference: -1.08; 95% CI: -1.38 to -0.77; Holm-adjusted p < 0.001), while the smaller baseline-to-two-month change did not remain statistically significant after adjustment for multiple comparisons. Menstrual cycle regularity showed a non-significant improving trend (regular cycles: 8.6% to 18.8%; p=0.250). Conclusions Six months of using the supplement blend was associated with a modest reduction in BMI and a statistically significant but small baseline-to-six-month reduction in Ferriman-Gallwey hirsutism scores, with no statistically significant improvement in menstrual-cycle regularity. These observational findings should be interpreted as preliminary and support further randomized controlled trials with standardized lifestyle monitoring, objective metabolic and hormonal outcomes, and systematic safety assessment.

articles.title: Immunotherapy in Advanced Epithelial Ovarian Cancer: Successes and Frustrations.
articles.authors: Marshall LA, Ayoub NL, Tseng J et al.
articles.abstract: Epithelial ovarian cancer (EOC) is most commonly diagnosed at an advanced stage and is known to recur frequently. Recurrent EOC can be difficult to treat, with limited effective options for systemic therapy. Platinum-resistant and -refractory recurrences are particularly difficult to treat, with even fewer therapeutic options than for platinum-sensitive recurrences. Less common histologic subtypes are also challenging, often with poor responses to typical systemic therapies and limited clinical trial data. With successes in the use of immunotherapy (IO) in other types of solid tumors, IO has been investigated extensively in EOC. However, the incorporation of IO in the treatment of EOC has yielded variable results; of the many clinical trials studying IO in ovarian cancer, there are very few positive results. This article discusses the role of the immune system in cancer proliferation and IO mechanisms of action, reviews clinical trials involving the use of immune checkpoint inhibition (ICI) in EOC, and considers the role of biomarkers in the use of IO. We also discuss the possible reasons for why most EOCs do not seem to respond as well as other solid tumors do to IO, as well as discuss the EOCs that have shown more promising responses, namely platinum-resistant disease and clear cell histology. The overarching aim of this review is to comprehensively digest the large volume of existing research pertaining to the use of IO in the treatment of ovarian cancer and examine the pitfalls and possibilities for future success in the use of IO in EOC.

articles.title: Hsa_Circ_0000615-Encoded 250-Amino Acid Polypeptide Suppresses Epithelial Ovarian Cancer Progression via Promoting HMGB1 Nuclear Accumulation.
articles.authors: Guo Z, Deng S, Meng J et al.
articles.abstract: Objectives: Circular RNAs (circRNAs) can encode functional peptides to regulate tumor progression, yet the roles of circRNA-encoded peptides in epithelial ovarian cancer (EOC) remain poorly understood. This study aimed to investigate the function of hsa_circ_0000615 (circ_0615) and its encoded polypeptide in EOC and explore its potential pre-clinical value as a candidate therapeutic target. Methods: We detected circ_0615 expression in EOC clinical tissues and cell lines. In vitro functional assays, in vivo xenograft and Patient-derived xenograft (PDX) models with adeno-associated virus (AAV)-mediated overexpression were used to assess tumor-suppressive phenotypes. Mass spectrometry, co-immunoprecipitation, western blotting, immunofluorescence, and chromatin immunoprecipitation were applied to characterize the circ_0615-encoded polypeptide Zinc Finger Protein 609-250-amino acid (ZNF609-250aa) and its interaction with high-mobility group box 1 (HMGB1). Results: circ_0615 was downregulated in EOC tissues and cell lines. Circ_0615 overexpression suppressed EOC proliferation and migration in vitro and in vivo. Mechanistically, circ_0615 promoted translation of ZNF609-250aa via eukaryotic translation initiation factor 2 subunit 1 (eIF2α). ZNF609-250aa bound HMGB1, reduced its ubiquitination, and promoted HMGB1 nuclear accumulation, which may contribute to repression of aldehyde dehydrogenase 1 family member A1 (ALDH1A1) transcription. AAV2/8-ZNF609-250aa restrained tumor growth in PDX models. Conclusion: Circ_0615-encoded ZNF609-250aa acts as a tumor suppressor in EOC, partially through modulating ZNF609-250aa-HMGB1-related molecular events. This study provides novel mechanistic insights and promising pre-clinical candidate targets requiring further validation for EOC intervention.

articles.title: Complication-specific microbial signatures in gestational diabetes mellitus, hypertensive disorders of pregnancy, and fetal macrosomia: a multi-site analysis of the maternal saliva-amniotic fluid-neonatal meconium continuum.
articles.authors: Li Y, Qiao B, Ma C et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM), hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP), and fetal macrosomia (FM) are common pregnancy complications threatening maternal-infant health. However, due to a lack of systematic analysis, whether these complications are associated with distinct cross-site microbial patterns along the saliva-amniotic fluid-meconium axis remains unclear.
METHODS: In this study, 162 samples (54 each of maternal saliva, amniotic fluid, and neonatal meconium) from 54 mother-neonate pairs (20 normal controls (NC), 18 GDM, 6 FM, and 10 HDP) were analyzed by 16S rRNA gene sequencing.
RESULTS: In the NC group, the microbial composition of meconium was significantly distinct from that of saliva and amniotic fluid, while saliva and amniotic fluid exhibited relatively similar structures. Microbial richness in meconium was significantly reduced in the HDP and FM groups. The HDP group was enriched with Klebsiella, Enterobacter, and Sphingomonas. The FM group was enriched with Staphylococcus and Methyloversatilis, and the GDM group was enriched with Bergeyella and Helicobacter. In amniotic fluid samples, the HDP group was enriched with Emticicia, the FM group with Comamonadaceae, and the GDM group with Lactobacillus iners. Cross-site concordance analysis revealed that Prevotella, Neisseria, Haemophilus, and Streptococcus exhibited a continuous abundance gradient across saliva, amniotic fluid, and meconium in the HDP group, suggesting potential cross-site microbial transfer. In the FM group, Fusobacterium showed a pattern of detection in amniotic fluid with increased abundance in meconium, while Paucibacter was predominantly detected in meconium, a pattern potentially consistent with maternal contact during delivery. Correlation analyses showed that Rothia was positively correlated with triglycerides, Neisseria with glycated hemoglobin, and Methyloversatilis with pre-pregnancy body mass index (BMI) (p < 0.05).
CONCLUSION: This study is the first to systematically compare the effects of GDM, HDP, and FM on the microbiota of maternal saliva, amniotic fluid, and neonatal meconium, revealing complication-specific microbial signatures and dynamic cross-site concordance patterns along the saliva-amniotic fluid-meconium axis.

articles.title: High-risk factors associated with persistence and progression of cervical intraepithelial neoplasia 2 in women of reproductive age undergoing conservative management: a retrospective analysis.
articles.authors: Chen M, Xiao G, Xiao H et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the high-risk factors associated with the persistence or progression of cervical intraepithelial neoplasia 2 (CIN2) to cervical intraepithelial neoplasia 3 (CIN3) in women of childbearing age undergoing conservative management, thereby providing guidance for selecting appropriate treatment strategies for women with CIN2 who wish to preserve their fertility.
METHODS: Univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses were performed using the clinical and pathological characteristics of the included patients to identify high-risk factors associated with the persistence or progression of CIN2.
RESULTS: In total, 226 patients were included in this study. Of these, 142 (62.8%) experienced lesion regression, 58 (25.7%) had persistent CIN2, and 26 (11.5%) progressed to CIN3. Univariate analysis indicated that age, high- squamous intraepithelial lesion (HSIL), human papillomavirus type 16/18 (HPV16/18) positivity, and P16/Ki-67 positivity were associated with persistence of CIN2 or progression to CIN3. Multivariate analysis revealed that age of >35 years (OR 2.732, 95% CI 1.350-5.529), HPV16/18 positivity (OR 1.506, 95% CI 1.129-17.611), HSIL (OR 4.693, 95% CI 3.554-19.211), and P16/Ki-67 positivity (OR 4.007, 95% CI 2.819-6.014) were associated with persistence or progression of CIN2.
CONCLUSION: Age of >35 years, HPV16/18 positivity, HSIL, and P16/Ki-67 positivity are associated with persistence and progression of CIN2. Conservative management with outpatient follow-up is an appropriate treatment option for carefully selected patients without these high-risk factors.

articles.title: PPP2R1A-mediated tumor-stromal adhesion as an unrecognized mechanism of immunosuppression.
articles.authors: Markosian C, Staquicini DI, Tang FHF et al.
articles.abstract: PPP2R1A, the predominant scaffolding subunit of the larger serine/threonine protein phosphatase 2A (PP2A), has been implicated in several solid tumors. Recently, somatic inactivating mutations in PPP2R1A have been shown to be associated with increased intratumoral inflammation and improved survival in patients undergoing dual immune checkpoint blockade for platinum-resistant ovarian clear-cell carcinoma. However, the structural and functional basis for this biological phenomenon has not yet been elucidated. We have previously reported PPP2R1A-mediated heterotypic-homodimeric protein-protein interactions between melanoma cells and lymphatic endothelial cells. Here, we demonstrate that PPP2R1A is also present on the surface of ovarian cancer cells. Moreover, we propose that the disruption of such tumor-lymphatic homodimeric interactions and thereby their interface may potentially be a causative factor for enhanced immune cell enrichment and inflammatory signaling within the tumor microenvironment, ultimately translating to improved survival with immune checkpoint inhibitors.

articles.title: Decoding the phosphorylation landscape of ITPR3 across calcium signaling and regulatory networks in cancer.
articles.authors: Rai SB, Sujina A, Kammarambath SR et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: ITPR3 is an endoplasmic reticulum Ca2+ release channel that plays an important role in intracellular calcium signaling and has been implicated in cancer-associated cellular processes. Although several phosphorylation sites have been identified in ITPR3, the downstream regulatory networks associated with individual ITPR3 phosphosites remain poorly understood.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this study, we integratively analysed the publicly available human phosphoproteomic studies to characterize the phosphorylation landscape of ITPR3. Qualitative profiling and quantitative differential datasets were curated to identify phosphosites, followed by co-regulation analysis, functional enrichment, protein-protein interaction network analysis, upstream kinase identification and analysis of cancer-associated phosphoproteomic data using cProSite.
RESULTS AND DISCUSSION: Analysis of qualitative profiling and quantitative differential phosphoproteomic datasets identified four predominant ITPR3 phosphosites (S1832, S934, S2670, and S916) based on their recurrent detection and perturbation across independent datasets. Functional enrichment analysis revealed associations with chromatin organization, transcriptional regulation, RNA processing, cytoskeletal organization, and cellular signaling, indicating distinct regulatory patterns across ITPR3 phosphosites. Mapping of co-regulated proteins to the KEGG calcium signaling pathway identified multiple components involved in receptor-mediated signaling, IP3 generation, intracellular Ca2+ release, store-operated calcium entry, and calcium-responsive signaling. Furthermore, analysis of cancer-derived phosphoproteomic datasets showed the recurrent detection of the four predominant phosphosites across diverse cancer cell lines. Analysis using cProSite revealed distinct tumor-specific phosphorylation patterns, including significant differential phosphorylation of S1832 residue in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, S2670 in breast cancer, S934 in ovarian cancer and S916 in kidney cancer. These findings provide a comprehensive view of ITPR3 phosphorylation and highlight potential regulatory networks connecting specific ITPR3 phosphosites with calcium signaling and cancer-associated processes. Further experimental studies are needed to determine the functional role of these phosphosites and to establish their association with ITPR3-mediated calcium signaling and tumor biology.

articles.title: Association between Some Demographic and Fertility-related Characteristics and Sleep Quality among Women with Infertility: A Cross-sectional Study.
articles.journal: International journal of community based nursing and midwifery
articles.ta: Int J Community Based Nurs Midwifery
articles.authors: Musdaq Jaafar ZM, Mushatet Alfartosy SH, Abdul-Razzaq SH
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Infertility is associated with a considerable psychological and social burden that can negatively impact women's quality of life and sleep quality. The current study aimed to examine the association of sleep quality with some demographic and fertility-related characteristics among women with infertility.
METHODS: A cross-sectional study was carried out in the fertility clinic of AL Kadhomiya Teaching Hospital from January to December 2024 in Baghdad, Iraq. In total, 273 women with infertility aged 20-49 years were recruited. Participants' sleep quality was assessed using the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index. Data analysis was done using descriptive statistics, chi-square test, and a binary logistic regression model through SPSS version 25.
RESULTS: At least 193 participants (70.70%) said they slept poorly. In binary logistic regression analysis, age and sleep duration were predictors of poor sleep quality. Women aged 40-49 years had significantly higher odds of poor sleep quality compared with women 20-29 years old (OR=2.53, 95% CI: 1.13-5.67, P=0.024). Women who slept 6-7 hours per night had reduced risks of poor sleep quality compared to those who slept less than 4 hours (OR=0.24, 95% CI: 0.13-0.46, P<0.001). Poor sleep quality was not associated with body mass index and the duration of trying to conceive (P>0.05).
CONCLUSIONS: Poor sleep was common among women with infertility. Older age and shorter sleep duration were found to be associated with poor sleep quality. Attention to these variables may help identify women with infertility at risk for sleep quality disturbances and design a program to manage their problem.

articles.title: Non-criteria antiphospholipid antibodies and pregnancy outcomes in recurrent pregnancy loss patients.
articles.authors: Zhou X, Luo E, Cai X et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study seeks to examine the prevalence of non-criteria antiphospholipid antibodies (NC-aPLs) in patients experiencing recurrent pregnancy loss (RPL) and to assess their potential association with pregnancy outcomes.
METHODS: In this study,247 patients who had experienced at least two pregnancy losses and had been screened for 14 NC-aPLs were recruited between February 2021 and March 2024. Serum levels of NC-aPLs were assessed using line immunoassay (LIA), with the exception of anti-phosphatidylserine/prothrombin IgM (aPS/PT), which was quantified via enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). Pregnancy outcomes were subsequently compared between patients testing positive and negative for NC-aPLs, following the exclusion of individuals with positivity for criteria antiphospholipid antibodies (aPLs), chromosomal abnormalities, uterine anomalies, or thyroid dysfunction. Binary logistic regression analysis was employed to identify factors associated with adverse pregnancy outcomes (APO).
RESULTS: The overall positivity rate for NC-aPLs was 38.46% (95 out of 247 participants), with anti-phosphatidylethanolamine (aPE) IgM being the most prevalent subtype, observed in 14.17% of cases. Patients who tested positive for NC-aPLs received more intensive therapeutic interventions, including low molecular weight heparin (LMWH), glucocorticoids, and hydroxychloroquine (HCQ). However, the incidence of APO did not significantly differ between NC-aPLs-positive and NC-aPLs-negative groups (53.68% vs. 46.71%, OR = 1.322, 95% CI 0.791-2.211, p = 0.286). Subgroup analyses did not reveal any significant associations between specific NC-aPLs subtypes [aPE IgM, anti-prothrombin (aPT) IgM, anti-annexin A5 (aAnxA5] IgM) and APO, nor between single and multiple NC-aPLs positivity. Binary logistic regression showed that medicinal degree was associated with lower odds of APO (1-2 drugs: aOR=0.177, 95% CI 0.055-0.569, P = 0.004; 3-4 drugs: aOR = 0.102, 95% CI 0.037-0.283, P < 0.001), while neither single positivity (aOR = 1.553, 95% CI 0.799-3.017, P = 0.194) nor multiple positivity for NC-aPLs (aOR = 1.942, 95% CI 0.798-4.726, P = 0.144) was significantly associated with APO.
CONCLUSION: NC-aPLs are detectable in a substantial proportion of patients with RPL. However, this study did not identify any association between NC-aPLs and APO. Patients who tested positive for NC-aPLs received significantly more intensive pharmacological treatment, which was associated with…

articles.title: Topological transition at midlife in the physiological network of Mexican women and divergent amplitude of topological change between sexes: allostatic load biomarkers across adult life.
articles.authors: Uriarte-Ortiz JB, Barajas-Martínez A, López-Mayorga RM et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Additive allostatic load indices treat cardiometabolic biomarkers as independent Q6 units and discard their covariation. Correlation networks recover it, yet previous physiological network studies were restricted to strictly healthy participants or specific diseases, leaving undescribed how topology changes across adult life in the general population.
METHODS: We analyzed 7,999 adults (5,058 women, 2,941 men) pooled from the Mexican National Health and Nutrition Surveys (ENSANUT) of 2016, 2020 and 2021, stratified by sex and five age groups (20-91 years) and, in an exploratory analysis, by dyslipidemia. For each stratum we built graphs of 22 anthropometric, hemodynamic and biochemical variables from Spearman correlations retained at p < 0.05 and averaged density, transitivity, mean distance and Louvain modularity over 100 subsamples of 79% of the participants.
RESULTS: Female topology followed two phases. Between the 20-29 and 40-49 age groups, density fell from 0.47 to 0.25 and transitivity from 0.70 to 0.50, whereas mean distance rose from 1.61 to 2.32 and modularity from 0.40 to 0.56 as blood pressure variables separated into a distinct module; all four then plateaued through the oldest group. Univariate biomarker trajectories changed gradually over the same ages. Men showed no such transition, with density between 0.34 and 0.42 across all strata, a range narrower than each female step during the first phase, and modularity rising only from 0.37 to 0.45 between the two youngest groups. The female decline was already present between the 20-29 and 30-39 groups, at ages preceding the menopausal transition. Edges persisted in graphs rebuilt from the 12 directly measured variables, and stratification by dyslipidemia, defined by three nodes of the network, did not fully account for the age trends.
DISCUSSION: These cross-sectional graphs describe covariation across individuals, and their reading as within-person regulation requires longitudinal confirmation. A male transition before age 20 and survivorship selection remain competing, testable explanations for male topological stability. The results extend to adult life the sexual dimorphism described in physiological networks of healthy young adults and locate in women a reorganization, completed by midlife, that univariate analyses did not reveal.

articles.title: A novel HPV mRNA vaccine candidate: immunogenicity and definition of immune correlates of protection.
articles.authors: Hwang H, An T, Seo EH et al.
articles.abstract: Human papillomavirus (HPV), the major cause of cervical cancer, continues to be associated with an increasing number of diagnosed cases despite the availability of licensed vaccines such as Cervarix™ and GARDASIL®. In addition, cervical cancer incidence remains especially high in low- and middle-income countries, while vaccine coverage remains low due to high costs and instability in supply. We developed a novel HPV vaccine candidate using mRNA platform and to propose immune correlates of protection (CoP) for efficacy evaluation. A protection threshold was established based on GARDASIL® 9, and the corresponding antibody titers were determined. These antibody titers were used as Reference for the immunogenicity analysis of the generated HPV16 mRNA. As a result, the vaccine was shown to induce a sufficiently significant level of protective efficacy. Furthermore, based on the immunogenicity data obtained from GARDASIL® 9 and HPV16 mRNA, the minimum antibody titers required for protection were determined, thereby defining CoP for HPV vaccine. Additionally, HPV16 mRNA induced cellular immune responses associated with CD4- and CD8-specific cytokine secretion, suggesting potential protective mechanism in which cellular immunity complements humoral immunity. This study proposes an objective evaluation framework for comparing and analyzing HPV vaccine efficacy across different vaccine platforms.

articles.title: Comparative effectiveness of GnRH antagonist, mild stimulation, and PPOS protocols in POSEIDON groups 3 and 4: a retrospective cohort study with entropy balancing.
articles.authors: Zhao H, Ni Y, Wang A et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients classified as POSEIDON groups 3 and 4 have diminished ovarian reserve and predicted poor ovarian response. Although GnRH antagonist, mild stimulation, and progestin-primed ovarian stimulation (PPOS) protocols are widely used, direct comparative evidence from homogeneous cohorts remains limited.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 592 first IVF cycles (GnRH antagonist: n = 203, mild stimulation: n = 243, PPOS: n = 146) in patients whose sole IVF indication was POSEIDON groups 3 or 4. Entropy balancing achieved near-perfect balance across nine baseline covariates. The primary outcome was cumulative live birth rate per initiated cycle.
RESULTS: After entropy balancing, cumulative live birth rates showed no statistically significant differences: 32.8% for antagonist, 29.2% for mild, and 35.8% for PPOS (global P = 0.452). Cumulative clinical pregnancy rates were also similar (37.9%, 34.6%, and 39.5%; P = 0.649). Weighted logistic regression confirmed no significant protocol differences (all P > 0.05). No significant interaction was observed between protocol and POSEIDON subgroup for either outcome (P for interaction = 0.384 and 0.213). Although the antagonist protocol yielded superior embryological outcomes (more oocytes, usable embryos, and high-quality embryos, all P < 0.001), this did not translate into higher cumulative live birth or pregnancy rates. Critically, rates of no oocytes retrieved (6.0%, 6.4%, and 7.6%; P = 0.888) and cancellation due to no usable embryos (16.5%, 19.3%, and 16.2%; P = 0.786) were nearly identical across groups, suggesting a potential threshold effect that warrants further investigation, as protocol choice did not significantly affect the probability of obtaining at least one embryo in this exploratory analysis. PPOS had the lowest premature LH surge rate (1.5%, global P = 0.047).
CONCLUSIONS: In POSEIDON groups 3 and 4 patients, the three protocols showed no statistically significant differences in cumulative live birth and clinical pregnancy rates despite differences in embryo yield. This exploratory finding suggests that embryo obtainability may be more strongly associated with intrinsic patient characteristics than with protocol choice, although this requires confirmation in future prospective studies.

articles.title: Parents' perception of enhanced oncofertility care in childhood cancer patients following routine fertility informing.
articles.authors: Stukaite-Ruibiene E, Clasen NHZ, van den Heuvel-Eibrink MM et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The 5-year survival rate of childhood cancer is >80%, indicating a large number of survivors. Infertility is a late effect of cancer treatment. This study aimed to evaluate the perception of early routine fertility informing of families of children with cancer as part of oncofertility care before and after the implementation of routine informing procedure.
METHODS: We evaluated and compared the quality of oncofertility care before and after routine fertility informing was implemented. The baseline group was evaluated between 1 July 2021 and 1 July 2022, using the oncofertility care evaluation questionnaire. Infertility risk was determined retrospectively in this group. On 1 July 2022, routine fertility informing was implemented. Thereafter, infertility risk was assessed prospectively, and families were informed by a dedicated staff member. The second group completed the same questionnaire.
RESULTS: Of the respondents in the second group, 63.6% reported having had an opportunity to discuss fertility (vs. 37.5% of the first group; p = 0.002), 42.4% had received supportive material (vs. 10.7%; p = 0.003), 24.2% had questions about fertility after education (vs. 42.9%; p = 0.003), and 59% felt knowledgeable about the effects of treatment on fertility (vs. 32.1%, p = 0.001). Infertility risk was estimated correctly by 15.2% of respondents before implementation of routine informing compared with 63.6% after implementation.
CONCLUSIONS: Routine and early fertility informing of families of children with cancer as standard of care significantly improved patients' perception of oncofertility care. Parental awareness of fertility-related issues increased substantially.

articles.title: Risk prediction for 12-month post-prostatectomy urinary incontinence to support survivorship care: development and same-center temporal validation of a perioperative model.
articles.authors: Tang L, Hao M, Luo M et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Persistent post-prostatectomy urinary incontinence (PPI) is a survivorship problem after radical prostatectomy with continuing implications for daily function, rehabilitation, follow-up, and supportive care. Risk stratification could help target these services, but uncommon events constrain model complexity and require evaluation beyond discrimination.
OBJECTIVE: To develop a perioperative model for PPI 12 months after catheter removal using LASSO-penalized logistic regression, compare it with a constrained gradient boosting machine (GBM), and examine temporal performance in a later same-center cohort.
METHODS: The development cohort comprised 726 patients with 51 PPI events (7.0%) and 19 candidate predictors. LASSO tuning used the one-standard-error rule within resampling, and the strategies were compared by nested repeated stratified five-fold cross-validation. The selected LASSO model was refitted to the full development cohort and applied without coefficient updating or recalibration to 465 later patients with 38 events (8.2%). Evaluation included ROC-AUC, average precision, Brier score, calibration-in-the-large (CITL), calibration slope, threshold-dependent measures, and decision-curve analysis.
RESULTS: Eight original predictors were retained: age, preoperative International Prostate Symptom Score, ln(1 + prostate-specific antigen), operative time, postoperative hospital stay, smoking history, hypertension, and neurovascular bundle preservation. Nested internal validation yielded a ROC-AUC of 0.913 (95% CI 0.871-0.946), average precision of 0.542 (0.404-0.675), and Brier score of 0.046 (0.035-0.058) for LASSO, versus 0.896, 0.488, and 0.048 for constrained GBM. In the temporal cohort, ROC-AUC was 0.836 (0.763-0.900), average precision 0.409 (0.277-0.564), and Brier score 0.062 (0.045-0.081). CITL was 0.445 (0.012-0.808) and the calibration slope 0.850 (0.621-1.174), indicating average underprediction. At the development-derived threshold of 0.128, sensitivity was 0.500 and specificity 0.913. Decision-curve analysis indicated potential net benefit across thresholds of 2-30%.
CONCLUSION: The LASSO model retained useful temporal discrimination but underestimated absolute risk, and the development-derived cutoff did not transport well. It is therefore better suited to continuous risk estimation for survivorship follow-up and rehabilitation planning than to a fixed binary triage rule. Independent geographic validation, local calibration…

articles.title: Genetic analysis of biopsy-related droplets and its potential applications in PGT-SR patients.
articles.authors: Huang Z, Chen Y, Cai X et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To investigate genetic material in biopsy-related droplets (BRDs) from blastocyst biopsy and its potential applications in preimplantation genetic testing for structural rearrangements (PGT-SR).
METHODS: BRDs were collected from 218 blastocysts by combining three types of biopsy-related droplets (biopsy, washing, and temporary storage droplets) into ~15 µL samples. Genomic DNA amplification and copy number variation (CNV) sequencing library preparation were performed. Next-generation sequencing (NGS) was conducted on BRD libraries with concentrations ≥0.5 ng/µL.
RESULTS: 69.27% of BRDs had a sequencing library concentration (CSL) ≥ 0.5 ng/µL, with a CNV detection success rate of 94.04%. CSL was significantly higher in biopsy-classified non-euploid than euploid blastocysts (P < 0.0001). Among 142 BRDs with successful CNV detection, 87.32% showed ploidy concordance with PGT findings. Complete or partial concordance was observed in 77.53% of blastocysts with structural rearrangement-related abnormalities. In 37 transferred biopsy-euploid blastocysts, clinical pregnancy rates were higher in the BRD-euploid and undetectable/non-informative BRD groups than in the BRD-non-euploid group (85.71% and 86.96% vs. 28.57%). In seven blastocysts undergoing secondary biopsy after initial testing failure, BRD and secondary biopsy results showed 85.71% ploidy concordance.
CONCLUSIONS: BRD-based genetic testing may serve as an adjunct to conventional biopsy-based testing in PGT-SR.

articles.title: Association of vitamin E and coenzyme Q10 pretreatment with embryological and pregnancy outcomes in women with diminished ovarian reserve: a retrospective study.
articles.authors: Wang S, Wang T, Zhang W et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the associations of adjunctive vitamin E (Vit E) and coenzyme Q10 (CoQ10) supplementation with embryological and pregnancy outcomes in patients with diminished ovarian reserve (DOR) undergoing IVF/ICSI-ET.
METHODS: In this retrospective observational study, 949 patients with DOR undergoing IVF/ICSI-ET were included. According to adjunctive treatment before controlled ovarian stimulation, patients were categorized into the Control (n=338), Vit E+CoQ10 (n=260), CoQ10 (n=224), or Vit E (n=127) groups. Demographic characteristics, ovarian reserve indicators, stimulation parameters, embryological outcomes, and pregnancy outcomes were compared. Multivariable Poisson regression models with a log link and robust standard errors adjusted for demographic characteristics, ovarian reserve indicators, stimulation parameters, fertilization method, and treatment cycle initiation year were used to assess associations between supplementation regimens and embryological outcomes. A 2 × 2 exposure-based interaction model including Vit E use, CoQ10 use, and their interaction was applied.
RESULTS: Baseline characteristics and stimulation parameters did not differ significantly among groups. The distribution of treatment cycle initiation year also did not differ significantly among the groups (P = 0.325). The numbers of transferable and top-quality embryos differed significantly across groups and were highest in the Vit E+CoQ10 group. Pairwise comparisons showed that Vit E+CoQ10 was associated with more transferable embryos than Control and Vit E, while the CoQ10 group had more transferable embryos than Control and Vit E. The Vit E+CoQ10 group also had more top-quality embryos than the other groups. After multivariable adjustment, combined supplementation and CoQ10 supplementation were associated with increased numbers of transferable embryos, whereas combined supplementation did not differ significantly from CoQ10 alone. A positive statistical interaction between Vit E and CoQ10 was observed for the number of top-quality embryos. Clinical pregnancy, live birth, and early miscarriage rates did not differ significantly.
CONCLUSIONS: In patients with DOR undergoing IVF/ICSI-ET, CoQ10 supplementation was associated with a higher transferable-embryo count, whereas combined Vit E+CoQ10 supplementation was associated with a higher top-quality-embryo count. However, these embryological differences were not associated with improved pregnancy outcomes.

articles.title: Mā te kimi ka kite, Mā te kite ka mōhio, Mā te mōhio ka Mārama Seek and discover, discover and know, know and become enlightened.
articles.journal: The Proceedings of the Nutrition Society
articles.authors: Parackal S, Smith C, Gibbs M et al.
articles.abstract: The 59th Annual Scientific Meeting of the Nutrition Society of New Zealand was held at Tūhura Otago Museum, Dunedin (26-28 November 2025) under the theme "Advancing Nutrition: Evidence, Translation, and Action", reflecting the imperative to translate nutrition science into equitable, culturally grounded policy and practice. Scientific sessions spanned sustainable food systems, best practice in research methods and reporting, data sovereignty, women's health, sports nutrition, Māori and Pacific health, mental wellbeing, chronic disease prevention and management, and nutrition across the lifespan. Plenary presentations addressed systems approaches to Pacific food environments and policy; Māori considerations for indigenous data sovereignty in administrative and health datasets; the CONSORT-Nut extension to strengthen reporting of nutrition randomised controlled trials; menopause and cardiometabolic health; regional action on non-communicable diseases (including the MANA monitoring framework); the benefits and risks of glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonists within a weight-inclusive, culturally responsive model of care; and critical appraisal of social media nutrition narratives affecting active women. The Muriel Bell Lecture, highlighted strengths-based Pacific nutrition initiatives informed by the Fonofale model of health. Workshops emphasised practical translation, including behaviour change, food waste reduction in aged residential care, weight-inclusive care for GLP-1 users, culinary nutrition, oral health, and dementia risk reduction. Overall, the conference showcased contemporary nutrition research and practice and underscored shared responsibility to turn evidence into action that improves population health and reduces inequities.

articles.title: From recommendations to practice: knowledge and implementation of infection screening in pregnancy among obstetricians and midwives in Italy.
articles.authors: Fernicola F, Corsi Decenti E, Arienti F et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: to assess, from a public health and guideline implementation perspective, obstetricians' and midwives' knowledge of the recommendations for screening of infections in pregnancy included in the 2023 update of the guideline on 'Uncomplicated Pregnancy' by the Italian National Guidelines System of the National Institute of Health (SNLG-ISS).
DESIGN: nationwide, cross-sectional survey.
SETTING AND PARTICIPANTS: an online survey disseminated through the main Italian scientific societies in the obstetrics and gynecological field one year after the publication of the updated ISS guideline. A non-probabilistic sample of obstetricians and midwives affiliated with scientific societies was included.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: knowledge of screening modalities for seven infections in pregnancy included in the 2023 update of the 'Uncomplicated Pregnancy' guideline.
RESULTS: a total of 606 healthcare professionals completed the questionnaire, including 51.3% (N. 311) obstetricians and 48.7% (N. 295) midwives. Nearly half of respondents (46.9%; N. 283) had more than 20 years of professional experience and 32.3% (N. 196) worked in secondary care settings. No participant answered all questions aligned with the update recommendations regarding the seven infectious conditions; for each infection, less than 20% demonstrated adequate knowledge of screening modalities.
CONCLUSIONS: the limited knowledge among obstetricians and midwives regarding updated recommendations for screening of infections in pregnancy represents a critical barrier to their effective implementation within the Italian National Health Service, with potential implications for appropriateness of care, equity of access, and quality of prenatal services. These findings highlight the need for structured strategies for guideline dissemination and implementation, including continuing education, audit&feedback, and integration into care pathways, in order to promote adherence to recommendations and improve maternal and perinatal health outcomes.

articles.title: Bridging modelling estimates and primary data: diabetes burden in Italy through GBD 2023 estimates and the Piedmont Diabetes Registry.
articles.authors: Armocida B, Zamagni G, Gnavi R et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: to describe the burden of type 1 (T1DM) and type 2 (T2DM) diabetes mellitus in Italy and across macro-regions using the Global Burden of Disease (GBD) 2023 estimates, and to compare prevalence estimates for the Piedmont Region (Northern Italy) with two primary data sources: the Diabetes Regional Registry (DRR) and the JACARDI preliminary algorithm for administrative case-finding.
DESIGN: descriptive epidemiological study based on GBD 2023 estimates (2010-2023) for all-age and age-standardised rates, and on a comparison between GBD, the DRR (2010-2019), and the JACARDI preliminary algorithm (2015-2019) for T1DM and T2DM prevalence in Piedmont.
SETTING AND PARTICIPANTS: Italian general population. Macro-regional analyses cover five areas (North-West, North-East, Centre, South, Islands). The data comparison concerns the Piedmont Region, through the DRR (operational since 1989) and the JACARDI preliminary algorithm for T1DM, T2DM, and gestational diabetes (GDM) case identification.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: all-age and age-standardised prevalence and incidence rates per 100,000 population for T1DM and T2DM. For the Piedmont comparison, percentage prevalence of T1DM and T2DM in the general population, both sexes, 2010-2019 (DRR) and 2015-2019 (JACARDI preliminary algorithm).
RESULTS: GBD 2023 estimates show a growing diabetes burden in Italy, confirming the well-established geographical gradient: the Islands show the highest rates for both diabetes types (2023 all-age T2DM prevalence: 10,197.0 per 100,000; T1DM: 526.7 per 100,000), followed by the South. Age-standardised T2DM prevalence remained essentially stable nationally (-2%), while all-age prevalence increased (+11%). T1DM prevalence increased in both all-age and age-standardised terms (+18%). In the Piedmont comparison, the DRR provided prevalence rate below GBD prevalence rates for both T2DM and T1DM. For T2DM, the JACARDI preliminary algorithm (2015-2019) produced estimates slightly below but close to GBD, with all values falling within the GBD uncertainty intervals. For T1DM, the JACARDI preliminary algorithm provided estimates above those of GBD, with absolute differences remaining small.
CONCLUSIONS: GBD estimates and primary data sources are complementary tools that, when systematically compared, help identify each other's strengths and limitations. For T2DM, the JACARDI preliminary algorithm yielded prevalence estimates close to GBD and consistently higher than those derived from the…

articles.title: DNA methylation patterns at the IGF2-H19 locus in offspring and maternal folate intake: a systematic review.
articles.journal: Journal of developmental origins of health and disease
articles.authors: Raffan Santoyo MM, Porras Ramírez A
articles.abstract: Folate is a critical methyl-group donor in one-carbon metabolism, and maternal folate exposure during pregnancy has been proposed to influence DNA methylation at imprinted loci involved in fetal growth and developmental programming. This systematic review evaluated the association between maternal folate intake during pregnancy and DNA methylation at the IGF2-H19 locus in offspring tissues. PubMed, Embase, and Epistemonikos were systematically searched for human studies assessing folate or folic acid exposure during pregnancy and DNA methylation at IGF2 and/or H19 in pregnancy-related tissues. Risk of bias was assessed using ROBINS-E for observational studies and the Cochrane RoB 2 tool for randomized controlled trials. Fifteen reports from nine countries met the eligibility criteria, including two randomized controlled trials, two cross-sectional studies, and eleven cohort studies. Findings were heterogeneous according to genomic region, tissue type, and exposure window. Folic acid supplementation showed the most consistent associations at the H19 imprinting control region, where inverse associations with methylation were reported in some cord blood analyses. Results for IGF2 DMR2 varied across studies, whereas associations involving blood folate biomarkers were generally weak and tissue-specific, and dietary folate intake was largely null. No observational study was judged at low overall risk of bias, and both randomized trials were assessed as having some concerns. Overall, maternal folic acid supplementation was associated with modest, region-specific differences in DNA methylation at the IGF2-H19 locus; however, methodological limitations and heterogeneity across studies preclude firm conclusions regarding the biological significance of these associations.

articles.title: Burden and Projections of Premenopausal and Postmenopausal Breast Cancer Worldwide: A Comprehensive Analysis of GLOBOCAN 2022 Data.
articles.authors: Ding R, Jia H
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Breast cancer is the most diagnosed cancer among women worldwide, yet important epidemiological differences exist between premenopausal and postmenopausal disease. Updated global estimates stratified by menopausal status are limited. This study aimed to quantify the global, regional, and national burden of premenopausal and postmenopausal breast cancer in 2022 and to project future trends through 2050.
METHODS: Breast cancer incidence and mortality data for 2022 were obtained from the International Agency for Research on Cancer GLOBOCAN database. Women aged 15-49 years were classified as premenopausal and those aged ≥ 50 years as postmenopausal. Age-standardized incidence rates (ASIRs), age-standardized mortality rates (ASMRs), cumulative risk, and mortality-to-incidence ratios (MIRs) were estimated for 185 countries. Countries were further stratified by the Human Development Index (HDI) published by the United Nations Development Programme. Temporal trends were assessed using estimated annual percentage change (EAPC), and projections to 2050 were derived using the World Health Organization Cancer Tomorrow tool.
RESULTS: In 2022, an estimated 2,296,607 new breast cancer cases and 666,061 deaths occurred globally. Premenopausal women accounted for 668,417 cases (29.1%) and 141,338 deaths (21.2%), while postmenopausal women accounted for 1,628,190 cases (70.9%) and 524,723 deaths (78.8%). Global ASIRs were 32.7 and 153.9 per 100,000 for premenopausal and postmenopausal women, respectively. Incidence rates were highest in very high-HDI countries, whereas mortality and MIR were markedly higher in low-HDI countries. Africa showed the highest MIRs for both premenopausal (40.3%) and postmenopausal (51.8%) breast cancer. HDI was positively correlated with cumulative incidence risk but strongly inversely correlated with MIR. By 2050, global cases are projected to increase to 795,908 for premenopausal and 2,756,889 for postmenopausal breast cancer.
CONCLUSIONS: Substantial global disparities exist in breast cancer burden and outcomes. While high-income countries experience higher incidence, low-resource settings bear disproportionately higher mortality. Strengthening early detection, treatment access, and cancer control systems is essential to reduce global inequities and address the growing burden of breast cancer.

articles.title: Simulation-based Bayesian deep learning enables uncertainty-aware tumor fraction estimation in cell-free DNA.
articles.authors: Volkov H, Raitses-Gurevich M, Grad M et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Estimating tumor fraction from whole-genome cell-free DNA sequencing is critical for liquid biopsy, but is hampered by weak signals and baseline noise at low tumor fractions. Existing computational methods often require matched controls or large labeled datasets for training and lack uncertainty quantification. To address these gaps, we developed purNPE, a Bayesian deep-learning framework trained without labeled cancer cell-free DNA samples. Specifically, purNPE leverages a two-part generative model: one component simulates diverse tumor copy-number profiles based on evolutionary genealogies, while a second, data-driven component learns and replicates realistic sequencing background patterns from cancer-free cell-free DNA. By training a Neural Posterior Estimator on synthetic tumor profiles augmented with learned noise, purNPE performs amortized inference in milliseconds without needing a reference sample set at inference.
RESULTS: In a real-world pan-cancer cohort, purNPE achieved comparable performance with existing methods against an orthogonal mutant-allele-fraction proxy (MAE [Formula: see text]). In semi-synthetic and in silico experiments, purNPE showed calibrated uncertainty estimates and a dose-response across low tumor-fraction spike-ins, with separation of approximately 1% TF spike-ins from blanks under the evaluated conditions.
CONCLUSIONS: This work provides a proof-of-concept framework for using simulation-based inference to derive calibrated, uncertainty-aware TF estimates. Larger prospective cohorts with stronger orthogonal ground truth are required before analytical sensitivity or clinical utility can be established.

articles.title: Clinical and genetic landscapes of mucopolysaccharidosis type III in 20 Chinese patients.
articles.authors: Su X, Zhang Y, Zhao X et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mucopolysaccharidosis type III (MPS III), also known as Sanfilippo syndrome, is a devastating lysosomal storage disorder characterized by severe, progressive neurodegeneration. Diagnosing this condition is challenging because early somatic signs are often mild, frequently leading to misdiagnosis as autism spectrum disorder or attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder. As the subtype distribution and genetic mutation spectrum show significant ethnic heterogeneity, population-specific data are essential for accurate clinical management. This study aimed to investigate the clinical features, biochemical indicators, and genetic landscape of 20 Chinese patients (10 with type IIIA and 10 with type IIIB) to improve early recognition and diagnostic accuracy. Phenotypes and genotypes were summarized using urinary glycosaminoglycan levels, lysosomal enzyme activity assays, and whole-exome sequencing.
METHODS: A retrospective analysis was conducted on 20 patients with MPS III (10 with type IIIA and 10 with type IIIB). Urinary glycosaminoglycan (GAG) levels, lysosomal enzyme activities in peripheral blood leukocytes, and genetic analysis using whole-exome sequencing (WES) were performed to summarize their phenotypes and genotypes.
RESULTS: All 20 patients exhibited progressive neurodegeneration, with initial symptoms primarily including delayed language development (100%) and cognitive regression, accompanied by varying degrees of hyperactivity, sleep disorders, and coarse facial features. Biochemical data showed the majority of patients (18/20, 90%) had significantly elevated urinary GAG excretion (with two patients showing values within normal limits), with type IIIA patients showing markedly decreased activity of heparan N-sulfatase (SGSH) and type IIIB patients showing significantly reduced α-N-acetylglucosaminidase (NAGLU) activity. Genetic testing revealed that in the SGSH gene, c.1129C>T and c.703G>A were the most frequent mutations, while in the NAGLU gene, c.1693C>T and c.1081T>C were common mutations. Compared with European populations, the proportions of IIIA and IIIB subtypes were similar in this cohort.
CONCLUSION: Chinese patients with MPS III exhibit significant clinical variability and delayed diagnosis. Delayed language development accompanied by mild facial dysmorphism is an important diagnostic clue. Population-specific high-frequency mutation sites exist in the SGSH and NAGLU genes, and clarifying the mutation spectrum can aid in…

articles.title: It's time to talk: exploring the role of couples' communication in improving health behaviors in Kebbi, Nigeria.
articles.journal: International journal for equity in health
articles.authors: Hutchinson P, Aisiri A, Oyedokun-Adebagbo F et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In societies with strong patrilineal traditions, such as in northern Nigeria, husbands play the primary role in many household decisions, including for the reproductive health of their wives and the health of other family members. While previous research has shown that couples who engage in health-related discussions are more likely to utilize health services, these discussions may be inhibited in northern Nigeria by entrenched gender norms and roles, as well as unfavorable attitudes towards certain health behaviors. Focusing on married couples in Kebbi state in northwestern Nigeria, this study investigates the prevalence of health-related discussions between spouses, focusing on which factors seem most likely to influence the probability of discussions.
METHODS: Data for this analysis comes from a 2021 household survey of 1,043 couple dyads involving husbands and wives with a child under the age of two. We focus on couples' discussions of breastfeeding, contraception for birth spacing, and reproductive and child health services (e.g., antenatal care, delivery care, childhood vaccinations). Multivariate logistic models are used to estimate the magnitude of relationships between couples' engagement in discussions and concordance and discordance in attitudes, norms, decision-making authority, social influences, and sociodemographic characteristics. Average marginal effects are used to present effect sizes (in percentage points) for each discussion topic.
RESULTS: We find that the prevalence of discussions varies by health topic. Discussions of family planning are the least common; nearly 10% of couples say that they have discussed fertility goals, and only one quarter of couples agree that they have discussed using contraception for birth spacing. Discussions of antenatal care and child health are more common, though still less than half of couples reported discussions. Husbands are considerably more likely to report discussions than wives. Husbands and wives who score higher on an index of gender equality attitudes are more likely to discuss health topics, perhaps reflecting a greater value placed on shared responsibilities. Other factors include holding positive norms and lower levels of stigma towards priority health behaviors and having more accurate knowledge/risk perceptions about health behaviors. Higher levels of education (for both husbands and wives) and household wealth also appear to contribute, perhaps indirectly. Couples report…

articles.title: Agatharesinol and sequirin C supplementation during in vitro maturation improves porcine oocyte maturation and is associated with improved subsequent embryonic development.
articles.journal: The Journal of veterinary medical science
articles.authors: Yamamura M, Hirata M, Namula Z et al.
articles.abstract: Agatharesinol (AR) and sequirin C (SC) are representative norlignans derived from Cryptomeria japonica that exhibit antioxidant properties. However, their biological applications in animal systems remain unclear. This study evaluated the effects of AR and SC supplementation during in vitro maturation (IVM) on porcine oocyte maturation, fertilization, and embryonic development in vitro. Cumulus-oocyte complexes were cultured with AR or SC at various concentrations, followed by in vitro fertilization and embryo culture. Both compounds improved maturation, fertilization, and blastocyst formation rates compared with the controls. Optimal concentrations were 0.5 and 5 µM for AR and SC, respectively. Therefore, AR or SC supplementation during IVM improved oocyte maturation and was associated with improved subsequent embryonic development, highlighting the potential of norlignan-type compounds as novel bioactive agents for improving in vitro embryo production.

articles.title: USP2 is associated with mitochondrial respiratory activity and cell viability in endometrial stromal cells in endometriosis.
articles.authors: Sun Q, Cao Y, Gu J et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mitochondrial dysfunction has been implicated in the pathophysiology of endometriosis, but the role of ubiquitin-specific protease 2 (USP2) remains unclear. This study aimed to determine whether USP2 modulates mitochondrial respiratory activity and proliferation in ectopic endometrial stromal cells (ESCs).
METHODS: Twenty women with ovarian endometriosis who underwent laparoscopic surgery at the Department of Obstetrics and Gynecology, Xuzhou Central Hospital, between April 2024 and April 2025 were enrolled. Paired eutopic endometrial and ectopic endometriotic tissues were collected from each participant. Primary ESCs were isolated and cultured, and USP2 expression was downregulated or upregulated by lentiviral transduction. USP2 mRNA levels were quantified by reverse-transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction, whereas the protein levels of USP2 and the mitochondrial complex IV subunits COX5B and COX6C were assessed by western blotting. Cell viability and proliferative activity were evaluated using the Cell Counting Kit-8 assay. Intracellular reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels were measured by flow cytometry, and the oxygen consumption rate (OCR) was determined using a Seahorse extracellular flux analyzer. Intracellular ATP content and mitochondrial complex IV enzymatic activity were measured using commercial assay kits.
RESULTS: Compared with paired eutopic ESCs, ectopic ESCs exhibited greater proliferative activity, lower intracellular ROS levels, a higher OCR, increased intracellular ATP content, and elevated mitochondrial complex IV activity (all P < 0.01). In ectopic ESCs, USP2 knockdown reduced proliferative activity (P < 0.001), increased intracellular ROS levels (P < 0.01), and decreased OCR, intracellular ATP content, mitochondrial complex IV activity, and the protein levels of the complex IV subunits COX5B and COX6C (all P < 0.01). Conversely, USP2 overexpression in eutopic ESCs produced reciprocal changes, including increased proliferative activity, reduced intracellular ROS levels, and higher OCR, ATP content, complex IV activity, and COX5B and COX6C protein levels (all P < 0.01). Treatment with carbonyl cyanide 4-(trifluoromethoxy) phenylhydrazone (FCCP), a mitochondrial uncoupler, attenuated the cellular and mitochondrial changes associated with USP2 overexpression.
CONCLUSIONS: USP2 was more highly expressed in ectopic than in paired eutopic endometrial tissues. Its manipulation altered ectopic ESC proliferation and…

articles.title: The influence of maternal complications on small for gestational age in very preterm, late preterm and term pregnancies: a Chinese study.
articles.authors: Ma Y, Xu Z, Wang J et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study aimed to assess the association between single or combined maternal complications and small-for-gestational-age (SGA) birth among very preterm, late preterm, and term births and to evaluate whether this association varied across gestational periods.
METHODS: This retrospective cross-sectional study included 46,829 singleton pregnancies. The maternal complications considered were gestational hypertension (GH), preeclampsia (PE), and gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM). The potential nonlinear association between gestational age and the risk of SGA birth was assessed using restricted cubic spline analysis. Binary logistic regression models were used to assess the associations between single or combined maternal complications and SGA birth within the very preterm, late preterm, and term groups. Results were reported as odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Additionally, effect modification by gestational age was assessed by incorporating interaction terms into the regression models.
RESULTS: Among the 46,829 women with singleton pregnancies, the mean maternal age was 31.7 years (SD, 3.8 years). Restricted cubic spline analysis revealed a significant nonlinear inverse association between gestational age and SGA risk, with the odds of SGA being higher at earlier gestational ages and gradually decreasing toward term. PE showed the strongest association with SGA across all gestational periods, particularly in the very preterm group. In contrast, GDM was associated with lower odds of SGA, although the co-occurrence of PE and GDM was associated with an increased risk of SGA. GH was associated with an increased risk of SGA in the very preterm group (OR = 2.430; 95% CI, 1.156-5.111) but not in the late preterm or term groups. Interaction analysis indicated that the association between maternal complications and SGA weakened with advancing gestational age, with substantially weaker associations observed in term pregnancies.
CONCLUSIONS: In contrast to GDM, PE and GH were associated with an increased risk of SGA, particularly in preterm pregnancies. These findings underscore the importance of early identification, close monitoring, and individualized management of women with PE or GH, particularly among pregnancies resulting in preterm birth.

articles.title: The association of dietary methionine, natural folate and folic acid supplementation with the risk of preterm birth during pregnancy: a case control study.
articles.authors: Zhou X, Wu W, Wang Z et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study aimed to investigate the association of dietary methionine, natural folate and folic acid supplementation with the risk of preterm birth during pregnancy and to assess the interaction between dietary methionine and folic acid.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: A case-control study conducted at Gansu Provincial Maternal and Child Health Hospital comprised 8,705 subjects, of whom 7,865 underwent normal delivery and 840 preterm birth. Eligible participants completed questionnaires to collect dietary and other baseline characteristic data. Unconditional logistic regression analysis was employed to assess the association between dietary methionine, natural folate and folic acid supplementation intake with preterm birth and its subtypes.
RESULTS: We found the risk of preterm birth was increased by 36% in the low dietary methionine intake group compared with the high group in late pregnancy (OR = 1.36, 95%CI: 1.10-1.70), and dietary methionine intake was significantly associated with medically induced preterm birth (P-trend = 0.0285). The risk of preterm birth was increased by 23% in the low natural folate intake group compared to the high group (OR = 1.23, 95%CI: 1.03-1.48) and natural folate intake was significantly associated with spontaneous preterm birth (P-trend = 0.0298). Those with low folic acid supplementation had a 105% increased risk of preterm birth (OR = 2.05, 95%CI: 1.15-3.65) and folic acid supplementation intake was significantly associated with spontaneous preterm birth (P-trend = 0.0195). Interaction analyses showed that the combination of low methionine and low natural folate further increased the risk (P-interaction < 0.0001). The combination of low methionine and low folate supplementation further increased the risk (P-interaction = 0.0005), and the risk of preterm birth was increased if intake of all three was low compared with the adequate intake group.
CONCLUSION: Inadequate intake of dietary methionine, natural folate, and folic acid supplementation may elevate the risk of preterm birth. Moreover, low levels of these nutrients during pregnancy-specifically reduced methionine intake, insufficient natural folate intake, and inadequate folic acid supplementation-may act synergistically to further increase this risk. Attention should be paid to ensuring adequate intake of methionine and folic acid during late pregnancy and throughout gestation to reduce the incidence of preterm birth.

articles.title: Mistreatment during facility-based childbirth in Benin City, Nigeria: A convergent mixed-methods study of prevalence and drivers.
articles.authors: Eluobaju D, Okonofua F, Toscano M et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mistreatment during facility-based childbirth undermines maternal health outcomes and trust in health systems, particularly in low- and middle-income countries. Nigeria bears one of the highest global burdens of maternal mortality, yet limited large-scale mixed-methods studies have examined how mistreatment is both experienced by women and shaped by health system conditions. This study assessed the prevalence, forms, and drivers of mistreatment during childbirth in Benin City, Nigeria, integrating women's and skilled birth attendants' (SBAs) perspectives.
METHODS: We conducted a convergent parallel mixed-methods study between July-August 2024 across three healthcare facilities (tertiary, secondary, and private) in Benin City. Postpartum women (≤ 12 months since delivery) completed a 45-item mistreatment survey (n = 656). Mistreatment was categorized across eight domains. Descriptive statistics and chi-square analyses were performed. In-depth interviews were conducted with postpartum women (n = 20), and four focus group discussions were held with SBAs (n = 26). Qualitative data were analyzed using constructivist grounded theory. Findings were integrated using a joint display matrix to assess convergence, divergence, and complementarity.
RESULTS: Overall, 89.5% of women reported experiencing at least one form of mistreatment, though only 2.6% labeled their experience as mistreatment. The most common domains were undignified care (70%) and loss of autonomy (48.2%), followed by physical abuse (37.5%) and abandonment (16.3%). Vaginal delivery, higher education, and antenatal care attendance were significantly associated with reported mistreatment (p < 0.05). Qualitative analysis identified five themes: divergent expectations between women and SBAs; shared labeling of laboring women as "uncooperative"; inconsistent definitions of mistreatment; provider burnout; and structural constraints including understaffing, limited infrastructure, and financial barriers. Both groups used the term "uncooperative" to describe laboring behavior, though with different interpretations. Women emphasized disrespect, lack of consent, and loss of autonomy, while SBAs contextualized care within systemic constraints and workload pressures. Integration showed strong convergence between quantitative autonomy violations and qualitative accounts of restricted companionship, hierarchical communication, and limited shared decision-making.
COMCLUSIONS: Mistreatment during…

articles.title: Regulatory Mechanisms and Therapeutic Targeting of Anoikis in the Metastasis of Gynecologic Malignancies.
articles.authors: Liu M, Hu H
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Anoikis is a special form of programmed cell death triggered by the detachment of cells from the extracellular matrix (ECM) or improper adhesion, and it is an important host defense mechanism against tumor invasion and metastasis. This study aims to systematically review the relevant mechanisms of anoikis in the metastasis of gynecological tumors and its therapeutic significance.
METHODS: We conducted a comprehensive review of the mechanisms underlying anoikis in gynecologic tumor metastasis and its therapeutic implications using the PubMed database.
RESULTS: Anoikis affects the metastasis of ovarian cancer, cervical cancer, and endometrial cancer through various molecules and unique regulatory mechanisms. Under normal physiological conditions, tumor cells that lose matrix adhesion undergo anoikis due to the interruption of key survival signals, making them unable to continue surviving and metastasizing; however, some cancer cells can develop resistance to anoikis, allowing them to survive even without cell adhesion, complete dissemination, colonization, and proliferation at distant sites, and ultimately form metastatic tumors. Various therapeutic drugs, including inhibitors, biologics, targeted drugs, small molecule drugs, and natural products, can exert anti-tumor effects by regulating these specific pathways.
DISCUSSION: The regulatory mechanisms of anoikis provide valuable experimental evidence and a theoretical framework for research related to gynecological tumor metastasis, helping to deeply understand how tumor cells spread to distant organs through the circulatory or lymphatic systems and evade anoikis after leaving the primary site. Intervention strategies targeting anoikis pathways may offer new therapeutic approaches to block the invasion and distant metastasis of gynecological tumors.
