CONCLUSION: Anoikis plays an important role in the metastasis of gynecological tumors, and its regulatory mechanism has potential therapeutic value, but the related clinical translational value still needs further research and verification.

articles.title: State-level disparities and socio-demographic determinants of intention to use contraception among non-using women in South-West Nigeria.
articles.authors: Otitoju O, Sani J, Awoniyi A et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Contraceptive intention is an important precursor to future contraceptive adoption and provides valuable insight into potential demand for family planning services. Although previous studies have examined determinants of contraceptive use and intention in Nigeria, limited evidence exists regarding state-level disparities in contraceptive intention among women who are not currently using any contraceptive method. This study examined state-level disparities and socio-demographic determinants of intention to use contraception among non-using women in South-West Nigeria.
METHODS: This study utilized data from the 2024 Nigeria Demographic and Health Survey (NDHS). The analysis was restricted to 3,307 women aged 15-49 years residing in South-West Nigeria who were not using any contraceptive method at the time of the survey. The outcome variable was intention to use contraception, categorized as intending or not intending to use contraception in the future. Weighted descriptive statistics and survey-adjusted binary logistic regression analyses were performed to estimate the prevalence of contraceptive intention and identify associated factors. Results were presented as crude odds ratios (CORs) and adjusted odds ratios (AORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Statistical significance was set at p < 0.05.
RESULTS: Overall, 32.4% of non-using women reported an intention to use contraception, while 67.6% reported no intention. Substantial state-level disparities were observed, with the prevalence of contraceptive intention ranging from 15.7% in Ondo State to 50.7% in Ekiti State. In the adjusted analysis, women residing in Ekiti were more than twice as likely to intend to use contraception compared with those in Oyo State (AOR = 2.10, 95% CI: 1.50-2.93), whereas women in Ondo had significantly lower odds of contraceptive intention (AOR = 0.39, 95% CI: 0.27-0.56). Women aged 35-39 years (AOR = 0.60, 95% CI: 0.38-0.95), 40-44 years (AOR = 0.34, 95% CI: 0.20-0.58), and 45-49 years (AOR = 0.06, 95% CI: 0.03-0.12) were less likely to intend to use contraception compared with those aged 15-19 years. Secondary education (AOR = 1.99, 95% CI: 1.15-3.44) and higher education (AOR = 1.99, 95% CI: 1.09-3.64) were associated with higher odds of contraceptive intention. Muslim women had lower odds of contraceptive intention than Christian women (AOR = 0.79, 95% CI: 0.65-0.97). Higher parity, exposure to family planning messages (AOR = 1.86, 95% CI: 1.39-2.47), and…

articles.title: Development and validation of a First Trimester Clinical Risk Score (FTRS) for predicting gestational diabetes mellitus in a low-resource setting: an observational cohort study.
articles.authors: Dash S, Mohini, Bose M et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Several models have been developed for early prediction of gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) during the first trimester; however, many rely on biochemical markers or are unsuitable for low-resource settings. This study aimed to develop and validate a simple first-trimester clinical risk score (FTRS) for early prediction of GDM using routinely available clinical variables.
METHODS: In this prospective cohort study, 730 pregnant women presenting before 14 weeks' gestation at a tertiary care teaching hospital in Eastern India were enrolled. GDM was diagnosed using the Diabetes in Pregnancy Study Group India (DIPSI) criteria based on a 75-g oral glucose challenge test performed at three time points during pregnancy. Eight clinical predictors were evaluated using multivariable Poisson regression. Equal- weighted and weighted FTRS models were developed and assessed using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis.
RESULTS: GDM developed in 271 (37.1%) participants. Eight clinical predictors were incorporated into the FTRS. The equal-weighted score (cut-off ≥ 3) achieved an area under the ROC curve (AUC) of 0.74, with 66.8% sensitivity and 82.9% specificity. The weighted score (cut-off ≥ 10) showed slightly better performance, with an AUC of 0.77, 70.2% sensitivity, and 83.4% specificity.
CONCLUSION: The first-trimester clinical risk score (FTRS) is a simple, practical, and non-invasive tool for early prediction of GDM using routinely available clinical variables. Its ease of application makes it particularly suitable for early risk stratification and targeted screening in low-resource settings.

articles.title: Longitudinal associations between maternal blood glucose levels in different pregnancies, glycemic control, and offspring myopia.
articles.authors: Shi R, Jing GZ, Lyu PP et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The association between maternal glycemic status and offspring vision remains unclear. This study aimed to examine the longitudinal associations between maternal glucose concentrations during different pregnancies, glycemic control, and myopia in preschool offspring.
METHODS: This cohort study enrolled 4227 mother-child pairs with children aged 3-6 years, and incorporated both a prospective analysis and a nested case-control analysis as its sub-studies. In the prospective cohort, suspected myopia was defined as non-cycloplegic spherical equivalent (SE)  ≤ 0.75 D; a stricter SE  ≤ 1.00 D cut-off was used for sensitivity analysis. Clinically-diagnosed myopia cases were extracted from electronic medical information in nested case control analysis. The exposures assessed were gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM), glycemic control, and glycemic indexes throughout pregnancy. All multivariable models were adjusted for key covariates including outdoor time, screen time, via modified Poisson regression and generalized linear regression.
RESULTS: A total of 559 (13.7%) children exhibited suspected myopia. Maternal GDM and each additional mmol/L fasting plasma glucose (FPG) in the third trimester were associated with myopia (RR = 1.29, 95% CI: 1.09-1.54; RR = 1.18, 95% CI: 1.04-1.34). Offspring of mothers with GDM and poor glycemic control‌ had a higher risk of myopia (RR = 1.34, 95% CI: 1.10-1.63) compared with unexposed offspring. The nested case-control analysis corroborated these results, and all associations remained significant in the sensitivity analysis with the stricter SE  ≤ 1.00 D threshold.
CONCLUSION: Maternal GDM, elevated FPG levels in the third trimester, and poorly-controlled glucose were associated with an increased risk of myopia in offspring.

articles.title: Spatiotemporal trends and multilevel determinants of coexisting maternal and child undernutrition in Nepal: evidence from Nepal Demographic and Health Survey 2006-2022.
articles.authors: Karki R, Samu GC, Ntaba DN et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coexisting maternal and child undernutrition (CMCU) is a critical aspect of intergenerational malnutrition. The evidence on its epidemiological trends and spatial distribution remains limited in Nepal. This study investigated the temporal trends, determinants, and spatial distribution of CMCU in Nepal from 2006 to 2022.
METHOD: We used data from the 2006, 2011, 2016, and 2022 Nepal Demographic and Health Survey (NDHS) databases. Maternal and child pairs with complete anthropometric records were included in the analysis. The co-occurrence of maternal undernutrition (height < 145 cm) and child stunting/wasting/underweight were defined as CMCU. Survey-weighted descriptive analysis was performed to assess prevalence trends. Individual- and community-level determinants of CMCU were assessed using multilevel logistic regression with a two-level hierarchy. Individual children and their households (level one) were grouped within community enumeration areas or clusters (level two). Global Moran's I and Getis-Ord Gi* Hotspot analysis were performed to assess spatial autocorrelation and local clustering, respectively.
RESULTS: The prevalence of CMCU decreased from 9.78% in 2006 to 4.68% in 2022, a 52.1% decrease over 16 years). A PCV of 0.802 in Model IV of the community level variation has been explained after adding both the individual and community factors. Even low ICC = 0.029 in Model IV shows that only 2.9% of the remaining, unexplained variances in Child and Maternal Co-undernutrition (CMCU) is caused by unmeasured community clustering factors as compared to ICC = 0.134 in model I which shows that 13.4% of the variance is explained by unobserved community level factors. This means Model IV shows that 97.1% variance is explained by individual and household level factors. CMCU odds were inversely associated with maternal education (AOR = 0.68(95% CI: 0.50-0.91), 0.39(95% CI: 0.26-0.58), 0.20(95% CI: 0.07-0.58) for primary, secondary, higher respectively relative to no education). Children aged 12-59 months had higher CMCU odds than < 12 months. Odds were lower in contraceptive users (AOR = 0.75(95% CI: 0.60-0.93)) and higher for perceived health facility distance (AOR = 1.24(95% CI: 1.00-1.52)). The spatial average was significantly clustered in 2022 (Moran's I = 0.058, Z = 2.548) with hotspots in the southern Terai.
CONCLUSION: Despite an overall decline in CMCU during 2006-2022, socioeconomic and regional inequalities were observed in Nepal. CMCU…

articles.title: Unveiling the associated factors of menstrual experience and its relation with health-related quality of life among the female university students: a cross-sectional study in the Balasore district of Odisha.
articles.authors: Ghatuary R, Mahato R, Gan GC et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Poor menstrual health poses a persistent challenge to young women, particularly to those navigating both academic life and experiencing a profound biopsychological transition. The university students often live in varied residential environments, experience issues like inaccessible sanitation infrastructure, lack of privacy, and peer influence, which shape their menstrual health and well-being. However, in a country like India, addressing such an evidence gap among the youth students is imperative to develop effective interventions and to restructure the institutional policies. In this purview, the present study explores the menstrual pattern, health, and ailments among the youth students in a higher education institutional setting, and explores their link with quality of life.
METHODS: The present study employed a cross-sectional survey in the district of Balasore, among the adult female university students. Multi-stage sampling was performed to identify study participants., Informed consent was obtained as well. Self-administered questionnaires were used to obtain data on socio-demographic characteristics, menstrual characteristics, ailments and disorders, and health-related quality of life. Both descriptive and inferential statistics were performed for data analysis.
RESULTS: The findings highlight that almost two-thirds of the total 284 students were hostel boarders, while a few resided in their homes. The use of sanitary pads was common (93.7%), but several followed an unhygienic method of disposal (13.0%). Study participants reported common issues like heavy bleeding, frequent delay in menstruation, and crampy abdominal pain. Interestingly, the prevalence of primary dysmenorrhea was around 72%. Around 36% of the study participants were dissatisfied with their menstrual experience, which was significantly associated with lower age and low maternal education. The study participants had poor physical functioning, poor vitality, and poor social functioning related to their menstrual health-related quality of life, especially in the case of the younger age cohort, those living in rented hostels, and those experiencing heavy menstrual bleeding. The study participants, who had dissatisfactory menstrual experiences and had multiple diagnosed menstrual disorders, showed a significantly greater likelihood of having poor menstrual health-related quality of life.
CONCLUSION: Overall findings highlight an alarming menstrual health scenario among…

articles.title: Effect of S-equol supplementation on menopausal symptoms, sleep complaints, pain, and work engagement: an exploratory, multicentre open-label study in Spanish women.
articles.authors: Palacios S, Castelo-Branco C, Sugaya K et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although S-equol has demonstrated efficacy in randomized trials conducted mainly in Japanese and American populations, evidence in European populations remains limited. Menopausal symptoms have been shown to negatively affect work productivity and engagement, yet interventions targeting both symptom relief and work-related outcomes remain poorly studied. This exploratory, multicentre, open-label, single-arm study aimed to confirm previous observations also in European women and further explore the impact of S-equol on quality of life and work engagement.
METHODS: Subjects received daily SE5-OH tablets providing 10 mg S-equol for 12 weeks, followed by 4 weeks without supplementation. A total of 159 women received at least one dose (included in the Intention to treat population) and 124 followed the treatment and visit schedule described in the study protocol (included in the Per Protocol analysis). Study participants had a mean (SD) age of 52.5 (4.1) years and included pre- (1.6%), peri- (26.6%) and post-menopausal (60.5%) women. The primary endpoint was Menopause Rating Scale (MRS) and secondary endpoints included Vasomotor Symptoms (VMS), Utrecht Work Engagement Scale (UWES) and Visual Analogue Scale (VAS) for pain and sleep complaints. Participants recorded their hot flashes/night sweats' frequency daily and menopausal symptoms' severity, pain, sleep complaints and work engagement were assessed at follow-up visits (at week 4, 12 and 16). Changes from baseline were analysed using paired parametric or non-parametric tests, as appropriate.
RESULTS: After 12 weeks, the MRS was significantly improved (-11.6 points; p < 0.0001) and a significant improvement was also observed on VMS frequency (20% to 70%; p < 0.0001), pain (-1.1 points for shoulder pain and -1.9 points for low back pain; p < 0.0001), sleep complaints (-2.1 points; p < 0.0001) and work engagement (0.2 points; p = 0.0097).
CONCLUSIONS: The results of the study are in line with previous findings, showing an improvement in menopausal symptoms and quality of life for women experiencing moderate to severe menopausal symptoms. S-equol may be considered as a potential complementary, non-hormonal option to relieve menopausal symptoms across different menopausal stages.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: clinicaltrials.gov ID: NCT06398236 - retrospectively registered on 9 April 2024.

articles.title: Quality of life improves after endometriosis surgery independent of #ENZIAN classification: a multicenter cohort study.
articles.authors: Perricos-Hess A, Gstoettner M, Heinzl F et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Endometriosis is a chronic inflammatory disease associated with substantial impairment of quality of life. Although the #ENZIAN classification enables detailed anatomical characterization of disease distribution, its relevance for predicting patient-reported outcomes after surgery remains uncertain. Clarifying this relationship is essential for patient counseling and outcome-oriented surgical decision making.
METHODS: This multicenter study, registered on ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05624567), prospectively recruited consecutive women aged 18 to 50 years undergoing surgery for suspected endometriosis at certified endometriosis centers in Austria, Germany, and Switzerland. Only women with surgically and histopathologically confirmed endometriosis who completed the baseline Endometriosis Health Profile-30 (EHP-30) questionnaire were included in the final analysis. Disease localization was classified intraoperatively using the #ENZIAN and rASRM systems. Quality of life was assessed using the EHP-30 questionnaire preoperatively and at 6 and 12 months after surgery. Longitudinal changes and predictors of quality-of-life outcomes were analyzed using ordinal logistic regression models.
RESULTS: A total of 627 women were included at baseline, with 430 and 325 completing 6- and 12-month follow-up, respectively. Surgical treatment was associated with a marked and clinically meaningful improvement in quality of life, with EHP-30 scores improving significantly within the first 6 months after surgery and remaining stable at 12 months. This improvement was observed consistently across all #ENZIAN compartments, including deep infiltrating and multifocal disease. Anatomical disease distribution and rASRM stage were not significantly associated with baseline quality-of-life or postoperative recovery trajectories. In contrast, baseline symptom burden and complete surgical resection emerged as the strongest predictors of early postoperative quality-of-life improvement.
CONCLUSIONS: Surgical treatment of endometriosis was associated with substantial and sustained improvement in patient-reported quality of life, independent of anatomical disease distribution as classified by #ENZIAN. These findings suggest that meaningful postoperative benefit can be achieved across all disease localizations and underscore the importance of focusing on symptom severity and surgical completeness rather than anatomical staging alone. Incorporating patient-reported outcome measures…

articles.title: Trajectories, bother, and risk factors of lower urinary tract symptoms during the first postpartum year: a prospective cohort study.
articles.authors: Wang X, Zhang L, Wang Y et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Lower urinary tract symptoms (LUTS) are common after childbirth and may adversely affect women's quality of life. However, most postpartum studies have focused on urinary incontinence or symptom prevalence at a single time point, with limited information on longitudinal symptom trajectories, symptom-specific burden, and factors associated with LUTS during the first postpartum year, particularly in Asian populations.
METHODS: This prospective cohort study was conducted at a tertiary referral hospital in Beijing, China. A total of 2,190 women completed assessments at 42 days and one year postpartum using the International Consultation on Incontinence Questionnaire-Female Lower Urinary Tract Symptoms (ICIQ-FLUTS). Prevalence, longitudinal trajectories, and symptom-specific bother were evaluated. Multivariable logistic regression identified factors associated with postpartum LUTS.
RESULTS: At one year postpartum, 56.0% of women reported at least one LUTS. Storage symptoms were more common than voiding symptoms (45.2% vs. 25.4%). Stress urinary incontinence (SUI) was the most prevalent symptom (26.3%). Nocturia and daytime frequency demonstrated the greatest improvement, whereas SUI was the only symptom to increase in prevalence, with 15.9% of women experiencing worsening or new-onset symptoms (P < 0.001). Although urgency urinary incontinence (UUI) affected 13.5% of women, it was the most bothersome symptom, with 93.1% reporting any bother and 32.3% reporting moderate-to-severe bother. Vaginal delivery, particularly forceps delivery, and multiparity were independently associated with several LUTS outcomes, whereas pelvic floor rehabilitation was associated with lower odds of urinary incontinence-related symptoms.
CONCLUSIONS: More than half of women continue to experience LUTS one year postpartum. Postpartum LUTS follow dynamic trajectories, and symptom burden may not be reflected by prevalence alone. These findings support extended postpartum surveillance and patient-centred outcomes.

articles.title: Acute cholecystitis during pregnancy: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.authors: Kyrtsonis GK, Bobotis S, Geropoulos G et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute cholecystitis is an uncommon non-obstetric surgical emergency in pregnancy, yet guidance on management remains inconsistent. This systematic review and meta-analysis examined presentation, diagnostics, management, and outcomes of pregnant patients diagnosed with acute cholecystitis.
METHODS: PubMed, Web of Science, and Scopus were searched from inception to February 2024 (PROSPERO CRD42022350290). Eligible studies reported acute cholecystitis in pregnancy with individual patient data or extractable cohort data. Risk of bias was assessed in duplicates. Descriptive statistics summarised individual data, and random-effects meta-analysis generated pooled risk ratios (RR) with 95% confidence interval (CI).
RESULTS: Ninety studies (1964-2023) were included: 48 case reports/series (n = 118), 19 descriptive cohorts (n = 5,702), 19 cohorts comparing operative versus non-operative care (n = 91,955), and 4 cohorts comparing laparoscopic versus open surgery (n = 62,620). Among cases with symptom data (n = 75), right-upper-quadrant pain (40%), vomiting (33%), nausea (29%), and fever (17%) predominated. Imaging (n = 92) most often showed gallstones (42%) and ultrasonographic cholecystitis or wall thickening (21%). Of the cases with management data (n = 93), surgery was performed in 81 (laparoscopic 71/81; percutaneous drainage 10/81; open 1/81);12 were managed non-operatively. Of 83 with outcomes, 84% had uncomplicated courses. Meta-analysis found no significant differences between operative and non-operative care for caesarean delivery, preterm birth, postpartum haemorrhage, or composite complications, but venous thromboembolism risk was lower with surgery (RR 0.55, 95% CI 0.37-0.82), although this outcome was reported by only two studies.
CONCLUSIONS: Ultrasound-based diagnosis and laparoscopic cholecystectomy appear safe across all trimesters of pregnancy, with obstetric outcomes comparable to non-operative management. Operative management was associated with a lower observed risk of venous thromboembolism, although this finding was based on limited evidence. Further prospective studies are needed to optimise patient selection and surgical timing.

articles.title: Evaluating the efficacy of a novel endometrial receptivity test in improving pregnancy outcomes for Chinese in vitro fertilization patients: a single-center retrospective study.
articles.authors: Ji C, Wang X, Yao J et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Current evidence on whether endometrial receptivity tests improve pregnancy outcomes among in vitro fertilization (IVF) patients remains conflicting and limited. This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy of HerRecepta, a novel transcriptomic endometrial receptivity test, in guiding personalized embryo transfer (pET) for Chinese IVF patients, with a focus on recurrent implantation failure (RIF) and clinical factors influencing the window of implantation (WOI).
METHODS: This retrospective study included 220 IVF patients who had undergone endometrial receptivity testing. Based on the receptivity test results, patients were stratified into the standard embryo transfer (ET) group or pET group. Pregnancy outcomes following frozen embryo transfer were then compared between groups.
RESULTS: Of the 220 patients, 124 (56.36%) had a receptive endometrium and underwent standard ET, while 96 (43.64%) had a non-receptive endometrium and underwent pET. Among the latter group, 69 (71.87%) were classified as pre-receptive. Advanced age (> 35 years, P = 0.036) and high anti-Müllerian hormone (AMH) levels (> 5 ng/mL, P < 0.001) were associated with a higher rate of non-receptivity. The overall clinical pregnancy rate (CPR) and live birth rate (LBR) were 46.50% and 32.11%, respectively. The pET group showed comparable outcomes to the standard ET group in CPR (46.36% vs. 46.67%, P = 0.966), and LBR (32.38% vs. 31.76%, P = 0.930). Similar results were observed in the RIF subgroup (124 patients: 79 in the standard ET group and 45 in the pET group).
CONCLUSION: HerRecepta-guided pET yielded pregnancy and live birth rates comparable to those achieved with standard ET. Given the retrospective design and lack of a control group, these findings support the feasibility of this test rather than demonstrating its effectiveness or superiority, and further randomized trials are warranted.

articles.title: Bladder augmentation and continent catheterizable channel creation in children: surgical, functional, and renal outcomes.
articles.authors: Tagcı S, Ekberli G, Saglam S et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The aim of this study was to present our institutional experience with continent catheterizable channel creation, with or without bladder augmentation, and to evaluate the surgical, functional, and renal outcomes of these reconstructive procedures in pediatric patients.
METHODS: A retrospective review was conducted of pediatric patients who underwent CCC creation with or without concurrent BA between January 2019 and December 2024. Demographic characteristics, primary diagnoses, surgical details, postoperative complications, ultrasonographic findings, glomerular filtration rate (GFR), urinary tract infection history, and continence outcomes were evaluated. Hydronephrosis was graded according to the Society for Fetal Urology classification, and renal function was assessed using the Schwartz formula.
RESULTS: A total of 40 patients were included in the study. Bladder augmentation combined with continent catheterizable channel (CCC) creation was performed in 27 patients, while 13 patients underwent CCC creation alone. In the augmentation group, the sigmoid colon was used in 16 cases and the ileum in 11 cases. Among patients undergoing bladder augmentation, mean bladder capacity increased from 51 ± 35.7 mL preoperatively to 328.5 ± 41.6 mL postoperatively. Continence was achieved in 36 of 40 patients during follow-up, and the frequency of symptomatic urinary tract infections decreased after reconstruction. Renal function and upper urinary tract status remained stable in most patients, with no significant deterioration in glomerular filtration rate or hydronephrosis grades. Procedure-related complications occurred in both groups and were mostly managed successfully with additional surgical intervention; one mortality related to superior mesenteric artery thrombosis was observed. No significant differences were observed in preoperative and postoperative GFR values or hydronephrosis grades between groups.
CONCLUSIONS: Despite a considerable complication burden, lower urinary tract reconstruction with bladder augmentation and/or continent catheterizable channel creation remains a valuable option for selected pediatric patients, providing favorable functional outcomes and supporting short- to medium-term stabilization of renal and upper urinary tract function.

articles.title: A systematic review and meta-analysis of the effects of continuous glucose monitoring compared to self-monitoring of blood glucose on glycemic control and maternal and infant outcomes in women with gestational diabetes mellitus.
articles.authors: Zheng L, Tian R, Zhang L et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) compared to self-blood glucose monitoring (SMBG) has been a controversial topic regarding glycemic control in pregnant women with gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM), as well as maternal and infant outcomes. The aim of this study was to assess and compare the effectiveness of CGM and SMBG in managing glycemic control and perinatal outcomes among homebound pregnant women with GDM.
METHODS: A comprehensive search was conducted across five databases-PubMed, Web of Science, Medline, Embase, and the Cochrane Library-commencing on July 15, 2024. We included four randomized controlled trials (RCTs) that compared CGM with SMBG in patients with GDM. The primary outcomes assessed were gestational weight gain (GWG), glycated hemoglobin(HbA1c), and the number of people treated with hypoglycemic drugs. Participants were excluded if they had received any glucose-lowering medication prior to enrollment. A meta-analysis of interventions on the basis of at least two studies with 95% confidence intervals and an assessment of heterogeneity via the I² statistic were performed.
RESULTS: The results of the study showed that CGM was significantly associated with a decrease in the number of women with excessive GWG and an increase in the number of GWG-appropriate (RR = 0.57; 95% CI: 0.41, 0.80; I² = 0.0%; P = 0.001), (RR = 1.55; 95% CI: 1.19, 2.03; I² = 0.0%; P = 0.001). However, GWG-insufficiency was not significantly different (RR = 1.03; 95% CI: 0.47, 2.26; I² = 0.0%; P = 0.948). Real-time continuous glucose monitoring (rt-CGM) may offer superior effectiveness in glycemic control management compared with SMBG (SMD=-0.70; 95%CI=-1.07, -0.34; P = 0.000; I2 = 0.0%), whereas retrospective continuous glucose monitoring (r-CGM) demonstrates greater effectiveness in reducing infant birth weight (SMD=-0.30; 95%CI=-0.54, -0.06; P = 0.018; I2 = 8.6%). No significant differences were observed in the other perinatal outcomes.
CONCLUSION: CGM may be more effective than SMBG in preventing excessive weight gain and maintaining appropriate gestational weight in women with GDM. Moreover, rt-CGM appears to offer superior glycemic control compared with SMBG. r-CGM may be more effective in reducing neonatal birth weight.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: The PROSPERO registration number is CRD42024571538.

articles.title: Factors associated with exclusive breastfeeding at 6 weeks postpartum in Southwest China: a cross-sectional study.
articles.authors: Yan P, Liu X, Wei L et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Breastfeeding is known to be shaped by a complex interplay of socio-demographic, medical, and psychological factors. However, there is a lack of research on the determinants of breastfeeding at 6 weeks postpartum. This study aimed to examine factors associated with exclusive breastfeeding (EBF) at 6 weeks postpartum in Southwest China and to provide evidence for early postpartum breastfeeding support.
METHODS: Sociodemographic information, infant feeding patterns at 6 weeks postpartum, and reasons for non-exclusive breastfeeding were collected using a self-designed questionnaire. Perinatal and postpartum clinical data were extracted from the electronic medical record system. The Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS) was used to assess postpartum depressive symptoms. Binary logistic regression analysis was used to identify factors associated with exclusive breastfeeding at 6 weeks postpartum.
RESULTS: A total of 10,730 valid questionnaires were included, with a valid response rate of 93.4%. At 6 weeks postpartum, 6,478 mothers (60.4%) maintained EBF. This study found that the most commonly reported reason for discontinuing EBF was perceived insufficient milk supply (n = 3,334, 78.4%). Factors associated with lower odds of EBF included maternal age ≥ 35 years, maternal illness severity, infectious diseases, postpartum hemorrhage, twin pregnancy, resumption of menstruation, and postpartum depressive symptoms. Factors associated with higher odds of EBF included higher educational level of the mother-in-law, multiparity, vaginal delivery, and infant NICU admission.
CONCLUSION: At 6 weeks postpartum, EBF was associated with clinical, psychological, and family-related factors. The 6-week postpartum follow-up may provide an opportunity to identify mothers who need additional lactation and psychological support, particularly older mothers, mothers of twins, women after cesarean delivery, and those reporting depressive symptoms or concerns about milk supply.

articles.title: CFAP47 is involved in sperm head-tail coupling via cooperating with Septin12 and SUN5: gene knockout and protein analysis.
articles.authors: Liu T, Su Y, Liu G et al.
articles.abstract:
CONTEXT: Sperm head-tail linkage is essential for maintaining sperm integrity and male fertility. Although CFAP47 is associated with multiple morphological abnormalities of the sperm flagella, its role in sperm head-tail coupling remains unclear.
AIMS: This study aimed to investigate the role of CFAP47 in sperm head-tail connection.
METHODS: A Cfap47 knockout mouse model was established to assess sperm motility and morphology. Molecular docking, co-immunoprecipitation and proximity ligation assays were used to investigate the relationships of CFAP47, Septin12 and SUN5.
KEY RESULTS: Cfap47 knockout mice exhibited impaired sperm motility and severe sperm morphological defects, with approximately 70% of sperm displaying abnormal head-tail connection or decapitation. Co-immunoprecipitation and proximity ligation assays demonstrated that CFAP47 cooperates with Septin12 and SUN5. CFAP47 deficiency reduced the protein expression levels and affected their localization at the sperm head-tail junction.
CONCLUSIONS: CFAP47 is essential for sperm head-tail coupling.
IMPLICATIONS: These findings provide new insight into the molecular basis of sperm head-tail connection.

articles.title: Structural Racism and Maternal Health Inequities: Healthcare System Mechanisms Affecting Black Women in the United States.
articles.journal: Journal of racial and ethnic health disparities
articles.authors: Bommagouni M, Sriram S
articles.abstract: Racial disparities in severe maternal morbidity (SMM) and pregnancy-related mortality in the United States disproportionately affect non-Hispanic Black women and persist across socioeconomic strata. While structural racism and social determinants of health are recognized as important upstream conditions, the healthcare-system processes through which these conditions may contribute to inequities remain insufficiently specified. This paper develops a conceptual framework linking structural racism to maternal health disparities through two key healthcare-system pathways: hospital quality stratification and continuity-of-care fragmentation. The framework was developed through a conceptual synthesis of relevant literature identified through purposive, manual searches focusing on structural racism, SDOH, maternal health disparities, hospital quality, healthcare access, and continuity of care. The literature was synthesized to identify recurring relationships across structural, socioeconomic, and healthcare-system levels, from which the two proposed pathways were identified. The framework conceptualizes structural racism as an upstream determinant operating through residential segregation, hospital disinvestment, and inequitable healthcare financing. These conditions may shape individual- and community-level socioeconomic circumstances, healthcare access and exposure, and subsequent differences in hospital quality and continuity of care. By integrating structural racism theory with healthcare-system analysis, the framework shifts attention from descriptive disparities toward potential pathways through which inequities may be produced. The proposed framework identifies testable relationships for future empirical research and potential intervention points for improving hospital capacity, continuity of maternal care, and racial equity in maternal health.

articles.title: Nectin-4 mediates rubella virus entry in airway and placental cells.
articles.authors: Mori Y, Sakata M, Nakatsu Y et al.
articles.abstract: Rubella virus (RuV) causes rubella and, when acquired during pregnancy, congenital rubella syndrome1. Despite its clinical significance, the cellular entry mechanism of RuV remains poorly characterized, owing to limited identification of host receptors2, which hinders pathogenesis research and therapeutic development. Here, using proximity biotin labelling-based proteomics coupled with CRISPR-Cas9 validation, we identify nectin-4 as a functional RuV entry receptor. Ectopic expression of nectin-4 conferred susceptibility to RuV in non-permissive cells, whereas blocking or genetic ablation of nectin-4 reduced infection, results that demonstrate that nectin-4 is a major entry factor. Mechanistically, nectin-4 directly interacts with the RuV envelope glycoprotein heterodimer and facilitates receptor-mediated endocytosis following initial calcium-dependent viral attachment to cellular lipids. In polarized airway epithelial models, nectin-4 mediates basolateral entry of RuV and supports apical progeny release, a finding that provides a molecular mechanism for respiratory transmission. In placental models, nectin-4 is highly expressed on syncytiotrophoblasts and facilitates infection at the maternal-fetal interface, although additional nectin-4-independent pathways contribute to infection of other trophoblast populations. Together, these data establish nectin-4 as a key factor for respiratory transmission and early placental infection of RuV and highlight it as a promising therapeutic target for the prevention of rubella and related diseases.

articles.title: The hMOF/PCNA Axis Mitigates Cisplatin Resistance in Ovarian Cancer Cells via Modulating DNA Damage Response.
articles.authors: Xu S, Li T, Liu H et al.
articles.abstract: Cisplatin (DDP) is a first-line chemotherapeutic agent for ovarian cancer (OC); however, acquired resistance frequently compromises treatment efficacy. This study investigates whether the hMOF/PCNA axis contributes to DDP resistance through modulation of the DNA damage response (DDR). DDP sensitivity was assessed by CCK‑8 assay in parental OVCAR3 and DDP-resistant OVCAR3/DDP cells. hMOF expression was evaluated by RT‑qPCR and Western blot. Lentivirus-mediated RNA interference was employed to establish hMOF-knockdown and negative control cell models. Functional evaluations included resistance profiling by CCK‑8 assay, apoptosis analysis by flow cytometry, detection of DDR foci (γ‑H2AX, 53BP1, p-ATM) via immunofluorescence, assessment of DNA strand breaks by comet assay, and measurement of MRP and LRP expression by RT‑qPCR and Western blot. The interaction and colocalization between hMOF and PCNA were examined by co‑immunoprecipitation and immunofluorescence. PCNA expression and its post-translational modifications were analyzed by Western blot and immunoprecipitation. For mechanistic investigation, cells were treated with MG149, TAK‑243, or cycloheximide. In rescue experiments, BMI1 was overexpressed in hMOF-knockdown cells, followed by comprehensive functional validation. hMOF expression was elevated in DDP-resistant OVCAR3/DDP cells with increased IC₅₀ values. hMOF knockdown reduced DDP IC₅₀ and resistance index, downregulated MRP and LRP, enhanced apoptosis, and aggravated DNA damage. Mechanistically, hMOF bound PCNA in the nucleus. hMOF knockdown decreased PCNA expression and acetylation, enhanced its ubiquitination, and shortened its half-life, as corroborated by MG149, TAK‑243, and cycloheximide treatments. BMI1 overexpression restored PCNA levels and acetylation, reversed ubiquitination, and attenuated sh‑hMOF-induced DDP sensitization, confirming PCNA-dependent regulation. hMOF is upregulated in DDP-resistant ovarian cancer cells and stabilizes PCNA through acetylation-mediated stabilization and suppression of ubiquitination, thereby enhancing DDR and promoting chemoresistance. The hMOF/PCNA axis represents a potential therapeutic target for overcoming DDP resistance in OC.

articles.title: NFE2L1 promotes cisplatin resistance by attenuating ferroptosis through SLC27A2-mediated fatty acid metabolism in ovarian cancer.
articles.authors: Zhang M, Yan S, Zhao B et al.
articles.abstract: Approaches that promote ferroptosis have emerged as promising therapeutic strategies for chemotherapy-resistant cancers; however, the mechanisms regulating ferroptosis during acquired therapeutic resistance remain incompletely understood. Using RNA sequencing, we identified that Nuclear Factor Erythroid-2 Related Factor 1 (NFE2L1) is upregulated in cisplatin-resistant ovarian cancer (OC) cells and patient tissues, as well as in ferroptosis-resistant models. Genetic knockdown of NFE2L1 resensitized cells to cisplatin both in vitro and in vivo. Notably, this effect was largely reversed by ferroptosis inhibitors, which significantly rescued cell survival following NFE2L1 depletion under cisplatin treatment. Further experiments demonstrated that modulating NFE2L1 expression affects the response to ferroptosis inducers by regulating iron accumulation and lipid peroxidation. Mechanistically, NFE2L1 silencing increased the transcription of long-chain fatty acid transport protein 2 (SLC27A2/FATP2). Chromatin immunoprecipitation and dual-luciferase reporter assays showed that NFE2L1 bound directly to the SLC27A2 promoter, where it competitively inhibited the recruitment of the transcription factor SP1. As a key member of the long-chain acyl-CoA synthetase family, FATP2 promotes the uptake and activation of long-chain fatty acids, processes that have been implicated in the regulation of ferroptosis. Subsequent LC-MS-based lipidomic analysis revealed that NFE2L1 reprogrammed intracellular fatty acid metabolism, characterized by increased polyunsaturated fatty acid (PUFA) levels and decreased monounsaturated fatty acid (MUFA) levels within phosphatidylethanolamines (PEs), thereby increasing cellular susceptibility to ferroptosis. Consistent with these findings, supplementation with exogenous unsaturated fatty acids modulated NFE2L1-mediated ferroptosis sensitivity. Collectively, our findings reveal a novel NFE2L1/SLC27A2 axis that drives cisplatin resistance in OC by suppressing ferroptosis, and suggest a potential therapeutic strategy for treating cisplatin-resistant ovarian cancer.

articles.title: Past, Present, and Future Implantable Neuromodulation Treatments for Management of Urinary Urge Incontinence (UUI): Implications for Clinical Effectiveness and Safety.
articles.authors: Siegel S, Ehlert MJ, Powell CR et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF THE REVIEW: This review examines the progress made in neuromodulation therapies for UUI since the original introduction of SNM devices until now. There are multiple current commercial neuromodulation therapies from which to choose, including those with sacral or tibial nerve targets. The intent is to provide critical evidence to help clinicians decide which device to offer their patients.
RECENT FINDINGS: Modern SNM systems consistently outperform both previous-generation SNM and contemporary iTNM. Modern SNM demonstrates substantially higher effectiveness than pooled averages including early device studies with outdated study designs, tools and implant techniques. Current iTNM outcomes are comparable to legacy SNM yet remain markedly lower than modern SNM. Contemporary data supports a clear hierarchy-modern SNM offers the highest effectiveness and the most favorable safety profile. We believe that our field is moving toward minimally invasive, highly targeted, patient-directed SNM systems-an evolution that aligns with both clinical outcomes and patient preferences.

articles.title: Preprimary education laws and women's gender attitudes, empowerment and reproductive autonomy in 117 low- and middle-income countries.
articles.authors: Lou S, Ma N, Chen S et al.
articles.abstract: Preprimary education is central to the global education agenda, including Sustainable Development Goal 4.2. Despite global momentum in low- and middle-income countries, cross-national evidence on long-term outcomes associated with preprimary education legislation remains limited. Here we applied a matrix-completion approach with subgroup and sensitivity analyses using 495 nationally representative surveys from 1990 to 2024, covering nearly 6.7 million women across 117 countries. Eligibility under the legislation was associated with higher educational enrolment and completion, and with more gender-egalitarian attitudes, more favourable empowerment-related behaviours and greater reproductive autonomy. For example, eligibility was associated with higher female primary-school enrolment (1.21 percentage points (pp); 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.52 to 1.91; P < 0.001) and completion (0.75 pp; 95% CI 0.24 to 1.25; P = 0.004), greater disapproval of wife-beating (1.04 pp; 95% CI 0.53 to 1.56; P < 0.001), greater participation in decisions about husbands' earnings (3.25 pp; 95% CI 2.50 to 4.00; P < 0.001) and greater ever use of contraception (2.96 pp; 95% CI 2.33 to 3.59; P < 0.001). Eligibility under the legislation was also associated with lower rates of adolescent childbearing (-2.41 pp; 95% CI -2.67 to -2.14; P < 0.001) and child marriage (-0.43 pp; 95% CI -0.71 to -0.15; P = 0.003). These findings provide cross-national evidence directly relevant to ongoing policy discussions surrounding Sustainable Development Goal 4.2 and broader global development agendas, while emphasizing the importance of implementation capacity and equitable system expansion.

articles.title: A 5-mm open umbilical entry technique for laparoscopic gynecologic surgery.
articles.authors: Robb C, Tetelbaun L, Xu P et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Laparoscopic entry carries a complication rate of up to 1.3%, including bowel and vascular injury. The Hasson, Veress, and 5-mm open entry techniques differ in approach: Hasson uses a 1-2 cm open incision, Veress involves blind needle access, and the 5-mm open entry technique uses a small umbilical incision with blunt peritoneal entry followed by insertion of a 5-mm bladeless optical trocar. Previously shown to be safe and easily mastered by both attendings and residents, this study re-evaluates the 5-mm technique in a multi-surgeon setting.
METHODS: The senior author's extensive clinical experience with this technique informed its continued use and motivated the present retrospective evaluation of all consecutive cases performed between 2021 and 2025. The technique involves tenting the umbilicus with three tonsil clamps, injecting 1 mL of 0.25% bupivacaine, making a 2-4 mm vertical incision within the umbilical scar that is then stretched to approximately 5 mm with a tonsil clamp, and bluntly dissecting the fascia to expose the mid-umbilical fascia and enter the peritoneal cavity. A 5-mm bladeless optical trocar is advanced under direct visualization, and carbon dioxide insufflation begins once placement is confirmed.
RESULTS: All cases achieved successful entry without conversion to Veress. One patient had a Hasson entry for concurrent cholecystectomy. Omental adhesions were present in 15 cases (7.7%). No entry-related complications occurred.
CONCLUSION: In this cohort, the 5-mm open entry technique was successfully performed without entry-related complications and demonstrated favorable cosmetic outcomes.

articles.title: Stromal APOL4 defines a cancer-associated fibroblast state that organizes a chemosensitive niche in ovarian cancer.
articles.authors: Lim SO, Park J, Lee K et al.
articles.abstract: Despite initial high response rates to platinum-based chemotherapy in high-grade serous ovarian carcinoma, most patients eventually develop resistance, and the contribution of the tumor microenvironment to treatment outcomes has remained underexplored relative to tumor cell-intrinsic mechanisms. Combining patient-derived ex vivo carboplatin screening with bulk and single-cell transcriptomics, functional perturbation in cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs), and high-resolution spatial transcriptomics, we identified stromal apolipoprotein L4 (APOL4) as a biomarker of platinum sensitivity. The ex vivo classification showed directional concordance with clinical platinum response, and stromal APOL4 expression predicted favorable outcomes across multiple validation cohorts. APOL4 specifically marked a transcriptionally distinct CAF subtype (CAF-1) that extended beyond canonical CAF states and exhibited high matrix metalloproteinase and immune-activating cytokine expression. APOL4 knockdown attenuated the CAF-1 transcriptional program, and in 3D tumor-CAF co-cultures conferred carboplatin resistance to 12 of 14 ovarian cancer cell lines, providing causal evidence that stromal APOL4 supports platinum sensitivity in a tumor cell-extrinsic manner. NicheNet analysis revealed bidirectionally asymmetric communication: CAF-1 engaged non-stressed cancer cells through epithelial integrity-supporting axes, whereas other CAFs preferentially reinforced stressed, drug-tolerant cancer cells through canonical chemoresistance circuits. High-resolution Xenium spatial transcriptomics revealed a contact-restricted spatial association between CAF-1 proximity and reduced cancer-cell stress, defining a low-stress, immune-infiltrated niche that is spatially and compositionally distinct from the stress-enriched, immune-poor niche associated with CAF-2, with CAF-3 sharing features of both compartments. These findings identify stromal APOL4-CAF-1 as a prognostic biomarker and a functional contributor linking stromal matrix remodeling to platinum sensitivity and associated with an immune-infiltrated microenvironment, highlighting CAF-1-targeted strategies to enhance chemotherapy efficacy.

articles.title: Olaparib plus tremelimumab in women with recurrent ovarian cancer and a germline BRCA1 or BRCA2 mutation: a phase I/II study.
articles.authors: Adams SF, Gimotty PA, Rutledge TL et al.
articles.abstract: Response rates to immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) in ovarian cancer are low. In preclinical studies, poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase inhibition (PARPi) synergized with CTLA4 ICB to achieve long-term survival in Brca1-deficient ovarian cancer models. Here we evaluated the safety and efficacy of combined treatment with the PARPi olaparib and the CTLA4 ICB tremelimumab for recurrent epithelial ovarian cancer in a multi-site single-arm phase I/II study enrolling 50 women with germline BRCA1 or BRCA2 mutations (NCT02571725). In phase I, no new toxicities were identified (n = 3). In the combined phase I and II safety cohort (n = 49), 57% of subjects experienced grade 3 or 4 non-hematologic toxicity, with tremelimumab discontinuation in 34.7%. The primary phase II endpoint, overall response rate was 32.7% (95% CI 19.5-45.8%), and disease control rate was 47.7% (95% CI 33.0-62.5%). Secondary outcomes were progression-free survival (PFS, 3.0 months, 95% CI 2.7-5.9), and overall survival (24.3 months, CI 14.9-30.4). In exploratory post-hoc biomarker analyses, low VSTM5 or IFIT1B expression was associated with treatment benefit and improved PFS (p < 0.001). Although the trial did not meet its prespecified efficacy endpoint, PFS > 12 months in 6 subjects among this heavily pre-treated cohort highlight the need for biomarkers to select regimens for patients with recurrent ovarian cancer.

articles.title: Complications and effectiveness at 3 years in women treated for pelvic organ prolapse with transvaginal mesh repair: results from the PRIMES Registry in China.
articles.authors: Liang S, Zhang Y, Zhang Y et al.
articles.abstract: Transvaginal mesh (TVM) repair for pelvic organ prolapse (POP) is controversial. Although the US FDA ordered manufacturers to stop selling TVM products for POP in 2019, synthetic mesh continues to be used for selected patients in parts of East Asia, Latin America, and Europe. In 2020, the Chinese Urogynaecology and Reconstructive Pelvic Surgery Association updated the indications for TVM to (1) recurrent POP; or (2) patients aged 60 years or older diagnosed with severe primary POP particularly anterior compartment prolapse who have low or no sexual activity and cannot tolerate abdominal repair surgery. This nationwide prospective registry evaluated 3-year complications and effectiveness of TVM in women meeting the updated indications. From July 1, 2019, to December 31, 2021, 3847 consecutive women undergoing TVM repair with lightweight mesh by experienced grade IV surgeons at 103 tertiary centres were registered. The mean age was 68.8 years (SD 5.7; range 60 to 90). At 3-year follow-up (84.2% completed), mesh exposure occurred in 2.8% (95% CI 2.2% to 3.5%), with high rates of anatomic cure (95.3%), subjective success (94.1%), composite surgical success (90.1%), and patient satisfaction (98.2%), respectively. Among women who resumed sexual activity and provided relevant follow-up data, 53.1% reported dyspareunia. In conclusion, among highly selected women with POP who met the updated indications, TVM repair using lightweight mesh and performed by experienced surgeons was associated with low mesh exposure rates and sustained effectiveness at 3 years. These observational registry findings may inform individualized decision-making for this defined patient subgroup.

articles.title: Alterations of fecal microbiome and metabolome in patients with diminished ovarian reserve.
articles.authors: Sun L, Li J, Zhu Y et al.
articles.abstract:
STUDY QUESTION: Are there distinct variations in the gut microbiome and metabolism among infertile women diagnosed with diminished ovarian reserve (DOR), and how might the gut microbiome influence ovarian function?
SUMMARY ANSWER: In DOR patients, Hoylesella abundance correlated with anti-Müllerian hormone (AMH)/antral follicle count (AFC), and stearic acid was identified as a key differential metabolite that was associated with activated PI3K-Akt signaling.
WHAT IS KNOWN ALREADY: Accumulating evidence underscores the presence of a 'gut-ovary axis', highlighting a substantial interplay between the intestinal microbiome and ovarian function. However, the specific microbial and metabolic profiles characterizing infertile individuals with DOR remain largely uncharacterized.
STUDY DESIGN, SIZE, DURATION: This study was a cross-sectional observational study. We enrolled participants receiving frozen embryo transfer at the First Affiliated Hospital of Zhengzhou University between 1 October 2024, and 31 December 2025. Each participant was limited to a single frozen embryo transfer within the study.
PARTICIPANTS/MATERIALS, SETTING, METHODS: A total of 190 participants were included: 91 with DOR and 99 with normal ovarian reserve (NOR). Clinical information and stool specimens were collected from every subject. Sequencing of 16S rRNA and non-targeted metabolomics were implemented to characterize the gut microbiome and metabolome, respectively. Molecular docking analysis and network pharmacology were then implemented to screen for overlapping genetic targets among DOR-associated targets and key metabolite-targeted proteins.
MAIN RESULTS AND THE ROLE OF CHANCE: Relative to NOR controls, the DOR population exhibited significantly lower Gut Microbiota Health Index (P = 2.52 × 10-22) and higher Microbiota Dysbiosis Index (P = 8.31 × 10-10). The genus Hoylesella was significantly depleted in the DOR group (P = 0.018). Spearman analysis demonstrated that Hoylesella proportions were significantly positively correlated with AMH and AFC levels. Metabolomics analysis identified 243 differential metabolites across the study cohorts. Among these, four metabolites were associated with Hoylesella, and stearic acid exhibited high predictive performance (area under the curve = 0.89) for distinguishing DOR. Network pharmacology analysis of stearic acid and DOR identified five core targets: tumor necrosis factor, AKT serine/threonine kinase 1, SRC proto-oncogene, non-receptor…

articles.title: Peers reaching peers: a case study on expanding contraceptive access for female sex workers in Uganda.
articles.authors: Kihumuro RB, Lume I, Ochen E et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Female sex workers (FSWs) face disproportionately high rates of unintended pregnancy and unmet family planning needs. Peer-led interventions offer a promising strategy to expand access to contraceptives for populations such as FSWs that are routinely stigmatized or otherwise left behind by traditional healthcare facilities.
METHODS: We trained 50 peer educators across four divisions of Nansana Municipality in Uganda to deliver contraceptive education and provide free short-acting contraceptives directly to FSWs. Peer educators also facilitated referrals as needed to a stigma-free clinic offering long-term contraceptives, and comprehensive sexual and reproductive health services. Peer educators were trained in destigmatizing sexual and reproductive health service provision for FSWs specifically. Providing these services at a designated clinic minimized structural barriers, such as stock-outs and disrespectful provider attitudes, enabling effective referrals and service uptake.
RESULTS: Over 12 months, 787 FSWs received contraceptive education: 5420 male and 510 female condoms were distributed, 232 FSWs accepted oral contraceptives, and 179 were referred for and received long-acting methods, with 74 receiving injectables and 105 implants or intrauterine devices.
CONCLUSIONS: Peer-led models can expand contraceptive access among FSWs in designated stigma-free facilities with reliable supply chains. To achieve sustainable contraceptive access among FSWs more broadly, this approach should be integrated into government sexual and reproductive health systems.

articles.title: Pre-implementation assessment of upstream domains on the uptake of HPV self-sampling in safety-net settings: a scoping review.
articles.authors: Huppe LG, Okechukwu CA, Nanbigne T et al.
articles.abstract: Human papillomavirus (HPV) screening can be used as an early detector for cervical cancer. The newly US Food and Drug Administration-approved HPV self-sampling tests can be used by safety net practices in the USA to help mitigate the current screening disparities seen in patients. As patient acceptability and capability have already been established, this scoping review synthesizes the barriers and facilitators of implementing HPV self-sampling from the perspective of safety net providers and leadership, and the upstream factors not yet explored in current research. Following PRISMA-ScR guidelines, a literature search was conducted exploring peer-reviewed publications and grey literature to establish the current landscape of HPV self-sampling. Findings were organized using the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research. From the 57 works included, it was found that safety net practices are capable of implementing HPV self-sampling by utilizing current workflows and team members. However, outer setting guidelines and policies heavily influence the implementation process, likely causing a delay in uptake by safety net practices. Recent guideline endorsements and forthcoming insurance coverage address several of these barriers, making post-approval implementation research in safety net settings an urgent priority.

articles.title: Climate change as a modifier of paediatric lung-function trajectories.
articles.journal: European respiratory review : an official journal of the European Respiratory Society
articles.authors: Drummond D, Renz HE, Beri C et al.
articles.abstract: Lung function follows a life-course trajectory, rising through childhood and adolescence to a peak in early adulthood; a low peak is associated with later COPD, cardiovascular morbidity and premature mortality. Childhood and adolescence are therefore the key periods during which adult respiratory reserve is built. Climate change is relevant to paediatric respiratory health not only because it triggers acute symptoms, but because it intensifies, prolongs and reschedules exposures already known to affect the developing lung, including heat, air pollution, wildfire smoke, aeroallergens and indoor damp. In this mini-review, we use lung-function trajectories as the organising framework and examine how climate-sensitive exposures may shift them downwards through three developmental pathways. First, early developmental disruption, including gestational air pollution and ambient temperature, may lower the starting point of the trajectory through fetal growth restriction, preterm birth and possibly direct effects on developing airways. Second, sustained exposure to air pollution, heat and indoor dampness across childhood and adolescence may impair postnatal lung growth and reduce lung-function growth and the peak attained. Third, climate-sensitive triggers increasingly precipitate exacerbations followed by incomplete recovery, particularly in asthma and cystic fibrosis, resulting in exacerbation-related step-down events. Crucially, these trajectories are not fixed; evidence that improving air quality accelerates lung-function growth shows that respiratory reserve can still be protected. We translate this trajectory-centred evidence into practical, climate-aware paediatric care, shifting the focus from short-term symptom prevention to preserving the lung-function reserve children carry into adulthood.

articles.title: MORPHOLOGICAL FEATURES OF THE CERVICAL EPITHELIUM AND STROMA IN CHRONIC RECURRENT CERVICITIS WITH AND WITHOUT SQUAMOUS INTRAEPITHELIAL LESIONS: A COMPARATIVE CROSS-SECTIONAL STUDY.
articles.authors: Khamdamova M, Khalilova M, Askarova Z et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic recurrent cervicitis may cause reactive epithelial and stromal changes that complicate the distinction between inflammation and squamous intraepithelial lesions. Persistent high-risk human papillomavirus (HPV) infection remains the principal etiological factor in cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN); inflammation should therefore be interpreted as an associated tissue background rather than an established independent cause.
OBJECTIVE: To compare cervical epithelial and stromal morphology in chronic recurrent cervicitis with and without squamous intraepithelial lesions and to assess clinical and colposcopic findings associated with histologically confirmed lesions.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This comparative cross-sectional observational study included 154 women examined in 2022-2025: 20 women with conditionally preserved cervical tissue obtained only for clinical indications, 71 patients with chronic recurrent cervicitis without a squamous intraepithelial lesion, and 63 patients with chronic recurrent cervicitis and a histologically confirmed low-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (LSIL) or high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (HSIL). Extended colposcopy, targeted biopsy, hematoxylin and eosin staining, and Van Gieson staining were performed. Unadjusted odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated for the two clinical groups. Holm correction was applied to 12 prespecified binary comparisons.
RESULTS: LSIL/CIN I was identified in 24 (38.1%) patients and HSIL/CIN II-III in 39 (61.9%). Disease duration longer than 5 years was associated with a squamous intraepithelial lesion (OR=3.04; 95% CI 1.47-6.29; p=0.002; Holm-adjusted p=0.028). Acetowhite epithelium was also associated with a lesion (OR=2.79; 95% CI 1.37-5.68; p=0.004; Holm-adjusted p=0.046). Associations with frequent recurrences, mosaic/punctation, and abnormal vessels did not remain statistically significant after multiplicity correction. LSIL and HSIL showed loss of stratification, an increased nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratio, hyperchromasia, anisokaryosis, and more pronounced qualitative stromal remodeling.
CONCLUSION: Squamous intraepithelial lesions in patients with chronic recurrent cervicitis were accompanied by more pronounced epithelial and stromal changes. Disease duration longer than 5 years and acetowhite epithelium remained significant after multiplicity correction. Because of age imbalance, absent HPV data, and lack of multivariable…

articles.title: PREVALENCE AND RISK FACTORS OF PELVIC ORGAN PROLAPSE AMONG WOMEN IN ALMATY: A HOSPITAL-BASED STUDY.
articles.authors: Laktionova M, Barmanasheva Z, Onglas A et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Pelvic organ prolapse (POP) is a common pelvic floor disorder in women and can substantially affect quality of life. Data on the prevalence and associated factors of POP in Kazakhstan remain limited. This study aimed to assess the prevalence and factors associated with clinically confirmed POP among women examined at a medical center in Almaty.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This hospital-based study included 1,500 women aged 28-55 years. POP was assessed by gynecological examination using the POP-Q system. Demographic, obstetric, lifestyle, and clinical factors were evaluated. Crude and age-specific prevalence was calculated, and multivariable logistic regression was used to identify factors independently associated with POP. Internal validation was performed using 1,000 bootstrap resamples.
RESULTS: The prevalence of clinically confirmed POP was 30.7% (460/1,500). Age-specific prevalence was 32.9% at 28-37 years, 31.3% at 38-47 years, and 27.5% at 48-55 years. Cystocele was the predominant anatomical component (81.7%). Higher BMI, birth trauma, instrumental delivery, fetal birth weight ≥3,700 g, chronic cough, constipation, single lifting of >10 kg, and family history were independently associated with POP. The final model showed moderate discrimination (AUC=0.799, 95% CI 0.774-0.824), with an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.793.
CONCLUSION: Clinically confirmed POP was present in 30.7% of women in this hospital-based cohort. Several obstetric, lifestyle, and clinical factors were independently associated with POP. These findings provide initial data for planning future population-based studies of POP in Kazakhstan.

articles.title: CLINICAL AND CULTURAL PERSPECTIVES ON POLYCYSTIC OVARY SYNDROME IN WOMEN BASED ON SYMPTOM CLUSTERING AND DIAGNOSTIC TRENDS.
articles.authors: Oufi H, Kutaif R, Alabd R et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is a heterogeneous endocrine disorder associated with reproductive, metabolic, and psychosocial complications. In Iraq, limited data are available on symptom patterns, diagnostic experiences, and treatment behaviors, particularly from data-driven analyses of subgroup heterogeneity.
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to explore symptom profiles, diagnostic pathways, and treatment behaviors among a convenience sample of Iraqi women reporting PCOS-related features, and to identify phenotype-like subgroups using unsupervised machine learning.
METHODS: A cross-sectional survey was conducted among 402 Iraqi women recruited through clinics, campuses, and social media platforms. Data were collected on demographic characteristics, menstrual irregularity, hirsutism, acne, body weight, fertility-related concerns, diagnosis history, and treatment practices. Because recruitment relied on convenience sampling, the sample was predominantly young, unmarried, and likely urban/suburban, educated, and internet-connected. Principal component analysis (PCA) was used for dimensionality reduction, followed by K-means clustering to identify phenotype-like subgroup patterns.
RESULTS: Among this convenience sample, 59.9% of participants reported a prior laboratory-supported diagnosis of PCOS, 30.2% reported a clinical diagnosis, and 9.7% reported symptoms without a prior diagnosis. Complementary or traditional medicine use was common in this sample (96.0%), and 93.3% expressed concern regarding future fertility. Symptom burden was observed across BMI categories. Unsupervised clustering identified three phenotype-like subgroups: a mild/lean profile, an acne-predominant/moderate profile, and a higher-weight profile with more marked hirsutism.
CONCLUSION: This study provides an exploratory view of PCOS-related symptom patterns, diagnostic pathways, and treatment behaviors among a predominantly young convenience sample of Iraqi women. Given the sampling strategy and reliance on self-reported information, the findings should be interpreted cautiously as hypothesis-generating rather than nationally representative of Iraqi women. Nevertheless, the observed heterogeneity and fertility-related concerns may help inform culturally sensitive counseling and future larger, more representative studies in Iraq.

articles.title: MATERNAL AND CORD-BLOOD HOMOCYSTEINE AND NEONATAL S100B IN PRETERM BIRTH: ASSOCIATIONS WITH IN-HOSPITAL NEONATAL OUTCOMES IN A PROSPECTIVE COHORT.
articles.authors: Adilbekova I, Bozhbanbayeva N, Issenova S et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: Preterm birth is associated with substantial neonatal morbidity, while relationships between maternal and neonatal biochemical characteristics and neonatal outcomes remain incompletely understood. This study investigated mother-newborn homocysteine relationships and associations of homocysteine and neonatal S100B with in-hospital neonatal outcomes.
METHODS: This prospective multicenter cohort included 280 mother-newborn pairs with singleton preterm births at 22+0-36+6 weeks. Maternal and umbilical cord blood homocysteine and neonatal S100B were assessed. A selected composite of IVH, invasive mechanical ventilation from birth, congenital or neonatal pneumonia, EOS, or LOS was analyzed post hoc. Separate adjusted logistic models evaluated maternal homocysteine, cord-blood homocysteine, and S100B, each with gestational age and birth weight; a combined five-variable model was retained as a sensitivity analysis.
RESULTS: The selected composite occurred in 185/280 infants (66.1%). Maternal and umbilical cord blood homocysteine concentrations were strongly correlated (ρ=0.663; p<0.001). In separate adjusted models, maternal homocysteine (aOR 1.057, 95% CI 0.989-1.130; p=0.100), cord-blood homocysteine (aOR 1.021, 95% CI 0.949-1.099; p=0.574), and neonatal S100B (aOR 0.981 per 10-ng/L increase, 95% CI 0.947-1.016; p=0.278) were not independently associated with the composite. Gestational age and birth weight were inversely associated with the composite in each model. The combined model and sensitivity analyses yielded consistent biomarker findings.
CONCLUSIONS: Maternal and umbilical cord blood homocysteine concentrations were strongly correlated, supporting a close maternal-fetal metabolic relationship; however, maternal homocysteine, cord-blood homocysteine, and neonatal S100B were not independently associated with the selected composite of in-hospital neonatal morbidity after adjustment for gestational age and birth weight.

articles.title: TWIST family in cervical cancer biology: From molecular mechanisms to clinical implications.
articles.authors: Sayed U, Kubaev A, Polatova D et al.
articles.abstract: Despite ongoing clinical efforts, cervical cancer remains one of the most common gynecologic tumors, largely due to its metastatic potential and resistance to chemotherapy. The transcriptional regulator TWIST has been implicated in these features, in part through the induction of epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT). The expression of TWIST is delicately regulated by several exogenous factors, including hypoxia-driven HIF-1α signaling and TGF-β pathways, as well as endogenous oncogenic cascades such as Wnt/β-catenin, NF-κB, PI3K/Akt, Hedgehog, Notch, and IL-6/JAK2/STAT3. Moreover, the E6 and E7 proteins from high-risk human papillomavirus strains promote TWIST upregulation, facilitating cellular plasticity and evasion of senescence. Post-transcriptional and epigenetic regulation is orchestrated by complex networks of non-coding RNAs and key transcription factors such as Mist1, FOXC1, and LMX-1A. Importantly, hypermethylation of the TWIST1 promoter has been proposed as a candidate biomarker for cervical intraepithelial neoplasia. TWIST has been reported to promote tumor-associated phenotypes through E-cadherin downregulation, induction of matrix metalloproteinases, and maintenance of stem cell-like properties. TWIST has been associated with chemotherapy and radiotherapy resistance, potentially through mechanisms involving DNA-damage responses and MDR1/P-glycoprotein-mediated drug efflux. The tumor microenvironment affects its expression and activity, including hypoxia, cancer-associated fibroblasts, inflammatory cytokines, tumor-associated macrophages, and extracellular vesicles. In a clinical context, high levels of TWIST are linked to poor outcomes in cervical cancer. Growing evidence links it to immune evasion through regulation of PD-L1, immunosuppressive cytokine signaling, macrophage polarization, T-cell exclusion, and immune resistance associated with cancer stem cells, underscoring its importance for translation in the current era of immune checkpoint blockade.

articles.title: Bakuchiol mitigates neuronal dysfunction in estrogen deficient chronic unpredictable mild stressed rats: insights from in vivo and in-silico studies.
articles.authors: Bag S, Bansal S, Chaudhary R et al.
articles.abstract: Estrogen deficiency in post-menopausal women leads to the development of neurodegenerative disorders. Phytoestrogens are plant-derived compounds that represent novel and safer alternatives to hormone replacement therapy for the treatment of neurological disorders in postmenopausal complications. Bakuchiol is a phytoestrogen exhibiting selective estrogen like effects. The present study aimed to investigate the neuroprotective and antidepressant potential of bakuchiol in ovariectomized rats subjected to chronic unpredictable mild stress (CUMS) exposure. Adult Female Wistar rats were bilaterally ovariectomized (OVX) and subjected to CUMS over a period of four weeks in order to mimic the development of depression and cognitive deficits in menopause. At the end of the study, basic physiological and neurobehavioral parameters, biochemical estimation, and serum corticosterone levels were evaluated. Levels of brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF), Acetylcholinesterase were evaluated and histopathological changes were also studied. In silico Molecular docking studies carried out against proteins TrkB receptor (PDB ID: 4AT5) and Human Acetylcholinesterase (PDB ID: 4EY7). Molecular dynamics studies carried out to study ligand-protein interaction stability. Treatment with bakuchiol and 17-β estradiol (E2) significantly restores the pathological changes towards normal levels. However, the protective effect of bakuchiol was completely abolished when administered in the presence of Fulvestrant in OVX + CUMS groups of rats. The in-silico results further corroborate the observed in vitro results. Bakuchiol showed binding affinities of -6.052 kcal/mol and -5.493 kcal/mol toward BDNF-TrkB and AChE, respectively showing its neurotrophic and antidepressant effects. Molecular dynamics studies also supported these results via showing stable and energetically favoured interactions of Bakuchiol with BDNF-TrkB and acetylcholinesterase. Our current study shows that Bakuchiol at doses of 20 & 40 mg/kg dose dependently possess the potential to alleviate the neurological disorder in estrogen deficient chronic stress conditions.

articles.title: Nigerian grown Hyptis verticillata leaf extract mitigates endocrine and metabolic disruptions in lipid-enriched diet and letrozole-induced polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome in wistar rats.
articles.authors: Ukam CI, Markus DE, Okonkwo CO et al.
articles.abstract: Polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS) is a hormonal disorder that manifests during the female reproductive lifespan. Hyptis verticillata previously demonstrated glucose-modulating effects and ameliorated metabolic aberrations associated with diabetes mellitus. The present study evaluated its potential to mitigate the metabolic and endocrine compromises associated with PMOS. Experimental PMOS induction was achieved using an oral regimen of 1 mg/kg body weight (b.w.) letrozole combined with a lipid enriched diet for 21 days. Thirty female rats were divided into five groups: a healthy control and four PMOS-induced groups that were orally administered either 10 mL/kg b.w of distilled water, 500 mg/kg b.w of metformin, or H. verticillata leaf extract (250 mg/kg and 500 mg/kg). Treatment lasted 28 days. From results, both doses of H. verticillata significantly (p < 0.05) restored normoglycaemia, improved insulin sensitivity, normalized body weight, and reversed hyperandrogenism. Furthermore, a significant elevation in follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) following extract treatment was accompanied by a marked decline in luteinizing hormone (LH) compared to the untreated PMOS group. Additionally, H. verticillata significantly reversed dyslipidaemia and boosted ovarian concentrations of antioxidant enzymes (SOD, CAT, and GPx) while decreasing malondialdehyde levels, performing similarly to metformin. Histopathological analysis revealed improved ovarian morphology with a decline in cystic follicles. It can be inferred from these findings that the beneficial potential of H. verticillata against PMOS-induced endocrine and metabolic compromise are elicited through a multi-mechanistic action that modulates glucose and hormone homeostasis, boosts antioxidant capacity, and restores ovarian structure, making it a promising alternative for managing PMOS.

articles.title: HPV vaccination uptake among adolescent girls in Nigeria: A multi-state pilot trial using linked mother-daughter data.
articles.authors: Iwelunmor J, Wapmuk AE, Okeke N et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Nigeria's human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination rollout creates opportunities to strengthen adolescent vaccination through participatory, family-engaged approaches. We examined HPV vaccination uptake and associated characteristics among adolescent girls in a multi-state pilot using linked mother-daughter data.
METHODS: We analyzed pilot data from 331 vaccine-naïve girls aged 9-14 years, 325 mothers/guardians, and 326 linked mother-daughter records across seven Nigerian states. The participatory approach combined community engagement, maternal HPV DNA self-sampling, and school- and community-linked access to routine HPV vaccination. The primary outcome was logbook-verified vaccination uptake. Exploratory associations were assessed using log-binomial generalized estimating equations to estimate adjusted risk ratios (aRRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs).
RESULTS: Of 331 girls, 314 (94.9%) received HPV vaccination, with complete outcome ascertainment. No vaccine-related serious adverse events were recorded. In exploratory adjusted analyses, uptake was higher among Igbo girls (aRR 1.13, 95% CI 1.06-1.22) and girls of other ethnicities (aRR 1.10, 95% CI 1.01-1.19) than among Yoruba girls. Maternal income was positively associated with uptake (aRR per income category 1.02, 95% CI 1.01-1.03). Associations involving maternal screening participation require caution because few mothers did not participate in screening.
CONCLUSIONS: HPV vaccination uptake was high among girls participating in this pilot. The exploratory findings suggest areas for further investigation but cannot establish intervention effectiveness or causal relationships. Larger studies should evaluate implementation processes, comparative effectiveness, and equity.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT06728085.

articles.title: Brain-derived neurotrophic factor in gynecological cancers and endometriosis: A candidate biomarker for diagnosis and disease monitoring.
articles.journal: Clinica chimica acta; international journal of clinical chemistry
articles.authors: Wu J, Liu M, Su J et al.
articles.abstract: Brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF), a member of the neurotrophin family, has functions beyond neuronal survival and synaptic plasticity, including the regulation of cellular proliferation, migration, angiogenesis, inflammation, and nociceptive signaling.
