Growing evidence suggests that abnormal BDNF expression and dysregulated BDNF/TrkB signaling may contribute to the development and progression of gynecological malignancies, including ovarian, cervical, and endometrial cancers, as well as endometriosis. In cancer, BDNF has been associated with epithelial-mesenchymal transition, anoikis resistance, metastatic spread, and therapeutic resistance through PI3K/Akt, MAPK/ERK, and PLCγ signaling. In endometriosis, increased circulating and tissue BDNF has been associated with neuroangiogenesis, pelvic pain, lesion severity, and inflammatory remodeling. Emerging clinical and translational evidence suggests that BDNF may have potential as a minimally invasive biomarker, mainly in endometriosis, whereas clinical data in gynecological cancers come largely from tissue expression studies; however, associations between circulating BDNF levels and disease presence, severity, or treatment response remain heterogeneous across studies. The review is based on searches of PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science from database inception to June 2025. This review critically synthesizes the molecular mechanisms underlying BDNF dysregulation and its interactions with hormonal, immune, and epigenetic pathways, while evaluating its potential clinical utility for diagnosis and disease monitoring. Particular emphasis is placed on methodological limitations, contradictory findings, and factors that may contribute to variability among studies. Key knowledge gaps and future research priorities, including standardized measurement approaches, prospective investigations, and independent cohort validation, are also discussed. Overall, current evidence supports further investigation of BDNF as a candidate biomarker, but its diagnostic and disease-monitoring utility has not been established and requires prospective clinical validation.

articles.title: Tranexamic Acid Prophylaxis During Cesarean Delivery Among Patients with and Without Hypertension.
articles.journal: American journal of obstetrics & gynecology MFM
articles.authors: Ayyash MK, Lewkowitz AK, Weiner SJ et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with chronic and pregnancy-related hypertension are at increased risk of postpartum hemorrhage and have fewer uterotonic options because methylergonovine is generally contraindicated. Hypertensive disorders are also characterized by endothelial dysfunction and altered coagulation-fibrinolytic pathways, providing biologic plausibility that tranexamic acid (TXA) may have differential effects in this population.
OBJECTIVE: The objective of this study was to examine whether the effect of prophylactic TXA during cesarean delivery (CD) on peripartum bleeding-related outcomes differed based on hypertensive status.
STUDY DESIGN: This is a non-prespecified secondary analysis of a multicenter, placebo-controlled trial of patients undergoing CD who were randomized to 1gram of TXA or placebo. For this analysis, all participants were included and divided into subgroups based on the presence of chronic and pregnancy-related hypertension (HTN) prior to delivery. The primary outcome was a composite of blood transfusion or maternal death before hospital discharge or seven days postpartum, whichever occurred first. Secondary outcomes included several measures of peri-partum bleeding related outcomes. Relative risks (RR) and 95% confidence intervals (CI) were calculated for categorical and mean differences for continuous outcomes. P values for interaction with HTN were calculated.
RESULTS: Of the 10,995 participants randomized in the parent trial, 2707 (24.6%) had HTN (7.1% chronic hypertension and 17.5% pregnancy related). The effect of TXA on the primary outcome did not differ by HTN status at randomization (HTN: TXA 4.9% vs placebo 6.0%; RR 0.84 (95% CI 0.62-1.16); no HTN: TXA 3.2% vs placebo 3.7%; RR 0.91 (0.73-1.14); p for interaction 0.64). For all secondary outcomes, the interaction p similarly was non-significant (all p >0.05).
CONCLUSION: The effect of prophylactic TXA at CD on blood transfusion or maternal death within one week postpartum, or other peripartum bleeding-related outcomes, did not differ by the presence of HTN.

articles.title: First- and second-generation antipsychotic use in pregnancy and risks of pregnancy and birth outcomes.
articles.journal: American journal of obstetrics & gynecology MFM
articles.authors: Blæhr EE, Semark BD, Petersen LV et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Antipsychotic use in pregnancy has increased, but evidence on potential maternal and neonatal complications remains limited.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the associations between continued first-generation antipsychotic (FG) or second-generation antipsychotic (SG) use during pregnancy and the risks of pregnancy complications and adverse birth outcomes.
STUDY DESIGN: We conducted a population-based cohort study including all liveborn singletons born to women in Denmark (2004-2022) who filled ≥1 antipsychotic prescription from one year to 30 days before conception. Women who continued FGs or SGs through 20 gestational weeks (for pregnancy complications) or throughout pregnancy (for birth outcomes) were classified as continuers. SGs were further categorized into high metabolic risk (olanzapine, quetiapine, clozapine) or low metabolic risk (risperidone, aripiprazole, ziprasidone). Outcomes included gestational diabetes, gestational hypertension, and adverse birth outcomes identified from medical records. Adjusted odds ratios (ORs) were estimated using generalized estimating equations, accounting for maternal characteristics and psychiatric history.
RESULTS: Among 7,417 pregnancies, 453 (6.1%) were exposed to FGs, 2,219 (29.9%) to SGs, and 4,745 discontinued treatment. Compared with their respective discontinuers, continuing SGs was associated with higher odds of gestational diabetes (OR = 1.19, 95% CI 0.96-1.48) and gestational hypertension (OR = 1.20, 95% CI 0.97-1.48), whereas no increased risk was observed for FGs (OR = 0.92, 95% CI 0.57-1.48 and OR = 1.01, 95% CI 0.60-1.71, respectively). Risks were similar for high- and low-metabolic risk SGs for gestational diabetes, whereas the increased risk of gestational hypertension was confined to high-metabolic risk SGs. Preterm birth was less common among SG continuers (OR = 0.77, 95% CI 0.64-0.93), but not among FG continuers (OR = 1.13, 95% CI 0.80-1.60). Neonatal intensive care unit admission was more frequent among FG continuers (OR = 1.28, 95% CI 1.01-1.62), but not among SG continuers (OR = 0.87, 95% CI 0.73-1.03).
CONCLUSIONS: Continuation of FGs during pregnancy was not associated with increased maternal risk but was associated with higher rates of neonatal intensive care admission, compared with discontinuation. Continuation of SGs was associated with increased maternal metabolic risk and a lower risk of preterm birth.

articles.title: Ophthalmic Artery versus Uterine Artery Doppler in the prediction of preterm pre-eclampsia at 11-13 weeks' gestation.
articles.journal: American journal of obstetrics & gynecology MFM
articles.authors: Kusuma RA, Al-Fattah AN, Puteri UE et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Preterm pre-eclampsia (PE) is a leading cause of maternal and perinatal morbidity and mortality. First-trimester screening using maternal factors (MF), mean arterial pressure (MAP), uterine artery pulsatility index (UtPI), and placental growth factor (PlGF) allows early risk stratification and effective prevention with aspirin. However, UtPI measurement is technically demanding and operator dependent. Maternal ophthalmic artery Doppler, expressed as the ophthalmic artery peak ratio (Oph-PR), reflects early maternal cardiovascular changes and may serve as an alternative or complementary marker for PE prediction.
OBJECTIVE: To compare the predictive performance of adding maternal Oph-PR versus uterine UtPI to the first-trimester prediction model for preterm PE that uses MF, MAP, and, PlGF.
STUDY DESIGN: This was a prospective observational study involving women attending first-trimester screening at 11+2 to 14+2 weeks of gestation. Maternal factors, measurement of MAP, serum PlGF collection, ultrasound examination for UtPI and Oph-PR measurement, were performed during the visit. Receiver-operating characteristics (ROC) curve analysis was used to determine the area under the curve (AUC), detection rates (DR), and positive screening cut-off from the Bayesian Accelerated Failure Time (AFT) survival models in predicting the occurrence of preterm PE (<37 weeks of gestation). De Long's test was performed to compare the superiority of the AUCs among models.
RESULTS: Of 946 eligible participants, 71 (7.49%) were affected by PE, and 21 (2.2%) had preterm PE. The predictive performance of the UtPI-based model (MF + MAP + UtPI and MF + MAP + UtPI + PlGF) was similar to that of the Oph-PR-based models (MF + MAP + Oph-PR and MF + MAP + Oph-PR + PlGF) in the prediction of preterm PE (AUC 0.805 and 0.837 vs 0.789 and 0.830; p=0.584 and 0.687, respectively). The combination of MF, MAP, UtPI, Oph-PR, and PlGF in predicting preterm PE demonstrated the highest AUC compared to the other prediction models (AUC 0.919, 95% CI 0.875-0.963).
CONCLUSION: UtPI and Oph-PR are comparable for first-trimester prediction of preterm PE. Combining both Doppler indices in a prediction algorithm may improve predictive performance for preterm PE.

articles.title: Outcomes in Stage II twin-twin transfusion syndrome with donor intermittent umbilical artery Doppler abnormalities.
articles.journal: American journal of obstetrics & gynecology MFM
articles.authors: Sun RC, Chon AH, Korst LM et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Twin-twin transfusion syndrome (TTTS) is a rare condition of monochorionic diamniotic twin pregnancies. The Quintero staging system was established to categorize the severity of this disease. Published outcomes for selective laser photocoagulation of communicating vessels (SLPCV) demonstrate a significant difference in dual survival outcomes among the different stages of TTTS. Intermittent donor umbilical artery (UA) absent or reversed end diastolic flow (AREDF) is classified as stage I (donor bladder visible) or II (donor bladder not visible), whereas persistent donor twin UA-AREDF is classified as stage III. This distinction between intermittent and persistent UA-AREDF appears to have been variably interpreted since the original publication.
OBJECTIVE: We evaluated laser surgery outcomes in 3 groups: stage II patients with intermittent UA-AREDF (Stage -II intermittent) vs stage II patients with a normal UA waveform (Stage II-Normal), using stage III patients with persistent donor twin UA-AREDF (Stage-III) for comparison.
STUDY DESIGN: Three groups of monochorionic diamniotic twins with TTTS treated with laser surgery (2006-2023) were analyzed: (1) Stage-II Normal; (2) Stage-II Intermittent; and (3) Stage-III (Stage III Donor + Stage-III Donor/Recipient). The groups were compared in bivariate analysis and in a multiple logistic regression model for the primary outcome of donor twin intrauterine fetal demise (IUFD).
RESULTS: For Stage-II Normal (n=126), Stage-II Intermittent (n=62), and Stage-III (n=212), respective rates of donor IUFD were 7.1% vs 8.1% vs 29.2% (P<.0001), and dual survivorship was 84.1% vs 82.3% vs 62.7% (P<.0001). Multiple covariates were eligible for inclusion in the logistic regression model, including gestational age at the procedure, the preoperative estimated fetal weight of the donor, and the presence of arterioarterial anastomoses (AA). Upon adjustment in a multiple logistic regression model, the Stage-II Intermittent group did not have an increased risk of donor IUFD vs Stage-II Normal (aOR 0.51, 95% CI 0.15-1.79).
CONCLUSION: TTTS stage II patients with intermittent UA-AREDF did not show increased risk of donor IUFD compared with stage II patients with normal UA Doppler findings. These results support the traditional Quintero staging classification, which classifies only persistent UA-AREDF as stage III TTTS.

articles.title: Management of Retained Products of Conception (RPOC) with Hysteroscopic Morcellator: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis of Efficacy, Safety, and Procedural Outcomes.
articles.authors: Damiani GR, Turoli D, Muzzupapa G et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the efficacy, safety, and procedural outcomes of hysteroscopic morcellation (HM) for the treatment of retained products of conception (RPOC).
DATA SOURCES: A systematic literature search of PubMed and The Cochrane Library was performed from inception to January 2026, combining Medical Subject Headings and free-text terms including "Retained Products of Conception," "RPOC," "Hysteroscopy," "Hysteroscopic Morcellation," and "Intrauterine Tissue Removal System." No restrictions on publication date were applied; the search was limited to peer-reviewed articles published in English. The protocol was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251247904).
METHODS OF STUDY SELECTION: Randomized controlled trials and prospective or retrospective observational studies evaluating HM for RPOC and reporting at least one outcome of interest (complete RPOC removal, additional procedures, de novo intrauterine adhesions, perioperative complications, or procedural outcomes) were eligible. Case reports, editorials, and conference abstracts were excluded. Two reviewers independently screened records and assessed full texts; four studies met the inclusion criteria (two randomized controlled trials, one prospective study, and one retrospective study).
TABULATION, INTEGRATION, AND RESULTS: Data were independently extracted by two investigators using a standardized form and verified by a third. Risk of bias was assessed independently by two reviewers. Pooled proportions and means with 95% CIs were calculated using random-effects models, and heterogeneity was assessed with the I² statistic. The pooled complete RPOC removal rate was 95.0% (95% CI 92.2-97.7%; I²=0%). The pooled rate of additional procedures was 6.6% (95% CI 2.5-10.6%; I²=35.4%) and of de novo intrauterine adhesions 5.2% (95% CI 0.4-10.0%; I²=48.7%). Intraoperative and postoperative complication rates were 7.5% (95% CI 3.4-11.6%; I²=31.3%) and 3.4% (95% CI 1.1-5.6%; I²=0%), respectively. The pooled mean procedural time was 11.18 minutes (95% CI 8.61-13.74; I²=98.8%).
CONCLUSION: Hysteroscopic morcellation is associated with high rates of complete RPOC removal and low rates of complications and intrauterine adhesions. However, current evidence is insufficient to establish its superiority over conventional surgical approaches, and adequately powered comparative studies are needed.

articles.title: Qualitative Interviews with PAG Fellowship Directors Support the Need to Develop a Best Practice Standard for Performing Trauma-Sensitive Pelvic Exams.
articles.journal: Journal of pediatric and adolescent gynecology
articles.authors: Geary-Souza MK, MacFife B, Boskey ER et al.
articles.abstract:
STUDY OBJECTIVE: Childhood sexual abuse (CSA) affects an estimated 1:4 girls and 1:6 boys. Sexual and early trauma survivors frequently carry long-term psychological and physiological effects that influence healthcare engagement, including heightened distress and avoidance of gynecological care. Pediatric and adolescent gynecology (PAG) examinations can be especially triggering, yet few evidence-based trauma-sensitive care (TSC) standards exist. This study explored how PAG gynecologists understand and incorporate TSC into adolescent pelvic examinations and identified gaps that shape the adolescent's experience and the gynecologist's clinical practice.
METHODS: Six of fourteen U.S. pediatric and adolescent gynecology fellowship directors participated in semi-structured interviews between August and November 2023. Interviews were recorded, transcribed, and analyzed using open coding and inductive content analysis.
RESULTS: Four themes emerged: (1) heterogeneity of trauma-sensitive practices and trauma knowledge, including variation in trauma screening and communication; (2) factors influencing trauma-sensitive PAG pelvic exam practice, e.g. limited TSC training, systemic barriers, provider discomfort, and the importance of collaborative care teams; (3) grappling with system-induced trauma, including medical trauma related to invasive procedures, inadequate communication, surgical or obstetric experiences, and mandated reporting; and (4) the intersection of cultural humility and TSC in PAG, with participants demonstrating greater comfort with cultural humility frameworks than with TSC-specific guidance. Across themes, PAG fellowship directors described uncertainty about how to conduct trauma-sensitive pelvic exams.
CONCLUSIONS: Findings highlight the need for consistent, evidence-informed practice standards and system-level support to integrate TSC into PAG. Developing trauma-sensitive pelvic exam guidelines could reduce re-traumatization, improve engagement, and strengthen patient-clinician trust.

articles.title: Circulating cell-free DNA and plasma nuclease activity in human aging.
articles.authors: Ershova E, Umriukhin P, Chudakova J et al.
articles.abstract: Circulating cell-free DNA (cfDNA) is an emerging biomarker of aging, but age-related changes in its abundance, oxidation, and plasma nuclease activity have rarely been examined together. We measured plasma cfDNA concentration and nuclease activity in 418 community-dwelling participants aged 7-95 years and quantified 8-oxo-7,8-dihydro-2'-deoxyguanosine (8-oxodG) in cfDNA from 333 participants. cfDNA concentration increased and nuclease activity decreased across ages 7-80 years, whereas participants aged 81-95 years showed lower cfDNA concentration and higher nuclease activity than the 61-80-year group. The cfDNA-to-nuclease activity ratio peaked at 61-80 years and declined thereafter. cfDNA 8-oxodG content increased with age and was highest in the oldest group. The estimated plasma concentration of DNA-bound 8-oxodG rose sharply up to approximately 45 years and then plateaued. An exploratory composite index integrating cfDNA concentration, oxidation, and nuclease activity increased up to approximately 45 years and subsequently stabilized. These cross-sectional findings identify coordinated age-related changes in cfDNA burden, oxidation, and extracellular nuclease activity and support further mechanistic studies of oxidized cfDNA turnover in human aging.

articles.title: Reproductive factors in women with familial hypercholesterolaemia.
articles.authors: Mulder JWCM, van Oortmerssen JAE, Klevmoen M et al.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Hypercholesterolaemia has been associated with earlier menarche and menopause; however, these observations may reflect reverse causation or confounding. Familial Hypercholesterolaemia (FH) provides a model to investigate these associations. This study compared reproductive characteristics and pregnancy outcomes in women with FH vs. women without FH.
METHODS AND RESULTS: Between November 2023 and April 2025, women with FH aged ≥40 years were recruited from two university hospital outpatient clinics in the Netherlands and Norway. Women without FH were selected from the Rotterdam Study and Norwegian population-based cohorts. FH cases were matched 1:2 to women without FH on age, smoking status, body mass index, and ethnicity using nearest-neighbour matching. Information on reproductive factors and pregnancy outcomes were obtained via an online survey. 484 women with FH and 968 matched women without FH (median age 55 years [IQR 48-62]; 93% North-Western European) were included. Cardiovascular disease prevalence was higher in women with FH (22% vs. 4%; P < 0.001). Most women with FH (95%) used lipid-lowering therapy, LDL cholesterol levels were lower compared to controls (2.5 vs. 3.5 mmol/L; P < 0.001). Women with FH more often had been pregnant (91% vs. 84%; P < 0.001). Prevalence of gestational diabetes (4% vs. 4%; P = 0.70) and hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (16% vs. 13%; P = 0.10) was similar; however, preeclampsia was more frequent in FH (11% vs. 7%; P = 0.030). Age at menarche (13.2 vs. 13.1 years; P = 0.43), age at menopause (50 years; P = 0.92), and reproductive lifespan (36 years; P = 0.98) were similar between groups.
CONCLUSION: Reproductive lifespan is comparable between women with and without FH, but FH was associated with a higher prevalence of preeclampsia, highlighting the importance of targeted pregnancy monitoring and prevention.

articles.title: Perinatal multidisciplinary management for neonates with prenatally-diagnosed congenital complete heart block undergoing early epicardial pacemaker implantation: a retrospective single-center case series.
articles.journal: The journal of maternal-fetal & neonatal medicine : the official journal of the European Association of Perinatal Medicine, the Federation of Asia and Oceania Perinatal Societies, the International Society of Perinatal Obstetricians
articles.authors: Cang H, Jia G, Zhang D et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To report our single-center multidisciplinary perinatal experience for neonates with prenatally diagnosed isolated congenital complete heart block (CCHB) requiring early epicardial pacemaker implantation.
METHODS: This retrospective case series included four consecutive neonates with prenatally diagnosed isolated CCHB (2016-2020). A multidisciplinary team coordinated perinatal planning. Maternal data, fetal echocardiography, delivery-room resuscitation, vasoactive support, and short-term neonatal outcomes were analyzed descriptively.
RESULTS: Four neonates (gestation 35 + 6-37 + 6 weeks; birth weight 2270-2500 g) were delivered by cesarean section. Umbilical vein catheterization was achieved rapidly in all. All neonates had a heart rate <50 bpm at birth and received immediate vasoactive resuscitation. All neonates underwent successful epicardial permanent pacemaker implantation within 10 days after birth with improved cardiac function and were discharged home. One infant was readmitted 8 days after discharge due to pocket infection and ultimately died on postnatal day 46.
CONCLUSIONS: Multidisciplinary coordination, early umbilical-vein access, and individualized vasoactive support are critical for managing these high-risk neonates. Our findings provide practical guidance but require validation in larger cohorts.

articles.title: Adenomyosis in Congenital Müllerian Anomalies: Pathogenetic Insights From a Systematic Review.
articles.journal: BJOG : an international journal of obstetrics and gynaecology
articles.authors: Saponara S, Angioni S, Picci F et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Adenomyosis is a prevalent gynaecological disorder whose pathogenesis remains incompletely understood. Congenital Müllerian anomalies provide an informative in vivo model, since obstructive and non-obstructive variants impose spatially defined alterations of intrauterine pressure, myometrial architecture, and contractility.
OBJECTIVES: To characterise adenomyosis localisation across Müllerian anomaly subtypes, assess concomitant endometriosis prevalence, and examine their topographic concordance with sites of uterine obstruction.
SEARCH STRATEGY: PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase and Scopus were searched from inception to October 2025 using MeSH/Emtree and free-text terms for adenomyosis and congenital Müllerian anomalies, without date restrictions.
SELECTION CRITERIA: Original case reports, case series, and observational studies in English explicitly describing the diagnostic modalities used for both conditions.
DATA COLLECTION AND ANALYSIS: Two reviewers independently screened and extracted data; methodological quality was assessed with the Joanna Briggs Institute tools. Data were synthesised descriptively by malformation subtype, with case-by-case laterality analysis where individual patient-level data were available.
MAIN RESULTS: Forty-two studies (135 patients) were included. Unicornuate uterus predominated (102/135, 75.6%). Among patients with directly reported localisation and a non-communicating functional rudimentary horn, adenomyosis involved the rudimentary horn in 10/12 cases (83.3%). In Robert's uterus, adenomyosis was ipsilateral to the blind hemicavity in 3/3 evaluable cases (100%). In Mayer-Rokitansky-Küster-Hauser (MRKH) syndrome, adenomyosis occurred in remnants lacking functional endometrium in 10/15 patients (66.7%). Concomitant endometriosis (43/134 evaluable patients, 32.1%) was most frequent in obstructive anomalies (Herlyn-Werner-Wunderlich syndrome (HWW) 3/5, 60.0%; Robert's uterus 2/4, 50.0%) and least frequent in septate uterus (0/2, 0%) and MRKH (2/15, 13.3%), localising ipsilateral to the obstruction in 9/10 (90.0%) reported obstructive cases.
CONCLUSIONS: Adenomyosis preferentially involved structurally abnormal or obstructed uterine compartments. The endometriosis gradient was compatible with impaired menstrual efflux as a shared mechanical determinant. These findings derive from a low-quality evidence base and should therefore be regarded as hypothesis-generating. Prospective confirmation is required, although these…

articles.title: Prenatal low-dose glyphosate exposure impairs ovarian development in offspring rats via disruption of maternal tryptophan metabolism.
articles.authors: Li S, Xie Y, Liu J et al.
articles.abstract: Glyphosate, the world's most widely used herbicide, is ubiquitous in the environment and poses potential reproductive health risks. However, the effects of environmentally relevant low-dose exposure during pregnancy on offspring ovarian development remain poorly understood, particularly regarding underlying metabolic mechanisms. This study aimed to investigate whether low-dose maternal glyphosate exposure disrupts ovarian development in offspring and to explore the role of maternal tryptophan metabolism in this process. Prenatal exposure to glyphosate (0.5 μg/kg/day) induced persistent ovarian impairment in offspring, characterized by disrupted oocyte meiosis and reduced follicular reserves. In fetal ovaries, glyphosate exposure delayed meiotic progression, while adult offspring exhibited decreased primordial and total follicle counts, along with elevated oxidative stress and early apoptosis in oocytes. Metabolomic analysis revealed that glyphosate exposure downregulated the tryptophan-kynurenine pathway in maternal plasma and fetal ovaries, and reduced ovarian levels of nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD), a downstream metabolite of tryptophan. Maternal tryptophan supplementation restored ovarian NAD concentrations, upregulated meiotic gene expression, and normalized oocyte meiotic progression in glyphosate-exposed offspring. Low-dose glyphosate exposure during pregnancy impairs offspring ovarian development via disruption of maternal tryptophan metabolism and subsequent meiotic dysregulation. Tryptophan supplementation alleviates these effects, highlighting a potential intervention strategy.

articles.title: Lymphovascular space invasion in stage I endometrial cancer: does quantity matter?
articles.journal: International journal of gynecological cancer : official journal of the International Gynecological Cancer Society
articles.authors: Palmieri E, Tarantino V, Giudici A et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the association between the extent of lymphovascular space invasion and recurrence-free survival and overall survival in patients with International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics stage I endometrial cancer, and to explore whether the number of involved vessels identifies a prognostic threshold.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed patients with International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics 2009 stage I endometrial cancer who underwent complete surgical staging, including sentinel lymph node biopsy (2015-2021). All lymphovascular space invasion-positive cases underwent pathology review. Lymphovascular involvement was categorized as absent, focal (<5 vessels), or substantial (≥5 vessels) and was also analyzed by exact vessel count (0 to ≥5).
RESULTS: Among 987 patients, 885 (89.7%) had no lymphovascular space invasion, 71 (7.2%) had focal lymphovascular space invasion, and 31 (3.1%) had substantial lymphovascular space invasion. On univariate analysis, both focal and substantial involvement were associated with shorter recurrence-free survival than no lymphovascular space invasion (log-rank p=.001 and p<.001), with no difference between focal and substantial lymphovascular space invasion (p=.37). On multivariate analysis, substantial involvement remained independently associated with an increased risk of recurrence within 5 years following surgery (hazard ratio 3.07, 95% confidence interval 1.37-6.87, p=.008), while focal involvement showed an increased hazard estimate that did not retain statistical significance (hazard ratio 1.95, 95% confidence interval 0.998-3.79). Overall survival did not differ according to lymphovascular space invasion status (log-rank p=.60). Vessel-by-vessel analysis showed elevated hazard estimates across categories of vessel involvement, without a consistent increase in the risk of recurrence with increasing vessel count.
CONCLUSIONS: Substantial lymphovascular space invasion was independently associated with recurrence risk, while focal involvement showed an increased recurrence risk that did not retain statistical significance after adjustment. Vessel-by-vessel analysis did not identify a definitive prognostic threshold, although limited vessel involvement may still carry prognostic relevance and warrant further investigation. No significant differences in overall survival were observed according to lymphovascular space invasion status.

articles.title: Distinct age-related associations of equol production status with cardiometabolic, oxidative stress and bone biomarkers in Japanese women.
articles.authors: Yoshikata R, Myint KZY, Taguchi J
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: We investigated equol production status (producer/nonproducer) and its relationships with cardiometabolic, oxidative stress and bone biomarkers across different age groups of women.
STUDY DESIGN: This is an observational study of 1904 women aged 20-91 years (mean 51.42 ± 12.9 years) who underwent annual health screening between July 1, 2020, and March 31, 2025. Equol production status was defined as a urinary equol concentration of 1 μM or more.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: We examined the associations between equol production status and cardiometabolic, oxidative stress and bone biomarkers across different age groups.
RESULTS: Among 1,904 women who underwent 2,996 equol tests, 29% were identified as equol producers, ranging from 22% to 31% across the age groups. However, among those who took the test at least two times, only 15% were stable equol producers, and 30% fluctuated between equol producers and nonproducer status. A Cochran-Armitage trend test revealed a significant linear increase in the proportions of equol producers across categories of more frequent soy consumption. Equol producer status was associated with oxidative stress biomarkers in younger women of reproductive age but was associated with metabolic and vascular biomarkers in women in the late reproductive period, around menopause and early post-menopause.
CONCLUSION: Approximately 29% of the study participants were equol producers, but their equol production might not be consistent. Equol producer status might be associated with multiple health benefits, but these might depend on the life stage of the individual.

articles.title: Hydrological redistribution shapes structural mismatch between water-energy-food sustainability and ecosystem services in an arid inland river basin.
articles.authors: Xia H, Yang L, Feng Q et al.
articles.abstract: Hydrological redistribution links ecosystem service (ES) supply with water-energy-food nexus sustainability (WEFNS) in arid inland river basins. However, how upstream-downstream hydrological gradients generate WEFNS-ES mismatch remains insufficiently understood, particularly in mountain-basin systems where runoff and key ecological functions are generated upstream, while irrigation agriculture and resource demand are concentrated in oasis areas. Here, we developed an integrated diagnostic framework combining ES assessment, mismatch diagnosis, random forest modeling, and partial least squares structural equation modeling to examine WEFNS-ES mismatch in the Shiyang River Basin, northwestern China, over 2000-2020. During this period, WEFNS declined in five of seven counties by 8.0%-22.5%, water yield and soil retention decreased by 6.6% and 4.9%, respectively, whereas carbon storage and food production increased by 2.3% and 47.9%. These divergent trajectories produced structural mismatch along the mountain-basin hydrological gradient. WEFNS became increasingly asynchronous with water yield and soil retention, but remained more closely aligned with food production and managed carbon storage in oasis and industrial areas. Further analysis showed that mismatch formation resulted from the interaction of hydrological redistribution, functional divergence among ES, and uneven regulatory capacity. The proposed framework provides a regionally grounded approach for diagnosing socio-ecological mismatch and supports zonal water governance in arid inland river basins.

articles.title: Exploring together: Dyadic coordination in object exploration and its role in early lexical development in preterm and full-term toddlers.
articles.authors: Raspanti A, Provera A, Belloni S et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Early language development emerges from the dynamic integration of sensorimotor experiences and caregiver-child interaction. The present study investigated how toddlers' manual object exploration and caregivers' behaviors jointly relate to early lexical development within a dyadic framework, comparing full-term (FT) and preterm (PT) toddlers at 18 months of age.
METHODS: Sixty-four dyads of 18-month-old toddlers and their parent (36 FT, 28 PT) participated in a semi-structured play session involving familiar and unfamiliar objects while the interaction was video-recorded using both head-mounted and external cameras. Toddlers' expressive vocabulary was assessed using the Italian version of the MacArthur-Bates Communicative Development Inventories. Micro-analytic coding captured toddlers and caregivers' manual object exploration, and caregivers' labelling.
RESULTS: Expressive vocabulary was associated with differences in toddlers' exploratory behaviors. Across groups, toddlers with higher vocabulary showed greater sensitivity to object familiarity, displaying more frequent manipulation of familiar objects. Within the PT group, toddlers with higher vocabulary spent longer exploring objects compared with both lower-performing PT peers and FT toddlers. Caregivers' verbal input differed across groups: caregivers of PT toddlers with lower vocabulary produced more object labels and more contingent labeling during toddlers' manipulation, suggesting an implicit increased verbal scaffolding strategy.
CONCLUSIONS: These findings highlight the importance of considering early language development as an embodied and relational process emerging from coordinated exploratory and communicative behaviors within caregiver-toddler dyads, particularly in contexts of developmental risk such as prematurity.

articles.title: Molecular detection of Waddlia chondrophila in aborted bovine placental and vaginal mucus samples in Japan.
articles.authors: Nagamine S, Endo N, Wu CF et al.
articles.abstract: Chlamydia-related bacteria have recently raised medical and veterinary concerns as emerging causes of abortion and pneumonia in ruminants and humans in Europe and Africa. However, these bacteria have not yet been investigated in ruminants in Japan. In this study, two species, Waddlia chondrophila and Parachlamydia acanthamoebae, were examined as potential pathogens of ruminant abortion. Vaginal mucus and placental samples were collected from 29 cows that had experienced abortion or stillbirth in Japan between August 2023 and December 2023. In real-time PCR analysis, W. chondrophila DNA was detected in both the vaginal mucus and placenta from one cow, whereas P. acanthamoebae was not detected in any individual. An 856 bp 16S rRNA sequence was obtained and identified as W. chondrophila through phylogenetic analysis. The bacterial genomic copy numbers were 3.47 × 10⁴ copies/mL in vaginal mucus and 2.36 × 10⁶ copies/g in placenta, indicating that the placental load was 30- to 130-times higher. This study represents the first report of W. chondrophila detection in a bovine abortion case in Japan and highlights the need for further investigation of Chlamydia-related bacteria and other pathogens affecting animal and human health.

articles.title: Image-guided photothermal therapy in ovarian cancer using a pH-sensitive ICG/TPZ nanoliposome to overcome thermoresistance.
articles.authors: Liu Q, Wang J, Li J et al.
articles.abstract: Ovarian cancer remains a lethal gynecological malignancy with limited effective therapies. Photothermal therapy (PTT) is promising but hindered by scarce clinically approved photothermal agents and intrinsic tumor thermoresistance. Herein, we developed a pH-sensitive nanoliposome, ICG@TPZ-Lipo, co-delivering FDA-approved indocyanine green (ICG) and the hypoxia-activated prodrug tirapazamine (TPZ). The liposome exhibited uniform spherical morphology (~50 nm) with a hydrodynamic diameter of ~72 nm (polydispersity index = 0.18). It showed pH-dependent charge reversal from -28.8 to + 2.0 mV when pH value decreased from 7.4 to 5.5. ICG and TPZ loading were 7.3% and 3.4%, respectively. In acidic tumor microenvironment, protonation of poly(2-ethyl-2-oxazoline) (PEOz) triggered disassembly and released > 80% of encapsulated TPZ. Unlike previously reported ICG/TPZ platforms relying on passive co-delivery, our system exploits PEOz-based pH-responsive charge reversal to achieve tumor-acidity-triggered ICG and TPZ tumor accumulation. Under 808 nm laser irradiation, ICG@TPZ-Lipo demonstrated a temperature increase of 17.9 °C with 19.3% photothermal conversion efficiency, and an ability of reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation. Furthermore, ICG@TPZ-Lipo aggravated hypoxia to activate TPZ, causing DNA damage, mitochondrial depolarization, and ATP depletion, which further caused the downregulation of HSF1/HSP90, thereby overcoming thermoresistance. In vitro, ICG@TPZ-Lipo showed superior tumor-cell killing to control nanoparticles. In SKOV3-tumor-bearing mice, ICG@TPZ-Lipo suppressed tumor growth under near-infrared II (NIR-II) fluorescence imaging guidance and achieved complete tumor regression in all treated mice without recurrence. Its therapeutic efficacy was superior than that of the control nanoparticles. Moreover, ICG@TPZ-Lipo demonstrated negligible systemic toxicity. These preclinical findings support further evaluation of this image-guided chemo-photothermal strategy for ovarian cancer.

articles.title: The hidden threat: Integrated molecular mechanisms of lead-induced reproductive toxicity from endocrine disruption to epigenetic reprogramming.
articles.journal: Journal of trace elements in medicine and biology : organ of the Society for Minerals and Trace Elements (GMS)
articles.authors: Samaga R, Ranade SD, Rajora AD et al.
articles.abstract: Lead (Pb²⁺) is a persistent environmental toxicant that adversely affects male and female reproductive health through endocrine disruption, oxidative stress, inflammation, mitochondrial dysfunction, DNA damage, apoptosis, and epigenetic alterations. Pb²⁺ disrupts the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal and hypothalamic-pituitary-ovarian axes while directly damaging reproductive cells. Excessive ROS generation, impaired antioxidant defense, and dysregulation of Nrf2 and NF-κB signaling promote oxidative and inflammatory injury, while mitochondrial dysfunction and impaired autophagy further accelerate cellular damage. In males, Pb²⁺ impairs Leydig and Sertoli cell function, steroidogenesis, blood-testis barrier integrity, spermatogenesis, sperm maturation, and fertilization, resulting in reduced sperm quality, motility, and DNA integrity. In females, Pb²⁺ disrupts ovarian steroidogenesis, follicular development, oocyte quality, and ovarian reserve, contributing to menstrual irregularities, impaired ovulation, subfertility, and adverse pregnancy outcomes. Epigenetic alterations may further contribute to persistent reproductive dysfunction and potentially affect offspring's health. Current management primarily involves exposure reduction and clinically indicated chelation, while antioxidant and micronutrient interventions may provide supportive protection. However, limitations in human evidence and incomplete understanding of molecular interactions remain important challenges. Integrating multi-omics approaches with reproductive phenotyping in the future may facilitate biomarker discovery and targeted therapy. Overall, Pb²⁺-induced reproductive toxicity is a multifactorial molecular disorder, emphasizing the need for early detection, preventive strategies, and targeted interventions to protect reproductive health.

articles.title: De-escalation strategies and fertility preservation in Stage I placental site trophoblastic tumor: an individual patient data systematic review and institutional series.
articles.authors: Chen J, Zhu G, Sun Y et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study evaluates the statistical robustness of the ISAP cutoff proposed by the 2025 guidelines, re-assesses traditional pathological prognostic factors, and identifies candidates for therapeutic de-escalation regarding chemotherapy omission and fertility-sparing surgery (FSS).
METHODS: We harmonized an institutional cohort (2015-2021, N = 36) with a systematic literature review (1990-2021, N = 193). Missing data were handled via multiple imputation. The optimal ISAP cutoff was determined using AIC/BIC; prognostic factors were evaluated via multivariate Cox regression.
RESULTS: Among 229 patients (50 [21.8%] undergoing FSS), ISAP ≥48 months emerged as the optimal cutoff, stratifying 174 low-risk (ISAP <48 months) and 31 high-risk patients. ISAP ≥48 months independently predicted progression-free survival (HR 14.92, 95% CI 3.68-60.38; P < 0.001) and overall survival (HR 20.90, 95% CI 2.22-196.73; P = 0.008). Pathological risk factors showed no prognostic significance. Among low-risk patients managed without chemotherapy, no progression or mortality events occurred (0/85). Four (8.0%) FSS patients required salvage hysterectomy; all achieved 100% survival and none required completion hysterectomy after childbearing.
CONCLUSIONS: ISAP ≥48 months is a robust prognostic determinant in Stage I PSTT. Surgery alone achieved excellent outcomes in low-risk patients; prospective trials should confirm whether chemotherapy can be safely omitted. FSS is viable for strictly selected low-risk candidates, with salvage hysterectomy providing effective control and subsequent term pregnancies documented.

articles.title: "We're like walking on thin ice for our happiness": Platform-mediated reproductive governance in Chinese women's IVF narratives on RedNote.
articles.authors: He Y, Xu K
articles.abstract: In vitro fertilization (IVF) has become an important component of population governance in China, particularly following its incorporation into the national health insurance system. Drawing on Foucauldian biopolitics and reproductive governance, this study examines how Chinese women publicly narrate their IVF journeys on RedNote and how platform-mediated interactions shape the governance of reproduction. Analysis of these narratives identifies four key themes-quantified visibility through self-tracking, stigma and negotiated visibility in narrating IVF failure, hope sustained through care and support in online sisterhood, and anticipatory motherhood articulated through self-positioning and relational affirmation. The findings show that through practices of self-disclosure, repeated posting, and peer interaction on RedNote, reproductive bodies, failure, hope, and maternal identities become publicly visible and relationally meaningful. The study conceptualizes this process as "platform-mediated reproductive governance," whereby peer-based monitoring, emotional support, and relational affirmation intersect with established medical and institutional authority. This perspective extends reproductive governance scholarship by adding a communicative and relational dimension and showing how digital platforms mediate not only the visibility of reproductive experiences but also the ways women negotiate bodily management, failure, hope, and maternal identity.

articles.title: First-Trimester Maternal Gut Microbiome and Small Vulnerable Newborns: A Prospective Cohort Study.
articles.journal: BJOG : an international journal of obstetrics and gynaecology
articles.authors: McMillan R, Dria RM, Moreau GB et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To investigate the relationship between the first trimester gut microbiome and small vulnerable newborns (SVN).
SETTING: Rural low- and middle-income country: Bangladesh.
POPULATION: 213 women were enrolled during the first trimester of pregnancy as part of the NICHD Global Network for Women's and Children's Health registry, Bangladesh.
METHODS: Observational study of the maternal gut microbiome and birth outcomes. Blood and stool samples were collected at enrollment. Birth outcomes were recorded within 72 h of delivery. Random forest machine learning models trained on microbiome data were used to predict SVN or first-trimester maternal features of interest. Hold out sets were used to test model accuracy.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: SVN (born preterm, low birth weight, or small for gestational age).
RESULTS: The birth outcome SVN (n = 106) was discriminated from non-SVN (n = 107) using a microbiome-trained random forest model (AUC = 0.653, 95% CI 0.518-0.789). The microbiome also predicted the inflammatory markers plasma alpha-1-acid glycoprotein and faecal calprotectin (AUC = 0.742, 95% CI: 0.616-0.868 and AUC = 0.793, 95% CI: 0.680-0.905, respectively), while micronutrient concentrations, anaemia, C-reactive protein and the presence of atypical Enteropathogenic E. coli were not reliably predicted. Higher alpha-1-acid glycoprotein was significantly associated with SVN (aOR = 1.98; 95% CI: 1.04-3.85) whereas calprotectin was not.
CONCLUSIONS: In this prospective cohort, first-trimester maternal gut microbiome composition showed modest discrimination for SVN and a marker of systemic inflammation. These findings support further investigation of early pregnancy microbiome-inflammation pathways in fetal growth restriction and preterm birth.

articles.title: Negotiating activity and rest during pregnancy at risk of preterm birth: A qualitative study of parents' experiences.
articles.authors: Farø J, Lou S, Bünemann K et al.
articles.abstract: Background Preterm birth (PTB), defined as birth before 37 weeks, is estimated to affect >10% of pregnancies worldwide. In Denmark, women with a short cervix (<15 mm) are often recommended to restrict physical activity to prevent preterm birth. It is uncertain how women and their partners balance rest and activity in daily life during a high-risk pregnancy in this situation. Aim To explore how women at risk of PTB and their partners navigate decisions regarding activity and rest. Methods Qualitative, semi-structured interviews with 13 women hospitalised for cervical shortening and risk of PTB and 9 partners. Data was analysed using reflexive thematic analysis. Results Three main themes were developed. 1) Following the prescribed boundaries of "safe" activity describes how couples relied on healthcare professionals (HCPs) to define acceptable activity, thereby distributing responsibility for potential adverse outcomes. 2) "She was pregnant, but the baby was ours" describes how some partners left the decision-making to the pregnant women, either trusting her embodied judgment or downplaying their own concerns. Others intervened when they perceived her behaviour as "risky". 3) Doing what felt right to me, illustrates how women adjusted activity in response to bodily sensations and negotiated between minimizing risk and maintaining self-care. However, for some, bodily sensations were difficult to interpret. Conclusion: When in risk of PTB, HCPs play a decisive role in women's decision-making regarding activity levels. However, professional advice is actively managed and negotiated in the context of the woman's relationship with her partner and her bodily sensations.

articles.title: Serum metabolomics analysis of individual variability in superovulation among Tan lamb Ewes and identification of lipid metabolism biomarkers.
articles.authors: Zhao M, Liu H, Lei A et al.
articles.abstract: Juvenile In Vitro Embryo Transfer (JIVET) can shorten generation intervals but is limited by large individual variation in superovulation response. To elucidate metabolic mechanisms and identify serum biomarkers, 18 female Tan lambs (4-8 weeks) received uniform superovulation and were classified into high, medium, and low production groups based on follicle counts and oocyte recovery. Pre- and post-superovulation serum samples were analyzed by LC-MS/MS untargeted metabolomics. A total of 1,899 metabolites were identified. Pre-superovulation, metabolic profiles of the high- and low-yield groups were clearly separated, with differential metabolites enriched in amino acid biosynthesis and glycine-serine-threonine metabolism. Post-superovulation, enrichment shifted to phenylalanine and linoleic acid metabolism. Intersection analysis revealed eight lipid metabolites consistently upregulated in the order high > medium > low at both pre- and post-superovulation stages, including medium-chain fatty acids (lauric, caprylic, capric acid), a bile acid (taurochenodeoxycholic acid), three lysophosphatidylcholines, and a sphingolipid (ganglioside GA2). Among these, lauric acid, taurochenodeoxycholic acid, and LysoPC(22:1(13Z)) showed significantly higher abundance in high-yield lambs. These findings indicate that superovulation efficiency is closely linked to basal lipid metabolism capacity. The eight lipid metabolites may serve as candidate serum biomarkers for predicting JIVET donor potential, providing a theoretical basis for pre-selection and advancing the understanding of metabolism-reproduction axis regulation.

articles.title: Mismatch Repair "Null" Immunophenotype in Endometrial Endometrioid Carcinoma: MLH1 Promoter Hypermethylation With Somatic Inactivation of MSH2.
articles.journal: International journal of gynecological pathology : official journal of the International Society of Gynecological Pathologists
articles.authors: Strickland KC, Zsiros E, Onel K et al.
articles.abstract: Up to 3% of endometrial cancers may be associated with Lynch syndrome (LS). For endometrial cancer, the preferred approach to universal LS screening is immunohistochemical staining for the mismatch repair proteins MLH1, PMS2, MSH2, and MSH6, with about one-third of endometrial cancers showing abnormal results. We describe the case of a 57-year-old woman with an endometrial endometrioid carcinoma that demonstrated a rare "null" mismatch repair protein immunohistochemical profile with complete loss of MLH1, PMS2, MSH2, and MSH6 expression, with positive staining in the internal and external controls. Subsequent MLH1 methylation testing, genetic counseling, and somatic tumor tissue testing revealed MLH1 promoter methylation, no germline alterations, a somatic frameshift mutation in MLH1 and 2 somatic nonsense mutations in MSH2, a high tumor mutational burden (68.8 mut/Mb), and microsatellite instability in 55 of 104 microsatellite sites assessed. Although the patient had a family history of colon cancer, the MMR-null immunophenotype is attributed to a combination of methylation and somatic events. However, in gastrointestinal cancer cases, the MMR-null immunophenotype has been associated with LS, and therefore, in gynecologic cases, we recommend MLH1 promoter methylation testing and germline genetic counseling and testing for cases demonstrating this rare finding.

articles.title: Cinnamic Acid Ameliorates D-Galactose-Induced Premature Ovarian Failure in Mice and Alters Antioxidant and Angiogenesis-Related Gene Expression.
articles.journal: Canadian journal of physiology and pharmacology
articles.authors: Taebi R, Pourdadashi A, Amini A
articles.abstract: Premature ovarian failure (POF) is characterized by ovarian dysfunction, infertility, and oxidative stress. Cinnamic acid (CA), a polyphenol with antioxidant properties, may protect ovarian function. This study evaluated the effects of CA in a D-galactose-induced mouse model of POF. Thirty NMRI mice were assigned to a control, a POF group, and three CA-treated groups (50, 100, and 200 mg/kg). POF was induced by daily D-galactose injection for 42 days, with CA co-administered during the last 14 days. Estrous cyclicity, ovarian histology, total antioxidant capacity (TAC), and mRNA expression of Nrf2, Foxo3a, Angpt1, Angpt2, and Vegfa were evaluated. D-gal disrupted estrous cycles, increased follicular atresia, and downregulated these genes. CA treatment improved estrous cyclicity, follicular development, and TAC, and increased gene expression relative to the POF group, with the most pronounced effects generally observed at 200 mg/kg. These findings suggest that CA may improve several features of D-galactose-induced ovarian dysfunction, potentially through enhanced antioxidant capacity. Changes in angiogenesis-related gene expression were inconsistent and should be considered exploratory rather than evidence of enhanced ovarian angiogenesis. Further protein-level, vascular, and functional studies are needed to clarify the biological significance and mechanisms of these effects.

articles.title: Reproductive Lifespan and Hormonal Therapy in Relation to Later-Life Neurovascular Health in Community-Dwelling Older Women.
articles.authors: Lorenzon G, Garcia-Lluch G, Coughlan GT et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Women are disproportionately affected by Alzheimer disease (AD), a vulnerability that may relate to estrogen fluctuations across the lifespan. Estrogen has neuroprotective and vasoprotective effects, suggesting that lifetime estrogen exposure may influence both AD-related neurodegeneration and cerebrovascular health. However, its association with late-life vascular and neurodegenerative brain changes remains unclear. We aimed to examine the associations of lifelong estrogen exposure-endogenous (reproductive span) and exogenous (oral contraceptives [OCs], menopausal hormone therapy [MHT])-with late-life vascular brain injury and AD-related atrophy and explore apolipoprotein-ε4 (APOE-ε4) effects.
METHODS: This population-based study included cognitively unimpaired women from the Gothenburg H70-1944 Birth Cohort who underwent brain MRI at age 70 and again 5 years later. Reproductive lifespan was calculated as age at menopause or oophorectomy minus age at menarche. OC and MHT use were categorized as ever vs never users. Outcomes included cerebral small vessel disease (SVD), AD-related cortical thickness, and white matter integrity (fractional anisotropy). SVD burden was a composite score derived from white matter hyperintensities (WMHs), lacunes, cerebral microbleeds (CMBs), and perivascular spaces (PVSs) (range 0-4). Linear, multinomial, and mixed-effects regression models were adjusted for relevant confounders and stratified by APOE-ε4.
RESULTS: Among 352 women (mean age 70 years), longer reproductive span was associated with lower SVD burden (OR = 0.92, 95% CI 0.86-0.99). MHT use was associated with fewer PVSs and CMBs. OC and MHT use were associated with greater white matter integrity, with combined use showing the highest fractional anisotropy compared with nonusers (β = 0.45, 95% CI 0.12-0.78). No multiplicative interaction between OCs and MHT was observed, although joint exposure analyses suggested cumulative effects. MHT use was associated with greater AD-related cortical thickness among APOE-ε4 carriers only (β = 0.38, 95% CI 0.01-0.76). Longer estrogen exposure was associated with stable cortical thickness and WMH trajectories over time.
DISCUSSION: Greater lifetime estrogen exposure, both endogenous and exogenous, was associated with lower cerebrovascular pathology in women and, among APOE-ε4 carriers, greater cortical thickness in AD-vulnerable regions. These findings support the potential role of cerebrovascular…

articles.title: Human Papillomavirus Genotypes Among Women With Invasive Cervical Cancer in Nigeria: A Scoping Review.
articles.authors: Obodoechina N, Smith JS, Kalulu P et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Invasive cervical cancer (ICC) cases remain a major public health concern for women in Nigeria. The purpose of this scoping review is to assess the reporting of common human papillomavirus (HPV) genotypes found in ICC cases among Nigerian women.
METHODS: We searched five databases, including Embase, Ovid Medline, Scopus, Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, and Google Scholar, to identify studies reporting HPV genotypes found in ICC cases in Nigeria. Study selection and data extraction were conducted in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews guidelines. Two researchers extracted data from each eligible article.
RESULTS: A total of 668 records were identified, of which 422 studies were screened and six articles met the eligibility criteria. The included studies reported on HPV genotypes detected in ICC among Nigerian women. Across the studies, high-risk HPV (hrHPV) types 16, 18, 35, and 45 were identified in approximately 50% of ICC cases, whereas other detected genotypes included hrHPV types 31, 33, 51, and 52. Notably, in addition to globally predominant hrHPV types 16 and 18, hrHPV types 35 and 45 were also frequently detected, indicating their significant contribution to the ICC burden among Nigerian women.
CONCLUSION: After an extensive search, this study provides a comprehensive assessment of the overall prevalence and distribution of hrHPV genotypes in Nigerian women with ICC. The most common hrHPV genotypes detected in ICC in Nigeria are 16, 18, 35, 45, 31, 33, 51, and 52. hrHPV types 16 and 18 account for the majority of cases, but in Nigeria and among women of African descent worldwide, hrHPV types 45 and 35 are also significantly present in ICC cases.

articles.title: Quantifying a Neglected Burden: Pregnancy-Associated Hepatocellular Carcinoma and Maternal Death in South Africa.
articles.authors: Venter K, Sobnach S, Kotze U et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) during pregnancy is rare, with the literature confined to isolated case reports and small series. Women in sub-Saharan Africa (SSA) face disproportionate risk due to chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection acquired perinatally, HCC in noncirrhotic livers at a young age, and fertility rates nearly three times those of Europe. To our knowledge, we report the largest cohort of pregnancy-associated HCC from SSA, drawn from a single South African center, and the first quantitative estimate of regional disparity versus Europe.
METHODS: Pregnant women with HCC at Groote Schuur Hospital, Cape Town, over 24 years (2001-2025) were identified from a prospectively maintained registry. A model integrating HCC incidence, age-at-diagnosis, fertility rates, and 1-year mortality compared the probability of pregnancy-associated HCC and maternal death in SSA versus Europe.
RESULTS: Of the 728 registry patients, 192 (26.4%) were female and 10 (5.2%) were pregnant or within 1 year postpartum. The median age was 32.5 (IQR, 28.5-35.3), 70% had chronic HBV infection, and three had cirrhosis. Seven (70%) died, six within 90 days. Two patients survived beyond 10 years following curative resection. Four pregnancies ended in intrauterine fetal demise and five in live births. The modeled probability of pregnancy-associated HCC was 16 per 100,000 women in SSA versus 0.14 per 100,000 in Europe-a 114-fold difference-with a 187-fold greater risk of maternal death.
CONCLUSION: Pregnancy-associated HCC in SSA is a quantifiable, preventable contributor to maternal mortality-nearly two orders of magnitude greater than in Europe. HBV endemicity, early-onset noncirrhotic HCC, and high fertility rates create a hostile environment for women of reproductive age. HBV-aware liver surveillance in antenatal care, strengthened prevention of mother-to-child transmission programs, and improved maternal mortality data systems are urgently needed.

articles.title: Factors Associated With the Absence of Fetal Autopsy: Perception of Healthcare Professionals From a French Cross-Sectional Survey.
articles.authors: Reyl C, Martin-Berenguer S, Sauveste F et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Despite recent recommendations highlighting the importance of fetal autopsy for genetic counseling and recurrence prevention, its uptake has declined. This study aimed to identify factors associated with absence of fetal autopsy from the perception of healthcare professionals (HP).
METHODS: National cross-sectional online survey among French HPs involved in the management of fetal loss was conducted. An anonymous questionnaire explored demographic characteristics, perceived medical, emotional, organizational and educational barriers to fetal autopsy, as well as potential strategies to improve uptake. Data were analyzed descriptively.
RESULTS: A total of 125 HP completed the survey. Opinions about estimated rate of fetal autopsy refusal in stillbirth cases ranged from 30% to 40% across institutions. Refusal rates varied according to the clinical context or reaching over 75% in terminations of pregnancy with known genetic diagnosis. Identified barriers were multifactorial, including emotional distress related to grief, religious beliefs, fetal bodily integrity. Organizational issues constraints also played a significant role. Additionally, many respondents reported that insufficient training influenced the absence of fetal autopsy.
CONCLUSION: Fetal autopsy refusal is driven by emotional, cultural, informational, and organizational factors according to practitioners' perceptions. The development of less invasive alternatives and improved training in communication and bereavement care may enhance acceptance and support for bereaved couples.

articles.title: Cardiometabolic dysfunction and age at natural menopause: a prospective study.
articles.authors: Quarpong W, Chandrasekaran S, Mehta PK et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Menopause marks a key reproductive milestone with significant implications for women's long-term cardiometabolic health. However, the influence of cardiometabolic health during the reproductive years on the timing of menopause remains poorly understood. We prospectively examined the association between cardiometabolic health profiles and menopause onset in South Asian women, a population at high risk of early cardiometabolic dysfunction.
METHODS: We analyzed longitudinal data from menstruating women aged 30-50 years in the CARRS cohort from 2010 to 2024. Baseline cardiometabolic measures included overweight/obesity (body mass index ≥25 kg/m2), hypertension (systolic blood pressure ≥140 or diastolic blood pressure ≥90 mmHg, prior history, or medication use), diabetes (hemoglobin A1c ≥6.5%, physician diagnosis, or use of glucose-lowering medication), and non-high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (non-HDL-C ≥ 130 mg/dl). Using Cox proportional hazards models, we examined associations between baseline cardiometabolic status and time to natural menopause, adjusting for sociodemographic and reproductive factors.
RESULTS: Among 2225 women (median age 37 years; IQR: 33, 40), 44% reached natural menopause at a median age of 46 (IQR: 43, 49) years. Women with hypertension reached natural menopause approximately 1 year earlier than those without hypertension. In adjusted models, women with hypertension experienced relatively earlier natural menopause over follow-up (HR 1.34, 95% CI: 1.19-1.52). In contrast, the timing of natural menopause did not differ by baseline diabetes, weight, or non-HDL-C status.
CONCLUSION: Hypertension was associated with earlier timing of menopause in South Asian women. Further research is needed to explore underlying mechanisms and long-term health implications.

articles.title: Physical activity and screen time in children and adolescents born very preterm: a cross-sectional study.
articles.authors: Haile S, Peralta GP, Adams M et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: We aimed to assess physical activity and screen time in a cohort of very preterm-born children and adolescents (aged 5-16 years), in comparison with their full-term siblings. We also aimed to identify potential correlates of these lifestyle factors among the very preterm-born.
DESIGN: Cross-sectional survey in the greater Zurich area of Switzerland.
PATIENTS: Children born <32 weeks gestation (n = 482) as well as their full-term siblings (n = 149).
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Physical activity (hours per day or meeting recommendations with >1 hour per day) and screen time (hours per day or <2 hours per day).
METHODS: Linear/logistic regression accounted for age group, sex and family unit. A classification tree analysis explored potential correlates of physical activity and screen time among the very preterm-born.
RESULTS: Physical activity of very preterm-born children was similar to that of their full-term siblings, but only one-third of participants met physical activity requirements (i.e. at least 1 hour per day). Screen time was similar in both groups, but much higher among adolescents regardless of preterm birth status. Chronic conditions and respiratory symptoms were not associated with insufficient physical activity. No correlates were identified for physical activity, while age group and socioeconomic status were associated with screen time.
CONCLUSIONS: No differences in physical activity and screen time were observed between very preterm-born children and their full-term siblings, but only one-third of participants met physical activity recommendations. Both groups were observed to be less active than the general population. Neither respiratory symptoms nor chronic conditions explained variation in these lifestyle outcomes. Both very preterm-born children and adolescents and their full-term siblings could benefit from better adherence to international physical activity and screen time guidelines.

articles.title: Beyond Silence: Body Mapping and the Study of Coercive Intrauterine Device (IUD) Insertion.
articles.authors: Zhao J
articles.abstract: This article makes a methodological case for body mapping as a way of studying coercive reproductive intervention that is remembered rather than observed, that sits decades in the past, and that is held in the body more readily than it is put into words. It emerges from a larger study of Chinese women's career experiences under the three-child policy. A recurring pattern emerged during fieldwork: participants' discussions of contemporary employment regularly returned to embodied memories of forced intrauterine device insertion under the one-child policy era, generating a methodological and epistemological challenge. How can qualitative researchers engage with coercive reproductive histories when participants speak decades after the event, memory is fragmented, and the topic sits at the intersection of pain, shame, and state policy? Drawing on a sub-sample of 28 participants who completed body maps in follow-up interviews, this article argues that body mapping is especially suited to studying reproductive intervention as an 'embodied afterlife' that continues to shape women's present decisions about work, fertility, and the future. Grounded in theories of reproductive governance, body memory, and sociological embodiment, the article makes three methodological contributions: body mapping reaches registers of experience that transcript-centred methods cannot fully access; in sequence with interviewing, it reshapes rather than simply supplements the analysis; and the analytic work of treating body maps as data, together with the ethical and relational demands of trauma-informed practice, is not a procedural addition to the method but part of what enables it to generate the knowledge it does.

articles.title: METTL3-mediated m6A modification of DNMT1 enhances ovarian cancer progression.
articles.authors: Kumari K, Pérez-Núñez I, Noguera Castells A et al.
articles.abstract: High-grade serous ovarian carcinoma (HGSOC), the most lethal subtype of ovarian cancer, is often diagnosed at advanced stages and remains associated with poor clinical outcome. In this study, we identify a critical oncogenic role of the RNA methyltransferase METTL3 and the N6-methyladenosine (m6A) RNA modification pathway in HGSOC. Suppression of METTL3, either genetically or pharmacologically, and depletion of its binding partner METTL14 impair ovarian cancer proliferation and tumor progression. Mechanistically, we show that METTL3-mediated m6A deposition enhances the translation of DNA methyltransferase 1 (DNMT1), the primary maintenance DNA methyltransferase responsible for preserving genome-wide methylation patterns and silencing tumor suppressor genes. Pharmacological inhibition of DNMT1 induces widespread DNA hypomethylation and up-regulation of the tumor suppressors TNFAIP3 and FBXO32. Consistently, METTL3 suppression reduces DNMT1 abundance and derepresses TNFAIP3 and FBXO32 expression. Knockdown and rescue studies further reveal that DNMT1 primarily mediates METTL3-dependent regulation of cell migration, whereas the antiproliferative effects of METTL3 suppression are likely driven by additional downstream targets. Collectively, these findings identify the m6A-METTL3-DNMT1 axis as a mechanistic link between RNA and DNA methylation pathways and a potential therapeutic vulnerability in HGSOC.

articles.title: Sibling Psychiatric Diagnoses and Risk of Postpartum Psychosis: A Nationwide Cohort Study.
articles.authors: Smout S, Milazzo F, Robakis TK et al.
articles.abstract: Objective: To evaluate associations between sibling psychiatric diagnoses and risk of postpartum psychosis and to determine whether these associations vary by sibling sex and the woman's own psychiatric history. Methods: In this population-based cohort study using Swedish national registers, we identified 1,213,829 women with a full sibling who delivered their first live-born child between January 1980 and October 2017. The primary outcome was postpartum psychosis, defined as mania, psychosis, or psychotic depression within 90 days postpartum. Associations between sibling psychiatric diagnoses and postpartum psychosis were estimated using logistic regression with cluster-robust standard errors, including stratification by the woman's own psychiatric history. Results: Overall, 1,831 women developed postpartum psychosis (1.5 per 1,000). The strongest associations were observed for sister's postpartum psychosis (OR=10.84; 95% CI, 5.76-20.40), cyclothymia (OR=8.29; 95% CI, 4.65-14.76), schizoaffective disorder (OR=7.90; 4.99-12.52), and bipolar disorder (OR=5.00; 95% CI, 4.23-5.90). Patterns were similar in brother and sister pairs. Sibling psychiatric history was most informative among women with no prior psychiatric diagnosis, where sibling schizoaffective disorder (OR=4.82; 95% CI, 2.99-7.74) and bipolar disorder (OR=3.07; 95% CI, 2.59-3.64) showed substantial risk increases. Among women with a history of mania or psychosis, sibling diagnoses contributed little additional predictive value. Conclusion: Postpartum psychosis shows strong familial aggregation across multiple sibling diagnoses, with a pattern supporting its conceptualization within the spectrum of severe mood disorders with psychotic features. Family psychiatric history may help identify at-risk women who lack established clinical predictors.

articles.title: Opportunities and challenges for introduction of balanced energy protein supplementation through routine antenatal care.
articles.authors: Waithira R, Fekadu H, Gaithuma J et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The World Health Organization (WHO) recommends balanced energy and protein (BEP) supplementation during pregnancy in contexts where prevalence of maternal underweight, defined as body mass index (BMI) < 18.5 kg/m2, is ≥ 20%. Evidence shows that BEP supplementation in underweight pregnant women reduces the risk of low birthweight, small for gestational age, and preterm birth. Yet little is known about how to introduce BEP through routine antenatal care (ANC). This paper explores challenges, opportunities, and recommendations for successful introduction of BEP supplementation through ANC service delivery.
METHODS: From August - December 2023, a mixed-methods landscape analysis was carried out, which comprised of a review of country antenatal care guidelines, as well as key informant interviews (KIIs) with thirteen global and country stakeholders. KIIs were recorded, transcribed, and analyzed by themes and subthemes using Dedoose qualitative software 10.0.
RESULTS: Findings revealed confusion around the definition of BEP, coupled with low awareness of the WHO ANC guideline on BEP supplementation among country stakeholders. Provider capacity for BEP provision is weak. Sharing, selling, and stockouts of BEP supplies are common. Data on the feasibility and cost-effectiveness of the introduction of BEP at country level is critical to inform implementation.
CONCLUSION: Successful introduction of BEP as part of ANC service delivery requires country program implementers to consider government commitments, health provider training, demand generation, compliance, supplies and logistics, local production, and routine monitoring of BEP indicators. Globally, standardized BEP guidance, indicators, and definitions are critical to support quality country implementation. For sustainability, emerging concerns around reductions in global health funding should be addressed in future program design and implementation.

articles.title: Risk factors for surgical site infections following lower-segment caesarean section.
articles.journal: The Indian journal of medical research
articles.authors: Annadanam N, Gokulanathan N, Pegu B et al.
articles.abstract: Surgical site infections (SSIs) in post-caesarean patients increase the risk of maternal morbidity, health care costs, and have implications for future pregnancies. In this cohort study, we aimed to determine the rates and risk factors of SSI until hospital discharge, as well as the bacterial profiles and antibiogram patterns among women undergoing lower-segment caesarean section (LSCS). SSI was observed in 4.5% of women undergoing LSCS (90/2000), with bacterial growth identified in 72/90 (80.0%). Escherichia coli and Acinetobacter baumannii were the predominant organisms. Lower gestational age [adjusted odds ratio (aOR) 0.880, 95% CI 0.796-0.972, per additional week], ≥4 vaginal examinations in labor (aOR 2.823, 95% CI 1.405-5.671), duration of surgery (with additional minute, aOR 1.014, 95% CI 1.005-1.022), and clinically suspected chorioamnionitis (aOR 9.409, 95% CI 4.538-19.512) were identified as independent risk factors of SSI before hospital discharge.

articles.title: In vivo Nupr1 regulates oxidative stress-endoplasmic reticulum stress crosstalk and mitochondria-dependent apoptosis in varicocele-related testicular injury.
articles.authors: Jiang X, Tang L, Ma Z et al.
articles.abstract: Varicocele (VCL) is a major cause of male infertility and is closely associated with oxidative stress (OS)-induced testicular injury. Increasing evidence suggests that endoplasmic reticulum stress (ERS) interacts with OS and mitochondrial dysfunction in the pathogenesis of spermatogenic impairment, but the molecular regulators linking these processes remain incompletely understood. In this study, we investigated the role of Nupr1 in VCL-related testicular stress responses. Re-analysis of transcriptomic data from VCL rat testes identified Nupr1 as a candidate gene associated with OS, ERS, and apoptosis. Nupr1 expression was significantly increased in VCL testes and was similarly upregulated in GC-2 and TM4 cells under H2O2-induced OS or tunicamycin-induced ERS. Stable knockdown of Nupr1 in GC-2 cells reduced viability under oxidative challenge, increased intracellular ROS accumulation, decreased mitochondrial membrane potential, and enhanced apoptosis, accompanied by increased cleaved caspase-3 expression and an elevated Bax/Bcl-2 ratio. Notably, Nupr1 deficiency attenuated the adaptive ERS response, as shown by reduced expression of GRP78, IRE1/p-IRE1, PERK/p-PERK, and ATF6. Pharmacological induction of ERS with tunicamycin further worsened cell injury in Nupr1-deficient cells, whereas 4-PBA failed to restore cell viability or GRP78 expression. Collectively, these findings indicate that Nupr1 is involved in the cellular stress response relevant to VCL and may help maintain adaptive UPR signaling and mitochondrial homeostasis in spermatogenic cells under oxidative stress.

articles.title: Contraception during the transition to menopause: a commentary.
articles.journal: Gynecological endocrinology : the official journal of the International Society of Gynecological Endocrinology
articles.authors: Versailles JBE, Bahamondes L, Grandi G et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The transition to menopause presents unique clinical challenges, requiring a balance between pregnancy prevention and the management of perimenopausal symptoms and age-related comorbidities. Although fertility declines with advancing age, unintended pregnancy after age 40 remains possible and is associated with increased maternal and neonatal risks. Women who wish to avoid pregnancy need effective contraception until menopause is established.
OBJECTIVE: To provide practical guidance on contraceptive counselling during the transition to menopause, considering the safety, effectiveness, noncontraceptive benefits, and limitations of available contraceptive methods.
RESULTS: Age alone is not a contraindication to any contraceptive method; however, the higher prevalence of cardiovascular, metabolic, and malignant conditions in this population requires individualised contraceptive counselling based on each woman's medical history, preferences, reproductive goals, and shared decision-making. Contraceptive care in midlife is more complex than pregnancy prevention alone. Contraceptive counselling should consider both the likelihood of user adherence and the noncontraceptive benefits of each method.
CONCLUSION: This commentary provides practical guidance on contraceptive counselling during the transition to menopause, reviewing the safety, effectiveness, noncontraceptive benefits, and limitations of both short-acting reversible contraceptives (SARCs) and long-acting reversible contraceptives (LARCs) to support informed, individualised contraceptive care.

articles.title: The Lived Experience of Postpartum Hemorrhage: A Phenomenological Study.
articles.authors: Murray MB, Modri ST, Terhaar MF et al.
articles.abstract:
