INTRODUCTION: Postpartum hemorrhage (PPH) is the fourth leading cause of pregnancy-related death in the United States. Although there is extensive evidence on best practices for the clinical management of PPH, no previous US studies have described the experience of individuals who lived it.
METHODS: Guided by a feminist theoretical framework and using a qualitative phenomenological research design, we explored the lived experiences of individuals with a PPH after childbirth within the context of the US health care system. The study was conducted in the Northeastern United States at one urban tertiary care hospital that has greater than 5000 births annually. Individuals who had a blood loss greater than 1000 mL were invited to participate. Semistructured interviews were conducted and analyzed according to the method of van Manen. Themes were identified using the 6 phases of inductive thematic analysis according to Braun and Clarke.
RESULTS: Ten individuals participated in the study. Five themes were identified, including (1) lack of clinician communication, (2) traumatic birth experiences, (3) need for immediate emotional support, (4) extended postpartum needs and impact on future pregnancies, and (5) effective teamwork.
DISCUSSION: The impact of PPH extends well beyond the acute clinical event, encompassing a complex array of physical, emotional, informational, and mental health needs. The findings underscore the critical importance of clear communication and ongoing emotional support for individuals who experience PPH. Addressing these multidimensional needs requires a coordinated response from health care systems, clinicians, and policymakers, with comprehensive postpartum care positioned as a priority in maternal health services.

articles.title: Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events Following Vaginal Estrogen Therapy 2004-2023.
articles.authors: Rustia G, Abou-Zeki J, Murphy J et al.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: This study reports on prescription patterns during years when estrogen use may have been influenced by a U.S. Food and Drug Administration black box warning.
OBJECTIVE: The objective of this study was to evaluate whether vaginal estrogen prescription for genitourinary syndrome of menopause (GSM) is associated with major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE).
STUDY DESIGN: This was a retrospective cohort analysis using the TriNetX database of women with GSM. MACE was evaluated using inverse probability of treatment weighted logistic regression and Cox proportional hazard models. High-risk patients had MACE 91 days to 2 years before the index; low-risk patients had no MACE during this period. Comparisons were made between women with and without vaginal estrogen prescription within 1 year of GSM diagnosis.
RESULTS: Between January 1, 2004, and May 16, 2023, 301,701 women were included in the analysis. Of these, 6,152 (2.0%) had a history of recent MACE. Overall, 159,776 (53%) received at least 1 estrogen (estradiol or conjugated estrogens) prescription following GSM diagnosis, of whom 81,446 (51%) only received vaginal estrogen. Compared with controls, the vaginal estrogen cohort had lower odds of MACE (odds ratio [OR]: 0.87, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.84-0.89) and no significant difference in MACE hazard (hazard ratio: 0.98, 95% CI: 0.95-1.01). Recent MACE history (OR: 12.3, 95% CI: 11.7-13.0) and obesity (OR: 1.25, 95% CI: 1.21-1.29; hazard ratio: 1.23, 95% CI: 1.19-1.27) were strongly associated with MACE.
CONCLUSIONS: Recent MACE history was strongly associated with subsequent MACE. Vaginal estrogen prescription was associated with lower odds of MACE and no increase in MACE hazard.

articles.title: RELAX Perinatal Digital Intervention to Prevent Increasing Anxiety: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.authors: Hirsch CR, Volkmer B, Sawjani Y et al.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Anxiety disorders affect 1 in 5 pregnant women and birthing people. Cognitive bias modification for interpretation reduces anxiety and repetitive negative thinking (RNT; a risk factor for anxiety) among nonpregnant samples.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate whether adding pregnancy-tailored cognitive bias modification for interpretation to usual maternity care (UC) prevents increased anxiety during pregnancy; reduces anxiety, depression, and RNT before and after birth; and improves functioning before and after birth compared with UC.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: The RELAX (Reducing Levels of Anxiety) 2-arm, parallel-group, multisite, superiority, phase 2b randomized clinical trial recruited participants from June 2023 to July 2024, with final assessment in April 2025. Participants included pregnant individuals in the UK at 16 to 28 weeks' gestation, with high RNT and up to moderate anxiety, recruited via antenatal clinics or self-referral.
INTERVENTION: Participants were randomized to the self-led digital intervention (RELAX plus UC), involving twelve 17-minute sessions over 4 weeks, or to UC.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Assessments took place at baseline before randomization (T0) and 4 weeks (T1), 8 weeks (T2), and 36 weeks (T3; 12-24 weeks after birth) after randomization. The primary outcome was anxiety, as assessed by the 7-item Generalized Anxiety Disorder scale (GAD-7) at T2 and as a secondary outcome at T3. Secondary outcomes included RNT (assessed by the 10-item trait version of the Repetitive Thinking Questionnaire [RTQ-10]), depression (general and perinatal, assessed by the Patient Health Questionnaire-9 [PHQ-9] and Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale [EPDS]), perinatal anxiety (assessed by the Perinatal Anxiety Screening Scale [PASS]), worry (assessed by the Penn State Worry Questionnaire [PSWQ]), and functioning (assessed by the Work and Social Adjustment Scale [WSAS]). Interpretation bias at T1 was the hypothesized mechanism. Analysis was performed using a modified intention-to-treat approach.
RESULTS: A total of 268 participants were randomized (mean [SD] age 33.7 [3.9] years; 174 [64.9%] married). Anxiety was significantly lower for RELAX participants vs UC (mean GAD-7 difference, -1.5; 95% CI, -2.4 to -0.6; P = .001). Depression (mean PHQ-9 difference, -0.8; 95% CI -1.5 to -0.1; and mean EPDS difference, -1.1; 95% CI, -2.0 to -0.2), RNT (mean RTQ-10 difference, -2.7; 95% CI, -4.5 to -0.9), worry (mean PSWQ difference, -3.6; 95%…

articles.title: Generative Artificial Intelligence and Maternal Health Outcomes in Pregnant and Postpartum Individuals: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.authors: Norell EM, Yue X, Mane H et al.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) chatbots are increasingly used to support maternal health, but randomized evidence is limited.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate whether access to a generative AI maternal health chatbot improved 12-month maternal health outcomes.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This 2-group randomized clinical trial enrolled 400 participants from October 2023 to December 2024, with 12-month follow-up completed in December 2025. Participants were recruited online across 49 US states and the District of Columbia. Eligible participants were English-speaking, aged 14 years or older, pregnant or parenting an infant younger than 6 months, and self-identified as members of racial and/or ethnic minoritized groups.
INTERVENTIONS: Participants were randomized 1:1 to receive access to the chatbot or an active control consisting of monthly children's books.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Primary outcomes were anxiety and depression symptoms at 12 months measured using the Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7 and Patient Health Questionnaire-9. Secondary outcomes included emergency department visits, pregnancy-related complications, postpartum care checkups, effective contraception use, and sleep duration.
RESULTS: Among 400 randomized participants, the mean (SD) age was 32.6 (5.1) years; 200 (50%) were parenting an infant at enrollment; and 10 (2%) identified as American Indian or Alaska Native, 80 (20%) Asian, 188 (47%) Black or African American, 57 (14%) multiracial, and 65 (16%) Hispanic or Latino. The AI chatbot was not associated with differences in anxiety scores (adjusted mean difference, 0.10; 95% CI, -0.77 to 0.96) or depression scores (adjusted mean difference, -0.23; 95% CI, -1.05 to 0.59), nor with emergency department visits, postpartum care, contraception use, or sleep duration. Among participants pregnant at enrollment, the chatbot was associated with more self-reported pregnancy-related complications in the secondary 12-month end point analysis, but not in longitudinal analyses. Higher chatbot engagement was associated with longer sleep duration and higher anxiety scores in exploratory within-group analyses.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this randomized clinical trial of pregnant and postpartum individuals from racial and ethnic minoritized groups, access to a generative artificial intelligence maternal health chatbot did not improve maternal anxiety or depression at 12 months compared with an active control. Secondary and…

articles.title: Gestational Age- and Altitude-Specific Hemoglobin Thresholds and Candidate Windows for Preterm Birth.
articles.authors: Yan G, Ning X, Chen X et al.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Maternal hemoglobin is a clinically accessible biomarker of preterm birth (PTB) risk, but abnormal thresholds are inconsistent and do not account for variation by gestational age or altitude.
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the association between maternal hemoglobin concentration and PTB across gestational ages and altitudes, including PTB subtype, and to define gestational age-specific, altitude-adapted hemoglobin thresholds and assessment windows.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This multicenter, retrospective cohort study used a multisource database integrating electronic medical records, preconception examination, and geospatial data from 5 medical centers in Yunnan, China, a region with a marked altitudinal gradient, and consecutively included singleton pregnancies delivered between January 1, 2017, and July 31, 2025.
EXPOSURE: Prepregnancy and prenatal hemoglobin values were assessed. Prenatal measurements were grouped into 2-week intervals (target gestational week ±7 days), with 36 weeks analyzed separately.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Preterm birth was operationally defined as live birth from 28 weeks 0 days through 36 weeks 6 days of gestation.
RESULTS: Of 141 943 singleton live births among women (mean [SD] maternal age, 29.7 [4.6] years), 12 607 (8.88%) were PTBs. Maternal hemoglobin measurement showed a gestational age-dependent U-shaped association with PTB, and thresholds varied across gestation. Compared with the intermediate group, a low hemoglobin concentration measured at 13 weeks (<12.00 g/dL; adjusted odds ratio [AOR], 1.46; 95% CI, 1.17-1.80) was associated with PTB, persisting from 27 weeks onward (<11.00 g/dL; AOR, 1.48; 95% CI, 1.25-1.74). A high hemoglobin concentration from 19 weeks onward was associated with PTB (>13.50 g/dL; AOR, 1.28; 95% CI, 1.04-1.55). At high altitude, thresholds were generally higher, and a low hemoglobin concentration from 21 weeks was persistently associated with PTB. Subtype analyses showed earlier low hemoglobin concentration associations for medically indicated PTB and middle- to late-pregnancy high hemoglobin concentration associations for both subtypes.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this cohort study, hemoglobin thresholds associated with PTB varied across gestation and were generally higher at high altitude; low- and high-hemoglobin assessment windows differed and varied by altitude. These findings may help refine gestational age- and altitude-specific interpretation of routine hemoglobin…

articles.title: A DPY19L2/FAM209-associated protein-Arp complex-CAPZA3 scaffold is essential for perinuclear theca assembly and fertilization.
articles.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
articles.ta: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
articles.authors: Ruan T, Shen G, Zhuo L et al.
articles.abstract: Fertilization is a fundamental biological process that enables the fusion of a spermatozoon with an oocyte to initiate embryonic development. However, the underlying mechanisms leading to fertilization failure remain poorly understood. Here, we demonstrated that the actin-related protein (Arp) family members ACTRT2 and ACTRT3 are essential for fertilization in both humans and mice, whereas ACTL10 is dispensable for fertility and the human-specific ACTL8 may play a role in early spermatogenesis. Ultrastructural and immunofluorescence analyses revealed that, during spermatogenesis, ACTRT2 or ACTRT3 deficiency disrupts the assembly of subacrosomal layer of the perinuclear theca (SAL-PT), leading to acrosome detachment and subsequent manchette abnormalities, which in turn impairs the formation of the postacrosomal sheath of the PT. These structural defects were accompanied by reduced abundance of the candidate sperm-borne oocyte-activating factors PAWP and PLCζ. Moreover, knockout of Actrt2 or Actrt3 severely impaired spermatozoa's ability to penetrate the zona pellucida during in vitro fertilization. Mechanistically, ACTRT2, ACTRT3, ACTL7A, ACTL7B, and ACTL9 form a testis-enriched Arp complex in the SAL-PT and maintain the stability of one another. This complex interacts with the PT protein CAPZA3, which subsequently binds and stabilizes PLCζ. Additionally, the Arp complex interacts with DPY19L2/FAM209-associated proteins to mediate acrosome anchoring to the nuclear envelope. Therefore, these findings established a sequential DPY19L2/FAM209-associated protein-Arp complex-CAPZA3 scaffold extending from the nuclear envelope to the acrosome that is indispensable for fertilization. Collectively, we defined a previously unidentified structural and molecular framework for fertilization and provided insights into the diagnosis and treatment of fertilization failure.

articles.title: Neuropharmacological effects of Salvia officinalis: molecular mechanisms, preclinical evidence, and clinical potential.
articles.authors: Sabet AZ, Ahmadnia H, Shahsavari K et al.
articles.abstract: Salvia officinalis (sage), a cornerstone of traditional medicine, has attracted significant scientific interest for its neuroprotective benefits. This review synthesizes evidence on the molecular and cellular mechanisms underlying its potential therapeutic efficacy, which are attributed to bioactive compounds including phenolic acids (rosmarinic and caffeic acid), flavonoids, and terpenoids. Six key mechanisms have been identified. First, S. officinalis enhances cholinergic activity by inhibiting acetylcholinesterase and butyrylcholinesterase, directly counteracting cognitive deficits in Alzheimer's disease. Second, it exerts significant antioxidant effects by neutralizing free radicals, upregulating catalase and superoxide dismutase, and reducing lipid peroxidation. Third, anti-inflammatory actions involve suppressing pro-inflammatory cytokines (TNF-α, IL-1β, IL-6) and inhibiting COX-2/PGE2 pathways. Fourth, S. officinalis modulates neurotrophic factors, upregulating BDNF and GDNF to support neuronal survival and synaptic plasticity. Fifth, it interacts with neurotransmitter systems-activating opioid receptors for analgesia, enhancing GABAergic activity for anxiolytic and anticonvulsant effects, and influencing serotonergic and adrenergic pathways for mood regulation. Sixth, it may reduce amyloid-beta aggregation and reduces tau hyperphosphorylation. Additionally, phytoestrogenic components may contribute to benefits against cognitive decline and mood disorders during menopause. By integrating findings from in vitro, in vivo, and clinical studies, this review provides a comprehensive overview of S. officinalis as a promising multi-target therapeutic agent for neurological and neuropsychiatric conditions, highlighting its potential as a natural alternative or complement to conventional pharmacotherapies in managing complex brain disorders.

articles.title: Evaluating the Cross-sectional Temporal Trends, Diagnostic and Clinical Relevance of Cell Free DNA in Acute Myocardial Infarction.
articles.authors: Mahajan B, Dar GM, Dash M et al.
articles.abstract: Circulating cell-free DNA (cfDNA) has emerged as a potential biomarker for cardiovascular injury, yet its clinical relevance in acute myocardial infarction (AMI) remains underexplored. cfDNA from 107 AMI patients and 32 healthy controls were isolated and its associations with clinical, demographic and biochemical profiling were explored. Patients were stratified by chest pain duration (0-24 h) to assess cross-sectional temporal trends. cfDNA levels showed six-fold elevation in AMI patients compared to controls and were associated with adverse cardiometabolic and lifestyle risk factors. cfDNA levels increased progressively with chest pain duration, peaking for 18-24 h (median:55.31 ng/mL), and strongly correlated with hs-cTnT (rho = 0.535) and NT-proBNP (rho = 0.615) during this phase. Overall diagnostic performance of cfDNA was good (AUC = 0.858), which further improved in late-phase AMI (AUC = 0.904). Strong diagnostic performance of cfDNA, particularly in the late phase AMI, suggests its potential as a complementary tool to existing cardiac biomarkers.

articles.title: Oocyte yield according to initiation timing in random-start controlled ovarian hyperstimulation.
articles.journal: Journal of assisted reproduction and genetics
articles.authors: Yoon SY, Choi J, Kim SE et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Random-start controlled ovarian hyperstimulation (COH) is an established strategy for fertility preservation (FP) in cancer patients. Although previous studies have demonstrated its efficacy using a binary classification of menstrual cycle phases (follicular vs. luteal), this approach might not fully reflect dynamic endocrine changes throughout the cycle. This study used a subdivided phase classification to evaluate the ovarian response according to the menstrual cycle phase at random-start COH initiation and further assessed the outcomes according to the ovarian reserve.
METHODS: This retrospective study included 255 cancer patients who underwent random-start COH. Patients were categorized into five menstrual cycle phases at the time of stimulation initiation: early follicular (EF), late follicular (LF), early luteal (EL), mid-luteal (ML), and late luteal (LL). Oocyte yield, total gonadotropin dose, and stimulation duration were compared among groups. A subgroup analysis was conducted in patients with low ovarian reserve (anti-Müllerian hormone [AMH] < 1.2 ng/mL).
RESULTS: Total oocyte yield was significantly higher in the LL group than in the EF group, though with a greater total gonadotropin dose and longer stimulation duration. Among patients with low ovarian reserve, luteal phase initiation was associated with significantly higher total and mature metaphase II (MII) oocyte counts compared with follicular phase initiation.
CONCLUSIONS: The menstrual cycle phase at stimulation initiation influences ovarian response during random-start COH. The LL phase represents an effective window for stimulation initiation, and luteal phase initiation is particularly advantageous for maximizing oocyte yield in patients with low ovarian reserve who require urgent FP.

articles.title: Association of anti-Müllerian hormone and antral follicle count discordance with embryological and pregnancy outcomes in the first IVF/ICSI cycle.
articles.journal: Journal of assisted reproduction and genetics
articles.authors: Wu Y, Cai J, Xu M et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To investigate the associations of anti-Müllerian hormone (AMH) and antral follicle count (AFC) concordance/discordance patterns with embryological and pregnancy outcomes among patients undergoing their first in vitro fertilization (IVF)/intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI) cycle.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 6456 patients undergoing their first IVF/ICSI cycle between January 2018 and January 2024. Patients were classified into the concordant normal group (AMH ≥ 1.2 ng/mL and AFC ≥ 5), the concordant reduced group (AMH < 1.2 ng/mL and AFC < 5), and the discordant group (AMH-normal/AFC-reduced: AMH ≥ 1.2 ng/mL with AFC < 5 or AMH-reduced/AFC-normal: AMH < 1.2 ng/mL with AFC ≥ 5). Regression models were used to evaluate their embryological and pregnancy outcomes.
RESULTS: Among 6456 patients, 816 (12.64%) exhibited AMH-AFC discordance. Compared with the concordant normal group, the discordant group had lower adjusted numbers of retrieved oocytes (β =  - 4.04, 95% CI - 4.44 to - 3.65), MII oocytes (β =  - 3.46, 95% CI - 3.83 to - 3.10), 2PN zygotes (β =  - 2.57, 95% CI - 2.87 to - 2.26), transferable embryos (β =  - 2.23, 95% CI - 2.52 to - 1.95), and high-quality embryos (β =  - 1.73, 95% CI - 1.98 to - 1.47) (all P < 0.001). No significant differences in these outcomes remained between the discordant and concordant reduced groups after adjustment. Among the 6188 patients who underwent their first embryo transfer, pregnancy outcomes did not differ significantly between the discordant and concordant normal groups, whereas the discordant group had higher adjusted odds of biochemical pregnancy (OR = 1.38, 95% CI 1.03-1.86, P = 0.031) and live birth (OR = 1.40, 95% CI 1.01-1.95, P = 0.042) than the concordant reduced group. Within the discordant group, the AMH-normal/AFC-reduced subgroup had higher oocyte and embryo yields, but their pregnancy outcomes were comparable.
CONCLUSION: AMH-AFC discordance was associated with lower ovarian response and embryo yield than concordant normal ovarian reserve. Among discordant patients, normal AMH with reduced AFC was associated with higher oocyte and embryo yields. The discordant group had modestly higher odds of biochemical pregnancy and live birth than the concordant reduced group, whereas pregnancy outcomes were otherwise broadly comparable across AMH-AFC patterns.

articles.title: Gossypetin and luteolin, alone and with cisplatin, preferentially reduce MCF-7 breast cancer cell viability, whereas HeLa cervical cancer cells are refractory.
articles.authors: Candan E, Ülker Z
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Dietary flavonoids have been proposed as partners for platinum chemotherapy, but their effects vary between tumour types, and sparing of normal cells has to be demonstrated. We examined gossypetin and luteolin, alone and combined with cisplatin, in MCF-7 breast and HeLa cervical carcinoma cells and in non-tumorigenic L929 fibroblasts.
METHODS AND RESULTS: Cells were exposed to 100 µg/mL cisplatin (CP), gossypetin (GOS), luteolin (LUT) or their double and triple combinations. Viability was measured by MTT assay (technical triplicates, one experiment), combination effects by Bliss independence, Bax, Bcl-2 and CASP3 transcripts by RT-PCR (2-ΔΔCt), and phosphatidylserine exposure by Annexin V-Cy3 staining of archived micrographs. At 48 h, six of the seven treatments reduced MCF-7 viability (61.8-85.0% of control; Tukey-adjusted p ≤ 0.018), gossypetin being the most active. Cisplatin plus luteolin exceeded the Bliss expectation in MCF-7 at 24 h (excess + 0.11), whereas all combinations were less than additive at 48 h. No treatment reduced HeLa viability, and HeLa cells showed Bcl-2 induction (1.9-30.2-fold) with Bax repression (Bax/Bcl-2 ratio 0.03-0.21). L929 viability was not reduced at either time point, and the archived L929 field showed no Annexin V labelling.
CONCLUSIONS: At this single concentration, gossypetin- and luteolin-based treatments reduced MCF-7 viability without reducing L929 viability, while HeLa cells were refractory at the viability and transcript levels. These retrospective data support dose-response and protein-level studies rather than mechanistic conclusions.

articles.title: Deciphering intratumoral heterogeneity: An interpretable radiopathologic framework for lymph node staging in early-stage cervical cancer.
articles.authors: Chen J, Shi Y, Song Y et al.
articles.abstract: Preoperative assessment of lymph node metastasis (LNM) informs treatment planning in early-stage cervical cancer (CC). Traditional radiomics (TR) may obscure intratumoral heterogeneity. We developed multiparametric MRI habitat radiomics (HR) for LNM prediction and explored its histopathologic context. Patients underwent radical surgery and lymphadenectomy. Part I comprised 148 training and 63 test patients; Part II comprised 14 for spatially matched histopathology. Intratumoral voxels were clustered into habitats by K-means using T2-weighted imaging (T2WI), diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI), and contrast-enhanced T1-weighted imaging (CE-T1WI) signals. The number of habitats was selected using validation AUC. HR/TR scores and clinical-radiological predictors were integrated by logistic regression. AUC and accuracy were compared by DeLong's and χ² tests. Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) assessed contributions. Subregion-matched histopathology quantified Ki-67, CD3, CD31, and tumor-stroma ratio (TSR). LNM prevalence was 27.1% (61/225). The four-habitat HR model achieved a test AUC of 0.841 with 14 DWI/CE-T1WI-derived features. Test AUCs for clinical model (CL), TR, and HR + CL were 0.804, 0.784, and 0.890. HR + TR+CL achieved the highest AUC (0.902) and accuracy (87.30%), without a significant AUC difference from HR + CL (P = 0.277). SHAP ranked HR score above clinical lymph-node status, tumor diameter, and TR score. HR-3 exhibited highest Ki67 and lowest TSR, CD3, and CD31; HR-1 had highest TSR and lowest Ki67; HR-2 showed higher CD31 than HR-4. MRI-based HR may support preoperative LNM assessment in early-stage CC, with HR + CL representing a parsimonious candidate model for further evaluation. Spatially matched exploratory histopathology suggests possible regional tissue differences across MRI-defined habitats.

articles.title: Osteoclastogenesis associated gene signatures in postmenopausal low bone mineral density: cross-dataset transcriptomics and whole-blood validation.
articles.authors: Anbreen N, Iqbal MJ, Wahab H et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Osteoporosis is characterized by reduced bone mass and increased fracture risk, yet minimally invasive molecular correlates of postmenopausal low bone mineral density remain limited.
METHODS: We independently reanalysed two human osteoclastogenesis RNA-seq datasets, GSE225974 and GSE246769, using differential-expression, Gene Ontology, KEGG, Hallmark gene set enrichment, and cross-dataset concordance analyses. Six candidate genes, LGALSL, FAXDC2, DHCR7, MYL9, RHOC, and ITGB5, were subsequently evaluated by RT-qPCR in whole blood from 100 postmenopausal women with normal bone mineral density (n=30), osteopenia (n=30), or osteoporosis (n=40).
RESULTS: Across the two RNA-seq datasets, 1,782 differentially expressed genes were shared, including 1,240 concordantly upregulated and 385 concordantly downregulated genes, with strong cross-dataset effect-size correlation (r=0.74). GO and KEGG analyses identified replicated sterol/lipid, skeletal-development, adhesion/integrin, and actin-cytoskeletal programs, while Hallmark GSEA identified 22 concordantly enriched gene sets, including oxidative phosphorylation, fatty-acid metabolism, and cholesterol homeostasis. BMD was positively correlated with calcium intake and physical activity. Conversely, deteriorating bone health was positively associated with high cholesterol, low BMI, early menopause. All six candidate genes were significantly and concordantly upregulated during osteoclastogenesis in both datasets. Whole-blood RT-qPCR analysis demonstrated progressively higher relative expression across normal-BMD, osteopenia, and osteoporosis groups for all six candidates. Expression analysis from the serum validated LGALSL, RHOC, MYL9 and ITGB5 elevated expression in osteoporosis cases.
CONCLUSION: These findings identify reproducible osteoclastogenesis-associated transcriptional programs and support the six candidate genes as candidate signature correlating with the postmenopausal BMD status.

articles.title: Urodynamic parameters of urethral sphincter function in men: methodology, age-related changes, and the impact of radical prostatectomy.
articles.authors: Tawanaie Pour Sedehi N, Dieffenbacher S, Buse S et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: The external urethral sphincter operates across three partly independent functional dimensions: maximum urethral pressure (MUP) at rest, voluntary sphincter contraction pressure (VSCP), and sustained voluntary contraction. Resting urethral pressure profilometry does not by itself quantify voluntary contraction pressure or sustained contractile output. This study presents a standardised measurement protocol combining these measures and compares them between non-operated men and patients with post-prostatectomy incontinence (PPI), adjusted for age.
METHODS: This prospective cross-sectional study included 101 men (46 PPI, 55 controls). Urethral pressure was measured using an air-charged triple-lumen T-Doc catheter positioned at the point of maximum urethral pressure. Parameters recorded were MUP at rest, VSCP (mean of three 1-second maximal voluntary contractions), and sustained contraction over 10 s expressed as area under the pressure-time curve (AUC, cm H₂O·s). A normalised endurance index (AUC/ MUP at rest) was calculated. Group comparisons used Welch's t-test; linear regression with a group × age interaction adjusted for age.
RESULTS: PPI patients were older than controls (72.9 ± 8.5 vs. 67.5 ± 10.1 years; p = 0.004). Compared with controls, PPI patients had lower MUP at rest (p = 3.3 × 10⁻⁴), lower VSCP (p = 4.0 × 10⁻⁴), and lower 10-s AUC (p = 2.0 × 10⁻⁶), whereas normalised endurance did not differ significantly (p = 0.110). Age-adjusted analyses confirmed significant group effects for the three absolute parameters without evidence of group × age interaction.
CONCLUSION: A single standardised urodynamic protocol quantifies three clinically relevant dimensions of male urethral sphincter function. In men with PPI, absolute sphincter function is reduced independent of age, whereas relative endurance is preserved.

articles.title: Associations between neurodevelopmental traits and perinatal depression: a prospective study in Japanese women.
articles.authors: Hasegawa K, Sasayama D, Honda H et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: This study examined how attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) and autism spectrum disorder (ASD) traits relate to depressive symptoms from late pregnancy through early postpartum in Japanese women, alongside perinatal factors.
METHODS: In a multicenter prospective study, 1,104 women completed questionnaires at late pregnancy (T1), 2 weeks postpartum (T2), and 1 month postpartum (T3). Depressive symptoms were assessed using the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS), ADHD traits with the Adult ADHD Self-Report Scale (ASRS), and ASD traits with the Autism Spectrum Quotient (AQ). Chi-square tests evaluated timepoint-specific associations, multivariable logistic regression identified independent predictors of EPDS positivity at T2, and a linear mixed-effects model assessed longitudinal changes.
RESULTS: EPDS scores and EPDS positivity were highest at T1 and declined postpartum (16.7%, 8.6%, 4.0%). Scores were correlated across timepoints. In univariate analyses, antenatal EPDS positivity showed associations with ASD traits (AQ+: OR = 6.08, 95% CI 2.17-16.99) and ADHD traits (ASRS+: OR = 4.86, 95% CI 3.06-7.72). In multivariable analysis, independent predictors of EPDS positivity at T2 included ADHD traits (OR = 1.37, 95% CI 1.13-1.66), primiparity, psychiatric treatment history, and antenatal EPDS scores. ASD traits were not associated with T2 EPDS positivity after adjustment for antenatal EPDS scores. In the mixed-effects model, both ADHD and ASD traits were associated with higher EPDS scores during pregnancy, with attenuated effects postpartum.
CONCLUSION: Neurodevelopmental traits are associated with perinatal mental health, and trait- and timing-informed support may enhance maternal psychological stability and caregiving outcomes.

articles.title: Gamma-sitosterol and male reproductive health: mechanistic insights, preclinical evidence, and clinical research gaps.
articles.authors: Ikuomola EO, Shehu UU, Ismahil AA et al.
articles.abstract: Male infertility affects approximately 7% of the global male population and remains a significant public health concern. Gamma-sitosterol, a plant-derived phytosterol abundant in saw palmetto, pumpkin seeds, and other botanical sources, has attracted increasing interest because of its antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and hormone-modulating properties that may improve male reproductive function. This narrative review synthesized current evidence on the mechanistic basis, preclinical efficacy, clinical evidence, and safety profile of gamma-sitosterol in male reproductive health. A structured literature search, informed by PRISMA reporting principles, was conducted in PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Google Scholar from database inception to December 2025. Of 1,247 records identified, 96 studies met the inclusion criteria and were included in the narrative synthesis. Direct preclinical evidence for purified γ-sitosterol in male reproductive models remains limited. Available reproductive evidence is derived predominantly from γ-sitosterol-containing plant extracts and studies of β-sitosterol, a close structural analogue, which report improvements in sperm parameters, testicular histology, oxidative stress, and reproductive outcomes. These findings support biological plausibility but cannot be attributed directly to purified γ-sitosterol. Dose-response evidence for purified γ-sitosterol remains insufficient to establish an optimal therapeutic dose. Clinical evidence also remains scarce, with no randomized controlled trials evaluating purified γ-sitosterol monotherapy in infertile men. Available human studies have primarily assessed multi-herbal formulations, limiting attribution of observed effects to gamma-sitosterol alone. Overall, γ-sitosterol remains a potential candidate for further investigation in male reproductive health; however, the limited direct evidence from purified γ-sitosterol prevents firm conclusions regarding its reproductive efficacy. Studies using purified γ-sitosterol, followed by adequately powered clinical trials, are required before its therapeutic role can be established.

articles.title: Diagnostic utility of body fat distribution parameters in distinguishing osteosarcopenia from osteoporosis or sarcopenia alone in postmenopausal women: a retrospective cross-sectional study.
articles.authors: Hong J, Chen B, Li H et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The occurrence of osteosarcopenia is usually accompanied by changes in body fat distribution (BFD). However, it is still unclear whether there are differences in the BFD patterns of individuals with osteosarcopenia compared to those with osteoporosis or sarcopenia alone.
AIMS: This study aims to evaluate the feasibility of BFD parameters as an auxiliary assessment tool for osteosarcopenia in postmenopausal women.
METHODS: In this retrospective cross-sectional study, 342 postmenopausal women who underwent musculoskeletal function assessments in our hospital between January 2015 and December 2022 were enrolled. Osteoporosis was diagnosed according to the World Health Organization criteria, whereas sarcopenia was diagnosed according to the 2019 consensus of the Asian Working Group for Sarcopenia.
RESULTS: After adjusting for confounding covariates, BFD parameters showed no significant independent association with bone mineral density (BMD), but were consistently associated with muscle mass and strength indicators. Compared with the osteosarcopenia group, participants in the osteoporosis alone group had significantly higher Android fat levels (odds ratio [OR]: 1.728, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.118-2.670), while participants in the sarcopenia alone group had significantly lower trunk-to-total body fat ratio and appendicular-to-trunk fat ratio (OR: 0.333, 95% CI: 0.132-0.842, and OR: 0.737, 95% CI: 0.573-0.948; respectively). The diagnostic panels containing Android fat demonstrated high accuracy in distinguishing osteosarcopenia from osteoporosis alone (area under the curve [AUC] values > 0.9). The diagnostic panels containing trunk-to-total body fat ratio and appendicular-to-trunk fat ratio exhibited moderate diagnostic accuracy in differentiating osteosarcopenia from sarcopenia alone (AUC values > 0.7).
CONCLUSIONS: Distinct BFD patterns are associated with different musculoskeletal phenotypes in postmenopausal women, with parameters more closely linked to muscle measures than to BMD. Specific fat distribution indicators correlate with osteosarcopenia, and these exploratory diagnostic panels provide preliminary reference value for differential diagnosis, while external validation in independent cohorts is required before clinical application.

articles.title: Time trends in ovarian pregnancy: a 5-decade experience from a single medical center.
articles.authors: Melcer Y, Maymon R, Levin A et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Despite diagnostic advancements, ovarian pregnancy remains rare and challenging to detect preoperatively. This study examines 5 decades of trends, clinical features, and surgical outcomes in a single tertiary care center.
METHODS: A retrospective review was conducted of 59 women with primary ovarian pregnancy treated between 1971 and 2025, categorized into four periods: 1971-1989 (n = 20), 1990-2001 (n = 19), 2002-2013 (n = 7), and 2014-2025 (n = 13). Long-term fertility outcomes were assessed using updated institutional medical records supplemented by telephone contact when patients were reachable.
RESULTS: Among 317,015 deliveries, 4357 ectopic pregnancies (1.4%) were diagnosed, including 59 ovarian pregnancies (1.4% of all ectopic pregnancies). The overall ectopic pregnancy rate increased across the study periods, whereas the ovarian pregnancy rate per delivery decreased. Poisson regression confirmed a significant temporal increase in the overall ectopic pregnancy rate (p < 0.001) and a significant temporal decrease in the ovarian pregnancy rate per delivery (p = 0.007). Hemodynamic shock differed across the study periods (p = 0.003), but no significant monotonic temporal trend was observed (Cochran-Armitage test, p = 0.515). IUD use demonstrated a significant decreasing trend, from 90 to 15.4% (Cochran-Armitage test, p < 0.001). Preoperative ultrasound diagnosis remained uncommon, occurring in only 2 of 13 cases (15.4%) in the final period, although an increasing trend was observed (Cochran-Armitage test, p = 0.024). Long-term follow-up revealed that among 37 women attempting conception after ovarian pregnancy, 27 (72.9%) achieved spontaneous intrauterine pregnancy.
CONCLUSION: Despite advances in imaging, preoperative diagnosis of ovarian pregnancy remains uncommon in routine emergency settings. Increased awareness of characteristic ultrasound findings and timely surgical management may improve clinical outcomes and reduce severe hemorrhagic complications. Over 5 decades, improvements in surgical management were associated with reduced blood transfusion requirements and shorter hospitalization, while hemodynamic instability varied across study periods without demonstrating a significant monotonic temporal trend.

articles.title: Highly polar pesticides and their metabolites in diverse foods including tea: analytical methods with LC-MS/MS and risk assessment.
articles.journal: Analytical methods : advancing methods and applications
articles.authors: Lin S, Yang H, Xu Y et al.
articles.abstract: To address growing safety concerns over highly polar pesticide residues in agricultural products, this study developed an efficient method for the simultaneous determination of glyphosate, glufosinate-ammonium, ethephon, and their key metabolites (AMPA, N-acetyl AMPA, N-acetyl glyphosate, N-methyl glyphosate, MPPA, and N-acetyl glufosinate) in thirteen food matrices using a novel ion chromatography column coupled with LC-MS/MS. Sample preparation employs pure water as the sole extraction solvent, followed by Oasis HLB SPE cleanup, thus completely eliminating organic reagents throughout the entire procedure. The method was fully validated across representative matrices, including vegetables, fruits, edible fungi, sugarcane, tea, and spices, showing excellent linearity (R > 0.992), acceptable recoveries (81.3-125.5%), and intra- and inter-day relative standard deviations (RSDs) ≤ 15%. The limit of quantification (LOQ) was 0.05 mg kg-1 for all analytes, meeting the maximum residue limits established by Codex Alimentarius and national regulatory bodies. Application to tea infusion analysis revealed that the first brew removed 56.5-99.2% of the total residues from dry tea, and a subsequent worst-case dietary risk assessment indicated that the resulting risk quotients were orders of magnitude below 1, implying negligible health risks. This sustainable method not only provides reliable technical support for routine monitoring and food safety assurance but also provides scientific evidence supporting the practice of discarding the first tea infusion as an effective risk-reduction measure.

articles.title: Structure-Dependent Chemical Order Modification in Strained Alloy Nanoparticles.
articles.authors: Wang Y, Chen Z, Toulkeridou E et al.
articles.abstract: Alloy nanoparticles (nanoalloys) exhibit tunable physicochemical properties that depend sensitively on atomic arrangement. While most theoretical studies consider nanoalloys in a vacuum, practical systems are typically supported, where strong cluster-substrate interactions can introduce significant lattice strain. Here, we investigate strain as a control parameter for chemical ordering in bimetallic nanoalloys using atomistic simulations. Imposing controlled strain through an implicit anchored interface, we probe the response of NiPt nanoparticles with distinct structural motifs. For truncated-octahedral particles, chemical ordering remains remarkably robust even under large strains, indicating that intrinsic thermodynamic preferences dominate. Conversely, icosahedral nanoparticles exhibit pronounced strain-induced chemical redistribution with a significant increase in surface Ni concentration under tensile strain, attributed to the combined effects of intrinsic geometric frustration and a high fraction of undercoordinated sites. Our results demonstrate that strain can selectively modulate chemical ordering in a structure-dependent manner, establishing a general framework for understanding strain-induced chemical ordering in nanoalloys.

articles.title: Women's Experience of Human Papillomavirus Self-Sampling in Cervical Cancer Screening Programs: A Scoping Review.
articles.authors: Holst CG, Nørgaard B, Marcussen M
articles.abstract: This study aimed to map, identify, and synthesize women's experiences with human papillomavirus (HPV) self-sampling in cervical cancer screening programs. The study was conducted as a scoping review, reported in accordance with PRISMA-ScR. Studies involving women of all nationalities who had been offered HPV self-sampling were included, of any qualitative study design, and published at any date in either English or a Scandinavian language. Systematic searches were conducted in the PubMed, CINAHL, PsycInfo, and EMBASE databases in May 2023, in September 2024, and in August 2025. Data were systematically charted by study characteristics, and the main findings were reported narratively. A total of 25 studies reporting qualitative or mixed methods were included. The synthesis resulted in three themes generated from the women's perspective: Women's perceptions of HPV self-sampling, Women's experiences of health professionals' HPV sampling, and Women's perceptions of community HPV sampling. Women experienced self-sampling to be highly acceptable with feelings of control over their own bodies, comfort in the procedure, and time-saving benefits. Some women experienced a lack of confidence in taking the sample themselves. The experience was influenced by the relationship with health professionals, for example, due to previous traumatic experiences, and by the women's immediate community, for example, relationships with other women or partners.

articles.title: Steroid 5α-reductase 2 and StAR protein expression in ovaries of rats with polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome.
articles.journal: Journal of obstetrics and gynaecology : the journal of the Institute of Obstetrics and Gynaecology
articles.authors: Liu Y, Lin W, Dong L et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS), formerly known as polycystic ovary syndrome, is characterised by hyperandrogenaemia, ovulatory dysfunction, and metabolic disturbances. Steroid 5α-reductase 2 (SRD5A2) converts testosterone to dihydrotestosterone (DHT), a potent androgen receptor agonist. However, the expression profile of SRD5A2 in the ovaries of women with PMOS and its potential contribution to hyperandrogenaemia remain unclear. The aim of this study was to investigate the expression of SRD5A2 and steroidogenic acute regulatory protein (StAR) in the ovaries of a rat PMOS model and to explore their associations with serum hormone levels.
METHODS: Rats were randomly assigned to three groups: PMOS (n = 20), model control (dimethyl sulfoxide [DMSO]; n = 10), and blank control (BC; n = 10). The PMOS model was established via subcutaneous injection of dehydroepiandrosterone. Oestrous cycles were evaluated using vaginal cytology. Serum hormones were quantified using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay. Protein and mRNA expression levels of SRD5A2 and StAR in ovarian tissues were evaluated using western blotting and reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction, respectively.
RESULTS: Rats in the PMOS group exhibited significantly increased body weight (P < 0.05); disrupted oestrous cycles; and significantly elevated serum levels of anti-Müllerian hormone, testosterone, luteinising hormone (LH), and LH/follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) ratio (P < 0.05). The protein and mRNA levels of SRD5A2 and StAR were significantly upregulated in the ovaries of the PMOS group compared with those of the BC and DMSO groups (P < 0.05). Ovarian volume and weight were similar among the groups, with no significant differences (P > 0.05).
CONCLUSIONS: SRD5A2 and StAR are highly expressed in the ovaries of rats with PMOS and are associated with hyperandrogenaemia and elevated LH secretion. These findings indicate that SRD5A2 and StAR may contribute to PMOS pathogenesis, although further studies are required to establish causality.

articles.title: Contemporary Management of Vesicouterine Fistula.
articles.authors: Bayrak O, Baturu M, Kirac M et al.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Vesicouterine fistula (VUF) is an uncommon complication that predominantly occurs after cesarean delivery. Current evidence regarding its diagnosis and management is limited and largely derived from small retrospective studies.
OBJECTIVE: The objective was to evaluate the etiological factors, clinical characteristics, diagnostic approaches, and surgical outcomes associated with VUF through a systematic review and proportional meta-analysis.
STUDY DESIGN: This systematic review and proportional meta-analysis was carried out following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines. A comprehensive search of PubMed/MEDLINE and Web of Science databases identified studies published between 2006 and 2026. Studies including at least 8 patients with VUF and reporting clinical or surgical outcomes were eligible. Pooled prevalence estimates with 95% CIs were calculated using random-effects models.
RESULTS: Eight retrospective studies involving 447 patients were included. Cesarean delivery was the predominant etiological factor (pooled proportion, 95.3%), while a history of repeat cesarean delivery was identified in 78.4% of patients. Cyclic hematuria represented the most characteristic symptom. Cystoscopy was the most frequently used diagnostic modality. Surgical treatment demonstrated a pooled success rate of 97.1%, with low recurrence and postoperative complication rates of 4.3% and 5.6%, respectively. Open abdominal repair remained the most common surgical approach, although minimally invasive surgery was increasingly reported.
CONCLUSIONS: Vesicouterine fistula has evolved into a predominantly cesarean delivery-related iatrogenic condition with diverse clinical manifestations. Surgical repair provides excellent outcomes with low recurrence when appropriate reconstructive principles are followed. Although the pooled surgical success rate of 97.1% is impressive, this estimate is derived entirely from retrospective observational studies, several of which are small case series. Minimally invasive surgery is a feasible option in selected patients, but comparative evidence is insufficient to determine whether it improves perioperative or long-term outcomes relative to open abdominal repair.

articles.title: Design, Synthesis, Molecular Docking, and Anticancer Activity Evaluation of Chalcone Derivatives as HDAC6 Inhibitors.
articles.authors: Yu M, Zhan Y, Liu Y et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Histone deacetylase 6 (HDAC6) is a pivotal regulator of multiple cellular pathways in tumors, thereby rendering HDAC6 a potential target for anticancer therapy.
METHODS: A series of HDAC6 inhibitors containing chalcone scaffolds was designed based on the principle of molecular hybridization. The antiproliferative activities of K562 and SiHa cells were assessed using the Cell Counting Kit-8 (CCK-8) assay. Fluorogenic assay kits were used to evaluate the enzyme activities of HDAC1 and HDAC6 in vitro. Western blot analysis was employed to assess the acetylation levels of α-tubulin (Ac-α-tubulin) and histone H3. Molecular docking was performed to elucidate the binding modes of the compounds with HDAC1 and HDAC6.
RESULTS: In total, 23 novel HDAC6 inhibitors containing a chalcone scaffold were synthesized. Most compounds demonstrated low nanomolar IC50 values against HDAC6, with compound 3v exhibiting the greatest potency, an IC50 value of 4.3 nM and approximately 215-fold selectivity for HDAC6 over HDAC1. All target compounds exhibited strong antiproliferative effects against K562 and SiHa cells, with low micromolar IC50 values. Nonetheless, compound 3v demonstrated strong antiproliferative effects against both cell lines, with IC50 values of 1.16 μM in K562 cells and 1.28 μM in SiHa cells, respectively. In addition, compound 3v significantly upregulated the level of acetylated α-tubulin in K562 cells in a dose-dependent manner. Molecular docking analysis further revealed that compound 3v exhibited a stronger binding affinity for HDAC6 than for HDAC1. Additionally, flow cytometry analysis revealed that compound 3v induced apoptosis and the cell cycle arrest.
CONCLUSIONS: Hydroxamic acid derivatives containing a chalcone fragment are potent HDAC6 inhibitors. These results indicate that chalcone substituents significantly affect enzyme and antiproliferative activities. Further studies are required to evaluate the anticancer potential and safety of these compounds.

articles.title: Advances in Pelvic Floor Muscle Training for Post-Prostatectomy Incontinence: From Isolated Muscle Contractions to Integrated Functional Training.
articles.authors: Yang Q, Yu S, Zheng B et al.
articles.abstract: Post-prostatectomy incontinence (PPI) is a common complication that affects patients' functional recovery and quality of life after radical prostatectomy. Pelvic floor muscle training (PFMT) is widely used as conservative treatment for PPI, but existing programs vary substantially in their target muscles, contraction types, training dose, body positions, and progression criteria. Conventional PFMT first requires patients to correctly identify and voluntarily contract the pelvic floor muscles involved in continence. Sustained contractions train muscular endurance, whereas brief, rapid contractions train rapid recruitment. However, in patients with PPI, urine leakage usually occurs during activities that may increase or rapidly change intra-abdominal pressure, such as coughing, standing up, and walking. This pattern implies that continence during daily activities may depend on more than voluntary pelvic floor muscle contraction. Timely pelvic floor muscle recruitment and coordination with breathing and postural adjustments may be important when intra-abdominal pressure changes. In response to these functional demands, recent studies have incorporated breathing and trunk coordination, progressive postural loading, and task-specific strategies such as the Knack into PFMT. This narrative review focuses on PFMT content and progression while distinguishing training content from training dose, intervention timing, delivery methods, and adjunctive technologies. Some multicomponent programs have reported favorable early- or intermediate-term continence outcomes and changes in pelvic floor muscle function. Comparisons remain difficult due to heterogeneity in interventions, comparator PFMT quality, outcome definitions, and follow-up schedules, and because added components are usually bundled, making their individual contributions hard to separate. No functional approach can therefore be considered universally superior to well-delivered conventional PFMT based on current evidence. We use four conceptual layers to organize the training elements identified in the literature: muscle identification and motor learning, contraction control, coordination and postural-load progression, and functional integration. These domains provide a framework for describing PFMT content rather than a validated clinical sequence.

articles.title: Association of Dyslipidemia With Reproductive Hormone Profiles and Menstrual Regularity in Patients With Polycystic Ovary Syndrome.
articles.journal: British journal of hospital medicine (London, England : 2005)
articles.authors: Shi X, Zhong Y, Zhao Q et al.
articles.abstract:
AIMS/BACKGROUND: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is a common endocrine and metabolic disorder among women of reproductive age, often accompanied by dyslipidemia. However, the direct association between dyslipidemia and reproductive hormone profiles and menstrual regularity remains unclear. This study aimed to retrospectively analyze the association of dyslipidemia with reproductive hormone levels and menstrual regularity in patients with PCOS.
METHODS: This was a single-center retrospective cross-sectional study that included 324 patients with PCOS who visited The First Affiliated Hospital of Soochow University between June 2021 and June 2025. Based on the inclusion and exclusion criteria, 236 patients were ultimately included. Patients were divided into a dyslipidemia group (n = 121) and a eulipidemia group (n = 115) based on their lipid profiles. General demographic data, lipid levels, reproductive hormone levels, and menstrual history were collected. Multiple linear regression was used to examine the independent associations between lipid levels and reproductive hormone levels, whereas multivariate logistic regression was used to examine the relationship between lipid levels and menstrual regularity.
RESULTS: Patients in the dyslipidemia group had significantly higher levels of follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH), luteinizing hormone (LH), and total testosterone (TT) than those in the eulipidemia group (all p < 0.001), significantly lower estradiol (E2) levels (p < 0.001), and a significantly higher incidence of menstrual irregularities (90.08% vs. 43.48%, p < 0.001). Multiple linear regression analysis showed that, after adjusting for age, body mass index (BMI), and homeostasis model assessment of insulin resistance (HOMA-IR), triglycerides (TG) and low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) were independently positively associated with TT, FSH, and LH, whereas high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C) was independently and negatively associated with TT and FSH (all p < 0.001). HDL-C was positively associated with E2, whereas LDL-C was negatively associated with E2; however, these associations did not remain significant after correction for multiple comparisons. TG and LDL-C were independently and negatively associated with sex hormone-binding globulin (SHBG) (all p < 0.01). Multivariate logistic regression analysis showed that TG (OR = 2.126, 95% CI: 1.088-4.156, p = 0.027) and HDL-C (OR = 0.153, 95% CI: 0.052-0.448, p < 0.001) were independently…

articles.title: Effectiveness of Pelvic Floor Muscle Training in Women Soccer Players and Its Relationship With Quality of Life and Pelvic Floor Muscle Strength: A Randomized Controlled Pilot Study.
articles.journal: Journal of strength and conditioning research
articles.authors: Sebastian-Rico JM, Muñoz-Fernández MJ, Martínez-Aranda LM et al.
articles.abstract: Sebastian-Rico, JM, Muñoz-Fernández, MJ, Martínez-Aranda, LM, Calvo-Lluch, Á, and Ortega-Becerra, M. Effectiveness of pelvic floor muscle training in women soccer players and its relationship with quality of life and pelvic floor muscle strength: a randomized controlled pilot study. J Strength Cond Res XX(X): 000-000, 2026-This study investigated the effects of a 6-week pelvic floor muscle training (PFMT) program on muscle strength, function, and the prevalence of related dysfunctions in professional female soccer players using a randomized controlled pilot study design. Twenty nulliparous professional soccer players from the Spanish professional league (2024-2025 season) were randomly assigned to an experimental group (n = 12) or a control group (n = 8). Assessments included anthropometric data, validated questionnaires (International Consultation on Incontinence Questionnaire-Short Form and Broome Pelvic Muscle Self-Efficacy Scale), clinical interviews, and physical examination using the PERFECT method and manometry. The intervention consisted of a 6-week supervised PFMT program (4 sessions/week, 30 minutes each) progressed through 4 phases: education, proprioception, strengthening, and functional integration. Results showed significant group × time interactions for pelvic floor self-efficacy (Broome Pelvic Muscle Self-Efficacy Scale), with scores in the PFMT group increasing by 48.8 and 59.6% (p < 0.05), representing large between-group effect sizes (d = 0.91-1.26). Pelvic floor muscle performance increased by 122.4% in the intervention group (d = 1.25), whereas no meaningful changes were observed in the control group. No adverse events were reported. In conclusion, a 6-week supervised PFMT program is an effective and safe intervention for professional female soccer players, significantly improving muscle function and self-efficacy. These findings support the integration of PFMT for both therapeutic and preventive purposes in elite, high-impact sports environments.

articles.title: MKP1 preserves testicular immune privilege and supports spermiogenesis by suppressing IKKβ/NF-κB/IL-6 signaling in Sertoli cells.
articles.authors: Min Z, Pan Y, Xiong Y et al.
articles.abstract: In brief: The testis maintains an immune-privileged environment to protect developing germ cells. This study reveals that MKP1 in Sertoli cells preserves this privilege by suppressing the IKKβ/NF-κB/IL-6 axis, and its deficiency leads to spermatogenic defects. Abstract: Mitogen-activated protein kinase phosphatase 1 (MKP1) in Sertoli cells has been shown to protect the blood-testis barrier during lipopolysaccharide-induced inflammation, but its role under physiological conditions is unclear. Here, we show that MKP1 knockout mice exhibit subfertility, reduced sperm counts, increased sperm abnormalities, and impaired spermiogenesis. MKP1 deficiency compromises blood-testis barrier integrity, elevates testicular interleukin (IL)-6 expression, and increases serum antisperm antibodies. Mechanistically, MKP1 interacts with IκB kinase β (IKKβ) in Sertoli cells to suppress IKKβ/nuclear factor (NF)-κB signaling and downstream IL-6 expression. Notably, IL-6 inhibition with LMT-28 rescues the spermatogenic defects in MKP1-deficient mice. Collectively, this study establishes that MKP1 in Sertoli cells maintains testicular immune privilege via the IKKβ/NF-κB/IL-6 axis to support spermiogenesis, offering a potential therapeutic target for inflammatory spermatogenic disorders.

articles.title: Advances in Understanding the Mechanisms of Oxidative Stress in Infertile Obese Men.
articles.authors: Xie J, Zhang Y, Sun P et al.
articles.abstract: Obesity-related male infertility has emerged as a significant global health concern, impacting both reproductive ability and overall well-being in men. A critical factor in the pathogenesis of infertility among obese men is oxidative stress, which not only affects reproductive hormone levels, sperm quality, and the function of reproductive organs but also potentially worsens infertility through mechanisms such as inducing inflammatory responses and promoting cell apoptosis. Although there has been some progress in understanding how oxidative stress contributes to obesity-related male infertility, further investigations into its specific biological mechanisms and potential intervention strategies are needed. The aim of this review was to synthesize recent research advances on oxidative stress in the context of obesity-related male infertility, thereby providing a foundation for the development of new therapeutic approaches.

articles.title: The Role of miRNAs in Regulating Cellular Senescence: A Potential Strategy for Overcoming Drug Resistance in Ovarian Cancer.
articles.authors: Szczepanek J
articles.abstract: Ovarian cancer remains one of the most lethal gynecological malignancies, largely due to late diagnosis and the frequent development of resistance to platinum-based chemotherapy and taxanes. Increasing evidence implicates microRNAs as key regulators of drug response through their control of DNA damage response and repair, apoptosis, epithelial-mesenchymal transition, and therapy-induced cellular senescence. Senescence is a double-edged process characterized by irreversible cell-cycle arrest and the secretion of pro-inflammatory factors collectively known as the senescence-associated secretory phenotype, which may suppress tumor growth but also promote chemoresistance and disease recurrence. This review summarizes current evidence on microRNA (miRNA)-mediated regulation of therapy-induced cellular senescence and its role in drug resistance in ovarian cancer. We integrate data from mechanistic studies, preclinical models, and clinical observations, focusing on senescence-associated miRNAs and their regulatory networks. miRNAs including miR-34a, miR-21, miR-146a, miR-200c, miR-506, and miR-433 regulate key senescence pathways, notably p53/p21 and p16-RB signaling, and modulate the senescence-associated secretory phenotype by controlling inflammatory mediators, extracellular matrix remodeling, and angiogenic factors. Several of these miRNAs are also associated with resistance to platinum-based chemotherapy, taxanes, poly ADP-ribose polymerase (PARP) inhibitors, and immunotherapies through effects on PI3K/AKT and Hippo signaling pathways, as well as DNA repair mechanisms. Emerging therapeutic strategies aim to modulate or eliminate senescent cells using miRNA mimics, inhibitors, or gene-editing approaches, including nanoparticle-based delivery systems. Although preclinical studies suggest that these approaches may restore chemosensitivity, clinical translation remains limited by delivery challenges, off-target effects, and the context-dependent role of senescence. Targeting miRNA-senescence regulatory axes may represent a strategy for addressing drug resistance in ovarian cancer and warrants further investigation as part of combination treatment strategies.

articles.title: Ketone Body Metabolism in Cancer-Associated Fibroblasts and FSTL3 as Prognostic and Therapeutic Determinants of Chemoradiotherapy Response in Cervical Cancer.
articles.authors: Yang H, Ma L, Ma R et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Concurrent chemoradiotherapy (CCRT) is a cornerstone of treatment for locally advanced cervical cancer, although many patients show a poor response. The tumor microenvironment (TME) is a key determinant of therapeutic resistance and prognosis, with the metabolic reprogramming within specific cellular subsets playing a particularly important role. However, the cellular sources of metabolic heterogeneity in cervical cancer and their clinical implications have yet to be firmly established.
METHODS: An integrated analysis of single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) datasets from eight patients cervical cancer, together with bulk RNA sequencing data retrieved from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) and Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) datasets, was conducted. Cellular heterogeneity was characterized using the Seurat and Harmony, while metabolic activity was assessed by integrating five algorithms (AUCell, UCell, singscore, ssGSEA, and AddModuleScore). The Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator (LASSO)-Cox regression was used to construct a prognostic model, which was subsequently validated in external cohorts. The functional role of the key gene FSTL3 was examined through both in vitro and in vivo experiments.
RESULTS: scRNA-seq analyses identified 10 major cell types within the cervical cancer TME. Among these, cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) showed the greatest enrichment of ketone body metabolism-related gene signatures. CAFs with high enrichment of these signatures exhibited enhanced cell-cell communication and were associated with activation of the AP-1 transcription factor network. Analysis of these CAFs led to the development of a nine-gene prognostic signature (KLF4, SERPINF1, CD74, PRPS2, ERRFI1, FSTL3, SOD2, JUN, and CXCL3). A risk model based on these genes predicted survival in the TCGA training and validation sets and in independent GEO cohorts (disease-free survival in GSE44001 and overall survival in GSE52903). A nomogram combining the risk score with clinical variables showed improved predictive performance compared with either the risk score or clinical variables alone. Knockdown of FSTL3 suppressed tumor growth and enhanced sensitivity to irradiation and cisplatin in both in vitro and in vivo models, supporting its functional role in cervical cancer progression and treatment response.
CONCLUSION: These analyses identify a CAF population enriched in ketone body metabolism-related gene expression that may be associated with…

articles.title: Oral hormonal contraceptive use and gastrointestinal symptoms in young women: a cross-sectional study.
articles.journal: The European journal of contraception & reproductive health care : the official journal of the European Society of Contraception
articles.ta: Eur J Contracept Reprod Health Care
articles.authors: Buzatu SE, Gofman S, Cassisi JE
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Gastrointestinal symptoms may affect contraceptive tolerability, yet domain-specific symptoms associated with oral contraceptive use remain insufficiently described.
OBJECTIVE: To compare gastrointestinal, physical, and psychological symptoms among young adults using no birth control, a combined oral contraceptive (COC), or a progestin-only pill (POP).
METHODS: Participants aged 18-25 years completed a cross-sectional online survey. The sample included 669 participants: 427 using no birth control, 196 using a COC, and 46 using a POP. Outcomes included five PROMIS gastrointestinal domains, a study-specific regional abdominal pain sum, eight Cohen-Hoberman Inventory of Physical Symptoms (CHIPS) domains, and anxiety, depressive symptoms, and health anxiety. Race/ethnicity and current sexual activity were included as additional fixed factors in primary models.
RESULTS: The multivariate PROMIS effect of contraceptive group was not significant. Constipation was the only PROMIS domain meeting the Bonferroni-corrected criterion, with higher adjusted estimated marginal means among COC users than participants using no birth control. COC users also reported higher regional abdominal pain scores than POP users. The CHIPS multivariate effect was not significant, but gastrointestinal subscale scores were higher among COC users than participants using no birth control. Psychological outcomes showed a small multivariate group effect, but no individual outcome met the Bonferroni-corrected criterion.
CONCLUSION: Oral contraceptive use was associated with modest, domain-specific gastrointestinal differences rather than a broad gastrointestinal or physical symptom profile. Because the study was cross-sectional and residual confounding remains possible, findings should be interpreted as associations rather than causal effects.

articles.title: Characterization of the immune landscape at the maternal-fetal interface and the role of endogenous T cells in the pathogenesis of preeclampsia.
articles.authors: Liu Y, Jiang Y, Zhang H et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Preeclampsia (PE) is a major cause of maternal and fetal mortality and morbidity worldwide. The roles and characteristics of immune cells in PE pathogenesis remain incompletely understood.
METHODS: We collected the basal decidua, placentas, fetal membranes and umbilical cord blood from PE patients and healthy pregnant women as well as the placentas, uteri, livers, spleens and peripheral blood from normal pregnant and N-nitro-L-arginine methyl ester (L-NAME) induced PE mice, and performed multicolor flow cytometry to characterize the immune-cell landscapes. In addition, endogenous CD4+ or CD8+ T cells were depleted in the PE mice by intraperitoneal injection of anti-CD4 (GK1.5) or anti-CD8 (2.43) depletion monoclonal antibody, and then PE-related symptoms were evaluated.
RESULTS: Immune cells showed distinct enrichment patterns across different tissues at the maternal-fetal interface in pregnant women, and the immune landscape at the maternal-fetal interface differed between PE patients and healthy pregnancies. Similar results were observed in the normal pregnant and L-NAME induced PE mice. Furthermore, in vivo depletion of CD4+ T cells, but not CD8+ T cells, could ameliorate PE-related symptoms by attenuating the elevated blood pressure, reducing the urine protein-to-creatinine ratio, and alleviating the placental impairment and maternal inflammatory responses in the PE mice.
CONCLUSION: Our study demonstrated a distinct landscape of immune cells at the maternal-fetal interface in normal and PE pregnancies and revealed a pathogenetic role of endogenous CD4+ T cells in PE development, which provided new insights into PE pathogenesis and potential targets for PE prevention.

articles.title: Estimating bone marrow adiposity from head MRI and identifying its genetic architecture.
articles.authors: Kaufmann T, Bjørnstad PM, Falck M et al.
articles.abstract: Bone marrow (BM) adiposity changes radically through the lifespan, but this phenomenon is poorly characterized and understood in humans. Large datasets of magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scans of the head have been collected to study the human brain, but also contain unexploited information about other organs. We developed an artificial neural network that localizes calvarial BM in T1-weighted MRI head scans, enabling us to study its composition in several large MRI datasets, and to model sex-dimorphic age trajectories, including the effect of menopause. We revealed high heritability in single-nucleotide polymorphism and twin data, and identified 41 genetic loci significantly associated with the trait, including six sex-specific loci. Integrating mapped genes with existing BM single-cell RNA-sequencing data revealed patterns of adipogenic lineage differentiation and lipid loading. Finally, we identified significant genetic correlations with several human traits, including cognitive ability and Parkinson's disease, which is intriguing in light of the recently discovered channels that link calvarial BM to the meninges.

articles.title: Biopsychosocial correlates and predictors of sexual function in perimenopause: a systematic review.
articles.authors: Kolbuszewska MT, Zhang J, Berthelot R et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Problems with the domains of sexual function-desire, arousal, orgasm, and pain-are highly prevalent during perimenopause. Individual studies have revealed the importance of biopsychosocial factors for sexual function during this reproductive transition; however, our understanding of risk and protective factors remains equivocal. To address this critical gap in knowledge, we conducted a systematic review examining biological, psychological, and social/interpersonal correlates and predictors of sexual function (ie, desire, arousal, orgasm, pain) in perimenopause.
METHODS: A systematic review of 42 studies focusing on perimenopausal women was conducted. Studies were included if they assessed biological (eg, hormonal levels, menopause symptoms), psychological (eg, mood, stress, resilience), or social/interpersonal (eg, relationship quality, intimacy) factors in relation to sexual function. Findings were narratively synthesized to identify consistent predictors and gaps across domains of sexual function.
RESULTS: With regard to biological factors, hormonal changes showed either no association or inconsistent associations with sexual function, whereas urogynecological menopause symptom severity was consistently associated with poorer sexual function. Psychological risk factors (eg, depression, anxiety, stress) were consistently associated with poorer sexual function outcomes, whereas resilience factors (eg, relationship quality, overall health) were associated with better sexual function in perimenopause. Assessment of social/interpersonal factors revealed that interpersonal factors (eg, relationship satisfaction and intimacy, low conflict) were associated with greater sexual function, whereas factors such as relationship length were not. The evidence linking other social factors (eg, sociodemographics) and sexual function was mixed. This systematic review also revealed important limitations of the current literature. Most notably, reliance on cross-sectional designs, which preclude estimates of change over time, inconsistent and sometimes poor measurement of sexual function, and conflation of perimenopause with other menopausal stages.
CONCLUSION: This review demonstrates that sexual function during perimenopause is influenced by interconnected biological, psychological, and social factors. Biological changes-particularly menopause-related symptoms-play a significant role, though hormonal influences remain inconsistent. Psychological factors and…

articles.title: Nonlinear dose-response relationship between cumulative anticholinergic use and the risk of dementia in adults with overactive bladder: a systematic review and dose-response meta-analysis.
articles.authors: Kim JH, Gwon YN, Shim SR et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Whilst anticholinergics (ACH) are standard treatments for overactive bladder (OAB), cumulative exposure is linked to an increased risk of dementia. Most evidence assumes a linear dose-response relationship, which may fail to capture complex biological dynamics. We aimed to characterise the functional form (linear vs. non-linear) of this association and identify clinically meaningful inflection points of risk escalation.
METHODS: A systematic literature search was conducted through 10 December 2025, in PubMed, Cochrane and Embase. Following PRISMA guidelines, we included comparative observational cohorts evaluating cumulative ACH exposure and incident dementia in OAB patients without baseline cognitive impairment. Pairwise meta-analysis and dose-response meta-analyses (DRMA) using one-stage and two-stage random-effects models with restricted cubic splines were performed to assess non-linearity.
KEY FINDINGS AND LIMITATIONS: Thirteen studies encompassing 7 891 574 participants were included. ACH use was associated with significantly increased dementia risk (HR: 1.52; 95% CI: 1.29-1.80). DRMA identified a significant non-linear, inverted U-shaped relationship. Risk escalated sharply during the initial 3 years: HRs at 90 days, 1 year, and 3 years were 1.11, 1.42 and 1.61, respectively. Peak risk occurred at ~874 cumulative defined daily dose (HR: 1.63 [95% CI, 1.32-2.00]), with apparent attenuation thereafter likely reflecting survivor bias and the depletion-of-susceptibles phenomenon rather than biological protection. Limitations include the observational nature of the data and heterogeneity in dementia ascertainment.
CONCLUSIONS AND CLINICAL IMPLICATIONS: Dementia risk in OAB patients follows a non-linear trajectory, with a critical vulnerability window during the first 3 years of cumulative ACH exposure. Clinical management should prioritise non-anticholinergic alternatives (e.g. mirabegron) or implement structured cognitive surveillance during this early treatment phase.

articles.title: Exosomal circ_0000387 Is Associated With Ovarian Cancer Metastatic Regulation Through IGF2BP3-Related Signalling and Endothelial VWF Responses.
articles.journal: Journal of biochemical and molecular toxicology
articles.authors: Xie Y, Shen P, Chen H et al.
articles.abstract: This study investigated the context-dependent roles of circ_0000387 in ovarian cancer (OC) metastasis, focusing on its tumour-cell-intrinsic effects and exosome-mediated tumour-endothelial communication. circRNA sequencing was performed on paired primary and metastatic ovarian cancer tissues to identify metastasis-associated circRNAs. Gain- and loss-of-function experiments in SKOV3 cells assessed malignant phenotypes, while CHIRP and RIP assays examined the interaction between circ_0000387 and IGF2BP3. Exosomes were isolated and characterised, and SKOV3-endothelial cell co-culture experiments evaluated exosome-associated effects on endothelial VWF responses and tumour-cell behaviour. An intraperitoneal dissemination mouse model was used for in vivo validation. circ_0000387 was expressed at higher levels in metastatic ovarian cancer tissues than in paired primary tumours. In SKOV3 cells, circ_0000387 interacted with IGF2BP3 and promoted cell viability, invasion, and migration, accompanied by AKT activation, AMPK inhibition, and increased YAP nuclear accumulation. In contrast, circ_0000387-enriched exosomes increased endothelial VWF secretion and were associated with reduced SKOV3 invasion and migration in an FVIII-modulated co-culture context, accompanied by increased AMPK activation and reduced YAP nuclear accumulation. These effects were attenuated by inhibition of exosome release or VWF blockade. In vivo, circ_0000387 overexpression was associated with reduced intraperitoneal dissemination and ascites formation, and these effects were attenuated by Rab27a silencing or VWF neutralisation. circ_0000387 exhibits context-dependent functions in ovarian cancer, promoting malignant phenotypes within tumour cells through IGF2BP3-associated AKT/AMPK/YAP signalling while being associated with reduced metastatic activity through exosome-dependent, VWF-related tumour-endothelial responses. These findings identify circ_0000387 as a potential regulator of ovarian cancer metastasis warranting further mechanistic and clinical validation.
