articles.title: ALDH4A1 and anti-ALDH4A1 emerge as a novel antigenic axis linked to atherosclerosis in rheumatoid arthritis.
articles.authors: Miranda-Prieto D, Alperi-López M, Pérez-Álvarez ÁI et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Cardiovascular risk excess in rheumatoid arthritis (RA) cannot be explained by traditional risk factors alone. Recent experimental data have identified ALDH4A1 as a mitochondrial self-antigen implicated in atherosclerosis, yet its clinical significance in human autoimmunity remains unexplored. We aimed to characterize ALDH4A1 and anti-ALDH4A1 antibody levels in early RA, and evaluate their associations with atherosclerosis burden and lipoprotein traits.
METHODS: ALDH4A1 and anti-ALDH4A1 antibodies (IgM, IgG, IgA, and IgG subclasses) were measured in early RA (n = 82), clinically suspect arthralgia (n = 14), healthy controls (n = 70), and a validation cohort of established RA. A prospective cohort (n = 13) explored therapeutic modulation under TNF blockade. Associations with atherosclerosis burden, lipid/lipoprotein profiles, oxylipin signatures, proteomics, and cell-free DNA were assessed.
RESULTS: ALDH4A1 serum levels were associated with apoptotic-related proteomic pathways, cell-free DNA and lipidomic signatures in early RA. Reduced anti-ALDH4A1 antibodies were found, although divergent patters were noted across isotypes. These differences were confirmed in a validation cohort. IgG (predominantly IgG3) anti-ALDH4A1 correlated with favourable lipoprotein traits and cardiometabolic risk factors. Increased ALDH4A1 and reduced IgM/IgG anti-ALDH4A1 antibodies independently predicted atherosclerosis and improved risk stratification beyond mSCORE, most notably for IgG. ALDH4A1 tracked with TNF dynamics under TNF blockade, whereas increases in IgG antibodies occurred in responders and paralleled changes in lipoprotein features.
CONCLUSIONS: The ALDH4A1/anti-ALDH4A1 axis emerges as a novel player bridging lipid disturbances and atherosclerosis along the whole RA continuum, hence highlighting the involvement of mitochondrial targets. These components hold promise as functional players, clinical tools and therapeutic targets.

articles.title: LncRNA Jpx recruits EEF1A1 to enhance Cul4b mRNA stability and translation efficiency, safeguarding mitophagy and spermiogenesis in mice.
articles.authors: Guo X, Wang R, Chen X et al.
articles.abstract: Long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) are abundantly expressed in the testis, but their roles in male fertility remain largely uncharacterized. Here, we generated Jpx knockout (KO) mice and found that Jpx deficiency did not affect spermatogonial proliferation or meiosis, but predominantly impaired the post-meiotic phase of spermiogenesis. KO males exhibited reduced testis size, prolonged reproductive cycles, smaller litters, decreased sperm count, and impaired progressive motility. Their spermatozoa also showed compromised in vitro fertilization (IVF) efficiency and lower blastocyst formation rates. Ultrastructurally, KO spermatozoa had elevated teratozoospermia manifested as excessive residual cytoplasm with dispersed mitochondria and autophagic vacuoles, as well as severe midpiece mitochondrial disorganization, including disrupted sheath assembly, cristae loss, and vacuolization. Metabolomics revealed a profound defect in spermatozoal mitochondrial energy metabolism, with significant reductions in multiple glycolytic and TCA cycle intermediates (e.g., G6P and isocitrate) as well as key energy molecules (ATP, GTP, and NAD+). Mechanistically, the predominantly cytoplasmic Jpx directly bound the elongation factor EEF1A1 to form a ribonucleoprotein complex, which specifically attached to the 3' untranslated region (3'UTR) of Cul4b mRNA, thereby stabilizing the transcript and enhancing its translation. Consequently, Jpx ablation led to a substantial reduction in Cul4b, defective mitophagy (as evidenced by decreased PINK1 and LC3-II/I ratio and increased p62), mitochondrial dysfunction, and elevated oxidative stress in spermatogenic cells. Together, our findings identify Jpx as an essential post-transcriptional regulator that control mitophagy via the EEF1A1-dependent stabilization and translational promotion of Cul4b, thereby ensuring mitochondrial homeostasis, metabolic competence, and functional spermatozoon maturation.

articles.title: microRNA-614 contributes to recurrent miscarriage through targeting FOXD1.
articles.journal: Journal of obstetrics and gynaecology : the journal of the Institute of Obstetrics and Gynaecology
articles.authors: Wan X, Che H, Lai L et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Recurrent miscarriage (RM) is a significant reproductive health issue affecting many women of childbearing age. The objective of this study was to evaluate the value of microRNA-614 (miR-614) as a potential biomarker for RM and to elucidate its functional mechanism.
METHODS: Differentially expressed miRNAs (DEmiRs) were first screened from the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) database using a bioinformatics approach. A total of 135 patients with RM and 135 healthy controls were included. The expression levels and diagnostic performance of miR-614 were evaluated by RT-qPCR and ROC curve analysis. CCK-8 and Transwell were performed to assess the impact of the miRNA on trophoblast cell proliferation, invasion, and migration. For target gene verification, TargetScan 8.0 was utilised for prediction, followed by a luciferase activity assay to confirm direct regulation by miRNA.
RESULTS: Bioinformatic interrogation of the GSE73025 dataset revealed a significant down-regulation of miR-614. Plasma miR-614 was significantly downregulated in RM patients. The area under the ROC curve (AUC) for miR-614 in distinguishing RM patients from controls was 0.865 (95% CI: 0.823-0.907, sensitivity = 77.78%, specificity = 77.78%). The AUC for predicting adverse pregnancy outcomes was 0.790 (95% CI: 0.708-0.870, sensitivity = 71.08%, specificity = 82.69%). Transfection with miR-614 mimics decreased the proliferation, invasion, and migration of HTR-8 and JEG3 cells. miR-614 Directly targets FOXD1 and negatively modulates its mRNA expression to drive RM progression.
CONCLUSION: In RM patients, miR-614 is downregulated, leading to increased FOXD1 expression. miR-614 mimics suppresses trophoblast proliferation, migration, and invasion by directly targeting FOXD1. Thus, miR-614 downregulation contributes to RM pathogenesis by directly targeting FOXD1, thereby upregulating FOXD1 and inhibiting the proliferation, invasion, and migration of trophoblast cells.

articles.title: Urinary complications following Bricker urinary diversion in gynecologic cancer: A retrospective analysis of 77 cases.
articles.authors: Jaafar E, El Hajj H, Maulard A et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: To evaluate postoperative urinary complications and their management in patients undergoing Bricker urinary diversion for gynecologic cancers, with a focus on identifying risk factors, especially uretero-ileal strictures.
MATERIAL AND METHODS: We conducted a retrospective single-center study of 77 patients who underwent Bricker urinary diversion for gynecologic cancers between 2000 and 2020. All surgeries were performed by the same gynecologic oncologic team.
RESULTS: Primary tumor sites included the cervix and uterine body in 87% of patients, with others involving the vagina, vulva, and adnexa. Preoperative pelvic radiotherapy was performed in 71%, and para-aortic/pelvic radiotherapy in 10%. Over a median follow-up of 21 months, uretero-ileal strictures occurred in 30%, and fistulas in 6%. Preoperative nephrostomy was significantly associated with a higher rate of strictures (p = 0.001), while preoperative ureteral stenting was associated with a reduced risk (p = 0.005). All patients with strictures or fistulas were initially managed with ureteral stenting; nephrostomy was subsequently required in 56% of stricture and 80% of fistula cases. Surgical treatment was eventually needed in 17% and 60%, respectively. Additional risk factors for strictures included preoperative chemotherapy (p = 0.023) and intraoperative evidence of chronic enteritis (p = 0.013). No significant differences were observed in overall or recurrence-free survival between patients with and without strictures (p > 0.05).
CONCLUSIONS: Uretero-ileal strictures occurred in 30% and fistulas in 6% of patients undergoing Bricker urinary diversion. Preoperative ureteral stenting may help reduce stricture risk, and appropriate bowel segment selection is essential to minimize complications.

articles.title: Someone to Watch Over Me: Perspectives From Health Professionals Involved in Womens' Health on Intimate Examinations.
articles.journal: The Australian & New Zealand journal of obstetrics & gynaecology
articles.ta: Aust N Z J Obstet Gynaecol
articles.authors: Caldow O, Zhuang N, McGurgan P
articles.abstract:
AIMS: This study sought to determine contemporary practice and opinions regarding the use of third parties when performing intimate examinations. Specifically: What constitutes an 'intimate examination', the role and preferred terminology of third parties involved in intimate examinations, the nature of the consent and regulatory processes.
METHODS: Prospective, cross-sectional, observational study with participants recruited using a convenience sampling approach. Following a scoping review, an anonymous, confidential online survey was developed and distributed to health professionals working within Western Australian outer metropolitan obstetrics and gynaecology units. Both qualitative and quantitative data were obtained.
RESULTS: 141 health professionals participated; the majority were female (86%), with 56 respondents from a nursing/midwifery background, 53 from a medical background. Most respondents agreed on which components of physical examination could be viewed as 'intimate', expressed strong preferences for the third party to be called 'chaperone' and had similar opinions on what the role involved and the importance of using registered health professionals. Compared to doctors, nurse/midwife participants were significantly more likely to obtain written consent, report health professional norms, and chaperone availability influenced their use of chaperones, and were less likely to offer a chaperone for a breast examination. More than one third of respondents considered a medical student appropriate to act as chaperone.
DISCUSSION: Although intimate examinations are an integral part of clinical practice, it remains under-researched. This study indicates that despite RANZCOG and MBA guidance, womens' health professionals prefer the term 'chaperone'. Respondents recognised the importance of consent and documentation, but it is concerning that a significant proportion of respondents consider it acceptable to use students in these roles.

articles.title: MaMi study: Perceptions of pregnancy and reproductive decision-making in women with migraine.
articles.authors: González-García N, Valverde BH, Gago-Veiga AB et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To characterize the influence of migraine on reproductive decision-making in women of childbearing age and to identify potentially modifiable beliefs that could guide preconception counseling in headache clinical practice.
BACKGROUND: Migraine is a highly prevalent neurological disorder that disproportionately affects women of childbearing age. Although pharmacological management during pregnancy has been widely addressed, less is known about how migraine shapes desire for motherhood, pregnancy planning, and family-related decisions.
METHODS: This observational, cross-sectional, multicenter study was conducted in six Spanish public hospitals. Women aged 18-49 years with episodic or chronic migraine were recruited by convenience during routine consultations between March 1 and November 30, 2023. Participants completed a structured questionnaire addressing reproductive decisions along with validated scales, including the Headache Impact Test-6 (HIT-6), the Migraine Disability Assessment Scale (MIDAS), and the Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS). Descriptive statistics were used for data analysis.
RESULTS: A total of 162 women were included, with a median age of 36 years (interquartile range [IQR]: 31-41); 117 (72.2%) had episodic migraine and 45 (27.8%) had chronic migraine. Headache burden was high: the median HIT-6 score was 65 (IQR: 61-68), and 131/162 participants (80.9%; 95% confidence interval [CI], 74.1-86.2) were classified as having severe headache impact. Emotional symptoms were also frequent, with abnormal HADS-A scores in 84/162 participants (51.9%; 95% CI, 44.2-59.4) and abnormal HADS-D scores in 34/162 (21.0%; 95% CI, 15.4-27.9). Migraine influenced reproductive decisions in 49/162 women (30.2%; 95% CI, 23.7-37.7). The most common consequence was postponing pregnancy, reported by 38/161 participants (23.6%; 95% CI, 17.7-30.7), whereas 9/161 (5.6%; 95% CI, 3.0-10.3) had definitively decided against childbearing and 6/160 (3.8%; 95% CI, 1.7-7.9) had considered adoption. The main perceived barriers were reduced ability to care for children during migraine attacks (129/161; 80.1%; 95% CI, 73.3-85.6), fear of treatment-related teratogenic risks (97/161; 60.2%; 95% CI, 52.5-67.5), concern about migraine worsening during pregnancy (63/161; 39.1%; 95% CI, 31.9-46.8), and fear of transmitting migraine to offspring (117/161; 72.7%; 95% CI, 65.3-79.0).
CONCLUSION: Migraine affected reproductive decision-making in nearly one-third of…

articles.title: Overcoming platinum resistance by the disulfiram metabolite CuET in novel preclinical models of human carcinomas.
articles.authors: Arampatzis S, Buchtová T, Bartkova J et al.
articles.abstract: Overcoming resistance to standard-of-care chemotherapy represents an unmet need in oncology. To help address this challenge, here we established and characterized a panel of human cisplatin-resistant lung and breast cancer cell lines and patient-derived organoids from high-grade serous ovarian carcinomas (HGSOC), and show that platinum resistance can be overcome by treatment with diethyldithiocarbamate-copper (CuET), a metabolite of the alcohol-aversion drug disulfiram. All platinum-resistant models remained sensitive to CuET, consistent with distinct cytotoxicity mechanisms: proteotoxic stress for CuET and DNA damage for cisplatin, respectively. Platinum adduct and DNA damage response analyses suggested diverse mechanisms of cisplatin resistance among our models. Considering potential CuET-based therapies, our gene knock-down and functional assays in preclinical models, complemented with immunohistochemical analysis of tissue samples from cohorts of triple-negative breast cancer and HGSOC patients indicate that levels of metallothioneins, rather than NPL4 (the molecular target of CuET) warrant further evaluation as candidate biomarkers of CuET sensitivity. This dataset provides a resource of platinum-resistant models of common carcinomas, identifies CuET as a compound overcoming such resistance and provides leads for predictive biomarker discovery, with potential clinical implications in oncology.

articles.title: The severity of preeclampsia in naturally conceived versus IVF-conceived pregnancies: a retrospective study.
articles.authors: Chen Y, Jiang P, Li X et al.
articles.abstract: Pregnancies conceived using in vitro fertilization (IVF) significantly increase the risk of developing preeclampsia. One possible explanation is that embryos grown outside the body may implant differently compared to natural conceptions, potentially affecting placental development and increasing the risk of preeclampsia. Clinically, preeclampsia is classified into early-onset and late-onset forms, as well as severe and mild forms. Although some studies suggested that preeclampsia severity may be more pronounced in IVF-conceived pregnancies, the findings were controversial. In this retrospective study, we compared the severity of preeclampsia between naturally conceived and IVF-conceived pregnancies. A total of 498 preeclampsia cases were included, with 401 cases occurring in naturally conceived pregnancies and 97 in IVF-conceived pregnancies. The mean gestational age at delivery in the IVF-conceived group was 36 weeks, significantly earlier than that in the naturally conceived group (37 weeks, p = 0.0002). Additionally, 27 (28%) women in the IVF-conceived group developed early-onset preeclampsia, which was no statistical difference from the naturally conceived group (78, 19%, p = 0.0732). There was no significant difference in the proportion of severe preeclampsia between the two groups (16% vs. 23%, p = 0.1667). Additionally, gestational age at the onset of preeclampsia and the incidence of preterm birth were not different between the two groups after adjusting for important confounders, including maternal age, BMI, parity, and twin pregnancy. In conclusion, there is a known link between IVF conception and the increased risk of developing preeclampsia. Our study found that the severity of preeclampsia, once it occurred, did not differ between the two modes of conception.

articles.title: Non-Hormonal Psychopharmacotherapy of Vasomotor Symptoms Related to Menopause.
articles.authors: Naguy A, Alsalem NJ, Singh A
articles.abstract: Vasomotor symptoms (VMS) are quite ubiquitous roughly experienced by up to 80% of women during their perimenopause. In this focused review, authors would touch briefly on the diagnosis, screening, risk factors, pathophysiology, and nonhormonal psychopharmacotherapy of VMS.

articles.title: Awareness, Attitudes, and Contraceptive Acceptance Among Women Attending a Tertiary-Care Center in Delhi: A Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.authors: Mendiratta SL, Dath S S, Sinha A
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: High contraceptive awareness does not always translate into favorable attitudes or actual uptake, particularly when family influence, misconceptions, and concerns about adverse effects shape reproductive decisions.
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to assess family planning awareness, attitudes, contraceptive acceptance, and factors associated with acceptance among women attending the gynecology outpatient department of a tertiary-care center in Delhi.
METHODS: This descriptive cross-sectional study included 556 women aged 18-48 years who attended the gynecology outpatient department from June 2024 to May 2025 and received family planning counseling. Data were collected using a structured, interviewer-administered data-collection proforma. Categorical variables were summarized as frequencies, percentages, and Wilson 95% confidence intervals. Associations with contraceptive acceptance were assessed using Pearson's Chi-square test, and effect size was estimated using Cramér's V.
RESULTS: Overall, 82.0% of participants were aware of family planning, but only 36.5% had a positive attitude. Following counseling, 313 women (56.3%; 95% CI 52.1-60.4) accepted a contraceptive method. Among acceptors, oral contraceptive pills (40.6%), condoms (28.8%), and copper intrauterine contraceptive device (IUCD) (17.3%) were chosen. Doctors were the principal source of information for 37.1% of participants. Husband or family opposition accounted for 80.7% of non-acceptance. A favorable opinion toward birth spacing was reported by 68.0%. Acceptance was significantly associated with age group (χ²=58.90, p < 0.001; Cramér's V = 0.325) and obstetric category (χ² = 13.50, p = 0.009; Cramér's V = 0.156), but not with educational status (χ² = 6.29, p = 0.099).
CONCLUSION: Despite high awareness, a substantial gap between awareness and contraceptive acceptance persisted. Person-centered counseling addressing misconceptions and family-related barriers may improve informed and voluntary contraceptive acceptance.

articles.title: In situ hydrogel nanovaccine based on whole-cell tumor antigen efficiently activates adaptive immunity for the prevention and treatment of ovarian cancer.
articles.authors: Yan J, Lin R, Liu Q et al.
articles.abstract: Due to the late diagnosis with widespread peritoneal metastases and frequent chemoresistance, ovarian cancer has limited survival rates and necessitates innovative therapies. Here, we present an in situ hydrogel nanovaccine (LCMP@ALG) for spatiotemporally-synchronized antigen-adjuvant delivery to stimulate robust antitumor immunity. The hydrogel continuously releases mannosylated nanoparticles LCMP which are effectively internalized by dendritic cells and actively accumulate in lymph nodes via the ligand-mediated targeting effect. Benefiting from autologous tumor cell lysates, the vaccines evade antigen-specific tolerance. LCMP can synergistically activate Toll-like receptor 4 and Toll-like receptor 9 to augment antigen processing and cross-presentation, further potentiating the activation of humoral and cellular antitumor immunity. In the mouse model, the vaccine LCMP@ALG induces specific antitumor responses as well as long-term immunological memory. When combined with Programmed cell death protein 1 blockade, LCMP@ALG demonstrates a superior efficacy in prevention and elimination of ovarian cancer.

articles.title: Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy With Superimposed Pre-Eclampsia in a Grand Multiparous Woman.
articles.authors: Boahene PY, Ampofo BK, Gyabaah S et al.
articles.abstract: This case report highlights the importance of clinical vigilance, the role of echocardiography, and the benefits of guideline-directed multidisciplinary management of pregnant women with HCM in resource-limited settings. Advocating for comprehensive multidisciplinary care models is essential in optimizing maternal and fetal health outcomes among pregnant women with cardiac pathologies.

articles.title: Qianjin Baoyun Wan reduces spontaneous abortion and the prothrombotic state in pregnant rats.
articles.journal: Journal of traditional and complementary medicine
articles.authors: Zeng H, Ding H, Wang T et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIM: Recurrent spontaneous abortion (RSA) is closely associated with a prothrombotic state (PTS) in the first trimester of pregnancy. Qianjin Baoyun Wan (QBW), a traditional Chinese medicine formula, has historically been prescribed to prevent threatened miscarriage and pregnancy-related lumbago, while its efficacy and underlying mechanisms in RSA complicated by PTS remain to be elucidated. This study aimed to investigate the therapeutic effects and potential pharmacological mechanisms of QBW in a rat model of RSA with PTS.
EXPERIMENTAL PROCEDURE: Spontaneous abortion was induced in pregnant rats by mifepristone, and PTS was established via epinephrine administration. The therapeutic effects of QBW were assessed by measuring miscarriage rate, uterine contractility, and uterine microcirculation morphology. Coagulation-related parameters (APTT, TT, PT, fibrinogen) were evaluated. Thrombosis-related and pregnancy-related biomarkers were quantified by ELISA. In addition, network pharmacology and network toxicology were employed to predict the potential pharmacodynamic targets and toxicological profiles of QBW.
RESULTS AND CONCLUSION: QBW reduced miscarriage rates and uterine contractility while improving pregnancy-related biomarkers. It restored uterine microcirculation (capillary density and diameter), prolonged coagulation time, lowered fibrinogen, and restored the balance between antithrombotic factors (e.g., AT-III, 6-keto-PGF1α) and prothrombotic factors (e.g., D-dimer, TXB2). Network pharmacology predicted immunoregulatory, anti-inflammatory, and antioxidant mechanisms underlying its effects against RSA with PTS, though potential signals of hepatic and reproductive organ effects were noted. These findings suggest that QBW may have therapeutic potential for RSA with PTS, although further preclinical and clinical validation is required.

articles.title: Association Between Joint Hypermobility and Pelvic Organ Prolapse: A Hospital-Based Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.authors: Aziz ZA
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Pelvic organ prolapse (POP) is a prevalent disorder of the pelvic floor with multifactorial etiology. Generalized joint hypermobility (JHM) is a sign of systemic collagen laxity. This study investigated the association between generalized JHM and POP and examined other clinical correlates including parity, body mass index (BMI), heavy occupational lifting, and family history in Middle Eastern females.
METHODS: This hospital-based cross-sectional study evaluated 812 non-pregnant women aged ≥ 20 years attending an outpatient gynecology clinic at Erbil Maternity Teaching Hospital between November 2021 and April 2024. POP was staged using the standardized Pelvic Organ Prolapse Quantification (POP-Q) system. Generalized JHM was defined as a Beighton score ≥ 4/9. Multivariable logistic regression and correlation analyses assessed independent correlates and severity trends.
RESULTS: Among 812 participants, 444 had POP (54.7%) and 368 served as non-POP controls (45.3%). JHM was present in 67.6% (300/444) of POP cases versus 10.9% (40/368) of controls (unadjusted OR 17.08, 95% CI: 11.64-25.07; p < 0.001). In multivariable logistic regression, JHM remained strongly associated with POP (adjusted OR [aOR] 28.11, 95% CI: 17.21-45.91; p < 0.001). Family history of POP (aOR 9.69, 95% CI: 5.58-16.83; p < 0.001), heavy lifting (aOR 6.48, 95% CI: 4.05-10.37; p < 0.001), and parity (per birth aOR 1.17, 95% CI: 1.08-1.27; p < 0.001) were also independently associated with POP. Beighton scores increased significantly across advancing POP-Q severity stages (Kruskal-Wallis p < 0.001; Spearman's ρ = 0.30, p < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: Generalized joint hypermobility is strongly and independently associated with pelvic organ prolapse, with Beighton scores showing a positive correlation across prolapse severity stages. While joint hypermobility screening represents a simple clinical examination tool, prospective longitudinal studies are needed to determine whether such screening can improve risk stratification or guide preventive pelvic floor care.

articles.title: Galectins at the maternal-fetal interface: shield or gateway to infections?
articles.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
articles.authors: Mattos GD, Pereira NZ, Sato MN
articles.abstract: Pregnancy relies on a tightly regulated immune balance at the maternal-fetal interface, where tolerance toward the semi-allogeneic fetus must coexist with effective defense mechanisms against invading pathogens. In this context, galectins (gals), a family of β-galactoside-binding lectins, play essential roles in placentation, angiogenesis, tissue remodeling, and immune regulation. Beyond their physiological functions, accumulating evidence indicates that these proteins also participate in host-virus interactions, acting either to restrict infection or to facilitate viral attachment, entry, replication, and persistence. In this review, we discuss the structural characteristics, unconventional secretion pathways, and major immunological functions of gal, with particular emphasis on gal-1, gal-3, gal-9 and gal-13, at the maternal-fetal interface. We also summarize the current evidence regarding their involvement in congenital infections caused by cytomegalovirus (CMV), Zika virus (ZIKV), and human immunodeficiency virus (HIV). Available studies indicate that gals modulate key processes, including viral entry, immune cell activation, inflammation, viral persistence, and maternal-fetal transmission, although their specific mechanisms of action within the placenta remain poorly understood. Collectively, the available evidence suggests that gals exert dual and context-dependent functions, acting as critical regulators of the delicate balance between immune tolerance and antiviral defense. A better understanding of these mechanisms may contribute to the identification of novel biomarkers and improve our understanding of the pathogenesis of congenital infections, ultimately leading to better pregnancy outcomes.

articles.title: Are Oocyte Maturation Rates Associated with LH Levels in GnRH Antagonist Cycles Using GnRH Agonist Triggering?
articles.authors: Nahshon C, Yanai E, Cohen N et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate whether oocyte maturation rates are influenced by basal LH levels, LH levels on the day of trigger, or the magnitude of LH decline during controlled ovarian stimulation in GnRH antagonist cycles using an agonist trigger.
METHODS: This retrospective study included patients treated at our IVF unit between 2014 and 2024. All 432 GnRH antagonist cycles triggered with GnRH agonist were analyzed. The primary outcomes were the associations between basal LH levels and the absolute number of oocytes retrieved, oocyte maturation rate, and fertilization rate. Fertilization analyses were restricted to cycles not performed for fertility preservation.
RESULTS: Basal LH levels were not associated with the number of oocytes retrieved, maturation rate, or fertilization rate in multivariable analyses. LH levels on the trigger day were not associated with retrieval, maturation, or fertilization outcomes. Similarly, the percentage decline in LH levels during stimulation was not associated with cycle outcomes.
CONCLUSION: Pre-trigger LH measurements, including basal LH, trigger-day LH, and LH decline during stimulation, were not significantly associated with oocyte retrieval, maturation, or fertilization outcomes. These findings suggest limited predictive value of pre-trigger LH measurements in this population, although a threshold effect at very low LH levels cannot be excluded.

articles.title: Knowledge, attitude and practice on continuous glucose monitoring and self-monitoring of blood glucose among healthcare professionals across India: A cross-sectional study.
articles.authors: Kapoor N, Sheikh S, Das S et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Uncontrolled glycemia remains a major concern in India, underlining the need for wider adoption of effective glucose monitoring methods in diabetes care. Despite the benefits of continuous glucose monitoring (CGM), its adoption remains low in India and is unevenly distributed across healthcare settings and patient populations.
METHODS: A cross-sectional, questionnaire-based survey was conducted among healthcare professionals (HCPs) practicing across private and public healthcare settings in India to assess their knowledge, attitudes and practices regarding CGM metrics using an 18-item questionnaire. Responses were measured using a 5-point Likert scale.
RESULTS: A total of 126 HCPs from different specialties participated in the study. Most HCPs (81.7%) expressed confidence in the use of CGM in patients with gestational diabetes mellitus. The majority of HCPs were confident or highly confident in interpreting CGM reports (80.1%) and explaining them to patients (81.8%). More than 90% of HCPs agreed that CGM improves overall diabetes management and 88.1% were confident that CGM helps reduce hypoglycemic and hyperglycemic episodes compared with self-monitoring of blood glucose (SMBG) alone. Most HCPs (78.6%) agreed that the cost of CGM is a major barrier to its wider adoption in diabetes care. Despite recognizing the clinical value of CGM, fewer than half of HCPs believed it could completely replace SMBG.
CONCLUSION: The study highlights the adoption-action gap of CGM use in diabetes care in Indian settings; however, the predominantly experienced, private-sector sample may limit generalizability to the broader HCP population. High costs, variable confidence in CGM interpretation and continued reliance on SMBG contributed to the gap despite HCPs' strong awareness of CGM's clinical value. Addressing these barriers and improving training may enhance CGM adoption nationwide.

articles.title: Research progress of extracellular vesicles in PMOS: molecular mechanisms, diagnostic value, and therapeutic strategies.
articles.authors: Qi L, Jiang Y, Han Y et al.
articles.abstract: Extracellular vesicles (EVs) carry proteins, lipids and nucleic acids that can influence ovarian and systemic metabolic function. This narrative review examines their molecular mechanisms, biomarker potential and experimental therapeutic applications in polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS), previously termed polycystic ovary syndrome. Follicular fluid EV cargo varies with disease phenotype and adiposity, but these associations have not established clinically validated diagnostic tests. Follicular fluid collection also requires an invasive procedure and should not be described as a non-invasive screening approach. Experimental studies indicate that selected mesenchymal stromal cell-derived EV preparations can modulate granulosa cell survival, mitochondrial quality control and endocrine function. Adipose stromal cell- and brown adipose tissue-derived preparations additionally affect metabolic pathways, while engineered small EVs can improve delivery of a PI3K agonist in mice. Disease-associated follicular fluid EVs may impair oocyte maturation or promote abnormal granulosa cell proliferation; their effects depend on source, cargo and recipient context. We distinguish PMOS-specific evidence from chemotherapy-related ovarian injury and premature ovarian insufficiency, summarize treatment models, administration and endpoints, and evaluate reporting in selected studies against MISEV2023 recommendations. The evidence remains predominantly preclinical. Incomplete EV characterization, heterogeneous doses and models, limited biodistribution data and uncertain long-term reproductive safety prevent direct extrapolation to patient care.

articles.title: Association Between Adherence to the Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension (DASH) Diet and Diminished Ovarian Reserve: A Case-Control Study.
articles.authors: Khodarahmi M, Mokari-Yamchi A, Vajdi M et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite the fact that dietary intakes are suggested to affect fecundity and reproductive outcomes, data about the favorable impacts of dietary quality indicators on diminished ovarian reserve (DOR) is scarce. So, we aimed to examine the relationship between the Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension (DASH) score and odds of DOR.
METHODS: This case-control study was conducted among 370 women (120 with DOR as the case group and 250 with normal ovarian reserve as the control group). Cases and controls were frequency-matched according to age and body mass index (BMI) at the study-design stage. Dietary information derived from a validated semi-quantitative food frequency questionnaire (FFQ) was used to count energy-adjusted DASH score based on eight components. Markers of ovarian reserve, including anti-Müllerian hormone (AMH) and antral follicle count (AFC) which were measured in serum samples and by transvaginal ultrasound, respectively. The multivariable-adjusted binary logistic regression was used to identify the association between energy-adjusted DASH score and odds of DOR.
RESULTS: Higher energy-adjusted DASH score was related to lower diastolic blood pressure (DBP) in women with DOR (p = 0.006). No statistically significant association was observed between DASH adherence and the odds of DOR. In the crude model, compared with the lowest tertile (T1), the odds ratios for DOR were 0.87 (95% CI: 0.51-1.49) for T2 and 0.78 (95% CI: 0.46-1.33) for T3 (P-trend = 0.370). After adjustment for potential confounders, the association remained non-significant in Model 1 (T2: 0.93, 95% CI: 0.53-1.63; T3: 0.76, 95% CI: 0.43-1.33; P-trend = 0.328) and Model 2 (T2: 0.88, 95% CI: 0.49-1.56; T3: 0.74, 95% CI: 0.42-1.30; P-trend = 0.288). Nevertheless, in an exploratory unadjusted analysis among women with DOR, AFC differed significantly across energy-adjusted DASH tertiles, with higher AFC observed among women in the higher DASH adherence categories (p = 0.015).
CONCLUSIONS: Higher adherence to the DASH dietary pattern was not significantly associated with the odds of DOR. Further prospective studies are warranted to clarify the potential relationship between dietary patterns and ovarian reserve.

articles.title: The gut-placental axis: microbial signals remodeling maternal-fetal immune tolerance.
articles.authors: Shi L, Li Y, Mo Y
articles.abstract: Pregnancy represents a unique immunological challenge requiring the establishment and maintenance of maternal-fetal immune tolerance. Emerging evidence demonstrates that the gut microbiota serves as a critical regulator of placental immune responses through systemic immune remodeling, constituting what is now recognized as the gut-placental immune axis. This narrative review examines the molecular pathways through which intestinal signals reach the maternal-fetal interface, encompassing short-chain fatty acids, tryptophan derivatives and their aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AhR) ligands, secondary bile acids, microbe-associated molecular patterns, bacterial extracellular vesicles, and placental exosomes. These signals collectively regulate key immune cell populations, including myeloid-derived suppressor cells, regulatory T cell subsets such as RORγt+ peripherally derived regulatory T cell (pTreg), Th17/Treg balance, macrophage polarization, and uterine natural killer (NK) cell function. We critically address the placental microbiome controversy, emphasizing that molecular signal transmission rather than live microbial colonization represents the prevailing paradigm for gut-placental communication. This paradigm shift redirects the research focus from identifying bacterial species to characterizing bioactive metabolites and microbe-associated molecular patterns. Furthermore, we elucidate how gut dysbiosis drives pathological cascades in major pregnancy complications, including preeclampsia, gestational diabetes mellitus, recurrent pregnancy loss, preterm birth, and fetal growth restriction. Finally, we evaluate clinical translation prospects encompassing probiotics, dietary fiber interventions, postbiotic metabolite supplementation, and engineered extracellular vesicle therapies, while acknowledging persistent challenges in establishing causal relationships, addressing individual heterogeneity, and ensuring long-term safety. This conceptual framework advances mechanistic understanding of microbiota-immune-placenta interactions and provides a foundation for developing microbiota-informed strategies to predict and prevent adverse pregnancy outcomes. Throughout, we explicitly distinguish human associative evidence from animal causal evidence.

articles.title: Elevated human epididymis protein 4 levels in chronic kidney disease compromise the accuracy of the risk of ovarian malignancy algorithm.
articles.authors: Ju DH, Kim SW, Yi SW et al.
articles.abstract: The present study aimed to compare the diagnostic accuracy of the risk of ovarian malignancy algorithm (ROMA) for differentiating ovarian tumors in patients with and without chronic kidney disease (CKD), using postoperative histopathological findings as the reference standard among patients who underwent surgery after ROMA testing. The retrospective study included 1,122 patients, including 21 with CKD, who met the inclusion criteria and underwent surgery for ovarian tumors at Gangneung Asan Hospital between August 2015 and August 2025. In patients with CKD, human epididymis protein 4 (HE4) levels were elevated in both benign and malignant groups compared with normal levels, with progressively higher levels observed with increasing CKD severity. Among patients with benign ovarian tumors, median HE4 levels were higher in those with CKD than in those without CKD (210.00 vs. 41.10 pmol/l). Cancer antigen 125 (CA125) levels did not differ significantly according to CKD status. Because of the elevated HE4 levels, ROMA scores were significantly higher in patients with CKD, resulting in low specificity {0.200 [95% confidence interval (CI), 0.066-0.470]} and reduced overall accuracy [0.429 (95% CI, 0.240-0.640)]. Receiver operating characteristic curve analysis demonstrated superior predictive performance of ROMA in patients without CKD [area under the curve (AUC), 0.724; 95% CI, 0.680-0.768] compared with those with CKD (AUC, 0.467; 95% CI, 0.217-0.717). In conclusion, in patients with CKD and ovarian tumors, ROMA should be interpreted with caution, and CA125 and imaging findings should be considered alongside other clinical information when assessing the risk of ovarian malignancy.

articles.title: Bidirectional association between thyroid autoimmunity/thyroglobulin antibody and diminished ovarian reserve: a systematic review and meta-analysis of observational studies.
articles.authors: Yang S, Wang J, Wang H et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Evidence suggests that thyroid autoimmunity (TAI) may be associated with ovarian dysfunction; however, most studies have focused primarily on thyroid peroxidase antibodies (TPOAb), while evidence regarding thyroglobulin antibodies (TgAb) remains limited and inconsistent. This study aimed to evaluate the association between TAI/TgAb and ovarian reserve.
METHODS: A systematic literature search was conducted in PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, CNKI databases for Chinese- and English-language articles published from January 2014 to January 2025. A bidirectional validation design was employed: (1) forward analysis, quantifying between-group differences in serum anti-Müllerian hormone (AMH) levels between TAI-positive women and healthy controls using standardized mean differences (SMD); and (2) reverse analysis, quantifying differences in TgAb levels (SMD for continuous variables) and TgAb positivity rates (odds ratios OR for dichotomous variables) between women with diminished ovarian reserve (DOR) and healthy controls. This study was prospectively registered with PROSPERO (CRD420251207428) and conducted in accordance with the PRISMA 2020 guidelines. The reverse analysis denotes a reverse-direction cross-sectional comparison in which the grouping and outcome variables are exchanged; it does not imply temporal or causal reversal.
RESULTS: Thirteen studies (total n = 4,286) were included. Forward analysis (4 studies, n = 870) demonstrated significantly lower serum AMH levels in TAI-positive women compared with controls (SMD=-0.20, 95% CI [-0.34, -0.06], P = 0.005, I2 = 0%). Reverse analysis of continuous variables (5 studies, n = 1,496) revealed significantly elevated TgAb levels in women with DOR compared with controls (SMD=0.93, 95% CI [0.36, 1.50], P = 0.001, I2 = 94%); however, this estimate should be interpreted with caution given the substantial heterogeneity. Reverse analysis of dichotomous variables (7 studies, n = 2,568) confirmed that women with DOR had significantly higher odds of TgAb positivity compared with controls (OR=1.65, 95% CI [1.29, 2.11], P < 0.0001, I2 = 32%).
CONCLUSIONS: A significant bidirectional association exists between diminished ovarian reserve and TgAb/TAI positivity. TAI may impair ovarian reserve, while women with ovarian insufficiency exhibit a higher burden of thyroglobulin autoantibodies. These findings highlight the clinical importance of TgAb screening in the evaluation of ovarian function among reproductive-age…

articles.title: Exploring LEPR Gene rs1137100 and rs1137101 Polymorphisms in Gestational Diabetes Mellitus: A Pilot Study From Bangladesh.
articles.authors: Tofail T, Shifat SK, Sayeed F et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) is a prevalent pregnancy complication that negatively impacts both the mother and the fetus. Leptin (LEP), a key regulator of glucose metabolism during pregnancy, is influenced by genetic factors. The rs1137101 single-nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) results in a glutamine-to-arginine substitution at position 223 in the LEP receptor, potentially affecting maternal and fetal metabolic outcomes.
METHODS: The study investigates the association of rs1137100 and rs1137101 polymorphisms in the LEPR gene with GDM. A total of 38 women with GDM and 72 controls were enrolled based on the WHO 2013 criteria, regardless of gestational age. Fasting insulin and LEP were measured using chemiluminescence immunoassay. Genetic samples were stored in ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid tubes, and genotyping of LEPR rs1137100 and rs1137101 was performed using Sanger sequencing. SNP analysis was done with SNPStats.
RESULTS: Fasting insulin (μIU/L) [GDM: 9.09 (4.18-14) vs normal glucose tolerance: 7.48 (3.06-11.9); P = 0.015] and LEP (ng/ml) [GDM: 170 (57.5-282.5) vs normal glucose tolerance: 118.4 (47.7-189.1); P = 0.031] levels were significantly elevated in GDM cases. Genotype frequencies of rs1137100 and rs1137101 showed no significant differences between GDM and controls (P > 0.05). Multivariate logistic regression under multiple genetic models also revealed no significant association. Linkage disequilibrium analysis indicated that the SNPs are not in linkage disequilibrium (D = -0.066, D' = 0.651, r2 = 0.106; P < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: This small pilot study found no statistically significant association of rs1137100 and rs1137101 polymorphisms in the LEPR gene with GDM in this Bangladeshi population cohort.

articles.title: Factors associated with breastfeeding difficulties in the early postpartum period in China: a cross-sectional study.
articles.authors: Lei F, Zhou S, Liu Y et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Within the unique clinical context of China, characterized by high cesarean section rates and specific postpartum practices, this study aims to investigate the prevalence and characteristics of breastfeeding difficulties in the early postpartum period (within 96 h postpartum) and identify associated factors, informing early clinical screening and targeted interventions.
METHODS: This cross-sectional study included 460 postpartum women recruited via convenience sampling from the obstetrics department of a tertiary specialized hospital in Chengdu between July 2023 and November 2024. All assessments were conducted between 24 and 96 h postpartum. Breastfeeding difficulty was operationally defined as the clinical presence of perceived insufficient milk, nipple/breast-related problems, or neonatal factors impeding effective feeding. Data were collected using a sociodemographic questionnaire, the Structured Clinical Breastfeeding Assessment Checklist, the LATCH scoring system, the Breastfeeding Self-Efficacy Scale-Short Form (BSES-SF), and the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS). Multivariate binary logistic regression was used to identify independently associated factors.
RESULTS: The prevalence of breastfeeding difficulties was 38.5% (177/460). The primary clinical manifestations were perceived insufficient milk supply (63.8%) and nipple-related problems (11.3%). Multivariate analysis demonstrated that infrequent breastfeeding (< 6 times/day; OR = 3.434), gestational diabetes mellitus (OR = 1.819), elevated pre-pregnancy BMI (24.0-27.9 kg/m2: OR = 2.484), and elevated postpartum depressive symptoms (OR = 3.365) were independently associated with higher odds of breastfeeding difficulties (all P < 0.05). Conversely, strong family support (OR= 0.911) and higher LATCH scores (OR = 0.646) showed a significant inverse association (all P < 0.05).
CONCLUSION: Breastfeeding difficulties are common during the early postpartum period and are associated with a combination of maternal physiological conditions, feeding skills, and psychosocial factors. Elevated BMI, gestational diabetes, infrequent early sucking, and elevated postpartum depressive symptoms are key independently associated factors, whereas strong family support and good latching skills show a significant inverse association. Clinical support should prioritize early screening for high-risk women, integrating physical, skill-based, psychological, and familial support to overcome early…

articles.title: Thoracic Endometriosis Mimicking a Lung Mass: Management With Single-Stage Biopsy and Microwave Ablation.
articles.authors: Hsieh M, Yang SM, Huang HN
articles.abstract: Thoracic endometriosis syndrome is a rare extrapelvic manifestation involving the pleura, diaphragm or lung parenchyma. Presentation as a solitary pulmonary nodule mimicking malignancy is uncommon. We report a 31-year-old asymptomatic woman with an enlarging right lower lobe nodule, measuring 1.8-2.1 cm over 3 months. Following shared decision-making, single-stage image-guided biopsy and microwave ablation (MWA) were performed. Histopathology confirmed pulmonary endometriosis. No clinically significant postoperative complications occurred, and the patient was discharged on postoperative Day 1. Follow-up CT at 6 and 12 months demonstrated no obvious local recurrence without additional treatment. This case describes a potential minimally invasive approach for selected pulmonary lesions, although the safety, efficacy and long-term outcomes of MWA for pulmonary endometriosis remain uncertain.

articles.title: Causes of discordance between noninvasive prenatal testing and fetal chromosomal status: a 10-year cohort study of 97, 743 cases.
articles.authors: Qi H, Chen H, Yuan X et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Noninvasive prenatal testing (NIPT) has been widely adopted for screening common fetal chromosomal aneuploidies, yet discordance between NIPT results and true fetal karyotypes remains a critical challenge limiting its clinical utility.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 97, 743 pregnant women who underwent NIPT at Ganzhou Women and Children's Health Care Hospital between April 2015 and December 2024 to evaluate the performance of NIPT and investigate the causes of discordance between NIPT results and fetal outcomes.
RESULTS: A total of 481 NIPT-positive cases were identified, yielding an overall positive rate of 0.49%. Of these, 380 cases underwent confirmatory testing (377 via invasive prenatal diagnosis and 3 via postnatal karyotyping). The overall positive predictive value (PPV) for the three common trisomies was 71.84%, with T21 showing the highest PPV (84.38%), followed by T18 (56.00%) and T13 (4.76%). Stratified analysis by Z-score demonstrated that PPVs for both T21 and T18 increased progressively with higher Z-score. For T21, PPV rose from 21.95% (Z: 3-6) to 100% (Z > 20); a similar upward trend was observed for T18. False-positive results were attributed to multiple mechanisms, including maternal chromosomal abnormalities (4 full 47, XX, + 21, 1 mosaic), vanishing twin (7 cases), uniparental disomy (2 cases), and confined placental mosaicism (CPM) (2 cases). Only 3 false-negative cases were identified, predominantly due to low-level placental mosaicism.
CONCLUSIONS: Discordance between NIPT and fetal karyotype exhibits a clear directional divergence: false-positive results are etiologically heterogeneous, involving maternal chromosomal abnormalities, substantially underestimated vanishing twin, CPM, and technical factors, whereas false-negative results are predominantly attributable to low-level CPM. Systematic analysis of Z-scores, maternal characteristics, and follow-up data can effectively identify most discordance causes, providing precise evidence for genetic counseling and pregnancy management. Our analytical framework provides a practical reference for optimizing NIPT screening strategies and reducing unnecessary invasive procedures in other regions.

articles.title: NGAL and traditional biomarkers in cervical cancer: a comparative evaluation using random forest.
articles.authors: Raci B, Stojkovska S, Hodolli G et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Tumor stage and biological aggressiveness have a significant impact on the prognosis of cervical cancer, which is still a serious global health concern.
METHODS: This work assesses an exploratory, leakage-free Random Forest model and describes longitudinal NGAL and traditional biomarker patterns in 100 individuals with cervical cancer. Since there was no independent radiologic, pathological, or defined response endpoint in the database, the machine-learning result was specifically characterized as an NGAL-decrease phenotype (post-treatment NGAL < pre-treatment NGAL), not clinical treatment response. All NGAL-derived variables and all post-treatment variables were removed from the predictor set in order to prevent target leakage.
RESULTS: The mean accuracy using stratified 5-fold cross validation was 43.0% (SD 7.6%) and the mean balanced accuracy was 42.1%, suggesting that there was no discriminative performance that was useful. Greater histological grades and more advanced broad-stage groups had descriptively greater NGAL concentrations.
DISCUSSION: These results do not prove clinical predictive usefulness; rather, they are hypothesis-generating.

articles.title: The effect of pelvic floor muscle exercise, progressive muscle relaxation exercise, and their combined application on comfort in women with stress urinary incontinence: a four-arm randomized controlled trial.
articles.authors: Şanlı A, Göke Arslan G, Çelik D et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Stress urinary incontinence (SUI) negatively affects women's physical, psychological, and social well-being and reduces comfort. Although pelvic floor muscle exercise (PFME) is the first-line conservative treatment, the additional contribution of progressive muscle relaxation exercise (PMR) to patient comfort remains unclear. This study aimed to evaluate the effects of PFME, PMR, and their combined application on comfort levels in women with SUI.
METHODS: This four-arm randomized controlled trial included 80 women diagnosed with SUI who were randomly assigned to the PFME group (n = 20), PMR group (n = 20), PFME + PMR group (n = 20), or control group (n = 20). Data were collected using a Descriptive Information Form and the Urinary Incontinence Frequency and Comfort Questionnaire (UIFCQ). Participants in the intervention groups performed the assigned exercise program for six weeks. Comfort was assessed at baseline and at Weeks 2, 4, and 6 through telephone interviews. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and mixed-design analysis of variance (Mixed ANOVA). A p-value of <0.05 was considered statistically significant.
RESULTS: Baseline comfort scores did not differ significantly among the groups (p > 0.05). Significant effects of time and the group×time interaction were observed (p < 0.001). Participants in the PFME group demonstrated significant improvements in comfort beginning at Week 2, which were maintained throughout the study. The PMR group showed gradual improvements in comfort across the follow-up period. In the combined PFME + PMR group, significant improvements became evident at the third and fourth assessments. Although slight changes were observed in the control group over time, the trajectories of improvement in all intervention groups were significantly greater than those in the control group.
CONCLUSIONS: PFME, PMR, and their combined application improved comfort over time in women with stress urinary incontinence. These findings suggest that structured conservative interventions, particularly the integration of PMR into pelvic floor rehabilitation programs, may enhance patient comfort and support comprehensive SUI management. Further multicenter randomized controlled trials with larger sample sizes and longer follow-up periods are warranted.
CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov, Identifier: NCT07762391, https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07762391.

articles.title: Embryos derived from small follicles (<8 mm) exhibit delayed blastulation: a retrospective time-lapse analysis.
articles.authors: Peker N, Yücetürk A, Karaosmanoğlu Ö et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Oocytes from small follicles are frequently discarded, although they may represent an additional resource in patients with few available oocytes. This study aimed to evaluate whether blastocysts derived from follicles <8 mm exhibit altered morphokinetic patterns compared with those from larger follicles.
METHODS: This retrospective study analyzed 62 blastocysts from 18 women undergoing ICSI: 20 from follicles <8 mm and 42 from follicles ≥11 mm. Morphokinetic parameters (tPNa-tB) were recorded by time-lapse monitoring. As several women contributed to both groups, linear mixed models with a random intercept for patient accounted for clustering. Oocyte- and embryo-level rates were compared using generalized estimating equations with patient as the clustering variable.
RESULTS: No between-group differences were observed for tPNa, tPNf or t2-t8. tSB occurred later in the <8 mm group (median 101.2 vs 95.3 h; p = 0.001), as did tB (108.1 vs 104.3 h; p=0.004). Differences persisted after accounting for within-patient clustering (tSB β = 7.91 h; tB β=8.29 h; both p<0.001). Day-5 blastocyst formation per fertilized oocyte was lower in the <8 mm group (28.8% vs 49.3%; p = 0.040), whereas overall blastocyst formation (38.5% vs 56.5%; p = 0.105) and day-6 rates (9.6% vs 7.2%; p = 0.683) did not differ significantly after accounting for within-patient clustering. Euploidy rates did not differ significantly between blastocysts derived from follicles <8 mm (5/10, 50.0%) and ≥11 mm (7/23, 30.4%; p = 0.433), although the number of biopsied embryos was small. Frozen-thawed single embryo transfer of two euploid blastocysts derived from follicles <8 mm resulted in two live births.
CONCLUSIONS: Follicle size is associated with the timing of blastocyst development, with embryos from smaller follicles showing an approximately 8-hour delay in blastulation. Day-6 blastocyst rates and euploidy rates did not differ significantly between groups. These exploratory findings suggest that delayed blastulation alone should not be taken as evidence of impaired developmental potential in embryos derived from small follicles.

articles.title: Expert Recommendations for Use of Combined Oral Contraceptives in Preadolescent and Young Adolescent Patients With Acne Vulgaris.
articles.authors: Zaenglein AL, Allen N, Bowden S et al.
articles.abstract: Acne vulgaris commonly presents in early adolescence with the onset of adrenarche. Treatments for acne in this age group typically mirror those in older adolescents. However, while combined oral contraceptives are an effective hormonal treatment for acne vulgaris in young women, the safety of using a systemic hormonal therapy in younger patients for the management of acne has not been established. Concerns include effects on pubertal development and weight, bone health, cancer risks, and psychiatric effects. This Pediatric Dermatology Research Alliance (PeDRA) consensus project convened a multidisciplinary work group to address these issues and, utilizing a modified Delphi process, to establish best practices regarding the use of combined oral contraceptives in patients under 16 years of age based on available evidence and expert opinion.

articles.title: Geographic Variation in Active Perinatal Management and Outcomes for Extremely Preterm Infants in New South Wales: A Population-Based Cohort Study.
articles.journal: The Australian & New Zealand journal of obstetrics & gynaecology
articles.ta: Aust N Z J Obstet Gynaecol
articles.authors: Williams N, Li C, Nassar N et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Perinatal management of infants born at 22-25 weeks' gestation varies internationally and may influence survival and long-term outcomes. In New South Wales (NSW), no contemporary statewide guideline exists.
AIMS: To evaluate rates of active delivery room management and associated survival and neurodevelopmental outcomes among infants born at 22-25 weeks' gestation in NSW.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Population-based cohort study of all live births at 22 + 0-25 + 6 weeks in NSW (2011-2019) using linked administrative and clinical datasets. Active management was defined as provision of respiratory support or higher in the delivery room. Primary outcomes were survival to 1 year and moderate or severe neurodevelopmental impairment (NDI) at 2-3 years.
RESULTS: Among 1285 live-born infants, 69.0% received active management, increasing from 61.7% in 2011 to 74.5% in 2019 (p < 0.001). Rates varied across local health districts (54.9%-83.5%). One-year survival was 44.9% overall (64.4% among actively managed infants) and increased with gestational age. Of 577 children eligible for follow-up, 440 (76.3%) underwent assessment at 2-3 years, of whom 18.4% had moderate or severe NDI. Maternal transfer to a tertiary centre was associated with a lower adjusted hazard of death (HR 0.79, 95% CI 0.63-0.98) but not with NDI.
CONCLUSIONS: Active management and survival increased over time; however, marked regional variation persists. Development of a statewide clinical practice guideline could support equitable, evidence-based care for extremely preterm births.

articles.title: A Comparative Study of Risk Factors and Neonatal Outcome between Preterm and Term Birth in a Tertiary Care Hospital.
articles.authors: Mandal M, Shrestha A
articles.abstract: Background Preterm birth is childbirth occurring at less than 37 completed weeks of pregnancy or before 259 days of gestation. These births lead to increased mortality and morbidity due to various short-term and long-term consequences. Identification of risk factors and early intervention are essential steps to decrease prevalence and ultimately reduce the associated neonatal mortality and morbidity. Objective To compare the risk factors and neonatal outcomes of preterm and term births in a tertiary care hospital. Method A comparative cross-sectional study was conducted in the Department of Obstetrics and Gynaecology at Dhulikhel Hospital from March 2024 to March 2025. A convenient sample of 160 participants (80 preterm and 80 term births) were enrolled using a non-probability sampling method. Data were collected through structured interviews and analysed using SPSS version 25. The Chi square test was applied to identify statistically significant characteristics, which were then analysed using multivariate logistic regression to explore the association of risk factors between preterm and term births. Result Factors found to be statistically significant on the Chi square test included maternal infection, irregular calcium consumption, previous history of preterm birth, exposure to indoor pollution, maternal comorbidities, and hospital admission of the neonate. Multivariate logistic regression analysis showed that women with Urinary tract infection (p= 0.008, AOR = 2.53), previous history of preterm birth (p = 0.02, AOR = 2.12), and hypertension (p = 0.018, AOR = 10.48) were significantly associated with the risk of preterm birth. Preterm babies had an increased risk of hospital admission (p = 0.003, AOR = 4.57). Conclusion Urinary tract infection, hypertension, and a prior history of preterm birth are major maternal risk factors for preterm delivery. Preterm neonates exhibit increased morbidity and are more likely to require hospital admission.

articles.title: Gay Fathers, Triplet Children: Trifecta Perfecta; Tribute to Dr Alec Roy / Twin Research Reviews: Twin Study of Dog Ownership; Twinning Rates in Awassi Ewes; MZ Male Twins with Mitochondrial Encephalomyopathy; Twin Study of Meditation / Human Interest Stories: Twins with Unrelated Parental Sets; Twins Born in Different Years; Valedictorian-Salutatorian Pair; Annual Twins Days Festival; FBI Identical Twin Identification Dilemmas; Identical Twin Doctors.
articles.journal: Twin research and human genetics : the official journal of the International Society for Twin Studies
articles.authors: Segal N
articles.abstract: The main feature of this essay concerns a dizygotic triplet set born to a gay male couple. In vitro fertilization (IVF), using egg donation and surrogacy, is becoming a more common method of choice for same-sex male couples wishing to have families. This story is followed by a tribute to a late colleague, Dr Alec Roy. The next section presents twin research reviews of dog ownership, twinning rates in Awassi ewes, monozygotic male twins with mitochondrial encephalomyopathy, and a novel twin study of meditation. Several human-interest items capture other informative aspects of twinship. They include twins with unrelated biological parents, twins born in different years, a valedictorian-salutatorian pair; highlights from the Annual Twins Days Festival, an FBI identical twin identification dilemma, and a pair of identical twin doctors.

articles.title: Single-cell profiling of cross-tissue features of fetal pig macrophages and their remodeling in fetal growth restriction.
articles.authors: Lai CL, Chen XY, Cai LP
articles.abstract: Macrophages are highly heterogeneous immune cells with context-dependent functions, yet their diversity across prenatal tissues of the whole body, sexes, and stages remains elusive. During fetal development, macrophages play essential roles in tissue formation and maintaining maternal-fetal immune balance, but their specific phenotypic and functional changes in the context of fetal growth restriction remain relatively underexplored. Herein, we constructed a cross-tissue macrophage atlas of 85 473 cells from 54 tissues of late-gestation fetal pigs. We identified 15 macrophage subtypes, among which two Hofbauer cell (HBC) subtypes were distinguished by their distinct transcriptional and functional characteristics between the amniotic and chorioallantoic membranes: HBC GPNMB+ cells upregulated glycolytic enzymes and extracellular matrix regulators such as LDHA and GPNMB, while HBC PEG10+ cells expressed immunomodulators and developmental regulators, including A2M and PEG10. Two dichotomous subtypes, LYVE1 highMHCII low and LYVE1 lowMHCII high, were delineated across 27 tissues, with a conserved transcriptional signature in pigs and humans. Transcriptional profiling of metabolic pathways revealed oxidative phosphorylation and the tricarboxylic acid cycle as core pathways across tissues, alongside tissue-specific adaptations such as enhanced glycolysis in amniotic macrophages. Cross-stage comparisons showed fetal macrophages mainly maintained developmental programs, whereas adult macrophages globally exhibited heightened immune activity. Cross-sex and cross-species analyses revealed high transcriptomic similarity in fetal macrophages. In growth-restricted fetuses, chorioallantoic HBCs showed profound remodeling, including increased inflammation, hypoxia response, and vascular dysfunction signaling, with altered intercellular communication. Collectively, this work provides a comprehensive resource for understanding fetal macrophage heterogeneity and offers insights into the potential mechanisms underlying fetal growth restriction.

articles.title: Next-generation incretin therapeutics for polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome: navigating current pipeline and clinical considerations.
articles.authors: Ozgen Saydam B, Yıldız BO
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS), formerly known as polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), is a complex metabolic-reproductive disorder managed with lifestyle interventions, metformin, and symptom-directed therapies. Incretin-based therapies offer substantial metabolic benefits, but their reproductive efficacy, durability, and phenotypic safety remain incompletely defined.
AREAS COVERED: This narrative review examines the therapeutic evolution from single glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonists to dual glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP)/GLP-1 receptor agonism with tirzepatide and triple GIP/GLP-1/glucagon receptor agonism with retatrutide. A structured PubMed search of studies published from January 2023 to October 2026 was supplemented by ClinicalTrials.gov and reference-list screening. Evidence was evaluated across metabolic, hormonal, and reproductive outcomes.
EXPERT OPINION: Single GLP-1 receptor agonists, particularly semaglutide, improve weight, adiposity, and insulin resistance, with emerging evidence of reproductive benefits. Multi-incretin therapies may provide greater reductions in body weight, visceral and ectopic fat, and insulin resistance. However, PMOS-specific reproductive evidence remains limited. Whether reproductive benefits are independent of weight loss, persist after treatment withdrawal, or differ across PMOS phenotypes is uncertain. Phenotype-stratified randomized trials with standardized reproductive, metabolic, cardiovascular and safety endpoints are needed to determine whether multi-incretins provide durable benefits beyond weight control while maintaining reproductive safety and accessibility.

articles.title: Evaluation of Fallopian Tube Patency in Patients With Endometriosis-Induced Infertility by SONAZOID Real-Time Four-Dimensional Salpingography.
articles.authors: Mao S, Zhang M, Dong W et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: To evaluate SONAZOID real-time four-dimensional hysterosalpingography (4D-HyCoSy) for assessing fallopian tube patency in endometriosis (EM)-induced infertility.
METHODS: A retrospective study of 100 patients (200 fallopian tubes) underwent SONAZOID 4D-HyCoSy. Patients were divided into six groups based on varying degrees of tubal patency or obstruction. A liquid injection machine was employed to record the peak pressure for contrast agent injection, and the corresponding pain score of the patients was noted. Contrast agent reflux and quantitative range were observed in each group. Hysteroscopy combined with laparoscopy was considered the gold standard.
RESULTS: The diagnostic accuracy of 4D-HyCoSy was 95.23% (20/21) compared to laparoscopy. Peak pressure and pain scores were significantly higher in patients with bilateral obstruction than in the other groups (p < 0.05). Effect sizes for significant comparisons were predominantly large (Hedges' g > 0.8), indicating clinically meaningful differences.
CONCLUSION: 4D-HyCoSy, combined with quantitative indicators like intrauterine peak pressure, pain score, and contrast reflux, provides an effective and objective assessment of tubal patency in EM-induced infertility, thereby offering a valuable imaging reference for clinical evaluation of tubal status.

articles.title: Thoracoamniotic shunting for fetal pleural effusion and congenital lung lesions: systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.journal: Ultrasound in obstetrics & gynecology : the official journal of the International Society of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology
articles.authors: Callado GY, Arechvo A, Ruíz-Román R et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To summarize reported outcomes associated with thoracoamniotic shunting (TAS) in fetuses with pleural effusion or congenital lung lesions.
METHODS: We conducted a search across MEDLINE, CINAHL, Cochrane CENTRAL, Web of Science, Scopus, and EMBASE databases, from inception to 6 November 2025, for studies reporting the incidence of perinatal outcomes after TAS in pregnancies complicated by fetal pleural effusion or congenital lung lesions. Quality and risk-of-bias assessments were performed utilizing the Downs and Black scale. Single-arm random-effects meta-analyses with generalized linear mixed-effects models were performed to generate pooled proportions with 95% CI. Heterogeneity was assessed using Cochran's Q and quantified by the I2 statistic. Subgroup analyses were conducted according to the primary diagnosis (pleural effusion or congenital lung lesions).
RESULTS: Overall, 45 studies, including 1976 fetuses that underwent TAS, were included in the systematic review. Among fetuses with pleural effusion, the pooled proportion of fetal death was 8.3% (95% CI, 5.8-11.6%) (I2 = 18.1%) and that of perinatal death was 29.5% (95% CI, 26.4-32.7%) (I2 = 27.7%). In cases of congenital lung lesion, the corresponding pooled proportions were 6.6% (95% CI, 3.5-12.1%) (I2 = 0%) and 22.6% (95% CI, 13.2-35.9%) (I2 = 0%), respectively. Shunt-related complications included shunt displacement (13.2% (95% CI, 8.8-19.4%) in cases of pleural effusion and 10.2% (95% CI, 4.3-22.3%) in cases of congenital lung lesion) and shunt obstruction or malfunction (14.1% (95% CI, 9.1-21.1%) and 8.6% (95% CI, 2.8-23.4%), respectively). Preterm prelabor rupture of membranes after TAS was reported in 19.3% (95% CI, 13.8-26.4%) of cases of pleural effusion and 15.4% (95% CI, 5.9-34.5%) of cases of congenital lung lesion, and birth < 37 weeks occurred in 64.3% (95% CI, 58.1-70.2%) and 41.6% (95% CI, 29.4-54.8%) of cases, respectively. In hydropic fetuses, resolution of hydrops was achieved in 63.3% (95% CI, 52.9-72.6%) of cases of pleural effusion and 95.1% (95% CI, 82.5-98.8%) of cases of congenital lung lesion.
CONCLUSIONS: TAS in fetuses with pleural effusion or congenital lung lesions is associated with prenatal thoracic decompression and may contribute to resolution of pleural effusion and hydrops in selected cases, with indirect comparisons with historical data suggesting a possible reduction in mortality. Standardized selection criteria and prospective and/or multicenter…

articles.title: Lifetime Endogenous Estrogen Exposure Predicts Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis Risk in Postmenopausal Women Based on a Nationwide Population Study.
articles.authors: Kim BG, Han K, Seo HT et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Conflicting results exist regarding the association between endogenous estrogen exposure and the risk of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF). We aimed to investigate the relationship between lifetime endogenous estrogen exposure and the development of IPF among postmenopausal women.
METHODS: Using the Korean National Health Insurance Service database for the period between 1 January 2009 and 31 December 2022, we analyzed a total of 1,388,645 postmenopausal women without previous history of IPF in 2009. The exposure was lifetime endogenous estrogen exposure (duration between the age of menarche and the age of menopause). The primary outcome was new-onset IPF. Participants were followed until the date of new IPF diagnosis, death, or 31 December 2022.
RESULTS: During the median follow-up period of 12.4 (interquartile range, 12.1-12.7) years, 0.13% of postmenopausal women developed IPF, with an incidence rate of 0.109 per 1,000 person-years. There was a dose-dependent inverse relationship between endogenous estrogen exposure and the incidence of IPF (0.144/1,000 person-years for < 30 years, 0.104/1,000 person-years for 30-39 years and 0.101/1,000 person-years for ≥ 40 years). Multivariable Cox-regression analysis showed that the risk of developing IPF was dose-dependently decreased as endogenous estrogen exposure increased (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR], 0.85; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.75-0.96 for 30-39 years; aHR, 0.77; 95% CI, 0.61-0.96 for ≥ 40 years compared to < 30 years).
CONCLUSION: Among postmenopausal women, lifetime endogenous estrogen exposure showed a protective role from developing IPF.

articles.title: Circulating Estradiol as an Independent Risk Factor for Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease and Fibrosis Risk in Women: Evidence From a Multicenter Health-Checkup Cohort.
articles.authors: Cho HJ, Kang SH, Chon HY et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) shows marked sexual dimorphism, with estrogen believed to be liver-protective. This study investigated the independent association between circulating estradiol levels, MASLD, and advanced fibrosis (defined by fibrosis index-4 [FIB-4] ≥ 1.3) in Korean women, utilizing stratified analyses by age and body mass index (BMI) to identify context-dependent effects.
METHODS: We analyzed cross-sectional data from the Korean Health Screening-Based Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease Registry, including 995 women (352 with MASLD). Multivariable logistic regression was used to evaluate the association of log2-transformed estradiol with MASLD and high-risk fibrosis, stratified by age (proxy for menopausal status, ≥ 50 vs. < 50 years) and BMI (≥ 25 vs. < 25 kg/m²).
RESULTS: In multivariable analysis of the entire cohort, lower estradiol levels were independently associated with MASLD (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 0.88; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.79-0.98; P = 0.025). This association was particularly evident in women with lower BMI (aOR, 0.84; 95% CI, 0.71-0.98), but not in high BMI women, suggesting attenuation of estrogen's metabolic protection in the presence of obesity. Estradiol demonstrated a strong and consistent inverse association with FIB-4 ≥ 1.3 (aOR, 0.65; 95% CI, 0.56-0.75; P < 0.001). This protective antifibrotic effect remained robust across BMI strata and was also significant in women aged ≥ 50 years (aOR, 0.70; 95% CI, 0.59-0.82; P < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: Low circulating estradiol independently increases the risk of MASLD and high-risk fibrosis in women. While its protective effect against steatosis weakens with obesity, its antifibrotic effect remains strong across all subgroups. Estradiol may serve as an important hormonal marker for risk stratification in female MASLD patients.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT06843421.

articles.title: Diagnostic accuracy of a systematic approach using Swedescore versus conventional colposcopy for the detection of cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 2 or worse: A multicenter, non-randomized clinical study.
articles.authors: Knudsen AS, Gustafson LW, Booth BB et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Globally, colposcopy is often performed by non-experts with no certification or routine use of colposcopic scoring tools. A systematic colposcopic scoring tool, the Swedescore, has been developed to enhance the detection rate of cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 2 or worse (CIN2+). We aimed to compare the diagnostic accuracy of two colposcopy methods (systematic use of the Swedescore versus conventional colposcopy) for detecting CIN2+.
MATERIAL AND METHODS: This multicenter, non-randomized clinical study included women (23-65 years) referred for colposcopy and with a visible transformation zone (type 1 and 2). Colposcopy was performed using the systematic scoring tool, Swedescore, or the conventional method. All women had four cervical biopsies collected. Colposcopists collected lesion-directed biopsies (target biopsies) from abnormal areas with or without non-lesion-directed biopsies (random biopsies) from areas that appeared normal. The gold standard was the most severe diagnosis (CIN2+) based on all four biopsies. The primary outcome was CIN2+. We calculated sensitivity (SN), specificity (SP), positive predictive value (PPV), and negative predictive value (NPV) with 95% confidence intervals and compared results between the two methods. Results were stratified by age, body mass index (BMI), human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination status, screening method, index cytology, index HPV type, and colposcopists. Clinical Trial Registration ClinicalTrials.gov NCT05870787.
RESULTS: Among 929 women included (Swedescore: 534, conventional: 395), the diagnostic accuracy for the detection of CIN2+ was slightly higher with the Swedescore compared to the conventional method (SN: 84.7% vs. 77.8%, SP: 37.3% vs. 30.9%, PPV: 47.6% vs. 43.9%, NPV: 78.3% vs. 66.7%). Sensitivity for CIN2+ was significantly higher with the Swedescore compared to the conventional method in women ≥50 years (92.9% vs. 62.5%), those with high-grade cytology (92.4% vs. 83.2%), and when colposcopy was performed by residents (91.8% vs. 70.6%). Regardless of HPV vaccination status and screening method, the Swedescore performed slightly better than the conventional method, although the differences were not statistically significant.
