CONCLUSIONS: Our findings may suggest that, in a non-expert setting, a systematic colposcopic examination using the Swedescore was associated with a slightly higher diagnostic accuracy for detecting CIN2+ compared to the conventional method. These…

articles.title: Genitourinary Syndrome of Lactation: Patient-Reported Survey of Symptom Burden, Care Gaps, and Treatment Utilization in the Postpartum Period.
articles.authors: Perelmuter S, Drian A, Vereecken SJ et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate genitourinary symptoms during lactation and identify barriers to care among postpartum individuals.
METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional survey study from March to May 2025 using an anonymous, 30-item online questionnaire. Eligible participants were postpartum individuals up to 24 months after delivery. Exclusion criteria included nulliparity, current pregnancy, prior genitourinary disorders, and incomplete responses. Participants were stratified into exclusive, nonexclusive, and nonlactating groups. Primary outcomes included genitourinary symptoms, treatments offered and utilized, and quality of life scores (0-100). Quantitative data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, chi-square tests, and multinomial logistic regression (α = 0.05). Qualitative data were assessed using thematic analysis.
RESULTS: Of 1,446 respondents (median age 36 years), 47.65% were exclusively lactating, 14.66% were mixed feeding, and 37.69% were nonlactating. Vaginal dryness was the most common symptom (exclusive: 100%; nonexclusive: 100%; nonlactating: 78.72%), followed by dyspareunia (57.04%, 50.00%, and 36.33%). Functional impairments were prevalent with 76.34% of exclusively lactating participants reporting difficulty with sexual activity. Despite symptom burden, 63.81% were never asked about genitourinary concerns, and only 28.42% were offered treatment. Awareness of lactation-compatible therapies was limited (60.03% unaware). Vaginal estrogen and pelvic floor physiotherapy were most commonly recommended, but to fewer than 30% of symptomatic individuals. Lactation status was significantly associated with symptom presence and treatment patterns (p < 0.001). Themes highlighted severe pain, disrupted intimacy, and lack of provider support.
CONCLUSIONS: Genitourinary symptoms during lactation are common yet inadequately managed. Care models should incorporate routine screening, provider education on lactation-safe therapies, and improved access to multidisciplinary interventions.

articles.title: Perceived Causes of Fertility Challenges and Utilization of Infertility Treatment Modalities: Insights from U.S. Black Women.
articles.authors: Morgan I, Clarke LS, Palmquist AEL et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: To qualitatively explore what Black women themselves perceive as the causes of their fertility challenges and examine the treatment modalities utilized to address infertility.
METHODS: The study included 40 Black women aged 25-45 years, with a history of fertility challenges, residing in the United States, who completed the Fertility Equity Study between 2021 and 2023. Participants completed a survey and up to two semi-structured interviews to discuss their fertility journeys and perceived causes of fertility challenges. We examined and synthesized participant perceptions about the causes of their challenges in conceiving or maintaining a pregnancy. Frequencies and percentages were calculated for each common cause of fertility challenges and treatment modalities used.
RESULTS: Participants described five common perceived causes of their fertility challenges: (1) clinically diagnosed reproductive health conditions (n = 26; e.g., fibroids, oligospermia); 2) age (n = 7); (3) unknown causes (n = 6); (4) structural issues (n = 4; e.g., limited access to Black donor sperm); and (5) stress (n = 4). Nearly half of participants (n = 19) only used medically assisted reproduction (MAR), whereas one-third (n = 13) had a history of using both MAR and holistic approaches (e.g., herbal teas). None of the participants who only used holistic fertility treatment modalities attributed their fertility challenges to reproductive health conditions.
CONCLUSIONS: This study reflects the nuanced ways that Black women conceptualize their fertility and the antecedents to fertility challenges. These results reflect the need to integrate holistic and spiritual approaches into fertility care and MAR to appeal to the needs of Black women and families navigating infertility.

articles.title: Fibroids and the risk of miscarriage: a prospective observational study in an early pregnancy population.
articles.journal: Journal of obstetrics and gynaecology : the journal of the Institute of Obstetrics and Gynaecology
articles.authors: Vasireddy A, Sampson U, Channing R et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The impact of fibroids on pregnancy outcomes has been studied extensively in the context of in vitro fertilisation; however, evidence in the general obstetric population is limited. No prospective studies from the United Kingdom have examined the relationship between fibroids and early pregnancy loss in a mixed population. This study evaluated the association between fibroids and miscarriage in women presenting to an Early Pregnancy Unit (EPU).
METHODS: Prospective observational study conducted over 15 months, involving 416 women with singleton pregnancies <10 weeks' gestation at a London tertiary EPU. Participants with fibroids (n = 104) were compared with controls (n = 312); all underwent systematic ultrasound, and confounder data were collected. The primary outcome was miscarriage before 24 weeks; secondary outcomes included gestation of miscarriage, second-trimester pain and bleeding.
RESULTS: Miscarriage occurred in 65 women: 22.9% with fibroids versus 14.6% without (unadjusted odds ratio [OR] 1.74, 95% CI 0.98-3.10; p = .059); after adjustment, the association was attenuated (adjusted OR [aOR] 1.49, 95% CI 0.82-2.70; p = .19). Increasing fibroid number was associated with higher risk (OR per additional fibroid 1.17, 95% CI 1.01-1.37; p = .04). First-trimester miscarriage was higher with fibroids (unadjusted relative risk ratio [RRR] 1.99, 95% CI 1.09-3.61, p = .024); although this association was attenuated with age (aOR 1.59, 95% CI 0.86-2.93, p = .14; adjusted RRR 1.63, 95% CI 0.88-3.04, p = .12). Other fibroid characteristics and uterine volume did not significantly influence miscarriage risk. Second-trimester pain was more common with fibroids (OR 2.92, 95% CI 1.43-5.97, p < .05); there was no difference in bleeding.
CONCLUSION: A higher miscarriage rate was observed with fibroids; however, there was no independent association after adjustment. Our study was underpowered to detect a small difference in miscarriage rate. Women of advanced maternal age can be counselled that their risk of miscarriage is influenced more by age than the presence of fibroids.

articles.title: Advances in the pharmacological management of genitourinary syndrome of menopause.
articles.authors: Messina S, Salvatore S, Petrone M et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Genitourinary syndrome of menopause (GSM) results from climacteric estrogens drop and leads to bothersome and progressive genital and lower urinary tract symptoms. Given the high frequency of GSM in the female population and the impact on quality of life, it is crucial to find a safe and effective treatment. Pharmacological therapies aim to modulate the hormonal system and to restore tissue morphology and function to a premenopausal state.
AREAS COVERED: We analyzed the scientific evidence indexed in PubMed, Google Scholar, and Medscape concerning the main pharmacological treatments, which include systemic and topical therapies. The aim of this review was to evaluate the efficacy of each treatment in the management of genital and urinary symptoms, as well as sexual dysfunction, associated with GSM.
EXPERT OPINION: Despite the availability of several pharmacological options, GSM management remains a complex and highly individualized clinical challenge. Current evidence supports the efficacy of local therapies and selective estrogen receptor modulators (SERMs) in improving genital, urinary, and sexual symptoms. Future perspectives should focus on a multimodal, personalized approach integrating pharmacological treatments with innovative therapies, guided by shared decision-making to optimize long-term outcomes and quality of life.

articles.title: Knockdown of mitotically associated long non-coding RNA dysregulates endothelial functions, transcriptome and proteome.
articles.authors: Zhang SY, Zhou C, Zheng J
articles.abstract: Preeclampsia (PE) is a hypertensive disorder during pregnancy, which is characterized by a wide spectrum of endothelial dysfunction. However, the mechanisms underlying PE-associated endothelial dysfunction remain poorly understood. Our previous RNA-sequencing analysis showed that PE down-regulated mitotically-associated long non-coding RNA (MANCR) in human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs). Herein, we tested the hypothesis that knockdown of MANCR dysregulates endothelial functions via disrupting the transcriptome and proteome using HUVECs as a cell model. Reverse transcription quantitative PCR (RT-qPCR) was conducted to confirm the down-regulation of MANCR in PE-HUVECs. MANCR was knocked down in HUVECs from normotensive pregnancy using antisense oligonucleotides (ASOs), followed by functional assays, RNA-sequencing and proteomics. RT-qPCR revealed that PE decreased MANCR in male and female HUVECs. Compared with scrambled ASOs, MANCR ASOs reduced MANCR by 71% and 74% in male and female HUVECs, respectively. Functionally, MANCR ASOs blocked fibroblast growth factor-2 (FGF2)- and vascular endothelial growth factor-A (VEGFA)-stimulated cell proliferation, whereas they did not affect cell chemotaxis and tube formation in responses to FGF2 and VEGFA. MANCR ASOs dysregulated the expression of 37 and 39 genes as well as 97 and 15 proteins in male and female cells, respectively. Bioinformatics analysis predicted that MANCR-regulated genes and proteins in male and female HUVECs were differently associated with diseases and biological functions, many of which are relevant to cell mitosis and hypertension. Thus, down-regulation of MANCR impairs endothelial functions and causes sex-specific disruption of transcriptome and proteome, possibly partially contributing to PE-associated fetal endothelial dysfunction. KEY POINTS: Preeclampsia causes widespread endothelial dysfunction, but the roles of long non-coding RNAs in endothelial cells remain poorly understood. Mitotically associated long non-coding RNA (MANCR) is down-regulated in human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs) obtained from preeclampsia. We provide the first evidence that down-regulation of MANCR blocks endothelial cell proliferation stimulated by fibroblast growth factor 2 and vascular endothelial growth factor A. We also demonstrate that down-regulation of MANCR disrupts transcriptome and proteome as well as pathways associated with cell division, cardiovascular disease-related processes…

articles.title: Clinical Criteria for Imaging in Children at Risk for Pulmonary Embolism.
articles.authors: Koul PB, Hanna I, Crisp A
articles.abstract: Pulmonary embolism (PE) is a rare but serious condition in children. Clinical guidelines for imaging a suspected pediatric PE in Pediatric Emergency Medicine (PEM) are lacking. The computerized tomography pulmonary angiogram (CTPA) is the preferred diagnostic modality for suspected PE in an emergency department. Our study aims to introduce a simplified clinical assessment tool for ordering CTPA in children in the emergency room. This is a retrospective review of patients managed in our Emergency Department from 2000 to 2020. Patients were identified using International Classification of Diseases codes for PE, deep vein thrombosis, or similar diagnoses. The control group consisted of patients with PE symptoms, seen within the same time frame as the study group, who had negative CTPA. Twenty-five CTPA-positive patients were identified. Twenty-three of 25 CTPA-positive patients were aged 13 to 18 years. Common risk factors include protein-losing state (ie, nephrotic syndrome), oral contraceptive pill use, and obesity. Chest pain and tachypnea were the most common complaint and clinical sign, respectively. The hypercoagulability screen was negative in 65% of the patients. The mean D-dimer was 5.27 g/mL, and 6 patients, of whom 4 had saddle PE, had D-dimer > 10. Recurrence of PE and neurologic deficits were noted in 2 patients each. We present clinical criteria for ordering CTPA in children with suspected PE based on data from our center and a literature review of pediatric studies. Further multicenter studies with larger samples are needed to validate our proposed criteria.

articles.title: Effects of progestin-primed ovarian stimulation protocol plus clomiphene citrate in patients with low basal LH levels: a randomized controlled trial.
articles.authors: Hu Z, Fan Y, Zhou X et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Infertile patients with low basal luteinizing hormone (LH) levels have low oocyte retrieval rate, but whether progestin-primed ovarian stimulation (PPOS) protocol with clomiphene citrate (CC) could enhance oocyte retrieval rate in these patients remains unclear.
METHODS: This prospective randomized controlled trial was performed between January 2018 and February 2021, included 230 infertile patients with low basal LH levels (LH < 2.27 mIU/mL). In study group, 115 patients received human menopausal gonadotropin (hMG) 150 or 225 IU/d + CC 50 mg/d + medroxyprogesterone acetate (MPA) 10 mg/d from the third day of menstruation. In control group, 115 patients received hMG 150 or 225 IU/d + MPA 10 mg/d from the third day of menstruation. Viable embryos were cryopreserved for later transfer. The primary outcome measure was the oocyte retrieval rate.
RESULTS: CC contributed to LH secretion. The hMG+MPA+CC group showed a decreased oocyte retrieval rate (0.71 ± 0.22 vs. 0.76 ± 0.18, mean difference (MD) -0.06 (-0.11 to -0.01); P = 0.043) and a decreased number of cryopreserved embryos (2.89 ± 2.43 vs. 3.90 ± 2.39, MD -0.89 (-1.50 to -0.28); FDR-P = 0.035). Two groups had similar number of retrieved oocytes (8.83 ± 5.41 vs. 10.69 ± 5.85, MD -0.99 (-2.27 to 0.29); FDR-P = 0.213) and oocyte utilization rate (0.40 ± 0.25 vs. 0.46 ± 0.24, MD -0.07 (-0.14 to -0.01); FDR-P = 0.084). Two groups had comparable cumulative clinical pregnancy rates (61.05% vs. 77.67%, hazard ratio (HR) 0.74 (0.53 to 1.06); P = 0.101; FDR-P = 0.214) and cumulative live birth rates (53.68% vs. 66.02%, HR 0.77 (0.53 to 1.13); P = 0.183; FDR-P = 0.214).
CONCLUSIONS: CC contributed to LH secretion, but PPOS protocol with CC resulted in a lower oocyte retrieval rate in patients with low basal LH levels. PPOS protocol with CC should be used cautiously in these patients.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ChiCTR number: ChiCTR1800014440. URL: https://www.chictr.org.cn/showproj.html?proj=24573 . Date of registration: 2018/01/13. Date of enrollment of the first subject: 2018/1/17.

articles.title: Temporal patterns of serial intraoperative peritoneal cytology among patients undergoing cup-assisted surgery for endometrial cancer: a single-center observational process-monitoring study.
articles.authors: Chen W, Lin L, Liu B et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The relationship between uterine manipulation during minimally invasive surgery for endometrial cancer and intraoperative peritoneal tumor-cell shedding remains uncertain. We described serial cytological patterns across predefined operative landmarks without estimating manipulator-specific or irrigation-specific effects.
METHODS: This single-center observational process-monitoring study included patients undergoing laparoscopically initiated surgery between June 2018 and August 2024. Eligibility for the cytology-evaluable cohort required a final diagnosis of primary endometrial cancer and at least one evaluable intraoperative cytology result. The primary analysis included cup-assisted cases; no comparable no-manipulator hysterectomy group was available. Cytology was obtained before cup placement (T0), after hysterectomy (T1), after 1,000 mL sterile-water irrigation and saline-based sampling (T2), and after cumulative 2,000 mL irrigation and repeat sampling (T3). Abnormal cytology comprised suspicious/atypical or positive/malignant findings. Adjacent transitions were assessed with exact McNemar tests; complete trajectories required evaluable T0-T3 data. No cytology values were imputed.
RESULTS: Of 163 screened patients, 119 were cytology-evaluable, 113 underwent cup-assisted surgery, and 96 had complete T0-T3 data. Abnormal cytology occurred in 4/96, 6/96, 1/96, and 1/96 patients at T0, T1, T2, and T3, respectively. A T0-negative to T1-abnormal transition occurred in 5/94 patients (5.3%; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.7-12.0). Five of six T1-abnormal results were suspicious/atypical and one was positive/malignant; all six were negative at T2 (100.0%; 95% CI, 54.1-100.0). The T1-to-T2 comparison included seven discordant pairs (exact McNemar P = 0.125). At the administrative data cutoff of May 1, 2026, 94 of the 119 cytology-evaluable patients (79.0%) had a verifiable last follow-up date, whereas 25 (21.0%) were lost to follow-up; no recurrence was documented among the 94 patients with confirmed follow-up.
CONCLUSIONS: Serial cytological changes were uncommon, but sparse events, indeterminate findings, incomplete sampling, procedural heterogeneity, absence of appropriate surgical and irrigation controls, and lack of centralized rereview, biological validation, recovered-volume measurement, and irrigation-specific safety assessment limit interpretation. Negative T2 cytology indicates non-detection in one specimen, not biological elimination.…

articles.title: Shared struggles: Muslim, migrant, lesbian, gay, single and older experiences of accessing assisted reproductive technology.
articles.journal: International journal for equity in health
articles.authors: Davies SG, Martin-Anatias N, Truyts C
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Access to assisted reproductive technology (ART) is shaped by intersecting medical, legal, cultural and financial factors. While biological infertility is well studied, social infertility (where societal conditions constrain reproductive possibilities) remains comparatively underexplored. Existing research identifies distinct barriers affecting LGBTQ+ people, migrants, religious communities, people of colour, rural populations, and those with limited financial resources. Although group-specific research reveals important forms of exclusion, a siloed approach can obscure shared institutional barriers. Comparative analysis is therefore needed to examine where barriers converge, where they operate differently, and how these differences shape access to ART.
METHODS: We conducted a qualitative study in Aotearoa New Zealand between 2020 and 2023, comprising 52 in-depth interviews with 73 individuals and four focus groups with 40 participants (total n = 113). Participants included heterosexual, gay, lesbian, older, single, coupled, Muslim, migrant, Māori and Pacific individuals. Recruitment occurred through fertility clinics, community organisations, and social networks. Data were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis, followed by structured comparison of where barriers converged, differed in form, were especially pronounced, or were not clearly evidenced across participant groups.
RESULTS: Six recurring barriers were identified: exclusionary clinical design; privileging of the heterosexual nuclear family; cultural and religious tensions around kinship and permissible reproduction; emotional labour and parental deservingness; scarcity and governance of gametes and surrogacy; and economic barriers. These barriers did not occur uniformly. For example, donor scarcity affected single women and lesbian participants through waitlists and donor availability, Muslim participants through restrictions on third-party gametes, and gay men through dependence on both egg donation and surrogacy. Funding rules were especially consequential where age, residency, BMI and pathway-specific costs intersected with migration trajectories, singlehood, sexuality, and later-life family formation.
CONCLUSIONS: The findings identify cross-group convergence in institutional barriers without suggesting that different social locations are interchangeable. Reproductive inequity is produced through distinct mechanisms, including formal funding rules, clinic and administrative…

articles.title: Barriers to and facilitators of gestational diabetes mellitus service utilization in Kenya: a qualitative analysis of women's and healthcare workers' perspectives.
articles.authors: Obongo A, Eger H, Tallarek M et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) is a growing global public health concern, particularly in low- and middle-income countries such as Kenya. Despite rising prevalence and associated maternal and neonatal risks, timely diagnosis and comprehensive GDM care remain limited by systemic, socioeconomic, and cultural barriers. This study identified barriers and facilitators influencing GDM care provision and utilization in Kisumu County, Kenya, from the perspectives of healthcare workers (HCWs) and women affected by GDM.
METHODS: A qualitative content analysis combined semistructured interviews and structured surveys. Participants were purposively sampled from two healthcare facilities in Kisumu County: Jaramogi Oginga Odinga Teaching and Referral Hospital and Kisumu Specialists Hospital. Interviews involved eight HCWs and two women diagnosed with GDM, and surveys were administered to eleven women with a history of GDM. Data collection instruments, developed from the health needs assessment and knowledge, attitude, and behaviour frameworks, were validated by an expert panel from Kenya and Germany. Thematic analysis identified key barriers to and facilitators of GDM care.
RESULTS: Stakeholders highlighted systemic gaps and resource constraints affecting GDM care, including high costs, inadequate insurance, supply shortages, and poor infrastructure, which especially affected rural and low-income women. Barriers including financial burden, distance, inconsistent protocols, communication gaps, and negative patient-provider relationships hindered access and adherence. Facilitators included family and social support, health worker education and follow-up, and self-management through dietary counseling, monitoring, and lifestyle changes. All groups advocated universal screening, expanded insurance, community outreach, and better education to strengthen GDM care and improve outcomes.
CONCLUSIONS: GDM care provision and utilization in Kenya are shaped by multilevel barriers spanning individual, systemic, and cultural domains. Addressing them requires targeted interventions, including enhanced HCW training, greater community awareness, and strengthened health system infrastructure. Integrating GDM services into existing maternal health programmes is essential to improving outcomes for women and their infants in resource-constrained settings.

articles.title: miR-93-5p Alleviates Intrauterine Adhesion by Inhibiting Endometrial Epithelial-Mesenchymal Transition via the Smad2 Pathway.
articles.authors: Yan X, Nian L, Zhu L et al.
articles.abstract: Intrauterine adhesion (IUA) is the second most common cause of female infertility, and epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) is a key mechanism in endometrial fibrosis during IUA. miR-93-5p has been shown to be involved in the EMT process, but its impact on EMT in IUA remains unclear. Therefore, this study aims to investigate the role of miR-93-5p in EMT during IUA and elucidate its underlying mechanisms. Human endometrial epithelial cells (hEECs) and human cervical epithelial cells (H8) were treated with human transforming growth factor β1 (TGF-β1) to induce an in vitro IUA model, and a mechanical injury method was used to establish a rat IUA model. The expression of miR-93-5p and key proteins was detected via RT-qPCR, Western blot, immunofluorescence, and immunohistochemistry. Endometrial tissue lesions and fibrosis were evaluated using H&E and Masson staining. Cell migration was assessed through Transwell and scratch assays. The interactions between molecules were detected through dual-luciferase reporter assays and RNA immunoprecipitation. The results show that​ miR-93-5p is downregulated in IUA, and miR-93-5p agomir can inhibit TGF-β1-induced EMT in hEECs and H8 cells, including suppressing N-cadherin and Vimentin expression, promoting E-cadherin expression, and effectively inhibiting cell migration. Meanwhile, miR-93-5p agomir​ can also ameliorate endometrial damage and fibrosis in IUA rats. Additionally, Smad2 expression is upregulated in IUA, and further studies revealed that miR-93-5p can target and inhibit Smad2 expression and phosphorylation. In TGF-β1-treated hEECs and H8 cells, overexpression of Smad2 attenuates the effects of miR-93-5p agomir, and the EMT phenotype is reversed. Overall, miR-93-5p can alleviate IUA by inhibiting the activation of the Smad2 signaling pathway and suppressing EMT in ​endometrial epithelial cells.

articles.title: Circular RNA-NLRP3 Crosstalk in Reproductive Biology: A Critical Appraisal of Direct Evidence and Testable Hypotheses.
articles.authors: Hsu CY, Abed HS, Ahmad I et al.
articles.abstract: Circular RNAs (circRNAs) are abundant and developmentally regulated in gonads, gametes, and preimplantation embryos, whereas NLRP3 inflammasome signaling has context-dependent roles in ovarian aging, spermatogenic stress, endometrial receptivity, implantation, and placental disease. Whether these two evidence streams constitute a functional regulatory axis in mammalian gametogenesis or early embryogenesis remains uncertain. In this regard, this review article aimed to identify direct reproductive mechanisms; reproductive functions without a demonstrated circRNA-NLRP3 bridge, association, or bioinformatic prediction; and mechanistic extrapolations from non-reproductive systems. Direct reproductive evidence was limited to four placental/trophoblast or granulosa-cell examples: circ_0001438/miR-942/NLRP3 signaling in preeclampsia-associated trophoblast models; circ_0081343-RBM8A regulation of NLRP3-linked pyroptosis in fetal-growth-restriction models; circ_0070987-associated pyroptosis in a dihydrotestosterone-treated granulosa-cell line; and hsa_circ_0003218 overexpression, which reduced NLRP3-pathway readouts in high-glucose HTR-8/SVneo trophoblasts in a gestational-diabetes study. No direct functional study was identified in mammalian sperm, oocytes, zygotes, cleavage-stage embryos, blastocysts, or the male germ line. Accordingly, circRNA detection, co-expression, host-gene enrichment, and predicted competing endogenous RNA networks should be regarded as hypothesis-generating rather than as proof of NLRP3 regulation. CircRNAs in seminal plasma and maternal blood show candidate biomarker potential, but external validation remains limited, and no combined reproductive circRNA-NLRP3 panel has been validated. Similarly, circRNA mimics, antisense approaches, circRNA-encoded peptides, extracellular vesicle (EVs) delivery, and combined circRNA/NLRP3 therapy remain preclinical or hypothetical in terms of reproduction. The most immediate priorities are cell-type- and stage-resolved perturbation studies, binding and rescue experiments, quantitative inflammasome readouts, reproductive safety assessment, and prospective biomarker validation.

articles.title: Estrogen-Progesterone Sequential Exposure Induces the Fibrosis of Adenomyosis in Mice.
articles.authors: Wang M, He H, Gao X et al.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Adenomyosis (ADS) is a common gynecological disorder characterized by dysmenorrhea, menorrhagia, and infertility, which markedly impair women's quality of life. Repeated cyclic bleeding of ectopic endometrial lesions may sustain local inflammation and tissue remodeling, leading to a "menstruation-inflammation-fibrosis" cycle. This study aimed to establish a mouse model that mimics this process and to evaluate the effect of estrogen-progesterone (EP) sequential exposure on uterine fibrosis in adenomyosis.
METHODS: A tamoxifen-induced mouse model of adenomyosis was established, followed by EP sequential exposure to induce a menstruation-like process. Histological staining and immunohistochemistry were performed to evaluate lesion formation, inflammatory responses, and fibrosis-related changes in uterine tissues.
RESULTS: EP sequential exposure successfully induced menstruation-like changes in the uterus of mice with adenomyosis. Compared with controls, mice exposed to sequential EP showed more prominent endometrial breakdown, inflammatory responses, and fibrotic remodeling. Collagen deposition and the expression of fibrosis-associated markers, including α-SMA, were increased in uterine lesions, indicating aggravated fibrosis.
CONCLUSION: EP sequential exposure promotes fibrosis in adenomyosis lesions in mice and may serve as a useful model for investigating the "menstruation-inflammation-fibrosis" cycle in adenomyosis.

articles.title: Heterogeneity of microbiome responses to menopausal hormone therapy among perimenopausal women.
articles.authors: Chen C, Hao L, Xie W et al.
articles.abstract: Menopausal hormone therapy (MHT) alleviates climacteric symptoms, yet its microbiome-wide effects and efficacy determinants remain unclear. Here we show that oral estradiol/dydrogesterone, given for 6 months to 356 perimenopausal women, improved neuroendocrine, metabolic and symptom outcomes and induced site-specific microbial remodeling. Vaginocervical and urinary niches showed the most pronounced restructuring, with moderate oral and minimal gut changes. MHT increased vaginocervical Lactobacillus crispatus and reduced Gardnerella vaginalis. Higher baseline vaginocervical L. crispatus predicted greater postintervention vaginocervical and urinary colonization and superior Female Sexual Function Index improvement. Baseline vaginocervical community types determined differential outcomes: G. vaginalis-dominated individuals shifted most toward healthier communities, whereas diversified individuals improved least. MHT efficacy also varied according to baseline gut community type: Phocaeicola vulgatus-dominated women exhibited greater hormonal responsiveness, superior clinical outcomes and were more likely to achieve 4-week rapid clinical remission than Prevotella copri-dominated women. These findings support a precision MHT framework integrating gut and vaginocervical community typing for personalized care. Chictr.org.cn ID: ChiCTR2100049768 .

articles.title: A randomized clinical trial comparing visual inspection with acetic acid (VIA) to Pocket Colposcopy for the triage of HPV+ women living with HIV in Kisumu, Kenya.
articles.authors: Santos MO, Dotson ME, Steinberg E et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The WHO recommends a "screen, triage, treat" approach for cervical cancer screening for Women Living with HIV (WLWH) in resource-limited settings, with HPV testing preferred for screening. We sought to compare Visual Assessment with Acetic Acid (VIA) assisted with the Pocket Colposcope to naked eye VIA for triage of HPV + WLWH.
METHODS: In a randomized clinical trial across six clinics in Kisumu, Kenya (November 2022 to June 2023), HPV + WLWH were randomized to VIA or Pocket colposcopy. Exam positivity was determined by presence of aceto-white epithelium (AWE); biopsies were taken from AWE or randomly if negative. Diagnostic accuracy was confirmed with pathology. Providers and participants completed post-exam surveys.
FINDINGS: Positive exam rates were 17.3% (VIA) and 14.3% (Pocket). Overall, CIN2/3 prevalence was 15.4% (12.2% VIA, 18.8% Pocket). Sensitivity, specificity, and negative predictive value were similar between arms. However, the Pocket showed a non-significant higher positive predictive value (37.5% vs 20.6%). Both providers and patients found the Pocket acceptable for triage.
CONCLUSION: The Pocket colposcope detected more treatable disease and reduced overtreatment. This study shows the Pocket colposcope is a feasible, lower-cost device that could facilitate biopsy confirmation, increase provider training, improve patient education, and enable remote diagnosis.

articles.title: Self-Management Interventions for Lower Urinary Tract Symptoms After Radical Prostatectomy: A Scoping Review of Intervention Components, Outcomes and Research Gaps.
articles.authors: Amano K, Suzuki K
articles.abstract:
AIM: To map the existing literature on self-management interventions for lower urinary tract symptoms (LUTS) following radical prostatectomy (RP) and clarify their characteristics and research gaps.
DESIGN: Scoping review.
REVIEW METHODS: The study followed the Arksey and O'Malley methodological framework. Eligibility criteria included studies of adult men after RP that evaluated interventions incorporating self-management components for LUTS. Data were extracted, categorized and synthesized according to intervention content.
DATA SOURCES: PubMed, CINAHL, PsycINFO and Web of Science were searched from their database inception to July 2026 to identify studies describing support programmes for patients undergoing RP.
RESULTS: Of the 480 identified records, 17 met the inclusion criteria. Interventions comprised lifestyle modification, follow-up care and LUTS-symptom management, delivered as standalone or combined approaches. Co-interventions included pelvic-floor muscle training, biofeedback, physical training and psychological counselling. Patients' self-efficacy, particularly their perceived ability to control LUTS, was reported as a factor associated with promoting self-management behaviours. While some studies reported improvements in key LUTS outcomes following the interventions, others found no significant between-group differences or reported worsening of certain symptoms.
CONCLUSION: Although self-management support for LUTS following RP is diverse, this review identified inconsistencies in intervention components and outcome measures, as well as a lack of comparable interventional studies. Strategies to enhance motivation, symptom monitoring, lifestyle modification and education on pelvic floor muscle training were commonly incorporated into multifaceted self-management interventions following RP.
IMPLICATIONS FOR THE PROFESSION AND/OR PATIENT CARE: Standardizing interventions description and adopting an LUTS-specific outcome framework will strengthen the evidence base and help guide nurse-led postoperative follow-up models.
IMPACT: Multifaceted and continuous self-management interventions may support patients' ability to proactively manage postoperative LUTS and promote greater autonomy in daily life.
REPORTING METHOD: PRISMA-ScR.
PATIENT OR PUBLIC CONTRIBUTION: No patient or public contribution.

articles.title: Maternal Anxiety and Depression From Pregnancy to Postpartum: Associations With Infants' Cortical Functional Connectivity at 1 Month.
articles.journal: Infancy : the official journal of the International Society on Infant Studies
articles.authors: Mian ZK, Carnevali L, Blanco B et al.
articles.abstract: Maternal anxiety and depression have been associated with alterations in functional connectivity (FC) in infancy, a period in which rapid brain development and functional network organization have been linked to longer term socioemotional outcomes. Investigating maternal anxiety and depression within the same sample is important, given that they frequently co-occur and may show distinct associations with infant brain development. A longitudinal approach is key to understanding whether and how changes in maternal mental health across the perinatal period relate to infant brain development. We examined associations of subclinical prenatal and postnatal maternal depression and anxiety, measured via questionnaires at 32 weeks of gestation and 1 month postpartum, with infants' FC at 1 month of age. Task-free FC data were collected during natural sleep using High-Density Diffuse Optical Tomography (HD-DOT) in the home. No associations were observed between maternal anxiety symptoms and FC, and neither postnatal depression nor anxiety alone predicted infant FC. Lower maternal prenatal depression scores were associated with stronger FC in the infants' frontal network (n = 39). In contrast, greater increases in maternal depressive symptoms from the prenatal to postnatal periods were linked to increased frontal FC, particularly when mothers had higher prenatal depression levels (n = 28). Most symptom changes were small in magnitude and did not cross clinical thresholds, suggesting largely subclinical and transient mood shifts. We speculate that while early prenatal exposure may signal vulnerability in specific neural circuits, the subsequent increase in symptoms could trigger compensatory or accelerated development in the same networks. Replication with larger, more diverse, samples and longitudinal research is needed to determine whether these subtle early fluctuations in maternal symptoms are associated with longer-term trajectories of infant brain development beyond the perinatal window.

articles.title: Sex-specific associations of preterm birth with adiposity and body composition among adolescents: A Brazilian birth cohort.
articles.authors: Silva Filho MFE, Abreu AM, Viana MO et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate associations of preterm birth with adiposity and body composition in adolescents and assess whether these associations differed by sex.
METHODS: This study included 2171 adolescents aged 18-19 years from the São Luís population-based birth cohort, Brazil. Preterm birth (<37 weeks) was ascertained prospectively from the last menstrual period or, retrospectively, from maternal reports verified against the Brazilian Live Birth Information System. Outcomes were body mass index (BMI), waist circumference (WC), percentage fat mass (%FM), fat mass index (FMI), and fat-free mass index (FFMI). Linear regression models included preterm birth, sex, and their interaction and were adjusted for adolescent skin color and maternal smoking during pregnancy. A complete-case sensitivity analysis used the full DAG-informed adjustment set.
RESULTS: In the primary adjusted models, preterm birth was associated among males with higher WC (β=3.59 cm; 95% CI: 1.03-6.15), %FM (β=3.38 %age points; 95% CI: 1.22-5.54), and FMI (β=1.10 kg/m²; 95% CI: 0.34-1.86), but not with BMI or FFMI. No associations were observed among females. Interactions between preterm birth and sex were significant for WC (P = 0.040), %FM (P = 0.008), and FMI (P = 0.015). In the sensitivity analysis, only %FM remained associated among males, and no interaction was statistically significant.
CONCLUSION: Preterm birth was associated with greater adiposity among male adolescents in the primary analysis, but evidence was weaker after full adjustment. These findings suggest possible sex-related heterogeneity that requires confirmation in studies with more complete prenatal data.

articles.title: Relationship between urinary incontinence symptoms and the properties of the obturator internus muscle in female patients with hip osteoarthritis.
articles.journal: Journal of orthopaedic science : official journal of the Japanese Orthopaedic Association
articles.authors: Fukutani S, Kadowaki M, Uchio Y
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with hip osteoarthritis may develop urinary incontinence (UI) due to obturator internus muscle (OIM) atrophy; however, no study has quantitatively measured the volume or evaluated the OIM tissue composition. This study clarifies the obturator internus muscle characteristics in patients with hip osteoarthritis and urinary incontinence symptoms.
METHODS: Of the 215 female patients who underwent total hip arthroplasty between October 2021 and March 2024, 26 with unilateral osteoarthritis aged <70 years were included. The UI group comprised 14 patients with UI symptoms, whereas the non-UI group comprised 12 patients without UI. To evaluate OIM characteristics, the skeletal muscle index (SMI), volume divided by height squared (m), muscle atrophy rate, percentage decrease in affected side volume relative to healthy side, mean computed tomography (CT) value, fatty degeneration rate, and percentage of voxels less than 30 Hounsfield Units (HU) were measured from preoperative CT scans.
RESULTS: The SMIs were 10.7 ± 3.4 and 12.1 ± 3.3 on the affected side and 15.5 ± 2.0 and 15.1 ± 3.7 on the healthy side in the UI and non-UI groups, respectively, showing no significant difference between the groups. However, the affected side was significantly smaller in both groups than the unaffected side. The atrophy rate (%) was 32.0 ± 17.5 in the UI group and 19.8 ± 11.7 in the non-UI group, with significantly more severe atrophy in the UI group. The mean CT values (HU) showed no significant group differences. The fatty degeneration rate was significantly higher on the affected side in the UI group.
CONCLUSION: Among patients with hip osteoarthritis, those with UI symptoms experience severe OIM atrophy.

articles.title: Reproductive Outcome Registration in Phase 3 Weight-Management Pharmacotherapy Trials: A Cross-Sectional Meta-Research Study.
articles.authors: Mondal R, Nandi M
articles.abstract:
AIMS: To quantify registered reproductive outcome measures in women and men in adult Phase 3 weight-management pharmacotherapy trials and compare them with registered body-composition measures.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Cross-sectional meta-research study of ClinicalTrials.gov records as registered on 31 August 2026. Eligible trials were randomised, controlled, Phase 3 or 2/3, with registered minimum age ≥ 18 years, a pharmacological intervention, weight or BMI as a registered primary outcome and a weight-related registered condition. Registered outcome fields were classified with a published dictionary. Analyses used exact Clopper-Pearson intervals and paired counts; programme-level, mechanism and age-relaxed analyses were post hoc.
RESULTS: Of 230 trials (91 development programmes; 3711 registered outcome measures), two registered any reproductive outcome measure (0.87%, 95% CI: 0.11-3.11), both in polycystic ovary syndrome populations with non-industry sponsors; none of 227 trials without a reproductive indication did. No trial enrolling men registered a named male gonadal-endocrine or semen measure (0/228, 95% CI: 0.00-1.60). Among trials of glucagon-like peptide-1-based agents it was 2/152 (1.32%). Body composition was registered in 33 trials, 31 without any reproductive measure and none the reverse; at programme level, 22 versus none. Admitting trials with minimum age below 18 years gave 7/254 (2.76%), including two industry trials registering gonadal hormones in adolescent safety panels.
CONCLUSIONS: Qualifying reproductive outcomes were rarely registered in adult Phase 3 weight-management pharmacotherapy trials on ClinicalTrials.gov, including 31 of 33 trials registering body composition. This identifies a gap in publicly registered evidence, not absence of measurement; registering reproductive assessments where undertaken would improve their discoverability.

articles.title: Efficacy of hysteroscopic curettage and niche resection in type II and III cesarean scar pregnancies.
articles.journal: The journal of maternal-fetal & neonatal medicine : the official journal of the European Association of Perinatal Medicine, the Federation of Asia and Oceania Perinatal Societies, the International Society of Perinatal Obstetricians
articles.authors: Zhang F, Xu G, Chen Y et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of hysteroscopic curettage combined with cesarean scar diverticulum canal-opening after focused ultrasound ablation surgery (FUAS) pretreatment in patients with type II and III cesarean scar pregnancy (CSP).
METHODS: Clinical data of 105 patients with type II/III CSP treated between January 2019 and October 2022 were retrospectively analyzed. All patients received FUAS pretreatment. The observation group (n = 47) underwent hysteroscopic curettage combined with niche canal-opening, while the control group (n = 58) received hysteroscopic curettage alone. Surgical parameters, postoperative recovery, complications, reintervention rates, and menstrual outcomes were compared.
RESULTS: The observation group had significantly shorter operation time [20 (15,25) vs. 25 (20,31) min, p = 0.001], less intraoperative blood loss [5 (5,10) vs. 10 (10,50) mL, p = 0.002], lower complication rate [4.3% vs. 17.2%, p = 0.038], and lower reintervention rate [4.3% vs. 19.0%, p = 0.023]. No between-group differences were observed in postoperative hemoglobin decline, hospital stay, vaginal bleeding duration, human chorionic gonadotropin normalization time, menstrual recovery time, or residual scar myometrial thickness (all p > 0.05). Among patients with preoperative prolonged menstruation, menstrual duration improved in both groups (p < 0.05), with a higher improvement rate in the observation group [75.0% vs. 23.1%, p = 0.005].
CONCLUSIONS: FUAS pretreatment combined with hysteroscopic surgery is safe and effective for type II/III CSP. Adding diverticulum canal-opening to hysteroscopic curettage further optimized surgical outcomes by reducing operation time, intraoperative blood loss, complication rates, and the need for reintervention, while also significantly improving prolonged menstruation. This combined strategy may serve as an optimized minimally invasive alternative for patients desiring fertility, though long-term reproductive safety requires further verification.

articles.title: Catastrophic fetal-neonatal thrombosis: a thromboinflammatory concept and the role of antiphospholipid antibodies.
articles.journal: The journal of maternal-fetal & neonatal medicine : the official journal of the European Association of Perinatal Medicine, the Federation of Asia and Oceania Perinatal Societies, the International Society of Perinatal Obstetricians
articles.authors: Makatsariya A, Vorobev A, Khizroeva J et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Fetal and neonatal thrombosis comprises a heterogeneous spectrum of disorders ranging from localized vascular events to rapidly progressive systemic thrombosis involving multiple vascular beds and organs. This review examines thromboinflammation and antiphospholipid antibodies (aPL) in severe fetal-neonatal thrombosis.
METHODS: This narrative, hypothesis-generating review draws on a structured, non-systematic literature search through August 31, 2026, distinguishing direct fetal and neonatal evidence from adult and experimental findings.
RESULTS: Neonatal hemostasis is characterized by a physiologically balanced but vulnerable state that may become destabilized by infection, hypoxia, endothelial injury, inflammation, and genetic or immune-mediated factors. Current evidence suggests that interactions between endothelial dysfunction, innate immune activation, platelets, coagulation, neutrophil extracellular traps, and the complement system may promote a transition from localized thrombosis to a self-amplifying thromboinflammatory process. However, a common mechanism of such progression has not been established across different fetal and neonatal thrombotic disorders. Maternal IgG aPL may cross the placenta, whereas aPL detected in some neonates may reflect presumed de novo production. The presence of aPL does not necessarily result in neonatal thrombosis, and additional prothrombotic factors reported in selected cases are consistent with, but do not establish, a "second-hit" or "multiple-hit" model.
CONCLUSION: We propose catastrophic fetal-neonatal thrombosis as an unvalidated clinical and pathogenetic framework rather than a distinct disease entity. Paired maternal-neonatal testing and longitudinal antibody assessment may help clarify antibody origin, although delayed testing limits causal interpretation. Its potential value for earlier recognition and etiologically directed diagnostic evaluation requires prospective assessment.

articles.title: Artificial intelligence research ın women's health: Bibliometric analysis of scientific publications between 2020-2025.
articles.authors: Kuşlu S, Eminoğlu Güven A
articles.abstract: Although AI applications in women's health are increasing rapidly, few bibliometric studies have systematically examined research trends and priority topics in this field. We conducted a bibliometric analysis of research on women's health and artificial intelligence published between 2020 and 2025 to interpret the field's evolution and identify gaps within it. We analyzed 3241 articles indexed in the Web of Science database, retrieved on 13.09.2025, using VOSviewer software and co--authorship, co-occurrence, citation, and country analysis techniques. We found that publications increased over the years, the USA produced the most, and the most-cited studies focused on obstetric imaging, gestational diabetes, and infertility. The most frequently used keywords were machine learning, pregnancy, artificial intelligence, deep learning, and fertility. Researchers in this field focus on clinically prioritized problems and use algorithm-based approaches. International collaboration and multidisciplinary approaches will accelerate its development.

articles.title: Qualitative clinician feedback on a systematic urinary incontinence screening and patient education intervention in primary care.
articles.authors: Brown T, Petrie C, Collins SA et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Systematic screening for bothersome urinary incontinence (UI) is underused in primary care settings, despite the high prevalence of UI and its negative impact on quality of life. Within one academic health system a quality improvement initiative was implemented within the electronic health record (EHR) to support screening for bothersome UI in adult women with a scheduled preventive visit. Understanding clinician perspectives around this workflow may lead to improvements in its acceptability to clinicians and use in routine care.
OBJECTIVE: To summarise qualitative clinician feedback about this UI screening initiative.
METHODS: We conducted interviews with participating primary care clinicians. Clinicians were eligible for participation if they spent the majority of their clinical time at a clinic that had adopted the UI screening interventions in the EHR for at least 3 months. The interview guide focused on the perceived impact, usability and challenges of the screening process and workflows. Interviews lasted approximately 30 min and were audio recorded and transcribed. Thematic analysis of transcripts was conducted.
RESULTS: We interviewed 22 clinicians from 10 unique clinics. Qualitative feedback revealed that clinicians valued UI screening but experienced significant time pressure and competing priorities within a routine preventive patient encounter. Clinicians were comfortable discussing UI symptoms and diagnoses. In discussing UI treatment, clinicians expressed concerns about the side effects and costs of UI medications, highlighting a preference for referring patients to pelvic floor physical therapy and subspecialty care. Clinicians had neutral or positive attitudes towards the screening intervention and provided suggestions to improve the EHR alerts and order set.
CONCLUSIONS: Primary care clinicians we interviewed believe UI screening is important, and this screening intervention was acceptable and may improve patient care. Underlying structural constraints on primary care are barriers to this initiative and likely will be for other quality improvement initiatives.

articles.title: Maternal and neonatal outcomes in SLE: comparison of 430 pregnancies from the French GR2 study with 1720 pregnancies from French perinatal surveys.
articles.authors: Dernoncourt A, Schmidt J, Guettrot-Imbert G et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pregnancy in women with SLE is considered high risk, particularly in the presence of active disease, organ damage or lupus anticoagulant (LA). Improvements in SLE and obstetric management may have enhanced outcomes.
METHODS: We compared pregnancies from the prospective GR2 (Groupe de Recherche sur la Grossesse et les Maladies Rares) cohort with those from the French general population using perinatal survey (Enquêtes Nationales Périnatales (ENP)) data. Eligible pregnancies resulted in a birth ≥22 weeks of gestation (WG) or ≥500 g, in accordance with the ENP inclusion criteria. Each GR2 pregnancy was matched with four ENP pregnancies based on maternal age, parity, number of fetuses and region. Live birth rates were evaluated after excluding minors, anonymous births and refusals. Adverse pregnancy outcomes (APOs) were assessed among live births with complete medical records and were defined as placental insufficiency-related preterm birth, severe small-for-gestational-age infant (birth weight <3rd percentile) or neonatal death.
RESULTS: We matched 430 GR2 pregnancies to 1720 ENP pregnancies. At inclusion, 336/397 (84.6%) women had no clinical lupus activity, 327/385 (84.9%) had no organ damage, 68/428 (15.9%) were LA-positive and 417/430 (97.0%) received hydroxychloroquine. Live births occurred in 423/430 (98.4%) GR2 pregnancies versus 1667/1720 (97.0%) ENP pregnancies (OR=1.49 (0.64 to 3.45); p=0.14). APOs occurred in 75/406 (18.5%) SLE pregnancies versus 134/1629 (8.2%) ENP pregnancies (OR=2.53 (1.86 to 3.44); p<0.001). APOs remained higher in GR2 pregnancies without disease activity, organ damage or LA positivity (30/209; 14.4%) than in ENP pregnancies (p<0.01). Univariate analysis identified SLE, nulliparity, smoking, chronic hypertension, twin pregnancy and fertility treatment as APO-associated factors. In multivariate analysis, SLE remained independently associated with APOs (aOR=2.91 (2.06 to 4.09); p<0.001).
CONCLUSION: Among pregnancies progressing beyond 22 WG (or birth weight ≥500 g), live birth rates were comparable to those in the general population, but APOs were more than two times as frequent in women with SLE.
TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: NCT02450396.

articles.title: Safe Maternal Care Anywhere: Improving Emergency Nurse Preparedness for Obstetrical Emergencies Through Maternal Early Warning Signs Education.
articles.authors: Glowzinski S, Klassa P, Roberman JL et al.
articles.abstract: Maternal mortality has been increasing nationally despite advances in care. Many obstetrical units are closing across the nation, decreasing access to this specialized care. This has increased the likelihood of patients with an obstetrical emergency presenting to an emergency department. Preparation and education regarding obstetrical emergencies for emergency nurses are often limited. This project aimed to enhance the knowledge and confidence of emergency nurses in recognizing and managing maternal early warning signs through targeted education. Education and simulation were provided to emergency nurses during their annual competency training. Nurses were surveyed before and after education to determine their confidence in identifying and managing maternal early warning signs. Statistically significant improvements across all 11 measured domains in the posteducation surveys were noted, demonstrating the effectiveness of the educational intervention in enhancing emergency nurses' confidence in caring for obstetrical patients. Based on the evaluation results, maternal early warning signs education with simulation for emergency nurses met the goal of improved confidence in caring for obstetrical patients.

articles.title: Integrating PET/CT and correlative biomarkers for prospective evaluation of extramedullary disease in relapsed/refractory B-ALL: implications for CAR T-cell therapy.
articles.authors: Solter ML, Wang YJ, Li G et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite advances in immunotherapy for B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (B-ALL), non-central nervous system extramedullary disease (non-CNS EMD) is increasingly recognized. Due to the lack of routine whole-body imaging, the incidence of non-CNS EMD is poorly understood. Fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography/CT (FDG PET/CT) offers a comprehensive approach in detecting EMD involvement, but its utility in B-ALL has not been prospectively evaluated. Furthermore, whether the utilization of cell-free DNA (cfDNA) in B-ALL can improve the identification of EMD is unknown.
METHODS: We conducted a prospective, single-center cohort study evaluating FDG PET/CT imaging and correlative molecular biomarkers in patients with relapsed/refractory (R/R) B-ALL undergoing evaluation for chimeric antigen receptor T-cell therapy. Baseline PET/CT was performed prior to infusion, and patients with identified non-CNS EMD underwent post-treatment imaging. Imaging metrics, using artificial intelligence with expert input, included standardized uptake values (SUV). cfDNA was evaluated longitudinally using personalized droplet digital PCR assays and compared with imaging findings and standard disease detection modalities, including flow cytometry, and next-generation sequencing. The primary endpoint was the proportion of non-CNS EMD detected on baseline PET/CT in adults.
RESULTS: Sixteen patients were enrolled; median age was 21.5 years (range, 5–38). Baseline PET/CT identified non-CNS EMD in 44% of patients (5 of 10 (50%) adults and 2 of 6 (33%) children). Non-CNS EMD was multifocal in all affected patients and most commonly involved lymph nodes, kidneys, testes, and soft tissue. Median SUVmax was 17 (range, 13.4–32.3). A prior history of non-CNS EMD was associated with EMD detection on PET/CT at enrollment (p=0.035). In one patient, widespread non-CNS EMD was identified on PET/CT despite negative bone marrow flow cytometry. Peripheral blood cfDNA detected leukemic sequences in 15 of 16 (93.8%) samples with active disease. Peripheral blood cfDNA detected isolated non-CNS EMD in three patients where all other biomarker testing was negative.
CONCLUSIONS: Prospective whole-body imaging revealed a high prevalence of multifocal non-CNS EMD. Integration of whole-body imaging with cfDNA may enable more comprehensive disease evaluation in patients with R/R B-ALL. Larger prospective studies are needed to define the true incidence and clinical significance of non-CNS…

articles.title: Cumulative exposure to heavy metals (chromium, copper, lead, manganese, mercury, nickel, and titanium) and age at natural menopause.
articles.journal: International journal of environmental health research
articles.authors: Novak B
articles.abstract: Exposure to heavy metals may lead to premature ovarian insufficiency. Research on the exposure to heavy metals and the age at menopause is scant. This study aimed to investigate the impact of heavy metal exposure on the age at the onset of natural menopause. Cox proportional hazards models were used to assess the risk of the onset of menopause. Logistic regressions were estimated to examine the relationship between heavy metals and early or premature menopause. Mean age at menopause was 47.3 (SD 5.5); 25.1% of women experienced either an early or a premature menopause. Hair nickel concentrations in the third and fourth quartiles of the distribution increased the risk of menopause and the odds of an early or premature menopause. High levels of chromium were marginally related to a lower risk of menopause. However, the likelihood of an early or premature menopause was 50% lower among women in the fourth quartile. Mercury concentrations show an increased risk of menopause only for the second quartile of the distribution. The odds of an early or premature menopause doubled for the second quartile. No significant relationships between hair copper, lead, manganese, and titanium concentrations and age at menopause were found.

articles.title: Predictors of Cesarean Birth During Labor According to Maternal BMI: Insights From a Multicenter Doppler-Based Analysis.
articles.journal: The journal of obstetrics and gynaecology research
articles.authors: Morales-Roselló J, Khalil A, Buongiorno S et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Maternal overweight and obesity are associated with increased cesarean birth rates, although the mechanisms linking maternal body mass index (BMI) to labor outcomes remain incompletely understood. Few studies have differentiated cesarean indications or incorporated fetal Doppler assessment.
OBJECTIVE: To identify BMI-specific maternal and fetal predictors of intrapartum cesarean birth, differentiating cesarean indications and incorporating fetoplacental Doppler parameters.
STUDY DESIGN: This retrospective multicenter observational study included 3290 singleton pregnancies ≥ 35 weeks' gestation from tertiary centers in Spain, Italy, and the United Kingdom. Maternal, fetal, and perinatal data were collected, including maternal BMI, labor characteristics, delivery outcomes, and fetal Doppler indices. Multivariable logistic regression assessed determinants of cesarean birth for intrapartum fetal compromise (CS-IFC) and failure to progress (CS-FP) according to maternal BMI categories.
RESULTS: Increasing maternal BMI was associated with higher rates of CS-IFC (5.6%-9.9%) and CS-FP (7.8%-10.9%). In normal-weight women, elevated umbilical artery pulsatility index (PI), reduced middle cerebral artery PI, and induction of labor independently predicted CS-IFC, while parity and induction predicted CS-FP. In overweight and obese women, maternal factors, primarily parity, were the main determinants, whereas Doppler indices were not independently predictive. The frequency of a 5-min Apgar score < 7 showed no significant trend across BMI groups (p = 0.272). Although arterial cord pH < 7.10 was most frequent in obese women, the trend across BMI categories was not statistically significant (p = 0.132).
CONCLUSION: Maternal BMI was associated with increasing rates of intrapartum cesarean birth. In stratified analyses, fetoplacental Doppler parameters were independently associated with CS-IFC in normal-weight women but not in women with overweight or obesity. However, the overall interaction test was not statistically significant, and these findings do not establish that the associations of all predictors differ according to BMI. The interaction involving MCA PI MoM warrants further investigation. Further studies are needed to assess the clinical value of BMI-specific predictive approaches.

articles.title: Cytotoxic and Pro-Apoptotic Effects of the Compound 2-Carboxy-2-Heptano-Indolin-3-One in HeLa Cell Spheroids.
articles.authors: Rocha ALC, Westin CF, Niekawa ETG et al.
articles.abstract: Indolinones are compounds with recognized antineoplastic properties and can act as inhibitors of multiple kinases. However, the antitumor effects of 2-carboxy-2-heptano-indolin-3-one (IDC) have not yet been investigated in cervical cancer models. This study investigated the cytotoxic and pro-apoptotic effects of IDC in HeLa cells, with emphasis on a three-dimensional spheroid model, and evaluated its effects on spheroid growth, cell cycle distribution, apoptosis, and the expression of genes associated with cell death and DNA damage responses. Cell viability was assessed in monolayer cultures using the resazurin assay, while spheroid growth and morphology were evaluated by microscopy and volumetric analysis. Apoptosis and cell cycle distribution were investigated by flow cytometry, and gene expression was assessed by RT-qPCR. IDC reduced cell viability by up to 80% in monolayer cultures and significantly inhibited spheroid growth, with loss of structural integrity and absence of recovery after treatment withdrawal. Flow cytometry revealed 81.7-83.6% apoptotic cells following IDC treatment, compared with 35.8% in the vehicle control. No significant changes in G1, S, or G2/M cell cycle distribution were observed. RT-qPCR showed increased mRNA levels of CASP8, CASP9, CASP3, BBC3, and GADD45A and decreased levels of TP53, CDKN1A, and MYC. These transcriptional changes suggest the involvement of apoptotic signaling and DNA damage response mechanisms. Overall, IDC exhibited cytotoxic and pro-apoptotic effects in HeLa cells and impaired three-dimensional spheroid growth and integrity, supporting further investigation of its antineoplastic potential in cervical cancer.

articles.title: Repeated measurements of urinary polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon metabolites in relation to ovarian reserve and in vitro fertilization outcomes: A prospective cohort study.
articles.authors: Qin S, Zhang Q, Qian X et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: This study aimed to explore the effects of urinary polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH) metabolites (PAHMs) on ovarian reserve and IVF outcomes.
METHODS: We included 737 women from the prospective Chongqing Environment and Reproductive Health cohort in Chongqing, China between January and September 2023. Eight urinary PAHMs were measured at three clinical time points, with the first one collected before treatment initiation (T1), the second one collected during the ovarian stimulation period (T2), and the third one collected on the oocyte retrieval day (T3). The outcome measures from electronic medical records comprised ovarian reserve indicators and IVF outcomes, such as the probabilities of mature oocytes and normal fertilization. Linear regression models, generalized linear models with negative binomial distribution, and modified Poisson regression models were utilized to evaluate the associations between individual PAHMs and the outcomes, adjusting for key confounders. Quantile G-computation regression models were used to assess the joint effects of multi-PAHMs on the outcomes. False discovery rate (FDR) correction was applied to all P values.
RESULTS: Urinary hydroxyphenanthrenes were negatively associated with probability of normal fertilization, which were robust after FDR correction and in sensitivity analyses. For the geometric mean concentrations of the three samples (T123), the percent change per interquartile ratio-fold increase ranged from -3.25% to -2.31%, and for the latter two (T23), the percent change ranged from -2.95% to -2.06%. Inverse associations with probability of mature oocytes were observed for 1-hydroxynaphthalene (1-OH-Nap) (third vs. first tertile: -4.09%), the summed concentrations of 1-OH-Nap and 2-hydroxynaphthalene (third vs. first tertile: -4.23%), and multi-PAH exposure (-3.36%). Conversely, 2-hydroxyphenanthrene (2-OH-Phen), the summed concentrations of 2-OH-Phen, 3-hydroxyphenanthrene, 9-hydroxyphenanthrene, and 4-hydroxyphenanthrene, and 1-hydroxypyrene were positively associated with oocyte number retrieved, with percent changes ranging from 5.17% to 6.83% (T123) and 5.52% to 8.62% (T23).
CONCLUSION: This study provided evidence of associations between PAH exposure and increased number of oocytes retrieved but decreased probabilities of mature oocytes and normal fertilization.

articles.title: HypoxIA: A bicenter study of machine learning-based prediction of fetal hypoxia using fetal heart rate and obstetric features.
articles.journal: American journal of obstetrics & gynecology MFM
articles.authors: Olgiati P, Bardon R, Bueno-Barthe G et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiotocography (CTG) is the gold standard to monitor fetal well-being during labor, but its clinical interpretation remains limited for detecting fetal hypoxia. Artificial intelligence approaches offer new perspectives to improve CTG-based fetal hypoxia detection.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the performance of an AI model combining intrapartum CTG signal and routinely collected clinical data to predict neonatal acidemia.
STUDY DESIGN: This bicenter study included 3574 singleton deliveries from May 2024 to August 2025. Neonatal acidemia was defined as umbilical arterial pH <7.15, and severe acidemia as pH <7.05. Raw CTG signals were segmented into 10-minute windows during the final hour and final three hours before birth. CTG-derived features were automatically extracted and combined with clinical variables in machine learning models. Model performance was evaluated using areas under the receiver operating characteristic curves (AUCs) with 95% confidence intervals (95% CIs), and compared with clinical intervention for suspected fetal hypoxia.
RESULTS: Neonatal acidemia occurred in 380/3574 newborns (10.6%), including severe acidemia in 65/3574 (1.8%). Medical intervention for suspected fetal hypoxia occurred in 580/3574 deliveries (16.2%). Model performance was higher for severe acidemia than for overall acidemia and was best during the final hour before birth. For the final-hour analysis, the AUC was 0.78 (95% CI, 0.71-0.85) for severe acidemia and 0.68 (95% CI, 0.61-0.75) for acidemia. For the final three hours, the AUC was 0.72 (95% CI, 0.66-0.78) for severe acidemia and 0.68 (95% CI, 0.62-0.74) for acidemia. At the same false-positive rate as clinical practice, the model achieved higher sensitivity for severe acidemia. Explainability analysis identified CTG-derived variables as the main contributors to prediction, whereas clinical variables had limited added value.
CONCLUSION: In this bicenter study, a machine learning model based on routinely collected CTG and clinical data showed its best performance for predicting severe neonatal acidemia. The predominance of clinically coherent CTG-derived predictors supports the biological plausibility of the model and suggests that explainable AI may support CTG interpretation during labor.

articles.title: Offering prenatal CFTR modulators to prevent cystic fibrosis-related organ damage in utero.
articles.journal: American journal of obstetrics & gynecology MFM
articles.authors: Saleeb C, Gore WD, Gajo MA et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: CFTR modulator therapy has drastically improved the prognosis and quality of life for those with cystic fibrosis (CF). CF complications begin to manifest in utero, including meconium ileus, and current regulatory approvals for CFTR modulator therapy does not have a pregnancy indication. Despite this, there have been several documented cases of women taking CFTR modulator therapy during pregnancy with promising results of potential CFTR correction in utero.
OBJECTIVE: To report one center's experience offering CFTR modulator therapy to pregnant women for prenatal CF treatment.
STUDY DESIGN: Eight pregnant women carrying a fetus at risk of having CF were presented with the option of CFTR modulator therapy during pregnancy with extensive counseling on the potential benefits and risks. Records from routine clinical care from prenatal, birth, and perinatal period were collected.
RESULTS: Of the eight pregnant women, three intended to take the CFTR modulator, elexacaftor/ tezacaftor/ ivacaftor (ETI), however only two were able, as the third was unable to obtain insurance authorization. In one case, the infant was homozygous for F508del(p.Phe508del, c.1521_1523delCTT, 1653delCTT) variant with signs of worsening bowel obstruction on fetal imaging, however after ETI initiation at 27 weeks he was born without meconium ileus. In the other case of CFTR modulator therapy treatment, the infant carried a CFTR variant of varying clinical consequence, Y1032C (c.3095A>G, p.Tyr1032Cys), and one disease causing CFTR variant. After ETI initiation, ultrasound findings suggestive of bowel obstruction improved and there was no meconium ileus at birth. The family who desired prenatal ETI therapy but was unable to obtain insurance coverage, also had one disease causing variant and one of varying clinical consequence, G622D (c.1865G>A, p.Gly622Asp). Despite fetal imaging concerning for bowel obstruction this infant had no meconium ileus at birth and was classified as CFTR related metabolic syndrome/CF Screen Positive Inconclusive Diagnosis. Of the remaining pregnant women, 3 declined prenatal CFTR modulator therapy, one ultimately had negative prenatal diagnostics, and another terminated the pregnancy.
CONCLUSION: Decisions to treat with prenatal CFTR modulators are complex and influenced by multiple factors including phenotype variability, inconsistent insurance coverage, and uncertain potential risks and benefits. Outcomes of these cases ranged from pregnancy…

articles.title: Personalized machine learning model for predicting successful vaginal delivery during the active phase of labor.
articles.journal: American journal of obstetrics & gynecology MFM
articles.authors: Reicher L, Attali E, Baruch Y et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Accurate personalized prediction of delivery mode during the active stage improves resource allocation, reduces unnecessary interventions, and enhances patient-centered care. However, current machine learning models lack focus on active labor and effective use of labor-related data. The "black box" problem further impedes understanding, accuracy, and patient safety. Our aim was to develop a personalized model using real-time data to predict successful vaginal deliveries in the active phase and provide an explanation of the model's decision-making process STUDY DESIGN: Labor records from a tertiary hospital were searched and labeled over a 12-year period (2010-2021). Three models were trained using both "static features" (e.g demographics) and "dynamic features" (e.g cervical dilatation, efficacy, and newly derived features calculated as ratios between adjusted dynamic measures and time differences). To assess the explainability of the best-performing model, we employed SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) analysis.
RESULTS: A total of 94,386 cases in which a trial of labor was attempted were identified. Of them 70,000 admitted to the active phase of labor (6 cm dilatation). We trained three types of classifier models predicting successful vaginal delivery: Random Forest classifier, Histogram-Based Gradient Boosting classifier, and neural network model. Histogram-Based Gradient Boosting model achieved the highest scores: ROC AUC score and Precision recall AUC score was 0.87 (95% confidence interval, 0.858-0.892) and 0.52 (95% confidence interval, 0.511-0.542) respectively. Explainability of the best model was analyzed using SHAP. The features that contributed the most for the model prediction were: rate of fetal descent, cervical opening rate, maternal age and clinical fetal weight estimation.
CONCLUSIONS: This study presents a personalized, explainable machine learning model that continuously predicts delivery mode in real time during active labor. By integrating dynamic intrapartum data with static maternal characteristics, the model provides interpretable, patient-specific risk estimates that can enhance intrapartum decision-making and optimize obstetric care.

articles.title: Delivery at 39 weeks in pregnancies at maternal age 40 years or older: an updated narrative review of evidence and international guidance.
articles.journal: Journal of gynecology obstetrics and human reproduction
articles.authors: Mihoci EC, Socolov D, Socolov RV et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pregnancy at maternal age 40 years or older is associated with progressively higher maternal and perinatal risk, with particular concern for term stillbirth as gestation advances. The clinical question is not whether age alone makes pregnancy high risk in a binary sense, but whether the balance between continuing pregnancy and planned birth shifts sufficiently by 39 weeks to justify age-specific delivery timing.
AIM: To critically synthesize the evidence supporting delivery during the 39th week for pregnancies at maternal age 40 years or older, compare contemporary international recommendations, and define how induction should be incorporated into individualized clinical decision-making.
METHODS: A targeted narrative review was undertaken using PubMed/MEDLINE, official guideline repositories, and publisher websites, with literature considered through 10 September 2026. Priority was given to specialty-society guidance, systematic reviews and meta-analyses, randomized trials, large population cohorts, and recent implementation studies. Earlier seminal studies were retained when they directly informed gestational-age-specific risk. Because evidence spans heterogeneous designs and outcomes, findings were synthesized narratively rather than pooled de novo.
RESULTS: Observational evidence consistently shows that stillbirth risk rises with advancing maternal age and with continuing term gestation, with the strongest age-specific signal at 40 years or older. In older maternal-age groups, neonatal morbidity appears lowest at 39 weeks of gestation and increases at later gestational ages. The 35/39 randomized trial and meta-analyses comparing induction with expectant management provide reassurance that planned induction at term does not increase cesarean delivery in women of advanced maternal age, although direct randomized evidence in women aged 40 years or older is limited and trials are underpowered for stillbirth. Contemporary guidance has moved toward age-specific timing: ACOG/SMFM recommends delivery at 39+0 to 39+6 weeks for well-dated pregnancies when anticipated age at delivery is 40 years or older; SOGC permits induction at 39 weeks; and the 2023 Irish guideline recommends offering induction at 39+0 to 40+0 weeks with shared decision-making. General-population WHO, NICE, and French guidance remains more conservative because it addresses uncomplicated pregnancy irrespective of maternal age.
CONCLUSION: For a well-dated, otherwise uncomplicated…

articles.title: UBAP2L O-GlcNAcylation contributes to DDX21-associated stress granule formation and suppression of trophoblast pyroptosis in preeclampsia.
articles.authors: Liu R, Wei J, Wang Z et al.
articles.abstract: Preeclampsia (PE) is a severe pregnancy disorder characterized by hypertension and multi-organ dysfunction. Impaired trophoblast function and defective spiral artery remodeling are considered the central pathological features of PE, leading to placental ischemia/hypoxia and a subsequent inflammatory cascade. Increasing evidence has demonstrated that pyroptosis contributes to placental dysfunction and the establishment of a pro-inflammatory microenvironment in PE; however, the mechanisms remain largely unclear. O-linked β-N-acetylglucosamine (O-GlcNAc) modification is a reversible post-translational modification (PTM) that plays critical roles in maintaining cellular homeostasis and regulating multiple forms of programmed cell death (PCD), yet its role in pyroptosis during PE has not been elucidated. In the present study, we found that O-GlcNAcylation was markedly reduced in placental tissues from patients with PE and negatively correlated with pyroptosis. In both an LPS-induced PE-like mouse model and trophoblast cells, enhancement of O-GlcNAcylation significantly suppressed pyroptosis and ameliorated PE-like phenotypes. IP-MS identified UBAP2L as a critical O-GlcNAcylated protein. Mechanistically, T446, an O-GlcNAcylation site of UBAP2L, contributed to maintaining its protein stability by preventing ubiquitin-mediated proteasomal degradation and promoted its interaction with DDX21, thereby promoting stress granule formation. This process suppressed inflammasome activation and pyroptosis, improved trophoblast function, and ameliorated PE-like phenotypes.
