Collectively, our findings define an O-GlcNAcylation-UBAP2L-DDX21-stress granule-pyroptosis axis in PE and nominate O-GlcNAc signaling as a therapeutic target.

articles.title: Timing of vaginal misoprostol administration for cervical priming among women undergoing vaginoscopic hysteroscopy: a randomized controlled trial.
articles.authors: Thippeswamy SP, Maurya DK, Puttaswamy RG et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare the ease of cervical entry after administration of vaginal misoprostol at 2 different intervals before vaginoscopic hysteroscopy.
METHODS: In this randomized, double-blinded study, 140 women undergoing vaginoscopic hysteroscopy were allocated into two groups: 1) short-interval: placebo tablet administered vaginally 12 hours before the procedure, followed by 200 mcg vaginal misoprostol 3 hours before, and 2) long-interval: 200 mcg vaginal misoprostol 12 hours before the procedure and a placebo tablet 3 hours before. The primary outcome was the ease of cervical entry, evaluated using a 5-point Likert scale, and the secondary outcomes included 1) time interval to cervical entry and completion of the procedure, 2) pain assessment using a visual analog scale (VAS), and 3) any adverse effects associated with the drug or procedure.
RESULTS: All except two patients with cervical stenosis underwent vaginoscopic hysteroscopy. The proportion of patients who reported "easy" or "very-easy" cervical entry was similar in both groups (64.3% [95% confidence interval [CI], 53.1-75.5%], vs. 72.9% [95% CI, 62.4-83.3%]; P=0.275). Pain perception was lower in the long-interval group than in the short-interval group (P=0.024). However, the temporal change in the pain score was not significantly different between the groups. The side effects of misoprostol were mild, self-limiting, and similar in both groups.
CONCLUSION: Vaginal misoprostol administration 12 hours before vaginoscopic hysteroscopy was associated with a similar ease of entry but a lower perception of pain using the VAS than misoprostol administration 3 hours before the procedure.

articles.title: Toxicological effects of acetyl tributyl citrate exposure on the progression of uterine fibroids and cervical cancer.
articles.authors: Wei Z, Wu Y, Li M et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Uterine fibroids (UFs) and cervical cancer (CC) are two common gynecological tumors, the pathogenesis of which has not yet been fully elucidated, with environmental factors playing a significant role. Acetyl tributyl citrate (ATBC), a widely used plasticizer, has been proven to pose a threat to human health. Although studies have indicated that ATBC exposure may be associated with tumorigenesis, the specific roles and molecular mechanisms of ATBC in UFs and CC remain unclear.
OBJECTIVE: This study aims to investigate the molecular mechanisms of ATBC-related UFs and CC using network toxicology, machine learning, and multidimensional bioinformatics approaches.
METHODS: Network toxicology methods were used to identify the relevant targets of ATBC, UFs, and CC. Gene Ontology and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes enrichment analysis were employed to explore the potential target gene pathways of ATBC-related UFs and CC. Transcriptomics analysis, Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator, and Support Vector Machine - Recursive Feature Elimination algorithms were used to determine the core targets of ATBC-related UFs and CC, and the discrimination of core genes among them was evaluated by receiver operating characteristic curve. Immune infiltration analysis was used to analyze the relationship between the expression of core target genes and the infiltration levels of various immune cells, while molecular docking and in vitro cell experiments were used to validate the above results.
RESULTS: We identified 12 targets related to UFs and 153 targets related to CC, of which 11 were common targets for UFs and CC, significantly enriched in the ERBB signaling pathway and oxidative stress response pathway. F10, ABCB1, MMP9, CDK2, PIK3CA, and GABRA2 were identified as the core targets of ATBC-related UFs, while CDK2 and DHFR were identified as the core targets of ATBC-related CC. Among them, CDK2 is a cross-disease hub target for UFs and CC. In UFs tissues (MMP9, GABRA2, and CDK2) and CC tissues (CDK2 and DHFR), the expression of these genes was significantly higher than that in normal tissues. These genes were significantly associated with immune cell infiltration. Molecular docking and in vitro cell experiments results confirmed the stable interactions between ATBC and these targets.
CONCLUSION: This study reveals that some key targets play important roles in the relationship between ATBC and UFs and CC, providing new insights into the mechanisms…

articles.title: Stellate ganglion block in contemporary anesthesia practice: perioperative applications, emerging indications, and risk management.
articles.authors: Su H, Wu N, Qing W et al.
articles.abstract: Stellate ganglion block (SGB), an interventional technique that modulates sympathetic activity, has been increasingly investigated beyond traditional pain management in cardiology, neuropsychiatry, and perioperative medicine. This narrative review examines the evolving role of SGB in contemporary anesthesia practice, emphasizing that its effects may extend beyond immediate peripheral sympatholysis to longer-lasting central neural modulation. Technically, ultrasound guidance facilitates precise needle placement and low-volume injection, with improved visualization of relevant anatomy and injectate spread. Dose-finding studies have refined local-anesthetic volume and concentration, whereas continuous blockade may extend sympatholysis in selected refractory conditions. Clinically, SGB has been used in selected pain conditions, including complex regional pain syndrome and herpes zoster-related pain, and has been investigated for non-pain indications such as post-traumatic stress disorder, refractory ventricular arrhythmias, and menopausal vasomotor symptoms. In perioperative settings, SGB has been evaluated for postoperative analgesia, modulation of inflammatory responses, and potential neuroprotective effects. Risk mitigation relies on real-time ultrasound visualization of the needle tip, adjacent vascular structures, and injectate spread, together with predefined management protocols for major complications. Future research should prioritize multicenter prospective studies, standardized procedural parameters, and individualized treatment pathways to support the safe, precise, and evidence-based use of SGB across clinical settings.

articles.title: Co-development of an educational toolkit to support young adult women following stroke.
articles.authors: Ghisi GLM, Ibrahim S, Akingbade A et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Young adult women who experience stroke face unique challenges related to parenting, employment, relationships, and emotional recovery, yet tailored educational resources addressing these needs are limited. This project aimed to co-develop, evaluate, and refine a patient-centered educational toolkit to support young adult women in navigating parenting roles, recovery, and long-term well-being following stroke.
METHODS: A multi-phase co-development quality improvement initiative was conducted between May 2024 and March 2026. Phase 1 involved virtual co-design sessions with women with lived experience of stroke (n = 6) to identify priority content areas. Phase 2 comprised development of an initial 90-page educational toolkit informed by lived experience and evidence-based literature. Phase 3 included: (1) readability assessment using the Flesch Reading Ease (FRE) formula and evaluation by healthcare providers (n = 13) using the Suitability Assessment of Materials (SAM) and Patient Education Materials Assessment Tool for Printable Materials (PEMAT-P); and (2) focus groups with women post-stroke (n = 25) to refine content and usability. Phase 4 involved patient-partner review and refinement of the toolkit.
RESULTS: Five overarching themes informed toolkit development: children's education and support, return to work, navigating healthcare, mental health and emotional well-being, and relationships and social roles. The initial toolkit demonstrated difficult readability (mean FRE=39.2), but superior suitability according to SAM evaluation (79.8%). PEMAT-P scores demonstrated high understandability (88.5%) and actionability (88.9%). Focus group participants emphasized the need for more practical guidance, simplified language, improved visual layout, and expanded women-specific content, including mental health, parenting, reproductive health, and menopause. Iterative revisions resulted in a final 151-page toolkit organized into six thematic modules. Final readability improved substantially (FRE=60.8), indicating standard plain-language readability.
CONCLUSIONS: A co-developed, patient-centered educational toolkit addressing the multidimensional needs of young adult women following stroke was successfully developed, evaluated, and refined through iterative input from women with lived experience and healthcare providers.
PRACTICE IMPLICATIONS: This toolkit has potential for integration across stroke care, rehabilitation, and community settings to…

articles.title: Experience-associated change in the use of sentinel lymph node biopsy alone in endometrial cancer: A multicenter retrospective analysis (TRSGO-SLN-016).
articles.journal: European journal of obstetrics, gynecology, and reproductive biology
articles.ta: Eur J Obstet Gynecol Reprod Biol
articles.authors: Gokce A, Ozturk C, Cetinkaya Sendur G et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate whether increasing institutional experience with sentinel lymph node (SLN) mapping in endometrial cancer influences bilateral mapping success and the surgeons' tendency to omit complementary pelvic lymphadenectomy.
METHODS: This retrospective, multicenter cohort study included 563 patients with apparent early-stage endometrial cancer treated at five high-volume gynecologic oncology centers in Turkiye between January 2016 and May 2023. Surgical staging was initiated with SLN mapping using minimally invasive approaches. Chronological institutional case order was used as a proxy for accumulated institutional experience. Two multivariable logistic regression models, adjusted for age, evaluated predictors of bilateral mapping success in the overall cohort and predictors of SLN biopsy alone among patients with successful bilateral mapping, with sensitivity analyses accounting for center clustering, calendar period, tracer type and non-linearity.
RESULTS: Bilateral mapping was achieved in 404 (71.8 %) of 563 patients. Neither clinicopathological factors nor increasing case order independently predicted bilateral mapping success, whereas older age was associated with lower odds of bilateral mapping (OR 0.73 per 10 years, 95 % CI 0.60-0.89, p = 0.002). Among bilaterally mapped patients, each 10-case increase in case order was associated with a 25 % increase in the odds of performing SLN biopsy alone (OR 1.25, 95 % CI 1.18-1.34, p < 0.001). High-grade tumors (OR 0.18, 95 % CI 0.07-0.46, p < 0.001) and LVSI (OR 0.29, 95 % CI 0.13-0.66, p = 0.003) were independently associated with lower odds of SLN biopsy alone. The case-order association persisted after accounting for center clustering and calendar period and in the subset mapped with indocyanine green.
CONCLUSIONS: In high-volume centers with experienced gynecologic oncologists, chronological institutional case order was not associated with improved bilateral mapping success but was independently associated with increasing use of SLN biopsy alone after successful bilateral mapping. This behavioral shift may reflect increasing confidence in SLN algorithms, secular changes in practice or center-specific implementation patterns. As an analysis of surgical behavior, the study cannot establish the oncologic safety of this shift, which warrants dedicated outcome studies.

articles.title: User satisfaction with Estetrol/Drospirenone combined oral contraception: A prospective observational study.
articles.journal: European journal of obstetrics, gynecology, and reproductive biology
articles.ta: Eur J Obstet Gynecol Reprod Biol
articles.authors: Pinto PV, Gomes C, Pinho AMD et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: This study evaluated women's overall satisfaction with a combined oral contraceptive containing estetrol 15 mg/drospirenone 3 mg (E4/DRSP) in clinical practice.
METHODS: This prospective, multicentre, six-cycle, non-interventional study included women aged 18-45 years who initiated hormonal contraception (starters) or switched from another hormonal contraceptive (switchers) to E4/DRSP.
RESULTS: Of 380 women starting E4/DRSP, 201 (52.9%) were switchers and 226 (59.5%) completed the six-cycle follow-up. In women with available follow-up data, satisfaction with E4/DRSP was high at Cycle 6 (starters 76.9% [95% CI 68.3-84.0], switchers 72.0% [95% CI 63.5-79.5]), with no significant differences between groups or over time (p > 0.05). Users reported a stable profile across well-being, mood, sexual life, premenstrual period and skin condition. Starters experienced significant improvements in breast tenderness between Cycles 3 and 6 (p = 0.024). Satisfaction with the cycle pattern improved significantly in both groups between baseline and Cycle 3, and baseline and Cycle 6 (all p < 0.05). Adherence among respondents was significantly higher for switchers (95.8%) than starters (83.3%) at Cycle 6 (p = 0.022), and approximately 80% of respondents intended to continue using E4/DRSP. Sixty-six women (17.4% [95% CI 13.6-21.2]) reported discontinuing E4/DRSP because of adverse events (AEs). The types of AEs most reported were consistent with those described in Phase 3 trials, with no new safety signals reported.
CONCLUSION: Among women who completed six cycles of follow-up, E4/DRSP users reported high satisfaction, high intention to continue use, and an AE profile generally consistent with that described in Phase 3 trials.

articles.title: Couple age interaction and cumulative live birth rate after IVF/ICSI: a large cohort study.
articles.authors: Ren X, Shen Y, Lv Q et al.
articles.abstract:
RESEARCH QUESTION: Does maternal age modify the association between paternal age and cumulative live birth rate (CLBR) after IVF/intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI)?
DESIGN: This retrospective cohort study included 22,013 first oocyte retrieval cycles using autologous oocytes and non-donor spermatozoa at a tertiary reproductive centre between 2016 and 2024. The primary outcome was CLBR within the first three embryo transfer attempts from a single retrieval. Paternal age was analysed per 5-year increase, and interaction with maternal age was tested formally. Multivariable models adjusted for female body mass index, duration of infertility, type of infertility, fertilization method, and major infertility aetiologies. Sensitivity analyses used CLBR within the first five embryo transfer attempts.
RESULTS: Among women aged <40 years, paternal age was not associated with CLBR within three embryo transfer attempts [adjusted OR (aOR) per 5-year increase 0.98, 95% CI 0.94-1.02]. Among women aged ≥40 years, increasing paternal age was associated with lower CLBR (aOR 0.78, 95% CI 0.75- 0.81), with a significant paternal age × maternal age interaction (P for interaction < 0.001). In the older maternal age group, increasing paternal age was also associated with a lower cumulative clinical pregnancy rate and higher risk of miscarriage, whereas fertilization rate and high-quality embryo rate did not decline. Results were consistent when CLBR was defined within the first five embryo transfer attempts.
CONCLUSIONS: Paternal age was not uniformly associated with CLBR after IVF/ICSI. Its adverse association became clinically evident mainly among couples in which the female partner was aged ≥40 years. These findings support joint consideration of paternal and maternal age when counselling couples about cumulative reproductive prognosis after assisted reproduction.

articles.title: 'On an assembly line': women's experiences of the ethical dimensions of assisted reproductive care in china.
articles.authors: Qiu RM, Dunn M, Mao W et al.
articles.abstract:
RESEARCH QUESTION: How do women experience the ethical dimensions of IVF care, and how are these experiences shaped by the clinical, organizational and sociocultural context in China?
DESIGN: Semi-structured, in-depth interviews between June and August 2025 with 28 women undergoing IVF or who had completed treatment within the preceding 6 months in China. Data were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis informed by patient-centred care, respectful maternity care and biomedical ethics as complementary conceptual resources.
RESULTS: 'Assembly-line IVF' emerged as the overarching interpretive metaphor, capturing organizational and sociocultural forces that converged to shape women's experiences of care. Four interrelated themes highlighted ethical dimensions warranting attention: informed consent was sometimes experienced as administrative compliance, weakening trust and autonomy; age-related medical discourse and limited privacy were perceived as challenging dignity; insufficient recognition of pain and emotional distress was perceived as compromising bodily integrity; and gendered asymmetries were experienced as concentrating treatment-related and emotional labour on women, raising concerns about justice.
CONCLUSIONS: Autonomy, dignity, bodily integrity and justice are identified as key ethical dimensions of IVF care in China. The findings challenge assessments focused solely on biomedical outcomes and demonstrate that the ethical quality of care is shaped by individual healthcare professionals and by organizational and sociocultural contexts.

articles.title: A synthetic microbial community derived from the roots of Kalidium gracile enhances its salt tolerance by modulating gene transcription and reshaping the rhizosphere soil microbiota.
articles.authors: Yue Y, Yuan M, Fan Z et al.
articles.abstract: Soil salinization and alkalinization are severe environmental problems in the desert-oasis transition zone of the Hexi Corridor, China. Rhizosphere microbial communities are key regulators of plant adaptation to saline-alkali environments. However, the functional microbial resources and ecological mechanisms underlying the contribution of the rhizosphere microbiome associated with Kalidium gracile to its saline adaptation remain poorly understood. In this study, we characterized the rhizosphere microbiome of K. gracile inhabiting severely saline-alkali soil and isolated two Bacillus strains with strong plant growth-promoting potential, which were subsequently used to construct a synthetic microbial community (SynCom). Inoculation experiments under salt stress demonstrated that SynCom increased plant biomass and chlorophyll content and modulated host transcriptional responses associated with the "growth-defense trade-off." Shortly after inoculation, plant growth-related pathways were suppressed, while CAT and POD activities surged by 45% and 213%, respectively. At later stages after inoculation, the expression of growth-related pathways was significantly upregulated. Metagenomic sequencing revealed that SynCom reshaped the rhizosphere microbial community, with the relative abundances of the halophilic bacteria Halomonas and Marinobacter increasing by 317% and 1162%, respectively. The abundances of functional genes involved in soil carbon, nitrogen, phosphorus, and sulfur nutrient cycling were all significantly increased. Collectively, these findings indicate that SynCom enhances plant salt tolerance through a multi-layered regulatory mechanism by coordinating host physiological responses and rhizosphere microbial functions. Collectively, these findings reveal a multi-level regulatory mechanism through which SynCom enhances plant salt tolerance by coordinating host physiological responses and rhizosphere microbiome functions.

articles.title: Rationale and design of randomized, double-blind trial evaluating the efficacy of single-dose HPV vaccine efficacy in women aged 18 to 30: The PRISMA trial.
articles.authors: Romero B, Liu D, Ocampo R et al.
articles.abstract: Evidence from the Costa Rica HPV Vaccine Trial suggested that a single dose may provide durable protection in young adult women. Subsequent studies confirmed the non-inferiority of one vs. two doses of the main vaccines among young girls. Vaccination of older cohorts might accelerate cervical cancer elimination, especially if a single dose provides adequate protection. Randomized data are needed to support extended-age, single-dose vaccination strategies. Herein, we present the design, rationale and recruitment results of a three-arm, randomized, double-blinded, clinical trial in Costa Rica to evaluate the efficacy of a single dose of the bivalent (Cervarix®) and nonavalent (Gardasil 9®) HPV vaccines compared with an active control (Tdap). 4925 HPV vaccine-naïve women aged 18-30 years old were enrolled, randomized 1:1:1, and followed for 36 months with cervicovaginal self-sampling every six months starting at 12 months, annual blood collection, and oral/anal sampling at selected visits, with high participation rates. Participants attended ~90% of planned study visits and >96% of attendees provided the necessary specimens. The primary endpoint is incident cerviccovaginal HPV16/18 infection persisting ≥6 months among women HPV16/18 DNA-negative at the enrollment and vaccination visits. Secondary endpoints include vaccine efficacy in the intention-to-treat cohort, oral and anal HPV16/18 protection, and immunogenicity profiles. Trial results will inform mathematical models estimating impact and cost-effectiveness of extending single-dose vaccination to adult young women and directly inform policy to enable extended-age, single-dose strategies to accelerate cervical cancer prevention globally. Furthermore, the study will provide the first evidence for single-dose efficacy against anal and oral HPV infection.

articles.title: Prognostic value of PD-L1 expression and association with HRD in high-grade serous ovarian cancer: an ancillary analysis of the PAOLA-1/ENGOT-ov25 trial (GINECO).
articles.authors: Bataillon G, Cyrille S, Salvioni A et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The prognostic significance of programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) in high-grade serous ovarian cancer (HGSOC) remains uncertain, because of heterogeneity in assays, scoring systems, and assessment of tumor and immune compartments across studies. We therefore evaluated its biological and prognostic relevance using a standardized pathological approach in a large, well-annotated phase III trial cohort.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this ancillary retrospective biomarker analysis of PAOLA-1/ENGOT-ov25, PD-L1 was assessed by 22C3 pharmDx immunohistochemistry on whole-slide sections from 324 International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics stage III-IV HGSOCs. Three predefined scoring systems commonly used in PD-L1 assessment were applied: tumor proportion score (TPS ≥1%), immune cell score (IC ≥1%), and combined positive score (CPS ≥1). Associations with homologous recombination deficiency (HRD), BRCA1/2 status, and survival were examined using multivariable Cox models adjusted for major clinicopathological factors.
RESULTS: PD-L1 positivity was observed in 38.2% of tumors by TPS, 62.4% by IC, and 66.1% by CPS. Positivity did not significantly vary by sampling site or timing of tissue collection relative to chemotherapy. PD-L1 positivity was enriched in HRD-positive tumors (TPS: 42.3% versus 28.0%, P = 0.017; IC: 65.1% versus 52.0%, P = 0.030; CPS: 70.4% versus 53.0%, P = 0.003) and remained independently associated with improved overall survival in adjusted analyses [TPS: adjusted hazard ratio (aHR) 0.70 (95% confidence interval 0.49-1.00), P = 0.046; IC: aHR 0.68 (0.49-0.95), P = 0.025; CPS: aHR 0.70 (0.50-0.97), P = 0.037]. Associations with progression-free survival were not statistically significant after adjustment.
CONCLUSIONS: In advanced HGSOC, standardized whole-slide PD-L1 assessment identifies an HRD-associated PD-L1-positive immune context independently associated with improved overall survival. Immune-integrated scoring approaches capture this signal more effectively than tumor-cell-restricted assessment and provide a robust framework for future ovarian cancer studies.

articles.title: HPV DNA integration is correlated with persistence or progression of cervical intraepithelial neoplasia 2 (CIN2).
articles.authors: Van Arsdale A, Gallego S, Mescheryakova O et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE(S): To determine whether identical HPV-human DNA integrations in cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 2 (CIN2) lesions are retained during progression to squamous cervical carcinoma (SCC) and whether such integrations can predict lesion persistence or progression.
METHODS: Longitudinal cervical samples were analyzed using multiplexed DNA hybridization-capture targeting 225 HPV types, followed by short-read sequencing to identify HPV-human DNA integration junctions. Integration events were evaluated in (i) serial samples from CIN lesions that progressed to SCC and (ii) a baseline cohort of 23 patients with incident CIN2. Clinical outcomes (regression vs persistence/progression) were compared by integration status using Fisher's Exact Test and multivariable Bayesian logistic regression to estimate effect sizes in the setting of small sample size.
RESULTS: Identical HPV-human DNA integrations were preserved across serial samples in seven CIN lesions that progressed to SCC, supporting their biological relevance in carcinogenesis. In the CIN2 cohort, no integrations were detected in any of the 12 patients whose lesions regressed, whereas integrations were present in four of eleven patients whose lesions persisted or progressed (p=0.04). Bayesian logistic regression estimated a 22-fold higher odds of persistence/progression when integration was detected at baseline CIN2 diagnosis. HPV16 positivity was also associated with persistence/progression, with a smaller estimated effect size (9.4-fold higher odds), consistent with prior epidemiologic observations.
CONCLUSION(S): HPV DNA integrations were associated with CIN2 persistence and progression, and identical integrations were retained during evolution to SCC. Integration analysis at CIN2 diagnosis may identify lesions at highest risk for progression, providing a biomarker to refine clinical management and reduce unnecessary excisional procedures.

articles.title: Fertility Preservation in Male Children, Adolescents, and Young Adults With Cancer: A Systematic Review and Appraisal of Guidelines.
articles.authors: Fields E, Kaushal S, Maher S et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Advances in child, adolescent and young adult oncology have shifted the focus of cancer treatment towards quality of life. Gonadotoxicity remains a devastating late effect of treatment for some survivors. While numerous guidelines exist for fertility preservation, referral rates for fertility preservation are low. We sought to recognize and understand systemic barriers to standardized fertility care for male child, adolescent and young adults with cancer.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: We performed a systematic review and database search of clinical practice guidelines. Eligible guidelines included male children, adolescents, and young adults between the ages of 0-39 years diagnosed with any cancer. Appraisal was performed using the AGREE II instrument. Concordance across 28 clinical and logistical areas was analyzed to identify areas of consensus and disagreement.
RESULTS: We identified 33 guidelines globally that met inclusion criteria. Seventy-two percent of appraised guidelines were rated as "high quality". Concordance across guidelines was low overall (25%), with complete discordance in ethical and logistical domains. Key consensus items included sperm cryopreservation as a preservation method, initiation prior to gonadotoxic treatment, and inclusion of an oncologist and fertility specialist on the care team. Guidelines disagreed on the specific makeup of a multidisciplinary care team, pre-pubertal treatments, and specific ethical/logistical aspects.
CONCLUSIONS: Although guidance for fertility preservation exists, it remains inconsistent and incompletely specified, particularly on ethical and logistical domains, thus limiting its clinical utility. Global efforts must prioritize standardization of logistical and ethical frameworks to enable implementation in real-world clinical practice and accelerate research in areas of controversy.

articles.title: Hepatitis C Treatment Access With Implementation of an Antenatal Linkage-to-Care Bundle.
articles.authors: McCrary LM, Marks LR, Kelly JC et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate a health system-wide quality-improvement bundle (HALT-C [hepatitis C antenatal linkage-to-care]) on its ability to integrate proactive patient identification, care coordination, and treatment timing options on direct-acting antiviral prescription by 6 months postpartum.
METHODS: We implemented our quality-improvement initiative at a large midwestern health system and evaluated its effect by comparing outcomes among eligible pregnancies identified preimplementation (December 1, 2021-May 31, 2023) with those identified postimplementation (March 1, 2024-August 31, 2025). Eligible patients were aged at least 18 years, with detectable hepatitis C virus RNA and at least one encounter in the health system before 35 weeks of gestation. The primary outcome was the percentage of patients prescribed direct-acting antivirals by 6 months postpartum. Secondary outcomes included linkage to care, the treatment timing decision, treatment completion, sustained virologic response (SVR), infant screening, and perinatal transmission. Comparison of antenatal initiation of treatment and postpartum initiation of treatment was also performed.
RESULTS: We identified 62 bundle-eligible pregnancies in the preimplementation period and identified 35 in the postimplementation period. Direct-acting antiviral prescription by 6 months postpartum increased from 48.4% to 77.1% (P=.009); treatment completion improved from 21.0% to 54.3% (P=.001). Treatment increases were greatest among patients who delivered regionally, rather than at the main hospital, with an increase in direct-acting antiviral prescription rates of 14.3% to 72.7% (P<.001). Thirty of 35 individuals identified postimplementation were successfully linked to care, and 75.0% of clinic attendees preferred antenatal treatment over postpartum treatment. Known treatment completion and SVR increased from 21.0% to 54.3% (P=.001). Those treated antenatally were twice as likely to complete treatment than those who deferred postpartum (92.3% vs 45.5%; P=.02). Infant screening and perinatal transmission rates did not change; however, no perinatal transmissions occurred among infants where treatment occurred antenatally.
CONCLUSION: The HALT-C bundle was associated with significantly improved direct-acting antiviral receipt across a regional health system. Most patients preferred treatment during pregnancy. Patients treated antenatally were twice as likely to complete treatment, highlighting pregnancy as an…

articles.title: Neoadjuvant Apalutamide With or Without Abiraterone Acetate Plus Prednisone and Gonadotropin-Releasing Hormone Agonist Prior to Nerve-Sparing Radical Prostatectomy in High-Risk Prostate Cancer: Protocol for a Randomized Phase 2 Trial.
articles.authors: Zhang AY, Stein MN, Ghodoussipour S et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Radical prostatectomy (RP) is an accepted, definitive treatment for appropriately selected men with high-risk localized prostate cancer (PCa). However, neoadjuvant androgen receptor inhibition prior to RP is not currently the standard of care. Wide resection of the neurovascular bundles may improve local oncologic control but can adversely affect postoperative erectile function and urinary continence. Apalutamide directly inhibits the androgen receptor, while abiraterone acetate inhibits cytochrome P450 17A1-mediated androgen synthesis and is often administered with prednisone. Gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) agonists further suppress testicular androgen production. Intensified androgen pathway inhibition prior to surgery may therefore downstage localized disease and facilitate bilateral nerve-sparing RP.
OBJECTIVE: This study was defined to evaluate whether 3 months of neoadjuvant apalutamide-based therapy before RP improves postoperative potency recovery by 12 months compared with immediate RP in men with high-risk localized PCa. Secondary objectives include evaluation of postoperative continence, pathological outcomes, biochemical recurrence, perioperative outcomes, and quality of life (QoL).
METHODS: This is a prospective, multicenter, randomized phase 2 clinical trial (ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT02949284). Eligible patients with high-risk PCa were randomized 1:1:1 to (1) apalutamide 240 mg daily for 3 months followed by RP, (2) apalutamide 240 mg daily with abiraterone acetate 1000 mg plus prednisone 10 mg daily and a GnRH agonist for 3 months followed by RP, or (3) immediate RP without neoadjuvant therapy. The primary end point is potency recovery by 12 months postoperatively, defined as the ability to penetrate in sexual intercourse in more than half of attempts. Secondary end points include continence recovery, pathological response, positive surgical margins, biochemical recurrence, perioperative outcomes, and QoL. The primary comparisons evaluate each experimental arm against the surgery-only arm. Pairwise comparisons of the primary end point will use 1-sided Fisher exact tests with a Bonferroni adjustment. Additional continuous and categorical outcomes will be analyzed using appropriate nonparametric or categorical tests, and biochemical recurrence-free survival will be assessed using Kaplan-Meier analysis.
RESULTS: As of March 2026, patient enrollment has been completed. A total of 96 patients provided consent and were screened,…

articles.title: Effects of music medicine on anxiety among primigravida mothers of preterm neonates: The CalM MOM randomised controlled trial protocol.
articles.authors: Mukherjee B, Rajendran T, Augustine AM et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Preterm birth and Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU) admission are significant stressors that heighten maternal anxiety. Although RCTs have reported that music-based interventions used alongside usual care (UC) are effective and low-cost in reducing maternal anxiety, evidence from India remains limited.
OBJECTIVE: Primary objective is to assess the impact of listening to recorded classical Indian Instrumental Saraswati Veena music (Ragas Kalyani and Hindolam) (30-minutes/day over 7-days) alongside UC on maternal anxiety (STAI-state anxiety) of primigravida women with preterm neonates in the NICU. Secondary objectives measure changes in anxiety (Perinatal Anxiety Screening Scale (PASS)), maternal-infant bonding, breast milk volume, and neonatal body weight.
METHOD: This three-arm parallel-group, superiority RCT among primigravida mothers with anxiety (screened using PASS) of preterm neonates (30-36 weeks of gestation, admitted to NICU) delivered vaginally at Government Lady Goschen Hospital, Mangalore. The intervention arm will receive Music Medicine (MM), the comparator arm Nature Sounds (NS), and the control arm UC. Participant blinding is not feasible (auditory intervention), and they serve as their own outcome-assessors (self-reported questionnaires); investigators and the independent statistician will remain blinded. Personnel interacting with participants are blinded to study objectives; enrolment/allocation staff blinded to the randomization sequence, and assessment staff blinded to group identity. Randomization will employ a STATA-generated, permuted stratified block design stratified by baseline anxiety severity and gestational age (Allocation concealment: Sequentially Numbered, Opaque, Sealed Envelopes; Allocation Ratio: 1:1:1). Sample size (66/arm; total N = 198) was determined through a simulation-based power analysis (5,000 iterations, base-R), assuming an MCID of 4 (MM) and 2 (NS) on the STAI, residual SD of ~8, powered at 80% (α = 0.05). Blinded sample-size re-estimation will be conducted at 50% enrollment completion. Primary powered analysis will employ ANCOVA (baseline-adjusted), and Secondary (exploratory) analyses will utilize a linear mixed-effects model for longitudinal continuous data with time × group interaction.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Clinical Trial Registry of India; CTRI/2025/06/088896; URL: https://ctri.nic.in/Clinicaltrials/pmaindet2.php?EncHid=MTM0Mzg0&Enc=&userName= Protocol version: Version 03, July 07, 2026.

articles.title: Examining individual and school-level predictors of positive attitudes towards condom use among adolescents in Tanzania: An exploratory analysis using hierarchical linear modeling.
articles.authors: Bryk S, Shichijo A, Kaaya S et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Adolescents shoulder a disproportionate burden of poor sexual and reproductive health (SRH) outcomes in many lower-income countries, including Tanzania. Availability, access, and use of contraception, including condoms, reduces unintended pregnancies and sexually transmitted infections. Research indicates that early attitudes can influence future behavior, yet little is known about young adolescents' attitudes toward condom use. This study examines whether and how knowledge, beliefs, and sociodemographic factors influence attitudes toward condom use among adolescents in Tanzania.
METHODS: Data are from a school-cluster randomized controlled trial with Standard 7 adolescents in two Tanzanian districts. Using an analytic sample of 1,057 adolescents from 20 primary schools, descriptive analysis and hierarchical linear modeling (HLM) were conducted to parse out individual- and school-level influences that shape attitudes towards condom use.
RESULTS: Individual and aggregate characteristics of the school environment were associated with attitudes toward condom use. At the individual level, more positive attitudes were associated with being male, having access to condoms, and having knowledge about condom use and pregnancy prevention. At the school-level, more positive attitudes were associated with a larger male population in classes, greater breadth of pregnancy knowledge among students, and having relationships with trusted adults.
CONCLUSIONS: Findings suggest that adolescents largely turn to peers and adults for information and guidance regarding condoms. In turn, the views and beliefs of others can influence attitudes towards condom use. Schools might be an effective unit of change for interventions to facilitate more group-based education about the prevention of negative SRH outcomes.

articles.title: Infant presence and mother-infant conflict predict fetal loss in wild mandrills.
articles.authors: Smit N, Roura-Torres B, Delaunay A et al.
articles.abstract: Female fitness depends on reproductive pace and offspring survival, both of which are determined by the ability to balance resource allocation between current and future reproduction. Using 11 years of data on 356 pregnancies (52 of which resulted in fetal loss) from 117 wild female mandrills, we show that females who conceive while still caring for a young infant experience a greater probability of fetal loss as well as increased mother-infant behavioral conflict in the form of maternal rejection. In addition, females whose infants throw more tantrums show a greater probability of fetal loss, consistent with observations from other species where living offspring can interfere in parental reproduction. Finally, females who lose a fetus show greater subsequent reproductive success (produce more surviving infants and show shorter inter-birth intervals) than females who give birth but their infants die soon after birth. These findings suggest that fetal loss may represent an adaptive physiological response to the energetic constraints imposed by overlapping gestation and maternal care, potentially limiting the fitness costs associated with short inter-birth intervals and concurrent investment in multiple dependent offspring.

articles.title: Depressive Symptoms and Central Obesity Over the Menopausal Transition and the Development of Type 2 Diabetes Later in Life: Decomposing Direct and Indirect Effects.
articles.authors: Chen Y, Brooks MM, El Khoudary SR et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study investigated the association between depressive symptoms during the menopausal transition and subsequent incident type 2 diabetes (T2D), with particular focus on: (1) quantifying the mediating role of central obesity in this association, and (2) examining differential effects by depressive symptom subscales (somatic vs. cognitive/affective symptoms).
METHODS: We analyzed data from 1719 participants in the Study of Women's Health Across the Nation, a multi-ethnic cohort study of midlife women. Depressive symptoms were assessed repeatedly using the Center for Epidemiologic Studies Depression Scale (CES-D). We calculated the total and subscales of depressive symptom burden during the menopausal transition. Causal mediation analysis within a counterfactual framework was employed to decompose the total effect between depressive symptoms and incident T2D during postmenopausal follow-up into natural direct effects (NDE) and indirect effects (NIE) mediated through central obesity measured at the first postmenopausal visit, adjusting for demographic, lifestyle, and health-related covariates.
RESULTS: During a mean postmenopausal follow-up of 11.60 (SD 3.58) years, 170 women (9.89%) developed T2D during follow-up. Central obesity mediated 21.4-23.5% of the total effect of depressive symptoms burden on T2D risk. Somatic subscales of CES-D scores showed strongest associations (OR=1.272 (95% CI:1.041-1.567) and NIE OR=1.100 (1.040-1.165)) in unadjusted models, with 21.3-25.0% mediated through central obesity after full adjustment. Cognitive/affective subscale showed weaker mediation effects (19.4-26.9%). Sensitivity analyses confirmed robustness to unmeasured confounding, with somatic symptom effects remaining significant under moderate confounding (NIE OR= 1.057 (95% CI:1.004-1.115)).
CONCLUSIONS: Greater cumulative depressive symptom burden during the menopausal transition, particularly somatic subscales, was associated with higher odds of incident T2D after postmenopause, with part of the association mediated through central obesity at postmenopause. These findings highlight the menopausal transition as a critical period for interventions targeting both mental health and metabolic risk factors.

articles.title: Temporal dynamics of spontaneous blastocyst re-expansion as a predictor of frozen embryo transfer success.
articles.authors: Golan-Accav N, Amir H, Rahav R et al.
articles.abstract:
ABSTRACT: Post-thaw blastocyst collapse is a frequent occurrence in frozen embryo transfer (FET) cycles, yet standard evaluation often relies on static post-thaw snapshots. This retrospective cohort study evaluated 438 single-blastocyst FET cycles using good-quality day 5 blastocysts vitrified without artificial shrinkage, introducing a dynamic evaluation framework based on two routine clinical time points: immediately post-thaw (t1) and pre-transfer (t2). Our results demonstrate that expansion status at transfer, rather than initial post-thaw appearance, is the primary predictor of success. Blastocysts that re-expanded prior to transfer achieved live birth rates (22.7%) comparable to continuously expanded embryos (20.0%; P > 0.05), whereas persistent collapse resulted in significantly lower success (7.8%; P < 0.03). Crucially, a significant interaction was revealed between initial collapse and the thaw-to-transfer interval: for every additional hour of incubation, the odds of remaining collapsed significantly decreased (OR = 0.49, P = 0.038). These findings demonstrate that spontaneous collapse is a transient, reversible state that can be successfully overcome through extended post-thaw incubation. Assessing embryos across two simple, routine time points provides clinicians with an accessible framework to manage incubation timing, maximize re-expansion probability, and optimize live birth outcomes.
LAY SUMMARY: When embryos are frozen and thawed for fertility treatment, they sometimes collapse, but does this mean they are no longer viable? This study evaluated 438 FET cycles to understand whether collapsed embryos can recover and whether giving them more time in the incubator before transfer makes a difference. The key finding is that what matters most is how an embryo looks atthe time of transfer, not immediately after thawing. Embryos that re-expanded before being transferred had similar success rates to those that never collapsed. Only embryos that remained collapsed at transfer had significantly poorer outcomes. Importantly, for every additional hour spent in the incubator, a collapsed embryo's odds of recovering improved substantially. This means that rather than discarding a collapsed embryo, clinicians may simply need to wait; giving it time to recover could meaningfully improve the chances of a successful pregnancy. Collapsed embryos that are given longer time to recover in the incubator before transfer may have the same chance of achieving a…

articles.title: Associations of Occupational Noise Levels, Psychological Distress, and Reproductive Aging Among Perimenopausal Female Workers: Correlational Pathways and Interaction Patterns.
articles.authors: Ma C, Jiao B, Zhao J et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Occupational noise exposure and psychological distress are significant occupational health risks faced by working women, both of which may affect reproductive health. This study aimed to investigate the correlational pathways and interaction patterns linking occupational noise exposure levels, psychological distress, and reproductive aging among perimenopausal female workers.
METHODS: Of the 5463 female workers screened, 1030 eligible workers (age: ≥40 years; 737 noise-exposed and 293 controls) were analyzed. Individual noise exposure, such as 8-h equivalent sound level (LA eq,8h ), was first measured, followed by the assessment of psychological distress using the Depression, Anxiety, and Stress Scale. Three reproductive aging outcomes-perimenopausal syndrome (measured by the Kupperman Index), early menopause, and self-reported premature ovarian insufficiency (POI)-were recorded using a structured questionnaire. Finally, Bayesian network models explored the correlational pathways, with a generalized additive model (GAM) used to model multiplicative interaction associations.
RESULTS: The prevalence rates of perimenopausal syndrome, early menopause, and self-reported POI were 37.77%, 21.26%, and 4.95%, respectively. Bayesian network analysis identified statistical direct correlations between the noise exposure levels and perimenopausal syndrome, as well as statistical indirect correlations between noise exposure levels and perimenopausal syndrome and self-reported POI via psychological distress. Furthermore, additive synergistic associations were detected between the noise exposure levels and psychological distress for perimenopausal syndrome (synergy index [SI] = 2.53, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.30-12.53) and early menopause (SI = 2.48, 95% CI: 1.28-12.18). The GAM confirmed a significant interaction only for perimenopausal syndrome, with a relative excess risk due to interaction of 1.10 (95% CI: 0.36-1.84) and an excess risk of 21.63% (95% CI: 2.02-45.01). Conclusion Perimenopausal female workers exposed to noise displayed high prevalence rates of psychological distress and perimenopausal syndrome. Noise exposure levels and psychological distress exhibited combined correlations with reproductive aging outcomes, particularly perimenopausal syndrome. Thus, integrated management of noise and psychological distress warrants attention to potentially improve female workers' reproductive aging outcomes.

articles.title: Effect of Acoustic Environment Improvement Combined with Roy Adaptation Model-Based Supportive Nursing on Self-Efficacy and Maternal Role Adaptation in Advanced-Age Primiparas.
articles.authors: Wang Y, Chen Q
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the effect of acoustic environment improvement combined with Roy adaptation model (RAM)-based supportive nursing on self-efficacy and maternal role adaptation in advanced-age primiparas.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 158 eligible advanced-age primiparas who gave birth in the obstetrics department of the Fourth Affiliated Hospital of Soochow University between February 2025 and February 2026. The primiparas were divided into a control group ( n  = 80) and an observation group ( n  = 78) according to the nursing method they actually received. The control group received RAM-based supportive nursing care, whereas the observation group received acoustic environment improvement combined with RAM-based supportive nursing care. The Perceived Maternal Parenting Self-Efficacy scale, Maternal Role Adaptation Scale, Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI), time to first lactation, and exclusive breastfeeding rate were compared between the two groups before and after nursing.
RESULTS: Repeated-measures analysis of variance showed significant effects of time, group, and time × group interaction on maternal role adaptation scores (all P < 0.05). Bonferroni-adjusted comparisons demonstrated significant within-group changes over time (all adjusted P < 0.05), and the observation group had higher scores than the control group at discharge and 6 weeks postpartum (both P < 0.05). For PSQI scores, significant effects of time ( P < 0.001), group ( P  = 0.003), and time × group interaction ( P  = 0.039) were observed. The observation group showed lower PSQI scores than the control group at discharge and 6 weeks postpartum ( P  = 0.004 and P  = 0.001, respectively). Time to first lactation in the observation group was significantly shorter than that in the control group (24.87 ± 3.53 h vs. 28.21 ± 4.12 h; P < 0.001). At 6 weeks postpartum, the exclusive breastfeeding rate was significantly higher in the observation group than in the control group (76.9% vs. 62.5%; P  = 0.049).
CONCLUSION: Among advanced-age primiparas, acoustic environment improvement combined with RAM-based supportive nursing was associated with improved sleep quality, enhanced self-efficacy and neonatal care capabilities, and promoted maternal role adaptation, and may help promote lactation and increase the exclusive breastfeeding rate.

articles.title: Biological sex-dependent hormonal signaling and metabolomic profiles in obesity alter tumor microenvironment and immunotherapy outcomes.
articles.authors: Vick LV, Rosario SR, Wang Z et al.
articles.abstract: Commonly viewed as a negative prognostic factor in cancer, obesity is associated with improved responses to cancer immunotherapy using immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs). Although data suggest a sexual dimorphism influencing the effects of obesity on immunotherapy responses, to our knowledge, the intersection of sex and obesity on immunotherapy requires further exploration. We demonstrate, in a pan-cancer analysis stratified by sex and BMI, that obesity (BMI ≥ 30) is associated with improved survival after ICI only in male patients. In preclinical models of diet-induced obesity (DIO), we observed that only DIO male tumor-bearing mice responded better to ICI. The differential effect of sex on outcomes was associated with alterations in the tumor microenvironment where DIO female mice demonstrated increased tumor-associated macrophages skewed toward a M2 phenotype. Ovariectomy of DIO female mice reduced M2 polarization and increased anti-tumor immune responses including increases in tumor-infiltrating T cells following ICI. Metabolomic analysis of DIO mice demonstrated distinct profiles base on sex. Re-stratification of female cancer patients revealed that obesity was associated with improved outcome, but only in post-menopausal (age ≥ 55) patients. We identify that the immunotherapy "obesity paradox" is sex-dependent and that hormonal and metabolomic status modulates the influence of obesity on ICIs.

articles.title: 'Estaba en muy buenas manos': Experiences of accompanied abortion after 17 weeks in Argentina, Chile, and Ecuador.
articles.authors: Doria CM, Bercu C, Zurbriggen R et al.
articles.abstract: In Latin America, where abortions later in pregnancy are legally and socially restricted, many individuals turn to the support of feminist accompaniment collectives. These accompaniment collectives provide practical information, access to medications, and emotional and physical support to individuals seeking to self-manage their abortions outside of clinical settings. Little research, however, has examined how people having abortions later in pregnancy experience the emotional and physical support provided by accompaniers. This study draws on 26 in-depth interviews to explore the lived experiences of individuals who received in-person accompaniment support for abortions after 17 weeks of pregnancy in Argentina, Chile, and Ecuador. Our findings reveal how participants experienced later accompanied abortion as safe and emotionally supportive, which countered the stigma and violence associated with medical care in the formal health system. Our analysis centres the model of abortion accompaniment as a feminist practice of care that not only reshapes the lived experiences of later abortion, but also presents a radically distinct, and preferable, model of abortion provision. This study demonstrates that accompanied abortions offer a meaningful alternative to accessing safe, supportive abortion care, while offering potential improvements to clinic-supported abortion care.

articles.title: Rising cell-free DNA level tracks cancer-associated methylation signal and improves multicancer detection.
articles.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
articles.ta: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
articles.authors: Basu S, Hiremath P, Rathod N et al.
articles.abstract: Cancer patients carry more circulating cell-free DNA (ccfDNA)-small DNA fragments shed into the blood-than healthy people. Most of this excess comes not from the tumor itself but from immune cells, suggesting that it would simply dilute the much smaller amount of tumor-derived DNA in a blood sample. Using a study of 1,480 previously untreated participants across 43 hospitals-including patients with 14 cancer types spanning all stages, patients with benign growths, and healthy volunteers-we show the opposite: as total ccfDNA rises, it becomes enriched, not diluted, in fragments carrying cancer-associated DNA methylation signatures, independent of cancer type, disease stage, and a broad panel of demographic, clinical, and technical covariates. In fact, total ccfDNA explains more variance in cancer-associated methylation signal than the disease stage itself. This basic biological finding suggests a coupling between immune cell activity and tumor methylation. It also has a practical implication: we show that rising ccfDNA concentration is associated with higher cancer detection sensitivity, even within disease stages and particularly in early-stage disease-stage I sensitivity varied from 0.55 in the lowest ccfDNA concentration tertile to 0.85 in the highest, and stage II from 0.59 to 0.86. This suggests that ccfDNA concentration should be considered as a stage-independent stratification variable for benchmarking cancer-detection tests. Interestingly, similar behavior was observed in patients with symptomatic benign lesions, suggesting a broader biological response to abnormal tissue growth and not something unique to malignancy.

articles.title: A Phase I Trial of Low-Dose Gemcitabine Combined with ATR Inhibitor Elimusertib for Advanced Solid Tumors.
articles.authors: Jayakrishnan T, Porter R, Chen A et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Preclinical data suggest that the anticancer efficacy of Ataxia telangiectasia and Rad3-related protein (ATR) inhibitors can be synergistically enhanced by low-dose gemcitabine. To test the clinical feasibility of this regimen, we conducted a phase I trial of low-dose gemcitabine combined with the ATR inhibitor elimusertib (BAY1895344).
PATIENTS AND METHODS: This phase I study evaluated the combination of gemcitabine and elimusertib in patients with previously treated, incurable solid tumors. The primary objective was to assess the safety and tolerability of this regimen and to determine the maximum tolerated dose (MTD). Secondary objectives included assessment of objective response rate (ORR) per Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors (RECIST) version 1.1 and characterization of the pharmacokinetic (PK) profile.
RESULTS: Fourteen patients were enrolled; most patients had pancreatic cancer (n = 6) or ovarian cancer (n = 6). The median age was 63.5 years, and the median number of prior therapies was 2. The regimen caused significant toxicity, and 4 (28%) patients discontinued the trial because of treatment-related adverse events. The trial was stopped prior to establishing an MTD because of the pharmaceutical company's decision to halt development of the agent. A confirmed partial response (PR) was observed in one patient with platinum-refractory ovarian cancer harboring a gain in CCNE1. Another patient with pancreatic adenocarcinoma harboring biallelic ATM loss remained on trial for 9.5 months with stable disease, with an 85% decrease in CA19-9.
CONCLUSIONS: The combination of low-dose gemcitabine and elimusertib was not tolerable. Although evidence of antitumor activity was observed, significant improvements in tolerability are required for future ATR inhibitor combinations to be clinically feasible.
SIGNIFICANCE: ATR inhibitors show immense promise, particularly for ATM-deficient malignancies, yet their clinical utility is currently constrained by a limited therapeutic index. The significant toxicity observed in this trial of gemcitabine and the ATR inhibitor elimusertib underscores the necessity of developing new approaches to improve the safety and feasibility of these agents for the clinic.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT04616534.

articles.title: Early Metformin Initiation and Glycemic Outcomes in Gestational Diabetes: A Secondary Analysis of a Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.authors: Aguilar Macías DA, Alvarez-Iglesias A, Ferguson JM et al.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Conventional approaches to analyzing composite end points in clinical trials may not fully capture clinically meaningful treatment effects.
OBJECTIVE: To estimate treatment effects of early metformin initiation on clinically ordered glycemic outcomes (insulin initiation and fasting hyperglycemia at gestational weeks 32 and 38) using generalized pairwise comparisons (GPCs).
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This secondary analysis of a double-masked, placebo-controlled randomized clinical trial (conducted from June 2017 through September 2022) at 2 centers in Ireland (1 tertiary hospital and 1 regional hospital) included participants with gestational diabetes based on World Health Organization 2013 criteria. Participants were followed up through 12 weeks post partum. The data analysis was performed between October 18, 2025, and February 2, 2026.
INTERVENTION: Participants were randomized 1:1 to metformin (maximum dose, 2500 mg) or matching placebo, in addition to usual care.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Generalized pairwise comparisons were performed using (1) a prioritized hierarchy (insulin initiation, fasting hyperglycemia at week 32, and fasting hyperglycemia at week 38) and (2) nonprioritized analyses of each end point, with overall summaries using equal weights and prespecified clinical weights (0.50, 0.25, and 0.25, respectively). Treatment effect sizes were summarized using win ratio (WR), net treatment benefit (NTB), and win odds (WO).
RESULTS: Of 535 randomized pregnancies, 526 (262 placebo [49.0%] and 264 metformin [51.0%]; mean [SD] age of participants, 34.4 [4.8] years) had primary outcome data. Prioritized GPCs favored metformin over placebo for the composite outcome (WR, 1.46 [95% CI, 1.13-1.89]; NTB, 13.7 percentage points [95% CI, 4.3-22.8 percentage points]; WO, 1.34 [95% CI, 1.10-1.64]) (P = .004). The largest separation was observed for insulin initiation (WR, 1.68 [95% CI, 1.19-2.38]; NTB, 12.7 percentage points [95% CI, 4.2-21.0 percentage points]) (P = .003). Nonprioritized overall summaries favored metformin (WR, 1.53 [95% CI, 1.16-2.01]; NTB, 7.5 percentage points [95% CI, 2.7-12.3 percentage points]; WO, 1.32 [95% CI, 1.10-1.57]) (P = .002), with consistent clinically weighted results (WR, 1.57 [95% CI, 1.19-2.08]; NTB, 8.8 percentage points [95% CI, 3.4-14.2 percentage points]; WO, 1.39 [95% CI, 1.14-1.70]) (P = .001).
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this secondary analysis of a randomized clinical trial, prioritized…

articles.title: National Trends in Severe Maternal Morbidity by Insurance and Race and Ethnicity.
articles.authors: Srajer A, Ronksley P, Quinn A et al.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Rates of severe maternal morbidity (SMM) and mortality are rising in the US, disproportionally affecting racial and ethnic minority groups and Medicaid beneficiaries. Contemporary analyses investigating the intersectional impact of insurance and race and ethnicity on SMM are lacking.
OBJECTIVE: To examine national trends in SMM and maternal mortality across deliveries and evaluate the intersectional association of insurance type and race and ethnicity with these outcomes.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This serial cross-sectional study used population-based National Inpatient Sample (a 20% stratified sample of hospital discharges) data on delivery hospitalizations from October 1, 2015, to December 31, 2022, in the US, with analyses completed between July 7, 2025, and January 30, 2026.
EXPOSURE: Assessment of insurance (private vs Medicaid) and race and ethnicity independently and cross-classified into 10 intersectional groups.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Primary outcomes were composite SMM, nontransfusion-only SMM, and mortality. Multivariable logistic regression was used to estimate adjusted odds ratios (AORs) for outcomes across insurance, race and ethnicity, and intersectional groups.
RESULTS: Among 27 341 986 weighted deliveries (mean [SD] maternal age, 29.0 [5.8] years; 6.3% of Asian or Pacific Islander, 16.2% of Black, 22.4% of Hispanic, 0.8% of Native American, and 54.3% of White race and ethnicity), 563 250 (2.1%) were complicated by SMM, 2320 of which (0.4%) resulted in death. From 2015 to 2022, composite SMM rates increased 40.5% (from 175.0 to 245.9 per 10 000 deliveries; P < .001), with 16 of 21 individual complications (76.2%) significantly increasing. Medicaid covered 11 658 119 weighted deliveries (45.5%), and included a greater proportion of Black, Hispanic, and Native American individuals than the privately insured population. Adjusted odds of composite SMM were elevated among all intersectional groups compared with White patients with private insurance (all P < .001). Within each racial and ethnic group, SMM odds were significantly higher with Medicaid vs private insurance (Asian or Pacific Islander: AOR, 1.28 [95% CI, 1.20-1.36]; Black: AOR, 1.13 [95% CI, 1.10-1.17]; Hispanic: AOR, 1.29 [95% CI, 1.24-1.34]; Native American: AOR, 1.44 [95% CI, 1.24-1.67]; White: AOR, 1.23 [95% CI, 1.20-1.26]). Significantly increased odds of mortality were primarily observed for Medicaid-insured Asian or Pacific Islander (AOR, 2.63 [95%…

articles.title: Fertility and Later-Life Mental Health: Evidence on Transfers and Instrumental Assistance From Adult Children in Indonesia.
articles.authors: Nasution MI, Nasrudin R, Ikhsan M et al.
articles.abstract: ObjectiveThis study examined whether completed fertility shapes later-life mental health in Indonesia and whether adult children's support explains this relationship.MethodsUsing the 2007 and 2014 Indonesian Family Life Survey, we instrumented fertility with differential exposure to Village Contraceptive Distribution Centers and estimated 2SLS and instrumental-variables mediation models.ResultsAn additional child reduced CES-D score and probability of elevated depressive symptoms. Financial and material transfers formed a protective pathway, while the remaining component outside measured transfers offset part of this effect. Higher fertility also increased instrumental assistance, although its mediating contribution was imprecisely estimated. Protective effects were more apparent among respondents with less than primary education, alongside adverse physical and nutritional outcomes.DiscussionCompleted fertility may improve later-life mental health partly through transfers from adult children, while supportive and burdensome consequences coexist, especially among socioeconomically constrained older adults. Estimates apply to the fertility-responsive population identified by the IV design.

articles.title: Perimenopause and Menopause: Estrogen-Deficient Skin and Impaired Quality of Life-Dermal Aging a Visible Mirror Reflecting Internal Aging and Health.
articles.authors: Lephart ED, Leverett J, Kong R et al.
articles.abstract: Increased awareness in women's health has taken place over the last 5 to 10 years, especially associated with aging, where perimenopause and menopause have been highlighted topics. This review examines how changes with age in women during perimenopause and menopause lead to estrogen-deficient skin and impaired quality of life (QOL). The topics presented include: (1) the reasons why women's health (perimenopause and menopause) is finally taking a prominent position in the public and medical mindset, (2) chronological (intrinsic) and photo (extrinsic) skin aging characteristics and skin changes by each decade of life, (3) the importance of and the changes to estrogen levels in aging women (especially with perimenopause and menopause) that lead to estrogen-deficient skin, (4) in brief, hormonal and selective estrogen receptor modulators (SERMs), including polyphenolic and isoflavonoid treatments, plus influencing lifestyle factors, and (5) using skin changes, as the "observable organ" and a reflective mirror of internal aging in women that may signal the potential decline of various unseen tissue/organ systems. This represents a different paradigm for the functional aspects in the body associated with the shifts in and loss of estrogen. Thus, skin health with aging (and the decline in and loss of estrogen) may provide nutritional and medical professionals, especially dermatologists, with a unique position to lead a discussion with patients to consider healthiness beyond dermal changes. Finally, potential treatments to assist and/or enhance women's healthspan and longevity may be part of this exchange in a collaborative examination.Graphical abstract available for this article.

articles.title: The modulation of PERK/ATF4/CHOP signaling by Neurokinin 3 receptor antagonists to ameliorate hepatic steatosis and endocrine dysfunction in PMOS mice - targeting the implication of endoplasmic reticulum stress.
articles.authors: Fernando T, Pan J, Gong Z et al.
articles.abstract: Lipotoxicity contributes to polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS) pathogenesis by inducing hyperandrogenism (HA) and insulin resistance (IR), while excess testosterone triggers endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress and the unfolded protein response (UPR) in PMOS models. However, ER stress and UPR activation under HA-obese conditions remain unexplored in granulosa cells (GCs) and PMOS mouse liver and ovary. Neurokinin 3 receptor antagonists (NK3Ra) reverse PMOS metabolic and reproductive impairments; therefore we established an HA-obese model by exposing KGN cells to palmitic acid (PA) and dihydrotestosterone (DHT), and an HFD-letrozole PMOS mouse model, both treated with NK3Ra. In KGN cells, ER and mitochondrial ultrastructure disruption was observed by TEM, UPR sensor protein and gene expression/phosphorylation was analyzed by qPCR and western blotting, and NK3Ra rescue of cell viability was evaluated, alongside peripheral and tissue biochemical/hormonal assays, immunohistochemistry for AMH, UPR sensor and cascade proteins, and redox metabolism assays. NK3Ra alleviated ER stress by modulating the PERK-ATF4-CHOP axis, improving steroidogenesis, redox homeostasis, and viability in HA-obese models. In PMOS mice, hepatic steatosis was reversed with associated downregulation of CHOP, decreased de novo lipogenic gene expression, and increased superoxide dismutase activity, while estrous cyclicity and steroid hormone metabolism were restored, accompanied by reduced ovarian ATF4, CHOP, and GRP78 expression by NK3Ra activity. Collectively, our findings suggest that NK3Ra alleviates lipotoxic-HA-induced ER stress via the modulation of the PERK-ATF4-CHOP pathway, thereby ameliorating metabolic and endocrine aberrations in PMOS.

articles.title: Artificial Urinary Sphincter in Women: A Systematic Review of Clinical Outcomes and Technological Evolutions.
articles.authors: Decombe O, Lenfant L, Faurie B et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Stress urinary incontinence (SUI) secondary to intrinsic sphincter deficiency (ISD) remains a challenging condition in women with persistent or recurrent incontinence despite conservative or surgical treatment. Artificial urinary sphincter (AUS) implantation represents an established salvage option. This review summarizes recent evidence on clinical outcomes, evolving surgical approaches, quality-of-life outcomes, and emerging device technologies in women undergoing AUS implantation.
RECENT FINDINGS: A PubMed search of studies published between 2019 and 2025, conducted according to PRISMA 2020 guidelines, identified 30 eligible studies. Reported continence rates ranged from 59% to 84%, while revision and explantation rates ranged from 6% to 69% and 2% to 34%, respectively. Contemporary patient populations increasingly comprise complex revision cases, particularly following synthetic sling removal. Minimally invasive and robotic approaches have emerged as promising alternatives, improving surgical precision and reducing perioperative morbidity, although comparative evidence remains limited and their impact on long term device survival is not established. Beyond continence, AUS implantation may improve quality of life. Early findings also suggest possible benefits in female sexual function, although further studies are needed to confirm these observations. Emerging electromechanical and pump-free systems may offer further improvements in device usability and complication profiles, but their clinical benefits remain to be established.
LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Over the last five years, the literature on female urinary sphincter devices has been dominated by retrospective studies, resulting in a generally low level of evidence. Most publications focus on AUS in women and consist of single-center retrospective case series. The European Association of Urology-led VENUS registry was established to address this limitation by collecting real-world data on AUS implantation and outcomes in women with stress urinary incontinence due to intrinsic sphincter deficiency. Patient recruitment has recently accelerated, with more than 13 centers currently enrolling and additional centers in the initiation process [1]. Emerging prospective studies on AUS and adjustable continence therapy (ACT) balloons may further strengthen the evidence base in the near future. AUS remains a valuable salvage therapy for severe female SUI related to ISD. Despite substantial…

articles.title: The risk of seizure-affected pregnancy in Australian women with epilepsy.
articles.journal: Epileptic disorders : international epilepsy journal with videotape
articles.authors: Vajda FJE, O'Brien TJ, Graham JE et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: We reported earlier that the occurrence of seizures in the pre-pregnancy year was the main determinant of the following pregnancy being seizure-affected. Additional risk factors were assessed in this study.
METHODS: The pregnancies involved first pregnancies of women with epilepsy. Two categories were compared. One category comprised 711 pregnancies in which seizures had occurred during the pre-pregnancy year and where seizures might reasonably be expected to continue to occur during the 9 months involved in any following pregnancy. The other category contained 634 pregnancies that were seizure-free in the pre-pregnancy year. Multivariate logistic regressions were fitted for 1345 subjects for seizure occurrence during pregnancy for co-variates listed to identify statistically seizure-related co-variates.
RESULTS: Seizure-affected pregnancy rates in the 1345 pregnancies studied remained stable over the consecutive 5-year intervals from 1999 onwards, viz. 50.5%, 53.9%, 50.3%, 52.8% and 48.2%. Seizure-affected pregnancy was more likely in WWE, who had: (1) Shorter durations of pre-pregnancy freedom from seizures. (2) Focal epilepsy. (3) Not taken ASMs while pregnant. (4) Not used pre-pregnancy folate supplementation. (5) Longer durations of epilepsy. (6) Earlier age onset of epilepsy. The hazard of a seizure-affected next pregnancy was over threefold higher when the pre-pregnancy year was seizure-affected than when it had been seizure-free.
SIGNIFICANCE: The finding that a year's pre-pregnancy seizure freedom was associated with a reduced risk of seizures in the next pregnancy was expected. The magnitude of the greater than threefold higher seizure risk in the next pregnancy if seizures had occurred in the pre-pregnancy year was not. It identifies a group of women with epilepsy whose medical management during pregnancy warrants particular care.

articles.title: Time-dependent diffusion MRI in determining mismatch repair status of endometrial cancer.
articles.authors: Zhang J, Shi D, Li JXJ et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Mismatch repair (MMR) proteins are important in determining therapeutic strategy in endometrial cancer (EC). We investigated the role of microstructural parameters derived from time-dependent diffusion magnetic resonance imaging (td-dMRI) in differentiating MMR status of EC.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This prospective single-center study enrolled patients with suspected EC who underwent preoperative td-dMRI. Tumors were classified as MMR-deficient (dMMR) and MMR-proficient (pMMR) by immunohistochemistry. The microstructural parameters, including intracellular volume fraction (  v i n   ), cell diameter ( d ), cellularity ( ρ ), extracellular diffusivity (  D e x   ), and water exchange rate constant (  k i n   ), were derived by fitting td-dMRI data with three methods (IMPULSED, JOINT, and EXCHANGE), together with the apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC). Differences in these microstructural parameters between dMMR and pMMR EC were compared. The diagnostic performances were evaluated by the areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC).
RESULTS: Eighty-two patients (17 dMMR, 61.8 ± 10.1 years and 65 pMMR, 58.6 ± 11.8 years) were recruited. dMMR EC exhibited higher  v i n   , ρ and lower  D e x   , ADC values than pMMR EC (p ≤ 0.003). IMPULSED and JOINT demonstrated higher AUCs than conventional ADC (p = 0.025 and 0.046, respectively). The combined selected microstructural parameters (  v in   and  D e x   ) derived from JOINT achieved an AUC of 0.903; JOINT demonstrated superior parametric stability and marginally better calibration than IMPULSED.
CONCLUSION: In this exploratory study, td-dMRI discriminated between dMMR and pMMR ECs, providing information on the intricate microscopic organizational structures in tumors. The microstructural parameters may serve as a promising method to improve the diagnostic efficacy of diffusion-weighted MRI in differentiating MMR status of EC.
KEY POINTS: Question There remains an unmet need for noninvasive, preoperative tools to assess DNA MMR status in EC. Findings td-dMRI showed significant differences in microstructural parameters between dMMR and pMMR tumors. Relevance statement td-dMRI shows potential as a noninvasive imaging approach for preoperative assessment of MMR status in EC and may support individualized treatment planning.

articles.title: Robotic-assisted versus laparoscopic hysterectomy in Stage I endometrial cancer: a real-world causal mediation analysis of operating time and length of hospital stay.
articles.authors: Jain V, Bhaumik J, Joshi R et al.
articles.abstract: This study estimated the impact of robotic-assisted surgery (RAS) versus laparoscopy (LPS) on operating time (OT), length of hospital stay (LOHS), and examined mediation through perioperative factors. A secondary analysis of individual patient data from a retrospective multicenter study was conducted. Women with histologically confirmed stage I endometrial cancer (EC) undergoing hysterectomy between January 2010 and December 2023 were included. After inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW), baseline covariates achieved standardized mean differences below 0.10. The IPTW-weighted effect estimate of LPS relative to RAS, interpreted as an adjusted association under the assumption of no unmeasured confounding was, 31.4 min for OT (95% CI: 17.8, 46.2) and 0.93 days for LOHS (95% CI: 0.59, 1.34). Blood loss accounted for 11.3 min (36%) of the OT difference and 0.46 days (49%) of the LOHS difference, while other mediators contributed minimally. Direct effects not explained by the measured mediators accounted for 18.6 min (59%) of the OT difference and 0.43 days (46%) of the LOHS difference. At an annual volume of 100 cases, the IPTW-weighted difference between RAS and LPS corresponded to an estimated difference of approximately 52.4 operating-room hours and 93 inpatient bed-days. RAS was associated with shorter OT and LOHS than LPS after adjustment for measured baseline differences. Reduced intraoperative blood loss explained a substantial proportion of these differences, although a considerable residual effect remained unexplained by measured perioperative mediators. Annual resource utilization difference should be interpreted as an illustrative planning estimate rather than a guaranteed operational saving.

articles.title: Secular trend in age at menarche in Egypt: a national study.
articles.authors: Hussein MA, Meatty EM, Eid EA et al.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Age at menarche (AAM) is an important marker of female pubertal development and population health. Secular declines in AAM have been reported worldwide, but national data from Egypt remain limited. To evaluate secular trends in AAM among Egyptian females and identify factors associated with menarcheal timing. A national cross-sectional study was conducted among Egyptian females aged ≥ 10 years from multiple governorates. Data on AAM, residence, parental education, maternal employment, season of birth, birth order, and retrospectively self-reported weight status at menarche were collected using a structured questionnaire.
