Participants were classified into six birth cohorts to assess secular trends. Associations between AAM and potential determinants were analyzed using appropriate statistical methods. A total of 3,643 Egyptian females aged ≥ 10 years were included. A significant secular decline in AAM was observed across successive birth cohorts, with an approximately one-year reduction between the oldest and youngest cohorts (p < 0.001). Earlier AAM was significantly associated with urban residence and higher parental education. Significant regional variation was observed across governorates. In contrast, season of birth and maternal employment were not significantly associated with AAM.
CONCLUSIONS: Egyptian females have experienced a continuing decline in AAM, consistent with global trends toward earlier pubertal onset. Urbanization and socioeconomic factors were associated with earlier menarche. Ongoing monitoring of pubertal timing is warranted.
WHAT IS KNOWN: • A secular decline in age at menarche has been reported globally. • Nutritional and socioeconomic transitions influence pubertal timing.
WHAT IS NEW: • This is among the first nationally distributed Egyptian studies evaluating secular trends in age at menarche. • Egyptian females demonstrated an approximately one-year decline in age at menarche across successive birth cohorts; earlier menarche was associated with urban residence and higher parental education in this Egyptian cohort.

articles.title: Nutraceutical and herbal interventions targeting inflammation and oxidative stress in PCOS-associated insulin resistance.
articles.authors: Kundu S, Jana R, Rahaman M et al.
articles.abstract: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is a complex endocrine and metabolic disorder affecting women of reproductive age. It is commonly associated with insulin resistance, hyperandrogenism, chronic low-grade inflammation, and oxidative stress. These factors contribute to metabolic dysfunction and increase the risk of developing type 2 diabetes and cardiovascular complications. This narrative review critically evaluates the available evidence regarding nutraceutical and herbal interventions targeting insulin resistance, inflammation, and oxidative stress associated with PCOS. A comprehensive literature search was conducted using PubMed, Google Scholar, EMBASE, Scopus, and CNKI databases, covering studies from database inception through 12 July to 21 November 2025 with keywords including PCOS, insulin resistance, hyperinsulinemia, oxidative stress, diabetes mellitus, nutritional supplements, and herbs. Relevant original research articles, randomized clinical trials, observational studies, systematic reviews, and meta-analyses were considered, and the available evidence was interpreted according to study design and evidence level. Evidence from preclinical studies and human clinical investigations indicates that selected nutraceutical and herbal interventions may influence metabolic, inflammatory, oxidative stress-related, hormonal, and reproductive parameters in PCOS. However, the magnitude and consistency of these effects vary substantially depending on the intervention, formulation, dose, treatment duration, participant characteristics, and the outcome assessed. Improvements in surrogate biochemical measures, such as HOMA-IR or inflammatory and oxidative stress biomarkers, should not be interpreted as direct evidence of improved fertility, reduced cardiovascular risk, or prevention of long-term diabetes. Therefore, the available evidence should be interpreted according to study design and evidence level, with greater weight given to findings from well-designed randomized clinical trials and systematic reviews or meta-analyses than to isolated preclinical or small clinical studies.

articles.title: T2-weighted MRI-based radiomics for preoperative prediction of homologous recombination deficiency status in high-grade serous ovarian carcinoma.
articles.authors: Zhou J, Jiang X, Deng M et al.
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to explore the feasibility of T2-weighted imaging (T2WI) - based radiomics in preoperative prediction of homologous recombination deficiency (HRD) status in patients with high-grade serous ovarian carcinoma (HGSOC), and to establish a non-invasive approach for guiding individualized treatment planning.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: A total of 133 patients with pathologically confirmed HGSOC who underwent MRI scan (T2WI, T1-contrast enhanced) were retrospectively enrolled in this study. All patients were stratified into HRD-positive and HRD-negative group. These 133 patients (41 in HRD-negative group and 92 in HRD-positive group) were randomly allocated to a training set (n = 93) and a validation set (n = 40) at a 7:3 ratio. Three different models were constructed and evaluated: clinical characteristics only (clinical model); T2WI-radiomics features only (radiomics model); and a combination of them all (combined model). The predictive performance was evaluated using the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis, and area under the curves (AUCs) were compared using the DeLong test. Calibration curves and decision curve analysis (DCA) were applied to validate the clinical-radiomic combined model.
RESULTS: In the training set, the combined model achieved the best performance (AUC = 0.889; all P > 0.05). The radiomics model achieved predictive performance comparable to the clinical model (AUC of 0.762 vs. 0.790; P = 0.676). In the validation set, the combined model performed significantly better than the clinical or radiomics model (AUCs of 0.853 vs. 0.805 vs. 0.706; all P > 0.05). DCA demonstrated that the combined model achieved superior net benefit across a wide range of threshold probabilities compared with the clinical and radiomics models alone.
CONCLUSIONS: Our research demonstrated that the combined model achieved the optimal predictive performance. It is feasible to apply radiomics to predict HRD status of HGSOC patients, which can further assist clinicians in formulating individualized treatment strategies.

articles.title: Comparison of Erect Sitting and Supine MRI Proctography in Women with Pelvic Organ Prolapse and Defecatory Symptoms.
articles.authors: Tadros M, Lemmon B, Bhide A et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION AND HYPOTHESIS: The optimal position for MRI proctography in women suffering from pelvic organ prolapse (POP) and defecatory symptoms remains uncertain. Typically, MRI proctography is performed in the supine position to assess for POP. Utilising an open-configuration MRI to image the pelvic floor in an erect sitting position may provide a more physiological assessment than a supine MRI for the evaluation of pelvic floor dysfunction. The aim was to compare the findings of MRI proctography performed in the conventional supine position compared with the erect sitting position in women with POP and defecatory symptoms.
METHODS: We performed a retrospective review of 333 women referred to a tertiary referral centre with POP and defecatory symptoms who underwent MRI proctography over a 4-year period. Of these, 144 women were imaged in the supine position and 189 women in the erect sitting position. Radiological findings of rectocele, rectal intussusception, enterocele, impaired defecation, and pelvic floor descent were compared.
RESULTS: Pelvic floor descent was identified in significantly more women in the erect sitting position (37.0%) than in the supine position (12.5%; p < 0.001). Similarly, rectal intussusception during straining was detected in significantly more women imaged in the erect sitting position (49.7%) than in the supine group (33.3%; p = 0.003). Enterocele was identified more frequently in the erect sitting position group (4.8% versus 0.7%; p = 0.048). Impaired defecation was identified more frequently in the supine group (56.9% versus 45.0%; p = 0.030). There were no significant differences in the prevalence of anterior rectocele between the two groups of women.
CONCLUSION: Erect sitting MRI proctography was associated with higher detection rates of pelvic floor descent, enterocele and rectal intussusception during straining. These findings suggest that patient positioning might influence the identification of certain pelvic floor abnormalities in the more physiological erect sitting position.

articles.title: Complications of Midurethral Sling Stratified by Surgical Route: A Litigation-Derived Case Series of 252 Women.
articles.authors: Azadi A, Marchand GJ, Ostergard DR
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION AND HYPOTHESIS: We hypothesized that, among women who develop complications after midurethral sling (MUS) placement, further revision is likely once a first revision has occurred. This cohort is selected on complications and litigation and cannot estimate population rates or support causal route comparison.
METHODS: A retrospective case series of 252 women who underwent MUS placement between September 2000 and February 2016 and subsequently pursued civil litigation, was abstracted through November 2019. Onset dates were unavailable for nonrevision endpoints; thus, complications are reported as crude proportions and as follow-up-adjusted frequencies per 100 person-years (exact Poisson 95% CI), not dated-event incidence rates. Time-to-event methods were applied only to revisions.
RESULTS: Of 252 women, 97 underwent retropubic placement, 124 transobturator, and 31 single-incision, the last reported descriptively; follow-up totaled 1,732 person-years. Recurrent stress urinary incontinence was the most frequently documented endpoint in every group (48% to 60%). Crude proportions and follow-up-adjusted frequencies by route are shown; all between-route confidence intervals overlapped and none was tested or adjusted. Among women reaching a first revision, a second was common (5-year cumulative incidence 51% retropubic, 47% transobturator); among those reaching a second, the exploratory 5-year cumulative incidence of a third revision reached 70% in the transobturator group. This estimate was derived from an analysis including 36 women at risk (those eligible for a third revision after undergoing a second revision) and 14 third-revision events across the retropubic and transobturator groups combined.
CONCLUSIONS: In this litigation-selected series, further surgery was common among women already revised. Because the cohort was selected on complications and litigation, baseline and surgeon characteristics were unavailable and no comparison was adjusted or tested, differences between routes cannot be attributed to route. These observations are hypothesis generating.

articles.title: Calcified foraminal metastasis from ovarian low-grade serous carcinoma mimicking a nerve sheath tumor.
articles.authors: Fawaz S, Ghaouche J, Bouthors C et al.
articles.abstract: Ovarian low-grade serous carcinoma (OLGSC) is an uncommon subtype of epithelial ovarian cancer, characterized by an indolent clinical course with potential for late local recurrence and metastatic disease. Musculoskeletal involvement is rare. We report a case of late OLGSC metastasis presenting as a slowly growing, thoracic foraminal mass in a 55-year-old woman, 33 years after initial cancer treatment. Rising CA-125 levels prompted 18F-FDG PET/CT, which revealed an FDG-avid mass in the left T9-T10 neural foramen (SUVmax 6.6). CT demonstrated foraminal widening and intralesional calcifications, while MRI showed a dumbbell-shaped mass extending into the epidural space and left costovertebral region, with heterogeneous signal intensity and mild diffuse heterogeneous enhancement. Retrospective review of a CT examination performed 12 years earlier revealed a smaller foraminal mass without visible calcifications. Given its location and morphology, the lesion initially suggested a nerve sheath tumor, while the presence of calcifications also raised the possibility of a chondroid lesion. Although nonspecific, calcifications are recognized in primary and metastatic OLGSC. The combination of increased FDG uptake and the patient's oncologic history, raised suspicion of metastatic disease. Image-guided biopsy confirmed metastatic OLGSC with psammoma bodies. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first reported case of OLGSC metastasis presenting as a slowly progressive, calcified paravertebral and foraminal mas mimicking a nerve sheath tumor. This case emphasizes the need for careful evaluation of atypical masses in patients with a history of cancer, even decades after initial treatment, and the importance of biopsy for diagnostic confirmation.

articles.title: Menopause, Weight Loss, and Pelvic Floor Changes: Clinical and Aesthetic Considerations.
articles.journal: Dermatologic surgery : official publication for American Society for Dermatologic Surgery [et al.]
articles.authors: Chirumamilla V, Tyler KH
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Menopause is associated with hormonal, structural, and functional changes affecting the vulvovaginal tissues, pelvic floor, and urinary tract. Weight loss may further alter soft-tissue volume and body composition, although effects on pelvic floor function remain incompletely understood.
OBJECTIVE: The aim of this study was to review menopause-associated vulvovaginal and pelvic floor changes and discuss implications for dermatologic evaluation, weight loss, symptom management, and procedural counseling.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: A narrative review of literature addressing menopause, pelvic floor dysfunction, weight loss, glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists, pelvic floor rehabilitation, and emerging vulvovaginal therapies was performed.
RESULTS: Menopause-associated tissue remodeling may contribute to genitourinary syndrome of menopause, urinary symptoms, sexual dysfunction, and pelvic floor disorders. Weight loss may improve obesity-associated urinary incontinence but can also reduce lean mass and external soft-tissue volume. Evidence regarding glucagon-like peptide-1 therapies and pelvic floor function remains limited. Pelvic floor physical therapy is an established treatment, whereas high-intensity focused electromagnetic therapy shows preliminary evidence of benefit.
CONCLUSION: Dermatologists should recognize functional symptoms, provide evidence-based counseling, and coordinate care with gynecology, urogynecology, urology, and pelvic floor physical therapy while approaching emerging procedural therapies cautiously.

articles.title: The "Elastotic Hemangioma" of the Vulva Is Nodular Vulvar Elastosis With Prominent Vascularization.
articles.authors: Fernandez-Flores A
articles.abstract: Acquired elastotic hemangioma is an uncommon benign cutaneous vascular proliferation first described in 2002 that typically presents as a solitary erythematous plaque arising on chronically sun-exposed skin. Histologically, it is characterized by a superficial, band-like, horizontally oriented capillary proliferation associated with marked solar elastosis. In contrast, vulvar elastosis develops in an anatomical site protected from ultraviolet radiation and has been linked to aging, hormonal changes, and inflammatory or reparative processes.In this article, we report the lesion of a 67-year-old woman with vulvar lichen sclerosus who presented with a palpable 1-cm nodule involving the left labium majus. Her medical history was notable for an undifferentiated ovarian carcinoma diagnosed 19 years earlier, treated with chemotherapy and currently in remission. Histopathological examination revealed superficial features of lichen sclerosus and, within the underlying dermis, a nodular accumulation of thick, irregular elastic fibers intermingled with numerous mature blood vessels lacking endothelial atypia.In conclusion, a prominent vascular component may represent a feature of nodular vulvar elastosis and should not necessarily be interpreted as evidence of a primary vascular neoplasm.

articles.title: High rates of obesity and excessive catch-up growth in children with perinatal HIV exposure in the United States.
articles.journal: Journal of acquired immune deficiency syndromes (1999)
articles.authors: Jacobson DL, Yu W, Geffner M et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Preterm birth (PTB) and small-for-gestational age (SGA) often occur in infants born to women with HIV and may influence growth among children perinatally HIV- exposed but uninfected (CHEU).
SETTING: U.S. cohort at 22 sites.
METHODS: CHEU were enrolled at birth into the SMARTT Dynamic cohort of the Pediatric HIV/AIDS Cohort Study network and followed through age 17 years. We calculated Z scores for singleton CHEU through age 7 years for weight (WAZ), length or height (LAZ/HAZ), and weight-for-length/body mass index (WFL/BMI)]; excessive catch-up growth was defined as WAZ increase >0.67 SD from birth to age 2 years. Birth weight-for-gestational age (GA) was categorized as small- (SGA), appropriate- (AGA), and large-for-GA (LGA). Piecewise linear regression models with slope changes were used to assess growth trajectories by SGA and PTB.
RESULTS: Among 2,765 CHEU born 2007-2022, 9.2% were SGA, 14.4% preterm, and 47% had excessive catch-up growth. Among term infants, those born SGA had the highest percent (65%) with excessive catch-up growth. Those born SGA had lower mean WAZ and WLZ/BMIZ than AGA through age 7 years. Infants with PTB had higher mean WAZ, LAZ/HAZ, and WLZ/BMIZ at birth than term infants, but were similar by age 7 years.
CONCLUSIONS: A high proportion of CHEU had excessive catch-up growth and obesity at age 5 years. While SGA infants had persistently lower Z-scores than AGA, obesity rates at age 5 years were comparable. These findings represent a paradigm shift from undernutrition to overnutrition, particularly in countries where obesity prevalence is high.

articles.title: Feasibility study of a S-shaped incision technique in endometrioma surgery: Cold dissection with no thermal injury.
articles.journal: Journal of obstetrics and gynaecology : the journal of the Institute of Obstetrics and Gynaecology
articles.authors: Mehdizadeh A, Chaichian S, Ajdary M et al.
articles.abstract: Preserving ovarian reserve while minimising recurrence remains a major challenge in endometrioma surgery. Conventional bipolar excision may cause thermal injury to the ovarian cortex and impair fertility potential. We conducted a pilot feasibility study of a technical modification of laparoscopic cystectomy using an S-shaped incision at the ovarian hilum with cold dissection to reduce thermal exposure and cortical damage. Twelve patients underwent cystectomy with this approach, and all procedures were completed without intraoperative complications. Postoperative evaluation included serum anti-Müllerian hormone (AMH), antral follicle count (AFC), pain score, CA-125, and sonographic assessment. Early postoperative findings were compatible with short-term technical feasibility and safety in this small initial series. The observed postoperative changes in ovarian reserve markers and symptoms provide preliminary data to inform future comparative studies with longer follow-up.

articles.title: Added Value of Preoperative Contrast Enhanced Mammography in Staging of Malignant Breast Lesions (PROCEM): A Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.authors: Gardfjell A, Rydén L, Niméus E et al.
articles.abstract: Background Contrast-enhanced mammography (CEM) is increasingly used in breast cancer diagnostics; however, randomized trials assessing the added value of CEM in preoperative staging of breast cancer beyond digital mammography, digital breast tomosynthesis, and US are lacking. Purpose To assess the added value of CEM for preoperative breast cancer staging in a randomized controlled trial. Materials and Methods This prospective randomized controlled trial (Added Value of Preoperative Contrast Enhanced Mammography in Staging of Malignant Breast Lesions) enrolled women diagnosed with early-stage breast cancer eligible for primary surgery at two breast centers in Sweden. Participants were randomized 1:1 to preoperative CEM or control from November 2020 through April 2024. The primary outcome was a 10% change in treatment due to preoperative CEM findings. Secondary outcomes included differences in reoperation and mastectomy rates between groups and accuracy of malignant extent estimation with CEM, mammography/tomosynthesis, and US using histopathologic extent as the reference, assessed with Bland-Altman statistics and concordance analysis. Subgroup analyses were performed according to menopausal status, breast density, histopathologic type of cancer, lesion size, and presence of microcalcifications at baseline imaging. Results In total, 415 participants (median age, 66 years; IQR, 56-73 years) completed the trial: 202 in the CEM group and 213 in the control group. Treatment was changed in 17 of 202 participants (8.4%; 95% CI: 5.3, 13.1) based on CEM findings. No evidence of differences was observed between the CEM and control groups with regard to mastectomy (17% [35 of 202] vs 18% [39 of 213]; P = .78) or reoperation (7.9% [16 of 202] vs 10% [22 of 213]; P = .39) rates. CEM showed the closest agreement with histopathologic malignant extent (bias, 3.5 mm), outperforming mammography and/or tomosynthesis (4.8 mm) and US (10.7 mm) overall and in nine of 10 predefined subgroups, except for ductal carcinoma in situ. Conclusion This trial did not meet its primary end point of a 10% treatment change; however, preoperative CEM improved malignant extent estimation. ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT04437602 © The Author(s) 2026. Published by the Radiological Society of North America under a CC BY 4.0 license. Supplemental material is available for this article. See also the editorial by Mesurolle and El Khoury in this issue.

articles.title: Interaction Between Previous Cesarean Delivery and Anterior Placental Location in Persistent Low-Positioned Placenta: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.journal: Journal of ultrasound in medicine : official journal of the American Institute of Ultrasound in Medicine
articles.authors: Wu M, Zhong X, Zheng C et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the interaction between previous Cesarean delivery and anterior placental location in persistent low-positioned placenta and the association between placental edge-to-internal-os distance and persistence among women with a low-lying placenta.
METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study included 1508 singleton pregnancies with a low-positioned placenta identified during routine mid-trimester fetal ultrasound between 2020 and 2024. Multivariable analysis was used to evaluate factors associated with persistence and the interaction between previous Cesarean delivery and anterior placental location. Among women with a low-lying placenta, the association between placental edge-to-internal-os distance and persistence was also assessed.
RESULTS: Previous Cesarean delivery and anterior placental location interacted significantly in relation to persistent low-positioned placenta (P for interaction = 0.003). The additive interaction risk difference was 20.0 percentage points (95% confidence interval [CI], 8.2-31.7). Placenta previa at the mid-trimester examination was associated with a higher risk of persistence than low-lying placenta (adjusted relative risk, 5.87; 95% CI, 4.95-6.96). Among women with a low-lying placenta, each 5-mm decrease in placental edge-to-internal-os distance was associated with a 63% higher risk of persistence (adjusted relative risk, 1.63; 95% CI, 1.45-1.83).
CONCLUSIONS: Previous Cesarean delivery and anterior placental location interacted significantly in relation to persistent low-positioned placenta, and women with both factors present may warrant closer attention during follow-up. Considering these factors together with the type of low-positioned placenta and placental edge-to-internal-os distance may help refine risk assessment and inform subsequent ultrasound follow-up and clinical management.

articles.title: Alcohol Consumption in Nigerian Pregnant Women and Maternal and Foetal Outcomes: A Systematic Review.
articles.authors: Ebeigbe PN, Musa J, Aziken ME
articles.abstract: The objectives of this systematic review were to provide a comprehensive overview of existing knowledge, assess the quality of the evidence, identify research gaps and propose directions for future research on the prevalence, predictors and maternal and foetal effects of alcohol consumption among pregnant Nigerian women. Eligibility Criteria: The Inclusion Criteria: Scientific research studies published in, or translated into the English language, in peer-reviewed local or international journals, presented at scientific conferences or published as technical reports from 1 June 2015 to 31 May 2025. These included observational studies such as cohort, case-control and cross-sectional studies. Exclusion Criteria: Editorials, commentaries and opinion pieces on the themes of study with no original research data; case reports and series with a sample size of <10, which may provide insufficient data for a comprehensive analysis; non-peer-reviewed articles and unpublished theses/dissertations, due to concerns about the verifiability of data and research quality; studies in which full texts were not accessible and studies not published in, or translated into English. Information Sources: Search engines and databases, including Google Scholar, PubMed, EBSCOhost, Medline, ScienceDirect, Directory of Open Access Journals and African Index Medicus (AIM), as well as the websites of the Federal Ministry of Health, Nigeria; the World Health Organization, Africa region and UNFPA, Nigeria. Risk of bias: The AXIS appraisal tool was used to assess the risk of bias/quality of cross-sectional studies, while the adapted Newcastle-Ottawa quality assessment scale was used for cohort studies included in this study. Synthesis of results: A narrative synthesis approach was used to summarise the eligible literature. We included information on the authors and date of publication, research design, description of the population and setting, research results, study characteristics, methodologies and outcomes, limitations of the research and the quality of the selected studies (risk of bias assessment), while noting patterns and discrepancies across studies. Included studies: 14 hospital-based studies; 13 cross-sectional and one cohort study. Synthesis of results. Prevalence of alcohol consumption: All 14 studies reviewed reported on the prevalence of alcohol consumption during pregnancy. The highest prevalence of 59.3% was reported in the South-South, while the lowest prevalence of 4.0%…

articles.title: Surgery for abnormal uterine bleeding at Sørlandet Hospital.
articles.journal: Tidsskrift for den Norske laegeforening : tidsskrift for praktisk medicin, ny raekke
articles.authors: Vistad I, Tveit TO, Berge GT
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIM: Abnormal uterine bleeding affects 15-20 % of women of reproductive age and is a common indication for surgery. The aim of this study was to describe the extent of surgical intervention and the choice of surgical procedure among premenopausal women with this condition and to identify factors associated with hysterectomy.
MATERIAL AND METHOD: Women aged ≤ 55 years who had contact with Sørlandet Hospital between 1. January 2011 and 31 December 2021 due to benign abnormal uterine bleeding (ICD-10 diagnosis codes N92.0-N92.6) were identified. Following data extraction from electronic patient records using a structured query language, the data were analysed using descriptive statistics.
RESULTS: Of 4947 women with abnormal uterine bleeding, 2278 (46 %) underwent surgery. Of these, 1830 (80 %) had one procedure, 415 (18 %) had two and 33 (1 %) had three. Thermal endometrial ablation was the most common initial procedure (902 of 2278, 40 %), while hysterectomy was performed on 649 women (28 %). Fibroids, pain and anaemia were associated with hysterectomy, but age was not.
INTERPRETATION: Over an 11-year period, almost half of the patients with benign abnormal uterine bleeding underwent surgery. More than a quarter of these had a hysterectomy. Our findings suggest that the overall symptom burden, in addition to the amount of menstrual blood loss, is associated with the likelihood of undergoing hysterectomy.

articles.title: Cultural and lived experiences of menopause among women from Global Majority backgrounds in Western countries: a qualitative systematic review.
articles.authors: Ashraf W, Cresswell C, Harrington J et al.
articles.abstract: Menopause is increasingly recognised as a significant stage of the female reproductive cycle; however, the experiences of women from Global Majority backgrounds (GMB) remain underrepresented within menopause research. To address this gap, this systematic literature review explored how women from Global Majority backgrounds living in Western countries perceive and experience menopause, and how cultural, social and structural factors shape these experiences. Multiple databases were searched in November 2025 for qualitative studies, or mixed-method studies with extractable qualitative findings. Eligible studies were appraised using the CASP qualitative checklist, and findings were synthesised using thematic synthesis. Fifteen studies conducted in US, Canada and Australia, involving women from East and Southeast Asian, South Asian, African American, Hispanic/Latina and Aboriginal backgrounds were included. Six interrelated themes were identified: menopause as a culturally constructed concept; as an embodied and identity-disrupting experience; the influence of social and gendered expectations; cultural and intersectional variation; coping strategies and healthcare navigation; and menopause as a potentially transformative life stage. Experiences were shaped by interactions among cultural beliefs, migration histories, family and community expectations, language barriers, socioeconomic circumstances and healthcare encounters. While some women described stigma, loss and disruption, others experienced greater freedom, resilience and personal transformation. These findings support the need for culturally responsive, intersectional menopause care that avoids cultural assumptions, attends to women's own understandings and treatment preferences, and strengthens clinicians' cultural awareness. Further research should include underrepresented groups and examine whether culturally adapted resources improve healthcare access, experiences and outcomes.

articles.title: Urinary Dysfunction in ALS Patients: Assessment With the Overactive Bladder Awareness Tool.
articles.authors: Libonati L, Cambieri C, Ceccanti M et al.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: To compare urinary symptom bother and overactive bladder screening positivity between patients with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) and controls using the Overactive Bladder Awareness Tool (OAB-V8).
METHODS: This retrospective study included 101 patients with definite ALS and 324 controls. OAB-V8 scores were compared using Welch's t-test and multiple linear regression adjusted for age and sex with HC3 robust standard errors. Screening positivity (OAB-V8 ≥ 8) was evaluated using Firth's logistic regression adjusted for age and sex.
RESULTS: Mean OAB-V8 scores were 14.0 ± 6.8 in ALS patients and 12.40 ± 5.10 in controls (unadjusted p = 0.026). The adjusted mean difference was 1.65 points (95% confidence interval [CI] 0.20-3.10; p = 0.026). Screening positivity was observed in 101/101 ALS patients (100%) and 272/324 controls (84.0%). The adjusted odds ratio was 41.03 (95% penalized profile-likelihood CI 5.75-5205.66; p < 0.001), indicating substantial uncertainty in its magnitude.
CONCLUSIONS: ALS patients reported modestly greater urinary symptom burden than controls after adjustment for age and sex. These findings support clinical attention to urinary symptoms in ALS but do not establish their underlying urodynamic mechanism.

articles.title: Perimenopause as a critical neuro-musculoskeletal window for healthy aging: integrating brain, bone and muscle health.
articles.journal: Climacteric : the journal of the International Menopause Society
articles.authors: Rey C, Carpintero P
articles.abstract: Perimenopause is increasingly recognized as a critical biological transition that extends beyond reproductive aging to influence multiple organ systems. Accelerated bone loss during the menopausal transition is supported by robust epidemiological, mechanistic and imaging evidence, whereas evidence for concurrent changes in muscle health and particularly neurocognitive function is more heterogeneous. Subjective cognitive complaints, including reduced concentration, forgetfulness and 'brain fog', are commonly reported, but objectively measured cognitive changes are generally modest and less consistent. Endocrine, inflammatory and mitochondrial pathways provide biological plausibility for interactions among bone, muscle and brain; however, direct evidence demonstrating an integrated relationship among these systems specifically during perimenopause remains limited. This narrative review critically synthesizes current evidence and proposes the bone-brain-muscle axis as an integrative conceptual framework. The model is presented as a biologically plausible clinical framework rather than a validated mechanistic pathway. Recognizing perimenopause as a potential neuro-musculoskeletal window may support earlier identification of multidimensional risk and individualized strategies to preserve physical function, cognitive health and healthy aging.

articles.title: Exploring menopause in undergraduate teaching: a mixed-methods case study in Dundee.
articles.authors: Fabri N, McElhinney Z, Kennedy C
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To effectively support women presenting with symptoms of menopause, it is crucial for doctors to be adequately prepared through their undergraduate education. This study explored the coverage of menopause in undergraduate teaching materials, and students' perceptions of their understanding of this topic.
STUDY DESIGN: A mixed-methods case study design was used to explore menopause teaching at the University of Dundee's (UoD) MBChB course. A two-stage content analysis identified menopause teaching within the 'Reproduction and Sexual Health' (RSH) teaching block. Data on students' knowledge of menopause and their views on the teaching they had received were gathered through a questionnaire and semi-structured interviews.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Quantitative and qualitative data included the content of teaching materials, perceptions of teaching, and learning about menopause.
RESULTS: Teaching about menopause was identified in five sessions of RSH block teaching. Teaching was predominantly lecture-based, and included discussion of the symptoms of menopause and possible treatments. All students reported a lack of confidence in both their knowledge of menopause and their ability to effectively consult a patient presenting with symptoms of menopause. Students expressed their wish for opportunities to reinforce and apply their learning.
CONCLUSIONS: Existing methods for teaching menopause may not be the most effective. Recommendations for improving student confidence include incorporating menopause teaching content into multiple teaching blocks and providing opportunities for students to apply their learning through case discussions or workshops.

articles.title: Long-term safety of Etrasimod in ulcerative colitis: a comprehensive review.
articles.authors: Colwill M, Honap S, Magro F et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Etrasimod is an oral sphingosine-1-phosphate receptor modulator approved for the treatment of moderate to severe ulcerative colitis. Its targeted mechanism, once-daily dosing and oral formulation make it an important addition to the therapeutic landscape. However, its safety profile and optimal clinical positioning require careful evaluation.
AREAS COVERED: This narrative review examines the pharmacology, efficacy and safety of etrasimod in ulcerative colitis, drawing on evidence from the OASIS, ELEVATE UC and ENLIGHT UC trial programmes, open-label extension studies, meta-analyses, pharmacovigilance reports and emerging real-world cohorts. The practicalities of prescribing and monitoring are also covered. A literature search was conducted in MEDLINE to identify appropriate studies.
EXPERT OPINION: Current evidence supports etrasimod as a generally well-tolerated treatment option, with low rates of serious adverse events, serious infections, opportunistic infections and malignancy which do not differ substantially from placebo. Key safety considerations include first-dose bradycardia, atrioventricular conduction abnormalities, macular oedema, hepatic enzyme elevations, and lymphopenia, all of which necessitate appropriate screening and monitoring. Etrasimod may be particularly useful in patients with moderately active disease and limited prior advanced therapy exposure, whilst its reassuring safety profile and low risk of serious infection make it an attractive candidate for use in advanced combination therapy.

articles.title: Patient-Reported Outcomes after Robotic Resection of Deep Endometriosis of the Bowel.
articles.journal: Diseases of the colon and rectum
articles.authors: Addison P, Stewart K, Ferrari D et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: While minimally invasive surgery is the current surgical standard of care for excision of deep endometriosis of the bowel, there is little literature evaluating patient-reported outcome measures following a multidisciplinary, robotic approach.
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to assess the functional outcomes of robotic surgery for patients undergoing resection of deep endometriosis involving the bowel.
DESIGN: Retrospective cohort review.
SETTINGS: A single academic tertiary institution.
PATIENTS: Patients with endometriosis of the bowel undergoing multidisciplinary resection between January 1, 2018, and October 1, 2023.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: A survey assessing functional outcomes on a Numeric Rating Scale preoperatively and at multiple points postoperatively.
RESULTS: Of 92 eligible patients, 41 completed a preoperative survey and at least one postoperative survey. Among these 41 patients, overall pain improved postoperatively from 5.3 ± 2.7 (Numeric Rating Scale) to a nadir of 1.6 ± 1.9 at 6 months and 2.3 ± 3.0 at 12 months (p < 0.001). Preoperative pain at ovulation (mean 4.2 Numeric Rating Scale ± 3.7), pre-period pain (4.9 ± 3.5), period pain (5.7 ± 3.6) and post-period pain (3.3 ± 3.3) all decreased to a mean of 1 at 12 months postoperatively (p < 0.001). The proportion of patients reporting pain impacting work decreased from 88% preoperatively to <40% postoperatively (p < 0.001). The proportion of patients happy with their bowel function increased from 39% preoperatively to 63.2% at 1 month, 80.0% at 6 months, and 69.2% at 12 months postoperatively (p = 0.014).
LIMITATIONS: Only 31.7% of patients responded to their 12-month survey, tertiary care center, low diversity in patient demographics, retrospective design.
CONCLUSION: In this cohort of patients undergoing multi-disciplinary robotic excision for advanced endometriosis involving the bowel, patients reported significantly improved pain and quality of life measures. See Video Abstract.

articles.title: Evaluation of Diagnostic Yield and Clinical Utility of Trio Whole-Genome Sequencing in Children With GDD/IDD in China.
articles.authors: Zhang J, Chen Z, Zhang Y et al.
articles.abstract: Accurate diagnosis and timely intervention are essential for improving outcomes in children with global developmental delay (GDD) or intellectual developmental disorder (IDD). Although genomic sequencing has improved diagnostic yield, studies integrating long-term clinical follow-up remain limited, hindering clinical translation. In this cohort study, 122 Chinese children with GDD/IDD were enrolled from a single center (2018-2023) and underwent Trio whole-genome sequencing (Trio-WGS). Trio-WGS achieved a 39.3% (48/122) diagnostic yield, identifying pathogenic/likely pathogenic variants in 48 cases, including 35 SNVs/Indels and 13 CNVs. De novo variants accounted for 75% (36/48) of findings, with autosomal dominant inheritance predominant. Enrichment analysis revealed that, beyond the generic neurodevelopmental signature, the GDD/IDD diagnostic gene set was specifically enriched for presynaptic function, GABAergic/chloride transport, and chromatin remodeling. A multidisciplinary team used results to optimize care: 3 children improved with targeted therapy, 30 had comorbidity management adjusted, 17 received diet modifications, and 7 families pursued preimplantation genetic testing. This study holds great significance for improving the genetic diagnosis rate of GDD/IDD and identifying new mutations, while also providing valuable information for the treatment of GDD/IDD and reproductive guidance.

articles.title: A High‑Throughput, Non-Derivatization Method for Determination of Glyphosate, Glufosinate, and Their Metabolites in Water and Sediments Using Pass-Through Cleanup and UHPLC-MS/MS.
articles.authors: Yang X, Lei Q, Suo W et al.
articles.abstract: Glyphosate (GLYP) and glufosinate (GLUF) are widely used herbicides that can persist in aquatic environments. Rapid, sensitive, and matrix-versatile analytical methods for the simultaneous monitoring of these herbicides, along with their major metabolites (aminomethylphosphonic acid: AMPA, and 3-(methyl-phosphinico)-propionic acid: MPPA), remain limited. Most existing liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) methods require derivatization or target only food matrices, with little attention to environmental water and sediment. In this study, we developed a high-throughput, non-derivatization ultra-high-performance LC (UHPLC)-MS/MS method incorporating solid-phase extraction using Oasis PRiME HLB cartridges to directly determine all four analytes in both water and sediment samples. The PRiME HLB cartridge effectively reduces interfering substances (such as salts, organic matter, and phospholipids) without conditioning or elution steps, thereby simplifying sample preparation and enabling high-throughput analysis. The method was validated across six distinct environmental matrices (pond, lake, river water, and corresponding sediments). Excellent linearity (R2 > 0.996), satisfactory recoveries (78.3%-104.7%), precision (RSD < 15%), and sensitivity (limits of detection [LODs]: 0.3-0.5 µg L- 1 for water and 2-3 µg kg- 1 for sediment) were achieved, with negligible matrix effects (<20%). Applied to 60 real environmental samples, the method detected GLYP and AMPA residues in sediments (up to 15.6 and 45.4 µg kg- 1, respectively), while GLUF and MPPA were below LODs. This simple, robust, and high-throughput workflow is well suited for routine monitoring of herbicide residues in aquatic systems.

articles.title: Factors associated with postmenopausal migraine persistence: A retrospective tertiary headache clinic-based study.
articles.authors: Hassan A, Hussein M, Elmazny A et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES/BACKGROUND: Migraine often improves after menopause; however, many women continue to have persistent symptoms. The factors associated with persistence and changes in migraine characteristics after menopause remain unclear. This study aimed to identify factors associated with migraine persistence after menopause and describe changes in migraine characteristics after menopause in a sample of Egyptian women compared to before menopause.
METHODS: Five Egyptian headache clinics participated in this retrospective cohort study (September 2025-March 2026). Women coded with migraine, born between 1971 and 1978, registered at any of these clinics, were invited to a face-to-face interview. Patients were classified as having persistent or resolved migraine after menopause. Premenopausal migraine severity and frequency, measured using a visual analog scale and monthly migraine days, were extracted from the database for comparison with postmenopausal values. Menopausal symptoms were assessed using the Menopause Rating Scale.
RESULTS: Two hundred nineteen women with persistent migraine after menopause, and another 96 women with resolved migraine, agreed to participate. Despite persistence, postmenopausal assessments showed significant reductions in median visual analog scale scores (7.0 [6.0-8.0] vs. 6.0 [4.0-7.0]), median monthly migraine days (8.0 [5.0-14.0] vs. 6.0 [3.0-10.0]), and the proportion of patients reporting aura (134/219 [61.2%] vs. 116/219 [53.0%]) (all p < 0.01) compared with the premenopausal period. Factors associated with postmenopausal migraine persistence are a first-degree relative with migraine (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] = 1.92, 95% CI = 1.07-3.43, p = 0.029), insomnia (aOR = 2.22, 95% CI = 1.16-4.24, p = 0.016), and surgical menopause (aOR = 4.00, 95% CI = 1.29-12.41, p = 0.017).
CONCLUSION: Migraine showed overall improvement in severity and frequency if it persisted after menopause. Persistence was associated with a first-degree relative with migraine and insomnia. Surgical menopause also showed an association, but this estimate was imprecise due to small numbers and should be interpreted cautiously. However, the generalizability of these results was limited because the study was clinic-based rather than population-based.

articles.title: Feasibility of Shallow Whole-Genome Sequencing-Based Circulating Tumour DNA Analysis in Canine Multicentric Lymphoma: A Pilot Study.
articles.authors: Kim GH, Jang JH, Kim SH et al.
articles.abstract: Lymphoma is a common canine malignancy with high morbidity and variable prognosis. Circulating tumour DNA (ctDNA) has emerged as a minimally invasive biomarker for tumour burden, treatment response and prognosis in human lymphoma. However, the feasibility of applying shallow whole-genome sequencing (sWGS)-based ctDNA analysis to canine lymphoma remains unclear. In this pilot study, plasma cell-free DNA (cfDNA) was quantitatively assessed and additional genomic features were evaluated using sWGS in dogs with multicentric lymphoma. cfDNA concentration was significantly higher in dogs with lymphoma (n = 13) compared with healthy controls (n = 24) (median 3.18 vs. 0.25 ng/mL; Mann-Whitney U test, p = 0.004). However, total cfDNA concentration was not significantly associated with time to progression (TTP) (p = 0.055). Tumour fraction (TF), a surrogate for ctDNA, showed preliminary association with clinical outcome, with a shorter median TTP in the high-TF group than in the low-TF group (77 vs. 302 days; p = 0.006). Genomic analysis further revealed copy number aberrations (CNAs); notably, gains on chromosome 13 containing the MYC locus were identified in three dogs, all of which belonged to the high-TF group. Dogs with lymphoma also displayed distinct cfDNA fragmentation profiles, characterized by an enrichment of shorter fragments within the analysed size range and a shift in the highest mean-profile peak compared with healthy controls. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of sWGS-based cfDNA analysis in canine lymphoma and suggest that TF may provide clinically relevant information beyond total cfDNA concentration. Validation in a substantially larger, independent cohort is warranted.

articles.title: The American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association classification of chronic hypertension in pregnancy has better clinical applicability and risk assessment than the traditional severe and mild hypertension approach - lessons from a population-based study.
articles.journal: The journal of maternal-fetal & neonatal medicine : the official journal of the European Association of Perinatal Medicine, the Federation of Asia and Oceania Perinatal Societies, the International Society of Perinatal Obstetricians
articles.authors: Rabinovich A, Dar Diab S, Shiloh A et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic hypertension (CHTN) increases the risk of superimposed preeclampsia, contributing to maternal and neonatal morbidity and mortality. Accurate hypertension classification is therefore essential for risk stratification, antenatal surveillance, prevention, and outcomes. The clinical impact of applying the American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association (ACC/AHA) classification, compared with the American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists (ACOG) criteria, in pregnancy remains uncertain.
OBJECTIVE: To determine the impact of ACC/AHA versus ACOG hypertension classifications on the prevalence of CHTN and pregnancy outcomes.
STUDY DESIGN: This population-based retrospective cohort study used a computerized maternity database from a tertiary hospital. All parturients with singleton gestations initiating prenatal care in the first trimester were included (n = 136,606). CHTN was categorized according to ACOG and ACC/AHA criteria. Maternal, fetal, and neonatal outcomes were assessed. Statistical analyses were performed using R-Studio, with ANOVA and Poisson regression models evaluating associations between CHTN severity and outcomes.
RESULTS: The prevalence of CHTN was 2.9% (4,127/137,606) by ACOG criteria and 3.9% (5,424/137,606) by ACC/AHA criteria (p < 0.001). Under ACOG classification, both mild and severe range CHTN were independently associated with preeclampsia or eclampsia (RR 4.15, 95% CI 3.69-4.65; and RR 3.19, 95% CI 2.82-3.59, respectively). Using ACC/AHA criteria, elevated blood pressure (EBP), stage 1 CHTN (S1CHTN), and stage 2 CHTN (S2CHTN) were each independently associated with preeclampsia or eclampsia (EBP: RR 2.34, 95% CI 2.04-2.65; S1CHTN: RR 4.00, 95% CI 3.56-4.50; S2CHTN: RR 3.32, 95% CI 2.88-3.80). Mild CHTN, S1CHTN, and S2CHTN were independently associated with small-for-gestational-age neonates, while both ACOG-defined CHTN and ACC/AHA-defined EBP, S1CHTN, and S2CHTN were associated with preterm birth.
CONCLUSION: Application of the ACC/AHA classification identifies a larger proportion of pregnant individuals as having CHTN. Notably, even those with elevated blood pressure had a two-fold increased risk of preeclampsia compared with the general obstetric population. These findings support the clinical relevance of the ACC/AHA classification in pregnancy and suggest that its implementation may improve identification of patients who may benefit from targeted preeclampsia prevention strategies.

articles.title: Artificial intelligence assisted genomic profiling of ovarian cancer liver metastases.
articles.authors: Sun L, Li Z, Chen S
articles.abstract: Liver involvement in ovarian cancer is often treated as a single clinical entity, although liver-surface implants and parenchymal deposits occupy different anatomical settings and may not share the same molecular history. Primary-tumor profiling is informative, but can miss lesion-specific evolution, treatment-associated cell states, and microenvironmental structure. This Mini Review examines how germline susceptibility, somatic change, spatial biology, and artificial intelligence might be combined in high-grade serous ovarian cancer. The central task is not simply outcome prediction. It is to distinguish constitutional from tumor-acquired variation, retain lesion identity and treatment timing, and relate molecular programs to defined spatial compartments. Current data support marked clonal and microenvironmental heterogeneity in ovarian cancer, but direct molecular evidence from hepatic lesions remains sparse. AI-based integration is therefore best viewed as a way to formulate and test reproducible hypotheses, rather than as a validated route to select liver-directed therapy. Paired sampling, orthogonal assays, patient-level validation, and decision-specific clinical endpoints will be needed before these models can influence management.

articles.title: Preimplantation Genetic Testing: Patient and Provider Preferences, Ethical Considerations, and Obstetrical and Neonatal Harms Analyses.
articles.authors: Ontario Health, Ontario Health
articles.abstract: Preimplantation genetic testing (PGT) refers to a group of genetic tests that analyze the DNA of embryos for chromosomal or genetic anomalies prior to the transfer to the uterus during in vitro fertilization (IVF). Ontario Health conducted a series of health technology assessments (HTA) of PGT, including assessment of PGT-A, PGT-M, and PGT-SR. In this report, we summarize the findings common to all 3 HTAS, including a rapid review of the qualitative literature, direct patient engagement, and a review of published literature examining ethical considerations relating to PGT. We also undertook a rapid review of the obstetrical and neonatal harms of PGT using trophectoderm biopsy. Reviews of the clinical and economic impact of PGT-A, the clinical impact of PGT-M, and the clinical impact of PGT-SR have been published separately.

articles.title: Preimplantation Genetic Testing for Structural Rearrangements: A Health Technology Assessment.
articles.authors: Ontario Health, Ontario Health
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Preimplantation testing for structural rearrangements (PGT-SR) is used to screen embryos for chromosomal imbalances that may result from parental structural rearrangements. We conducted a health technology assessment of PGT-SR for carriers of structural rearrangements or people who may have a child with a genetic condition affected by structural rearrangements, which included an evaluation of effectiveness. A report describing a rapid review of the qualitative literature, direct patient engagement, a review of published literature examining ethical considerations relating to PGT, and a rapid review of the obstetrical and neonatal harms of PGT using trophectoderm biopsy has been published separately.
METHODS: We performed a systematic literature search of the clinical evidence. We assessed the risk of bias of each included study using the Risk of Bias Assessment Tool for Nonrandomized Studies version 2 (RoBANS 2) and the quality of the body of evidence according to Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation (GRADE) Working Group criteria.
RESULTS: We included 4 studies in the clinical evidence review. Compared with in vitro fertilization (IVF) without PGT-SR, PGT-SR may result in similar live birth rates (first transfer and cumulative) (GRADE: Very low), pregnancy rate (clinical and ongoing) (GRADE: Very low), and spontaneous pregnancy loss (GRADE: Very low). Compared with natural conception or expectant clinical management, PGT-SR may result in similar live birth rates (first transfer and cumulative) and time to pregnancy, reduced spontaneous pregnancy loss (GRADE: Very low), and increased multiple gestation pregnancy (GRADE: Very low).
CONCLUSIONS: PGT-SR may result in similar outcomes compared with IVF without PGT-SR, may reduce spontaneous pregnancy loss compared with natural conception, and may increase multiple gestation compared with natural conception, although the evidence is very uncertain.

articles.title: Preimplantation Genetic Testing for Aneuploidy: A Health Technology Assessment.
articles.authors: Ontario Health, Ontario Health
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In vitro fertilization (IVF) is a type of assisted reproductive technology that can help couples or individuals conceive a child. Embryos with extra or missing chromosomes, known as aneuploidy, can result in a failure to implant, early spontaneous pregnancy loss, or lead to a child born with a chromosomal abnormality. Preimplantation genetic testing for aneuploidy (PGT-A) is a genetic screening test used to identify embryos with aneuploidy and select or prioritize embryos with the correct number of chromosomes for transfer. We conducted a health technology assessment of PGT-A for people undergoing IVF, which included an evaluation of the effectiveness and budget impact of publicly funding PGT-A. A report describing a rapid review of the qualitative literature, direct patient engagement, a review of published literature examining ethical considerations relating to PGT, and a rapid review of the obstetrical and neonatal harms of PGT using trophectoderm biopsy has been published separately.
METHODS: We performed a systematic literature search of the clinical evidence. We assessed the risk of bias of each included study using the Cochrane Risk of Bias tool and the quality of the body of evidence according to the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation (GRADE) Working Group criteria. We performed a systematic economic literature search, but we did not conduct a cost-utility analysis because of the uncertainty in the benefit of PGT-A. We also analyzed the budget impact of publicly funding PGT-A for individuals undergoing IVF in Ontario.
RESULTS: We included 6 RCTs in the clinical evidence review. We found PGT-A may not improve the cumulative live birth rate (GRADE: Very low) and may result in little to no difference in live birth rate after the first planned embryo transfer when evaluated per person undergoing PGT-A (GRADE: Low). PGT-A may not improve, and may decrease, cumulative pregnancy rates (GRADE: Low). After the first planned embryo transfer, PGT-A may not improve ongoing pregnancy (GRADE: Moderate) and may result in little to no difference in clinical pregnancy rate (GRADE: Very low) when evaluated per person receiving PGT-A. PGT-A may reduce the cumulative frequency of clinical pregnancy loss (GRADE: Low), but the evidence is very uncertain about the effect after the first planned embryo transfer when evaluated per person (GRADE: Very low). The annual budget impact of publicly funding PGT-A in Ontario over the…

articles.title: Impact of Hormonal Contraceptive Exposure on Pancreatic β-Cell Adaptation and Glucose Homeostasis: A Systematic Review.
articles.authors: Niyomugabo AP, Onaadepo O, Ntakirutimana L et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hormonal contraceptives (HCs) modulate endocrine and metabolic function. Some formulations have been associated with reduced insulin sensitivity, increasing the functional demand on pancreatic β-cells. This systematic review synthesised evidence on pancreatic β-cell adaptation to HC exposure.
METHODS: In accordance with PRISMA 2020, PubMed, Scopus and Wiley Online Library were searched for records published from January 2000 to December 2025, combining terms for β-cell function and adaptation with terms for hormonal contraceptives and for glucose homeostasis and insulin resistance. Eligible studies were original investigations in humans and rodents examining β-cell structural, functional or signalling adaptation to HC exposure, with a comparison group or pre-exposure baseline. Risk of bias was assessed by design using RoB 2, NIH and Newcastle-Ottawa criteria, SYRCLE, and adapted in vitro indicators. Findings were synthesised thematically.
RESULTS: Of 502 records identified, seven studies met the criteria: four human, two rodent in vivo and one isolated islet study. In women, ethinylestradiol with norgestimate improved insulin sensitivity in lean participants but reduced it in those with obesity; a drospirenone-containing pill raised HOMA-IR; an oral levonorgestrel preparation reduced insulin sensitivity more than an etonogestrel vaginal ring, with β-cell function unaltered by either; and androgenic formulations amplified postprandial glucose and insulin responses despite unchanged fasting values. In rodents, drospirenone-containing exposure produced hyperinsulinemia with preserved glucose tolerance, attributable to enhanced secretory activity and reduced insulin clearance; levonorgestrel impaired glucose tolerance and raised HOMA-IR, HOMA-β and circulating corticosterone. In isolated rat islets, gestodene metabolites increased insulin and glucokinase expression and glucose-stimulated insulin secretion via oestrogen receptor-dependent pathways.
CONCLUSION: Effects of HC on glucose metabolism and β-cell function appear to depend on progestin composition, route of administration and pre-existing metabolic status. Longitudinal human studies using direct measures of secretory capacity are needed to establish whether compensatory capacity is sustained under continued exposure.

articles.title: Recurrent CNVs in constitutional CMA: a ClinGen-anchored single-center postnatal and prenatal experience.
articles.authors: Satkın NB, Atlı E, Yalcintepe S et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Recurrent copy-number variants (CNVs) mediated by low-copy repeats or segmental duplications constitute an important subset of constitutional chromosomal microarray analysis (CMA) findings. Although ACMG/ClinGen standards have improved CNV classification, the burden of recurrent CNVs is not routinely quantified as a canonical, interval-matched, direction-specific category in clinical CMA output. We applied a strict ClinGen-anchored framework to quantify recurrent genomic disorder intervals in a consecutive single-center CMA series.
METHODS: Constitutional array-CGH and SNP-array records from a single center (2014-2026) were retrospectively reviewed, including 1,661 postnatal probands and 401 prenatal samples, with aneuploidies excluded. Recurrent regions were defined using the ClinGen Dosage Sensitivity Map and restricted to canonical intervals presumed to be mediated by non-allelic homologous recombination. Assignment required breakpoint concordance with the flanking low-copy repeat blocks and canonical interval size; terminal, unbalanced, and atypical imbalances were excluded. All records were re-curated against a single ClinGen release, with earlier GRCh37 coordinates converted to GRCh38.
RESULTS: Pathogenic or likely pathogenic findings were identified in 278/1,661 postnatal probands (16.74%) and 28/401 prenatal samples (6.98%). Recurrent CNVs were detected in 92/1,661 postnatal (5.54%, 95% CI 4.54-6.74) and 17/401 prenatal cases (4.24%, 95% CI 2.66-6.68). Pathogenic/likely pathogenic CNVs were found in 66/92 postnatal (71.74%) and 7/17 prenatal carriers (41.18%); the remaining findings were of uncertain significance or benign. Pathogenic recurrent CNVs thus accounted for 66/278 (23.74%) of postnatal and 7/28 (25.00%) of prenatal non-aneuploid pathogenic findings. Proximal 22q11.21 and 16p11.2 were most frequent. Deletions predominated postnatally (64/93, 68.82%); duplications comprised 11/17 (64.71%) of prenatal recurrent CNVs. Postnatal pathogenic recurrent-CNV yield was 58/1,589 (3.65%) in phenotype-driven testing (no suspected recurrent-CNV syndrome) and 6/19 (31.58%) with syndrome-specific suspicion; neurodevelopmental referrals contributed most cases.
CONCLUSION: ClinGen-defined recurrent CNVs were a substantial component of constitutional CMA findings. However, only about three-quarters of postnatal and fewer than half of prenatal carriers harbored pathogenic/likely pathogenic CNVs, indicating that a recurrent-region label alone is…

articles.title: Retraction: Study on the Effect of Berberine, Myoinositol, and Metformin in Women with Polycystic Ovary Syndrome: A Prospective Randomised Study.
articles.authors: Mishra N, Verma R, Jadaun P
articles.abstract: [This retracts the article DOI: 10.7759/cureus.21781.].

articles.title: Micro- and nanoplastic exposure: male reproductive toxicity, underlying mechanisms, and research prospects.
articles.authors: Wang M, Zheng J, Shen C et al.
articles.abstract: Diagnosis and treatment of male infertility present persistent clinical challenges, with etiologies spanning genetic anomalies, endocrine disturbances, genital tract infections, varicocele, lifestyle factors, and environmental exposures. Among these, exposure to environmental contaminants is increasingly recognized as a critical contributor to male reproductive impairment and declining sperm quality. Micro- and nanoplastics (MNPs), as ubiquitous emerging environmental pollutants, can enter the human body via three primary routes: gastrointestinal ingestion, respiratory inhalation, and dermal contact. Upon internalization, MNPs trigger male reproductive toxicity through diverse molecular pathways, including the induction of oxidative stress, DNA damage, disruption of sex hormone secretion, energy metabolism dysfunction, gut microbiota dysbiosis, ferroptosis, and aberrant autophagy. Cumulative evidence suggests that these mechanisms may act in concert to compromise sperm quality and male fertility; furthermore, such exposure has been associated with an elevated risk of developmental abnormalities in offspring in certain experimental models. In this review, we systematically elucidate the mechanisms linking MNP exposure to the pathogenesis and progression of male infertility. We also aim to offer novel insights for the clinical diagnosis and management of male infertility, provide theoretical references for preconception care and reproductive health, and establish a scientific foundation for advancing targeted prevention and control strategies against MNP pollution.

articles.title: Reproductive Autonomy Under Pressure: A Qualitative Exploration of Reproductive Coercion in Intimate Relationships in Canada.
articles.authors: Rousseau C, Lévesque S, Chevet J et al.
articles.abstract: Reproductive coercion refers to behaviors that interfere with another person's reproductive trajectory, whether by sabotaging contraceptive use, exerting pressure to become pregnant, or coercion to continue or terminate a pregnancy. Despite its profound impact, the repercussions of reproductive coercion on reproductive autonomy remain poorly documented. To address this gap, we conducted semi-structured interviews with women and non-binary people, which were transcribed and analyzed using a reflexive thematic approach. This article focused on 30 participants, aged 18 and over, who experienced reproductive coercion from a male intimate partner. Three overarching themes emerged from the analysis. These themes illustrated the spiral, in which control over one's reproductive health gradually erodes and becomes threatened; followed by the chain reaction, leading to an unplanned pregnancy; the irreversibility, whereby some participants experience their bodies as being placed at the service of others. A conceptual model was then developed to illustrate the progressive narrowing of reproductive autonomy. The findings further highlight the importance for health and social service providers of considering reproductive coercion within its broader structural context, including the cultural and social influences that shape it.

articles.title: Preimplantation Genetic Testing for Monogenic Disorders: A Health Technology Assessment.
articles.authors: Ontario Health, Ontario Health
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Monogenic (or single gene) disorders are caused by 1 or more pathogenic variants in a single gene. Monogenic disorders are inherited and can result in substantial morbidity, disability, and mortality. Preimplantation genetic testing for monogenic disorders (PGT-M) can be used to screen embryos that are created via in vitro fertilization (IVF) for pathogenic variants of interest. We conducted a health technology assessment of IVF with PGT-M among people at risk of transmitting single gene disorders with an evaluation of clinical effectiveness. A report describing a rapid review of the qualitative literature, direct patient engagement, a review of published literature examining ethical considerations relating to PGT, and a rapid review of the obstetrical and neonatal harms of PGT using trophectoderm biopsy has been published separately.
METHODS: We performed a systematic literature search of the clinical evidence. We conducted an overview of reviews to describe the body of systematic review evidence. We assessed the quality of each included systematic review using AMSTAR 2 (A Measurement Tool to Assess Systematic Reviews 2).
RESULTS: We included 4 systematic reviews in the clinical evidence review: 2 were of low quality and 2 were of critically low quality. We did not identify any data evaluating PGT-M with relevant comparators, such as conception (natural or via IVF) with prenatal diagnostic testing. The evidence is very uncertain about the effect of PGT-M on live births, clinical pregnancy, ongoing pregnancy, and pregnancy loss. The reported frequency of false-negative test results appears low, but the evidence is very uncertain. The impact on parental psychological outcomes is unknown. There was no evidence identified on number of IVF cycles to achieve an unaffected embryo or live birth, or parental quality of life.
CONCLUSIONS: Owing to the current body of noncomparative evidence, the clinical effectiveness of PGT-M is inconclusive.

articles.title: Genetic Landscape and Carrier Screening of Deafness-Associated Genes in a Prenatal Cohort from Fujian, China.
articles.authors: Tang J, Zeng Y, Lin Q et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: This study aimed to investigate the carrier frequencies of pathogenic variants in the GJB2, SLC26A4, GJB3, and MT-RNR1 genes among a Chinese pregnant population and their male partners in southern China.
METHODS: In this retrospective cohort, 1402 pregnant women underwent carrier screening for these four deafness-related genes using targeted next-generation sequencing, and those not willing to participate the study were excluded. Spouses received follow-up testing and counseling were also included. Prenatal diagnosis and postnatal genetic testing with hearing screening were performed to assess newborn outcomes.
RESULTS: Among the 1192 pregnant women included in the final analysis, 611 were identified as carriers of pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants in GJB2, SLC26A4, GJB3, or MT-RNR1. GJB2 showed the highest carrier frequency (23.6%), with c.109G>A and c.235delC being the most frequently detected variants. Additionally, 349 spouses underwent the testing, with similar predominance of GJB2. Cascade screening identified 41 at-risk couples, including three high-risk couples undergoing prenatal diagnosis. Among 39 newborns, most were heterozygous carriers of deafness-associated variants; three infants homozygous for GJB2 c.109G>A variant exhibited mild hearing loss but maintained normal communication ability. These findings support the utility of carrier screening and genetic counseling in assessing hereditary hearing loss risk.
CONCLUSIONS: This study demonstrated a substantial carrier frequency of deafness-associated variants among pregnant women and their partners in southern China. Sequential partner screening following identification of maternal carriers enabled the detection of couples at reproductive risk, facilitating genetic counseling and prenatal diagnosis for high-risk pregnancies.

articles.title: Residual Invasive Disease After Neoadjuvant Therapy in Triple-Negative Breast Cancer: Risk Stratification and Postoperative Radiotherapy-Pembrolizumab Integration.
articles.authors: Jia X, Eerdemutu, Ren Y et al.
articles.abstract: Residual invasive disease (RD) after neoadjuvant systemic therapy identifies patients with triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) at increased but heterogeneous recurrence risk. Continued perioperative pembrolizumab may overlap with postoperative radiotherapy (RT), raising unresolved questions about treatment timing and long-term net clinical benefit. This narrative review examines the pathologic definition and distribution of RD, prognostic stratification, mechanistic evidence, and clinical studies of postoperative RT-pembrolizumab integration. Breast-only, nodal-only, and combined breast and nodal RD should be distinguished alongside residual burden. Residual cancer burden, nodal status, tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes, and circulating tumor DNA may inform prognosis or research stratification, but none is validated to predict benefit from a specific RT-pembrolizumab schedule. Longitudinal molecular monitoring and cell-free DNA fragmentomics remain investigational for postoperative treatment selection. DNA repair, hypoxia, metabolic adaptation, tumor-cell plasticity, and immune suppression provide plausible mechanisms of resistance. However, features measured in surgically removed RD cannot be assumed to persist in occult postoperative disease, and much of the supporting evidence is preclinical or derived from other treatment settings. RT may stimulate antitumor immunity while also injuring immune cells. Small nonrandomized postoperative studies support short-term feasibility of concurrent treatment, but do not establish comparative efficacy or long-term safety. Severe adverse events and treatment interruptions have occurred, and late cardiopulmonary injury, fibrosis, and reconstruction outcomes remain insufficiently characterized. Management should preserve timely, guideline-concordant RT and base pembrolizumab continuation or interruption on clinical recovery and toxicity. Prospective comparisons with clearly defined schedules, prespecified RD subgroups, biomarker analyses, and adequate follow-up are needed to establish long-term net clinical benefit.

articles.title: Barriers and facilitators to deimplementing activity restriction in pregnancy: A qualitative study of prenatal care clinicians.
articles.authors: Keegan E, Levine LD, Mumford S et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Activity restriction and bedrest are frequently prescribed in pregnancy with the goal of preventing preterm birth, despite evidence that these practices are ineffective and harmful. While these practices persist, the American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists (ACOG) and the Society for Maternal-Fetal Medicine (SMFM) guidelines recommend against the routine use of activity restriction. Understanding clinicians' perspectives related to guideline-informed activity recommendations is essential to inform deimplementation strategies. This study aims to identify barriers and facilitators of deimplementation of activity restriction in pregnancy from the perspective of prenatal care clinicians, using the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research 2.0 (CFIR) in a qualitative approach.
METHODS: We conducted a qualitative study using semi-structured individual interviews with prenatal care clinicians (n = 14) at sites within or affiliated with a large urban academic medical center between November 2024 and September 2025. Participants included obstetrician-gynecologists, a maternal-fetal medicine physician, a family medicine physician, nurses, a certified nurse midwife, and office staff from both academic and community practice settings. Interviews were coded and analyzed using NVivo software. Emergent themes were mapped to CFIR domains and constructs.
RESULTS: Clinicians universally endorsed the benefits of physical activity in pregnancy but demonstrated significant knowledge gaps regarding current evidence and professional society guidelines. No clinicians recognized the inverse relationship between physical activity and preterm birth. Many followed outdated guidance, citing contraindications to exercise that have been removed from current ACOG recommendations. Key barriers to deimplementation included a perceived lack of evidence, patient anxiety, social media misinformation, cultural expectations around rest during pregnancy, and fear of rare adverse outcomes. Trust in ACOG and SMFM as credible sources and system-level infrastructure such as consensus meetings and standardized recommendations were described as facilitating decision support.
CONCLUSIONS: In this exploratory, single-institution study, deimplementation of activity restriction in pregnancy was less constrained by clinician opposition to physical activity and more by knowledge gaps, patient expectations, and fear of rare adverse outcomes. Strategies that leverage…

articles.title: Prevalence of short birth interval and associated factors among women, who gave birth in the past three years in Shebedino woreda, sidama region, Ethiopia, 2023.
articles.authors: Ali YY, Biratu AK, Defar S et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Short birth intervals significantly increase the risk of adverse maternal and neonatal outcomes like preterm birth, low birth weight, and maternal anemia. While optimizing birth spacing is critical for reproductive health interventions, localized and up-to-date epidemiological data from Shebedino Woreda remains scarce.
OBJECTIVE: To assess the prevalence of short birth intervals and associated factors among women who gave birth within the past three years in Shebedino Woreda, Sidama Region, Ethiopia.
METHODS: A community-based cross-sectional study was conducted from July 30 to August 30, 2023. A sample of 620 multiparous women was selected using multistage sampling. Data were collected via structured interviewer-administered questionnaires using the Open Data Kit and analyzed with SPSS version 27. Bivariate and multivariable logistic regression models were used to identify associated factors. Multicollinearity and model fitness were verified using variance inflation factors and the Hosmer-Lemeshow test.
RESULTS: Out of 620 eligible women, 617 participated (99.5% response rate). The prevalence of short birth intervals was 37.1% [95% CI: 33.3, 41.0]. In the multivariable analysis, the odds of practicing short birth interval were significantly higher among Muslim women (AOR = 2.31; 95% CI: 1.03, 5.18), unable to read and write (AOR = 4.00; 95% CI: 1.01, 15.85), who delivered the index child at home (AOR = 2.05; 95% CI: 1.23, 3.41), No antenatal care (ANC) visit during the pregnancy of the index child (AOR = 2.45; 95% CI: 1.25, 4.80), and who did not use modern contraceptives prior to the index pregnancy (AOR = 4.20; 95% CI: 1.71, 10.30).
CONCLUSION: this study demonstrates a high prevalence of short birth intervals (37.1%) among multiparous women in Shebedino Woreda, determined by low maternal literacy, home deliveries, a lack of ANC attendance during pregnancy, and modern contraceptives. Therefore, we strongly recommend that the Sidama Regional Health Bureau deploy a multi-sectorial intervention that integrates culturally tailored family planning counseling within routine ANC and postpartum services, expands structural access to institutional delivery care, prioritizes community-based literacy programs for women, and actively engages Muslim religious leaders to advocate for the health benefits of maternal birth spacing.

articles.title: A Rare Constellation of Omphalocele, Myelomeningocele, and Encephalocele in a Neonate Born to a Mother With Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: A Case Report.
articles.authors: Amin JHJ, Shakeel N, Mohammed ASK et al.
articles.abstract: Pre-gestational diabetes with reported poor glycemic control may be associated with rare and severe multiple congenital anomalies, such as omphalocele and multiple concurrent neural tube defects (NTDs). Early antenatal screening, strict maternal glycemic control, and multidisciplinary neonatal management are crucial to improving outcomes.

articles.title: Integrative follicular fluid biomarkers for oocyte competence and IVF outcomes: from molecular networks to multianalyte panels.
articles.authors: Chen CY, Lu YT, Chang PH et al.
articles.abstract: Accurate assessment of oocyte developmental competence remains a major challenge in assisted reproductive technology because conventional morphological grading and ovarian-reserve markers provide limited information about the molecular state of individual follicles.
