Follicular fluid offers a minimally invasive window into this microenvironment, integrating systemic endocrine inputs with bidirectional oocyte-somatic cell communication, steroidogenesis, metabolic coupling, extracellular-matrix remodeling, periovulatory inflammation, redox homeostasis, mitochondrial function, and angiogenesis. This narrative review synthesizes mechanistic and clinical evidence concerning follicular-fluid biomarkers associated with oocyte maturity, fertilization, embryo development, blastocyst formation, implantation, and live birth. Particular attention is given to granulosa cell-associated signaling networks involving epidermal growth factor-like ligands, pentraxin 3, transforming growth factor-β and bone morphogenetic protein family members, activins and follistatin, glial cell line-derived neurotrophic factor, cytokines, steroid hormones, metabolic intermediates, lipids, oxidative-damage markers, and extracellular-matrix components. Available evidence indicates that individual analytes generally lack sufficient reproducibility, discrimination, and calibration for routine clinical prediction because their concentrations are influenced by patient phenotype, ovarian-stimulation regimen, follicular stage, sampling strategy, preanalytical handling, analytical platform, and outcome definition. Follicular heterogeneity and the statistical non-independence of multiple oocytes obtained from the same patient further complicate biomarker evaluation. We therefore propose a transition from single-analyte measurements toward mechanism-informed, outcome-specific multianalyte panels integrating follicular-fluid measurements with cumulus- or granulosa-cell transcriptomic, proteomic, metabolomic, and lipidomic features. Phenotype-specific models, particularly for polycystic ovary syndrome, may further improve biological interpretation. Clinical translation will require standardized individual-follicle sampling, one-to-one linkage between biomarkers and oocyte or embryo outcomes, targeted assay development, multilevel statistical modeling, independent prospective validation, and demonstration of incremental clinical utility beyond established patient and embryological variables. The…

articles.title: Efficacy and safety of PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors plus chemotherapy ± bevacizumab for recurrent or metastatic cervical cancer: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
articles.authors: Luo R, Li M, Ma L et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The efficacy of adding PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors to chemotherapy ± bevacizumab in recurrent or metastatic cervical cancer is under active investigation.
OBJECTIVE: To systematically evaluate the efficacy and safety of PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors combined with chemotherapy ± bevacizumab in this setting through a meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs).
METHODS: A systematic search of PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, Scopus, and ClinicalTrials.gov was conducted for RCTs published up to January 14, 2026. Primary outcomes were overall survival (OS) and progression-free survival (PFS); hazard ratios (HRs) were derived from reconstructed Kaplan-Meier curves.
RESULTS: Six RCTs involving 2,242 patients were included: 1,131 received PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors plus chemotherapy ± bevacizumab, and 1,111 received chemotherapy ± bevacizumab alone. The combination regimen significantly prolonged median OS (28.7 vs. 19.4 months) and median PFS (12.0 vs. 8.7 months). Pooled risk ratios (RRs) for complete response, partial response, stable disease, progressive disease, and objective response rate were 1.606 (95% CI, 1.333-1.936), 1.127 (95% CI, 0.994-1.277), 0.733 (95% CI, 0.612-0.878), 0.460 (95% CI, 0.305-0.695), and 1.235 (95% CI, 1.153-1.322), respectively. The risk of any-grade adverse events did not differ significantly between groups (RR 0.999, 95% CI 0.991-1.008), whereas the combination was associated with an increased risk of grade ≥3 adverse events (RR 1.069, 95% CI 1.019-1.121). Frequently reported adverse reactions included nausea, anemia, constipation, arthralgia, neutropenia, hypertension, alopecia, and peripheral neuropathy.
CONCLUSION: In patients with recurrent or metastatic cervical cancer, the addition of PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors to chemotherapy ± bevacizumab significantly improves OS and PFS, though with a modest increase in high-grade toxicity.
SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/, identifier CRD420261472748.

articles.title: Male initiation in contraceptive negotiation among Boda-Boda riders in Kampala, Uganda.
articles.authors: Mugisa KM, Rujumba J, Chien LY
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: This study examined male initiation of contraceptive negotiations, related factors, and associations with method agreement and use frequency among Boda-Boda riders motorcycle taxi operators in Uganda.
METHODS: A cross-sectional survey (August-September 2023) included 421 sexually active male Boda-Boda riders in Kampala. Logistic and multinomial logistic regression models were used to analyze the data.
RESULTS: Overall, 54.39% of participants initiated contraceptive negotiations, mostly regarding hormonal methods (55%). Initiation was positively associated with age <45 years, history of sexually transmitted infections, recent receipt of family planning information, and partner contraceptive side effects. Factors unexpectedly negatively associated included income ≥1M Ugandan shillings, commercial sex work, and discussing family planning with healthcare workers, the last potentially reflecting reverse causation (men consulting providers after a partner raised the topic). Initiators had significantly higher odds of adopting all contraceptive methods and reporting consistent contraception use.
CONCLUSION: Results highlight the need for targeted, male-friendly, and couple-centered interventions. Risk-tailored social behavioral change communication practices and inclusive family planning services are recommended to strengthen reproductive health decision-making.

articles.title: Assisted reproduction in the public sector: why secondary-level hospitals matter for equity and continuity of care.
articles.authors: Endara-Mina J, Bermúdez-Gavilanes J, Salazar FR et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Infertility is a major public health challenge, yet access to assisted reproductive technology (ART) remains unequal, particularly where public provision is limited. This Policy and Practice Review examines the role of secondary-level hospitals in integrating ART into public health systems.
METHODS: A structured literature search was conducted in PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, and LILACS, without publication-date restrictions, including literature in English, Spanish, and Portuguese. Evidence on access, service organization, referral pathways, continuity of care, workforce, health information systems, governance, and financing was synthesized thematically and interpreted through expert-informed policy analysis.
RESULTS: The review identified geographic, financial, organizational, and health-system barriers to equitable ART access. Integrated models may allow specialized centers to retain high-complexity procedures while secondary-level hospitals support infertility assessment, referral coordination, follow-up, and pregnancy surveillance. Eight policy priorities were identified: integration of secondary-level hospitals; standardized referral pathways; workforce development; national ART registries; equity-oriented evaluation; patient and community participation; integrated governance and quality assurance; and sustainable financing. An implementation framework specifying responsible actors, minimum resources, implementation phases, barriers, and monitoring indicators was developed.
CONCLUSION: Integrating secondary-level hospitals into coordinated ART networks may strengthen continuity of care, geographic accessibility, and use of specialized resources. These potential benefits require prospective evaluation during implementation.

articles.title: Chemotherapy-refractory high-grade serous ovarian carcinoma: single-cell findings, TCGA-OV transcriptomic context, and a single-case MRI-transcriptome illustration.
articles.authors: Chen L, Fu P, Wu S et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Primary chemotherapy refractoriness remains a clinical challenge in high-grade serous ovarian carcinoma (HGSC) and may reflect pre-existing tumor-cell states and microenvironmental heterogeneity. We examined public single-cell and bulk transcriptomic resources, a barcode-matched MRI case, and an in vitro cisplatin-perturbation RT-qPCR experiment.
METHODS: We reanalyzed GSE300897, comprising 19,156 annotated cells from nine treatment-naïve HGSC biopsy libraries (four chemotherapy-refractory and five chemotherapy-sensitive), with response summaries retained at the library/patient level. The Cancer Genome Atlas Ovarian Cancer (TCGA-OV) provided 421 unique primary tumors for cohort-scale transcriptomic and overall survival context. One TCGA-OV case (TCGA-24-1423) linked a multiparametric MRI examination to a tumor RNA-seq barcode. OVCAR-3 and Caov-3 cells were exposed to cisplatin (5 μM, 24 h), and IFIT1, MX1, SNAI1, and HIF1A expression was measured by RT-qPCR.
RESULTS: Across the nine GSE300897 libraries, no cancer-cell program passed Benjamini-Hochberg (BH) q < 0.05. Refractory libraries showed a lower type-I interferon (IFN-I) score (-0.15 log1p(CP10k)) and epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT) balance (-0.16), with a small increase in hypoxia (+0.05). In TCGA-OV, none of the six displayed program scores reached BH q < 0.05 in age- and stage-adjusted Cox models; IFN-I tertiles separated nominally by Kaplan-Meier analysis (log-rank p = 0.029), whereas continuous IFN-I was not significant after adjustment (HR = 0.96 per SD, BH q = 0.927). In TCGA-24-1423, the paired transcriptome showed an IFN-I score at the 86.8th TCGA-OV percentile, with IFIT1 and MX1 at the 87.5th and 93.7th percentiles. RT-qPCR showed lower IFIT1/MX1 and higher SNAI1/HIF1A after acute cisplatin exposure in both cell lines (all Holm-adjusted p < 0.05).
CONCLUSION: These findings support a conservative, hypothesis-generating interpretation of chemotherapy response-associated transcriptional heterogeneity in HGSC. Reduced IFN-I and altered cell-state programs were directional features of the small refractory single-cell cohort, whereas TCGA-OV provided context rather than independent response validation. The MRI-linked case demonstrates imaging-transcriptome pairing but does not establish an imaging biomarker. The RT-qPCR experiment demonstrates cisplatin-responsive changes in selected genes but models acute drug perturbation rather than the pretreatment clinical…

articles.title: Application of semidefinite programming approach for detection of genomic copy number variations from peripheral blood in ovarian cancer.
articles.authors: Kalab M, Sharma A, Klopf A et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In 2025, we developed and published a detection test using digital droplet polymerase chain reaction (ddPCR) from cell-free DNA that indicates the presence of ovarian cancer (OC) in peripheral blood immediately before surgery with a sensitivity and specificity of 80%.
METHODS: By applying a new classification approach based on semidefinite programming (SDP), we were able to significantly improve the predictive power of this test, which consists of six ddPCR combinations that indicate genomic imbalances. In addition to the previously used ratio of the ddPCR combination products, we now also include the sum of the ddPCR combination products.
RESULTS: Data from the already published 57 controls without tumor background and a positive cohort of 15 OC were expanded by 5 additional OCs. With these data, we were able to define a separating boundary plane in a multidimensional space that better distinguishes the test results.
CONCLUSIONS: This new method allows the detection of cell-free tumor DNA from OC with high tumor burdens in the plasma with high sensitivity and specificity. Further studies using larger and independent cohorts are needed to evaluate the robustness of our approach to evaluate its potential use as a screening algorithm and to assess the diagnostic potential of minimally invasive blood-based ddPCR tests in OC.

articles.title: A nomogram integrating YTHDC2 expression and clinicopathological parameters for predicting endometrial cancer recurrence: a multicenter retrospective study.
articles.authors: Gong Y, Hou L, Xiong J et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Endometrial cancer (EC) is one of the most common gynecological malignancies worldwide, with persistently rising incidence and mortality. Reliable molecular biomarkers for predicting EC recurrence remain lacking. This study aimed to develop a nomogram integrating YTHDC2 expression with clinicopathological parameters to predict postoperative recurrence-free survival (RFS) in EC patients.
METHODS: A total of 520 stage I-III EC patients undergoing initial standard surgical treatment were enrolled as the training cohort, and 243 patients from three independent hospitals constituted the validation cohort. Univariate and multivariate Cox regression analyses were performed to identify independent prognostic factors for RFS in the training cohort, and a nomogram was constructed accordingly. Internal validation was conducted using the concordance index (C-index) and calibration curves in the training cohort, and external validation was performed in the validation cohort. Risk stratification was based on the Nomogram-predicted 3-year RFS probability, and Kaplan-Meier curves were used to evaluate the clinical utility of the model. The nomogram's discriminative performance was further compared with three published EC prediction models.
RESULTS: Univariate and multivariate Cox regression analyses identified age (HR = 2.02, P = 0.006), International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics (FIGO) stage (HR = 4.20, P < 0.001), lymphovascular space invasion (LVSI; HR = 1.81, P = 0.022), CA125 level (HR = 1.66, P = 0.048), depth of myometrial invasion (HR = 1.68, P = 0.039), histological type (HR = 3.42, P < 0.001), p53 protein status (HR = 2.61, P < 0.001), and YTHDC2 high expression level (HR = 0.26, P < 0.001) as independent prognostic factors for RFS. A nomogram incorporating these eight factors was constructed to predict RFS in EC. Internal and external calibration curves demonstrated good agreement between predicted and observed outcomes. The model achieved a C-index of 0.892 in the training cohort and 0.859 in the validation cohort, significantly outperforming single-indicator models. It also surpassed three published EC prediction models in both cohorts. The nomogram consistently outperformed single-indicator models in predicting 1-, 3-, and 5-year RFS.
CONCLUSION: The nomogram integrating YTHDC2 expression with clinicopathological parameters demonstrated favorable accuracy in predicting RFS for patients with EC and may effectively guide long-term…

articles.title: Synergistic antitumor effects of combined pembrolizumab and anlotinib via EGFR inhibition and tumor microenvironment remodeling in high-grade serous ovarian cancer.
articles.authors: Yin X, Zhang L, Mu Y et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: High-grade serous ovarian cancer (HGSOC) remains difficult to treat, particularly in platinum-resistant or recurrent cases. Despite ongoing clinical trials investigating pembrolizumab combined with anlotinib, the synergistic mechanisms of this regimen are poorly understood.
METHODS: This study constructed humanized patient-derived xenograft models via implanting HGSOC tumor cells into NSG mice and subsequently infusing human peripheral blood mononuclear cells to dissect synergistic mechanisms.
RESULTS: Relative to controls and pembrolizumab monotherapy, combination therapy raised the fractions of CD4+ T cells and CD8+/NK cells while decreasing myeloid-derived suppressor cell abundance. Enhanced cell-cell interactions from monocyte and CD8+/NK-cell senders to epithelial targets were observed in the combination group. Upregulation of GRN-SORT1 signaling mediated communication between myeloid subclusters 1, 7 and epithelial subclusters 0, 2, 3, whereas CCL7-CCR1 signaling was activated between myeloid subcluster 7 and lymphocyte subcluster 0. A decreased Treg proportion was also achieved under combined treatment. Multicolor immunofluorescence of patient HGSOC tissues showed close spatial contacts between CD14+CCL7+ monocytes and CD8+CCR1+ T cells, and CCL7 as well as CCR1 expression positively correlated with intratumoral CD8+ T-cell infiltration.
CONCLUSION: These findings suggest that pembrolizumab and anlotinib may synergize through both limiting tumor-promoting pathways and enhancing anti-tumor immunity. This combinatorial regimen may represent a promising therapeutic strategy for improving clinical outcomes in HGSOC patients.

articles.title: The Heaviest White.
articles.authors: Post W
articles.abstract: The Heaviest White is a poetic inquiry into the symbolic and moral weight of the white coat within the landscape of the U.S. maternal mortality. Through layered imagery and reflective narrative, the poem examines silence, complicity, and professional responsibility as they operate within medical authority when mothers die preventable deaths. Centered in a first-person clinician perspective, the piece engages in moral reckoning and self-accountability, positioning eyewitnessing and forensic truth as ethical acts within clinical practice. Rather than presuming to hold institutions accountable on its own, the poem invites clinicians, researchers, and readers into justice-oriented reflection-particularly in relation to the disproportionate and enduring loss of Black women. By weaving together clinical insight and creative expression, The Heaviest White challenges its audience to confront the emotional and ethical burden carried by medicine and to imagine a future in which no woman dies unseen, unheard, or unremembered.

articles.title: Metabolic risk factors for fungal ball sinusitis in perimenopausal women.
articles.authors: Wang SY, Xu W, Liu YX et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Rising incidence of fungal ball sinusitis (FBS) is frequently observed in perimenopausal women. This study aimed to explore the relationships between TyG-BMI, HDL-C and FBS in this specific population.
STUDY DESIGN: This single-center retrospective study enrolled FBS patients from 2015 to 2025. Perimenopausal women aged 45-60 years were selected as the study subjects, and patients with chronic non-fungal sinusitis (CNFS) were selected as the control group. Biochemical indicators were compared, and participants were stratified by TyG-BMI quartiles. Logistic regression was used to identify independent risk factors, and ROC curves were applied to assess predictive efficiency.
RESULTS: The cases of FBS showed an increasing trend. The patients were predominantly middle-aged and elderly individuals, and the proportion of female patients was significantly higher than that of males (63.96% vs. 36.04%), with the peak age of female morbidity concentrated between 45 and 60 years. Intergroup comparison demonstrated that the FBS group had significantly lower HDL-C levels and significantly higher TyG and TyG-BMI values than the CNFS group. With the elevation of TyG-BMI quartiles, the HDL-C level decreased progressively, accompanied by a significantly rising trend in the prevalence of FBS (P < 0.05). Logistic regression analysis confirmed that HDL-C and quartile of TyG-BMI were independent influence factors for FBS in perimenopausal women (P = 0.008, OR = 0.482,95%CI:0.282-0.823; P = 0.04, OR = 1.192, 95%CI:1.008-1.409; respectively). ROC analysis revealed that the combined model of TyG-BMI and HDL-C exhibited limited predictive value for FBS.
CONCLUSION: The incidence of FBS has been increasing annually, especially in perimenopausal women. Decreased HDL-C and elevated TyG-BMI are independent metabolic risk factors for FBS in perimenopausal women. Targeted metabolic monitoring and early intervention may be associated with lower FBS risk.

articles.title: Adjunctive effects of acupuncture and moxibustion in women with premature ovarian insufficiency receiving hormone replacement therapy: protocol for a multicenter, assessor-blinded, 2 × 2 factorial randomized controlled trial.
articles.authors: Lu C, Ye T, Cui J et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Premature ovarian insufficiency (POI) is characterized by impaired ovarian function before 40 years of age and is associated with menstrual disturbance, infertility, hypoestrogenic symptoms, psychological distress, and long-term health risks. Hormone replacement therapy (HRT) is recommended for symptom control and prevention of estrogen-deficiency-related complications but does not reliably restore ovarian activity or fertility potential. Acupuncture and moxibustion are used as complementary interventions for ovarian dysfunction; however, evidence regarding their independent and combined adjunctive effects in women with POI remains limited.
METHODS: This prospective, multicenter, assessor-blinded, 2 × 2 factorial randomized controlled trial will recruit 144 women with POI from three clinical centers. Participants will be randomly assigned in a 1:1:1:1 ratio to estradiol/dydrogesterone alone, acupuncture plus estradiol/dydrogesterone, moxibustion plus estradiol/dydrogesterone, or combined acupuncture and moxibustion plus estradiol/dydrogesterone. The intervention period will last 12 weeks. The primary outcome is the change from baseline to week 12 in antral follicle count (AFC). Secondary outcomes include serum anti-Müllerian hormone (AMH), sex hormones, ovarian hemodynamic parameters, menopausal and anxiety symptoms, Traditional Chinese Medicine syndrome scores, and menstrual status. Clinical pregnancy will be analyzed as an exploratory reproductive outcome during treatment and follow-up at weeks 24 and 48. Factorial models will estimate the main effects of acupuncture and moxibustion, whereas the acupuncture × moxibustion interaction will be considered exploratory.
CONCLUSION: This trial will evaluate the adjunctive effects of acupuncture and moxibustion on AFC and related secondary clinical outcomes in a selected subgroup of women with POI receiving standard HRT. The factorial design will permit estimation of the independent effects of both interventions and exploratory assessment of their potential interaction.
CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: https://itmctr.ccebtcm.org.cn/, identifier ITMCTR2025002408.

articles.title: TyG indicator-TyHGB and the risk of gestational diabetes mellitus: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.authors: Li X, Bu W, Liang W et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The objective was to explore the association between triglyceride-high-density lipoprotein cholesterol-glucose body index (TyHGB) and gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) among Chinese pregnant women.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study enrolled 1,063 pregnant women who underwent GDM screening using the oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT). The TyHGB was calculated according to the following formula: TyHGB = TG/HDL-C + 0.7*fasting plasma glucose (FPG) (mmol/L) + 0.1*pre-pregnancy body mass index (pre-BMI, kg/m2). Multivariate logistic regression was performed to calculate odds ratios (ORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) and evaluate the association between TyHGB and GDM among Chinese pregnant women. We performed subgroup analyses as well as receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis to evaluate the diagnostic efficacy of TyHGB for GDM.
RESULTS: Of the total study participants, 190 women (17.87%) were newly diagnosed with GDM. The median age of the cohort was 31.00 years (IQR, 28.0-34.0). After adjusting for relevant confounding factors, multivariable logistic regression revealed that increased TyHGB levels was significantly associated with increased GDM risk, with an odds ratio (OR) of 1.82 (95% CI: 1.37-2.44). In addition, the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) for TyHGB was 0.675 (95% CI: 0.646-0.703). The optimal cut-off value was 5.995, yielding a specificity of 63.12% and a sensitivity of 66.32%. Notably, the TyHGB exhibited superior diagnostic performance for GDM relative to maternal age, pre-BMI, FPG and the triglyceride-glucose index.
CONCLUSION: The TyHGB represents a promising indicator for the identification of pregnant women at high risk of GDM.

articles.title: Postoperative vaginal anatomy and dyspareunia after vNOTES hysterectomy without apical suspension: a comparative study.
articles.authors: Tunc S, Arkan K, Kayaalp H et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study compared postoperative vaginal length, apical support, dyspareunia, and sexual function outcomes among vNOTES, laparoscopic, and abdominal hysterectomy in patients who did not undergo concomitant apical suspension.
METHODS: This retrospective comparative study included 140 women aged 40-55 years who underwent hysterectomy for benign indications between June 2018 and June 2024. Patients were allocated to three groups according to the surgical approach: vNOTES (n = 60), total laparoscopic hysterectomy (TLH; n = 40), and total abdominal hysterectomy (TAH; n = 40). None of the included patients had undergone concomitant apical suspension at the time of hysterectomy. The primary anatomical outcomes were vaginal length (VL) and apical support, assessed using the Pelvic Organ Prolapse Quantification (POP-Q) C-point, at 6 months postoperatively. Sexual function was assessed using the Female Sexual Function Index (FSFI), and dyspareunia severity was evaluated using a 10-cm visual analog scale (VAS).
RESULTS: Postoperative vaginal length was shortest in the vNOTES group (7.2 ± 0.6 cm), compared with the TLH (7.9 ± 0.7 cm) and TAH (8.4 ± 0.8 cm) groups (p < 0.001). Similarly, the C-point was located more caudally in the vNOTES group (-4.5 ± 1.0 cm) than in the TLH (-6.1 ± 0.9 cm) and TAH (-6.8 ± 1.0 cm) groups (p < 0.001). Significant differences in FSFI and dyspareunia scores were observed at 6 months, with lower FSFI and higher dyspareunia scores in the vNOTES group (p < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: The surgical approach was associated with differences in postoperative vaginal anatomy and dyspareunia. Compared with TLH and TAH, vNOTES without apical suspension was associated with shorter vaginal length, a more caudal apical position, and higher dyspareunia scores. Because apical suspension was not directly evaluated, whether concomitant apical support would modify these outcomes remains unknown and warrants prospective investigation.

articles.title: Association of Conception Mode with Antenatal Anxiety, Depression, and Delivery Outcomes: A Multicenter Cohort Study.
articles.authors: Li Y, Liu C, Li Y et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study compared antenatal anxiety and depression risks across modes of conception and examined their associations with adverse maternal and neonatal outcomes and cesarean delivery without medical indication.
METHODS: This multicenter cohort included 3458 pregnant women receiving antenatal care at three Chinese obstetric centers from December 2023 to December 2025, including 1954 natural conceptions and 1504 conceptions after infertility treatment. Infertility treatment was classified as assisted reproductive technology, surgery, or medical treatment. Anxiety and depression risks were assessed at 26-28 weeks using the GAD-7 and EPDS. Multivariable logistic regression was performed.
RESULTS: Women conceiving after infertility treatment had higher risks of anxiety than those with natural conception (21.0% vs 14.0%, P<0.001) and depression (15.2% vs 12.5%, P=0.023). Assisted reproductive technology was independently associated with anxiety risk (aOR, 1.40; 95% CI, 1.12-1.74), whereas no infertility treatment pathway was associated with depression risk. Neither anxiety nor depression risk was associated with adverse maternal and neonatal outcomes, although assisted reproductive technology was associated with this outcome (aOR, 1.61; 95% CI, 1.32-1.96). Cesarean delivery without medical indication occurred in 16.5% of women and was associated with anxiety risk, depression risk, assisted reproductive technology, and medical treatment, with aORs of 1.88, 1.55, 1.43, and 1.53, respectively.
CONCLUSION: Assisted reproductive technology was associated with increased antenatal anxiety risk. Positive anxiety and depression screens were associated with cesarean delivery without medical indication, supporting antenatal psychological screening, clinical assessment, and individualized counseling.

articles.title: The lost scent of excitation: dissociation between cognitive desire and physical arousal in Kallmann syndrome.
articles.authors: Seminara G, D'Aleo E, Leuzzi M et al.
articles.abstract: Kallmann syndrome (KS) is a rare form of congenital hypogonadotropic hypogonadism (CHH) that causes delayed puberty and infertility, accompanied by a lifelong loss of smell. While hormone replacement therapy (HRT) restores standard hormone levels, the specific impact of an absent sense of smell on sexual relationships and desire remains largely unstudied. This study examined how lifelong smell loss shapes the psychosexual experiences of affected individuals. 38 adults were evaluated: 19 patients receiving stable HRT (10 with KS who lacked a sense of smell and 9 with CHH but normal smell) and 19 healthy matched individuals. Participants completed validated questionnaires assessing sexual desire, physical arousal, romantic behaviors, and attitudes toward intimacy. HRT effectively restored baseline sexual desire and general attitudes across all patients. However, individuals with KS reported significantly lower physical sexual arousal and engaged in far fewer sexual behaviors than those with an intact sense of smell. The lack of smell independently predicted lower arousal levels, despite patients maintaining normal mental desire and positive attitudes toward sex. These findings show that hormone therapy alone is insufficient to fully restore the sexual experience in KS. The lifelong absence of smell creates a distinct divide between mental desire and physical arousal, undermining sexual confidence and intimacy. Healthcare providers should therefore incorporate psychosexual counseling into routine clinical care to help patients navigate these sensory and emotional challenges.

articles.title: Plant-derived nutrition and perimenopausal emotional health: current evidence and research priorities.
articles.authors: Sun Z, Liu X, Dong S et al.
articles.abstract: Perimenopause combines ovarian hormone variability with changes in stress regulation, inflammatory-redox balance, neuroplasticity, and gut-brain metabolism, creating a period of increased vulnerability to depressive symptoms, anxiety, irritability, and sleep disturbance. This narrative review synthesizes evidence on plant-derived foods, bioactives, dietary supplements, and standardized botanical preparations relevant to emotional health during the menopausal transition. Targeted searches of PubMed/MEDLINE, Web of Science, and Scopus identified literature published through 31 July 2026. Evidence was classified by consumed form and reproductive-stage directness and integrated across three regulatory axes: endocrine-stress regulation, immune-redox-neuroplasticity, and gut-brain-metabolic communication. Human evidence includes small randomized trials of standardized saffron, rhapontic rhubarb, fenugreek, ashwagandha, and shatavari preparations, with product-specific psychological-symptom signals, as well as a null Hypericum-Vitex trial. Evidence for plant-rich dietary patterns and isolated bioactives derives mainly from broader menopausal or adult populations. Across studies, reproductive stage, exposure composition, symptom endpoint, and preparation standardization emerge as key determinants of interpretation. Linking symptom clusters with proposed pathway involvement generates hypotheses for prospective phenotype-stratified nutrition trials. Future studies should combine reproductive staging using the Stages of Reproductive Aging Workshop + 10 (STRAW+10) framework, prespecified emotional outcomes, dietary assessment, standardized product characterization, exposure biomarkers, metabotype profiling, and safety monitoring. This framework positions plant-derived nutrition as a testable component of perimenopausal emotional-health research and functional-food development.

articles.title: A modified ovarian-adnexal reporting and data system ultrasound for differentiating ovarian carcinoma: integration of the risk of malignancy algorithm into the American College of Radiology's O-RADS US framework.
articles.authors: Liu M, Li D, Jin Z
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Most ovarian cancer cases are diagnosed at advanced stages, primarily due to the limited efficacy of current classification systems that rely on imaging modalities with variable accuracy. Transvaginal ultrasound as an imaging modality is commonly achieved using the detection of morphological features, which has some limitations mainly related to sonographer experiences and subjective nature of the assessment. To address this limitation, we developed a novel scoring system by incorporating the risk of malignancy algorithm (ROMA) into the ovarian-adnexal reporting and data system ultrasound lexicon (O-RADS US) framework, aiming to refine ultrasound-based risk stratification.
METHODS: This retrospective study enrolled 151 patients (mean age, 51.6 years ± 15.3), with 159 ovarian-adnexal masses (median, 8.2 cm; range, 2.1-24.9cm) between January 2023 and May 2026. The masses were assessed according to O-RADS US criteria, while ROMA values were calculated preoperatively. Then, the modified O-RADS US system reclassified lesions by integrating ROMA-derived malignancy probabilities into O-RADS US categories.
RESULTS: The modified O-RADS US system demonstrated superior diagnostic efficiency for ovarian cancer detection, achieving an AUC of 0.922 (95% CI: 0.878-0.966), significantly outperforming both the original O-RADS US system (AUC = 0.815, 95% CI: 0.740-0.890; p < 0.05) and ROMA alone across premenopausal (AUC = 0.861, 95% CI: 0.812-0.910; p < 0.05), postmenopausal (AUC = 0.902, 95% CI: 0.860-0.943; p > 0.05), and combined cohorts (AUC = 0.894, 95% CI: 0.865-0.923; p > 0.05). A marked reduction in O-RADS 4 lesions and an increase in O-RADS 2/3 lesions, while O-RADS 5 lesions remained stable (23.3% vs. 23.9%), and the malignancy rate for Categories 4 and 5 lesions increased from 44.0% with the original system to 58.1% with the modified system.
CONCLUSION: The incorporation of ROMA into the ACR O-RADS US framework significantly enhances diagnostic performance for ovarian carcinoma, and improves risk stratification accuracy, reducing unnecessary biopsies for low-to-moderate risk lesions.

articles.title: Association between carotid intima-media thickness and preeclampsia: Prospective observational comparative study.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.authors: Sarikaya S, Uysal E, Toprak E et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Preeclampsia is associated with widespread endothelial dysfunction and shares several pathophysiological mechanisms with atherosclerosis. Carotid intima-media thickness (CIMT) is a well-established marker of subclinical atherosclerosis and may reflect early maternal vascular remodeling. This study aimed to compare CIMT between pregnant women with and without preeclampsia and to evaluate the association between CIMT and preeclampsia.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this prospective observational cohort study, pregnant women with singleton pregnancies who attended the outpatient obstetrics clinic between 24 and 37 weeks of gestation and met the eligibility criteria were prospectively enrolled. Participants diagnosed with preeclampsia formed the study group, and pregnant women who were not diagnosed with preeclampsia during the evaluation phase and during pregnancy formed the control group. CIMT measurements were performed at the time of evaluation for all patients, concurrently with the clinical and laboratory assessment used for diagnosis. Demographic characteristics, routine laboratory parameters, and CIMT measurements were compared between groups. Correlation analyses and receiver operating characteristic curve analysis were performed to evaluate the association between CIMT and preeclampsia.
RESULTS: Women with preeclampsia had significantly greater CIMT than pregnant women without preeclampsia. Maternal age, body mass index, serum uric acid, urea, and creatinine levels were significantly higher, whereas serum albumin levels were significantly lower in the preeclampsia group. CIMT demonstrated significant correlations with several biochemical parameters related to renal function and systemic vascular involvement. In multivariable logistic regression analysis, median CIMT remained independently associated with preeclampsia after adjustment for maternal age, body mass index, and gestational age at CIMT measurement (adjusted odds ratio 2.53 per 0.1 mm increase; 95% confidence interval 1.36-4.71; P = 0.003). Receiver operating characteristic analysis showed that CIMT had a moderate ability to discriminate women with and without preeclampsia (area under the curve 0.75).
CONCLUSION: Women with preeclampsia exhibited significantly increased CIMT compared with pregnant women without preeclampsia. Median CIMT demonstrated moderate discriminatory performance for distinguishing women with and without established preeclampsia; however, the clinical utility of…

articles.title: Lipid-inclusive metabolomics of infants born after suspected preterm labor according to whether delivery occurred preterm or at term: A prospective cohort study.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.authors: Youssef L, Abadía-Cuchí N, Lerma-Irureta J et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To characterize the cord blood metabolic profile of infants born after suspected preterm labor (sPTL) according to whether delivery occurred preterm or at term compared with infants from uncomplicated pregnancies.
STUDY DESIGN: Prospective observational cohort study including singleton pregnancies complicated by sPTL and uncomplicated pregnancies. Lipid-inclusive metabolomics was performed by liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS), and data were analyzed using multivariate and univariate approaches.
RESULTS: Of 507 detected metabolites, 506 were present in at least 70% of samples and were included in the analysis. Multivariate analyses showed separation between sPTL with preterm delivery and uncomplicated controls, whereas sPTL with term delivery showed an intermediate metabolic profile. Univariate analysis identified 122 metabolites that differed across the three groups after Benjamini-Hochberg correction. The metabolites contributing most strongly to group discrimination were predominantly lipids, including phosphatidylcholines, cholesteryl esters, sphingomyelins, lysophosphatidylethanolamine, and cholesterol-derived hormones. Hierarchical clustering of the top 25 metabolites identified three clusters, with most sPTL pregnancies resulting in term delivery falling within an intermediate cluster. As antenatal corticosteroid exposure was common among pregnancies with sPTL, and as the sample size of the non-exposed subgroup was limited, the study could not reliably disentangle the effects of sPTL from those of corticosteroid treatment.
CONCLUSION: Cord blood metabolomic profiles differed between infants from pregnancies complicated by sPTL and infants from uncomplicated term pregnancies. The persistence of an intermediate metabolic profile among infants born at term after sPTL raises the possibility of a metabolic signature associated with the preceding episode of sPTL. However, the observational design and frequent antenatal corticosteroid exposure preclude the attribution of these differences specifically to sPTL. Larger studies with adequate representation of corticosteroid-exposed and non-exposed pregnancies are warranted.

articles.title: Fangchinoline as a Dual-action Therapeutic Agent: Recent Advances in Cancer and Infectious Disease Research.
articles.authors: Tailor NK
articles.abstract: Fangchinoline (FC) is a naturally occurring bisbenzylisoquinoline alkaloid isolated from medicinal plants of the Menispermaceae family that has attracted considerable attention owing to its diverse pharmacological properties and therapeutic potential. Recent studies have highlighted its potent anti-cancer and anti-infective activities, which are mediated through the regulation of multiple cellular and molecular targets. FC has demonstrated significant anticancer efficacy against a wide range of cancers, including colon adenocarcinoma, non-small cell lung cancer, lung cancer, esophageal squamous cell carcinoma, conjunctival melanoma, gallbladder cancer, nasopharyngeal carcinoma, renal cell carcinoma, hepatocellular carcinoma, osteosarcoma, ovarian cancer, glioblastoma multiforme, cholangiocarcinoma, breast cancer, and gastric cancer. Its anticancer effects are primarily attributed to the modulation of key signaling pathways, including PI3K/Akt/mTOR, MAPK, NF-κB, and AMPK, as well as to the induction of ROS-mediated apoptosis, cell-cycle arrest, and autophagy. Beyond anticancer activity, FC exhibits broad-spectrum anti-infective activity against viral, bacterial, and fungal pathogens. Notably, it has demonstrated potent antiviral effects against influenza A viruses, SARS-CoV, MERS-CoV, SARS-CoV-2, and several SARS-CoV-2 variants. Moreover, FC exhibited enhanced antiviral efficacy when used in combination with remdesivir or clofazimine. This review provides a comprehensive overview of the chemistry, pharmacological activities, molecular mechanisms, and therapeutic applications of FC, with special emphasis on its anti-cancer and anti-infective potential. Overall, FC represents a structurally versatile and multifunctional lead compound with considerable promise for further therapeutic development.

articles.title: Network Diffusion on a Multiscale Interactome Reveals Novel Herbal Candidates and Bioactive Compounds Converging on Shared Effectors in Anemia.
articles.authors: Lee WY
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION/OBJECTIVE: Anemia is a prevalent hematological disorder driven by heterogeneous mechanisms-iron deficiency, chronic inflammation, impaired erythropoiesis, and hemolysis-that single-target therapies often fail to address. We systematically prioritized candidate herbs and their active compounds for anemia using a multiscale interactome-based network pharmacology framework.
METHODS: Herb-compound-target data were aggregated from OASIS, DrugBank, TTD, and STITCH; anemia disease targets came from DisGeNET. We generated diffusion profiles using a biased random walk with restart on the tripartite multiscale interactome, and ranked herbs by cosine similarity to the anemia profile. Hypergeometric testing, GO/KEGG enrichment, compound-level subnetwork analysis, and HERB-based transcriptome validation followed.
RESULTS: The top 10 prioritized herbs-led by Swertiae Herba, Geranii Herba, and Salviae Miltiorrhizae Radix-were enriched in TNF/NF-κB, HIF-1, and JAK-STAT/PI3K-Akt pathways. Four high-ranking herbs and seven constituent compounds (e.g., swertiamarin, p-hydroxybenzoic acid, physcion, salvianolic acids A/B) had not previously been proposed as therapeutic candidates for anemia. Transcriptome validation of tanshinone IIA implicated the cell cycle, PI3KAkt, and FoxO pathways and recovered GDF15 and CXCL12.
DISCUSSION: Across all subnetworks, divergent compound-target architectures converged on shared downstream effectors (PLEC, ITGB4, ELANE, TNF), supporting a multi-target paradigm. Mechanistic profiles further suggested subtype relevance: swertiamarin to inflammation-associated anemia; p-hydroxybenzoic acid to telomere/bone-marrow-failure anemias; physcion/epicatechin to oxidative-stress and hemolytic anemias.
CONCLUSION: The framework offers a reproducible route to nominating multi-target herbal therapeutics for anemia, identifying novel candidates that warrant experimental validation.

articles.title: Bioinformatics-Guided Scutellaria Flavonoids Ameliorate Memory Impairment Induced by Ovariectomy and D-Galactose in Rats.
articles.authors: Chao C, Lihua G, Yan C et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: This study aimed to explore the protective effects of flavonoids extracted from the stems and leaves of Scutellaria baicalensis (SSFs) against memory deficits in rats induced by combined ovariectomy and D-galactose treatment, as well as the underlying regulatory mechanisms linked to apoptosis-related molecules, estrogen receptors, and Paired Helical Filaments (PHFs).
METHODS: Comprehensive bioinformatic analysis was performed to screen Alzheimer's Disease (AD)- related Differentially Expressed Genes (DEGs) and conduct functional pathway enrichment analysis. An estrogen-deficient menopausal-like rat model-associated memory impairment was established via ovariectomy combined with D-galactose administration, and the Morris Water Maze (MWM) assay was used to verify model establishment. Rats with successful model induction were randomly divided into a model group and three SSF treatment groups with distinct doses. The learning and memory capacities of rats were assessed using the MWM. Immunohistochemistry was used to detect the protein expression of 5- Bromo-2'-deoxyuridine (BrdU). Quantitative real-time Polymerase Chain Reaction (qPCR) was used to quantify the mRNA level of BCLAF1. Western Blotting (WB) was applied to measure the protein levels of Estrogen Receptor α (ERα), Estrogen Receptor β (ERβ), the anti-apoptotic protein Bcl-2, BCLAF1, non-phosphorylated tau, and PHFs in the cerebral cortex and hippocampus.
RESULTS: Bioinformatic analysis identified 13 AD‑related DEGs along with their enriched functional pathways. Combined ovariectomy and D‑galactose treatment induced severe memory impairment in rats (P < 0.01), accompanied by a prominent decrease in BrdU‑positive cells in the hippocampal dentate gyrus (P < 0.01). In the cerebral cortex and hippocampus of model rats, the mRNA and protein expression of BCLAF1, as well as protein levels of ERα and PHFs, were significantly upregulated (P < 0.05, P < 0.01). By contrast, the expression of ERβ, Bcl‑2 and non- phosphorylated tau was markedly downregulated (P < 0.05, P < 0.01). SSFs dose- dependently ameliorated the above behavioral and molecular abnormalities triggered by ovariectomy plus D- galactose.
DISCUSSION: Our bioinformatic analysis identified 13 Alzheimer's disease-related differentially expressed genes, mainly enriched in ion-channel- and GABA-receptor-associated pathways, providing potential molecular clues for postmenopausal cognitive impairment. The ovariectomy-combined-Dgalactose…

articles.title: Integrative Multi-Model Analysis Identifies a Core Gene Signature Associated with WEE1 Inhibitor Resistance, the Resistance-Associated Tumor Microenvironment, and Therapeutic Vulnerability in Ovarian Cancer.
articles.authors: Lei C, Xiong J, Chen Y et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ovarian cancer is the most lethal gynecological malignancy, and acquired resistance to chemotherapy and targeted therapy is a central cause of treatment failure. The WEE1 inhibitor AZD1775 (adavosertib) has shown clinical activity in ovarian cancer, particularly in tumors with TP53 dysfunction, but acquired resistance frequently emerges, and its molecular basis remains incompletely understood. This study aims to identify a conserved, cross-species gene signature associated with the AZD1775-resistant state, to characterize its relationship with the Tumor Immune Microenvironment (TIME) and patient prognosis, and to nominate candidate drugs for combination testing.
METHODS: Transcriptomic data from a self-established murine AZD1775-resistance model (ID8 vs ID8R; RNA-seq, GSE313926) and from publicly available human AZD1775-resistant ovarian cancer cells (ES-2 vs ES-2R clones; GSE142124) were integrated. Differentially Expressed Genes (DEGs) were intersected across models, Weighted Gene Co-Expression Network Analysis (WGCNA) was applied to the ID8/ID8R data, and a Protein-Protein Interaction (PPI) network was used to prioritize connected candidates. In the TCGA Ovarian Cancer (TCGA-OV) cohort, ESTIMATE and five immune deconvolution algorithms (CIBERSORT, EPIC, TIMER, MCP-counter, and quanTIseq) were used to estimate stromal/immune admixture. The prognostic associations were assessed in Kaplan-Meier Plotter. Candidate drugs were prioritized from CellMiner using a pre-specified effect-size threshold, and drug combinations with AZD1775 were tested in ID8R cells by CCK-8 with Chou-Talalay analysis.
RESULTS: A nine-gene signature (VCAN, RNASEL, PROS1, TNFRSF9, PXDN, KCNH1, KLF11, ATF3, and CDK15) was consistently upregulated across resistant models and within the resistance-associated WGCNA module. ESTIMATE and deconvolution analyses associated the signature with stromal/CAF and endothelial compartments, with weaker, method-dependent associations with immune-cell fractions. The nine-gene score was associated with overall survival, with heterogeneous direction for individual genes (VCAN, ATF3, CDK15, KLF11, and PXDN adverse; TNFRSF9, KCNH1, RNASEL protective). CellMiner drug sensitivity prediction and in vitro validation revealed that cell lines with high expression of the core gene set were more sensitive to Bleomycin, Lenvatinib, and Dasatinib; combinations with AZD1775 produced additive-to-synergistic effects under the standard Chou-Talalay grading…

articles.title: Emerging Role of Human Long Non-coding RNA HOST2 as a Regulator and Biomarker across Multiple Cancer Types.
articles.authors: Du Q, Zhou L, Song D et al.
articles.abstract: Long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) have emerged as important regulators of tumor initiation and progression. Human ovarian cancer-specific transcript 2 (HOST2), also known as competing endogenous lncRNA 2 for microRNA let-7b (CERNA2), is an oncogenic lncRNA that is aberrantly upregulated in several malignancies. This review summarizes current evidence regarding the expression patterns, clinical relevance, and molecular mechanisms of HOST2 in eight cancer types that have been comparatively well studied, including Stomach Adenocarcinoma (STAD), Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma (PAAD), ovarian serous cystadenocarcinoma (OV), cervical squamous cell carcinoma and endocervical adenocarcinoma (CESC), non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), sarcoma (SARC), glioma, and Breast Invasive Carcinoma (BRCA). Mechanistically, HOST2 promotes malignant phenotypes through multiple pathways, most notably by acting as a competing endogenous RNA (ceRNA) for members of the let-7 miRNA family, thereby regulating downstream oncogenic targets. HOST2 has also been implicated in Epithelial-Mesenchymal Transition (EMT), cell-cycle progression, JAK2/STAT3 signaling, and resistance to anticancer drugs such as gemcitabine and gefitinib. Clinically, elevated HOST2 expression has been associated with advanced tumor stage, lymph node or distant metastasis, and unfavorable overall survival in several cancer types, suggesting potential value as a prognostic biomarker and therapeutic target. However, current evidence is derived predominantly from in vitro and in vivo preclinical studies and relatively small retrospective patient cohorts. Further prospective, multicenter, and mechanistic studies are therefore required to validate the clinical utility of HOST2 and to clarify its cancer-specific regulatory functions.

articles.title: Nrf2 Immunohistochemical Expression in Stillbirths: A Potential Marker of Early Fetal Hypoxic Stress.
articles.journal: Pediatric and developmental pathology : the official journal of the Society for Pediatric Pathology and the Paediatric Pathology Society
articles.authors: Bonasoni MP, Camatti J, Santunione AL et al.
articles.abstract: Stillbirth remains a major challenge in perinatal and forensic pathology, particularly when the timing of fetal death and the mechanisms of hypoxic injury are difficult to establish using conventional morphological criteria alone. Nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (Nrf2) is a key regulator of cellular responses to oxidative stress and may represent an early marker of fetal cellular stress. We conducted a retrospective forensic study of stillbirth cases that underwent complete autopsy between 2017 and 2024. Clinical, pathological, and placental data were examined to estimate the timing of fetal distress and the death-delivery interval. Immunohistochemical analysis of Nrf2 expression was performed on fetal cardiac tissue sections, and cases were classified as Nrf2-positive or Nrf2-negative based on unequivocal nuclear immunoreactivity. Nrf2 nuclear expression was identified in 10/44 cases (22.7%) and was observed more frequently in cases with shorter death-delivery intervals and clinicopathological patterns compatible with acute or subacute fetal hypoxic stress, particularly placental abruption and selected acute umbilical cord-related events. These findings suggest that Nrf2 nuclear immunoreactivity may represent a potential ancillary marker of early fetal cellular stress in well-preserved stillbirth tissues. However, tissue preservation may represent an important confounding factor. Further prospective studies with controlled temporal parameters are needed to clarify its diagnostic and forensic value.

articles.title: Prevalence and factors associated with intrapartum and immediate postpartum obstetric complications in Ethiopia: a secondary analysis of a national longitudinal survey.
articles.authors: Geremew AB, Roberts CT, Ullah S et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Most maternal deaths in Ethiopia occur during childbirth and the immediate postpartum period, yet population-level evidence on intrapartum and immediate postpartum complications and their determinants remains limited. In particular, the roles of intimate partner violence (IPV) during pregnancy and pregnancy complications have been underexplored.
OBJECTIVE: To determine the prevalence and factors associated with intrapartum and immediate postpartum obstetric complications in Ethiopia.
METHODS: We conducted a secondary analysis of the Performance Monitoring for Action Ethiopia (PMA-E) longitudinal survey (October 2019 and September 2020) using a two-stage stratified cluster sampling design. Multilevel modified Poisson regression analysis was used to estimate adjusted prevalence ratio (aPR) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs).
RESULTS: A total of 2558 women were included in the analysis. The prevalence of intrapartum and immediate postpartum complications was 37.6% and 31.6%, respectively. Rural residence (aPR = 1.72,95% CI: 1.34-2.20), intimate partner violence (IPV) during index pregnancy (aPR = 1.31,95% CI: 1.14-1.50), pregnancy complications (aPR = 1.78, 95% CI: 1.55-2.06), and nulliparity (aPR = 1.30, 95% CI: 1.07-1.58) were associated with intrapartum complications. Factors associated with immediate postpartum complications were complications during pregnancy (aPR = 1.65, 95% CI: 1.40-1.93) and prolonged labour (aPR = 1.34, 95%CI: 1.14-1.57). Childbirth at health facility was associated with a lower prevalence of immediate postpartum complications (aPR = 0.83, 95% CI: 0.70-0.98).
CONCLUSION: Intrapartum and immediate postpartum obstetric complications are common in Ethiopia. IPV during pregnancy, pregnancy complications, and nulliparity were associated with intrapartum complications. Pregnancy complications and prolonged labour were associated with a higher prevalence of immediate postpartum complications, while health-facility childbirth was associated with a lower prevalence.

articles.title: Concentration-Based Short-Course Hyperthermic IntraPEritoneal Chemotherapy (HIPEC) at Interval Cytoreductive Surgery (iCRS) for Advanced Ovarian Cancer: Final Analysis of Overall Survival in a Phase 2 Trial.
articles.authors: Batista TP, de Barros ABD, Carneiro VCG et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The optimal regimen for Hyperthermic IntraPEritoneal Chemotherapy (HIPEC) remains controversial. We aim to present long-term overall survival results from our phase 2 trial evaluating a concentration-based short-course regimen for ovarian cancer at the time of interval CytoReductive Surgery (iCRS).
METHODS: This was a multicenter, single-arm, phase 2 trial including patients with advanced ovarian cancer undergoing iCRS after neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NACT). HIPEC was administered via the closed-abdomen technique for 30 min at 41°C-43°C, comprising the use of cisplatin (25 mg/L of perfusate/m2, total limit 240 mg) alone, or in combination with doxorubicin (15 mg/L, total limit 90 mg).
RESULTS: Between February 2015 and July 2019, fifteen patients were enrolled and followed for a median of 110.6 months (95% CI, 85.2 - not reached). Median overall survival was 83.9 months (95% CI, 31.3 - not reached), with a 5-year survival rate of 53.3% (95% CI, 33.2-85.6) and a restricted mean survival time truncated at 5 years of 45·6 months (95% CI, 37.2-54.0). At the time of this analysis, 13.3% were alive without disease, 13.3% remained on systemic therapy, and 73.3% had died.
CONCLUSION: Concentration-based short-course HIPEC is a feasible and safe regimen for ovarian cancer patients. This approach is associated with favorable long-term overall survival, highlighting the need for head-to-head comparisons of different HIPEC regimens.

articles.title: Postpartum placental ischemic dams display elevate blood pressure, kidney cortex TNF-α, and kidney medulla nitric oxide bioavailability.
articles.journal: American journal of physiology. Renal physiology
articles.authors: Smith SL, Smith J, Jones K et al.
articles.abstract: Women who experience a placental ischemic (PI) pregnancy, such as preeclampsia, have an increased risk of developing chronic kidney disease (CKD) as early as 5-20 years postpartum (PP). The underlying mechanisms leading to this increased risk for CKD are unknown. Mechanisms that contribute to the development of CKD are hypertension and changes in renal molecular factors such as inflammation, oxidative stress, and nitric oxide (NO) bioavailability. To determine the relationship between blood pressure, renal molecular factors, and CKD in women after a PI pregnancy, we used the reduced uterine perfusion pressure model of preeclampsia in rats. In this study, two groups were utilized: normal pregnant (NP) and PI dams. At 6 wk postpartum (∼2-3 human years), we examined the dams' blood pressure via carotid catheterization, collected the plasma to measure creatinine, and obtained the kidneys to evaluate the abundance and concentrations of renal molecular factors. PI dams exhibited an increase in blood pressure (125 ± 3 vs. 111 ± 3 mmHg, P = 0.002), TNF-α in the kidney cortex (81.38 ± 1.1 vs. 67.48 ± 0.58 pg/mL/mg Protein, P < 0.0001), and NO bioavailability (0.64 ± 0.08 vs. 0.41 ± 0.05 µmol NO3/mg Protein, P = 0.03) in the kidney medulla. However, serum creatinine, renal kidney injury molecule 1 (KIM-1), endothelial nitric oxide synthase (eNOS), neutrophil gelatinase-associated lipocalin (NGAL), and oxidative stress did not have significant changes. In summary, PI dams exhibited alterations in kidney inflammation and NO bioavailability, with no indications of renal dysfunction or injury. Thus, suggesting that changes in renal molecular factors may precede the onset of CKD. This study is clinically relevant because it highlights the potential contributions of altered renal molecular factors in the development of CKD postpartum.NEW & NOTEWORTHY Postpartum (PP) placental ischemic dams display elevated blood pressure, kidney cortex inflammation, and kidney medulla nitric oxide (NO) bioavailability, with no changes in kidney function or injury. These findings are clinically relevant because postpartum preeclamptic women who have placental ischemia have an increased risk of developing chronic kidney disease (CKD) (∼5-20 yr after birth). Examining postpartum dams in the early postpartum period is important because it may provide insights into the pathogenesis and pathophysiology of CKD development.

articles.title: Bronchopulmonary Dysplasia Starts in Utero: MicroRNA Dysregulation Across the Fetal-Neonatal Continuum in the Bronchopulmonary Dysplasia Development.
articles.journal: Journal of cellular and molecular medicine
articles.authors: Perrone S, Carloni S, Beretta V et al.
articles.abstract: Bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD) is a heterogeneous developmental lung disorder resulting from the interaction between antenatal susceptibility and postnatal injury. Increasing evidence suggests that its biological origins may precede preterm birth, with placental dysfunction, fetal growth restriction, inflammation and oxidative stress influencing pulmonary developmental trajectories before exposure to the extrauterine environment. MicroRNAs (miRNAs), small non-coding RNAs that regulate gene expression at the post-transcriptional level, are emerging as potential molecular mediators linking these fetal and neonatal processes. This educational review examines miRNA dysregulation across the fetal-neonatal continuum of BPD. We first discuss the role of miRNAs in physiological lung development and their disruption following premature birth. We then explore how placental dysfunction and fetal growth restriction may influence miRNA networks, including placenta-enriched C19MC miRNAs, thereby contributing to antenatal susceptibility to BPD. Particular attention is given to miRNA-mediated regulation of pulmonary angiogenesis and VEGF signaling and to the bidirectional relationship between miRNAs and oxidative stress, including modulation of NRF2-dependent antioxidant responses. Beyond their mechanistic relevance, miRNAs offer potential translational opportunities. Their stability and detectability across different biological compartments-including placenta, cord blood, peripheral blood, respiratory samples and extracellular vesicles-make them attractive candidates for longitudinal biomarker profiling, while experimental modulation using miRNA mimics and inhibitors provides proof of concept for future therapeutic approaches. However, heterogeneity in biological sampling, analytical methods, developmental timing and BPD phenotypes, together with challenges in tissue-specific delivery and off-target effects, currently limit clinical translation. Rather than identifying a single 'BPD miRNA', future research should focus on dynamic, multi-compartment miRNA networks integrating antenatal programming with postnatal exposures. Such an approach may improve molecular endotyping, early risk stratification and ultimately the development of individualized preventive and therapeutic strategies for BPD.

articles.title: Cardiovascular Disease in Women the Two Decades Following Uteroplacental Disorders: A Population-Based Data-Linkage Study.
articles.journal: BJOG : an international journal of obstetrics and gynaecology
articles.authors: Burger RJ, Kalkman DN, Gordijn SJ et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Uniform recommendations on cardiovascular follow-up after complicated pregnancies are lacking, partly due to limited evidence. This study aimed to investigate the incidence and timing of premature cardiovascular disease (CVD) after different uteroplacental disorders, to inform the timing and content of cardiovascular follow-up.
DESIGN: Population-based cohort study, linking data from the Dutch perinatal registry with national hospital admissions data.
SETTING: Netherlands, 2000-2022.
POPULATION: 1 669 681 nulliparous women, with a singleton pregnancy.
METHODS: Cox regression was used to estimate hazard ratios for overall CVD and specific cardiovascular conditions after uteroplacental disorders, adjusted for confounders. Time-dependent Cox regression and interaction analyses for education attainment, income, and migration background were performed.
RESULTS: Risks of premature hypertension, atherosclerosis, ischaemic heart disease, cardiac arrest, cardiomyopathy, heart failure, and cerebrovascular disease were significantly increased among women with a history of a uteroplacental disorder, adjusted for confounders (overall CVD: aHR 1.70, 95% CI 1.67-1.74; median follow-up time 11 years, IQR 6-17 years). Hazard ratios were similar after pregnancy induced hypertension (PIH), preeclampsia (PE), fetal growth restriction (FGR), or fetal death, while risks after spontaneous preterm birth (sPTB) were less elevated. Most relative CVD risks were highest shortly after pregnancy but remained elevated more than 10 years postpartum. After hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP), hypertension risk was most pronounced, whereas after FGR the increased risk of atherosclerosis was most notable. Socioeconomic factors had limited impact on these associations.
CONCLUSIONS: All uteroplacental disorders-not only PE-serve as women-specific markers of CVD risk, shortly after pregnancy and later in life, highlighting the need for early cardiovascular screening. Pathological processes contributing to the increased CVD risk might differ across uteroplacental disorders.

articles.title: Happiness among nulliparous women of advanced maternal age (AMA): The mediating role of psychosocial factors.
articles.authors: Kim M, Choi H
articles.abstract: This study examined the association between pregnancy stress and happiness and explored the indirect associations through psychosocial factors (maternal identity, childbirth confidence, marital intimacy, and maternal-fetal attachment) among nulliparous women of advanced maternal age. This analytical cross-sectional study was conducted in South Korea using a web-based convenience sample of 165 nulliparous women aged 35 years or older recruited through the country's largest online community for pregnant women. Data were collected from September to October 2023 through a structured online survey and analyzed using IBM SPSS Statistics Version 25.0 and Hayes' PROCESS Macro model 4. The analysis estimated cross-sectional indirect associations rather than causal mediation. Pregnancy stress showed significant total and direct associations with happiness. Significant indirect associations were observed through maternal identity, childbirth confidence, and marital intimacy, whereas maternal-fetal attachment did not show a significant indirect association. These findings may inform programs aimed at reducing pregnancy stress and strengthening psychosocial resources to support positive pregnancy experiences and psychological well-being among nulliparous women of advanced maternal age.

articles.title: Preferential toxicodynamic effects of fenbendazole in ovarian cancer and nonmalignant ovarian cell models.
articles.authors: Katirci E, Kendirci-Katirci R, Karadeniz-Saygili S et al.
articles.abstract: Ovarian cancer remains a major cause of death among gynecologic malignancies because of late diagnosis, frequent recurrence, and resistance to standard chemotherapy. Drug repurposing offers a cost-effective strategy for identifying alternative therapeutic agents, but the comparative toxicodynamic effects of fenbendazole in malignant and nonmalignant ovarian cell models remain incompletely characterized. In this study, the toxicodynamic effects of fenbendazole were evaluated in malignant ovarian cell lines (OVCAR8 and A2780) and compared with those in a nonmalignant ovarian epithelial comparator (IOSE-80) using integrated in vitro approaches, with exploratory in silico analysis as supportive structural context. Fenbendazole reduced viability in ovarian cancer cells in a time- and concentration-dependent manner. At 72 h, IC50 values were lowest in A2780, intermediate in OVCAR8, and remained above the tested concentration range in IOSE-80, yielding lower-bound selectivity indices in favor of malignant cells. Fenbendazole also increased G2/M accumulation, γ-H2AX and cleaved caspase-3 signals, and Annexin V-positive cell populations in malignant cells. These findings indicate that fenbendazole exerts preferential toxicodynamic effects in malignant ovarian cell models relative to the nonmalignant comparator used in this study. An exploratory molecular docking analysis provided limited supportive structural context for a possible tubulin-related mechanism but was not interpreted as evidence of direct target engagement.

articles.title: Serum alarin in relation to depression and anxiety in women with polycystic ovary syndrome.
articles.journal: Hormone molecular biology and clinical investigation
articles.authors: Abd Elhamed H, Fawzy O, Sayed D et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is a common endocrine disorder associated with metabolic, reproductive, and psychological disturbances. Alarin, a neuropeptide of the galanin family, has been implicated in energy metabolism and insulin resistance, and experimental studies suggest a role in mood regulation. However, its association with psychiatric features in PCOS remains unclear. This study aimed to evaluate circulating alarin levels in women with PCOS and their relationship with depression, anxiety, and metabolic-hormonal parameters.
METHODS: This case-control study included 180 women divided into four groups: PCOS with depression, PCOS without depression, depression without PCOS, and healthy controls (45 participants each). Clinical, biochemical, and hormonal assessments were performed, including measurement of serum alarin levels. Depression and anxiety were assessed using validated Hamilton rating scales.
RESULTS: Serum alarin levels were significantly higher in women with PCOS, irrespective of comorbid depression, compared with healthy controls and women with depression without PCOS. Women with depression alone showed alarin levels comparable to controls. Factorial analysis showed significant effects of PCOS status and depression status, with no significant PCOS × depression interaction (p=0.37). Serum alarin correlated positively with fasting insulin, HOMA-IR, and luteinizing hormone, but not with depression or anxiety severity. Multivariate analysis identified luteinizing hormone and PCOS status as independent predictors of serum alarin levels. Receiver operating characteristic analysis demonstrated excellent discriminative performance for PCOS.
CONCLUSIONS: Circulating alarin is closely associated with the metabolic and reproductive features of PCOS rather than psychiatric symptom severity, indicating a stronger link to endocrine-metabolic dysregulation.

articles.title: Perioperative Morbidity and Recurrence After One-Stage Laparoscopic Resection for Multicompartment Deep Endometriosis: A Multicentre Cohort Study.
articles.journal: BJOG : an international journal of obstetrics and gynaecology
articles.authors: Pagano F, Sík PB, Imboden S et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate perioperative morbidity, factors associated with postoperative complications and documented recurrence after one-stage laparoscopic resection for multicompartment deep endometriosis.
DESIGN: Retrospective multicentre cohort study.
SETTING: Two tertiary referral centres specialised in endometriosis surgery (Bern, Switzerland; Budapest, Hungary).
POPULATION: A total of 299 consecutive patients with pathologically confirmed deep endometriosis undergoing one-stage laparoscopic resection between January 2017 and December 2025.
INTERVENTIONS: One-stage laparoscopic resection of multicompartment deep endometriosis.
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Clinically relevant postoperative complications were defined as Clavien-Dindo Grade ≥ II. Multivariable logistic regression assessed associated factors. Recurrence-free survival was evaluated using Kaplan-Meier analysis in patients with an available recurrence time or censoring time. Postoperative complications occurred in 36/299 patients (12.0%), including 35/299 (11.7%) with Grade ≥ II complications and 14/299 (4.7%) with Grade ≥ IIIb complications. Greater #ENZIAN deep endometriosis anatomical extent was independently associated with clinically relevant complications (adjusted odds ratio 1.51 per additional involved compartment, 95% confidence interval 1.04-2.18). Documented recurrence occurred in 43/299 patients (14.4%) and 26/299 (8.7%) underwent reoperation for recurrence. Follow-up duration was available for 231/299 patients (77.3%). Recurrence-free survival did not differ significantly according to bowel (log-rank p = 0.431) or bladder surgical technique (p = 0.116).
CONCLUSION: Greater #ENZIAN deep endometriosis anatomical extent was independently associated with clinically relevant postoperative complications following one-stage surgery for multicompartment deep endometriosis, suggesting that overall anatomical disease extent may better reflect surgical complexity than involvement of a single anatomical site. These findings support the role of anatomical disease extent in preoperative counselling and individualised surgical planning.

articles.title: Placental Histological Lesions in Monochorionic Twins With Selective Fetal Growth Restriction Versus Growth-Restricted Singletons: A Cohort Study.
articles.journal: BJOG : an international journal of obstetrics and gynaecology
articles.authors: Spekman JA, Groene SG, Noll ATR et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To determine the prevalence of placental histological lesions in the smaller twin's placental territory in monochorionic (MC) twins complicated by selective fetal growth restriction (sFGR), and compare it to FGR singletons.
DESIGN: Cohort study with 1:1 comparison.
SETTING: Leiden University Medical Center, The Netherlands.
POPULATION: Forty-four MC twin placentas with sFGR and 44 FGR singleton placentas, histologically evaluated between 2020 and 2025.
METHODS: FGR was defined as birthweight < 10th percentile. sFGR was defined as birthweight discordance ≥ 20% between twins and birthweight < 10th percentile for the smaller twin. Placental parenchyma was examined using Amsterdam Consensus Statement criteria for maternal vascular malperfusion (MVM), fetal vascular malperfusion (FVM), and acute and chronic inflammation. Analyses of placental lesions were adjusted for gestational age at diagnosis of (s)FGR.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Prevalence of histological lesions.
RESULTS: Median gestational age at birth was 37.1 weeks (IQR 32.0-38.1) for FGR singletons and 32.3 weeks (IQR 30.1-35.0) for sFGR twins (p < 0.001). FVM was more common in smaller twins than sFGR singletons (45% versus 16%; OR 3.7 (95% CI: 1.0-13.2); p = 0.046), alongside a higher prevalence of abnormal cord insertions (84% versus 21%; p < 0.001). MVM prevalence was similar between smaller twins and FGR singletons (73% versus 75%; OR 0.8 (95% CI: 0.2-2.9); p = 0.779), as was chronic inflammation (27% versus 34%; OR 0.7 (95% CI: 0.2-2.3); p = 0.549).
CONCLUSIONS: The smaller twin's placental territory in sFGR showed lesions consistent with placental insufficiency, with prevalences of MVM and chronic inflammation comparable to FGR singletons and increased prevalence of FVM. These findings suggest that placental insufficiency may be involved in the pathophysiology of sFGR alongside unequal sharing.

articles.title: Thromboembolic Complications of Orthopedic Surgery.
articles.authors: Richards M, Walles M, Frishman WH
articles.abstract: Orthopedic surgery is a major risk factor for thromboembolic events such as deep venous thrombosis and pulmonary embolism following a variety of surgeries such as total hip and knee replacements, fracture fixations, spinal surgeries, orthopedic traumas, and arthroscopic surgeries. Many other risk factors contribute, such as age, immobilization, combined oral contraceptive medications, genetic causes, cast immobilization, tourniquet use, and comorbidities. Prophylaxis can be done through chemoprophylaxis and/or mechanoprophylaxis. Diagnosis of deep venous thrombosis is made through ultrasonography, and pulmonary embolism diagnosis is made using risk stratification and a variety of possible tests including D-dimer levels, computed tomography pulmonary angiogram, and ventilation/perfusion scans. Treatment requires using anticoagulants for a minimum of 3 months or possibly inferior vena cava filters if anticoagulation therapy is contraindicated.

articles.title: Pregnancy loss and prevalent cardiometabolic multimorbidity: a two-stage individual participant data analysis of CHARLS, ELSA, and HRS.
articles.authors: Yang Y, Rao K, Pan F et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular disease remains the leading cause of death worldwide, and cardiometabolic multimorbidity (CMM) is associated with substantially higher mortality and reduced life expectancy. Pregnancy loss is common and has been linked to later cardiovascular risk, but multinational evidence using harmonized individual participant data and CMM as the outcome remains limited.
OBJECTIVE: To examine the cross-sectional association between self-reported pregnancy loss and prevalent cardiometabolic multimorbidity (CMM) among middle-aged and older women in three nationally representative ageing cohorts, and to evaluate the consistency of findings across countries.
DESIGN: Cross-sectional analysis using the last valid observation for each woman as the individual-level main analysis, with person-wave analyses as sensitivity analyses. The study did not model incident CMM or CMM progression. Country-specific estimates were combined using a two-stage individual participant data approach.
DATA SOURCES: The China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS, 2011-2018), the English Longitudinal Study of Ageing (ELSA, 2002-2018), and the Health and Retirement Study (HRS, 2017/2019 Life History Mail Survey).
PARTICIPANTS: Women aged 45 years or older with available pregnancy history and cardiometabolic outcome data (CHARLS: n = 7,514; ELSA: n = 3,773; HRS: n = 1,630; total N = 12,917).
EXPOSURE: Self-reported history of pregnancy loss. In CHARLS and HRS, pregnancy loss corresponded to miscarriage or stillbirth; in ELSA, the available variable combined miscarriage, stillbirth, and induced abortion and could not be disaggregated.
MAIN OUTCOME: CMM, defined as the coexistence of at least two of five self-reported physician-diagnosed conditions: hypertension, diabetes, dyslipidemia, heart disease, and stroke.
RESULTS: The prevalence of pregnancy loss was 25.2% in CHARLS, 24.9% in ELSA, and 35.3% in HRS; the individual-level prevalence of CMM was 30.1%, 46.6%, and 36.9%, respectively. In the fully adjusted individual-level model (M3), pregnancy loss was associated with higher odds of prevalent CMM in CHARLS (OR = 1.45, 95% CI: 1.20-1.75, p < 0.001), but not in ELSA (OR = 1.08, 95% CI: 0.90-1.29, p = 0.424) or HRS (OR = 1.24, 95% CI: 0.71-2.17, p = 0.455). The DerSimonian-Laird random-effects pooled OR was 1.24 (95% CI: 0.99-1.56, p = 0.062; HKSJ 95% CI: 0.82-1.89). In the person-wave M3 sensitivity analysis, the pooled OR was 1.15 (95% CI: 0.98-1.34, p = 0.083;…

articles.title: Could pelvic ischemia be a new indicator for OAB? Insights from internal iliac artery doppler analysis.
articles.authors: Yuce A, Altas H, Basar D et al.
articles.abstract:
