BACKGROUND: We aimed to examine whether blood flow in the internal iliac artery differs between patients with overactive bladder (OAB) and healthy individuals and to investigate whether reduced pelvic blood flow plays a role in OAB.
METHODS: 42 patients diagnosed with OAB and 42 healthy controls were included in the study. Their general health status, habits, biochemical, and behavioral data were examined. Blood flow in the internal iliac artery was assessed using Doppler ultrasonography. Peak systolic velocity (Vmax), end-diastolic velocity (Vmin), resistive index (RI), and pulsatility index (PI) were measured and compared between the groups.
RESULTS: The groups were similar in terms of age, comorbidities, habits, and biochemical parameters. In the OAB and control groups, the Vmax value of the right iliac artery was measured as 95.28 ± 11.48 to 116.17 ± 17.93 (p < 0.001), and the Vmin value of the left iliac artery was measured as 18.01 ± 4.41 to 21.14 ± 4.91 (p = 0.003). The calculated RI values were found to be 0.82 ± 0.05 vs. 0.79 ± 0.05 (p = 0.015) on the right side and 0.83 ± 0.05 vs. 0.80 ± 0.06 (p = 0.016) on the left side in the OAB and control groups. The PI value was found to be 4.38 ± 0.74 and 3.87 ± 0.65 on the right side (p < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: In this study, Doppler flow patterns suggestive of increased vascular resistance and altered pelvic vascular hemodynamics were observed in the OAB group. These findings may indicate an association between pelvic vascular alterations and OAB. Measurement of internal iliac artery blood flow using Doppler ultrasonography may represent a promising adjunctive imaging approach for investigating vascular factors associated with OAB.

articles.title: Factors influencing individual decision-making in contraceptive method selection: a comprehensive analysis.
articles.authors: Cao Z, Li J, Sun L et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Contraceptive methods vary in effectiveness, side effects, cost, and other characteristics that influence individuals' preferences. Understanding these preferences is essential for supporting patient-centered care and improving contraceptive decision-making. However, there remains a lack of comprehensive synthesis of the key attributes driving contraceptive choices across diverse populations.
OBJECTIVE: The aim of this systematic review was to identify the key attributes that are most important to individuals when selecting a contraceptive method.
METHODS: This review follows the PRISMA 2020 guidelines and includes studies published between 2000 and 2024. A comprehensive literature search was conducted across Embase, PubMed, and Web of Science databases. Studies that employed Discrete Choice Experiment (DCE), conjoint experiments, surveys, or structured interviews to assess contraceptive preferences were included.
RESULTS: A total of 22 studies were included in the final analysis, encompassing 53,730 participants. We identified 44 distinct attributes related to contraceptive choice, which were grouped into eight categories: effectiveness and safety, convenience and suitability, economy and cost, social and interpersonal relationships, privacy and control, information and advice, lifestyle and behavior, and services and support. Among the most frequently assessed attributes were effectiveness, side effects, cost, convenience, safety, and privacy. Effectiveness and safety were consistently rated as the most important factors in contraceptive choice, followed by cost and privacy considerations. Variations were observed in preferences across regions, with cost being a primary concern in the United States and privacy being particularly important in African countries.
CONCLUSION: This review identifies several key attributes associated with contraceptive choice, with consistent emphasis on effectiveness, safety, cost, and privacy. These findings may provide reference points for contraceptive counseling and the development of decision-support tools. However, further research is needed to better understand socio-cultural and emotional determinants of contraceptive decision-making, as well as the temporal dynamics of preference formation across life stages.

articles.title: Genomics screening views and practices in South East Asian, Indian and Chinese populations: a scoping review.
articles.authors: Bylstra Y, Juann MY, Zhang J et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Population genomics screening can stratify individual health and reproductive risks for carriers of genetic conditions. As global implementation expands, insights from diverse settings will help shape equitable and contextually appropriate practice. This scoping review maps views and genomics screening practices for populations in South East Asia, a multicultural yet underrepresented region. Chinese and Indian populations were also included given their cultural and demographic relevance to communities in this region.
METHODS: A systematic search was conducted in Ovid, Embase and Web of Science for studies published until December 2025. Eligible studies reported views and uptake of population screening amongst participants and healthcare professionals; studies reporting screening for clinical indications were excluded. From 1,971 records retrieved, 31 studies met inclusion criteria. Study characteristics such as knowledge, attitudes, screening uptake barriers and facilitators, reproductive intentions and views of healthcare professionals were tabulated.
RESULTS: Studies were published between 1998 and 2025 from six countries, predominantly from China (n = 18), and largely reported carrier screening initiatives (n = 29). Fifteen studies explored views towards screening, 12 reported implementation outcomes and four addressed both. Screening engagement was limited by knowledge gaps, religious and cultural influences, and cost; however, attitudes were favourable following education and health system integration. When screening was implemented, uptake and consideration of reproductive options was high.
CONCLUSIONS: Effective implementation in South East Asia requires targeted educational interventions for both communities and healthcare professionals, affordable delivery models and clinician-supported integration into healthcare services to provide equitable and culturally sensitive delivery.

articles.title: Menopausal arthralgia and longitudinal changes in sex hormones and climacteric symptoms.
articles.authors: Xie Z, Tang R, Huang F et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Musculoskeletal discomfort (menopausal arthralgia) is the most prevalent and debilitating complaint during the menopausal transition. Despite its high prevalence, menopausal arthralgia has historically been overlooked, and establishing a direct association with menopause remains challenging. We aimed to study the relationship of menopausal arthralgia with respect to changes in estradiol, follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) levels, and climacteric symptoms during the menopausal transition.
METHODS: Participants from a longitudinal community-based cohort in Beijing, China recruited since 2005 were studied. Women in the menopausal transition (within 5 years before or after the final menstrual period) with ≥ 2 assessment visits were included. Menopausal arthralgia was defined as the presence of moderate or severe muscle and/or joint pain affecting multiple sites, with onset or worsening during the menopausal transition, our reference condition being arthralgia symptoms reported by breast cancer patients undergoing estrogen suppression with aromatase inhibitor therapy. Participants with any history of rheumatoid arthritis or other autoimmune diseases were excluded. Menopausal symptoms and serum levels of FSH and estradiol were evaluated at each annual visit. Multivariable binary logistic regression assessed associations.
RESULTS: Among 327 women (mean age 48.48±3.65), 212 (64.83%) experienced menopausal arthralgia. Lower initial FSH levels [aOR 0.71 (95% CI 0.53, 0.96)], and a more rapid rise of FSH during the menopausal transition [aOR 2.97 (95% CI 1.02, 8.68)], increased risks for menopausal arthralgia after adjustment for age, BMI, and menopausal status. Concomitantly, higher initial estradiol levels were associated with increased risk [aOR 1.34 (95% CI 1.05, 1.71)]. The presence of hot flashes [aOR 3.58 (95% CI 2.10, 6.07)], night sweats [aOR 3.33 (95% CI 1.92, 5.76)], and vulvo-vaginal discomfort [aOR 3.19 (95% CI 1.86, 5.46)] was also associated with menopausal arthralgia after covariate adjustment.
CONCLUSIONS: Menopausal arthralgia was associated with rapid hormonal fluctuations, characterized by a higher longitudinal rate of FSH change and lower initial FSH levels, alongside higher initial estradiol levels. Given its strong association with classic climacteric symptoms, menopausal arthralgia should be recognized as an integral component of the menopausal syndrome.

articles.title: Urinary incontinence symptoms and knowledge across activity levels in young women (UI-SKY Project): a mixed-methods comparative study.
articles.authors: Ratanaarsanarom V, Aimjirakul K, Manonai J et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Urinary incontinence (UI) in young women is increasingly recognized but remains under-reported and insufficiently addressed. While physical activity has been implicated in pelvic floor dysfunction, evidence regarding its relationship with urinary incontinence remains heterogeneous and context-dependent. This study aimed to evaluate UI prevalence, symptom burden, and knowledge, and to explore perceptions and care-seeking behaviors among young women.
METHODS: A nationwide mixed-methods comparative study was conducted among 461 women aged 18-40 years in Thailand. Participants were categorized into three groups based on physical activity levels: athletes (n = 141), recreationally active (n = 152), and sedentary (n = 168). Quantitative data were collected using validated questionnaires including ICIQ-UI SF, IIQ-7, and PIKQ-UI which assessed UI severity, impact on quality of life, and knowledge of urinary incontinence, respectively. Multivariable regression analyses were performed to assess associations between activity level and outcomes. In-depth interviews were conducted with 30 participants and analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis. Findings were integrated using an explanatory sequential approach.
RESULTS: Overall, 30.8% of participants reported UI, with prevalence decreasing across activity levels (39% sedentary, 30% recreationally active, 22% athletes; p = 0.004). Athletes had significantly lower odds of UI compared with sedentary women (adjusted OR 0.45, 95% CI 0.25-0.80; p = 0.007). Physical activity was not associated with symptom severity among symptomatic individuals. Both athletes and recreationally active women reported lower quality-of-life impact compared with sedentary participants (adjusted OR 0.55 and 0.52, respectively). Despite these favorable outcomes, athletes demonstrated significantly lower pelvic floor knowledge (adjusted OR 0.17, 95% CI 0.08-0.34; p < 0.001), indicating a knowledge-behavior gap. Qualitative findings revealed consistent themes of age-related misperception, symptom normalization, stigma, and delayed care-seeking. Participants commonly relied on self-management and informal information sources, and a substantial gap between PFMT awareness and practice was identified.
CONCLUSION: UI in young women in this study population represents an under-recognized public health issue, with prevalence highest among sedentary individuals. While physical activity is associated with lower UI prevalence and better…

articles.title: Phenotypic characteristics associated with preterm births in the Indian population.
articles.authors: Gadekar VP, Sadhu A, Thakur SB et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Preterm birth (PTB), defined as the birth of an infant before 37 weeks of gestation, poses significant health risks, including increased mortality and long-term disabilities. India stands as a major contributor to global PTB-related mortality, primarily due to its substantial prevalence. The complex temporal relationship among multiple etiological factors makes predicting PTB occurrence challenging. This is further complicated by the diverse PTB phenotypic categories, namely maternal, fetal, placental, parturition, and pathway-to-delivery features, which affect birth outcomes.
METHODS: Our study focused on PTB in the Indian population using a comprehensive dataset from the GARBH-Ini cohort. We analyzed 21 variables across maternal, fetal, placental, parturition-related, and other phenotypic categories in the context of Phenotype I (PTB/Non-PTB) and Phenotype II, which classifies PTB based on the pathway to delivery as either Spontaneous Onset of Labor (SOL) or Caregiver-Initiated (CGI). We assessed the prevalence of these phenotypic variables and their co-occurrences using the complete dataset. We applied hierarchical clustering to identify key PTB-associated phenotypic patterns and their impact on neonatal outcomes, including NICU admissions and early neonatal mortality. The optimal number of clusters (K = 20) was selected based on silhouette scores. Clusters with intermediate PTB composition (40-80% PTB, "grey zone") were excluded to minimize misclassification and improve interpretability. Additionally, we used one-year follow-up data to examine infant-related phenotypic variables and their distribution across PTB and non-PTB cases.
RESULTS: We identified key phenotypic variables across maternal, fetal, placental, and parturition categories that significantly influenced PTB outcomes. In SOL cases, fetal (perinatal sepsis, polyhydramnios) and parturition-related (PROM, short cervix, peripartum bleeding) features were significantly associated. In contrast, CGI cases were predominantly associated with maternal complications like illness suggestive of birth asphyxia, hypertension, and hypothyroidism. Placental abnormalities, such as placenta previa, in combination with PROM and short cervix, were notably prevalent in PTB cases, impacting neonatal mortality, NICU admissions, and infant health.
CONCLUSIONS: Compared with non-PTB births, PTB cases showed higher prevalence of several key phenotypic features, including short cervix (10.84% vs 3.42%),…

articles.title: Association of genetic predisposition to immune-related biomarkers with premenstrual disorders and symptom severity.
articles.authors: Luo Y, Sun J, Chen M et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Premenstrual disorders (PMD), including premenstrual syndrome (PMS) and the more severe premenstrual dysphoric disorder (PMDD), are burdensome conditions with unclear mechanisms. While inflammation is implicated, biomarker research is challenged by inconsistent findings and cyclical fluctuations. This study utilized polygenic risk scores (PRS) to investigate the association between lifelong genetic predisposition to altered immune-related cell counts and PMD risk and symptom severity.
METHODS: This cross-sectional study included 1,730 Chinese college students from the Care of Premenstrual Emotion cohort. PRS were calculated for seven immune biomarkers: white blood cell (WBC), basophil, eosinophil, lymphocyte, monocyte, neutrophil, and C-reactive protein. Probable PMD cases and symptom severity (total, physical, affective) were assessed using a modified Calendar of Premenstrual Experiences. Generalized estimating equations estimated risk ratios (RR) and β-coefficients, adjusting for confounders.
RESULTS: Overall, 424 (24.5%) participants met probable PMD criteria, including 379 (21.9%) with PMS and 45 (2.6%) with PMDD. The PRS for WBC showed a suggestive, non-significant association with diagnosis (RR, 1.08; 95% CI, 1.00-1.18; P = 0.062). No other immune PRS showed significant associations. A higher PRS for WBC was associated with physical symptom severity (β = 0.05; 95% CI, 0.00-0.10; P = 0.047). This association was stronger in women with symptom onset at menarche (β = 0.47; 95% CI, 0.15-0.78; P = 0.008). The highest quintile of PRS for WBC exhibited greater severity across all domains versus the lowest, suggesting a possible graded pattern. Item-level analyses suggested signals for limb swelling, increased appetite, and food cravings.
CONCLUSIONS: The PRS for WBC may be associated with premenstrual symptom severity, specifically physical domains. These findings suggest that inflammatory liability may contribute to the physical symptom burden of PMD, but replication in prospectively phenotyped cohorts with detailed gynecologic and medical comorbidity data is needed.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Not applicable.

articles.title: Loneliness, social support and stress among Black pregnant women during the COVID-19 pandemic: a mixed methods approach.
articles.authors: Giurgescu C, Misra DP, Esparza L et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The lockdowns implemented during the COVID-19 pandemic may have led to increases in isolation, loneliness and psychological distress among pregnant women. We explored Black pregnant women's experiences during the COVID-19 pandemic.
METHODS: We conducted a convergent mixed methods pilot study with women who were enrolled in the Biosocial Impact on Black Births (BIBB) study and were pregnant during the COVID-19 pandemic. The BIBB study is a prospective study that examines the role of maternal factors on preterm birth among Black women. Women were enrolled in the BIBB study if they self-identified as Black or African American, were 18-45 years old, had singleton pregnancies, and were 8-29 weeks gestation. A sample of 16 women who participated in the BIBB study and were still pregnant in May-June 2020 completed an online survey and participated in phone qualitative interviews about their experiences during the COVID-19 pandemic.
RESULTS: The participants were 21-39 years of age and 29-38 weeks gestation. About 50% of the participants described feelings of loneliness or isolation either on the survey or during the interview. More than half of the participants reported feelings of seclusion from staying at home. Feeling secluded may have led some women to feelings of increased stress due to their inability to have alone time or to leave the house for activities that relieved stress. Participants described the impact of social distancing on the emotional or affective aspect of social support. Nearly all participants described some degree of stress or anxiety during the pandemic.
CONCLUSION: These results suggest that a markedly high proportion of Black pregnant women experienced loneliness, isolation and stress during the COVID-19 pandemic.

articles.title: Effects of e-Health interventions on psychological outcomes among high-risk pregnant women: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.authors: Song JE, Kim GR, Park H et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: High-risk pregnant women face not only physical health issues but also substantial psychological challenges. With the growing interest in innovative strategies, e-Health interventions have gained recognition as a supportive approach for high-risk pregnant women. This systematic review and meta-analysis examined the effects of e-Health interventions on psychological outcomes in high-risk pregnant women.
METHODS: Interventional studies were identified through searches of PubMed, Cumulative Index to Nursing and Allied Health Literature (CINAHL), Embase, Cochrane Central, and Scopus databases. A total of 15,996 articles were retrieved, and 42 interventional studies published between 2007 and 2024 were included in this systematic review and meta-analysis.
RESULTS: Among 42 studies, 24 (57.2%) were published after 2020, and 32 (76.2%) were randomised controlled trials. The e-Health interventions focused on psychological support (47.6%), physical health management (42.9%), and parenting role education (9.5%). The meta-analysis indicated that e-Health interventions were associated with reductions in anxiety (p = 0.017), depression (p = 0.048), and stress (p = 0.006) among high-risk pregnant women. The heterogeneity was high for the overall anxiety and depression analyses (I2 > 80%), and these pooled estimates should be interpreted with caution.
CONCLUSIONS: Given their accessibility, e-Health interventions may offer potential benefits for the psychological support of high-risk pregnant women; however, these findings should be interpreted cautiously owing to the high heterogeneity in the anxiety and depression estimates. Further research is required to confirm these effects and to evaluate their optimal design, long-term effects, and cost-effectiveness.

articles.title: The effect of grief counseling on depression and post-traumatic stress disorder in women following perinatal deaths.
articles.authors: Nournorouzi L, Hakimi S, Esmaeilpour K et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Fetal or neonatal death is a tragic event that frequently leads to the mother experiencing grief, as well as the development of depression and post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD). The present study aimed to determine the impact of grief counseling on depression and PTSD in women following perinatal deaths.
METHODS: This experimental study was conducted on 56 women who had experienced perinatal deaths within the previous 1-3 months in Tabriz, Iran. Participants were randomly assigned to either the intervention or control group based on the type of perinatal loss (stillbirth or neonatal death). For the intervention group, grief counseling was provided individually in three sessions, one per week, lasting 45-60 min. Data collection tools included a demographic and obstetric questionnaire, the Edinburgh Depression Scale, and the PTSD Checklist for DSM-5 (PCL-5). Data analysis was performed using SPSS version 24. ANCOVA was employed to compare depression and PTSD ratings pre- and post-intervention while adjusting for confounding variables.
FINDINGS: The two groups had no significant demographic differences (p > 0.05). One month after the intervention, the mean depression score in the intervention group was significantly lower than in the control group (adjusted mean difference = - 2, 95% confidence interval: - 3.2 to - 0.8, p = 0.01). However, the mean PTSD score did not differ significantly between the two groups (adjusted mean difference = - 1.5, 95% confidence interval: - 7.5 to 4.4, p = 0.59).
CONCLUSION: Grief counseling after fetal or neonatal loss led to a reduction in depression, but no significant effect on PTSD symptoms was observed with this intervention. It is recommended to use other counseling approaches and assess their effectiveness for PTSD following perinatal deaths.

articles.title: Global, regional and national burden of cervical cancer in 1990-2023 with forecasts to 2050: a Global Burden of Disease study.
articles.authors: GBD 2023 Cervical Cancer Collaborators
articles.abstract: Although highly preventable, cervical cancer remains one of the most common malignancies among women worldwide. As part of the Global Burden of Disease study, we estimated cervical cancer incidence, mortality and disability-adjusted life-years (DALYs) across 204 countries and territories from 1990 to 2023, with forecasts to 2050. In 2023, 887,000 new cases (95% uncertainty interval 682,000-1,170,000), 369,000 deaths (292,000-475,000) and 13.3 million DALYs (10.1-17.4) were estimated globally. Age-standardized incidence rate (ASIR) and age-standardized mortality rates (ASMR) were more than four and seven times higher in low- versus high-income countries. Between 1990 and 2023, global ASIR was largely stable (-0.4% (-26.6 to 34.7)), whereas ASMR changed by -17.5% (-36.2 to 13.4). All cervical cancer DALYs were attributable to human papillomavirus infection, with tobacco use contributing 5.9% (3.2-9.3) globally. By 2050, global ASIR and ASMR are forecast to change by -12.5% (-25.7 to 3.5) and -9.0% (-21.5 to 6.6) from 2024, yet absolute cases and deaths are forecast to rise by 20.2% (4.6-38.5) and 39.3% (23.6-57.3). ASIR and ASMR are forecast to remain highest in low-income countries. Intensified action is needed to accelerate progress.

articles.title: Anorectal function after transanal natural orifice specimen extraction for colorectal cancer: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.authors: Chua MWE, Lee ASH, Palanisamy P et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Natural orifice specimen extraction (NOSE) eliminates the abdominal extraction incision after minimally invasive (MIS) colorectal resection and offers favourable short-term recovery, but transanal extraction raises concerns regarding sphincter stretch and anorectal dysfunction. This review evaluated anorectal functional outcomes after transanal NOSE compared with transabdominal specimen extraction (TASE) in MIS colorectal cancer surgery.
METHODS: MEDLINE and EMBASE were searched from inception to August 2024 for comparative studies reporting postoperative anorectal or pelvic floor functional outcomes following transanal NOSE versus TASE. The primary outcome was anorectal continence at the postoperative interval closest to 6 months.
RESULTS: Ten retrospective cohort studies were included, of which seven (1362 patients) contributed quantitative data for meta-analysis. Three studies contributed to the pooled Wexner incontinence score analysis and four to the pooled Pelvic Floor Distress Inventory short form (PFDI-20) analysis. At the interval closest to 6 months, Wexner scores were numerically higher after transanal NOSE than TASE, but the difference was small and non-significant (MD 0.17, 95% CI - 0.01 to 0.35; p = 0.07). PFDI-20 scores did not differ between groups (MD - 0.02, 95% CI - 0.21 to 0.18; p = 0.86). Both estimates were robust in leave-one-out and overlap-adjusted analyses excluding potentially overlapping Harbin Medical University cohorts. Early differences appeared to diminish over time, with no clear separation beyond 12 months.
CONCLUSION: Transanal NOSE was associated with a small, non-significant trend toward higher early Wexner scores after MIS colorectal cancer surgery, while broader pelvic floor symptom burden appeared comparable to TASE. The difference was of uncertain clinical significance, was robust to sensitivity analyses, and longer-term data suggested no persistent functional disadvantage.

articles.title: Uterine Artery Embolization for Postpartum Hemorrhage: A 5-Year Single-Center Experience with Emphasis on Embolization Technique and Factors Associated with Clinical Failure.
articles.authors: Lee S, Lee H, Kwon H et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To describe the embolization technique and clinical outcomes of uterine artery embolization (UAE) for refractory postpartum hemorrhage (PPH), and to identify variables associated with clinical failure.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 150 consecutive patients who underwent UAE for PPH at a single tertiary center (2021-2025). Clinical failure was defined as hysterectomy or repeat embolization (≥ 2 sessions). Variables associated with clinical failure were identified by univariable logistic regression and Fisher's exact test; pre-UAE transfusion was analyzed separately to assess reverse causality.
RESULTS: Clinical success was achieved in 140/150 patients (93.3%); clinical failure occurred in 10/150 (6.7%), comprising hysterectomy in 4/10 and repeat embolization in 6/10. Uterine atony was the most common etiology (107/150, 71.3%). Additional vessel embolization was required in 47/150 patients (31.3%). In an exploratory subgroup analysis, emergency cesarean section had a higher failure rate than elective cesarean Sect. (5/32, 15.6% vs. 1/56, 1.8%; p = 0.022). On univariable analysis, higher total pRBC transfusion (OR 1.144; p = 0.003) and lower platelet count (OR 0.982; p = 0.023) were associated with clinical failure; pre-UAE transfusion was not (OR 1.168; p = 0.161), suggesting total pRBC reflects hemorrhage burden rather than antecedent risk.
CONCLUSION: UAE achieved clinical success in 140/150 patients (93.3%); additional vessel embolization was required in 47/150 (31.3%). Total pRBC transfusion and platelet count were associated with clinical failure in univariable analysis; procedural variables were not.
LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level 4, Case Series.

articles.title: Evaluating the Performance of Five Leading Large Language Models in Generating Health Education Materials for Patients With Infertility: Comparative Analysis.
articles.authors: Lu R, Wei Y, Wu S et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with infertility often have inadequate reproductive health literacy (RHL), while existing health education materials may be difficult to read, overly complex, and insufficiently tailored to individual needs. In recent years, large language models (LLMs) have created new opportunities to improve health education through their ability to generate and interpret medical information. However, their applicability and content quality in infertility education remain insufficiently evaluated.
OBJECTIVE: This study systematically evaluated the readability and content quality of LLM-generated health education materials for patients with infertility, identified model strengths and limitations, and provided evidence to support their standardized use in reproductive health.
METHODS: This study selected DeepSeek-R1, ChatGPT (GPT-5.2 Plus), Kimi 2.5, Qwen 3, and Gemini 3 as the study subjects. Based on the theoretical framework of RHL, this study developed a standardized question list comprising 6 dimensions and 93 items, and used unified prompts to generate health education texts in both Chinese and English. In this study, the Datayze Readability Analyzer was used to assess readability via the Flesch Reading Ease, Gunning Fog Index, and Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level (FKGL). Meanwhile, the content quality was evaluated in a double-blinded manner by reproductive medicine experts across 3 dimensions: accuracy, comprehensiveness, and humanistic care. Repeated-measures analysis of variance was used to compare performance across the LLMs, and Pearson correlation analysis was conducted to examine the associations between readability and content quality. A radar chart was used to evaluate the overall performance of each model.
RESULTS: The 5 LLMs differed significantly in both text readability and content quality. In terms of readability, Gemini 3 and Qwen 3 performed best, with significantly higher FRE scores than the other 3 models. DeepSeek-R1 and Kimi 2.5 performed least favorably, with FKGL scores corresponding to a ninth-grade reading level. ChatGPT (GPT-5.2 Plus) showed intermediate performance. In terms of content quality, Kimi 2.5 performed best across accuracy, comprehensiveness, and humanistic care, followed by DeepSeek-R1. ChatGPT (GPT-5.2 Plus) performed least favorably. Analysis revealed significant negative correlations between readability and content comprehensiveness for texts generated by Kimi 2.5, indicating a trade-off between these 2…

articles.title: BOLSTER: strengthening support for patients with complex care needs from advanced cancers and their caregivers.
articles.journal: International journal of gynecological cancer : official journal of the International Gynecological Cancer Society
articles.authors: Iniesta MD, Pozzar RA, Enzinger AC et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Complications of advanced solid tumors include bowel, urinary or biliary obstructions and ascites, which often require invasive interventions (eg, venting gastric tubes, nephrostomy tubes, or drainage catheters) for palliation. Although these procedures are necessary, patients and caregivers often feel overwhelmed and ill-prepared to manage complex care needs at home and experience decreased quality of life and repeated hospitalizations.
PRIMARY OBJECTIVE: To improve patient quality of life, alleviate symptoms, reduce caregiver burden, and decrease hospital-based care.
STUDY HYPOTHESIS: The BOLSTER intervention will improve patient quality of life, reduce caregiver burden, and decrease health care use compared with usual care by increasing self-efficacy in managing symptoms and complex care needs at 6 and 12 weeks post-randomization. It involves 6 weekly telehealth sessions between the patient-caregiver dyad and a bachelor's-prepared nurse, 2 caregiver-specific telehealth sessions, and access to virtual resources.
TRIAL DESIGN: Prospective, multi-center randomized controlled trial.
MAJOR INCLUSION CRITERIA: Patients (≥18 years old) diagnosed with an advanced solid tumor with a complex care need (eg, ostomy, ileostomy, urostomy, nephrostomy, biliary drain, venting gastric tube, intraabdominal, or pleural catheter) who have a plan to receive ongoing oncology treatment as needed, are English- or Spanish-speaking, and have an English or Spanish-speaking caregiver aged ≥18 years who is willing to participate.
MAJOR EXCLUSION CRITERIA: Oncologist-determined prognosis ≤3 months, planned hospice enrollment, or absence of a caregiver.
PRIMARY ENDPOINT: Change in Functional Assessment of Cancer Therapy-General score from baseline to week 6.
SAMPLE SIZE: 300 patient-caregiver dyads.
ESTIMATED DATES FOR COMPLETING ACCRUAL AND PRESENTING RESULTS: At present, 126 dyads have been randomized. Based upon this, accrual should be completed in April 2028 and results will be presented in September 2028.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: NCT06936878 (registered on April 13, 2025).

articles.title: One-year Outcomes of Female Artificial Urinary Sphincter Implantation in Europe: The VENUS Registry.
articles.authors: Peyronnet B, Chartier-Kastler E, López-Fando-Lavalle L et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Artificial urinary sphincter (AUS) implantation is the gold-standard surgical treatment for severe stress urinary incontinence (SUI) in men, but its use in women remains limited because of technical challenges and the absence of prospective data.
OBJECTIVE: The VENUS registry aimed to prospectively evaluate perioperative, functional, and 1-yr device outcomes of AMS 800 AUS implantation in women with SUI because of intrinsic sphincter deficiency (ISD).
DESIGN SETTING PARTICIPANTS: VENUS is a European Association of Urology Research Foundation prospective multicenter registry that includes adult women undergoing primary AUS implantation for SUI because of ISD across 19 institutions in seven countries. All surgical approaches were permitted.
INTERVENTION: Artificial urinary sphincter implantation.
OUTCOME MEASUREMENT STATISTICAL ANALYSIS: The primary end point was continence at 1 yr, defined as no pad use or use of one security pad. Secondary outcomes included changes in validated questionnaires (International Consultation on Incontinence Questionnaire-Urinary Incontinence Short Form [ICIQ-UI-SF], International Consultation on Incontinence Questionnaire Lower Urinary Tract Symptoms Quality of Life Module, International Consultation on Incontinence Questionnaire Female Sexual Matters Associated with Lower Urinary Tract Symptoms Module, and Patient Global Impression of Improvement), results of the 24-h pad test, 90-d complications (Clavien-Dindo), and 1-yr revision- and explanation-free survival (analyzed using Kaplan-Meier analysis).
CONCLUSIONS AND CLINICAL IMPLICATIONS: This first prospective multicenter study demonstrates that female AUS implantation provides high 1-yr continence rates (>80%) with acceptable short-term device survival and manageable morbidity. These findings support AUS as an effective option for women with SUI because of ISD. Longer-term and comparative data are needed to further define its position in treatment algorithms and international guidelines.

articles.title: A positive maternal anti-red blood cell antibody test: A critical alert for neonatal bilirubin neurotoxicity.
articles.authors: Pickard C, Bhutani VK
articles.abstract: A positive maternal anti-red blood cell (RBC) antibody test is a critical indicator of postnatal isoimmune hemolytic disease and risk of neonatal bilirubin neurotoxicity. Though rare, it remains consequential. Rh negativity and a positive anti-RBC test reveal a high-risk pregnancy that can lead to hemolytic disease of the fetus and newborn (HDFN), requiring supervised skilled perinatal and neonatal expertise. Thus, public health systems have mandated policies to minimize severe postnatal adverse outcomes such as symptomatic postnatal anemia and hemolytic hyperbilirubinemia -a neurotoxic risk factor. Review of interviews with families of alloimmunized mothers have revealed concerns of inconsistent prenatal education of potential postnatal sequelae. Many felt inadequate to cope with a premature infant and needs for intensive care, repeated blood testing, prolonged phototherapy, breastfeeding disruption, and blood transfusions or possible exchange transfusions. Therefore, expert and skilled counseling throughout the pregnancy and at birthing are especially needed with interpreting test results. Specific "hand-off" at birthing of the pivotal test result of anti-RBC antibody is essential. Partnering of both perinatal-neonatal teams with families should increase parental education so that they can monitor their own baby's well-being to ensure a healthy childhood and school age outcomes.

articles.title: Association between maternal mid-pregnancy glucose levels and offspring wheezing in early childhood: a prospective multicentre birth cohort study in Eastern China.
articles.authors: Ni H, Qin J, Zhuang Y et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: We examined maternal glucose concentrations and diabetes status in relation to wheeze in early childhood.
METHODS: We analysed 2986 singleton mother–child pairs from a prospective multicentre birth cohort in three centres in Jiangsu Province, China. Participants had recorded wheeze status and complete same-day oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT) measurements at 24–28 gestational weeks. The outcome was a wheeze recorded during early childhood follow-up. The protocol targeted wheezing before age 3, although ascertainment ages were not uniformly available. Adjusted logistic regression estimates were pooled across 50 imputations.
RESULTS: Wheeze was recorded in 293 children (9.8%). Adjusted ORs per 1 mmol/L higher glucose were 0.98 (95% CI 0.76 to 1.26) for fasting, 1.03 (0.96 to 1.11) for 1 hour and 1.02 (0.94 to 1.11) for 2 hour measurements, with no evidence of nonlinearity. In a secondary analysis, recorded maternal gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) was associated with higher odds of wheeze than no diabetes (adjusted OR 1.39, 95% CI 1.06 to 1.82; Holm-adjusted p=0.034). Standardised risks were 12.1% and 9.1%, respectively, a difference of 3.0 percentage points (95% CI 0.4 to 5.6).
CONCLUSION: Mid-pregnancy glucose concentrations showed no clear association with early-childhood wheeze, with a secondary association between recorded GDM and higher odds of wheeze. Unavailable diagnostic and treatment details and residual confounding limit interpretation. These findings concern wheeze, not subsequent asthma, and do not support changing GDM screening or treatment thresholds.

articles.title: Follow-up after fertility-sparing surgery for cervical cancer: should human papillomavirus testing be used routinely? A narrative review.
articles.journal: International journal of gynecological cancer : official journal of the International Gynecological Cancer Society
articles.authors: Viveros-Carreño D, Beshar I, Mora-Soto N et al.
articles.abstract: Fertility-sparing surgery for early-stage cervical cancer aims to preserve reproductive potential without compromising oncologic outcomes. Post-operative surveillance must balance 3 priorities: early detection of treatable recurrence, detection, and management of premalignant disease in the residual cervix or upper vagina, and avoidance of low-yield tests that trigger additional procedures, cancer-related distress, and potentially detrimental effects on fertility. This narrative review summarizes the best available evidence on follow-up after fertility-sparing surgery for human papillomavirus-related cervical cancer, with specific attention to the comparative value of human papillomavirus testing versus symptom review, pelvic examination, colposcopy, and cervical cytology. Key findings include: (1) Many clinically relevant central recurrences occur early, although extra-cervical relapse remains important in higher-risk cohorts, supporting careful clinical follow-up in the first post-operative years; (2) Cervical cytology after trachelectomy frequently yields abnormalities that rarely change management, highlighting the importance of confirmatory colposcopy; and (3) Combining human papillomavirus status and cytology results stratifies risk for subsequent recurrent cervical intra-epithelial neoplasia grade 2 or worse, suggesting a role for risk-adapted surveillance intervals. Currently, evidence does not support indiscriminate routine human papillomavirus testing for all patients after fertility-sparing surgery as a standalone strategy to detect invasive recurrence. However, selective use in combination with cytology and colposcopy, particularly to tailor visit frequency in patients with reassuring results after the first year, is supported by emerging evidence and is consistent with contemporary guidance. Any implementation should define management pathways for positive tests and account for the low pre-test probability of recurrence in many patients, so that harms from false positives do not outweigh benefits.

articles.title: Validating an early pregnancy HbA1c as the screening test for gestational diabetes mellitus: findings from PRISMA Pakistan cohort.
articles.authors: Naz S, Yazdani NS, Hoodbhoy Z et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: We assessed whether early-pregnancy glycosylated haemoglobin (HbA1c), alone or with common risk factors, can predict gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) and reduce the need for oral glucose tolerance testing (OGTT) in a peri-urban cohort in Karachi, Pakistan.
DESIGN: We conducted a secondary analysis of the Pregnancy Risk Infant Surveillance and Measurement Alliance (PRISMA) Pakistan cohort.
SETTING: The PRISMA Pakistan study is being conducted in two peri-urban communities (Rehri Goth and Ibrahim Hyderi) in Karachi, Pakistan.
PARTICIPANTS: We included women enrolled before 20 weeks’ gestation with available early-pregnancy HbA1c and a 2-hour 75 g OGTT at 24–28 weeks.
PRIMARY AND SECONDARY OUTCOME MEASURES: We externally validated GDM prediction models originally developed in the STRiDE-India cohort. We evaluated model performance using receiver operating characteristic curves and area under the curve (AUC). We assessed four models: HbA1c alone (model 1a); age, body mass index (BMI) and family history of diabetes mellitus (FH DM) (model 1b); HbA1c combined with age, BMI and FH DM (model 2); and an extended model, that is, model 2 combined with socioeconomic status, gestational age, parity and systolic and diastolic blood pressure (model 3). A dual-threshold approach to assess rule-in and rule-out performance and the Youden index were used to identify the cut-off that maximised the combined sensitivity and specificity for each model.
RESULTS: Among 2485 women, GDM incidence was 7.5% (n=186). Models with a broader set of predictors had higher AUCs, with model 2 achieving an AUC of 0.61 (95% CI 0.57 to 0.66). Including additional factors (model 3) did not further improve predictive ability (AUC 0.62; 95% CI 0.58 to 0.66). At predefined thresholds, model 2 achieved sensitivity of 73.7% (rule-out) and specificity of 83.5% (rule-in), with potential to reduce OGTT requirements (58.5%). At the Youden index cut-off, model 2 had the highest index (0.20), with sensitivity of 68.8% and specificity of 50.8%.
CONCLUSIONS: Early-pregnancy risk stratification using HbA1c combined with simple clinical predictors offers a pragmatic approach to streamline GDM screening among high-risk pregnant women. A dual-threshold strategy using model 2 could reduce reliance on universal OGTT while prioritising high-risk women for confirmatory testing.

articles.title: Psychological STress, Anxiety, and Depression After miscarriage in comparison to successful pregnancy and abortion: design and protocol for the observational cohort study STRADA.
articles.authors: Sorasto H, Mentula M, Räikkönen K et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Miscarriage occurs in 15%–20% of clinically recognised pregnancies. It may cause acute or prolonged psychological distress such as anxiety, depression and post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD). Data on symptom severity and duration after miscarriage are limited. This study assesses the prevalence, severity, risk and protective factors of acute and prolonged psychological symptoms as well as the impact of prolonged distress on future general and reproductive health.
METHODS AND ANALYSIS: This prospective observational cohort study enrols patients and partners at the time of miscarriage diagnosis. As controls, we enrol patients with spontaneous or assisted reproductive technology (ART)-conceived ongoing pregnancies and patients requesting induced abortion. Participants complete validated questionnaires within 1 week after enrolment, and at 3 and 9 months. The primary objective is to study the prevalence and severity of acute and prolonged psychological symptoms, including anxiety, depression and PTSD, to determine the need for psychological support. Secondary objectives include studying the effects of patient characteristics, socioeconomic background and previous physical and psychiatric health on symptom persistence and possible effects on subsequent pregnancies. Information is collected both through prospective self-reported questionnaires and retrospectively through national registries. A voluntary blood sample at enrolment is collected to search for endocrine, metabolic, inflammatory and genetic markers involved in miscarriage and psychiatric morbidity. Based on power calculations we plan to enrol 439 patients in the miscarriage and ongoing pregnancy groups and 220 patients in the induced abortion and ART groups. Partners are invited to participate.
ETHICS AND DISSEMINATION: The study will be performed in accordance with ethical principles consistent with the Declaration of Helsinki, ICH/GCPE6 (R2), European Union Clinical Trials Directive and applicable local regulatory requirements. The study has received approval from the ethics committee of the Helsinki University Hospital and from the Helsinki University Hospital. A collaborative agreement with the Helsinki Biobank has been made for depositing blood samples. The results of this study will be disseminated via publication in peer-reviewed journals.

articles.title: 100 Most-Cited Publications on Spontaneous Preterm Birth: A Bibliometric Analysis.
articles.journal: The journal of obstetrics and gynaecology research
articles.authors: Cao D, He W, Chen M
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This bibliometric analysis systematically maps the global research landscape of spontaneous preterm birth (SPTB) by examining the top 100 most-cited publications, identifying key contributors, prevailing trends, and emerging research frontiers.
METHODS: The top 100 most-cited SPTB articles were retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection. Bibliometric indicators-citations, authors, institutions, and journals-were extracted. Visualization and trend analysis were performed using VOSviewer, CiteSpace, and the R package "bibliometrix".
RESULTS: Publications spanned 1980-2021. The United States dominated (71% of articles). Leading institutions included the National Institutes of Health and Wayne State University. The American Journal of Obstetrics and Gynecology was the most prolific journal (28 articles; H-index: 28). Mean authors per article were 8.8, with 26% involving international collaboration. Six major research clusters emerged: clinical prevention and therapeutic interventions; epidemiology, psychosocial determinants, and pregnancy outcomes; infection, inflammation, and parturition pathways; maternal and obstetric characteristics; population-level adverse outcomes and oxidative stress; and cervical assessment, prediction, and procedural interventions. Within the citation-defined corpus, later-appearing terms included "short cervix," "expression," and "vaginal microbiome".
CONCLUSION: SPTB research has evolved from clinical risk factors toward a multidisciplinary field integrating epidemiology, molecular biology, and translational medicine. Continued interdisciplinary collaboration and advanced molecular/data-driven approaches hold promise for future breakthroughs.

articles.title: Menarche and ADHD: associations between puberty, ADHD traits and mental health in female adolescents.
articles.journal: Journal of child psychology and psychiatry, and allied disciplines
articles.authors: Friedel E, Grech L, Skvarc D et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Adolescents with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) may be more vulnerable to cooccurring mental health challenges during puberty, and some evidence suggests that puberty impacts ADHD traits. However, pubertal influences on psychological outcomes in female adolescents with ADHD are poorly understood. We investigated how menarche relates to ADHD traits and its potential moderation of associations between ADHD status or traits and mental health.
METHODS: Analyses used Adolescent Brain Cognitive DevelopmentSM Study data from baseline to wave 3 (N = 5,318; 100% female; baseline age M = 9.9, SD = 0.6; 52.3% non-Hispanic White). ADHD traits, internalising difficulties and externalising difficulties were measured using the Child Behavior Checklist. Bayesian generalised linear mixed models examined cross-sectional and longitudinal associations between menarche status and ADHD traits. Interactions between menarche status and ADHD status or traits as predictors of mental health outcomes were also investigated. In comparative analyses, breast development replaced menarche status.
RESULTS: ADHD traits did not differ between pre- and post-menarche adolescents in cross-sectional analyses, but post-menarche adolescents had higher ADHD traits the following year. Complete breast development (vs. not started) also predicted higher ADHD traits the next year. Interactions between menarche and ADHD status were not associated with mental health outcomes cross-sectionally or longitudinally. Positive associations between ADHD traits and mental health difficulties were marginally stronger in post-menarche adolescents. The association between higher wave 2 ADHD traits and greater wave 3 externalising difficulties was substantially stronger with more advanced breast development at wave 2.
CONCLUSIONS: Longitudinal findings provide preliminary evidence that more advanced gonadarche in early adolescence is prospectively associated with elevated ADHD trait expression in females when controlling for individual differences in ADHD trait levels. More advanced breast development may reflect physiological and psychosocial changes that could contribute to a stronger relationship between higher ADHD traits and greater subsequent externalising difficulties.

articles.title: Circulating Tumor DNA and Cell-Free DNA as Candidate Biomarkers After Image-Guided Locoregional Therapy in Hepatocellular Carcinoma and Colorectal Liver Metastases: A Systematic Review.
articles.journal: Journal of vascular and interventional radiology : JVIR
articles.authors: O'Sullivan NJ, Temperley HC, Mac Curtain BM et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To review ctDNA and cfDNA as biomarkers after locoregional therapy in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and colorectal liver metastases (CRLM).
MATERIALS AND METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, and Web of Science were searched (July 2026) for ctDNA/cfDNA studies in HCC or CRLM patients undergoing TACE, Y90, or ablation; Newcastle-Ottawa Scale assessed risk of bias.
RESULTS: Eleven studies were included (eight HCC, three CRLM; n≈820). Pre-treatment ctDNA mutations predicted survival after TACE (CTNNB1: HR 5.3, 95% CI 1.4-20.6; TP53: HR 5.3, 95% CI 1.4-10.1; KEAP1: HR 22.0, 95% CI 2.2-221.0). A cfDNA/ctDNA score stratified progression-free survival after TACE (1.3 vs 10.3 months; p=0.002). ctDNA predicted death after ablation in HCC (HR 2.6, 95% CI 1.5-4.7; p=0.001) and recurrence in CRLM (HR 2.97, 95% CI 1.47-6.03; P=0.003). Y90 evidence was limited.
CONCLUSION: CtDNA and cfDNA correlated with treatment outcomes after locoregional therapy; evidence is heterogeneous and biomarker-driven trials are required before clinical implementation.

articles.title: Sedentary behaviour and female urinary incontinence. A systematic review with subtype-specific analysis.
articles.authors: Pannozzo C, Cornu JN, Steenstrup B
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To systematically evaluate the association between sedentary behaviour and female urinary incontinence (UI), with emphasis on subtype-specific outcomes (stress UI [SUI], urgency UI [UUI], mixed UI [MUI]), assessment methods, and confounding factors.
METHOD: Systematic review following PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Observational studies (cross-sectional, cohort, case-control) published in English, French or Spanish (2010-2026) were identified via PubMed, Cochrane, and PEDro. Eligible studies assessed sedentary behaviour (objective/self-reported) and UI in women, excluding non-original research. Risk of bias was assessed using revised JBI tools, and evidence certainly was evaluated with GRADE.
RESULTS: Eight studies (n=35 - 10,768 participants) met inclusion criteria. Greater sedentary exposure was generally associated with higher UI prevalence or severity, particularly for UUI (low-certainty evidence). Associations with UUI and UI severity appeared more consistent in accelerometry-based studies than in studies using self-reported measures, but this limited evidence does not establish that objective measures yield stronger associations. For SUI, findings were inconsistent (very low-certainty evidence). Adjusted analyses (controlling for age, BMI, parity, physical activity) often attenuated associations, though some remained significant. Heterogeneity in UI definitions, sedentary assessment, and confounders limited meta-analysis.
CONCLUSION: Sedentary behaviour appears associated with UUI in women, but the direction of the association cannot be established and reverse causation is plausible. Evidence for SUI is inconclusive. Prospective studies using objective measures and subtype-specific outcomes are needed to establish temporal ordering.

articles.title: Association of vaginal microecological indicators with neutrophil extracellular trap markers in vaginal secretions across cervical lesion grades.
articles.journal: Clinica chimica acta; international journal of clinical chemistry
articles.authors: Wang Y, Gao J, Jin X et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Vaginal microenvironment disorder is related to cervical lesion development, and neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) participate in tumour progression. Whether vaginal microecology indicators are associated with NET markers in vaginal secretions has not been examined.
OBJECTIVE: To quantify the association between vaginal microecology indicators and vaginal secretion NET marker levels across cervical lesion grades.
METHODS: Two hundred women formed control, cervicitis, low-grade and high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion groups (n = 50, 50, 51, 49). Thirteen vaginal microecology indicators and HPV genotype were recorded. In 35 stratified vaginal secretion supernatants, myeloperoxidase-DNA (MPO-DNA), citrullinated histone H3 (CitH3) and cell-free DNA (cfDNA) were measured. Spearman correlation and linear regression were applied. NET scores in GSE63514 and GSE7803 were derived by ssGSEA.
RESULTS: Individual microecology indicators did not differ across groups after false discovery rate (FDR) correction. MPO-DNA and Cit-H3 were elevated in HPV-positive groups versus controls (P ≤ 0.003) without differing among lesion groups. Leukocyte esterase correlated with MPO-DNA (rho = 0.528, FDR = 0.037) and Cit-H3 (rho = 0.455, FDR = 0.049), and remained associated with MPO-DNA after adjustment for leukocyte grade (partial rho = 0.441, P = 0.009). In GSE63514, NET score increased with lesion grade (P = 0.003) and correlated with neutrophil infiltration (rho = 0.547, P < 0.001), which was not replicated in GSE7803 (trend P = 0.623).
CONCLUSION: Vaginal inflammatory indicators, particularly leukocyte esterase, are positively associated with vaginal secretion MPO-DNA levels, reflecting local neutrophil-related inflammation rather than a mediating link in cervical lesion progression.

articles.title: Beyond Folate: Non-Folate Risk Factors in Neural Tube Defect Pathogenesis.
articles.journal: American journal of obstetrics & gynecology MFM
articles.authors: Beals C, Weiss H, Kunda H et al.
articles.abstract: Globally, an estimated 214,000-322,000 infants are born each year with a neural tube defect (NTD), which represents a spectrum of disease severity. The landmark discovery of folic acid in the early 1990s reduced open NTD prevalence by nearly 30%, but closed NTD prevalence rates remain unchanged. This suggests an incompletely solved mechanism of action. Current prevention efforts target open NTDs while other forms of NTDs remain less understood. This review synthesizes evidence from 74 peer-reviewed English-language studies assessing factors associated with NTDs beyond folic acid. Results are organized across two domains: genetic pathways and environmental exposures with environmental exposures encompassing A) general exposures, B) iatrogenic exposures, and C) metabolic and dietary factors. NTDs are biologically heterogeneous, and it has become clear that folic acid supplementation and fortification alone is unlikely to eliminate their global incidence. Additional research, prevention efforts, and multidisciplinary strategies are necessary to reduce NTD burden.

articles.title: Characteristics and severe maternal morbidity associated with penicillin allergy among pregnant people.
articles.journal: American journal of obstetrics & gynecology MFM
articles.authors: Bayard KE, Reyes DR, Rao NA et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Penicillin allergy is commonly reported during pregnancy and may influence antibiotic selection for obstetric care. However, severe maternal morbidity at delivery among pregnant individuals with penicillin allergy continues to be understudied.
OBJECTIVE: To assess clinico-obstetric characteristics and severe maternal morbidity at delivery associated with penicillin allergy among pregnant people.
STUDY DESIGN: This serial cross-sectional study queried the Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality's Healthcare Cost and Utilization Project's National Inpatient Sample in the United States. The study population included 24,976,627 hospital deliveries from 2016 to 2022. Exposure was a diagnosis code of penicillin allergy, identified per the American Academy of Allergy Asthma and Immunology and the American College of Allergy, Asthma and Immunology schemas. The primary outcome measure was severe maternal morbidity, identified based on the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention definition. The exposure-outcome association was assessed with propensity score-adjustment model.
RESULTS: A total of 729,475 (2.9%) deliveries had a diagnosis code of penicillin allergy with a numerical increase in prevalence from 2.5% in 2016-2018 to 3.5% in 2021-2022 (adjusted-prevalence rate ratio [aPR] 1.35, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.35 to 1.36). The prevalence rate of penicillin allergy exceeded 5% among pregnant people with asthma (5.5%) exhibiting the largest association among the assessed clinico-obstetric characteristics (aPR 1.85, 95%CI 1.84 to 1.87), followed by Group B Streptococcus carrier status (aPR 1.52, 95%CI 1.52 to 1.53). In a classification-tree model, White people with asthma who were Group B Streptococcus carrier had the highest penicillin allergy prevalence rate (8.3%). Pregnancy with penicillin allergy was associated with higher incidence of severe maternal morbidity at delivery compared to those without penicillin allergy (any composite, 108.3 vs 81.9 per 10,000 deliveries, adjusted-incidence rate ratio [aIR] 1.19, 95%CI 1.16 to 1.21). In exploratory analysis, penicillin allergy was associated with sepsis (19.6 vs 11.0 per 10,000 deliveries, aIR 1.68, 95%CI 1.59 to 1.77) and shock (11.1 vs 7.1 per 10,000 deliveries, aIR 1.49, 95%CI 1.39 to 1.60).
CONCLUSION: The results of this nationwide assessment in the United States suggest that penicillin allergy may be associated with high-risk pregnancy characteristics and severe maternal morbidity at…

articles.title: Prognostic accuracy of the maternal serum IGFBP4/SHBG ratio for spontaneous preterm birth in asymptomatic pregnancies: a systematic review.
articles.journal: American journal of obstetrics & gynecology MFM
articles.authors: Dela Cruz FSE, Wapano REB, Garcia PMS et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This review evaluated the prognostic accuracy of the maternal serum insulin-like growth factor binding protein 4 to sex hormone-binding globulin (IGFBP4/SHBG) ratio for spontaneous preterm birth in asymptomatic pregnancies.
DATA SOURCES: PubMed, Scopus, and EBSCO were searched from inception to October 23, 2024; reference lists were hand-searched, and one study was identified during peer review. The review was registered in PROSPERO (CRD42024605191).
STUDY ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA: Cohort, case-cohort, nested case-control, and randomized studies that measured the serum IGFBP4/SHBG ratio in pregnancy and reported spontaneous preterm birth.
STUDY APPRAISAL AND SYNTHESIS METHODS: Two reviewers independently extracted data and assessed risk of bias (QUADAS-2), a third reviewer resolved disagreements, and large language models cross-checked the results. We derived each study's 2×2 table and recorded the threshold, test form, outcome definition, cohort overlap, and funding. Because few studies had 2×2 data and two shared participants, study-level estimates were presented in a paired forest plot rather than pooled. Certainty was rated with GRADE for test accuracy.
RESULTS: Seven studies from five countries (2016 to 2024) were included. Two screen-and-treat studies, one randomized, were synthesized narratively, and two studies did not report 2×2 data. For spontaneous preterm birth, the ratio alone had sensitivities of 0.75 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.43-0.95) and 0.52 (95% CI, 0.40-0.64) and specificities of 0.74 (95% CI, 0.52-0.90) and 0.64 (95% CI, 0.61-0.66) in two studies that shared participants. In a third study, the ratio plus a clinical factor had a sensitivity of 0.50 (95% CI, 0.44-0.55) and a specificity of 0.71 (95% CI, 0.67-0.75) for all-cause preterm birth. A bivariate model could not be reliably estimated, so no pooled estimate is reported. All seven studies were funded by the test developer or included its employees among the authors. Certainty of evidence was very low.
CONCLUSIONS: The maternal serum IGFBP4/SHBG ratio shows modest prognostic accuracy for spontaneous preterm birth, based on few, partly overlapping studies funded by or involving the test developer. Accuracy data alone neither establish nor exclude clinical benefit; decisions about screening should rest on randomized evidence and independent validation.

articles.title: Effects of insulin resistance on pregnancy outcomes and complications in women with polycystic ovary syndrome.
articles.journal: The Journal of international medical research
articles.authors: Hua Z, Shen L, Chen WN
articles.abstract: ObjectiveTo investigate whether early-pregnancy insulin resistance in women with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is associated with adverse maternal pregnancy complications and neonatal/perinatal outcomes after adjustment for common metabolic confounders.MethodsThis retrospective cohort study included 168 pregnant women diagnosed with PCOS who were consecutively enrolled at Tongren Hospital from July 2023 to December 2024. Of these, 52 patients with insulin resistance (homeostasis model assessment of insulin resistance ≥ 2.77) were assigned to the PCOS with insulin resistance group, whereas 116 patients without insulin resistance were assigned to the PCOS without insulin resistance group. Multivariable binary logistic regression was performed to estimate adjusted associations between insulin resistance and gestational diabetes mellitus, adjusting for age, body mass index, family history of diabetes, and conception mode.ResultsBody mass index was significantly higher in the PCOS with insulin resistance group (p = 0.02). No significant differences were found in thyroid function indices or blood lipid levels across trimesters, neonatal birth weight, or perinatal outcomes (all p > 0.05). The incidence of gestational diabetes mellitus was higher in the PCOS with insulin resistance group than in the PCOS without insulin resistance group (30.77% vs. 17.24%, p = 0.04). After adjustment for potential confounders, insulin resistance (adjusted odds ratio = 2.09, 95% confidence interval: 1.02-4.28, p = 0.044) and higher body mass index (odds ratio = 1.19 per kg/m2, p = 0.038) remained independently associated with increased odds of gestational diabetes mellitus. No significant differences were observed in gestational hypertension, polyhydramnios, or premature rupture of membranes.ConclusionsIn this observational cohort, early-pregnancy insulin resistance was associated with a higher incidence of gestational diabetes mellitus after adjustment for body mass index and other confounders. These findings do not establish a causal relationship. Early standardized screening and targeted metabolic management of insulin resistance may help reduce gestational diabetes mellitus incidence; however, prospective studies are warranted to confirm this association.

articles.title: Diagnostic value of maternal serum prokineticin-1 for predicting placenta accreta spectrum and adverse maternal outcomes.
articles.authors: Oğlak SC, Ölmez F, Bağlı İ et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate maternal serum prokineticin-1 (PROK1) levels in women with placenta accreta spectrum (PAS) of varying degrees, to compare them with cases of placenta previa (PP) and uncomplicated healthy pregnancies, and to determine whether this biomarker can predict disease severity and clinical outcomes.
METHODS: In this observational case-control study involving 153 pregnant women, 54 had singleton pregnancies with PP complicated by PAS, 51 had PP without PAS, and 48 were healthy gestational age-matched singleton controls. Demographic and clinical data, maternal and neonatal outcomes, and maternal serum PROK1 levels were collected for all participants. A receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve was generated to assess the sensitivity and specificity of PROK1, and the optimal cut-off value was determined using the Youden index. Associations between PROK1 levels and continuous clinical variables were analyzed using Spearman's rank correlation.
RESULTS: The mean maternal serum PROK1 level was markedly elevated in both the PAS group (9.29±10.53 pg/mL) and the PP group (6.65±2.88 pg/mL) compared with the control group (3.19±0.81 pg/mL, p<0.001). A cut-off value of 6.81 pg/mL for maternal serum PROK1 distinguished pregnancies complicated by PAS with a sensitivity of 96.3% and a specificity of 97.9%. A statistically significant negative linear correlation was found between maternal serum PROK1 levels and gestational week at delivery (r=-0.598, p<0.001). Additionally, a statistically significant positive correlation was observed between maternal serum PROK1 concentrations and the duration of maternal hospital stay after delivery (r=0.511, p<0.001). Women who required interventions such as transfusion, ICU admission, arterial ligation, uterine resection, or hysterectomy had significantly higher mean PROK1 levels than those who did not.
CONCLUSION: PROK1 is a crucial factor associated with PAS pregnancies, and an increased PROK1 expression in these cases may alter trophoblast function and placentation. The increased PROK1 expression may be considered a potential indicator of disease severity and adverse maternal outcomes.

articles.title: Contribution of in vitro fertilization to multiple births in South Korea: a nationwide cohort study.
articles.authors: Kim S, Kim T, Oh JW et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Multiple births expose mothers and infants to disproportionate risks and incur substantial healthcare costs. We quantified the contribution of in vitro fertilization (IVF) to multiple births after universal national insurance coverage for IVF was introduced in South Korea.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study used the Korean National Health Insurance Service Mother-Child Linked Database and included 403,708 deliveries from October 2018 to December 2023. IVF exposure was identified from procedure claims, and plurality was determined from linked infant records. We estimated the adjusted relative risk (RR) of multiple births for IVF versus non-IVF deliveries and the population-attributable fraction (PAF) of multiple births attributable to IVF, overall and by age group.
RESULTS: Of 403,708 deliveries, 65,442 (16.2%) involved IVF; this proportion increased from 9.4% in 2018 to 22.6% in 2023. Multiple births occurred in 21.9% of IVF deliveries and 1.9% of non-IVF deliveries. The overall adjusted RR for IVF was 8.67 (95% confidence interval [CI]: 8.40-8.94). Age-specific adjusted RRs were highest in women aged 25-29 years (12.37; 95% CI: 11.09-13.80) and lowest in those aged 40-49 years (7.43; 95% CI: 6.68-8.26). The overall PAF was 55.4%, driven largely by women aged 40-49 years (66.1%). In women aged 30-34 years, the PAF was 46.8%.
CONCLUSION: IVF accounts for more than half of multiple births in South Korea, with a substantial contribution among women aged ≤35 years. These findings support policies that promote elective single embryo transfer.

articles.title: CircRNA SNX11 promotes endometrial cell proliferation through GPER1 by sponging hsa-miR-1343-3p.
articles.authors: Shi Y, Liang X, Li M et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Approximately 15% of couples of reproductive age experience infertility. In vitro fertilization (IVF) is the most useful treatment for patients with infertility. However, repeated implantation failure (RIF) is one of the most difficult challenges for the success of IVF, caused by poor endometrial receptivity due to decreased endometrial cell proliferation. This study aimed to investigate the mechanism regulating endometrial cell proliferation to overcome RIF.
METHODS: Hub genes involved in RIF were identified by RNA sequencing for endometrial tissues. The regulatory effects of circular RNA (circRNA) and microRNA (miRNA) in human endometrial stromal cells (hESCs) were determined using miRNA pulldown and dual-luciferase reporter gene assays. Cell proliferation was detected using a Cell Counting Kit-8 assay.
RESULTS: G protein-coupled estrogen receptor 1 (GPER1) expression was dramatically downregulated in endometrial tissues obtained from patients with RIF, suggesting that GPER1 might be a hub gene involved in RIF. Additionally, circRNA SNX11 increases GPER1 expression via hsa-miR-1343-3p in hESCs. Additionally, circRNA SNX11 promotes cell proliferation, reduces apoptosis, and modulates RIF-related pathways through GPER1 by sponging hsa-miR-1343-3p in hESCs.
CONCLUSION: This study reveals that circRNA SNX11 facilitates endometrial cell proliferation by upregulating GPER1 by sponging hsa-miR-1343-3p, providing novel therapeutic targets to overcome RIF.

articles.title: Oral calcium intake during labor in healthy women: a pharmacokinetic study.
articles.authors: Blake L, Michel G, Callihan P et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Recent studies suggest that intravenous calcium may reduce postpartum hemorrhage due to uterine atony. However, intravenous lines may be unavailable in low-resource settings. We thus evaluated the time course of change in serum ionized calcium after pregnant women ingested commonly available oral calcium formulations.
METHODS: Term, laboring patients 18-45 years of age received oral calcium carbonate (1200 mg). Blood samples were obtained to measure ionized calcium before and after ingestion. Following interim analysis demonstrating minimal effect, the protocol was amended to calcium citrate (1250 mg). Enrollment was stopped at 20 of 60 planned participants for futility without a prespecified statistical futility boundary.
RESULTS: We observed minimal to no increase in serum ionized calcium in ten patients who received calcium carbonate and eight patients who received calcium citrate.
CONCLUSION: The package insert-recommended dose of two oral calcium formulations failed to meaningfully increase serum ionized calcium in laboring patients. Future studies should center on intravenous calcium until alternative oral calcium dosing or formulations successfully increase maternal ionized calcium.

articles.title: Prenatal exposure to perchlorate, thiocyanate, and nitrate: Associations with maternal thyroid function and child neurodevelopment in the MARBLES cohort.
articles.authors: Jang H, Bennett DH, Hoofnagle AN et al.
articles.abstract: Perchlorate, thiocyanate, and nitrate are widespread environmental anions that inhibit iodide uptake via the sodium-iodide symporter (NIS), potentially disrupting maternal thyroid hormone production. Maternal thyroid dysfunction during pregnancy has been linked to child neurodevelopment, but the interrelationships among prenatal exposure to these NIS inhibitors, maternal thyroid function, and child neurodevelopment remain unclear. We analyzed 195 mother-child pairs from the MARBLES prospective pregnancy cohort, enriched for familial likelihood of autism. Prenatal urinary perchlorate, thiocyanate, and nitrate and maternal serum thyroid function tests (TFTs) were measured during pregnancy. Child neurodevelopmental outcomes were classified as autism (n = 49), non-typically developing (non-TD, n = 24), or TD (n = 122). Robust Poisson regression was used to estimate relative risks, and exploratory single-mediator analyses were conducted to evaluate potential indirect effects through maternal thyroid function. Primary analyses detected no statistically significant associations between prenatal NIS inhibitor exposures and child neurodevelopment. Higher nitrate and perchlorate-equivalent concentrations were associated with increased maternal total thyroxine levels after false discovery rate correction. Exploratory mediation analyses did not detect statistically significant indirect effects through maternal TFTs. However, these findings were inconclusive given the limited statistical power to detect small indirect effects. Overall, prenatal NIS inhibitor exposures were associated with selected maternal thyroid markers but not significantly associated with child neurodevelopment in the current analytical sample. Larger studies are needed to further evaluate the potential role of maternal thyroid function in these associations.

articles.title: Anti-CD38 therapy in kidney allograft antibody-mediated rejection and microvascular inflammation: a systematic review and evidence map.
articles.authors: Liang C, Wang C, Yin S et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Anti-CD38 agents have been used to treat antibody-mediated rejection (AMR) after kidney transplantation, but the evidence consists of one small randomized trial, uncontrolled case series, conference abstracts, and case reports. We systematically mapped clinical, biological, and safety outcomes across individual agents and AMR-related phenotypes.
METHODS: We searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science Core Collection, Ovid MEDLINE, the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, and ClinicalTrials.gov, with an updated search through August 25, 2026. We included kidney-transplant studies of felzartamab, daratumumab, or isatuximab that reported clinical, biological, or safety outcomes. Full articles, conference abstracts, extensions, and companion reports from the same study were linked. Clinical outcomes comprised kidney function, proteinuria, graft failure, and survival; biological outcomes comprised histology, molecular AMR, donor-derived cell-free DNA (dd-cfDNA), and donor-specific antibody (DSA). Studies with inseparable mixed phenotypes were retained only as contextual evidence. We used RoB 2 for the randomized trial, the corresponding JBI tools for case series and case reports, and outcome-specific GRADE assessments. Evidence was stratified by agent, design, phenotype separability, and concomitant treatment, without pooled effects across studies or agents.
RESULTS: Thirty-seven reports were included, comprising one 22-participant randomized felzartamab trial, uncontrolled daratumumab studies and case reports, and one four-recipient isatuximab case series. Patient overlap with larger cohorts remained unconfirmed for five daratumumab case reports or case series. Across the felzartamab main trial and extension, 15 unique participants received felzartamab. At week 24, morphologic AMR resolved in 9/11 felzartamab recipients and 2/10 placebo recipients who completed biopsy; after classifying the placebo recipient with graft failure as not having remission, the result was 9/11 versus 2/11. The between-group mean difference in microvascular inflammation score was -1.95 (95% confidence interval [CI], -2.97 to -0.92). These measures were exploratory secondary or surrogate outcomes. The between-group difference in annualized estimated glomerular filtration rate slope at week 52 was 4.14 mL/min/1.73 m2/year (95% CI, -3.20 to 11.48). During the 52-week randomized study, infusion-related reactions occurred in 8/11 felzartamab and 0/11 placebo…

articles.title: Air pollution and polycystic ovary metabolic syndrome (PMOS) in a heavily industrialized Middle Eastern city: A cross-sectional study.
articles.authors: Karimi B, Kord M, Shokarpour M et al.
articles.abstract: Globally, polycystic ovary metabolic syndrome (PMOS) affects 5% to 20% of women of childbearing age. Despite the high burden of ambient air pollution in the Middle East, epidemiological evidence linking long-term exposure to PMOS remains limited. This cross-sectional study examined associations between long-term residential exposure to criteria air pollutants and PMOS prevalence in Arak, Iran. We enrolled 301 women (153 PMOS cases, 148 non-PMOS controls) from gynecology clinics (April 2024-March 2025). Long-term (365-day) residential exposures were estimated using inverse distance weighting (IDW) interpolation from three fixed monitoring stations. Modified Poisson regression was prioritized to estimate prevalence ratios (PRs), given the high prevalence of the outcome. Robustness was assessed via alternative exposure windows (90-day, 30-day), extreme value exclusion, and propensity score matching. Women with PMOS had significantly higher exposures to PM2.5 (mean difference: 3.00 μg/m3), PM10 (7.50 μg/m3), NO2 (2.96 ppb), and SO2 (11.35 ppb) (all p ≤ 0.025). Per 1-SD increase, adjusted PRs were: PM2.5 = 1.22 (95% CI: 1.09-1.35; p = 0.001); PM10 = 1.23 (95% CI: 1.09-1.36; p = 0.001); NO2 = 1.21 (95% CI: 1.07-1.33; p = 0.003); and SO2 = 1.15 (95% CI: 1.01-1.28; p = 0.032). All sensitivity analyses supported the robustness of these associations. Exploratory analyses suggested specificity to menstrual/ovulatory dysfunction.
