This first Middle Eastern study reports statistical associations between long-term PM2.5, PM10, NO2, and SO2 exposure and PMOS prevalence in a high-pollution industrial setting. Because of the cross-sectional design, these findings cannot establish causality and are strictly hypothesis-generating, highlighting the urgent need for prospective cohort studies.

articles.title: Fertility and pregnancy concerns and needs after fertility-sparing surgery in young women with gynecological cancer and their partners: A qualitative study.
articles.authors: Stroeken Y, van den Berg MC, Zusterzeel PLM et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Many young women treated for gynecological cancer are assumed to experience long-term concerns about fertility and pregnancy, and psychological distress. However, evidence on patients' post-treatment reproductive concerns, decisions to pursue pregnancy, and oncofertility needs is limited. This study aims to provide insight into the perspectives of women treated with fertility-sparing surgery (FSS) for gynecological cancer and their partners.
METHODS: Women and their partners were selected for semi-structured interviews from our previously performed questionnaire study through purposive sampling based on self-reported reproductive concerns and pregnancy attempts. Interviews were coded and analyzed using a framework approach until data saturation was reached.
RESULTS: Data saturation was achieved after 32 interviews with 24 participants and eight partners. Three participants did not pursue pregnancy and decided not to in the future. Participants expressed reproductive concerns and encounter post-treatment challenges, including a sense of time pressure, fear of cancer recurrence, and a common need for assisted reproductive techniques. Nearly all participants expressed their need for post-operative fertility counseling, although the preferred timing for this support varied. Partners considered their primary role as providing support throughout the treatment (decision) process, deciding to conceive and pursuing pregnancy. Some partners emphasized the importance, but lack of partner support.
CONCLUSIONS: Women treated with FSS for gynecological cancer and their partners face persistent uncertainty regarding fertility and pregnancy, yet most women remain motivated to pursue pregnancy. Partners play a supportive role, but also have unmet needs. These findings highlight that reproductive issues should be systematically incorporated into routine clinical care pathways.

articles.title: Second Stage Caesarean Section and Subsequent Preterm Birth.
articles.journal: The Australian & New Zealand journal of obstetrics & gynaecology
articles.ta: Aust N Z J Obstet Gynaecol
articles.authors: Lau K, El-Achi V, Yang JM
articles.abstract: Caesarean section during the second stage of labour has been associated with an increased risk of subsequent preterm birth. This risk has been hypothesised to be a product of inadvertent cervical trauma, compromising the integrity of the cervix in the subsequent pregnancy. Understanding the biological complications of this procedure may help guide clinician decision-making to reduce future risk of preterm birth within this population.

articles.title: A high-resolution wireless sensing platform for the characterization of urodynamic events in murine models.
articles.authors: Cortina RE, Delgado Lezama R, Pérez-Escamirosa F et al.
articles.abstract: Cystometry in murine models is fundamental for understanding lower urinary tract dysfunctions. However, the high cost of commercial equipment and the mechanical limitations of wired systems, which can introduce electronic noise and restrict mobility, often hinder implementation and can compromise animal welfare. This work presents CISTREC, a low-cost, high-signal-integrity wireless pressure monitoring platform designed for preclinical research. The system integrates a digital sensor with on-chip signal conditioning and a 24-bit digital output, enabling direct digitization at the sensor and minimizing susceptibility to electromagnetic interference. Data transmission was performed via Bluetooth Low Energy 5.0 (BLE), providing galvanic isolation and portability. Validation included in vitro characterization from 0 to 160 cmH2O, and in vivo evaluation in an overactive bladder (OAB) model induced by acetic acid in Wistar rats. In vitro tests demonstrated a coefficient of determination of 0.999946, a root-mean-square error of 0.3454 cmH2O, an effective experimental resolution of 0.0742 cmH2O, and a full-scale signal-to-noise ratio (SNRFS) of 76.23 dB. In the in vivo experiment, the high resolution enabled accurate capture of biomarkers, including high-frequency oscillations (HFOs) and non-voiding contractions (NVCs). Significant changes were observed in the pathological model, including a reduction in the inter-contraction interval and a decrease in bladder compliance. The CISTREC system achieves metrological performance in line with reported specifications of high-end commercial systems, at a low cost. Its wireless architecture and high sensitivity facilitate access to advanced urodynamics, promoting the principle of refinement in animal experimentation without compromising rigorous scientific standards.

articles.title: A Retrospective Audit of Maternal Bacteraemia in a Tertiary Referral Maternity Hospital in Brisbane, Australia From 2015 to 2024.
articles.journal: The Australian & New Zealand journal of obstetrics & gynaecology
articles.ta: Aust N Z J Obstet Gynaecol
articles.authors: Morton A, Parkes-Smith J
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Maternal infection is a major cause of pregnancy-related maternal morbidity and mortality in Australia.
OBJECTIVES: To determine the prevalence, microbiology, probable source, clinical characteristics, laboratory results, time to antibiotic therapy, reasons for intensive care admission, and maternal morbidity and mortality of maternal bacteraemia at a tertiary referral maternity hospital in Brisbane, Australia, over a ten-year period.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: A retrospective review of pregnant patients with positive blood cultures between January 2015 and December 2024 at a tertiary level obstetric hospital in Brisbane, Australia, was performed.
RESULTS: There were 59 patients with pathogenic organisms grown on blood cultures (0.96 per 1000 deliveries) and 29 patients with presumed contaminants. Physical signs and laboratory investigations were not useful in differentiating between patients whose blood cultures grew pathogenic bacteraemia, those which grew presumed contaminants, and those whose blood cultures were negative. The predominant bacterial species were Streptococcus species and Escherichia coli (E. coli). Despite 57 of the 59 patients with pathogenic bacteraemia receiving antibiotics and fluid resuscitation within 60 min of presentation, 10 patients were admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU), principally because of hypotension developing 6-24 h after initial treatment. Seven of the 10 ICU admissions were due to E. coli bacteraemia, four secondary to urosepsis, and three secondary to chorioamnionitis. There were no maternal deaths.
CONCLUSIONS: A continuing policy of early identification of possible maternal infection, and prompt antibiotic therapy and resuscitation are indicated. Despite expeditious management, a significant proportion of patients deteriorated and required admission to an intensive care unit, emphasising the importance of close observation following initial antibiotic therapy, particularly in patients with suspected urosepsis and/or E. coli bacteraemia.

articles.title: Redefining the EPCAM Phenotype: Deletion Architecture Determines Lynch Syndrome Cancer Risk.
articles.authors: Kohler K, Marsh APL, Hernandez F et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To characterize the cancer phenotype and clinical presentation across molecularly distinct EPCAM deletion subgroups and determine how the phenotype varies with MSH2 involvement.
METHODS: We retrospectively evaluated 662 unrelated probands undergoing hereditary cancer multigene panel testing (MGPT) with isolated EPCAM full-gene deletions (n = 22), isolated EPCAM 3' deletions (n = 96), contiguous EPCAM full-gene deletions extending into MSH2 (n = 64), contiguous EPCAM 3' deletions extending into MSH2 (n = 116), MSH2 gross deletions (n = 155), and MSH2 nonsense/frameshift (ns/fs) variants (n = 209). Lynch syndrome (LS)-associated cancer prevalence, tumor spectrum, and PREMM5 scores were compared across cohorts. Multivariable logistic regression estimated cancer-specific associations relative to a MGPT-negative reference cohort.
RESULTS: Isolated EPCAM full-gene deletions, comprising 18.6% of observed isolated EPCAM deletions, were not significantly associated with LS-associated cancers. The LS-associated cancer prevalence was 13.6% in this cohort, compared with 54.6% with isolated EPCAM 3' deletions and 64.1%-72.2% in MSH2-involving cohorts (P < .001). Relative to MGPT-negative individuals, isolated EPCAM 3' deletions were strongly associated with colorectal cancer (odds ratio [OR], 17.59; P < .001) but not endometrial cancer (OR, 0.76; P = .790). MSH2-involving cohorts demonstrated strong associations with both colorectal (ORs, 8.50-16.03; P < .001) and endometrial cancers (ORs, 17.31-30.47; P < .001).
CONCLUSION: These findings provide new insights into the molecular and clinical heterogeneity of germline deletions involving EPCAM. Expanded detection across the full EPCAM gene and its 3' region distinguishes isolated full-gene deletions, which do not disrupt downstream MSH2 and are not associated with LS phenotypes, from isolated 3' deletions with a colorectal-predominant phenotype, and contiguous EPCAM-MSH2 deletions with an MSH2-like LS phenotype. Precise delineation of EPCAM deletion boundaries and MSH2 involvement define three clinically relevant risk groups and support more precise risk assessment, counseling, and surveillance.

articles.title: Enablers and barriers to human papillomavirus vaccination implementation among key stakeholders in Ethiopia: A qualitative study.
articles.authors: Assefa KT, Worku AG, Muche AA et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination is an effective and lifesaving intervention against cervical cancer. However, achieving high, equitable, and sustainable uptake remains a significant challenge in low-resource settings, including Ethiopia. Therefore, this study aimed to explore the enablers and barriers to HPV vaccination implementation in Ethiopia.
METHODS: An interpretive descriptive qualitative design was employed in purposively selected settings representing diverse socio-ecological contexts (Afar, Amhara, Addis Ababa, and Dire Dawa). Six focus group discussions were conducted with adolescent girls (n = 14), parents of eligible adolescent girls (n = 14), and community representatives (n = 14). In addition, nineteen key informant interviews (KIIs) were conducted with healthcare providers, Expanded Programme on Immunization (EPI) coordinators, and technical advisors from governmental and non-governmental organizations. Data were analysed using a combined deductive-inductive content analysis guided by the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research (CFIR 2.0).
RESULTS: Multiple interacting factors influenced HPV vaccination implementation in Ethiopia, categorised as enablers and barriers across community, health system, and policy levels. Enablers included the Perceived Vaccine Attributes and Delivery Adaptability, Supportive Policy and Multisectoral Strategic Partnerships, Socio-cultural and Belief-based Drivers, and Health System Readiness and Workforce Motivation. However, several barriers limited implementation, including Suspicions About Targeting 9-14-year-old Girls and Consent-related Administrative Obstacles, Pervasive Misinformation and Cognitive Resistance, Health System Resource Constraints and Coordination Gaps, Donor Dependency Risks and Financial Sustainability Concerns, and Structural Access Constraints and Equity Gaps.
CONCLUSIONS: While policy shifts, external strategic partnerships, and frontline worker dedication have accelerated vaccine reach, the long-term sustainability of Ethiopia's HPV vaccination program remains constrained by multi-level barriers. Progress toward the global 2030 cervical cancer elimination targets requires trust-building risk-communication strategies to counter fertility myths, simplified consent procedures, targeted domestic resource mobilization, and context-specific delivery models tailored to underserved pastoralist and urban sub-populations.

articles.title: Female sexual dysfunction in premenopausal women with diabetes mellitus in northern Nigeria: A cross-sectional study from two tertiary hospitals examining associations with glycaemic control and reproductive hormones.
articles.authors: Damagum FM, Hassan AH, Uloko AE et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Female sexual dysfunction (FSD) is a recognised complication of diabetes mellitus (DM), but evidence on its clinical and biological correlates in sub-Saharan Africa remains limited. FSD is defined as a disorder characterized by disturbances in sexual desire, arousal, orgasm, and/or pain that causes interpersonal difficulty or distress. This study examined associations between glycaemic control, reproductive hormonal status, and FSD among premenopausal women with diabetes in northern Nigeria.
METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional study among 180 premenopausal women aged 18-45 years attending diabetes clinics at two tertiary hospitals in Kano, Nigeria. Sexual function was assessed using the Female Sexual Function Index (FSFI), with scores ≤26 indicating FSD. Glycaemic control was measured using glycated haemoglobin (HbA1c), categorised as optimal (≤7.0%) or suboptimal (>7.0%). Reproductive hormones (FSH, LH, Oestrogen, testosterone, prolactin, and progesterone) were measured at phase-specific points of the menstrual cycle. Multivariable logistic regression models were used to assess associations with FSD, and linear regression models were used to examine associations with FSFI domain scores.
RESULTS: Overall, 51.7% of participants screened positive for FSD. Suboptimal glycaemic control was associated with higher odds of FSD (adjusted odds ratio [AOR] 2.80; 95% CI 1.05-7.72). It was also associated with lower orgasm (β -0.77; p = 0.032) and satisfaction (β -0.88; p = 0.003) scores. No statistically significant associations were observed between reproductive hormonal imbalance (including FSH, LH, Oestrogen, testosterone, prolactin, and progesterone) and FSD or FSFI domain scores.
CONCLUSIONS: FSD was common among premenopausal women with diabetes in this setting. Suboptimal glycaemic control was associated with FSD and with lower orgasm and satisfaction scores, while reproductive hormonal measures were not associated with FSD. These findings provide evidence on clinical correlates of FSD in a sub-Saharan African population.

articles.title: Holistic Approaches to Postpartum Mental and Pelvic Healthcare for Home-Based Providers.
articles.authors: Woods L
articles.abstract: The transition into the postpartum period brings deep physical, emotional, and relational shifts, placing individuals at a significant risk for both pelvic floor dysfunction (PFD) and perinatal mood and anxiety disorders (PMADs). Despite their prevalence, symptoms of both PFD and PMADs are frequently overlooked during routine postpartum follow-up visits, ultimately compromising maternal role performance, daily functioning, and family well-being. Home-based health practitioners (HHPs) can address these gaps during home visits by applying trauma-informed assessment strategies, using brief validated screening tools, and establishing a safe environment for open discussion. This article defines the intersection of PFD and PMADs, describes a methodology for evidence-based home intervention, and provides practical strategies to enhance functional postpartum recovery in the home setting.

articles.title: Prognostic Significance of Early Donor-derived Cell-free DNA Trajectories After Kidney Transplantation.
articles.authors: Sureshkumar K, Klein JA, Kumar D et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Early post-transplant elevations in donor-derived cell-free DNA are often attributed to ischemia-reperfusion injury, with uncertain prognostic significance. We assessed whether donor-derived cell-free DNA (dd-cfDNA) results during the first 4 mo post-transplantation are associated with long-term graft outcomes.
METHODS: We analyzed 1137 kidney transplant recipients enrolled in the prospective multicenter Kidney Outcomes AlloSure Registry. Recipients were categorized into 4 trajectory groups based on dd-cfDNA measurements obtained within the first 4 mo post-transplant: consistently low, transient-elevation, late-elevation, and persistent-elevation. Associations with donor-specific antibody (DSA) development, rejection, graft dysfunction, and graft loss were evaluated over 3 y using hazard regression, with multivariable models adjusted for calculated Panel Reactive Antibody (cPRA) and retransplant.
RESULTS: Among the 1137 recipients, 83.7% exhibited consistently low dd-cfDNA, 9.8% transient-elevation, 3.2% late-elevation, and 3.3% persistent-elevation. Late elevation was associated with the highest cumulative incidence of DSA development, whereas persistent-elevation had the highest incidence of rejection, graft dysfunction, and graft loss. Graft loss occurred in 20.0% of recipients with persistent-elevation and 8.8% with late-elevation and was uncommon among consistently low (2.2%) and transient (2.9%) groups. On multivariable analysis, late elevation was independently associated with DSA development, rejection, and graft loss, and persistent-elevation with rejection, graft dysfunction, and graft loss, regardless of prior transplantation or sensitization status.
CONCLUSIONS: Early dd-cfDNA trajectories stratify kidney transplant recipients into clinically meaningful risk phenotypes. Persistent or late-emerging elevation identifies patients at independently increased risk of rejection and graft loss, with persistent-elevation also associated with graft dysfunction, supporting serial dd-cfDNA monitoring as a tool for early post-transplant risk stratification.

articles.title: Formulation, In Vitro and In Vivo Evaluation of Lutein-Myo-Inositol Microspheres in a Letrozole-Induced Rat Model of PCOS.
articles.authors: Bhardwaj S, Sharma N, Sharma K et al.
articles.abstract: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is a prevalent and complex hormone-metabolic condition that impacts females of reproductive age. Current pharmacological treatments often address limited symptoms, may involve long-term use of synthetic drugs, and are frequently associated with adverse effects and limited patient adherence. In recent years, natural therapeutic agents such as Lutein and Myo-inositol have acquired increasing interest due to their promising biological properties and minimal side effects. Strong antioxidant lutein aids in lowering inflammation and oxidative stress, while Myo-inositol, a naturally occurring sugar alcohol, has insulin-sensitizing and ovulation-inducing effects, making them ideal candidates for addressing the multifaceted pathophysiology of PCOS. Nevertheless, the application of these compounds in therapy is restricted by their limited solubility, reduced bioavailability, and brief half-life. To overcome these challenges, the present research focused on the development and assessment of sustained-release poly-herbal microspheres incorporating Lutein and Myo-inositol using the emulsification method. Nine different formulations (F1 to F9) were prepared and characterized for in vitro parameters. Among the nine formulations developed, one optimized formulation demonstrated high encapsulation efficiency (>90%), satisfactory production yield (>85%), and sustained drug release of approximately 90% over 8 h. In the letrozole-induced PCOS rat model, treatment significantly reduced malondialdehyde (MDA) levels and increased glutathione (GSH) levels compared with the disease control group (p < 0.001). Histopathological evaluation showed a marked reduction in cystic follicles and restoration of normal ovarian morphology in the treated group. Furthermore, in vivo efficacy was confirmed through histopathological examination of ovarian tissues in animal models, where treated groups, especially T3, receiving the highest concentration demonstrated restoration of normal ovarian architecture, reduction in cystic follicles, and improved follicular development. These outcomes support the hypothesis that a combination of Lutein and Myo-inositol, when delivered through a sustained-release microsphere system, can effectively target oxidative stress, insulin resistance, hormonal imbalance, and ovarian dysfunction, which are central to PCOS pathogenesis.

articles.title: Baicalein enhances radiosensitivity in cervical cancer by targeting ALOX15 and regulating lipid metabolism.
articles.authors: Wang R, Liu J
articles.abstract: Radiotherapy is the mainstay for locally advanced cervical cancer, but its efficacy is compromised by radioresistance. Dysregulated lipid metabolism contributes to therapeutic resistance, offering a promising strategy to improve radiosensitivity. This study aimed to explore the effect and mechanism of baicalein in enhancing radiosensitivity of cervical cancer cells. In vitro experiments were performed to assess the radiosensitizing effect of baicalein, while potential targets were identified through bioinformatics and network pharmacology. The key target was further validated by gene knockdown, and in vivo experiments were conducted to confirm the effects of baicalein combined with radiotherapy. ALOX15 was identified as a key target of baicalein, and high ALOX15 expression was associated with poor prognosis in cervical cancer. Both baicalein treatment and ALOX15 suppression enhanced radiosensitivity, reduced lipid droplet accumulation, and downregulated the SREBP1/FASN/ACC protein expression. In vivo, baicalein combined with radiotherapy reduced lipid accumulation and serum lipid levels, with effects comparable to those of the ALOX15 inhibitor AA861. Collectively, these findings suggest that baicalein enhances radiosensitivity in cervical cancer by targeting ALOX15 and modulating lipid metabolism via the SREBP1/FASN/ACC pathway. ALOX15 may be a potential regulator of radioresistance, and baicalein warrants further investigation as a potential radiosensitizer.

articles.title: Using Theory of Change Models to Evaluate the Implementation of Urinary Incontinence Management in Primary Care Initiatives.
articles.authors: Alvarado G, Huilgol S, Malika N et al.
articles.abstract: Theory of change (ToC) models articulate how and why implementation interventions are expected to produce specific outcomes and can guide both program design and evaluation. As part of a theory-driven evaluation for a federal initiative to improve non-surgical management of urinary incontinence among women in primary care, we co-developed ToC models for five funded projects. Each model depicted intervention approaches, hypothesized mechanisms of change, and expected outcomes. Using a six-step process which included document review, consensus-based element identification, open coding, iterative refinement, and stakeholder validation, we created and refined a separate ToC for each grantee. The Technical Expert Panel, convened for the broader initiative, provided multidisciplinary feedback to ensure methodological rigor and contextual accuracy. Sharing the models in annual meetings supported cross-grantee learning and revealed common implementation themes: reliance on technology-based patient education and clinician training, challenges with practice recruitment, tailored facilitation to reduce clinician burden, and gaps in patient-level evaluation measures. The ToC models served four primary functions: orientation for evaluators, technical assistance for grantees, monitoring and evaluation of implementation processes, and cross-site collaboration. Key lessons included the importance of early stakeholder engagement, flexibility in model development, and the value of visual tools for communication and shared understanding. Although resource requirements and retrospective development were challenges, ToC models proved to be adaptable, dynamic tools that enhance evaluation and collaboration in complex, multi-site health initiatives. Their systematic application can strengthen future national and international implementation efforts.

articles.title: Infertility and Quality of Life in Women with CKD: A Case Control Study.
articles.authors: Bhaduri M, Sarris I, Nicolaides K et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Parenthood and pregnancy are important life goals for many individuals, including those with CKD. However, fertility concerns and their impact on quality of life (QoL) are often overlooked in people with complex medical needs. The Fertility QoL (FertiQoL) questionnaire is a validated tool that assesses fertility-related QoL across six domains. This study aimed to assess FertiQoL in women with CKD compared to healthy control women of reproductive age.
METHODS: We conducted a case-control study including 102 women with CKD and 84 healthy controls. Participants completed the FertiQoL survey during a study visit. Domain and total scores were compared between groups, with subgroup analyses among women with prior fertility treatment, those actively trying to conceive, and nulliparous women. Findings were reviewed with an independent expert patient group of women with CKD to evaluate result interpretation and co-develop recommendations.
RESULTS: Women with CKD and controls were similar in age, BMI, parity and history of conception attempts. Median total scaled FertiQoL score was significantly higher in women with CKD than healthy controls (66.2 [IQR 54.8-77.8] vs. 56.6 [IQR 50.5-64.1]; p < 0.001). Women with CKD also had significantly higher scores in emotional, mind-body and social domains. However, among women with prior fertility treatment or those actively trying to conceive, fertility-related QOL did not differ significantly by CKD status. The expert patient group suggested these findings were an adaptation to the demands of long-term ill health rather than any underlying differences in reproductive aspirations.
CONCLUSIONS: This is the first study to assess fertility-related QoL in CKD. Women with CKD reported comparable or better fertility-related quality of life than controls, likely reflecting adaptation to chronic illness. Fertility remains a key priority for women with CKD, highlighting the need for proactive, multidisciplinary fertility counselling and access to reproductive care.

articles.title: Exercise, Dynamic Functional Connectivity, and Sex in Alzheimer's Disease: A Hypothesis-Generating Framework for the Sex-Dependent Dynamic Reconstitution Model.
articles.authors: Gong Z, Xiang Z, Xiang L et al.
articles.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is increasingly viewed as a disorder of large-scale brain network dynamics. Whether exercise-related changes in dynamic functional connectivity (dFC) reflect neural reorganization, vascular effects, or both remains uncertain, and most studies have not tested sex as a moderator. We propose the Sex-Dependent Dynamic Reconstitution Model (SDDRM) as a hypothesis-generating framework. Exercise may influence temporal flexibility (a dynamic connectivity metric) through partially sex-dependent pathways. In females, estrogen-BDNF signaling may potentiate medial temporal lobe (MTL) flexibility gains from aerobic exercise, but this possibility is constrained by menopausal status, age, menopausal hormone therapy (MHT; also known as hormone replacement therapy, HRT) exposure, and limited direct evidence. In males, structured exercise may preferentially influence default mode-frontoparietal coupling through IGF-1-related mechanisms. Evidence for these pathways is predominantly indirect and preclinical, and male and female pathways may overlap substantially. We outline four candidate, sex-stratified predictions: (1) sex may moderate exercise-related MTL flexibility changes, with menopausal status as an exploratory moderator; (2) dynamic flexibility changes may partially mediate cognitive improvement, with indirect pathway magnitudes compared using moderated mediation; (3) exercise cessation may produce different flexibility decay trajectories by sex; and (4) exercise modality may interact with sex. We emphasize dFC methodological caveats-including scan duration, motion, test-retest reliability, and neurovascular coupling-and distinguish biomarker-confirmed AD from MCI and cognitively unimpaired populations. This framework is intended to guide hypothesis-driven, sex-stratified research, not clinical exercise prescriptions.

articles.title: Moral Distress Among Abortion-Providing Clinicians After the US Supreme Court Dobbs Decision.
articles.authors: Wascher J, Howard D, Bornstein M et al.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Moral distress among abortion-providing clinicians could lead to burnout and attrition from the workforce, worsening reproductive care disparities.
OBJECTIVE: To describe situations associated with moral distress among abortion-providing clinicians since the US Supreme Court's Dobbs v Jackson Women's Health Organization decision across a range of policy environments.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: For this qualitative study, purposive sampling was conducted from May to December 2023 through listservs and snowball sampling across the US. Participants were clinicians providing abortion care in the US in the year following Dobbs. Data were analyzed from March 2024 to April 2025.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was determining which situations were associated with moral distress in both protective and restrictive abortion policy environments. Deductive and inductive coding approaches were used to analyze open-ended responses.
RESULTS: Of 310 respondents completing the full survey (271 women [87.7%]; 132 aged 36-45 years [43.6%]), 160 (51.6%) responded to the optional open-ended question. The 160 respondents described situations associated with moral distress in state policy environments that were both protective and restrictive of abortion. Through thematic analysis, 3 main themes of situations associated with moral distress were identified: (1) bans prohibiting conscientious provision of abortion care; (2) forced adjustments to medical practice, including being forced to provide inaccurate information, substandard care, or to limit care due to resource scarcity; and (3) distress related to the broader national environment.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this qualitative study, clinicians in both abortion-protective and abortion-restrictive environments reported situations associated with moral distress. Solutions for combating moral distress should be targeted to specific situations and sources, including at institutional, state, or national levels.

articles.title: SARS-CoV-2 mRNA Vaccination in Pregnancy and Child Neurodevelopment at 18 to 30 Months.
articles.authors: Hughes BL, Clifton RG, Metz TD et al.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Little is known about neurodevelopmental outcomes of children exposed to SARS-CoV-2 messenger RNA (mRNA) vaccine during pregnancy. Evidence on long-term offspring outcomes after in utero exposure to SARS-CoV-2 mRNA vaccination is needed to inform vaccine recommendations in pregnancy.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate whether there is an association between SARS-CoV-2 vaccination during or shortly before pregnancy and offspring neurodevelopmental measures.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This multicenter, prospective, cohort study of 18- to 30-month-old children was conducted at 14 centers of the Eunice Kennedy Shriver National Institute of Child Health and Human Development Maternal-Fetal Medicine Units Network from 2024 through 2025. Women who received a SARS-CoV-2 mRNA vaccine during or within 30 days prior to pregnancy (exposed) were matched with women who did not (unexposed) by delivery site, delivery date, insurance status, and race and ethnicity. These data were analyzed from June 2025 to May 2026.
EXPOSURES: Maternal receipt of at least 1 dose of an mRNA SARS-CoV-2 vaccine during, or within 30 days prior to, the index pregnancy vs no SARS-CoV-2 vaccination during pregnancy or within 30 days prior.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was Ages and Stages Questionnaire version 3 (ASQ-3) total score, which was deemed to be equivalent between the exposed and unexposed groups if the 90% CI of the median difference was between -10 and 10. Secondary outcomes included domain-specific ASQ-3 scores, the Child Behavior Checklist, Modified Checklist for Autism in Toddlers, and Early Childhood Behavior Questionnaire scores.
RESULTS: Of 3956 screened, 271 exposed and 240 unexposed children were enrolled. Matching on all characteristics was possible in 217 pairs. Of the 434 children enrolled, 258 (59.4%) were Non-Hispanic White, 96 (22.1%) Non-Hispanic Black, 52 (12.0%) Hispanic, and 28 (6.5%) were not represented by any of the above racial or ethnic groups. Median age at assessment was 25.8 [24.6 to 28.3] months, 221 were female (50.9%), and 213 were male (49.1%). Exposed mothers were more likely to be nulliparous; their children were slightly younger at assessment and more likely to have been vaccinated against SARS-CoV-2. The primary outcome of ASQ-3 score was equivalent between the exposed and unexposed groups (255 vs 260, adjusted median difference, -3.4; 90% CI, -9.8 to 3.0). There were no significant differences in secondary…

articles.title: Global research landscape, intellectual structure, and thematic evolution of robot-assisted surgical management of pelvic urinary tract fistulas: a bibliometric and knowledge-mapping analysis.
articles.authors: Wu G, Li D, Liu H et al.
articles.abstract: Robot-assisted surgery has been applied to a range of pelvic urinary tract fistulas, but the literature is dispersed across urology, gynecology, colorectal surgery, and reconstructive practice. We examined how this literature developed, how its contributing communities interact, and whether its clinical themes converge. English-language articles and reviews indexed in the Science Citation Index Expanded within the Web of Science Core Collection from inception to 1 August 2026 were screened for clinical or technical relevance. The final corpus contained 104 publications, comprising 85 articles and 19 reviews, published between 2005 and 2026. Publication and disciplinary trends, geographic collaboration, historical foundations, reference-based networks, Author Keyword themes, thematic evolution, and journal citation pathways were analyzed. Output remained low and uneven, although higher annual counts became more frequent after 2021. Urology remained the principal disciplinary setting, with broader participation from gynecology, reproductive health, and surgery. Authors from 31 countries or regions contributed; the United States led in both publication output and citations, while international collaboration remained concentrated within a limited network. Historical and thematic analyses identified vesicovaginal fistula repair as the main intellectual and conceptual backbone; colovesical, ureteral, rectourinary, and congenital applications formed smaller, partly separate streams. The literature has acquired a recognizable cross-specialty structure, but its principal clinical strands have not yet converged into a comparable evidence base. Future studies should prioritize multicenter designs and consistent reporting of anatomy, prior treatment, reconstruction, and clinically relevant outcomes.

articles.title: TEX15 variants in male infertility: a real-world cohort study.
articles.journal: Journal of assisted reproduction and genetics
articles.authors: Graziani A, Grande G, Rocca MS et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate the clinical phenotype and interpretability of TEX15 gene variants in a real-world cohort of patients with primary testicular disease.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective single-center study including patients with primary testicular dysfunction. Patients carrying isolated TEX15 gene variants (n = 7) were compared with a pathological control group (n = 145) from a cohort of infertile patients with primary testicular failure without identifiable genetic alterations. Clinical, hormonal, and seminal parameters were analyzed using non-parametric tests. Effect size was estimated using Cliff's delta.
RESULTS: TEX15 gene variants were identified in 0.9% of the cohort. No pathogenic biallelic variants were identified. Compared to pathological controls, TEX15-positive patients showed lower FSH concentrations (p = 0.031), higher sperm concentration (p = 0.002), and higher total sperm count (p = 0.002). Azoospermia was absent among TEX15 cases but present in 62.1% of controls (p = 0.002). No significant differences were observed in LH, testosterone levels, estradiol concentrations, or testicular volume. Sensitivity analyses excluding biologically atypical subjects attenuated most observed differences. Overall, TEX15-positive patients showed heterogeneous clinical presentations with limited phenotypic specificity compared to other forms of primary testicular dysfunction.
CONCLUSIONS: Our findings indicate that TEX15 gene variants, particularly in heterozygous state, have limited clinical interpretability and do not define a clearly distinguishable clinical phenotype. These findings suggest that isolated TEX15 variants, particularly in heterozygous state, should be interpreted cautiously in routine male infertility diagnostics pending further functional validation.

articles.title: Cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic outcomes in women with hypertensive disorders of pregnancy at 12 months postpartum : The PreCareFem Cohort.
articles.authors: Findl K, Halmer S, Klee S et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy are risk factors for later cardiovascular and chronic kidney disease. Early postpartum trajectories of blood pressure and metabolic recovery in this high-risk population are still insufficiently defined.
METHODS: A prospective, single-center, observational cohort study was conducted in the Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic Women's Healthcare Prevention Program (PreCareFem) at the University Hospital St. Pölten, Austria. Participants were enrolled on presentation between 1 June 2023, and 31 March 2025. Cardiovascular and metabolic surrogate parameters, including automated blood pressure measurement, anthropometric evaluation, cardiovascular, kidney and metabolic parameters, lifestyle assessment following the components of the "Life's Essential 8", and urine albumin-creatinine ratio were assessed peripartum and at 3-6 and 12 months postpartum.
RESULTS: A total of 91 women with preeclampsia (PE; n = 66) and gestational hypertension (GH; n = 25) were enrolled. At 12 months postpartum, 31% met the diagnostic criteria for arterial hypertension (PE 29%, GH 36%), 18% for prediabetes and 3% for diabetes. More than half (52%) had LDL levels > 100 mg/dL and 32% had low HDL levels. Obesity was diagnosed in 24% of participants, 8% of women were diagnosed with CKD 12 months postpartum. Low-grade albuminuria (uACR 10-30 mg/g) was observed in 21% of women with PE compared to 8% in women with GH.
CONCLUSION: A significant number of women were diagnosed with arterial hypertension, early kidney impairment and/or metabolic abnormalities 1 year following hypertensive disorders of pregnancy. These findings highlight the need for a structured, multidisciplinary postpartum follow-up to address an underutilized opportunity for prevention of cardiovascular and chronic kidney disease.

articles.title: Parental outcomes in congenital lung malformations: a transdisciplinary family-centered model.
articles.authors: Bolis ME, Sgobbi B, Antichi L et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: The study aimed to evaluate a family-centered care model, the "Respiriamo, insieme" project, that supports families from prenatal diagnosis through postoperative follow-up.
METHODS: We conducted a posttest-only study comparing families of children with CLM. The intervention group received an integrated pathway combining multidisciplinary counseling, prenatal and postnatal psychological support, music therapy, minimally invasive surgery, locoregional anesthesia, and fast-track perioperative management. The standard care group included families managed at other centers where the integrated pathway was not implemented. One month after surgery, mothers and fathers separately completed validated questionnaires assessing anxiety, post-traumatic stress, and perceived quality of care.
RESULTS: Forty-one families participated (26 in the intervention group, 15 in the standard care group). Mothers in the intervention group reported significantly lower anxiety and post-traumatic stress and higher perceived quality of care; fathers showed the same direction with weaker evidence. All quality-of-care domains were significantly higher among intervention mothers; among fathers, only communication and general satisfaction differed significantly. Exploratory maternal analyses suggested lower distress with both prenatal and postnatal support.
CONCLUSION: A structured, family-centered care model reduced parental distress and improved perceived quality of care in CLM. Integrating psychosocial support into perioperative management may strengthen parental resilience and should be standard care.

articles.title: Why have four decades of research into decreased ovarian reserve (DOR) failed to improve live birth rates?
articles.authors: Rafael ZB, Orvieto R
articles.abstract: Despite forty years of intense research and multitudinous clinical innovations, live birth rates (LBR) among women diagnosed with decreased ovarian reserve (DOR) remain disappointingly poor. Is this because a solution has not yet been discovered, or are we searching in the wrong way? This persistent failure is probably the product of both undisputable biological realities, the exponential decline in oocyte euploidy with advanced maternal age, and persistent methodological flaws, most notably the inclusion of highly heterogeneous cohorts in clinical trials and inadequate stratification by critical variables, such as age. No ovarian stimulation protocol, adjuvant therapy, or laboratory add-on has consistently improved outcomes. The grouping of young and older DOR women in clinical studies, the focus on surrogate endpoints over live birth, and failure to account for cycle-to-cycle and operator variability further obscure valid conclusions and mislead both clinicians and patients. In this review, we delineate the evolution of DOR research, drilling down to the biological, technical, and methodological roots of failed progress. We argue that only by rigorously stratifying study populations by narrow age bands, repeated response criteria and prioritizing true endpoints, can future research genuinely advance the field and provide realistic, evidence based counseling. Clinical humility and research rigor are prerequisites for sparing patients needless interventions and false hope.

articles.title: Protecting Reproductive Health in Nuclear Emergencies: A Review of Shielding Devices and Radioprotective Agents.
articles.authors: Zhang X, Zhao H
articles.abstract: Nuclear emergencies can generate ionizing radiation that potentially induces severe, irreversible gonadal injury and theoretically heritable genetic risks among exposed emergency responders. Because germ cells and gonadal tissues are highly radiosensitive, reproductive organs are susceptible to radiation-mediated harm. Clinically observed radiation-associated reproductive outcomes cover impaired spermatogenesis in males, progressive ovarian follicle loss in females, and temporary or permanent infertility. It should be noted that authoritative assessments by the International Commission on Radiological Protection and the United Nations Scientific Committee on the Effects of Atomic Radiation indicate minimal population-level heritable disease risks under routine low-dose nuclear emergency exposure. Physical shielding tools and radioprotective pharmaceuticals serve as core countermeasures to lower gonadal absorbed dose and preserve responders' fertility, yet their field applicability differs substantially from clinical radiotherapy settings. This narrative review systematically elaborates on radiation-induced reproductive hazards specific to nuclear accident conditions, categorizes mainstream gonadal shielding hardware and radioprotective agents alongside their technical performances, and highlights prominent research gaps as well as targeted developmental suggestions. The summarized evidence provides evidence-based references for formulating standardized radiation protection and fertility conservation protocols for frontline nuclear emergency personnel.

articles.title: Exploration of vetiver-derived compounds for addressing remedy against male infertility using in silco approach.
articles.authors: Mohapatra S, Preethika A, Raja S et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The rising prevalence of reproductive disorders, including male infertility, necessitates innovative therapeutic strategies. Plant-based extracts, particularly those from Chrysopogon zizanioides (vetiver plant), have emerged as promising candidates. This study employs in silico methodologies to evaluate the therapeutic potential of vetiver-derived compounds against male infertility. This research aims to investigate the pharmacokinetic profiles, bioactivity, toxicity, and molecular interactions of vetiver compounds with proteins implicated in male reproductive health.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: The study integrates Absorption, Distribution, Metabolism, and Excretion (ADME) predictions, protein-protein interaction (PPI) analysis, bioactivity and toxicity evaluations, and molecular docking and simulation studies to assess therapeutic viability. ADME tools analyzed the pharmacokinetic profiles of vetiver compounds. Network pharmacology approaches and PPI analysis mapped interactions with target proteins. Bioactivity and toxicity assessments ensured compound safety and efficacy. Molecular docking and simulations examined the binding affinities and dynamic interactions of selected compounds with target proteins.
RESULTS: Out of 120 screened compounds, phenolic derivatives were prioritized. Channaine (Ligand-4) exhibited strong therapeutic potential, with 91.2% intestinal absorption, favorable tissue distribution (Vdss: 1.214 log L/kg), and low toxicity (lethal dose 50%: 2.953 mol/kg). Docking revealed strong binding affinities with Nuclear Factor Erythroid 2-Related Factor 2 (NFE2 L2) (-7.4 kcal/mol), Krüppel-like factor (KLF5) (-4.4 kcal/mol), and Nuclear Factor Kappa B Subunit 1 (NFKB 1) (-7.0 kcal/mol).
CONCLUSION: Simulations confirmed stable protein-ligand interactions, supporting its therapeutic promise. Vetiver extracts show significant potential for treating male infertility, offering favorable pharmacokinetics, low toxicity, and effective target interactions. These findings warrant further experimental and clinical validation.

articles.title: Comparison of the opioid-sparing effects of a combination of dexamethasone, paracetamol, and ketorolac versus paracetamol and ketorolac in patients undergoing total laparoscopic hysterectomy: A prospective double-blind randomized controlled trial.
articles.authors: Nene I, Lalwani P, Khanna P et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Total laparoscopic hysterectomy (TLH) is quickly replacing the open abdominal hysterectomy, but is associated with unexpectedly high levels of pain.
OBJECTIVES: The objective of this study was to compare the analgesic efficacy of adding dexamethasone to paracetamol and ketorolac (PaK) combination versus PaK combination in female patients undergoing elective TLH.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: After approval from the institutional ethical committee, 100 American Society of Anesthesiologists I and II patients aged 18-60 years undergoing TLH under general anesthesia were included in this study. The patients were assigned to one of the two treatment groups (C and D). Patients in Group D received dexamethasone (0.2 mg/kg) intravenously (IV) dissolved in 100 ml of 0.9% saline 1 h before surgery and ketorolac 30 mg + paracetamol (PCM) 1 g IV prior to anesthesia being induced, while the patient in Group C received a placebo (100 ml of 0.9% normal saline) 1 h before surgery and ketorolac 30 mg + PCM 1 g IV before induction of anesthesia.
RESULTS: Fentanyl consumption in the first 24 h was significantly higher in Group C (231.72 ± 84.07 μg) than in Group D (138 ± 48.7 μg) (P < 0.0001). Pain scores on the 0-100 Visual Analog Scale demonstrated notable variations at each point among the groups (P < 0.05). Postoperative nausea and vomiting scores differed at 15 and 30 min (P < 0.05). A transient rise in blood glucose occurred in Group D at 16 h (122 g/dl vs. 115 g/dl in Group C, P = 0.013).
CONCLUSION: In patients undergoing TLH, a combination of dexamethasone, PCM, and ketorolac reduced 24-h opioid use, improved pain scores, and minimized immediate postoperative nausea and vomiting.

articles.title: Department of War-Funded Women's Health Research: A Portfolio Analysis of Investments.
articles.authors: Hamlin L
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To assess the current state of Department of War (DoW)-funded women's health research by analyzing the distribution of funded projects across major clinical and scientific domains for years 2018-2025.
DESIGN: Portfolio analysis of DoW Women's Health Research-funded projects categorized by topic area. A narrative synthesis was conducted to characterize funding distribution, identify dominant research domains, and highlight gaps.
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: DOW-funded research demonstrates substantial investment in several domains, with the largest funding concentration in cancer research ($118.5M), followed by reproductive and gynecological health ($19.2M) and musculoskeletal conditions (14.4M). Additional domains include menopause, mental health, and sex-based biological differences. Several areas-including cardiovascular disease, autoimmune disorders, and pain-show minimal or no recorded funding in this dataset. The portfolio reflects a strong emphasis on disease-specific and reproductive health topics, with comparatively limited investment in acute and chronic disease and implementation science.
CONCLUSIONS: DoW-funded women's health research is concentrated in a small number of domains, particularly cancer and reproductive health. Significant gaps exist, suggesting opportunities for strategic expansion to better align with the evolving health needs of women service members.

articles.title: Colonization of allogeneic germline stem cells in mature nonablated mouse testes by inhibition of retinoic acid signaling†.
articles.authors: Morimoto H, Ogonuki N, Matoba S et al.
articles.abstract: Autologous transplantation of spermatogonial stem cells (SSCs) is a promising approach to restore fertility in young cancer patients who often become infertile due to gonadotoxic treatment. Because only a small number of SSCs can be collected from a biopsy, in vitro expansion of these cells is necessary before auto-transplantation. However, residual spermatogenesis in these patients poses.a significant barrier to efficient colonization of transplanted SSCs. Here, we report that inhibition of retinoic acid signaling by WIN18446, an ALDH1A2 inhibitor, allows colonization of cultured SSCs in nonablated mature testes. Cultured SSCs successfully colonized mouse testes lacking Cldn11-a key molecule for maintaining the blood-testis barrier (BTB)-but failed to colonize wild-type testes, suggesting that the BTB is a major hurdle for colonization. Although WIN18446 treatment did not downregulate CLDN11, it induced a deficiency in CLDN3, possibly through enhancing BTB permeability, and allowed for complete spermatogenesis even in allogeneic recipient testes without immunosuppression. Microinsemination resulted in the production of allogeneic offspring. These results indicate that inhibition of the BTB by WIN18,446 is applicable in cases where endogenous SSCs prevent donor SSC colonization and further demonstrate the unique ability of cultured SSCs to colonize allogeneic testes.

articles.title: Liver Injury Due to Hormonal Contraceptives in the Modern Era.
articles.journal: Liver international : official journal of the International Association for the Study of the Liver
articles.authors: Vuppalanchi R, Barritt AS, Rai A et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Hormonal agents and their association with liver injury remain a concern in clinical practice. This study aimed to characterise the biochemical and clinical features of hormonal agent-associated liver injury and compare them with a control group of age- and gender-matched cases of liver injury caused by non-hormonal drugs.
METHODS: Of 2123 adjudicated drug-induced liver injury cases enrolled in the Drug-Induced Liver Injury Network (2004-2024), 20 high-confidence cases (1.3%) were attributed to hormonal agents. These cases were compared with age- and sex-matched non-hormonal drug-induced liver injury (DILI) controls, and analyses assessed clinical features, biochemical patterns, outcomes, HLA alleles and candidate genetic variants associated with cholestatic liver disease.
RESULTS: The median age of women was 22 years. Most presented within 2-12 weeks with jaundice and pruritus, predominantly with cholestatic or mixed patterns of liver enzyme elevations, but a hepatocellular pattern was not uncommon at 28%. The route of administration did not appear to influence DILI risk. Half underwent a liver biopsy, and half required hospitalization, but none died or required liver transplantation. Compared with other DILI cases, hormonal agent-associated liver injury was more often cholestatic, with jaundice and pruritus, and less frequently associated with fever or rash. No HLA association was identified, although the intronic MROH2A variant rs6722064 ranked as the top potential candidate for increased risk [OR (95% CI) = 3.58 (1.67, 7.65), p = 0.001].
CONCLUSIONS: Hormonal agent-associated liver injury presents with a distinctive mixed or cholestatic pattern and often lacks the inflammatory features seen in other DILI cases. These findings underscore the need for greater clinical awareness to improve patient outcomes.

articles.title: Machine learning prediction of IVF outcomes in unexplained infertility.
articles.journal: Turkish journal of obstetrics and gynecology
articles.authors: Kaya Y, Aydın Y, Kaya C et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To develop and evaluate machine learning (ML) models to predict clinical pregnancy (CP) outcomes in couples with unexplained infertility (UI) undergoing in vitro fertilization (IVF), thereby enhancing early treatment decision-making and patient counseling.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: A retrospective analysis was conducted on 145 couples diagnosed with UI and treated at a single-center IVF clinic. Live birth data were not available; therefore, CP was used as the primary outcome. Demographic, clinical, and laboratory parameters were collected, and five ML algorithms-light gradient boosting machine (LGBM), random forest, logistic regression, extra trees classifier, and eXtreme gradient boosting-were applied to predict CP outcomes. Model performance was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC-AUC), accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity. Permutation-based feature importance analysis was performed to identify key predictive variables.
RESULTS: Among the evaluated models, the LGBM model achieved the highest test-set ROC-AUC (0.712) and an accuracy of 65.2%. Given the small test sample and the lack of external validation, these findings should be interpreted as exploratory. Variables receiving the highest permutation feature-importance scores included total gonadotropin dose, initial gonadotropin dose, total sperm count, progressive motile sperm count, and infertility duration. These findings should be interpreted as exploratory and do not establish that these variables are independent predictors of CP.
CONCLUSION: This study presents the first ML-based approach tailored to predicting CP outcomes in couples with UI undergoing IVF. The results highlight the potential of artificial intelligence to inform personalized reproductive care. These exploratory findings demonstrate the feasibility of applying ML methods in UI. Larger prospective multicenter studies are required to determine whether clinically useful prediction models can be developed.

articles.title: Treatment outcome and adverse effects of new regimens (bedaquiline and linezolid) for multidrug-resistant tuberculosis during pregnancy: A systematic review.
articles.journal: The International journal of risk & safety in medicine
articles.authors: Murtiani F, Ilhamy M, Norma N et al.
articles.abstract: BackgroundManaging tuberculosis treatment during pregnancy, especially in women with multidrug-resistant tuberculosis (MDR-TB). The World Health Organization recommends a 9-month oral regimen that includes bedaquiline and linezolid, but the effects on pregnancy are not well understood.ObjectiveThis study aimed to assess the impact of a bedaquiline- and linezolid-containing regimen on maternal and fetal health in pregnant women with MDR-TB.MethodsA systematic review was conducted in accordance with the PRISMA guidelines, searching multiple databases for relevant studies published between 2004 and 2025. Study quality was assessed using the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) tool.ResultsFour studies were included. The regimen showed favorable treatment outcomes for mothers, with treatment success rates ranging from 60.7% to 98%. However, a high incidence of adverse pregnancy outcomes was reported, including preterm birth (28%-55%), low birth weight (32%-35%), and miscarriage or stillbirth. One study reported a 35% pregnancy termination rate.ConclusionWhile the bedaquiline and linezolid regimen appears highly effective against MDR-TB in mothers, it is associated with significant adverse fetal outcomes. Close monitoring and further research are essential to determine whether the drugs or the underlying MDR-TB disease causes these outcomes.

articles.title: Patient Expectations and Experiences With Postoperative Bowel Function.
articles.authors: Chu CM, Tholemeier L, Agu I et al.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Postoperative constipation can affect quality of life and satisfaction in patients undergoing urogynecologic surgery.
OBJECTIVES: The objectives of this study were to compare preoperative expectations regarding postoperative bowel function to patients' actual experiences after surgery, and to examine patient-reported use and satisfaction with polyethylene glycol.
STUDY DESIGN: This was a prospective cohort study of women undergoing urogynecologic surgery. Before surgery, participants were asked to complete a survey on baseline bowel function and postoperative bowel function expectations, which included the validated Wexner constipation questionnaire. Participants were again surveyed at 1 week and 6 weeks postoperatively regarding their experiences with postoperative bowel movements and use of polyethylene glycol. Patient Global Impressions of Improvement were used to measure postoperative improvement in bowel function.
RESULTS: Of 86 enrolled participants, 83 (96.5%) completed the 1-week and 77 (89.5%) completed the 6-week follow-up. Some participants reported improvement in bowel movements at 1 week (53%), and more at 6 weeks (65%). Presence of preoperative concerns about first bowel movement did not influence perception of improvement at 1 week (55% vs 45%, respectively, P=0.33) or at 6 weeks (62.2% vs 52.5%, P=0.37). At 6 weeks, those who continued to use polyethylene glycol were more likely to report postoperative bowel improvement (84.4% vs 50%, P=0.002).
CONCLUSIONS: Most patients experience improvement in bowel function after urogynecologic surgery. Preoperative concerns do not seem to affect self-reported improvement. Some patients taking polyethylene glycol experience improvement in bowel function as early as 1 week after urogynecologic surgery, with more improvement at 6 weeks.

articles.title: Awareness and knowledge level of gestational diabetes mellitus among women in the UAE and variations across sociodemographic factors: A cross-sectional study.
articles.authors: Alblooshi S, Abdelwahab M, Khalid A et al.
articles.abstract: BackgroundThe prevalence of Gestational Diabetes Mellitus (GDM) is rising in the United Arab Emirates (UAE), with estimates ranging from 8% to 40%, depending on diagnostic criteria. Despite its implications for maternal and neonatal health, research on public knowledge around GDM in the UAE remains limited, particularly in relation to gender equity and women's health empowerment.ObjectivesThis study aimed to evaluate GDM knowledge among adult women in the UAE and assess demographic variations in understanding health information.DesignA cross-sectional study was conducted.Methods1039 female UAE residents aged 18 and above completed an online questionnaire assessing GDM-related knowledge, perception, and access to information. Data were analysed using SPSS, and Chi-Square Tests and logistic regression model were used to identify associations between GDM-related knowledge levels and sociodemographic factors.ResultsAmong participants, 72.2% had heard of GDM, and 52.3% demonstrated adequate knowledge. Adequate knowledge was significantly associated with older age, higher education, employment, abnormal BMI, prior pregnancy, chronic disease, knowing someone with GDM, and having experienced GDM (all p < 0.05). In multivariable analysis, prior pregnancy (OR = 2.22, p = 0.003) and a history of GDM (OR = 2.10, p = 0.042) were the strongest predictors of adequate knowledge. The most common information sources were family and friends (57%), hospitals (43%), and social media (36%).ConclusionAlthough overall awareness of GDM in the UAE was moderate, knowledge levels varied significantly by age, education, employment status, and personal or familial experience with the condition. These findings highlight the need for culturally tailored, nurse-led, community-based education programs to enhance GDM knowledge, particularly among younger and nulliparous women. Targeted interventions can reduce disparities, promote informed decision-making, and support equitable and sustainable maternal health in Arab societies.

articles.title: Management of Overactive Bladder After Radical Prostatectomy: Safety and Clinical Pathways Following Intradetrusor OnabotulinumtoxinA.
articles.authors: Tsai RG, Muramoto LPK, Nitti VW
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Men with overactive bladder (OAB) following radical prostatectomy may undergo intradetrusor onabotulinumtoxinA (onabotA), including in the setting of artificial urinary sphincter (AUS) or male sling placement. However, data regarding urinary retention and de novo clean intermittent catheterization (CIC), as well as longitudinal treatment patterns, remain limited in this population. We evaluated the safety and treatment patterns of onabotA in men with OAB following radical prostatectomy, with particular attention to patients undergoing continence surgery.
METHODS: We performed a retrospective single-center cohort study of adult men with a history of radical prostatectomy undergoing intradetrusor onabotA between 2018 and 2025. Patients were categorized as: (1) onabotA only after radical prostatectomy or (2) an AUS/sling group comprising patients who underwent continence surgery before or during onabotA treatment. The primary outcome was de novo CIC following treatment. Secondary outcomes included elevated postvoid residual (PVR), treatment characteristics, dose escalation, treatment persistence, and descriptive analyses of clinical pathways and urodynamic findings among patients undergoing prior continence surgery. Kaplan-Meier methods were used to evaluate treatment persistence among patients receiving at least two injections.
RESULTS: Thirty-two men underwent intradetrusor onabotA after radical prostatectomy. Fourteen comprised the onabotA-only group and 18 the AUS/sling group, including 17 who underwent continence surgery before onabotA and one who underwent male sling placement after treatment with onabotA. Median follow-up after first onabotA injection was 1.75 years (IQR 0.57-2.91). Twenty-two patients (68.8%) received at least two injections, including 50.0% (7/14) and 83.3% (15/18) in the respective groups (p = 0.062). No patient developed de novo CIC following treatment. Elevated PVR (≥ 200 mL) occurred in 9.4% (3/32) of patients, all in the onabotA-only group. Among patients receiving repeat treatment, dose escalation to 200-300 units occurred in 50.0% (11/22). Treatment persistence did not differ between groups (log-rank p = 0.851).
CONCLUSION: Intradetrusor onabotA demonstrated a favorable safety profile among men with OAB following radical prostatectomy, including those undergoing AUS or male sling placement, with no patients requiring de novo CIC. These findings support consideration of onabotA in appropriately selected patients…

articles.title: Deflux and Botulinum Toxin Type A as Combined Therapeutic Approach in Pediatric Vesicoureteral Reflux and Concurrent Non-Neurogenic Dysfunctional Voiding: Insights From a Prospective Single-Arm Study.
articles.authors: Ganjaroudi NM, Jarrah N, Pezeshki PS et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: We aimed to assess uroflowmetric measurements and quality-of-life outcomes following synchronous Deflux injection and pelvic floor and inter-sphincteric Botulinum toxin type A (BTX-A) injection in pediatric patients diagnosed with vesicoureteral reflux (VUR) and non-neurogenic dysfunctional voiding (NNDV) at 6-month and 1-year follow-ups.
METHODS: This prospective study included female children aged 5-18 years with concurrent VUR and NNDV. All participants underwent pre-and postoperative ultrasonography, uroflowmetry study and quality-of-life assessment. Deflux injection was performed using the hydrodistension implantation technique in the refluxing ureter. BTX-A injection was administered to the periurethral and perineal body areas. Participants with functional constipation, confirmed by ROME Ⅳ criteria, received perianal BTX-A injection. All statistical analyses were conducted using R Statistical software (version 4.4.2), with a significance threshold set at p < 0.05.
RESULTS: Among 30 patients, near bell-shaped voiding patterns were observed in 23 (76.7%) at 6-month and 27 (90%) at 1-year follow-ups with a significant overall change across three assessment timepoints (LR = 37.47, p < 0.001). Complete VUR resolution was observed in 40 of 46 (87%) refluxing renal units at 6 months (p < 0.001). Volume-adjusted maximal and average flow indices improved significantly over time (p = 0.003 and p < 0.001, respectively). PinQ scores decreased from 20.83 ± 8.55 preoperatively to 11.26 ± 6.91 at 1-year follow-up (p < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: This prospective study indicated that the combined BTX-A and Deflux injections were associated with improvements in dysfunctional voiding severity, voiding flow parameters, voiding diaries, and quality-of-life outcomes in children with concurrent NNDV and VUR.

articles.title: Navigating Intermediate Bladder Outflow Obstruction: A Combined DCI-BOOI Framework Incorporating BWT for Predicting Surgical Outcomes in Men With Lower Urinary Tract Symptoms.
articles.authors: Shi Y, Xu Z, Xi J
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The 2023 ICS-SUFU pressure-flow standard recommends the ICS Bladder Outflow Obstruction Index (BOOI) and ICS Detrusor Contraction Index (DCI) as continuous parameters for grading bladder outflow obstruction (BOO) and detrusor voiding contraction (DVC) in men. Patients with intermediate BOO (BOOI 20-40) may nevertheless represent a heterogeneous population, making it difficult to determine whether transurethral resection of the prostate (TURP) is likely to provide clinical benefit.
OBJECTIVE: To explore whether detrusor overactivity (DO) and ultrasound-estimated bladder wall thickness (BWT) are associated with postoperative outcomes among men with intermediate BOO undergoing TURP.
METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study included 234 men who underwent TURP after preoperative urodynamic testing and sonographic evaluation between January 2021 and June 2024. Pressure-flow findings were classified using ICS-BOOI and ICS-DCI, with particular attention to intermediate BOO (BOOI 20-40). The primary outcome was surgical success, defined as a ≥ 50% reduction in International Prostate Symptom Score (IPSS) at 6 months. Multivariable logistic regression and receiver operating characteristic curve analyses were performed to assess the exploratory value of BOOI, DO, and BWT.
RESULTS: The overall surgical success rate differed across pressure-flow phenotypes. Patients with BOO and normal DVC had a higher success rate than those with weak DVC. Among 85 patients with intermediate BOO, the overall success rate was 47.1%, with marked heterogeneity across DO-BWT subgroups. Intermediate-BOO patients with both DO and BWT > 2.5 mm had a substantially higher success rate than those without DO and with BWT ≤ 2.5 mm. The full model incorporating BOOI, DO, and BWT had an area under the curve of 0.799, compared with 0.528 for BOOI alone; however, subgroup sparsity and complete overlap of increased BWT with DO in the intermediate group limit interpretation of their independent contributions.
CONCLUSIONS: Men with intermediate BOO were heterogeneous in this retrospective cohort. Increased BWT was associated with a higher surgical success rate, but no patient in the intermediate group had increased BWT without DO; therefore, the independent contribution of DO could not be determined. BWT may provide adjunctive screening information, whereas the role of DO remains exploratory and requires prospective validation.

articles.title: Clinical Practice Variation Between Paediatricians and Urologists in the Management of Daytime Urinary Incontinence in Children.
articles.authors: Linde JM, Ypma DR, Hofmeester I et al.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: This study aimed to examine clinical practice variation between urologists and paediatricians managing children with daytime urinary incontinence (DUI) to identify unwarranted variation and improve care pathways.
METHODS: A single-centre retrospective database study was conducted, including children aged 4-18 years referred for DUI between 2016 and 2018. Patient characteristics, diagnostic evaluations, and treatment trajectories were extracted using standardised case report forms and analysed descriptively, with comparative statistics applied to evaluate differences between urologists and paediatricians.
RESULTS: Of the 395 included children, 327 (82.8%) were referred to paediatrics and 68 (17.2%) to urology. Median age was 6 years in paediatrics and 9.5 years in urology, with paediatricians receiving more GP referrals (96.6% vs. 77.9%). Paediatric care showed more comprehensive history-taking and more frequent physical examination (96.7% vs. 64.2%), whereas urologists routinely performed voiding diaries (98.5%) and uroflowmetry (100%), which paediatricians used less consistently (85.5% and 60.7%) and generally later in the care trajectory. Urotherapy was provided more often by paediatricians (97.5% vs. 74.6%), while urologists prescribed anticholinergics more frequently (70.1% vs. 16.4%).
CONCLUSIONS: This study confirms our initial impression that notable practice variation exists in the care of children with DUI. Awareness of such variation is essential, and we aim to draw attention to this issue among clinicians. Based on our findings, we developed a consensus document outlining shared care pathways. Further research is needed to determine its impact on clinical practice and patient outcomes.

articles.title: An Objective Uroflowmetry Curve Score and Five Descriptive Curve Groups in Men: A Single-Centre Retrospective Study.
articles.authors: Wang X, Yao G, Ding W
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Uroflowmetry curve shape is judged by eye, with only fair-to-moderate agreement between readers. We aimed to describe male flow curves objectively with one score and a few descriptive groups that other centres can compute.
METHODS: Retrospective single-centre study of male free uroflowmetry (voided volume ≥ 150 mL; 2022-2026). Seven measures described each curve: four from the report (maximum flow rate [Qmax], flow time, time to Qmax, average flow) and three from the stored curve (flow dips, variability, plateau). The score was their first principal component; five descriptive groups were formed by k-means clustering. Age, a benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) label and post-void residual (PVR), not used to build either, served as checks.
RESULTS: We analyzed 2414 examinations from 2154 identified men (median age 64 years). The score captured 37% of variation. Groups ranged from low, prolonged, fluctuating curves (group A, 11%) to bell/plateau (D, 27%) and brisk, peaked curves (E, 22%). The score fell with age (Spearman ρ = -0.21; Qmax alone: -0.19) and PVR (ρ = -0.35, n = 465); median PVR was 89 mL in group A versus 23 mL in D. BPH labeling did not differ between groups (p = 0.12). A report-values-only score correlated 0.91 with the full score.
CONCLUSIONS: The score and groups give an objective, shared description of male curve shape for research and audit. The five groups describe a continuum of curve shapes, with no clear-cut boundaries between them. They track age and PVR about as strongly as Qmax and are not a diagnostic test. Constants, a worked example and code are provided.

articles.title: Accuracy of plasma cell-free DNA PCR versus mNGS for non-invasive diagnosis of invasive mold disease.
articles.authors: Pusz-Bochenska K, Murugesan K, Senchyna F et al.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Cell-free DNA (cfDNA) detection in plasma is a novel testing modality for non-invasive diagnosis of invasive mold disease (IMD) in immunocompromised patients. The accuracy of PCR compared to metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) for diagnosis of IMD remains unknown. Plasma samples from patients with proven and probable IMD and no IMD were tested with mold PCR and shotgun mNGS. Mold PCR detected Aspergillus species, Mucorales agents, Fusarium species, Scedosporium species, and Lomentospora prolificans. The sensitivity and specificity of mold PCR and mNGS were measured. Ninety-four patients with proven (48) and probable (48) IMD due to Aspergillus species (64), Mucorales agents (13), Scedosporium species and Lomentospora prolificans (13), and Fusarium species (6), and 62 patients with no IMD were included in this study. 99.4% (155) of the patients were immunosuppressed. The overall sensitivity and specificity were 62.5% (60/96; 95% CI 52.0-72.2) and 99.8% (535/536; 95% CI 99.0-100), respectively, for mold PCR and 43.8% (42/96; 95% CI 33.6-54.3; P < 0.001) and 99.6% (534/536; 95% CI 98.7-100; P = 1.0), respectively, for mNGS. The proportion of mold PCR-positive mNGS-negative results was 16.0% (4/25) in focal cases compared with 25.0% (11/44; P = 0.384) and 18.5% (5/27; P = 0.810) in multifocal and disseminated cases, respectively. The median PCR cycle threshold was 40.6 (IQR, 37.5-41.5) in PCR-positive mNGS-negative cases compared with 37.3 (IQR, 34.5-39.3; P = 0.004) in PCR-positive mNGS-positive cases. Plasma cfDNA PCR is more sensitive than mNGS for the diagnosis of IMD in immunocompromised patients. Lower sensitivity of mNGS was associated with lower mold cfDNA burden.
IMPORTANCE: Invasive mold disease (IMD) is a major cause of morbidity and mortality in immunocompromised patients. Early diagnosis and initiation of tailored antifungal therapy are critical for optimizing outcomes in patients with IMD. Detection of circulating fungal cell-free DNA (cfDNA) in the acellular fraction of blood is a novel testing modality that is increasingly used for early and non-invasive diagnosis of IMD. This study represents the first head-to-head accuracy study to compare the sensitivity and specificity of PCR with mNGS for the diagnosis of IMD. The study showed that the overall mold PCR was significantly more sensitive compared with mNGS, while both assays demonstrated very high specificity. Similar trends were observed in a smaller subgroup of…

articles.title: Perimenopause and cardiometabolic risk: emerging evidence, therapeutic opportunities and unanswered questions.
articles.journal: Climacteric : the journal of the International Menopause Society
articles.authors: El Khoudary SR, Deckey I, Fidecicchi T et al.
articles.abstract: Perimenopause is increasingly recognized as a critical period for cardiometabolic health. During the years surrounding the final menstrual period, adverse changes in lipid profiles, insulin sensitivity, body composition and vascular function accelerate beyond those expected from aging alone, concurrent with the emergence and peak severity of menopause symptoms. Accumulating evidence suggests that vasomotor symptoms and sleep disturbance are associated with adverse cardiometabolic profiles and increased cardiovascular disease risk. Mechanistic data indicate that autonomic dysregulation, inflammation and neuroendocrine systems may represent shared pathways linking symptom burden and cardiometabolic dysfunction. Complementing these findings, prospective studies demonstrate that poor cardiovascular health and metabolic dysfunction may predict subsequent symptom development, suggesting that cardiometabolic health influences the menopause transition experience itself. Together, these findings support a model in which perimenopause represents a physiologic convergence point where symptom burden and cardiometabolic risk intersect, with implications for symptom management and primary prevention. However, major evidence gaps remain, including the absence of interventional studies during perimenopause and uncertainty regarding whether these relationships are causal or therapeutically modifiable. Future research should determine whether targeting cardiometabolic health during this window can improve both cardiovascular outcomes and the symptom experience of the menopause transition.

articles.title: Twelve-Month Discontinuation of Contraceptive Methods: A Global Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.authors: Araújo FG, de Andrade GN, Borges ALV et al.
articles.abstract: Monitoring contraceptive discontinuation is crucial to reduce unmet needs and unintended pregnancies while supporting person-centered counseling. The objective is to summarize discontinuation rates by method type (long-acting reversible contraceptive [LARC] or short-acting reversible contraceptive [SARC]), type (abandonment or switching), and to describe reasons for discontinuation. This systematic review and meta-analysis searched for studies published between 2010 and 2020, with data collected before the COVID-19 pandemic,among women of reproductive age. Random-effects models were used to pool 12-month discontinuation rates and estimate the likelihood of switching versus abandoning methods. Fifty-four studies were included.
