The 12-month discontinuation rate (unit of analysis: women) was 16.2 percent for LARC users (n = 867,658) and 57.9 percent for SARC users (n = 18,882). SARC users had lower odds of switching than abandoning their method (odds ratio: 0.17; 95 percent confidence interval: 0.06-0.54), whereas no significant difference was observed among LARC users. By episode use, 12-month discontinuation was 53.7 percent (n = 13,445) for SARC and 16.0 percent for LARC (n = 2,277), lower in postpartum women (8.5 percent) and higher among married women (22.5 percent). Pregnancy desire was the main reason for discontinuation among women not in need of contraception, whereas side effects predominated among those still in need. Monitoring contraceptive discontinuation is essential to guide public health policies and meet sexual and reproductive rights.

articles.title: Pregnancy in a Woman with PGM1-CDG: Longitudinal Metabolic Follow-up During a Lactose-Supported Diet.
articles.journal: Journal of clinical research in pediatric endocrinology
articles.authors: Akyüzlüer Güneş MS, Koç Yekedüz M, Sürücü Kara İ et al.
articles.abstract: Phosphoglucomutase-1 deficiency (PGM1-CDG) is an ultra-rare, treatable congenital disorder of glycosylation characterized by multisystem involvement. Although galactose supplementation improves biochemical and clinical manifestations, data on pregnancy management and metabolic follow-up in affected women remain extremely limited. We report a woman with genetically confirmed PGM1-CDG who achieved a successful pregnancy with detailed longitudinal metabolic monitoring and maintenance of galactose intake through a lactose-supported diet. The patient was diagnosed during adolescence with a multisystem phenotype including short stature, craniofacial dysmorphism, hepatic involvement, elevated creatine kinase, reduced antithrombin III and left ventricular hypertrophy. She harbored a homozygous PGM1 c.1508G>A (p.Arg503Gln) variant. Long-term pharmaceutical D-galactose supplementation was associated with biochemical improvement, while cardiac involvement remained clinically stable. At 25 years of age, pregnancy was achieved through assisted reproductive technology with her spouse, who was heterozygous for a different PGM1 variant classified as a variant of uncertain significance (VUS). Given the limited safety data on pharmaceutical D-galactose use during pregnancy and uncertainty regarding potential fetal effects, galactose intake was maintained through a lactose-supported diet (estimated galactose intake of approximately 0.5 g/kg/day). Liver enzymes, coagulation parameters and cardiac status remained stable and creatine kinase levels did not worsen. Gestational diabetes was successfully managed with dietary modification alone. No thrombotic, hepatic or cardiac complications occurred. A healthy female infant was delivered by elective cesarean section at 38 weeks. The newborn had a normal metabolic evaluation and was a heterozygous carrier of the maternal PGM1 variant. This case provides detailed longitudinal data on pregnancy in PGM1-CDG and describes the maintenance of dietary galactose intake derived from lactose during a pregnancy with favorable maternal and neonatal outcomes.

articles.title: Sex and Menopausal Status Do Not Independently Predict Survival in Colorectal Liver Metastases.
articles.authors: Kim SJ, El Moheb M, Shen C et al.
articles.abstract: BackgroundEstrogen has been suggested to influence the development and progression of colorectal cancer, but its role in colorectal liver metastases (CRLM) remains unclear. We sought to explore the prognostic effects of estrogen in CRLM using sex and menopausal status as clinical proxies for endogenous estrogen exposure.MethodsPatients diagnosed with metastatic colorectal cancer to the liver between 2004 and 2017 were queried from the National Cancer Database. We performed three analyses to study the effect of estrogen on the overall survival (OS). First, we compared female patients <50 to age-matched males. Second, we compared female patients ≥50 to those <50. Finally, we compared female patients aged <45, 45-55, and >55. The totality of these analyses aimed to isolate sex at a fixed age, and to address age as a confounder.ResultsAmong 29,818 patients with CRLM, there was no difference in survival between pre-menopausal females and similar aged males (P = .850). Females <50 had a longer median survival (23.7 months) compared with females ≥50 (9.9 months, P < .001). When comparing pre- (<45), peri- (45-55), and post-menopausal (>55) females, we saw post-menopausal females experiencing shorter median survival (9.8 months) compared to pre-menopausal (24.4 months, P < .001) and peri-menopausal females (23.8 months, P < .001). However, there was no difference between pre- and peri-menopausal females (P = .763).DiscussionSex and menopausal status demonstrated no consistent survival difference among patients with CRLM. These results suggest that neither should be used as an independent prognostic indicator of survival benefit in CRLM.

articles.title: The Evolving Landscape of Stage III Endometrial Cancer-A Narrative Review of Management in Australia.
articles.journal: Journal of medical imaging and radiation oncology
articles.authors: Fong E, Lapuz C, Alvarez RJM et al.
articles.abstract: In Stage III endometrial cancer (EC), treatment paradigms have evolved from being based on a purely surgical pathology classification to a nuanced system integrating molecular risk stratification and advances in immunotherapy and targeted agents. This narrative review summarises current adjuvant management of stage III EC with an emphasis on clinical management in Australia, given the challenges in decision-making with the development of new predictive and prognostic markers and systemic agents. We discuss the importance of surgical staging, the evidence for radiotherapy and chemotherapy, explore emerging targeted and immunotherapy options, and outline barriers such as cost, access to molecular testing and systemic therapy in the Australian context. Molecular profiling is transforming adjuvant therapy in EC, but gaps in knowledge persist. Further research will help clarify the role of targeted treatments and immunotherapy in the adjuvant setting in this group of patients.

articles.title: Causal inference study on the influence of the anxious/worrier trait on the risk of endometriosis: Two-sample Mendelian randomization.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.authors: Wan R, Fan W, Chen D et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Recent observational studies have identified an association between the anxious/worrier trait and endometriosis. However, the causal nature of this relationship remains unclear.
METHODS: Summary statistics from genome-wide association studies were used to identify independent genetic variants associated with the anxious/worrier trait, which served as instrumental variables in a two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) study. Causal estimates for the effect of emotional factors on endometriosis risk were obtained using inverse variance weighting, MR-Egger regression, and weighted median methods. Reverse MR analysis was then used to assess the impact of endometriosis on emotional indicators. Sensitivity analyses included the MR-Egger intercept test, leave-one-out analysis, and Cochran's Q test, which were used to detect potential pleiotropy and heterogeneity.
RESULTS: The inverse variance weighted analysis indicated that the anxious/worrier trait significantly elevated the risk of developing endometriosis (odds ratio 3.84; 95% confidence interval 1.42-10.41, P = 0.008). The results of the reverse MR analysis did not indicate a significant causal effect of endometriosis on emotional indicators (P > 0.05).
CONCLUSION: This study provides genetic evidence for a causal relationship between emotional factors (anxious/worrier trait) and endometriosis. However, the specific biological pathways involved warrant further investigation.

articles.title: Fertility preservation for patients undergoing pelvic malignancy treatment: Current strategies, emerging approaches, and clinical considerations.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.authors: Apelian S, Mathyk B, Agarwal N et al.
articles.abstract: Advances in cancer treatment have improved survival rates for many patients with pelvic malignancies, highlighting the importance of long-term reproductive outcomes and overall quality of life. Pelvic radiotherapy, chemotherapy, and multimodal treatment can cause substantial and permanent injury to ovarian reserve, uterine function, or both. Oncofertility can be clinically complex because reproductive risks and available options vary according to patient age, pubertal status, cancer type, treatment urgency, planned radiotherapy field, chemotherapy regimen and dosage, baseline ovarian reserve, desire for future pregnancy, and expertise. The present review summarizes established and emerging fertility preservation options for patients undergoing treatment for pelvic malignancies. Cryopreservation focused options, including embryo, oocyte, and ovarian tissue cryopreservation, can preserve gametes, embryos, or ovarian tissue before gonadotoxic therapy but do not protect the uterus from radiation related injury. Surgical approaches, including ovarian transposition, uterine ventrofixation, and uterine transposition, are aimed at reducing radiation exposure to reproductive organs, although their effectiveness depends on surgical technique, radiation planning, and use of systemic therapy. Uterine transplantation may provide a restorative option for selected patients with irreversible uterine factor infertility but remains highly specialized and resource intensive. Because each option differs in timing, evidence base, risks, costs, resource requirements, and applicability across patient groups, fertility preservation should be discussed early and incorporated into multidisciplinary cancer care. Continued research is needed to better define reproductive outcomes, pregnancy safety, complications, and comparative effectiveness of emerging approaches.

articles.title: Association between urine protein-to-creatinine ratio and postpartum resistant hypertension in patients with severe preeclampsia: A retrospective cohort study.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.authors: Annicchiarico W, Gutiérrez Marin JH, Posada RAG et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Our objective was to investigate the association between elevated urine protein-to-creatinine ratio (UPCR) and resistant hypertension during postpartum hospitalization in patients with severe preeclampsia at a tertiary care center in Colombia.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study was conducted in Medellín, Colombia. Patients aged >18 years diagnosed with severe preeclampsia who underwent UPCR assessment were included. Associations between elevated UPCR (≥0.3) and resistant hypertension during postpartum hospitalization were evaluated using robust Poisson regression models.
RESULTS: A total of 261 patients were included in the study. Bivariate analysis showed that resistant hypertension in the postpartum period was more frequent in the UPCR ≥0.3 group than in the UPCR <0.3 group (43.2% vs. 12.7%; risk ratio 3.69; 95% confidence interval 1.92-7.07). After adjustment for maternal age, body mass index, and gestational age at diagnosis, elevated UPCR remained independently associated with resistant hypertension (adjusted risk ratio 4.87; 95% confidence interval 1.86-12.76). Earlier gestational age at diagnosis was also independently associated with resistant hypertension.
CONCLUSION: The UPCR is independently associated with the development of resistant hypertension during postpartum hospitalization in patients with severe preeclampsia.

articles.title: Identifying a critical cervical length threshold for predicting early delivery at 24-34 weeks.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.authors: Anteby M, Dominsky O, Wertheimer KO et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study evaluates the association between cervical length measured at first diagnosis of a short cervix and delivery within 14 days among symptomatic and asymptomatic singleton pregnancies at 240/7-336/7 weeks of gestation.
METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted comprising singleton pregnancies diagnosed with a short cervix (≤ 25 mm) at 240/7-336/7 weeks, including both symptomatic and asymptomatic women. The primary outcome was spontaneous delivery within 14 days with delivery within 7 days as a secondary outcome. The optimal cervical length (CL) threshold was identified using Youden's index and internally validated. Predictors for delivery within 14 days were analyzed using multivariable logistic regression.
RESULTS: Among 1027 pregnancies, 94 (9.2%) delivered within 14 days and 53 (5.2%) within 7 days. CL was significantly associated with gestational age at delivery (P < 0.001). A CL of ≤ 14 mm was the optimal threshold for both outcomes (14 days: area under the receiver operating characteristic curve [AUC] 0.59, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.52-0.65, sensitivity 38.3%, specificity 79.0%, positive predictive value 15.5%, negative predictive value 92.7%; 7 days: AUC 0.65, 95% CI 0.57-0.73). Delivery within 14 days occurred in 15.5% of women with CL ≤ 14 mm versus 7.3% of those with longer cervices, and CL ≤ 14 mm remained independently associated with the outcome after adjustment (adjusted odds ratio 2.62; 95% CI 1.59-4.27; P < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: In singleton pregnancies with a newly diagnosed short cervix at 240/7-336/7 weeks, a CL of ≤ 14 mm is independently associated with delivery within 14 days, although discrimination is modest. The threshold might have greater value when combined with symptoms, gestational age, and other clinical factors.

articles.title: Construction of a clinical model for early prediction of gestational diabetes mellitus based on women of increased maternal age singleton pregnant women.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.authors: Zhou W, Zhang J, Li C et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: This study develops and validates an early clinical prediction model for gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) specifically in women of increased maternal age with singleton pregnancies, thereby facilitating early identification of high-risk individuals and timely targeted intervention.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 338 women of increased maternal age with singleton pregnancies (82 diagnosed with GDM) who received prenatal care at the First People's Hospital of Changde between January 2023 and June 2024, comprising the training set. An additional 232 women (70 with GDM) seen between July 2024 and June 2025 comprised the validation set. Clinical data were collected and risk factors for GDM were identified using logistic regression analysis. A prediction model was constructed using R software. Model performance was assessed using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves, with internal validation performed via K-fold cross-validation, and external validation carried out in the independent validation set.
RESULTS: A significant between-group difference was observed in assisted reproductive technology history between the training and validation sets (Z = 8.631, P = 0.003). In the training set, pre-pregnancy body mass index (BMI, calculated as weight in kilograms divided by the square of height in meters), fasting plasma glucose, uric acid, and triglyceride levels differed significantly between the GDM and non-GDM groups (P < 0.05 for all). Multivariate logistic regression identified all four parameters as independent risk factors for GDM (P < 0.05). The ROC curve analysis yielded an area under the curve of 0.773 for the training set and 0.808 for the validation set, indicating good predictive performance.
CONCLUSION: We established a GDM prediction model for women of increased maternal age with singleton pregnancies, incorporating four readily available clinical indicators. The model demonstrated satisfactory discrimination and generalizability upon both internal and external validation.

articles.title: Postpartum Medicaid Extension (PME): The Emergence of a National Policy and the Illinois Experience in Adopting the PME.
articles.journal: Journal of health care for the poor and underserved
articles.authors: Handler A, Johnson K, Mondestin T et al.
articles.abstract: The U.S. faces a maternal health crisis. In response, the Postpartum Medicaid Extension (PME), giving states the option to provide Medicaid coverage through 12 months postpartum, arose as a central policy solution. Using the policy streams framework of Kingdon, we provide an overview of the history of the federal action to pass the PME. A case study of PME adoption in Illinois follows. Given increased attention to the maternal health crisis, maternal mortality was identified as a problem on the federal agenda. Dozens of bills were introduced across multiple sessions of Congress and Presidential administrations. Policy entrepreneurs, including advocates from the Black Maternal Health movement, seized a window of opportunity, leading to the passage of the PME. As of February 2026, virtually all states have adopted the PME with many lessons to be learned. Ultimately, the success of the PME will depend upon a commitment to protecting Medicaid.

articles.title: Dinoprostone Versus Balloon Catheter for Cervical Ripening in Multiparous Women Undergoing Induction of Labor: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.journal: The journal of obstetrics and gynaecology research
articles.authors: Abu Shqara R, Maklade R, Haj L et al.
articles.abstract:
AIM: To compare maternal and neonatal outcomes of induction strategies initiated with slow-release vaginal dinoprostone (10 mg) or balloon catheter in multiparous women undergoing term induction of labor with an unfavorable cervix.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 802 multiparous women with singleton pregnancies at ≥ 37 weeks' gestation, Bishop score < 8, and a medical indication for induction of labor at a tertiary university-affiliated center (2020-2025). Women underwent cervical ripening with either a balloon catheter (n = 522) or a slow-release vaginal dinoprostone insert (n = 280). The co-primary outcomes were the cervical ripening-to-delivery interval and delivery within 24 h. Multivariable analyses identified independent predictors of delivery interval and cesarean birth.
RESULTS: Compared with balloon catheter, dinoprostone was associated with a shorter cervical ripening-to-delivery interval (11.6 vs. 19.4 h; p < 0.001). Delivery within 12 h was more frequent with dinoprostone (51.4% vs. 26.1%; p < 0.001), whereas delivery within 24 h did not differ significantly between groups (75.7% vs. 71.1%; p = 0.183). Dinoprostone was also associated with a higher spontaneous vaginal delivery rate (95.0% vs. 90.0%; p = 0.015) and a lower cesarean delivery rate (3.2% vs. 8.2%; p = 0.006). Intrapartum fever occurred less frequently with dinoprostone (1.4% vs. 4.2%; p = 0.036), while no statistically significant differences were observed in measured neonatal outcomes, including NICU admission.
CONCLUSIONS: Among multiparous women undergoing term induction of labor, dinoprostone was associated with a shorter cervical ripening-to-delivery interval, higher spontaneous vaginal delivery rates, and lower cesarean rates than balloon catheter. Delivery within 24 h was similar between groups, with no significant differences in measured neonatal outcomes.

articles.title: Sex Hormones as Regulators of the Age- and Sex-Dependent Benefits of Caloric Restriction: An Emerging Research Protocol of a Controlled Dietary Intervention (The GendAge Weight Loss Study).
articles.authors: Lonnie M, Speakman J, Horgan G et al.
articles.abstract: With nearly two-thirds of the UK population living with overweight or obesity, there is an urgent necessity for evidence-based public health guidance to promote a healthy weight. Current weight management advice centres on lifestyle modification. However, existing dieting recommendations fail to consider sex or age. This is a surprising oversight, as it is well established that health outcomes vary significantly between men and women across the lifespan. Our preliminary work in mice and humans suggests young females are more resistant than males to calorie-restriction (CR)-induced fat loss and reductions in energy expenditure, and that this resistance diminishes in older, post-menopausal participants-implicating oestrogen as a possible modulator of CR response. Further, the menopause may have an impact on fat storage linked to changes in sex hormones. This article describes emerging research being done through a controlled feeding study in 75 younger and older men and women. This study will directly test whether CR's effects on fat mass, energy expenditure and glucose homeostasis are age- and sex-dependent, and whether HRT use in post-menopausal women restores a CR response more similar to that of younger women. Energy expenditure and body composition will be assessed using gold-standard techniques, including doubly labelled water, alongside blood and abdominal adipose tissue sampling to investigate underlying hormonal mechanisms. The findings of this new study will clarify whether dietary weight-management advice should be tailored by sex, age, or menopausal/HRT status, informing more precise, evidence-based obesity guidance and supporting women's health and healthy ageing.

articles.title: Exploring Implicit Bias Training in Nursing: An Integrative Review.
articles.authors: Killam BA, Dyck MJ, Blakeman JR et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Implicit bias refers to unconscious attitudes and beliefs about a person that can influence decisions without awareness. Nurses may hold biases that lead to lower quality care and contribute to health care disparities, such as higher maternal mortality rates and unequal pain management for black women. Efforts to address this issue have generated interest in implicit bias training (IBT), which aims to increase awareness and reduce biased behavior.
PURPOSE: We aimed to explore and describe the existing research interventions related to IBT that have been used in nursing.
METHODS: We conducted an integrative review using Whittemore and Knafl's integrative review approach. Database searches were conducted in spring 2025. Database included Cumulative Index to Nursing and Allied Health Literature, PubMed, and PsycINFO. The Johns Hopkins Evidence-Based Practice Model was adopted to evaluate the level and quality of the studies.
RESULTS: Fourteen studies were included. IBT led to positive experiences among nursing professionals and an immediate improvement in implicit bias awareness and knowledge. The studies employed diverse methods of delivery and educational strategies. Limitations of the studies include a lack of long-term follow-up on awareness, knowledge, and mitigation practice behaviors. Other significant limitations involve small sample sizes and a lack of methodological rigor.
CONCLUSIONS: While IBT appears to positively impact nursing practice, additional research is needed. Significant gaps remain in demonstrating robust evidence, long-term effectiveness, and impact on patient outcomes.

articles.title: Recurrent venous thromboembolism despite natural cycle frozen embryo transfer in a woman with a history of pregnancy-related venous thromboembolism: A case report.
articles.authors: Sato Y, Nishio E, Oikawa S et al.
articles.abstract: Pregnancy-associated venous thromboembolism (VTE) is a major cause of maternal morbidity and mortality. Pregnancies achieved by in vitro fertilization carry an increased risk of VTE, particularly during early gestation. A 33-year-old woman developed deep vein thrombosis during late pregnancy in her first spontaneous conception despite no identifiable thrombophilia. During a subsequent pregnancy achieved by natural cycle frozen embryo transfer, which was selected to avoid exogenous estrogen exposure and potentially reduce the thrombotic risk compared with hormone replacement cycles, she developed recurrent VTE at 8 weeks of gestation. Anticoagulation therapy was initiated, and an inferior vena cava (IVC) filter was placed in late pregnancy because of persistent thrombus and delivery-related risk. A cesarean section was successfully performed, and the IVC filter was removed postpartum after regression of the thrombus. Although natural cycle frozen embryo transfer may reduce the thrombotic risk compared with hormone replacement cycles, it does not eliminate the risk of recurrent VTE in women with a history of pregnancy-associated thrombosis. Early initiation of anticoagulation and careful peripartum management, including selective use of IVC filters, are essential in high-risk patients.

articles.title: Blood Management Strategies in Placenta Accreta Spectrum.
articles.authors: Abu-Nayla U, Bashir Fazari A, Sulaiman K et al.
articles.abstract: Placenta accreta spectrum (PAS) presents a major challenge in obstetric care because attempted placental separation may result in rapid and life-threatening hemorrhage. As PAS is often suspected before delivery, there is an opportunity to identify correctable risks and prepare for anticipated blood loss. This narrative review examines blood-management strategies throughout the antenatal, intraoperative, and postoperative periods. A targeted narrative search of PubMed and PubMed Central, supplemented by searches of journal and publisher websites, was conducted for literature available through September 2026. Antenatal management focuses on identifying and treating maternal anemia, referring patients to experienced centers, and developing a multidisciplinary delivery plan. Perioperative preparation includes coordination with the transfusion service, timely access to appropriate blood components, clear criteria for activating a major obstetric hemorrhage protocol, and defined responsibilities for each team member. Blood-product preparation should be individualized according to the severity suggested by prenatal imaging and the anticipated anatomical extent of placental invasion, ranging from suspected accreta to increta or percreta. Key intraoperative blood-conservation measures include intraoperative cell salvage and timely administration of tranexamic acid when clinically indicated, particularly during significant hemorrhage. Viscoelastic hemostatic testing, fibrinogen-directed therapy, and selected interventional radiology procedures may also contribute to individualized management. However, evidence supporting these interventions remains inconsistent and is frequently derived from observational studies, expert consensus, or broader obstetric hemorrhage populations rather than PAS-specific randomized trials. Consequently, blood-management plans should reflect the anticipated severity of PAS, the patient's clinical condition, and the expertise and resources available at the treating institution. A structured and individualized approach linking antenatal optimization, multidisciplinary preparation, timely hemorrhage control, and postoperative surveillance may support safer and more efficient care for patients with PAS.

articles.title: Agreement Between Immediate and Six-Week Postpartum Testing for Detecting Abnormal Glucose Tolerance in Women with Gestational Diabetes Mellitus.
articles.authors: Chunsanit S, Kamlungkuea T, Jatavan P et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the prevalence of abnormal glucose tolerance at six weeks postpartum among women with gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) and to evaluate the agreement between early postpartum and six-week postpartum oral glucose tolerance test (GTT).
METHODS: This prospective repeated-measures study included Thai women with singleton pregnancies, no pregestational diabetes, and a diagnosis of GDM. Participants were consecutively recruited upon admission to the labor and delivery unit. All participants underwent a 75 g, 2-hour GTT both during the immediate postpartum prior to hospital discharge and at six weeks postpartum. Glucose tolerance status was categorized as normal glucose tolerance and abnormal GTT. Agreement between the two testing periods was evaluated using Cohen's kappa coefficient.
RESULTS: A total of 158 women were included in the analysis. The prevalence of abnormal glucose tolerance at six weeks postpartum was 44.9% (71/158), including impaired GTT in 66 women (41.8%) and diabetes mellitus in 5 women (3.2%). Among women with abnormal GTT at six weeks postpartum, 42.3% (30/71) had normal early postpartum results. Conversely, 44.6% (33/74) of women with abnormal early postpartum findings demonstrated normal GTT at six weeks. The Cohen's kappa coefficient was 0.197, indicating poor agreement. Agreement for diabetes mellitus diagnosis was similarly low (kappa = 0.201).
CONCLUSION: Early postpartum OGTT demonstrated poor agreement with six-week postpartum testing and showed limited utility as a standalone screening strategy for postpartum dysglycemia among women with GDM. Early postpartum testing may not accurately reflect glycemic status at 6 weeks postpartum, potentially leading to misclassification.

articles.title: E-Cervix Assessment of Cervical Softening During Medication Abortion: A Single-Center Observational Study.
articles.authors: Li W, Shi H, Lian H et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cervical softening is essential for successful medication abortion in early pregnancy, yet existing assessments do not adequately quantify biomechanical changes in cervical tissue. This study primarily aimed to characterize cervical changes before and after medication abortion using E-Cervix, with an exploratory secondary analysis of their association with cumulative carboprost methylate suppository dose.
METHODS: This single-center observational pre-post study included 91 women undergoing medication abortion in early pregnancy. All participants received the same mifepristone regimen, and the cumulative carboprost methylate dose ranged from 0.5 to 3.5 mg. Pre-post changes in six cervical parameters were evaluated, and baseline-adjusted linear regression was used to compare the 0.5-1 mg and >1 mg groups.
RESULTS: After medication abortion, ECI increased by 0.92 (95% CI, 0.68-1.16), HR decreased by 0.18 (95% CI, 0.15-0.20), IOS increased by 0.11 (95% CI, 0.08-0.13), and EOS increased by 0.08 (95% CI, 0.06-0.10); CL shortened, and the IOS/EOS ratio increased. The FDR-adjusted P values for all six comparisons were <0.05. The 0.5-1 mg and >1 mg groups included 68 and 23 participants, respectively; after baseline adjustment, dose group was not significantly associated with any post-treatment cervical parameter.
CONCLUSIONS: E-Cervix quantitatively characterized multidimensional cervical softening during medication abortion, supporting its potential utility for objective assessment of cervical changes. In the exploratory observational dose analysis, no association was observed between higher cumulative carboprost methylate dose and greater cervical softening.

articles.title: Mechanism Analysis of Chronic Inflammation in Polycystic Ovary Syndrome and Targeted Therapeutic Strategies Based on Bioactive Constituents of Traditional Chinese Medicine.
articles.authors: Zhang L, Gao Y, Fan R et al.
articles.abstract: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is a prevalent endocrine and reproductive disorder in women of childbearing age. Chronic inflammatory status is common among PCOS patients, and numerous studies have verified that this population exhibits dysregulated inflammatory cytokines and immune cell imbalance. Such inflammatory disorders are characterized by aberrant expression of pro-inflammatory cytokines, inflammasomes and inflammatory markers. These abnormalities not only impair the female reproductive system and trigger pathological conditions including irregular menstruation and infertility, but also exert long-term adverse impacts on multiple systemic organs such as the liver and cardiovascular system. Hyperandrogenism, insulin resistance, hyperinsulinemia, obesity, gut microbiota dysbiosis and hypothalamic-pituitary-ovarian axis dysfunction observed in PCOS patients can all induce inflammatory dysregulation. In recent years, bioactive constituents of traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) have been widely adopted in the clinical management of PCOS with remarkable therapeutic efficacy. Starting from the prevalent inflammatory phenotype in women with PCOS, this review elaborates on the pathological correlation and underlying mechanisms between PCOS and inflammation. It summarizes the roles of five inflammation-related signaling pathways (NF-κB, PI3K/Akt, NLRP3, JAK/STAT, and AMPK) and the mechanisms of action of 18 TCM bioactive constituents that target these pathways in PCOS-related inflammation, providing a reference for future PCOS research directions and therapies.

articles.title: Evolving Systemic Intensification Strategies Beyond CCRT in Locally Advanced Cervical Cancer.
articles.authors: Cheng T, Niu R, Li X et al.
articles.abstract: Concurrent chemoradiotherapy (CCRT) remains the standard of care for locally advanced cervical cancer (LACC); however, 30-40% of patients experience recurrence, prompting evaluation of systemic treatment intensification to improve outcomes over CCRT alone. This critical review synthesizes evidence from PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library up to January 2026, evaluating clinical trials of intensification strategies categorized by treatment timing: neoadjuvant, concurrent, and adjuvant modalities. Historical attempts to intensify treatment through adjuvant chemotherapy have failed to confer survival benefits with the regimens studied, often increasing toxicity without efficacy (OUTBACK). However, recent Phase III trials have reported survival benefits with specific treatment regimens. Specifically, induction chemotherapy followed by CCRT (INTERLACE) and pembrolizumab with CCRT followed by maintenance (KEYNOTE-A18) have demonstrated significant improvements in overall survival, whereas additional concurrent cytotoxic agents have not consistently improved outcomes and may increase toxicity. CCRT remains the cornerstone; intensification should follow the tested regimen, eligibility criteria, and toxicity profile. PD-L1-based selection and the independent benefit of adjuvant immunotherapy require further validation.

articles.title: Serum inhibin B/follicle-stimulating hormone ratio as a predictor of testicular pathology in azoospermic men undergoing testicular sperm extraction: a retrospective study.
articles.authors: Ogras MS, Yildirim K, Emiroglu M
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Non-obstructive azoospermia (NOA) represents a severe form of male infertility characterized by impaired spermatogenesis and heterogeneous histopathological findings. Identifying candidate non-invasive biomarkers associated with underlying testicular histopathology before surgical sperm retrieval may provide additional information during preoperative evaluation and patient counseling.
INTRODUCTION: This study aimed to investigate the association of serum inhibin B (INHB), follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH), and their ratio (INHB/FSH) with histopathological groups in men undergoing microdissection testicular sperm extraction (micro-TESE).
MATERIALS AND METHODS: A total of 73 men with NOA who underwent micro-TESE were retrospectively analyzed. Patients with obstructive azoospermia, endocrine disorders, or incomplete data were excluded. Serum FSH, luteinizing hormone (LH), testosterone, and INHB levels were measured within 2 months before surgery. Based on histopathological evaluation, patients were classified into five histopathological groups: Sertoli cell-only syndrome (SCOS), early maturation arrest (EMA), late maturation arrest (LMA), hypospermatogenesis (HSG), and normospermatogenesis (NS). The association between hormonal parameters and histopathological groups was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis and binary logistic regression.
RESULTS: The INHB/FSH ratio differed significantly among the histopathological groups (p < 0.001). Receiver operating characteristic analysis demonstrated moderate-to-high discriminative performance, with area under the curve values ranging from 0.77 to 0.91. In this exploratory cohort, provisional thresholds were observed across the histopathological groups, with lower values generally associated with SCOS, EMA, and LMA and higher values associated with HSG and NS. These findings should be considered hypothesis-generating and require internal and external validation before clinical application. Binary logistic regression demonstrated that higher INHB/FSH ratios were significantly associated with favorable sperm retrieval outcomes, with an odds ratio of 2.36 per 10-unit increase.
CONCLUSIONS: The serum INHB/FSH ratio was associated with histopathological groups and sperm retrieval outcomes in men with NOA undergoing micro-TESE. These findings suggest that the INHB/FSH ratio may warrant further investigation as a candidate non-invasive biomarker associated with histopathological…

articles.title: Facilitators and Barriers to Discharge Education for Puerperal Sepsis Prevention After Caesarean Section: A Qualitative Study at a Tertiary Health Facility in Southwestern Uganda.
articles.authors: Luwaga R, Ngonzi J, Bajunirwe F et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Maternal mortality remains a major global health concern, disproportionately affecting low- and middle-income countries. Puerperal sepsis remains an important contributor to maternal morbidity and mortality, with caesarean delivery increasing women's risk of infection. As caesarean deliveries increase, strengthening strategies to prevent puerperal sepsis throughout the continuum of care is increasingly important. Although prevention efforts have focused largely on antenatal and intrapartum care, post-discharge self-care and education remain insufficiently emphasized. Evidence from Mbarara Regional Referral Hospital indicates gaps in women's knowledge and practices regarding post-caesarean self-care, highlighting the need for effective discharge education to support prevention, early recognition, and timely care-seeking for puerperal sepsis. However, the effectiveness of discharge education depends not only on the information provided but also on healthcare providers' ability and willingness to deliver it within the available health-system environment. The COM-B framework provides a useful lens for understanding these influences by examining providers' capability, opportunities within the health system, and motivation to deliver discharge education. Understanding these factors is therefore important for identifying barriers and facilitators that can be addressed to strengthen puerperal sepsis prevention after discharge. The study aimed to explore the facilitators and barriers to the provision of discharge education for puerperal sepsis prevention following caesarean delivery.
METHODS: This study employed an exploratory qualitative design at Mbarara Regional Referral Hospital. A total of 12 healthcare providers, comprising six senior house officers and six midwives, were purposively selected, provided informed consent, and participated in in-depth interviews. The interviews were audio-recorded and transcribed verbatim. Thematic analysis was conducted by systematically coding statements from the transcripts, organizing similar codes into subthemes, and subsequently synthesizing the subthemes into overarching themes.
RESULTS: Twelve healthcare providers (six midwives and six senior house officers) participated in the study. Under Capability, knowledge, clinical experience, and awareness of puerperal sepsis and its prevention facilitated discharge education. Opportunity was facilitated by the availability of discharge forms and opportunities to…

articles.title: Ovarian Fibroma With Minor Sex Cord Elements and Luteinized Cells in an 81-Year-Old Woman: A Case Report With Molecular Findings and Review of the Literature.
articles.authors: Ali A, Gandhi S, Potts C et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ovarian fibroma with minor sex cord elements (MSCE) is a fibroma or fibrothecoma containing scattered sex cord-type elements that occupy less than 10% of the tumor area. First described by Young and Scully in 1983, it is not recognized as a separate entity in the current World Health Organization classification, and its behavior follows that of the underlying stromal tumor. About two dozen ovarian cases have been published, a number that probably reflects under-reporting rather than true rarity. Reported patients range from 13 to 81 years of age.
CASE: An 81-year-old woman with a remote total hysterectomy with ovarian preservation presented with abdominal discomfort, constipation, and a pelvic mass that computed tomography initially described as uterine. Pelvic ultrasonography showed a 10.6 cm complex cystic mass adjacent to the vaginal cuff. Robotic-assisted bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy removed a 9 cm right ovarian mass. Histology showed a fibroma with scattered tubules, trabeculae, and nests of sex cord-type cells and a few clusters of luteinized cells, together less than 10% of the tumor; the sex cord elements expressed SF-1, WT1, calretinin, and inhibin. A targeted next-generation sequencing panel performed by the consulting reference laboratory showed no reportable variants, including no FOXL2 c.402C>G mutation, and microsatellite stability. Pelvic washings were negative. She had no clinical signs of hormone excess before surgery; hot flashes reported at follow-up were not investigated biochemically and have several possible explanations. There was no recurrence at 8 months.
CONCLUSION: This case adds an octogenarian patient and targeted sequencing data to the limited published experience with ovarian fibroma with MSCE. Recognition of the minor sex cord component did not change management; its practical importance lies in excluding adult granulosa cell tumor, for which adequate sampling and, when needed, FOXL2 mutation analysis are useful.

articles.title: Maternal Mortality Across a Multi-Hospital Health System in Saudi Arabia: A Retrospective Study (2016-2024).
articles.authors: Saeid N, Alshabanah R, Aldraihem HS et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Maternal mortality remains a pressing global health challenge and is a vital indicator of healthcare quality. Despite improvements in Saudi Arabia, preventable maternal fatalities continue to occur, with insufficient research on regional disparities.
OBJECTIVE: This study seeks to assess the maternal mortality ratio (MMR) and its causes across five hospitals within the Ministry of National Guard Health Affairs in Saudi Arabia and evaluate it is main causes,thereby addressing a gap in maternal mortality data in the Gulf region.
METHODS: This retrospective, multicenter, descriptive study included all maternal deaths occurring during pregnancy or within 42 days postpartum between 2016 and 2024 across five National Guard hospitals in Riyadh, Jeddah, Madinah, Al-Ahsa, and Dammam. Data were extracted from hospital records and analyzed descriptively using SPSS version 28.
RESULTS: Eighteen maternal deaths were identified over the nine-year period, yielding an overall MMR of 6.2 per 100,000 live births (mean age at death 29.8 ± 6.3 years). MMR varied considerably by year, from 0.00/100,000 in 2017 to 37.5/100,000 in 2020. Pregnancy-related complications accounted for 50% of deaths (9/18), most commonly venous thromboembolism (66.7%). Non-obstetric causes included COVID-19 (16.7%), unknown cause (16.7%), brain tumor (5.6%), and myocarditis (5.6%). Most deaths occurred in women with parity 1-3 (61.1%), split evenly between vaginal and caesarean delivery (50% each). Geographic variation was marked: Riyadh recorded deaths in most years with a peak in 2020; Dammam and Al-Ahsa each showed sporadic extreme spikes; Jeddah showed intermittent elevations; no deaths occurred in Madinah.
CONCLUSION: The overall MMR at these hospitals is comparatively low to global figures, significant variations across different cities and years, alongside a notable number of deaths with unspecified causes, underscore the need for standardized mortality reviews, autopsy confirmations for suspected embolic deaths, and continuous targeted monitoring.

articles.title: Prospective case series of an articulated laparoscopic camera system in minimally invasive surgery in gynaecology: an IDEAL stage 2a study.
articles.authors: Ng TY, Ngu SF, Ng SY et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Precision Robotics' Sirius Robotic Flexible Endoscopic System is a new fully integrated compact laparoscopic camera system with a disposable single-use flexible tip that can change its viewing direction. The aim of this Idea, Development, Exploration, Assessment, Long-term follow-up stage 2a study was to assess its clinical performance and safety.
DESIGN: Prospective multi-institution, multisurgeon study.
SETTING: The study was conducted in two multispecialty hospitals.
PARTICIPANTS: Women aged 18-70 years scheduled for gynaecological laparoscopic surgery were invited to participate. An information sheet and consent form were available for the women and an informed consent was obtained. Twenty-five participants completed this study.
INTERVENTIONS: The laparoscopic procedures were done in the usual manner. The only difference was the Sirius system was used in place of the usual conventional laparoscope. All other procedures and instruments including the number of ports used remained the same.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Primary outcome was camera users and surgeon's view and experience; iterations and modifications to the system. Secondary outcomes were the incidence of intraoperative and postoperative complications during the first 6 weeks following surgery and duration of surgery.
RESULTS: 100% (25/25) of women had their procedure completed successfully using the Sirius System. There were no intraoperative complications. The median operating time was 68 min (range: 32-257 min). Users agreed that the improved field of view was beneficial for laparoscopic surgery. Iterative improvements were made in the user interface and manufacturing quality.
CONCLUSIONS: The study demonstrated stability and safety of the Sirius System across different institutions and teams for intermediate and major minimally invasive laparoscopic procedures in gynaecology. Further studies are needed to confirm it can replace a conventional laparoscope in the surgical workflow.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: NCT05048407.

articles.title: Association between interspousal communication on family planning and contraceptive use: a cross-sectional study in Temeke municipality, Tanzania.
articles.authors: Mshubilo AT, Upor R, Mbotwa CH et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Interspousal communication is a key determinant of contraceptive use. In Tanzania, where fertility rates remain high, the extent to which spousal dialogue influences the adoption of family planning (FP) methods remains underexplored. This study examined the association between interspousal communication and contraceptive use among couples in Temeke Municipality.
METHODS: A cross-sectional study was conducted in Temeke, Tanzania, involving 342 married couples aged 18-49 years. Participants were selected using two-stage cluster random sampling. Data on FP use and interspousal communication were collected via structured questionnaires and analysed using STATA V.18. We examined crude associations using bivariate logistic regression and an adjusted analysis using a multivariable logistic regression model.
RESULTS: The prevalence of FP use among women was 88%. Overall, 78.9% of couples had concordant reports indicating that both spouses independently confirmed discussing FP with each other. In multivariable analysis, couples who engaged in FP discussions were significantly more likely to use contraceptives (adjusted OR=15.2, 95% CI 5.87 to 39.49, p<0.001). Other significant predictors included the number of children and exposure to FP programmes. Education and employment status were not independently associated with FP use after adjustment.
CONCLUSIONS: Interspousal communication is associated with contraceptive use among couples in Tanzania. These findings highlight the significance of incorporating couple-based communication strategies into reproductive health programmes. Interventions that encourage open dialogue between spouses could enhance contraceptive uptake and facilitate informed decision-making regarding reproductive health.

articles.title: Cost-effectiveness of a blended learning approach for maternal and child health professional development training in Ethiopia: a quasi-experimental economic evaluation.
articles.authors: Tiruneh GT, Tezera R, Hunegnaw BM et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Ethiopia has integrated blended learning into the national continuous professional development system to address persistent gaps in in-service training access, cost and quality and strengthen primary healthcare providers' capacity to deliver reproductive, maternal, newborn and child health (RMNCH) services. However, evidence on its effectiveness and cost-effectiveness remains limited, particularly regarding provider adherence, client experience and quality of care. Guided by implementation science principles, the Kirkpatrick framework and activity-based costing, we assessed the cost-effectiveness of blended learning for improving RMNCH service delivery.
METHODS: We conducted a quasi-experimental, post-test economic evaluation with a separate control group. Data were collected in October 2025 through facility audits, direct observations and exit interviews with providers trained through blended learning and untrained providers in control sites. The primary effectiveness outcomes were composite quality indices integrating adherence to evidence-based antenatal care (ANC) and family planning practices and client experience of care. Costs were estimated using activity-based costing from a health-system perspective. We assessed cost per trainee, incremental costs and savings and cost-effectiveness.
RESULTS: Blended learning improved ANC provision scores by 10.4 percentage points and family planning scores by 25.9 percentage points compared with controls (Cohen's d=0.72 and 1.30 respectively; p<0.01). Client experience improved by 3.3 percentage points (Cohen's d=0.36; p<0.01). Composite quality indices increased by 10.8 and 22.9 percentage points for ANC and family planning, respectively (Cohen's d=0.64 and 1.35; p<0.01). Training cost US$262.81 per trainee with blended learning versus US$360.10 for face-to-face training, saving US$97.29 (27%). Blended learning was dominant for both ANC and family planning, combining lower costs with greater effectiveness.
CONCLUSION: Blended learning improved RMNCH service quality while reducing training costs. Sustaining and scaling this approach will require investment in digital infrastructure, supportive implementation systems and health-worker capacity, alongside longer term monitoring to determine whether improvements in provider performance translate into population-level RMNCH outcomes.

articles.title: Severe intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy associated with thiopurines: Case report and review of the literature.
articles.authors: Benhaddadi C, Xu JJ, Tan J et al.
articles.abstract: Intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy (ICP) is associated with significant maternal morbidity and fetal risk. We describe a 31-year-old primiparous patient with quiescent systemic lupus erythematosus and lupus nephritis on azathioprine, hydroxychloroquine, and tacrolimus who developed generalized pruritus at 29 weeks. Workup showed markedly elevated bile acids (234 µmol/L) with mild alanine aminotransferase elevation. She was diagnosed with ICP and started on ursodiol and hydroxyzine, but symptoms persisted. Given reports of thiopurine-associated cholestasis, the medication was discontinued, and 6-methylmercaptopurine levels were found to be supratherapeutic. Within days, bile acids and pruritus improved, with normalization over three weeks. She remained asymptomatic, delivered at 36 weeks, and later resumed azathioprine without issue. We summarize 17 cases of thiopurine-associated cholestasis, typically with early onset, severe bile acid elevation, and poor response to ursodiol. This case highlights the importance of medication review, and assessment for possible secondary contributors in atypical or refractory ICP presentations.

articles.title: Effects of cell size on incidence of chromosome aneuploidy: Analysis using a cultured cell model.
articles.authors: Kato Y, Tsutsumi M, Abe T et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Chromosomal aneuploidy arises from errors in chromosome segregation during cell division, and embryonic aneuploidy is a major cause of implantation failure and miscarriage, which is primarily attributed to maternal meiotic errors. However, recent data accumulated from preimplantation genetic testing have suggested that chromosome segregation errors may also frequently occur during mitotic divisions in early embryos. One proposed factor for these errors is that the cell size in early embryos is larger than that of somatic cells after cleavage, but the exact mechanisms remain unclear.
METHODS: To determine the effect of cell size on the incidence of aneuploidy, we established a cultured cell model in which the cell size was artificially enlarged. This model harbored a chromosome carrying the GFP gene, and disappearance of GFP fluorescence served as a quantitative marker for aneuploidy events. By overexpressing genes that increase cell size, we measured the cell size and frequency of aneuploidy using flow cytometry.
RESULTS: We observed a significant increase (p=3.67×10-9) in the incidence of aneuploidy in large cells, which supports the hypothesis that a large cell size characteristic of early embryos contributes to the occurrence of chromosomal segregation errors.
CONCLUSIONS: Our finding may partly explain the high prevalence of aneuploid mosaicism in human preimplantation embryos.

articles.title: Chemotherapy-Associated Ovarian Damage: Pathological Mechanisms and Current Interventions.
articles.authors: Qi W, Jia Z, Shi M et al.
articles.abstract: Chemotherapy drugs such as cyclophosphamide (CTX), doxorubicin (DOX), and cisplatin (CIS) are widely used in the treatment of malignant tumors, including head and neck cancers, leukemia, ovarian cancer, and breast cancer. However, these drugs are frequently associated with severe side effects, particularly ovarian toxicity, which significantly compromises fertility and quality of life in female patients. Current research has revealed that chemotherapy associated ovarian damage(CAOD) involves a range of pathological and molecular mechanisms, including extracellular matrix(ECM) deposition, stromal fibrosis, ovarian vascular injury, DNA damage, redox imbalance, immune microenvironment dysregulation, and excessive activation of primordial follicles(PMFs). From a clinical perspective, embryo and oocyte cryopreservation, as well as ovarian tissue cryopreservation in appropriate patients, represent established fertility-preservation approaches, whereas ovarian-protective interventions such as GnRH agonists (GnRHa) remain subject to ongoing clinical evaluation. In contrast, stem cell therapy, antiapoptotic agents, antioxidants, and strategies targeting excessive follicle activation are predominantly supported by preclinical evidence and have not yet been established as routine clinical treatments. This article provides a narrative review of the major pathological features and molecular mechanisms of chemotherapy-induced ovarian damage, evaluates the limitations of existing prevention and treatment strategies, and aims to advance academic discourse in the field of CAOD prevention and treatment, while offering insights for future research.

articles.title: Optimising a national screen-and-treat cervical cancer strategy in Uganda: a microsimulation cost-effectiveness and budget impact analysis.
articles.authors: Rukundo-Ayeh T, McBain RK, Rasmussen PW et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cervical cancer is the leading cause of cancer mortality for women in Uganda, yet fewer than a third of Ugandan women have ever been screened. Screen-and-treat programmes using visual inspection with acetic acid (VIA) are a key prevention strategy. Current guidelines recommend screening for women aged 25-49 every 3 years. However, there is limited evidence comparing the trade-offs between health gains, costs and implementation feasibility across alternative programme designs at scale.
METHODS: We conducted a cost-effectiveness and budget impact analysis of 30 VIA screen-and-treat cervical cancer policies using a microsimulation parameterised to represent Ugandan women aged 25-49 over a 15-year time horizon. Policies varied across three implementation dimensions: (1) screening frequency, (2) screening uptake among eligible women and (3) treatment follow-through for precancerous lesions. We estimated population-level costs, deaths averted, quality-adjusted life years (QALYs) gained and incremental cost-effectiveness ratios (ICERs).
RESULTS: We found that, depending on screening frequency, uptake and treatment follow-through, between 13% and 50% of deaths could be averted compared with the base case (current levels). The 15-year total costs ranged from $32.9 million to $158.6 million, or $5 to $23 per eligible woman. Both incremental costs and deaths averted increased at a diminishing rate as screening intensified. Policy scenarios with lower levels of treatment were dominated by those with higher treatment follow-through, regardless of screening uptake. ICERs ranged from $88 to $313 per QALY gained, and $2219 to $6881 per death averted.
CONCLUSION: The most effective and efficient policy scenarios were not simply those with the highest levels of screening or treatment, but those that optimally configured all three programme levers simultaneously. The findings revealed interactive effects of screening frequency, uptake and treatment follow-through on costs and health outcomes. These results equip Ugandan policymakers with context-specific evidence to prioritise screening policies that balance health impact, cost and implementation capacity.

articles.title: Digital Health Coaching in Pregnancy: A Scoping Review of Interventions and Outcomes.
articles.authors: Jahangiri Mirshekarlou S, Nikniaz L, Rezaei Haches P et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Health coaching is an innovative model of health promotion, empowering individuals to enhance self-care, make informed choices, and develop health knowledge and skills. Integrating digital technologies like mobile apps, web platforms, wearables, and artificial intelligence into health coaching enables personalized, accessible, and continuous support to improve disease management. In maternal health, digital coaching promotes healthy behaviors in nutrition, physical activity, sleep, and mental well-being. This review explores digital health coaching interventions during pregnancy and their impact on maternal and fetal outcomes.
METHODS: We conducted a scoping review of English-language articles from 2000 until December 2024 in PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, IEEE, and Google Scholar. Keywords that formed the search strategy were "digital health"," health coaching ","pregnancy" along with synonyms and related terms.
RESULTS: Thirty- one studies were included. Most interventions used smartphones, text messaging, coaching applications, virtual sessions, and wearable devices focusing on nutrition and physical activity to manage weight and gestational diabetes. Nutritionists, obstetricians, and midwives were the main contributors, using motivational interviewing, goal setting, and social cognitive theories. Outcomes showed acceptability and satisfaction in 45% of studies, feasibility in 35%, and effectiveness in lifestyle behaviors in 68%. Improvements in weight management, glycemic control, and body composition were observed in 42% of studies.10% noted benefits in maternal and newborn health. One study reported cost-effectiveness; however, some found no significant differences in gestational weight gain or diabetes.
CONCLUSION: Digital health coaching in pregnancy can have favorable potential to support mothers' health and change their behavior. However, more research is needed on the most effective components, including psychological aspects and socio-economic measures.

articles.title: Ferroportin deficiency drives olaparib resistance in ovarian cancer via the cGAS-STING-STAT3 survival axis.
articles.authors: Song J, Guo Z, Yang D et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ovarian cancer (OC) remains the most lethal gynaecological malignancy, and acquired resistance to PARP inhibitors such as olaparib represents a major clinical challenge. Although dysregulation of iron metabolism has been implicated in tumorigenesis, the specific role of the iron exporter SLC40A1 (ferroportin, FPN) in mediating olaparib resistance remains poorly understood. The study aimed to elucidate the clinical significance of FPN deficiency and to explore therapeutic strategies for reversing olaparib resistance.
METHODS: FPN expression was evaluated in OC samples from a clinical cohort of 19 patients, stratified by olaparib responsiveness, to determine its prognostic value. Functional mechanisms were investigated using multiple OC cell lines, patient-derived organoids (PDOs), and mouse xenograft models. We integrated analyses of iron homeostasis, ROS dynamics, DNA repair capacity, and innate immune signaling, with a focus on the cGAS-STING-STAT3 signaling cascade. The therapeutic potential of combining olaparib with the ferroptosis inducer erastin or the STING inhibitor C-176 was assessed as a strategy to overcome FPN deficiency-driven resistance.
RESULTS: Clinically, FPN expression was significantly downregulated in olaparib-resistant tissues compared with sensitive controls (p < 0.05), and low FPN levels were strongly associated with poor therapeutic outcomes. Mechanistically, FPN deficiency promoted intracellular iron accumulation and ROS generation, which led to increased ferroptosis vulnerability, impaired homologous recombination repair (HRR) and concomitant activation of the cGAS-STING-STAT3 inflammatory axis, thereby driving olaparib resistance. Notably, in vivo studies demonstrated that combining olaparib with either erastin or C-176 significantly suppressed tumour growth and restored drug sensitivity compared with monotherapy (p < 0.01), supporting the translational potential of targeting this axis.
CONCLUSIONS: Our study establishes a clinically relevant mechanistic connection between ferroportin deficiency and cGAS-STING-STAT3-mediated olaparib resistance in OC. We identify the FPN-ROS-cGAS-STING-STAT3 axis as an actionable vulnerability in resistant OC, indicating that this pathway is a promising therapeutic target to overcome olaparib resistance.
HIGHLIGHTS: FPN loss drives olaparib resistance and predicts poor outcomes in ovarian cancer. FPN loss causes iron and ROS accumulation, impairing HRR and activating the…

articles.title: Factors influencing breastfeeding intention among hepatitis B virus-infected mothers: An ABC-X cross-sectional analysis.
articles.authors: Jiang Y, Geng Z, Yang W et al.
articles.abstract: Despite international guideline recommendations supporting breastfeeding among HBV-infected mothers, breastfeeding rates remain suboptimal. This study investigated factors influencing breastfeeding intention among HBV-infected mothers using the ABC-X theoretical framework. A hospital-based cross-sectional study was conducted from January to December 2025 among 119 HBV-infected pregnant women. Structured questionnaires assessed demographic characteristics, disease-related factors, social support, self-efficacy, stigma, breastfeeding attitudes, and breastfeeding intention. Descriptive statistics, t-tests, chi-square tests, and multivariate logistic regression were performed. Among participants, 45.3% (n = 54) intended to breastfeed. Univariate analysis showed significant differences in self-efficacy (p = 0.003) and breastfeeding attitude scores (p = 0.046) between mothers with and without breastfeeding intention. After adjustment for potential confounders, self-efficacy was the only independent predictor of breastfeeding intention (OR = 3.71, 95% CI: 1.35-10.19, p = 0.011). The prediction model showed good discrimination, with an area under the ROC curve of 0.782. Maternal self-efficacy was the strongest predictor of breastfeeding intention among HBV-infected mothers. Interventions enhancing self-efficacy and clearly communicating breastfeeding safety with immunoprophylaxis may improve breastfeeding support in this population.

articles.title: Food-to-food fortification: Effectiveness of red spinach-enriched snakehead fish floss for maternal anemia.
articles.authors: Ummah W, Putri SI, Utami WT et al.
articles.abstract: Iron deficiency anemia remains a major public health challenge among pregnant women, while adherence to iron supplementation is frequently limited by gastrointestinal side effects. This study evaluated the effectiveness of a ready-to-eat red spinach-fortified snakehead fish (Channa striata) floss as a complementary food-based intervention for improving hemoglobin levels among pregnant women with anemia. A quasi-experimental pre-post study involved 60 pregnant women with mild-to-moderate anemia in Malang Regency, Indonesia. Participants were allocated to an intervention group receiving fortified fish floss alongside routine iron-folic acid supplementation or a control group receiving standard supplementation alone for 21 days. Hemoglobin concentrations were measured before and after the intervention and analyzed using paired and independent t-tests. The intervention group demonstrated a greater increase in hemoglobin levels than the control group (p<0.001). These findings suggest that integrating a locally produced ready-to-eat fortified food into routine antenatal care may enhance hemoglobin recovery as a complementary nutritional strategy.

articles.title: Assessment of the health literacy mediating role in the relationship between fatalistic tendency and family planning among women.
articles.authors: Ahi S, Çetinkaya F
articles.abstract: Promoting family planning is an essential public health goal for improving maternal and infant health; however, sociocultural barriers-particularly fatalism-continue to shape women's behaviors and attitudes. This study examined the mediating role of health literacy in the relationship between women's fatalistic tendencies and their family planning attitudes. Using a cross-sectional correlational design, data were collected from 657 married women aged 18-49 in Kırşehir, Türkiye, through 30-cluster sampling. Data were collected through face-to-face interviews conducted during home visits between February 28 and June 1, 2022, using structured questionnaires. Measures included the Fatalistic Tendency Scale, Family Planning Attitude Scale, and the Turkey Health Literacy Scale-32. Data were analyzed using IBM SPSS Statistics v23. Mediation analysis was conducted using PROCESS v3.5 with 5,000 bootstrap samples. Fatalistic tendency was negatively associated with health literacy, while health literacy showed a positive association with family planning attitudes. An indirect effect of fatalistic tendency on family planning attitudes through health literacy was identified. Findings highlight the importance of improving health literacy to mitigate fatalistic beliefs and support informed reproductive decision-making, emphasizing culturally sensitive, interdisciplinary interventions.

articles.title: Medication abortion care pathways and women's experiences in Oromia state, Ethiopia: A qualitative study.
articles.authors: Chekol BM, Sheehy G, Rezene B
articles.abstract: Despite Ethiopia's liberal abortion law, approximately half of abortions occur outside health facilities. Medication abortion (MA) use has increased dramatically, yet data on women's experiences - both facility-based and self-managed - remains limited. This study explored MA experiences in Oromia, Ethiopia through in-depth interviews with 20 post-abortion care clients across seven public facilities from August-October 2021. Most women (n=18) obtained MA from private clinics or pharmacies and self-managed at home. Seventeen participants used mifepristone/misoprostol combipacks, while three used misoprostol alone. Nearly all received minimal counseling on proper MA use. All participants ultimately sought post-abortion care due to concerning symptoms, most commonly heavier-than-expected bleeding. These findings highlight critical gaps in MA information and counseling in Ethiopia. Improving women's understanding of expected symptoms could significantly enhance MA experiences. This study offers rare evidence on self-managed abortion pathways in Ethiopia, providing valuable insights for stakeholders working to improve MA access, efficacy, and safety.

articles.title: Quality of contraceptive counseling short scale: Turkish validity and reliability study.
articles.authors: Cansızlar GA, Beydağ KD
articles.abstract: This study aimed to evaluate the validity and reliability of the Turkish version of the 10-item Quality of Contraceptive Counseling Scale. This cross-sectional methodological study was conducted at a training and research hospital in Turkey with 125 women who received contraceptive counseling, including 100 participants for the main validation analyses and 25 for test-retest reliability. The scale was adapted through forward-backward translation, expert review, and cultural adaptation. Construct, criterion, and discriminant validity, internal consistency, and temporal stability were assessed. The Turkish version demonstrated a unidimensional structure with acceptable model fit, high internal consistency, and excellent test-retest reliability. Significant associations with patient satisfaction supported criterion validity, while discriminant validity analyses showed that the scale distinguished between groups with different perceptions of counseling quality. The findings support its use as a valid and reliable tool in clinical practice and research. (Afr J Reprod Health 2026; 30 [20]: 71-82).

articles.title: Mechanistic Study of GSDME and CXCL10 in SUV39H1-Mediated Pyroptosis and Immune Suppression in Cervical Cancer.
articles.authors: Zhang L, Sheng P, Cai D et al.
articles.abstract: Cervical cancer (CC) remains a major global health challenge characterized by high incidence and mortality. The histone methyltransferase suppressor of variegation 3-9 homolog 1 (SUV39H1) has emerged as a key epigenetic regulator in tumor progression, but its role in modulating pyroptosis and remodeling of the immune microenvironment in CC remains unclear. In this study, we demonstrate that SUV39H1 promotes CC progression through dual epigenetic regulation, specifically repression of gasdermin E (GSDME) and activation of chemokine (C-X-C motif) ligand 10 (CXCL10). Overexpression of SUV39H1 in HeLa and SiHa cells enhanced histone 3 lysine 9 tri methylation (H3K9me3) deposition at the DFNA5 (GSDME) promoter, resulting in reduced transcription and suppressed GSDME-dependent pyroptosis-like cell death. Interestingly, it also upregulated CXCL10 expression. Functional assays confirmed that SUV39H1 attenuated GSDME-mediated pyroptosis-like cell death and enhanced cell migration via induction of epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT). Moreover, SUV39H1 drives CXCL10 secretion, which activates the chemokine (C-X-C motif) receptor 3 (CXCR3) signaling axis in macrophages and upregulates immunosuppressive molecules including programmed death ligand 1 (PD-L1), T cell immunoglobulin and mucin-domain containing-3 (Tim-3), and secreted phosphoprotein 1 (SPP1), thereby fostering an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME), and these effects appear parallel to GSDME suppression. Collectively, these findings reveal a multifaceted oncogenic role of SUV39H1 in CC, highlighting its potential as a therapeutic target for epigenetic and immunomodulatory intervention.

articles.title: Diagnostic and clinical value of the HALP (hemoglobin, albumin, lymphocyte, and platelet) score in preeclampsia.
articles.authors: Dera AA
articles.abstract: Preeclampsia (PE) is a leading cause of maternal morbidity, linked to systemic inflammation and nutritional imbalance. The hemoglobin, albumin, lymphocyte, and platelet (HALP) score, an immune-nutritional index, was assessed in PE. A retrospective case-control study included non-pregnant healthy women (NonP), healthy pregnant women (HP), and women with PE. HALP was calculated and compared across groups. Correlations, principal component analysis (PCA), regression, and ROC analysis were performed. HALP was significantly lower in PE than HP and NonP (p < 0.001), with the steepest decline in women >36 years. HALP correlated positively with lymphocytes, albumin, and hemoglobin, but negatively with neutrophils and WBCs. PCA highlighted albumin and lymphocytes, while regression identified WBCs as an independent predictor. ROC analysis showed good discrimination for NonP vs PE (AUC = 0.764). HALP is reduced in PE and may serve as a simple, accessible biomarker for risk stratification. La prééclampsie (PE) est une cause majeure de morbidité maternelle, associée à une inflammation systémique et à un déséquilibre nutritionnel. Le score HALP (hémoglobine, albumine, lymphocytes et plaquettes) — un indice immuno-nutritionnel — a été évalué dans le contexte de la PE. Une étude cas-témoins rétrospective a inclus des femmes non enceintes en bonne santé (groupe NonP), des femmes enceintes en bonne santé (groupe HP) et des femmes atteintes de PE. Le score HALP a été calculé et comparé entre les groupes. Des analyses de corrélation, une analyse en composantes principales (ACP), des analyses de régression et une analyse par courbe ROC ont été réalisées. Le score HALP était significativement plus faible chez les femmes atteintes de PE que chez celles des groupes HP et NonP (p < 0,001), la baisse la plus marquée étant observée chez les femmes de plus de 36 ans. Le score HALP présentait une corrélation positive avec les lymphocytes, l'albumine et l'hémoglobine, mais une corrélation négative avec les neutrophiles et les globules blancs. L'ACP a mis en évidence le rôle de l'albumine et des lymphocytes, tandis que l'analyse de régression a identifié les globules blancs comme un facteur prédictif indépendant. L'analyse par courbe ROC a montré une bonne capacité de discrimination entre les groupes NonP et PE (AUC = 0,764). Le score HALP est diminué en cas de PE et pourrait constituer un biomarqueur simple et accessible pour la stratification du risque.

articles.title: Development of machine learning models for fetal birth weight prediction: A single-center study in a Turkish population.
articles.authors: Osmanoglu UO, Dursun A, Dulger O
articles.abstract: Fetal birth weight (BW) is a critical indicator of the prognosis of perinatal health. Accurate estimation of BW is essential in determining the appropriate delivery method. This single-center study aims to evaluate the performance of various machine learning (ML) algorithms in estimating BW. The study population consisted of 456 pregnant women with singleton pregnancies evaluated at a single tertiary center in the Karaman region of Turkiye between 38 and 41 weeks based on their last menstrual period, who gave birth to a phenotypically normal live newborn within 7 days after the ultrasound examination. Seven out of the nine models developed using ML algorithms had the lowest mean absolute error (MAE) values ranging from 184.30 to 190.00 grams. The formula closest to these values was Hadlock III, with an MAE value of 223.33 grams. In our study, the model demonstrating the highest predictive accuracy was provided by Linear Regression algorithm with an MAE value of 184.30 grams. Our findings indicate that data-driven predictive modelin.

articles.title: Cervical cancer awareness among Namibian women: Perspectives of primary healthcare nurses.
articles.authors: Nashandi TN, Downing C
articles.abstract: Cervical cancer remains a major public health concern in sub-Saharan Africa, particularly in Namibia, where high rates of HIV and HPV infections and early sexual activity increase its prevalence. Limited awareness of cervical cancer among Namibian women contributes significantly to delayed screening and treatment, reducing the likelihood of successful outcomes. This qualitative study explored the perceptions and experiences of 73 professional nurses purposively selected from public primary healthcare facilities across Namibia's fourteen regions. Data were collected through focus group discussions and analysed thematically, with an independent coder to ensure rigor. Findings revealed a substantial lack of awareness among women, highlighting the need for nurses to lead educational initiatives. The study advocates empowering nurses to strengthen patient-nurse relationships and implement community-based awareness programs, including media outreach to isolated populations. It contributes to public health knowledge by emphasizing strategies to promote prevention, early diagnosis, and improved cervical cancer outcomes in Namibia.

articles.title: Genital Involvement in Female Patients With Congenital Type 1 Plasminogen Deficiency: A Case Series and Updated Literature Review.
articles.journal: Haemophilia : the official journal of the World Federation of Hemophilia
articles.authors: Dalla Porta C, Sartori MT, Saggiorato G et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Congenital type 1 plasminogen deficiency (PLGD1) is an ultra-rare disorder characterized by the formation of fibrin-rich pseudomembranes on mucosal surfaces across multiple organ systems. In affected females, ligneous lesions may involve the genital tract.
AIM: We aimed to characterize the clinical manifestations and therapeutic approaches associated with genital involvement in females with PLGD1.
METHODS: A structured literature review was performed to identify previously reported females with PLGD1 and genital lesions. In addition, PLGD1 patients followed at Padua University Hospital were included.
RESULTS: A total of 57 females with genital manifestations consistent with PLGD1 were identified, including 4 cases from our institution, 8 patients enrolled in a phase 2-3 clinical trial, and 9 cases described before recognition of the association with plasminogen deficiency. Reported plasminogen activity levels ranged from < 2% to 50%. Pseudomembranous lesions involved the vagina, cervix, endometrium, ovaries, and fallopian tubes.
