Genital involvement represented the sole clinical manifestation in 13 of 57 patients (22.8%). The most common symptoms included dysmenorrhea, vaginal discharge, post-coital bleeding, and infertility (18/38 cases, 47.4%). Surgical excision was associated with a high rate of recurrence. Data on topical and systemic treatments for genital involvement were limited and largely empirical. The most effective therapeutic approach was replacement therapy with human Glu-plasminogen concentrate and fresh frozen plasma.
CONCLUSIONS: Genital tract involvement in PLGD1 is not uncommon and may represent the sole manifestation of the disease, with potential implications for fertility. Glu-plasminogen replacement therapy has shown promising results, although its availability remains limited worldwide.

articles.title: Trends and determinants of peripartum blood transfusions.
articles.authors: VanWormer JJ, Kreuziger LB, Mcintosh JJ et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Blood transfusion is critical in mitigating blood loss during delivery, but the epidemiology of peripartum blood transfusion in the United States is not fully understood. The objective of this study was to estimate trends in peripartum blood transfusions, including severe hemorrhage, and identify transfusion risk factors.
STUDY DESIGN AND METHODS: A retrospective cohort was assembled from the Recipient Epidemiology and Donor Study IV Pediatric (REDS-IV-P) database, which includes a network of hospitals and blood centers across four U.S. regional hubs. This included in-hospital deliveries ≥24 weeks gestation from 2019 to 2024, with the outcome being any peripartum (within ±7 days of delivery) blood product transfusion. Bayesian Model Averaging (BMA) was used to examine associations.
RESULTS: There were 158,322 deliveries, with transfusion occurring in 4246 (11% were severe hemorrhage). Overall incidence of transfusion increased from ~2% early in the study period to ~3% in later years (p < 0.001). The odds of peripartum transfusion were higher for deliveries where patients had an underlying hemoglobinopathy (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] [95% confidence interval; CI] aOR = 3.35 [2.65, 4.24]), venous thromboembolism (aOR = 3.25 [2.47, 4.26]), received hemostatic factor (aOR = 10.30 [9.58, 11.06]), mechanical ventilation (aOR = 13.91 [8.76, 22.11]), or hysterectomy (aOR = 13.68 [9.86, 18.96]).
CONCLUSION: Peripartum transfusions are increasing across the REDS-IV-P hubs and are associated with underlying medical-obstetric risk factors such as bleeding disorders and hemoglobinopathies. Our findings support the importance of early prenatal healthcare and identification of conditions that may help prevent peripartum hemorrhage and associated transfusions.

articles.title: Dynamic Hydrogel-Mediated Co-Delivery of Clotrimazole and Nifuratel for Safe and Effective In Vivo Cervical Cancer Treatment.
articles.journal: Journal of biomedical materials research. Part B, Applied biomaterials
articles.ta: J Biomed Mater Res B Appl Biomater
articles.authors: Gosecka M, Gosecki M, Urbaniak M et al.
articles.abstract: Systemic combination chemotherapy for cervical cancer is often limited by poor drug solubility and high toxicity. Over the past decade, there has been growing interest in local therapy using hydrogel-based drug carriers that remain at the site of the lesion, thereby reducing side effects. However, to date, research has been limited mainly to in vitro studies. In this study, we demonstrate the use of dynamic hydrogels to ensure effective delivery of water-insoluble drugs for in vivo anti-cervical cancer therapy in a mouse model. The main structural component of the hydrogel was a non-linear poly(benzyl glycidyl ether)-poly(glyceryl glycerol ether) copolyether, which increases the solubility of the poorly water-soluble clotrimazole and nifuratel and enables reversible cross-linking, confering injectability and self-healing behavior to the hydrogel. Two-dose intratumoral implementation of hydrogel formulations resulted in a superior effect in the reduction of the tumor volume by > 90% within a 14-day therapy. Unexpectedly, 50% of the mice with induced tumors were completely cured with a hydrogel constructed of copolyethers, whose molar ratio of constitutional repeating units of GGE to BGE was equal to 2:1. The drug loading of both drugs can be a key parameter crucial for the achievement of the superior efficacy of this formulation, making it a highly therapeutic delivery system. The use of copolyethers enhanced controlled drug delivery, as evidenced by a statistically significant reduction in tumor volume (p < 0.001) compared to the efficacy of pure drugs (> 0.05). Furthermore, copolyether-based formulations provide a safer therapeutic alternative to pure drugs. This was confirmed by blood biochemical analyses, which showed no increase in LDH or CRP levels, and by histopathological evaluations of mouse livers, which demonstrated that, unlike pure clotrimazole, the formulations do not induce liver damage. The high yield point detected for hydrogel and the strong mucosal adhesion of the synthesized hydrogels up to 18.7 kPa allow the formulation to remain at the target site. Surprisingly, we observed that incorporating clotrimazole into the hydrogel significantly increased mucosal adhesion strength. Permeability investigations performed on ex vivo porcine vaginal mucosa showed a sustained permeation reaching 40% and 25% of permeated nifuratel and clotrimazole, respectively. The presented dual drug-loaded dynamic hydrogels are highly promising for clinical use…

articles.title: Physiologically Based Pharmacokinetic Modeling to Predict the Exposure and Provide Dosage Regimens of Oseltamivir in Pregnant Women with Comorbid CES1 Polymorphism and Hepatic Cirrhosis.
articles.authors: Xu J, Zhang S, Zhou P et al.
articles.abstract: Oseltamivir (OSE) is widely prescribed for pregnant women with influenza; however, its optimal dosing strategy remains undefined in cases involving carboxylesterase 1 (CES1) gene polymorphism and hepatic cirrhosis. This study aimed to explore OSE dosing regimens for pregnant patients with comorbid CES1 polymorphism and hepatic cirrhosis. A mechanistic physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) model of OSE was first built and verified in healthy populations, then extrapolated to adult patients with CES1 polymorphism, hepatic cirrhosis, and pregnant patients. The PBPK model successfully predicted and verified the PKs of OSE and its active metabolite oseltamivir carboxylate (OSC) in both non-pregnant and pregnant women. Simulation results showed that the fold errors of the predicted and observed values of the area under the curve (AUC) and peak plasma concentration (Cmax) values ranged from 0.5 to 2.0, with the average folding error and absolute average folding error for all concentration-time data points reaching 0.89 and 1.38, respectively. Importantly, for pregnant patients, OSE administration is recommended to be tailored by CES1 genotype, cirrhosis severity, and pregnancy trimester, to achieve post-dosing AUC levels comparable to those of the non-pregnant reference population. This integrated pregnancy PBPK model enables us to comprehensively and extensively explore the PK characteristics of OSE and OSC in pregnant women under complex scenarios, thereby providing valuable guidance for clinical applications and precise management of influenza during pregnancy.

articles.title: Integrating Omics to Advance Antiretroviral Pharmacology in Pregnancy: Dolutegravir-Based Regimens as a Case Study.
articles.authors: Eke AC
articles.abstract: Dolutegravir is central to antiretroviral therapy in pregnancy, although conventional pharmacokinetic measures cannot fully explain variability in maternal cardiometabolic outcomes or fetal exposure. This narrative review proposes an integrated omics framework linking pharmacogenomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, and metabolomics with longitudinal pharmacokinetics and clinical phenotyping. Using dolutegravir as a case study, we examine genetic determinants of drug disposition, gestational changes in molecular pathways, and emerging evidence implicating adipose dysfunction, mitochondrial metabolism, lipid remodeling, and insulin resistance. We distinguish established pharmacokinetic findings from mechanistic hypotheses requiring pregnancy-specific validation. Proposed studies combine serial maternal sampling, targeted placental and adipose investigations, and offspring follow-up, while accounting for HIV, antiretroviral backbone, gestational physiology, and environmental confounding. Prespecified analyses, analytical validation, and independent replication are essential to avoid overinterpretation. Integrated omics should complement, not replace, pharmacometrics, ultimately identifying reproducible mechanisms and clinically useful biomarkers to inform individualized monitoring and treatment strategies while preserving dolutegravir's proven virologic benefits.

articles.title: The Use of Maternal Race in Antenatal Screening Tests: A Narrative Review.
articles.authors: Harkins SE, Gure S, Canty L et al.
articles.abstract: The historical legacy of white supremacy in the United States has been institutionalized in ways that contribute to maternal health care inequities, including the treatment of race as a biological risk factor in health care. Race is a social construct with neither a genetic nor biological basis, and racism is the major contributor to adverse outcomes. Recently, medical specialties have identified and reduced the use of race in clinical tests and decision-making. Identifying the use of race in antenatal care is essential to dismantling institutional racism and improving perinatal outcomes. We conducted a narrative review to describe the role of race in currently recommended antenatal care tests. We identified tests considered routine and gold standard for antenatal care in the United States based on the 2025 American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists Clinical Consensus for Tailored Prenatal Care Delivery. We searched bibliographic databases and reference lists. Of the 18 tests found in routine antenatal care, 3 currently use race, 3 previously used race, and 12 do not and have not used race. Currently, Black race is considered a moderate risk factor for preeclampsia, and race-specific adjustment factors remain embedded in the first-trimester combined and second-trimester quadruple aneuploidy screening for the interpretation of maternal serum markers. Historically, anemia diagnosis definitions included race-specific thresholds, and race and ethnicity were considered alongside other risk factors when recommending screening for hemoglobinopathies and gestational diabetes. Although the inclusion of race was likely an attempt to address maternal health care inequities, it can perpetuate racist rhetoric that an individual's increased risk is attributable to inherent biological differences. These findings reinforce the need to review antenatal care practices and eliminate race-based clinical guidelines to provide evidence-based health care and advance perinatal health equity.

articles.title: Pregnancy Outcomes Following Maternal Exposure to Pramipexole: A TERAFAR Case Series.
articles.authors: Bakirli DC, Horoz E, Kuragi CC et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: To evaluate pregnancy outcomes following maternal pramipexole exposure using data from the Izmir Kâtip Celebi University Teratology Information, Training and Research Center (TERAFAR).
METHODS: Pregnant women exposed to pramipexole and referred to the TERAFAR between 2011 and 2025 were evaluated. Maternal demographic data, medical history, and exposure details were recorded at the initial visit; pregnancy outcomes and neonatal data were collected through postpartum telephone interviews. The primary outcome was the rate of major congenital malformations, while secondary outcomes included miscarriage, stillbirth, preterm birth, and low birth weight.
RESULTS: A total of 11 pregnancies were evaluated. Median maternal age was 36 years, and restless legs syndrome was the primary indication in 10 of the 11 pregnancies. The median daily dose was 0.25 mg. Of the 11 pregnancies, 10 resulted in live births and one ended in miscarriage. No major congenital malformations were observed. A minor congenital anomaly (infantile hemangioma) was detected in only one premature infant.
CONCLUSIONS: In this case series, maternal exposure to pramipexole was not associated with a consistent pattern of congenital anomalies suggestive of a teratogenic signal. Given the clinical context, the minor anomaly observed (infantile hemangioma) is more likely attributable to prematurity and maternal factors than to pramipexole exposure. Given the small sample size, findings should be interpreted with caution but may inform individualized counseling of pregnant women with inadvertent pramipexole exposure. Further studies are warranted.

articles.title: Effects of a simplified hormonal treatment comprising a single FSH administration and induction of follicular wave emergence by CIDR and estradiol benzoate prior to ovum pick-up on IVP and embryo transfer outcomes in Japanese Black cows.
articles.journal: The Journal of reproduction and development
articles.authors: Okami K, Ho TC, Nabenishi H et al.
articles.abstract: We evaluated a simple, short hormonal protocol comprising follicular wave synchronization using a progesterone-releasing device and estradiol benzoate 5 days before ovum pick-up (OPU) followed by a single follicle-stimulating hormone injection 2 days before OPU to improve oocyte quality and outcomes of in vitro embryo production (IVP) and embryo transfer (ET) in Japanese Black cows. A total of 12 cows were used in this study, with 6 cows in each of the Treatment and Non-Treatment groups. The proportion of good-quality oocytes, transferable blastocysts per OPU session, and pregnancy rate following ET of IVP-derived blastocysts were all higher in the Treatment group than in the Non-Treatment group (63.0 ± 7.7% vs. 47.5 ± 7.6%, 4.0 ± 0.7 vs. 2.6 ± 0.5, and 55.6% vs. 19.0%, respectively; P < 0.05). These results demonstrate that the present protocol, which requires only two procedures before OPU, effectively improves OPU-IVP and ET outcomes in Japanese Black cows.

articles.title: Association between a maternal FOXP3 variant and reproductive stayability in Holstein Friesian cows in Japan.
articles.journal: The Journal of reproduction and development
articles.authors: Okawa H, Fushimi Y, Yamato O et al.
articles.abstract: Reproductive failure is a major cause of economic loss and involuntary culling in dairy herds, with endocrine and immunogenetic factors contributing to impaired fertility. FOXP3 modulates regulatory T cells, which play an essential role in maternal immune tolerance during pregnancy. A maternal X-linked FOXP3 variant (g.87298881A>G) has been associated with impaired fertility and reduced anti-Müllerian hormone (AMH) concentrations in cattle; however, its association with reproductive performance and herd stayability remains unclear. This study investigated the associations of the FOXP3 variant with serum AMH concentrations and reproductive performance in Japanese Holstein Friesian cows. A total of 118 lactating cows from two dairy farms in Japan were genotyped using real-time PCR or Sanger sequencing. After excluding one cow that died from an acute condition unrelated to reproductive or production performance, 117 cows (A/A, n = 35; A/G, n = 56; G/G, n = 26) were included in the final analyses. Serum AMH concentrations were measured using an enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay, and reproductive outcomes were monitored during the study period. Serum AMH concentrations did not differ significantly among the three genotype groups. Kaplan-Meier analysis showed a significant difference in time to pregnancy between G/G and A/G cows (P = 0.026), with G/G cows remaining nonpregnant for longer. In the univariate Cox proportional hazards analysis, cows with the FOXP3 risk genotype (G/G) had a lower pregnancy hazard than that of cows with non-risk genotypes (A/A and A/G) (HR = 0.583, 95% CI: 0.343-0.991, P = 0.046). After adjustment for farm and parity, the risk genotype remained significantly associated with a lower pregnancy hazard (adjusted HR = 0.45, 95% CI: 0.26-0.77, P = 0.004). These findings suggest that the FOXP3 risk genotype is associated with impaired reproductive performance, independent of farm and parity. The absence of a significant difference in serum AMH concentrations further suggests that this association cannot be explained solely by differences in ovarian reserve and raises the hypothesis that FOXP3-related immunological mechanisms contribute to the establishment and maintenance of pregnancy.

articles.title: Retrospective Chart Review Indicates Earlier Age of Endometrial Cancer Diagnosis and Elevated Housing and Transportation Vulnerability in Hispanic and Native American Populations.
articles.authors: Jimenez NR, Mendoza R, Flores E et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In 2025, Endometrial cancer (EC) is the 6th most common cancer in women globally, with rising cases in younger patients and communities of color. EC risk factors include postmenopausal status, family history, diabetes, and hyperestrogenic state conditions.
METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed charts of patients who received hysterectomies or hysteroscopies for either cancerous and/or benign diagnoses between 2016 and 2021 at a university hospital in Phoenix (AZ). Sociodemographic and clinical data were collected. The Arizona Social Vulnerability Index was utilized to understand contributors to EC diagnosis outcomes. Kruskal-Wallis, Fisher's exact, and multinomial logistic regression tests were used to compare EC to benign conditions.
RESULTS: Two hundred sixty-one patients were diagnosed with benign conditions (n = 31), hyperplasia (n = 53), or EC (n = 168). EC patients were older (p = 0.016), mostly post-menopausal (p = 0.008), and more frequently had diabetes (p = 0.001) compared to patients with benign conditions. Native Americans had a higher percentage of EC cases relative to other races (p = 0.07) and presented with EC at significantly younger ages (49.79 years, p = 0.001) and with more comorbid diagnoses of diabetes (38.5%, p = 0.051) compared to Whites (61.99 years, 27.1%). Hispanic patients also presented with EC at younger ages (53.74,p = 0.006) compared to non-Hispanics (61.56 years). Higher vulnerability in Housing Type and Transportation scores (p = 0.045) among patients diagnosed with EC was observed.
CONCLUSION: Public health initiatives should target modifiable risk factors contributing to increased EC rates at younger ages, especially in Native American and Hispanic communities. Differences in housing and transportation highlight social structures and health accessibility as areas for improving EC outcomes.

articles.title: Prevalence and associated factors of repeat induced abortion among women at a tertiary obstetrics and gynecology hospital in Vietnam: a cross sectional study.
articles.authors: Huynh Nguyen Khanh T, Quach Lan L, Le Quang T et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Repeat induced abortion remains a major reproductive health concern, particularly in low- and middle-income countries. Although abortion is legal in Vietnam up to 22 weeks of gestation, the country continues to report high abortion rates in Southeast Asia, with limited recent data on repeat abortion. This study aimed to estimate the prevalence of repeat induced abortion and identify associated demographic, reproductive, and contraceptive factors among women seeking abortion services in Vietnam.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: A hospital-based cross-sectional study was conducted from March to September 2025 at the Department of Family Planning, Hung Vuong Hospital, Ho Chi Minh City. Women aged 18-49 years presenting for induced abortion were recruited using convenience sampling. Data were collected through face-to-face interviews using a structured questionnaire. Repeat induced abortion was defined as a history of one or more previous induced abortions. Descriptive statistics were used to summarize participant characteristics, and multivariable logistic regression was performed to identify factors independently associated with repeat abortion. Adjusted odds ratios (AORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were reported.
RESULTS: Among 385 participants, 141 (36.6%; 95% CI: 32.0-42.0%) reported a history of one or more previous induced abortions. In multivariable logistic regression, women aged 31-40 years (AOR = 2.40; 95% CI: 1.30-4.34; p = 0.005) and 41-49 years (AOR = 4.76; 95% CI: 2.04-11.15; p < 0.001) had significantly higher odds of repeat abortion compared with those aged 18-30 years. Having at least one living child was independently associated with markedly higher odds of repeat abortion compared with nulliparity (AOR = 20.80; 95% CI: 2.48-174.50; p = 0.005). Never-married women also had significantly higher odds of repeat abortion compared with those who were or had previously been married (AOR = 19.50; 95% CI: 1.63-233.10; p = 0.020). Use of traditional contraceptive methods was associated with lower odds of repeat abortion compared with no contraceptive use (AOR = 0.33; 95% CI: 0.12-0.88; p = 0.026). No other variables remained statistically significant after adjustment.
CONCLUSION: Over one-third of women seeking abortion services at this tertiary hospital had experienced repeat induced abortion. Increasing age was a strong independent predictor. These findings underscore the need for targeted reproductive health counselling and improved…

articles.title: Preimplantation genetic testing for aneuploidy (PGT-A) vs. morphology-based blastocyst selection for transfer: cost-effectiveness analysis within Israel's publicly funded IVF system.
articles.journal: Israel journal of health policy research
articles.authors: Zivi E, Leshno M, Hammerman A et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Israel operates one of the most extensive publicly funded in vitro fertilization (IVF) programs worldwide. Alongside IVF, adjunct technologies aimed at improving reproductive outcomes, such as preimplantation genetic testing for aneuploidy (PGT-A), have been increasingly adopted. PGT-A is designed to identify chromosomally normal embryos before transfer. Despite its growing use, PGT-A is not included in Israel's National Health Basket. Given the local high utilization of IVF and the substantial public expenditure, evaluating the economic value of PGT-A is essential for evidence-based health policy decision-making. Most available analyses of PGT-A originate from private or mixed healthcare systems, where treatment costs and reimbursement structures differ from Israel's fully publicly funded IVF model. This study aimed to determine whether PGT-A is cost-effective when provided as part of Israel's IVF program.
METHODS: A theoretical model-based cost-effectiveness analysis using a Markov decision framework compared PGT-A with morphology-based embryo selection from the perspective of the Israeli public healthcare payer. The model simulated repeated embryo transfers for various age groups and blastocyst availability scenarios. Relevant cost estimates of the two strategies were based on Israeli Ministry of Health data (2025). The probabilities of main clinical outcomes were derived from the American Society for Assisted Reproductive Technology (SART) database. The effectiveness outcome was live birth. Deterministic one-way sensitivity analyses were performed.
RESULTS: The cost-effectiveness analysis showed dominance for the no-PGT-A strategy; PGT-A was associated with higher costs and lower effectiveness compared with no-PGT-A. Across all age groups and blastocyst numbers, PGT-A was consistently more costly than no-PGT-A. Sensitivity analyses identified the cost of the PGT-A test per tested embryo and the number of available blastocysts as the most influential factors on the incremental cost. It was demonstrated that although PGT-A is a less effective strategy, reducing the costs of the PGT-A test could make it a less costly strategy for women aged 38 years and above. In this circumstance, a trade-off between strategies can be considered.
CONCLUSIONS: PGT-A cannot be recommended for public funding within the Israeli public IVF program. Its application may be considered for advanced-age patients if the cost of the PGT-A test is reduced.

articles.title: Utilization and outcome estimates of cervical precancer screening and associated factors among female health workers in Ghana: implications for primary screening programs.
articles.authors: Effah K, Tekpor E, Wormenor CM et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Toward attaining the WHO's 90-70-90 targets for cervical cancer elimination, female health workers (FHWs) play a crucial role in educating women about the importance of regular cervical screening and HPV vaccination. This study primarily examined the prevalence of hr-HPV infection and cervical lesions among FHWs screened using a variety of approaches in a primary care context in Ghana. It further sought to model factors associated with hr-HPV infection as a screening outcome and prior screening as a proxy for screening utilization among the FHWs.
METHODS: This cross-sectional study evaluated 307 otherwise asymptomatic FHWs who underwent cervical screening between June 2019 and March 2023 in a primary care context- either at the clinic of the Cervical Cancer Prevention and Training Center (CCPTC), Battor, Ghana, or during any of its outreach activities (at satellite clinics). Screening approaches included standalone testing, concurrent testing, or tritesting. Factors associated with hr-HPV infection and screening utilization were modelled using nominal logistic regression.
RESULTS: Three-hundred and seven FHWs [mean age, 33.1 (SD 7.0) years] were screened. Prevalence estimates of screening outcomes were 8.6% (95% CI, 5.7 - 12.3) for visual inspection 'positivity', 9.1% (95% CI, 0.2 - 41.3) for abnormal cytology (ASCUS), and 23.8% (95% CI, 19.0 - 29.3) for hr-HPV infection [stratified as 27.0% (95% CI, 19.8 - 35.1) using AmpFire and 20.3% (95% CI, 13.9 - 28.0) using MA-6000]. Factors associated with hr-HPV infection were age, parity (aOR, 1.42; 95% CI, 1.02 - 1.97), current contraceptive use (aOR, 5.86; 95% CI, 1.33 - 25.72), visual inspection 'positivity' (aOR, 2.89; 95% CI, 1.11 - 6.82), and past (aOR, 0.18; 95% CI, 0.06 - 0.51) or current (aOR, 0.05; 95% CI, 0.01 - 0.41) non-estrogen-containing contraceptive use. Factors associated with prior cervical screening were age and marital status.
CONCLUSIONS: Our study suggests that cervical screening based on visual inspection strategies was relatively poorly utilized by FHWs. The cross-sectional prevalence of hr-HPV and precancerous lesions suggests that FHWs maintain a similar risk for hr-HPV infection and cervical cancer as the general population. Health authorities planning to implement primary HPV screening should explore ownership strategies to improve the participation of FHWs through community engagement initiatives.

articles.title: Association between epidural analgesia in the second delivery among women with a prior epidural and maternal and neonatal outcomes: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.authors: Zhang Y, Su S, Li Q et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The impact of epidural analgesia use in the second delivery among women with a prior epidural on maternal and neonatal outcomes remains unclear.
METHODS: A retrospective study was conducted to assess the impact of epidural analgesia use in the second delivery among women with a prior epidural on maternal and neonatal outcomes between July 1, 2016 and December 31, 2023. Demographic information, as well as gestational and delivery characteristics, were obtained from the hospital's electronic health record system. Multivariable linear and logistic regression models were employed to assess the association between epidural analgesia use among multiparous women with a prior labor epidural exposure and maternal and neonatal outcomes.
RESULTS: A total of 1827 women were included for analysis. The total duration of labor and the duration of first-second stage of labor were significantly longer in labor epidural analgesia group than in the non-labor epidural analgesia group (342.3 ± 140.9 min vs. 273.9 ± 114.6 min, p < 0.001; 336.2 ± 140.9 min vs. 267.9 ± 114.4 min, p < 0.001, respectively). Neither neonatal asphyxia nor NICU admission occurred in either group. Labor epidural analgesia was independently associated with prolonged the total duration of labor (β 68.01, 95% CI 55.35-80.67, p < 0.001) and the duration of first-second stage of labor (β 67.92, 95% CI 55.26-80.57, p < 0.001). Additionally, labor epidural analgesia was associated with a significantly increased length of stay (β 0.31, 95% CI 0.19-0.43, p < 0.001). Labor epidural analgesia did not significantly increase the risk of assisted delivery (aOR 0.4, 95% CI 0.07-2.28, p = 0.3), postpartum hemorrhage (aOR 0.98, 95% CI 0.52-1.84, p = 0.954) and postpartum complications (aOR 2.63, 95% CI 0.75-9.22, p = 0.131).
CONCLUSION: Epidural analgesia use in the second delivery among women with a prior epidural was associated with increased length of labor and extended hospital length of stay. However, it did not increase the rates of assisted delivery, postpartum hemorrhage, or postpartum complications.

articles.title: Association between breastfeeding and pelvic floor dysfunction: a systematic review.
articles.authors: Manzini C, Kortman MCP, Bosschaart N et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This systematic review evaluates the association between breastfeeding and pelvic floor (dys)function. Since breastfeeding has well-known positive effects, exclusive breastfeeding is recommended for the first 6 months after birth. At the same time, the postpartum period is the period in which mothers recover from pregnancy and delivery. It has been hypothesized that breastfeeding can negatively affect pelvic floor regeneration by sustaining a hypoestrogenic state. Considering the health benefits of both breastfeeding and optimal pelvic floor recovery, the association between the two was assessed.
METHODS: PubMed and Cochrane CENTRAL library were searched on the 29th of November 2023. Studies on the association between breastfeeding and pelvic floor (dys)function were included. The results were grouped into five domains: (1) dyspareunia, (2) urinary incontinence (UI), (3) pelvic organ prolapse (POP), (4) anal incontinence (AI), and (5) pelvic floor muscles function (PFMF). A qualitative synthesis of the results was performed.
RESULTS: Nineteen studies were retrieved for dyspareunia, eight for UI, two for POP and AI, and three for PFMF. Fourteen studies showed a significant association between breastfeeding and dyspareunia, with a greater risk of dyspareunia in the breastfeeding group. The studies on UI, POP and AI, and PFMF reported conflicting results. A meta-analysis was not performed due to heterogeneity among studies.
CONCLUSIONS: The available literature shows an association between breastfeeding and postpartum dyspareunia. However, no causal relation can be inferred. In the case of symptoms, women should be informed of the multifactorial nature of dyspareunia and of the benefits of breastfeeding. The association of breastfeeding with UI, POP and AI has not been established. Any advice to discontinue breastfeeding because of these symptoms is not supported by scientific evidence.

articles.title: Comparison of the anaesthetic efficacy and safety of different doses of esketamine combined with propofol in hysteroscopic surgery: a randomised, double-blind controlled trial.
articles.authors: Li R, Chi Z, Chen J et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hysteroscopy is increasingly performed under day-surgery total intravenous anaesthesia, but propofol alone provides insufficient analgesia and the routine adjunct of opioids is associated with respiratory depression and emetic complications. Esketamine, the S-enantiomer of ketamine, offers analgesia together with sympathomimetic support and represents a promising opioid-sparing alternative; however, its optimal dose for combination with propofol in this setting has not been firmly established.
METHODS: In this prospective, randomised, double-blind, controlled trial, 160 women aged 18-60 years (ASA I-II) scheduled for elective hysteroscopy were assigned to four groups using computer-generated random numbers: K1 (esketamine 0.15 mg/kg), K2 (esketamine 0.3 mg/kg), K3 (esketamine 0.5 mg/kg) or S (sufentanil 0.1 µg/kg). All patients received an induction dose of propofol 1.5 mg/kg followed by maintenance infusion of 4-6 mg·kg⁻¹·h⁻¹. The primary outcomes were postoperative pain (Numeric Rating Scale, NRS) and total intra-operative propofol consumption; secondary outcomes were perioperative haemodynamics, recovery time and adverse events. After exclusion of three patients with major protocol deviation, 157 patients were analysed (K1 = 40, K2 = 38, K3 = 40, S = 39).
RESULTS: Demographics, surgical and anaesthesia times were comparable between groups. NRS scores at 10 and 30 min post-recovery were significantly lower in groups K2, K3 and S than in group K1 (p < 0.001). Mean arterial pressure at the start of surgery (T2, immediately after the start of surgery) and at the end of surgery (T3) was significantly higher in K1 than in the other three groups (p < 0.001). Total propofol consumption did not differ between groups (p = 0.95). The incidence of intra-operative hypertension was significantly greater in K1 (22.5%) than in K2 (0%), K3 (5.0%) and S (5.1%) (p = 0.002), and the incidence of SpO₂ < 90% was significantly greater in S (20.5%) than in K1 (0%), K2 (5.3%) and K3 (5.0%) (p = 0.004). The incidence of emergence agitation differed among groups, with the highest incidence observed in K3 (10.0%) (p = 0.034).
CONCLUSIONS: Among the regimens tested, esketamine 0.3 mg/kg combined with propofol 1.5 mg/kg was associated with a favourable balance of analgesia, haemodynamic stability and safety. articles.title: Comparison of intraoperative hemodynamic changes and recovery outcomes between non-menopausal and postmenopausal women undergoing total abdominal hysterectomy under general anesthesia.
articles.authors: Mashak B, Abdollahi S, Habib H et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Menopausal status may influence autonomic and hemodynamic responses during surgery because of hormonal changes affecting vascular tone and thermoregulation. However, evidence comparing perioperative physiological responses and post-anesthesia care unit outcomes between non-menopausal and postmenopausal women undergoing total abdominal hysterectomy remains limited. This study compared perioperative hemodynamic changes and early postoperative recovery between these two populations.
METHODS: In this prospective observational study, 48 women (25 non-menopausal and 23 postmenopausal) undergoing elective total abdominal hysterectomy under standardized general anesthesia were enrolled. Intraoperative and recovery physiologic parameters, postoperative shivering, pain, nausea and vomiting, agitation, and consciousness were assessed and compared between groups using appropriate statistical analyses.
RESULTS: Non-menopausal women demonstrated significantly higher postoperative HR, higher incidence of postoperative shivering, and lower body temperature than postmenopausal women (both P < 0.05). In contrast, MAP was significantly higher in postmenopausal patients throughout the perioperative period (P = 0.001), although no significant time-by-group interaction was observed. HR and temperature showed a significant interaction between time and menopausal status (P = 0.001). No significant between-group differences were found in postoperative pain, nausea and vomiting, agitation, oxygen saturation, level of consciousness, or recovery time (all P > 0.05).
CONCLUSION: Menopausal status was associated with differences in postoperative heart rate and thermoregulatory responses during recovery after total abdominal hysterectomy under general anesthesia, while overall early recovery outcomes remained comparable between groups.
